data.v: तं हीनपर्णं पतिताग्रशाखं; विशीर्णपुष्पं प्रसमीक्ष्य वायुः । उवाच वाक्यं स्मयमान एनं; मुदा युतं शल्मलिं रुग्णशाखम् ॥
data.md: Seeing him divested of top, branches, leaves and flowers, the Wind, filled with joy, smilingly said to that lord of the forest which had before such a huge appearance.

data.v: अहमप्येवमेव त्वां कुर्वाणः शल्मले रुषा । आत्मना यत्कृतं कृत्स्नं शाखानामपकर्षणम् ॥
data.md: The Wind said-Filled with anger, O Shalmali, I would have done to you exactly what you have done to yourself by cutting off all your branches.

data.v: हीनपुष्पाग्रशाखस्त्वं शीर्णाङ्कुरपलाशवान् । आत्मदुर्मन्त्रितेनेह मद्वीर्यवशगोऽभवः ॥
data.md: You are now shorn of your proud top and flowers, and you are now without your shoots and leaves. For your own bad counsels, you have been brought under my control.

data.v: एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचो वायोः शल्मलिर्व्रीडितस्तदा । अतप्यत वचः स्मृत्वा नारदो यत्तदाब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of the Wind, the Shalmali feit great shame. Remembering also the words of Narada, he began to repent greatly for his mistake.

data.v: एवं यो राजशार्दूल दुर्बलः सन्बलीयसा । वैरमासज्जते बालस्तप्यते शल्मलिर्यथा ॥
तस्माद्वैरं न कुर्वीत दुर्बलो बलवत्तरैः । शोचेद्धि वैरं कुर्वाणो यथा वै शल्मलिस्तथा ॥
data.md: Thus, O foremost of kings, a weak and foolish person, by exciting the enmity of a powerful enemy, is at last compelled to repent like the Shalmali in story. Therefore, a weak person should not behave hostility with a strong person.

data.v: न हि वैरं महात्मानो विवृण्वन्त्यपकारिषु । शनैः शनैर्महाराज दर्शयन्ति स्म ते बलम् ॥
data.md: Even when gifted with equal might, people do not suddenly create enmities with those who have injured them. On the other hand, they show their power gradually, O king.

data.v: वैरं न कुर्वीत नरो दुर्बुद्धिर्बुद्धिजीविना । बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतो याति तूलेष्विव हुताशनः ॥
data.md: A foolish person should never excite the hostility of an intelligent person. In such cases the intelligence of the intelligent man works like fire penetrating a heap of dry grass.

data.v: न हि बुद्ध्या समं किंचिद्विद्यते पुरुषे नृप । तथा बलेन राजेन्द्र न समोऽस्तीति चिन्तयेत् ॥
data.md: Intelligence is the most valuable thing that a person can have. Likewise, O king, a man can have nothing here more valuable than power.

data.v: तस्मात्क्षमेत बालाय जडाय बधिराय च । बलाधिकाय राजेन्द्र तद्दृष्टं त्वयि शत्रुहन् ॥
data.md: One should, therefore, pass over the wrongs inflicted by a person possessed of superior strength, as one should overlook the acts of a child, an idiot, or one who is blind or deaf. The wisdom of this saying is seen in your case, O slayer of foes.

data.v: अक्षौहिण्यो दशैका च सप्त चैव महाद्युते । बलेन न समा राजन्नर्जुनस्य महात्मनः ॥
data.md: The eleven Akshauhinis (of Duryodhana), and the seven (collected by yourself), were not, in power, equal to the single-handed Arjuna of great soul.

data.v: हतास्ताश्चैव भग्नाश्च पाण्डवेन यशस्विना । चरता बलमास्थाय पाकशासनिना मृधे ॥
data.md: All the troops (of Duryodhana), therefore, were dispersed and killed by that illustrious Pandava, that son of Paka's chastiser, as he moved about in the field of battle, depending on his own strength.

data.v: उक्तास्ते राजधर्माश्च आपद्धर्माश्च भारत । विस्तरेण महाराज किं भूयः प्रब्रवीमि ते ॥
data.md: I have, O Bharata, described to you the duties of kings and ethics of con-in detail. What else, O king, do you wish to hear.

data.v: पापस्य यदधिष्ठानं यतः पापं प्रवर्तते । एतदिच्छाम्यहं ज्ञातुं तत्त्वेन भरतर्षभ ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said-I wish, O foremost of Bharata's race, to hear fully the source from which sin proceeds and the basis upon which it depends.

data.v: पापस्य यदधिष्ठानं तच्छृणुष्व नराधिप । एको लोभो महाग्राहो लोभात्पापं प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Hear, O king, what is the origin of sin! Covetousness alone is a great destroyer. From covetousness originates sin.

data.v: अतः पापमधर्मश्च तथा दुःखमनुत्तमम् । निकृत्या मूलमेतद्धि येन पापकृतो जनाः ॥
data.md: Sin and impiety proceed from this source, along with great misery. This covetousness is the root of also all the cunning and hypocrisy in the world. It is covetousness that makes men perpetrate sin.

data.v: लोभात्क्रोधः प्रभवति लोभात्कामः प्रवर्तते । लोभान्मोहश्च माया च मानस्तम्भः परासुता ॥
data.md: From covetousness originates anger, from covetousness grows lust; and it is covetousness which begets loss of judgement, decision, pride, haughtiness, malice, vindictiveness shamelessness, loss of prosperity, loss of virtue, anxiety, and infamy.

data.v: अक्षमा ह्रीपरित्यागः श्रीनाशो धर्मसंक्षयः । अभिध्याप्रज्ञता चैव सर्वं लोभात्प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: From covetousness originates anger, from covetousness grows lust; and it is covetousness which begets loss of judgement, decision, pride, haughtiness, malice, vindictiveness shamelessness, loss of prosperity, loss of virtue, anxiety, and infamy.

data.v: अन्यायश्चावितर्कश्च विकर्मसु च याः क्रियाः । कूटविद्यादयश्चैव रूपैश्वर्यमदस्तथा ॥
सर्वभूतेष्वविश्वासः सर्वभूतेष्वनार्जवम् । सर्वभूतेष्वभिद्रोहः सर्वभूतेष्वयुक्तता । हरणं परवित्तानां परदाराभिमर्शनम् ॥
वाग्वेगो मानसो वेगो निन्दावेगस्तथैव च । उपस्थोदरयोर्वेगो मृत्युवेगश्च दारुणः ॥
ईर्ष्यावेगश्च बलवान्मिथ्यावेगश्च दुस्त्यजः । रसवेगश्च दुर्वारः श्रोत्रवेगश्च दुःसहः ॥
कुत्सा विकत्था मात्सर्यं पापं दुष्करकारिता । साहसानां च सर्वेषामकार्याणां क्रियास्तथा ॥
जातौ बाल्येऽथ कौमारे यौवने चापि मानवः । न संत्यजत्यात्मकर्म यन्न जीर्यति जीर्यतः ॥
यो न पूरयितुं शक्यो लोभः प्राप्त्या कुरूद्वह । नित्यं गम्भीरतोयाभिरापगाभिरिवोदधिः । न प्रहृष्यति लाभैर्यो यश्च कामैर्न तृप्यति ॥
यो न देवैर्न गन्धर्वैर्नासुरैर्न महोरगैः । ज्ञायते नृप तत्त्वेन सर्वैर्भूतगणैस्तथा । स लोभः सह मोहेन विजेतव्यो जितात्मना ॥
दम्भो द्रोहश्च निन्दा च पैशुन्यं मत्सरस्तथा । भवन्त्येतानि कौरव्य लुब्धानामकृतात्मनाम् ॥
सुमहान्त्यपि शास्त्राणि धारयन्ति बहुश्रुताः । छेत्तारः संशयानां च क्लिश्यन्तीहाल्पबुद्धयः ॥
द्वेषक्रोधप्रसक्ताश्च शिष्टाचारबहिष्कृताः । अन्तःक्षुरा वाङ्मधुराः कूपाश्छन्नास्तृणैरिव । धर्मवैतंसिकाः क्षुद्रा मुष्णन्ति ध्वजिनो जगत् ॥
data.md: Covetous men are swayed by malice and spite. They are beyond the range of good conduct. Wily as they are in their hearts, their speeches are sweet. They are like dark pits whose mouths are covered with grass.

data.v: कुर्वते च बहून्मार्गांस्तांस्तान्हेतुबलाश्रिताः । सर्वं मार्गं विलुम्पन्ति लोभाज्ञानेषु निष्ठिताः ॥
data.md: They dress themselves in the hypocritical garb of religion, Low minded as they are, they rob the world, showing the standard of religion and virtue. Depending upon the strength of palpable reasons, they create various divisions in religion. Being anxious to serve cupidity, they destroy the ways of righteousness.

data.v: धर्मस्याह्रियमाणस्य लोभग्रस्तैर्दुरात्मभिः । या या विक्रियते संस्था ततः साभिप्रपद्यते ॥
data.md: When wicked men under the influence of covetousness practise for the inere show of righteousness, the result is that the desecrations committed by them, soon become current among men.

data.v: दर्पः क्रोधो मदः स्वप्नो हर्षः शोकोऽतिमानिता । तत एव हि कौरव्य दृश्यन्ते लुब्धबुद्धिषु । एतानशिष्टान्बुध्यस्व नित्यं लोभसमन्वितान् ॥
data.md: Pride, anger, arrogance, insensibility, fits of joy and sorrow, and self-conceit, all these, O descendant of Kuru, are to be seen in persons under the influence of covetousness.

data.v: शिष्टांस्तु परिपृच्छेथा यान्वक्ष्यामि शुचिव्रतान् । येषु वृत्तिभयं नास्ति परलोकभयं न च ॥
नामिषेषु प्रसङ्गोऽस्ति न प्रियेष्वप्रियेषु च । शिष्टाचारः प्रियो येषु दमो येषु प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
सुखं दुःखं परं येषां सत्यं येषां परायणम् । दातारो न गृहीतारो दयावन्तस्तथैव च ॥
पितृदेवातिथेयाश्च नित्योद्युक्तास्तथैव च । सर्वोपकारिणो धीराः सर्वधर्मानुपालकाः ॥
सर्वभूतहिताश्चैव सर्वदेयाश्च भारत । न ते चालयितुं शक्या धर्मव्यापारपारगाः ॥
न तेषां भिद्यते वृत्तं यत्पुरा साधुभिः कृतम् । न त्रासिनो न चपला न रौद्राः सत्पथे स्थिताः ॥
ते सेव्याः साधुभिर्नित्यं येष्वहिंसा प्रतिष्ठिता । कामक्रोधव्यपेता ये निर्ममा निरहंकृताः । सुव्रताः स्थिरमर्यादास्तानुपास्स्व च पृच्छ च ॥
data.md: They are free from lust and anger. They are not attached to any worldly object. They have no pride. They observe excellent vows. They always command respect. Do you, therefore, always attend them and seek instruction from them.

data.v: न गवार्थं यशोर्थं वा धर्मस्तेषां युधिष्ठिर । अवश्यकार्य इत्येव शरीरस्य क्रियास्तथा ॥
data.md: They never acquire virtue, O Yudhishthira, for the sake of riches or of fame. They acquire error it only, because they know it as a duty like that of supporting the body.

data.v: न भयं क्रोधचापल्यं न शोकस्तेषु विद्यते । न धर्मध्वजिनश्चैव न गुह्यं किंचिदास्थिताः ॥
data.md: Fear, anger, restlessness, and sorrow do not live in them. They carry no external garb of religion for misleading their fellow-men. They observe no mystery.

data.v: येष्वलोभस्तथामोहो ये च सत्यार्जवे रताः । तेषु कौन्तेय रज्येथा येष्वतन्द्रीकृतं मनः ॥
data.md: They are perfectly contended. They have of judgement originating from covetousness. They always follow truth and sincerity. Their hearts never deviate from righteousness. You should always respect them, O son of Kunti!

data.v: ये न हृष्यन्ति लाभेषु नालाभेषु व्यथन्ति च । निर्ममा निरहंकाराः सत्त्वस्थाः समदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: They are never overjoyed at any acquisition or pained at any loss. Without being attached to anything, and shorn of pride, they are devoted to the quality of Goodness, and they regard all impartially.

data.v: लाभालाभौ सुखदुःखे च तात; प्रियाप्रिये मरणं जीवितं च । समानि येषां स्थिरविक्रमाणां; बुद्धात्मनां सत्त्वमवस्थितानाम् ॥
data.md: Gain and loss, happiness and misery, the agreeable and the disagreeable, life and death, are held in equal estimation by those men of firm mind, engaged in acquiring (divine) knowledge, and wending the path of tranquility and righteousness.

data.v: सुखप्रियैस्तान्सुमहाप्रतापा;न्यत्तोऽप्रमत्तश्च समर्थयेथाः । दैवात्सर्वे गुणवन्तो भवन्ति; शुभाशुभा वाक्प्रलापा यथैव ॥
data.md: Keeping your senses under control and without yielding to carelessness, you should always adore those great persons who bear such love for virtue. O blessed one, one's words always yield good only through the favour of the gods. Under other circumstances, words beget evil consequence. words always yield good only through the favour of the gods. Under other circumstances, words beget evil consequence.

data.v: अनर्थानामधिष्ठानमुक्तो लोभः पितामह । अज्ञानमपि वै तात श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said You have said, O grandfather, that the root of all evils is covetousness. I wish, O sire, to licar fully of ignorance.

data.v: करोति पापं योऽज्ञानान्नात्मनो वेत्ति च क्षमम् । प्रद्वेष्टि साधुवृत्तांश्च स लोकस्यैति वाच्यताम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said The person who commits sin out of ignorance, who does not know that his end is near, and who always hates persons of good conduct, soon incurs infamy in the world.

data.v: अज्ञानान्निरयं याति तथाज्ञानेन दुर्गतिम् । अज्ञानात्क्लेशमाप्नोति तथापत्सु निमज्जति ॥
data.md: In consequence of ignorance one goes to hell. Ignorance one suffers miseries and incurs great danger.

data.v: अज्ञानस्य प्रवृत्तिं च स्थानं वृद्धिं क्षयोदयौ । मूलं योगं गतिं कालं कारणं हेतुमेव च ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said I wish, O king, to hear fully the origin, the place, the growth, the decay, the rise, the root, the attribute, the course, the time, the cause, and the result of ignorance. The misery that is felt here is the outcome of ignorance.

data.v: श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वेन यथावदिह पार्थिव । अज्ञानप्रभवं हीदं यद्दुःखमुपलभ्यते ॥
रागो द्वेषस्तथा मोहो हर्षः शोकोऽभिमानिता । कामः क्रोधश्च दर्पश्च तन्द्रीरालस्यमेव च ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Attachment, hate, loss of judgement, joy, sorrow, vanity, lust, anger, pride, procrastination, idleness, desire, aversion, jealousy, envy, and all other sinful habits pass by the common name of ignorance.

data.v: इच्छा द्वेषस्तथा तापः परवृद्ध्युपतापिता । अज्ञानमेतन्निर्दिष्टं पापानां चैव याः क्रियाः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Attachment, hate, loss of judgement, joy, sorrow, vanity, lust, anger, pride, procrastination, idleness, desire, aversion, jealousy, envy, and all other sinful habits pass by the common name of ignorance.

data.v: एतया या प्रवृत्तिश्च वृद्ध्यादीन्यांश्च पृच्छसि । विस्तरेण महाबाहो शृणु तच्च विशां पते ॥
data.md: Hear fully now, O king, about its nature, growth and other characteristics after which you enquire.

data.v: उभावेतौ समफलौ समदोषौ च भारत । अज्ञानं चातिलोभश्चाप्येकं जानीहि पार्थिव ॥
data.md: These two, viz., ignorance and covetousness, know, O king, are the same. Both produce the same fruits and same faults, O Bharata.

data.v: लोभप्रभवमज्ञानं वृद्धं भूयः प्रवर्धते । स्थाने स्थानं क्षये क्षैण्यमुपैति विविधां गतिम् ॥
data.md: Ignorance originates from covetousness. Ignorance grows along with coveteousness. Ignorance exists simultaneously with covetousness. Ignorance decreases with covetousness. It rises with the rise of covetousness. Manifold again is its course.

data.v: मूलं लोभस्य महतः कालात्मगतिरेव च । छिन्नेऽच्छिन्ने तथा लोभे कारणं काल एव हि ॥
तस्याज्ञानात्तु लोभो हि लोभादज्ञानमेव च । सर्वे दोषास्तथा लोभात्तस्माल्लोभं विवर्जयेत् ॥
data.md: The root of covetousness is loss of judgement. Loss of judgement, again, is its inseparable quality. Eternity is ignorance's course. The time when ignorance occurs is when the objects of covetousness are not gained.

data.v: जनको युवनाश्वश्च वृषादर्भिः प्रसेनजित् । लोभक्षयाद्दिवं प्राप्तास्तथैवान्ये जनाधिपाः ॥
data.md: From ignorance proceeds covetousness, and from the latter proceeds ignorance. Covetousness produces all faults. For these reasons every one should avoid covetousness. Janaka, Yuvanashva, Vrishadarbhi, Prasenajit, and other kings acquired heaven for their having conquered covetousness.

data.v: प्रत्यक्षं तु कुरुश्रेष्ठ त्यज लोभमिहात्मना । त्यक्त्वा लोभं सुखं लोके प्रेत्य चानुचरिष्यसि ॥
data.md: Do you before all persons, avoid covetousness by a strong determination, O Kuru chief. Avoiding covetousness you will acquire happiness both here and in the next world.

data.v: स्वाध्यायकृतयत्नस्य ब्राह्मणस्य पितामह । धर्मकामस्य धर्मात्मन्किं नु श्रेय इहोच्यते ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of virtuous soul, what, indeed, yields great merit for a person assiduously engaged in the study of the Vedas and desirous of gaining virtue.

data.v: बहुधादर्शने लोके श्रेयो यदिह मन्यसे । अस्मिँल्लोके परे चैव तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: That which yields in this world high merit is of various kinds as described in the scriptures. Tell me, O grandfather, about what is regarded as such both in this world and in the next.

data.v: महानयं धर्मपथो बहुशाखश्च भारत । किं स्विदेवेह धर्माणामनुष्ठेयतमं मतम् ॥
data.md: The path of duty is long and has numberless branches, O Bharata. Amongst those duties what are those few which should, in your opinion, be observed in preference to all others?

data.v: धर्मस्य महतो राजन्बहुशाखस्य तत्त्वतः । यन्मूलं परमं तात तत्सर्वं ब्रूह्यतन्द्रितः ॥
data.md: Tell me, O king, fully about that which is so vast and which has so many branches.

data.v: हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि येन श्रेयः प्रपत्स्यसे । पीत्वामृतमिव प्राज्ञो ज्ञानतृप्तो भविष्यसि ॥
data.md: Bhishma said I shall describe to you that by which you may acquire high merit. Wise as you are, you will be satisfied with the knowledge I will impart to you, like a person gratified with having drunk ambrosia.

data.v: धर्मस्य विधयो नैके ते ते प्रोक्ता महर्षिभिः । स्वं स्वं विज्ञानमाश्रित्य दमस्तेषां परायणम् ॥
data.md: The rules of duty described by the great Rishis, each depending upon his own wisdom, are many. The highest among them all is selfcontrol.

data.v: दमं निःश्रेयसं प्राहुर्वृद्धा निश्चयदर्शिनः । ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण दमो धर्मः सनातनः ॥
data.md: Those amongst the ancient Rishis that were acquainted with truth said that self-control, leads to the highest merit. Self-control is the eternal duty of the Brahmanas especially.

data.v: नादान्तस्य क्रियासिद्धिर्यथावदुपलभ्यते । दमो दानं तथा यज्ञानधीतं चातिवर्तते ॥
data.md: It is from self-control that he acquires the due fruition of his acts. Self-control of surpasses (in merit) charity and sacrifice and study of the Vedas.

data.v: दमस्तेजो वर्धयति पवित्रं च दमः परम् । विपाप्मा तेजसा युक्तः पुरुषो विन्दते महत् ॥
data.md: Self-control increases (his) energy. Selfcontrol is highly sacred. Through self-control a man becomes purified of all his sins and gifted with energy, and therefore, acquires the highest blessedness.

data.v: दमेन सदृशं धर्मं नान्यं लोकेषु शुश्रुम । दमो हि परमो लोके प्रशस्तः सर्वधर्मिणाम् ॥
data.md: We have not heard that there is any other duty in all the worlds equal to self-control. Self-control, according to all virtuous persons, is the highest virtues in this world.

data.v: प्रेत्य चापि मनुष्येन्द्र परमं विन्दते सुखम् । दमेन हि समायुक्तो महान्तं धर्ममश्नुते ॥
data.md: Through self-control, O foremost of men, a person enjoys the highest happiness both in this world and in the next. Gifted with self-control, one wins great virtue.

data.v: सुखं दान्तः प्रस्वपिति सुखं च प्रतिबुध्यते । सुखं पर्येति लोकांश्च मनश्चास्य प्रसीदति ॥
data.md: The self-controlled man sleeps in happiness and awakes in happiness, and moves through the world in happiness. His mind is always cheerful.

data.v: अदान्तः पुरुषः क्लेशमभीक्ष्णं प्रतिपद्यते । अनर्थांश्च बहूनन्यान्प्रसृजत्यात्मदोषजान् ॥
data.md: The man who is without self-control always suffers misery. Such a man brings upon himself many calamities all begotten by his own faults.

data.v: आश्रमेषु चतुर्ष्वाहुर्दममेवोत्तमं व्रतम् । तस्य लिङ्गानि वक्ष्यामि येषां समुदयो दमः ॥
data.md: It has been said that in all the four modes of life self-control is the best of vows. I shall now describe to you the characteristic marks the sum-total of which is called self-control.

data.v: क्षमा धृतिरहिंसा च समता सत्यमार्जवम् । इन्द्रियावजयो दाक्ष्यं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
data.md: Forgiveness, patience, abstention from injury, impartiality, truth, sincerity, control of the senses, cleverness, mildness, modesty, firmness, liberality, freedom from anger, contentment, sweetness of words, benevolence, freedom from malice, all these combined make up self-control.

data.v: अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः संतोषः प्रियवादिता । अविवित्सानसूया चाप्येषां समुदयो दमः ॥
data.md: Forgiveness, patience, abstention from injury, impartiality, truth, sincerity, control of the senses, cleverness, mildness, modesty, firmness, liberality, freedom from anger, contentment, sweetness of words, benevolence, freedom from malice, all these combined make up self-control.

data.v: गुरुपूजा च कौरव्य दया भूतेष्वपैशुनम् । जनवादोऽमृषावादः स्तुतिनिन्दाविवर्जनम् ॥
data.md: It also consists, O son of Kuru, of respect for the preceptor and mercy for all. The selfcontrolled man avoids both adulation and slander. Depravity, infamy, falsehood, lust, covetousness, pride, arrogance, self-edification, fear, envy, and disrespect, are all shunned by the self-controlled man.

data.v: कामः क्रोधश्च लोभश्च दर्पः स्तम्भो विकत्थनम् । मोह ईर्ष्यावमानश्चेत्येतद्दान्तो न सेवते ॥
अनिन्दितो ह्यकामात्माथाल्पेच्छोऽथानसूयकः । समुद्रकल्पः स नरो न कदाचन पूर्यते ॥
data.md: He never incurs obloquy. He is free from envy. He is never satisfied with trivial acquisitions. He is like the ocean which can never be filled.

data.v: अहं त्वयि मम त्वं च मयि ते तेषु चाप्यहम् । पूर्वसंबन्धिसंयोगान्नैतद्दान्तो निषेवते ॥
data.md: The self-controlled man is never fettered by the attachments originating from earthly connections and sentiments like these,-'I am yours, You are yours. They are in me, and I am in them.

data.v: सर्वा ग्राम्यास्तथारण्या याश्च लोके प्रवृत्तयः । निन्दां चैव प्रशंसां च यो नाश्रयति मुच्यते ॥
data.md: Such a man who follows the practices of either cities or the woods, and who never vilifies others nor indulges in adulation, acquires liberation.

data.v: मैत्रोऽथ शीलसंपन्नः सुसहायपरश्च यः । मुक्तश्च विविधैः सङ्गैस्तस्य प्रेत्य महत्फलम् ॥
data.md: Practising universal friendliness, and virtuous conduct, and possessed of cheerful spirit and psychic knowledge, and freed from the various attachments of the Earth, a person acquires great reward in the next world.

data.v: सुवृत्तः शीलसंपन्नः प्रसन्नात्मात्मविद्बुधः । प्राप्येह लोके सत्कारं सुगतिं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Of excellent behaviour and observant of duties, cheerful and endued with learning and knowledge of self, such a man acquires esteem while in this world and attains to a high end hereafter.

data.v: कर्म यच्छुभमेवेह सद्भिराचरितं च यत् । तदेव ज्ञानयुक्तस्य मुनेर्धर्मो न हीयते ॥
data.md: All acts that are considered as good on Earth,-all those acts that are practised by the righteous, form the path of the ascetic endued with knowledge. A person that is good never transgresses that path.

data.v: निष्क्रम्य वनमास्थाय ज्ञानयुक्तो जितेन्द्रियः । कालाकाङ्क्षी चरन्नेवं ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
data.md: Retiring from the world, and living in the woods, that learned person, having a complete mastery over the senses who treads in that path, expecting his own demise, is sure to acquire the state of Brahma.

data.v: अभयं यस्य भूतेभ्यो भूतानामभयं यतः । तस्य देहाद्विमुक्तस्य भयं नास्ति कुतश्चन ॥
data.md: He who has no fear of any creature, and whom no creature fears, has, after, the dissolution of his body, no fear to meet.

data.v: अवाचिनोति कर्माणि न च संप्रचिनोति ह । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मैत्रायणगतिश्चरेत् ॥
data.md: He who exhausts his merits without trying to hoard them up, who considers all creatures equally and cherishes friendship for the entire universe, attains to Brahma.

data.v: शकुनीनामिवाकाशे जले वारिचरस्य वा । यथा गतिर्न दृश्येत तथा तस्य न संशयः ॥
data.md: As the route of birds along the sky or of fowl over the surface of water cannot be made out, so the path of such a person (on Earth) does not attract notice.

data.v: गृहानुत्सृज्य यो राजन्मोक्षमेवाभिपद्यते । लोकास्तेजोमयास्तस्य कल्पन्ते शाश्वतीः समाः ॥
data.md: O king, many bright worlds await him for eternal enjoyment, who renouncing his domestic life, adopts the religious course of emancipation. acts,

data.v: संन्यस्य सर्वकर्माणि संन्यस्य विधिवत्तपः । संन्यस्य विविधा विद्याः सर्वं संन्यस्य चैव ह ॥
data.md: If abandoning all abandoning penances in due time, leaving off the various branches of study, in fact, leaving off all things, one becomes pure in his desires, freed from all restraints, of cheerful soul, conversant with self, and of pure heart, he then acquires esteem in this world and at last attains to heaven.

data.v: कामेषु चाप्यनावृत्तः प्रसन्नात्मात्मविच्छुचिः । प्राप्येह लोके सत्कारं स्वर्गं समभिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Of excellent behaviour and observant of duties, cheerful and endued with learning and knowledge of self, such a man acquires esteem while in this world and attains to a high end hereafter.

data.v: यच्च पैतामहं स्थानं ब्रह्मराशिसमुद्भवम् । गुहायां पिहितं नित्यं तद्दमेनाभिपद्यते ॥
data.md: That eternal region of the grandfather which originates from Vedic penances, and which is concealed in a cave, can only be acquired by self-control.

data.v: ज्ञानारामस्य बुद्धस्य सर्वभूताविरोधिनः । नावृत्तिभयमस्तीह परलोके भयं कुतः ॥
data.md: He who finds pleasure in true knowledge, who has become enlightened, and who never injures any creature, has no fear of returning to this world, not to speak of any fear from the other.

data.v: एक एव दमे दोषो द्वितीयो नोपपद्यते । यदेनं क्षमया युक्तमशक्तं मन्यते जनः ॥
data.md: There is only one fault in self-control. No second fault is seen in it. A person who has self-control is considered by men as weak and imbecile.

data.v: एतस्य तु महाप्राज्ञ दोषस्य सुमहान्गुणः । क्षमायां विपुला लोकाः सुलभा हि सहिष्णुना ॥
data.md: you of great wisdom, this attribute has only one defect. Its merits are many. By forgiveness, the man of self-control may easily acquire numberless worlds.

data.v: दान्तस्य किमरण्येन तथादान्तस्य भारत । यत्रैव हि वसेद्दान्तस्तदरण्यं स आश्रमः ॥
data.md: Of what use is forest to a man of selfcontrol. Likewise, O Bharata, of what use is the forest to him that has no self-control? That is a forest where the man of self-control lives, and that is even a sacred asylum.

data.v: एतद्भीष्मस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा युधिष्ठिरः । अमृतेनेव संतृप्तः प्रहृष्टः समपद्यत ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of Bhishina, Yudhishthira became highly pleased as if he had drunk nectar.

data.v: पुनश्च परिपप्रच्छ भीष्मं धर्मभृतां वरम् । तपः प्रति स चोवाच तस्मै सर्वं कुरूद्वह ॥
data.md: Again the king asked that foremost of virtuous men. That perpetuator of Kuru's race once more began to discourse cheerfully on the subject.

data.v: सर्वमेतत्तपोमूलं कवयः परिचक्षते । न ह्यतप्ततपा मूढः क्रियाफलमवाप्यते ॥
data.md: Bhishma said They who arc endued with knowledge say that everything springs from penance. That foolish person who has not practised penances does not get the rewards of even his own acts.

data.v: प्रजापतिरिदं सर्वं तपसैवासृजत्प्रभुः । तथैव वेदानृषयस्तपसा प्रतिपेदिरे ॥
data.md: The powerful Creator created all this universe with the help of penances. In ihe same way, the Rishis won ihe Vedas by the power of penanccs.

data.v: तपसो ह्यानुपूर्व्येण फलमूलानिलाशनाः । त्रीँल्लोकांस्तपसा सिद्धाः पश्यन्ति सुसमाहिताः ॥
data.md: It was by the help of penances that the Grandfather created food, fruits and roots. It is one by penances that ascetics behold the three worlds, with enraptured souls.

data.v: औषधान्यगदादीनि तिस्रो विद्याश्च संस्कृताः । तपसैव हि सिध्यन्ति तपोमूलं हि साधनम् ॥
data.md: Medicines and all antidotes to poisonous articles, and the various acts (seen here), produce their intended results through the help of penance. The fulfilment of all purposes depends upon penance.

data.v: यद्दुरापं दुराम्नायं दुराधर्षं दुरुत्सहम् । सर्वं तत्तपसा शक्यं तपो हि दुरतिक्रमम् ॥
सुरापोऽसंमतादायी भ्रूणहा गुरुतल्पगः । तपसैव सुतप्तेन नरः पापाद्विमुच्यते ॥
data.md: A person who takes intoxicating liquors, who appropriates others' properties without their consent, one guilty of foeticide, one who violates his preceptor's bed, are all purified by penance duly performed.

data.v: तपसो बहुरूपस्य तैस्तैर्द्वारैः प्रवर्ततः । निवृत्त्या वर्तमानस्य तपो नानशनात्परम् ॥
data.md: Penances manifold. They throw themselves through various channels. Of all sorts of penance, however, that one may practise after abstaining from pleasure and enjoyment, abstention from food is the greatest and best.

data.v: अहिंसा सत्यवचनं दानमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः । एतेभ्यो हि महाराज तपो नानशनात्परम् ॥
data.md: The penance of abstention from food is superior, O king, even to mercy, truthfulness, gifts, and restraint of senses.

data.v: न दुष्करतरं दानान्नातिमातरमाश्रमः । त्रैविद्येभ्यः परं नास्ति संन्यासः परमं तपः ॥
data.md: There is not act more hard to perform than gift. There is no mode of life which is superior to serving one's mother. There is no creature are superior to those who are conversant with the three Vedas. Likewise, Renunciation is the highest penance.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणीह रक्षन्ति धनधान्याभिगुप्तये । तस्मादर्थे च धर्मे च तपो नानशनात्परम् ॥
data.md: People restrain their senses for taking care of their virtue and heaven. There is no penance higher than abstention from food in control over the senses as also in the acquisition of virtue.

data.v: ऋषयः पितरो देवा मनुष्या मृगसत्तमाः । यानि चान्यानि भूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥
तपःपरायणाः सर्वे सिध्यन्ति तपसा च ते । इत्येवं तपसा देवा महत्त्वं चाप्यवाप्नुवन् ॥
इमानीष्टविभागानि फलानि तपसा सदा । तपसा शक्यते प्राप्तुं देवत्वमपि निश्चयात् ॥
data.md: The luminous bodies in the sky have got their position through penance. Forsooth, through penance the very status of godhead may be gained.

data.v: सत्यं धर्मे प्रशंसन्ति विप्रर्षिपितृदेवताः । सत्यमिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Brahmanas, Rishis, Pitris and the gods all speak highly of the duty of truth. I wish to hear of truth. Describe it to me, O grandfather.

data.v: सत्यं किंलक्षणं राजन्कथं वा तदवाप्यते । सत्यं प्राप्य भवेत्किं च कथं चैव तदुच्यते ॥
data.md: What are the marks, O king of truth? How may it be acquired? What is acquired by practising truth, and how? Tell me all this.

data.v: चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य धर्माणां संकरो न प्रशस्यते । अविकारितमं सत्यं सर्ववर्णेषु भारत ॥
data.md: Bhishma said A confusion of the duties of the four castes is never highly spoken of. What is called Truth always exists in a pure and unmixed state in every one of those four castes.

data.v: सत्यं सत्सु सदा धर्मः सत्यं धर्मः सनातनः । सत्यमेव नमस्येत सत्यं हि परमा गतिः ॥
data.md: Truth is always a duty with the good. Indeed, Truth is eternal duty. One should respectfully bow to Truth. Truth is the greatest refuge (of all).

data.v: सत्यं धर्मस्तपो योगः सत्यं ब्रह्म सनातनम् । सत्यं यज्ञः परः प्रोक्तः सत्ये सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
data.md: Truth is duty; Truth is penance; Truth is Yoga; and Truth is the eternal Brahma. Truth has been said to be a great sacrifice. Everything depends upon Truth.

data.v: आचारानिह सत्यस्य यथावदनुपूर्वशः । लक्षणं च प्रवक्ष्यामि सत्यस्येह यथाक्रमम् ॥
data.md: I shall now tell you the forms of Truth one after another, and its characteristic marks also in due order.

data.v: प्राप्यते हि यथा सत्यं तच्च श्रोतुं त्वमर्हसि । सत्यं त्रयोदशविधं सर्वलोकेषु भारत ॥
data.md: You should hear also as to how Truth may be won. Truth, O Bharata, as it exists in all the world, is of thirteen sorts.

data.v: सत्यं च समता चैव दमश्चैव न संशयः । अमात्सर्यं क्षमा चैव ह्रीस्तितिक्षानसूयता ॥
data.md: The various forms of Truth are impartiality, self-control, forgiveness, modesty, endurance, goodness, renunciation, meditation, dignity, fortitute, compassion, and abstention from injury. These, O great king, are the thirteen forms of Truth'.

data.v: त्यागो ध्यानमथार्यत्वं धृतिश्च सततं स्थिरा । अहिंसा चैव राजेन्द्र सत्याकारास्त्रयोदश ॥
data.md: The various forms of Truth are impartiality, self-control, forgiveness, modesty, endurance, goodness, renunciation, meditation, dignity, fortitute, compassion, and abstention from injury. These, O great king, are the thirteen forms of Truth'.

data.v: सत्यं नामाव्ययं नित्यमविकारि तथैव च । सर्वधर्माविरुद्धं च योगेनैतदवाप्यते ॥
data.md: Truth is immutable, eternal, and unchangeable. It may be won through practices which do not oppose any of the other virtues. It may also be won through Yoga.

data.v: आत्मनीष्टे तथानिष्टे रिपौ च समता तथा । इच्छाद्वेषक्षयं प्राप्य कामक्रोधक्षयं तथा ॥
data.md: When desire and hatred, as also lust and anger, are destroyed, that quality by virtue of which one is able to look impartially upon one's own self and one's enemy, upon one's good and one's evil, is called impartiality.

data.v: दमो नान्यस्पृहा नित्यं धैर्यं गाम्भीर्यमेव च । अभयं क्रोधशमनं ज्ञानेनैतदवाप्यते ॥
data.md: Self-control consists in never wishing for another man's property, in gravity and patience and power to remove the fears of others regarding one's own self, and freedom from disease. It may be won through knowledge.

data.v: अमात्सर्यं बुधाः प्राहुर्दानं धर्मे च संयमम् । अवस्थितेन नित्यं च सत्येनामत्सरी भवेत् ॥
data.md: Devoted to liberality and the performance of all duties are considered by the wise as forming good-will. One gains universal good will by continued devotion to Truth.

data.v: अक्षमायाः क्षमायाश्च प्रियाणीहाप्रियाणि च । क्षमते सर्वतः साधुः साध्वाप्नोति च सत्यवान् ॥
data.md: Regarding unforgiveness and forgiveness, it should be said that the quality by which an esteemed and good man puts up with both what is agreeable and disagreeable, is said to be forgiveness. This virtue may be acquired by the practice of truthfulness.

data.v: कल्याणं कुरुते गाढं ह्रीमान्न श्लाघते क्वचित् । प्रशान्तवाङ्मना नित्यं ह्रीस्तु धर्मादवाप्यते ॥
data.md: That virtue by which an intelligent man contended in mind and words performs mnany good deeds and is never blamed by others, is called modesty. It is acquired by the help of righteousness.

data.v: धर्मार्थहेतोः क्षमते तितिक्षा क्षान्तिरुच्यते । लोकसंग्रहणार्थं तु सा तु धैर्येण लभ्यते ॥
data.md: That virtue which forgives for the sake of virtue and religious profit is called endurance. It is one of the form of forgiveness. It is gained through patience, and its object is to attach people to one's self.

data.v: त्यागः स्नेहस्य यस्त्यागो विषयाणां तथैव च । रागद्वेषप्रहीणस्य त्यागो भवति नान्यथा ॥
data.md: The casting off of worldly desires as also of all earthly possessions, is designated renunciation. Renunciation can never be gained except by one who is shorn of anger and malice.

data.v: आर्यता नाम भूतानां यः करोति प्रयत्नतः । शुभं कर्म निराकारो वीतरागत्वमेव च ॥
data.md: That virtue under the influence of which one does good, with diligence and care, to all creatures is designated goodness. It has no particular form and consists in the casting off of all selfish attachments.

data.v: धृतिर्नाम सुखे दुःखे यथा नाप्नोति विक्रियाम् । तां भजेत सदा प्राज्ञो य इच्छेद्भूतिमात्मनः ॥
data.md: That virtue by which remains unchanged in weal and woe is called fortitude. That wise man who seeks his own well-being always practises this virtue.

data.v: सर्वथा क्षमिणा भाव्यं तथा सत्यपरेण च । वीतहर्षभयक्रोधो धृतिमाप्नोति पण्डितः ॥
data.md: One should always practise forgiveness and be devoted to truth. The wise man who can renounce joy, fear and anger, can gain fortitude.

data.v: अद्रोहः सर्वभूतेषु कर्मणा मनसा गिरा । अनुग्रहश्च दानं च सतां धर्मः सनातनः ॥
data.md: Abstention froin injury to all creatures in thought, word, and deed, and kindness, and gift, are the permanent duties of the good. one

data.v: एते त्रयोदशाकाराः पृथक्सत्यैकलक्षणाः । भजन्ते सत्यमेवेह बृंहयन्ति च भारत ॥
data.md: These thirteen qualities, though seemingly different, have but one and the same shape, namely Truth. All these, O Bharata, hold up truth and strengthen it.

data.v: नान्तः शक्यो गुणानां हि वक्तुं सत्यस्य भारत । अतः सत्यं प्रशंसन्ति विप्राः सपितृदेवताः ॥
data.md: It is impossible, o king, to exhaust the merits of Truth. For these reasons the Brahman as, the Pitris and the gods speak highly of truth.

data.v: नास्ति सत्यात्परो धर्मो नानृतात्पातकं परम् । स्थितिर्हि सत्यं धर्मस्य तस्मात्सत्यं न लोपयेत् ॥
data.md: There is no duty which is higher than Truth, and no sin more dreadful than untruth. Indeed, Truth is the very root of righteousness. Therefore one should never destroy Truth.

data.v: उपैति सत्याद्दानं हि तथा यज्ञाः सदक्षिणाः । व्रताग्निहोत्रं वेदाश्च ये चान्ये धर्मनिश्चयाः ॥
data.md: From Truth originate gifts, and sacrifice with presents as well the threefold Agnihotras the Vedas and everything else which leads to righteousness.

data.v: अश्वमेधसहस्रं च सत्यं च तुलया धृतम् । अश्वमेधसहस्राद्धि सत्यमेवातिरिच्यते ॥
data.md: A thousand Horse-sacrifices and Truth were once weighed in the balance. It was seen that Truth weighed heavier than a thousand. Horsesacrifices.

data.v: यतः प्रभवति क्रोधः कामश्च भरतर्षभ । शोकमोहौ विवित्सा च परासुत्वं तथा मदः ॥
लोभो मात्सर्यमीर्ष्या च कुत्सासूया कृपा तथा । एतत्सर्वं महाप्राज्ञ याथातथ्येन मे वद ॥
त्रयोदशैतेऽतिबलाः शत्रवः प्राणिनां स्मृताः । उपासते महाराज समस्ताः पुरुषानिह ॥
data.md: Bhishma said These thirteen vices are known as very powerful enemies of all creatures. These, O king, approach men and tempt them from all sides.

data.v: एते प्रमत्तं पुरुषमप्रमत्ता नुदन्ति हि । वृका इव विलुम्पन्ति दृष्ट्वैव पुरुषेतरान् ॥
data.md: They goad and afflict a careless or a foolish man. Indeed, as soon as they see a person, they attack him powerfully like wolves jumping upon their pray.

data.v: एभ्यः प्रवर्तते दुःखमेभ्यः पापं प्रवर्तते । इति मर्त्यो विजानीयात्सततं भरतर्षभ ॥
data.md: From these originate all sorts of grief. From these originate all sorts of sin. Every man, O foremost of men, should always know this.

data.v: एतेषामुदयं स्थानं क्षयं च पुरुषोत्तम । हन्त ते वर्तयिष्यामि तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
data.md: I shall now describe to you their origin, the objects upon which they rest, and the means of their destruction, O king. Listen, first, О king, with rapt attention, to the origin of anger truly and fully.

data.v: लोभात्क्रोधः प्रभवति परदोषैरुदीर्यते । क्षमया तिष्ठते राजञ्श्रीमांश्च विनिवर्तते ॥
संकल्पाज्जायते कामः सेव्यमानो विवर्धते । अवद्यदर्शनाद्व्येति तत्त्वज्ञानाच्च धीमताम् ॥
विरुद्धानि हि शास्त्राणि पश्यन्तीहाल्पबुद्धयः । विवित्सा जायते तत्र तत्त्वज्ञानान्निवर्तते ॥
data.md: Men, O you of Kuru's race find divergent scriptures. Therefrom originates the desire for various kinds of action. When true knowledge has been acquired, that desire is satisfied.

data.v: प्रीतेः शोकः प्रभवति वियोगात्तस्य देहिनः । यदा निरर्थकं वेत्ति तदा सद्यः प्रणश्यति ॥
data.md: The sorrow of an embodied creature originates from affection which is created by separation. When, however, one learns that the dead do not come back, it disappears.

data.v: परासुता क्रोधलोभादभ्यासाच्च प्रवर्तते । दयया सर्वभूतानां निर्वेदात्सा निवर्तते ॥
data.md: Envy of others originates from between anger and covetousness. It disappears by mercy and knowledge of self. For mercy for all creatures, and for disregard for all worldly objects, it disappears. It also springs from seeing the weakness of other people. But in intelligent men it quickly disappears by virtue of true knowledge.

data.v: सत्त्वत्यागात्तु मात्सर्यमहितानि च सेवते । एतत्तु क्षीयते तात साधूनामुपसेवनात् ॥
data.md: Malice springs from the casting off of truth and indulgence in wickedness. This vice, O child, disappears when one waits upon the wise and good.

data.v: कुलाज्ज्ञानात्तथैश्वर्यान्मदो भवति देहिनाम् । एभिरेव तु विज्ञातैर्मदः सद्यः प्रणश्यति ॥
data.md: Pride, in men, originates from birth, learning and prosperity. When those three, are truly known, that vice immediately disappears.

data.v: ईर्ष्या कामात्प्रभवति संघर्षाच्चैव भारत । इतरेषां तु मर्त्यानां प्रज्ञया सा प्रणश्यति ॥
data.md: Jealousy originates from lust and delight in low and mean people. It is destroyed by wisdom.

data.v: विभ्रमाल्लोकबाह्यानां द्वेष्यैर्वाक्यैरसंगतैः । कुत्सा संजायते राजन्नुपेक्षाभिः प्रशाम्यति ॥
data.md: Slander originates from errors of men's daily conduct and through disagreeable speeches expressing aversion. It disappears, O King, when the whole world is seen.

data.v: प्रतिकर्तुमशक्याय बलस्थायापकारिणे । असूया जायते तीव्रा कारुण्याद्विनिवर्तते ॥
data.md: When the person that injures is powerful and the one injured is unable to avenge the injury, hate appears. It disappears, however, through kindless.

data.v: कृपणान्सततं दृष्ट्वा ततः संजायते कृपा । धर्मनिष्ठां यदा वेत्ति तदा शाम्यति सा कृपा ॥
data.md: Mercy proceeds from seeing the helpless and miserable persons with whom the world abounds. It disappears when one understands the strength of virtue.

data.v: एतान्येव जितान्याहुः प्रशमाच्च त्रयोदश । एते हि धार्तराष्ट्राणां सर्वे दोषास्त्रयोदश । त्वया सर्वात्मना नित्यं विजिता जेष्यसे च तान् ॥
data.md: It has been said that tranquility of soul, can alone conquer all these thirteen faults. All these thirteen faults visited the sons of Dhritarashtra. Yourself, always desirous of truth, have conquered all the those vices of virtue of your respect for your elders,

data.v: आनृशंस्यं विजानामि दर्शनेन सतां सदा । नृशंसान्न विजानामि तेषां कर्म च भारत ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said I know what benevolence is, because I have always marked the conduct of good people. I de not, however, know them who are malevolent, nor the nature of their deeds, O Bharata.

data.v: कण्टकान्कूपमग्निं च वर्जयन्ति यथा नराः । तथा नृशंसकर्माणं वर्जयन्ति नरा नरम् ॥
data.md: Indeed, people always shun malevolent persons of ruthless deeds even as they avoid thorns and pitfalls and fire.

data.v: नृशंसो ह्यधमो नित्यं प्रेत्य चेह च भारत । तस्माद्ब्रवीहि कौरव्य तस्य धर्मविनिश्चयम् ॥
data.md: It is evident, О Bharata, that he who is malevolent is sure to be consumed with misery both in this world and in the next. Therefore, O you of Kuru's race, tell me what, in sooth, the acts of such a person are.

data.v: स्पृहास्यान्तर्हिता चैव विदितार्था च कर्मणा । आक्रोष्टा क्रुश्यते चैव बन्धिता बध्यते च यः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Malevolent persons always commit sinful acts and feel an irresistible inclination for doing them. They speak ill of others and are themselves censured. They always consider themselves as cheated of what is their due.

data.v: दत्तानुकीर्तिर्विषमः क्षुद्रो नैकृतिकः शठः । असंभोगी च मानी च तथा सङ्गी विकत्थनः ॥
data.md: A malevolent person always speaks of his own charitable acts. He sees others with malicious eyes. He is very mean. He is deceitful, and wily. He never pays others their dues. He is haughty. He lives in evil company and is always boastful.

data.v: सर्वातिशङ्की परुषो बालिशः कृपणस्तथा । वर्गप्रशंसी सततमाश्रमद्वेषसंकरी ॥
data.md: He fears and suspects all with whom he mixes. He is foolish in understanding. He is miserly. He praises his companions. He feels excessive aversion and hatred for all hermits who have retired into the forest.

data.v: हिंसाविहारी सततमविशेषगुणागुणः । बह्वलीको मनस्वी च लुब्धोऽत्यर्थं नृशंसकृत् ॥
data.md: He finds pleasure in injuring others. He is perfectly careless in marking the merits and faults of others. He is a liar. He is discontented. He is highly covetous, and always acts cruelly.

data.v: धर्मशीलं गुणोपेतं पाप इत्यवगच्छति । आत्मशीलानुमानेन न विश्वसिति कस्यचित् ॥
data.md: Such a man considers a virtuous and qualified person as a pest, and thinking every one else to be like himself never trusts any one.

data.v: परेषां यत्र दोषः स्यात्तद्गुह्यं संप्रकाशयेत् । समानेष्वेव दोषेषु वृत्त्यर्थमुपघातयेत् ॥
data.md: Such a person trumpets the faults of other people however unsuspected those faults might be. But about similar faults in his ownself, he does not refer to them even remotely, for the sake of the advantage he reaps from them.

data.v: तथोपकारिणं चैव मन्यते वञ्चितं परम् । दत्त्वापि च धनं काले संतपत्युपकारिणे ॥
data.md: He considers the person who does him good as a simpleton whom he has imposed upon. He repents for having at any time made any gift of wealth even to a benefactor.

data.v: भक्ष्यं भोज्यमथो लेह्यं यच्चान्यत्साधु भोजनम् । प्रेक्षमाणेषु योऽश्नीयान्नृशंस इति तं विदुः ॥
data.md: Know him for a malevolent and a wicked person who quietly and alone takes choice foods and drinks even when persons stand by with eager eyes.

data.v: ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रदायाग्रं यः सुहृद्भिः सहाश्नुते । स प्रेत्य लभते स्वर्गमिह चानन्त्यमश्नुते ॥
data.md: He, however, who dedicates the first portion of Brahmanas, and takes the residue, dividing it with friends and kinsmen acquires great felicity in the next world and infinite happiness here.

data.v: एष ते भरतश्रेष्ठ नृशंसः परिकीर्तितः । सदा विवर्जनीयो वै पुरुषेण बुभूषता ॥
data.md: I have now, O foremost of Bharatas, said to you what the marks are of the wicked and malevolent man. Such a person should always be shunned by a wise man.

data.v: कृतार्थो यक्ष्यमाणश्च सर्ववेदान्तगश्च यः । आचार्यपितृभार्यार्थं स्वाध्यायार्थमथापि वा ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Wealth and knowledge, O Bharata, should be given to such pious and impoverished Brahmanas as have been robbed of their wealth (by thieves), as are engaged in the celebration of sacrifices, as are well-read in all the Vedas, and as are desirous of acquiring the merit of righteousness, so that they may satisfy their duties to preceptors and the Pitris, and spend their days in reciting and studying the scriptures.

data.v: एते वै साधवो दृष्टा ब्राह्मणा धर्मभिक्षवः । अस्वेभ्यो देयमेतेभ्यो दानं विद्याविशेषतः ॥
अन्यत्र दक्षिणा या तु देया भरतसत्तम । अन्येभ्यो हि बहिर्वेद्यां नाकृतान्नं विधीयते ॥
data.md: Only the Dakshina, O best of the Bharatas, should be given to those Brahmanas who are not poor. Uncooked food should be given beyond the limits of the sacrificial altar, to those Brahmanas that have fallen away in consequence of their sinful deeds) from their own dignity.

data.v: सर्वरत्नानि राजा च यथार्हं प्रतिपादयेत् । ब्राह्मणाश्चैव यज्ञाश्च सहान्नाः सहदक्षिणाः ॥
यस्य त्रैवार्षिकं भक्तं पर्याप्तं भृत्यवृत्तये । अधिकं वापि विद्येत स सोमं पातुमर्हति ॥
data.md: That Brahmana who has sufficient stores for feeding his family for three or more years, deserves to drink the Soma.

data.v: यज्ञश्चेत्प्रतिविद्धः स्यादङ्गेनैकेन यज्वनः । ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण धार्मिके सति राजनि ॥
यो वैश्यः स्याद्बहुपशुर्हीनक्रतुरसोमपः । कुटुम्बात्तस्य तद्द्रव्यं यज्ञार्थं पार्थिवो हरेत् ॥

data.v: अमानुषीषु गोवर्जमनावृष्टिर्न दुष्यति । अधिष्ठातारमत्तारं पशूनां पुरुषं विदुः ॥

data.md: Nakula said-The bow, O grand-father, known as the foremost of weapons in this world. I, however, prefer the sword, since when the bow, O king, is cut off or broken, when horses are dead or weakened, a good warrior, well-trained in the sword, can protect himself by means of his sword.

data.md: Disregarding all restraints of duty and religion, these and many other Daityas and Danavas sported and found pleasure in all sorts of wicked acts.

data.md: Considering themselves equal in point of birth with the gods, they began to challenge them and the pure sages.

data.md: After the expiration of a thousand years, the powerful lord made arrangements for a grand sacrifice according to the ordinances prescribed in the scriptures.

data.md: The platform was further adorned with Sadasyas who were all high regenerate Rishis. I have heard from the Rishis that something very awful soon took place in that sacrifice.

data.md: When that being appeared, the Earth shook. The Ocean became agitated with mountain billows and dreadful eddies.

data.md: Seeing that dreadful agitation of the universe and that Being originated from the sacrificial fire, the Grandfather said to the great Rishis, the gods, and the Gandharvas.

data.v: मयैतच्चिन्तितं भूतमसिर्नामैष वीर्यवान् । रक्षणार्थाय लोकस्य वधाय च सुरद्विषाम् ॥
data.md: This Being was thought of by me. Highly energetic his name is Asi (sword or scimitar). I have created him for the protection of the world and the destruction of the enemies of the celestials.

data.v: ततस्तद्रूपमुत्सृज्य बभौ निस्त्रिंश एव सः । विमलस्तीक्ष्णधारश्च कालान्तक इवोद्यतः ॥
data.md: Leaving off the form he had first assumed, that being then took the shape of a sword of great effulgence, highly polished, sharp-edged, and sprang like the all-destructive Being at the end of the cycle.

data.v: ततस्तं शितिकण्ठाय रुद्रायर्षभकेतवे । ब्रह्मा ददावसिं दीप्तमधर्मप्रतिवारणम् ॥
data.md: Then Brahman handed over that sharp weapon to the blue-throated Rudra who has for his emblem the foremost of bulls, for empowering him to suppress irreligion and sin.

data.v: ततः स भगवान्रुद्रो ब्रह्मर्षिगणसंस्तुतः । प्रगृह्यासिममेयात्मा रूपमन्यच्चकार ह ॥
data.md: At this, the divine and great Rudra, praised by the great Rishis, took up that sword and assumed a different forin.

data.v: चतुर्बाहुः स्पृशन्मूर्ध्ना भूस्थितोऽपि नभस्तलम् । ऊर्ध्वदृष्टिर्महालिङ्गो मुखाज्ज्वालाः समुत्सृजन् । विकुर्वन्बहुधा वर्णान्नीलपाण्डुरलोहितान् ॥
data.md: Displaying four arms, he became so tall that though he stood on the Earth he touched the very sun with his head. With eyes turned upwards, and with every limb extended wide, he began to eject flames of fire from his mouth.

data.v: बिभ्रत्कृष्णाजिनं वासो हेमप्रवरतारकम् । नेत्रं चैकं ललाटेन भास्करप्रतिमं महत् । शुशुभाते च विमले द्वे नेत्रे कृष्णपिङ्गले ॥
data.md: Assuming various hues such as blue, white and red, and wearing a black deer-skin set with stars of gold, he bore on his forehead a third eye resembling the effulgent sun. His two other eyes, one of which was black and the other twany, shone very brilliantly.

data.v: ततो देवो महादेवः शूलपाणिर्भगाक्षिहा । संप्रगृह्य तु निस्त्रिंशं कालार्कानलसंनिभम् ॥
त्रिकूटं चर्म चोद्यम्य सविद्युतमिवाम्बुदम् । चचार विविधान्मार्गान्महाबलपराक्रमः । विधुन्वन्नसिमाकाशे दानवान्तचिकीर्षया ॥
तस्य नादं विनदतो महाहासं च मुञ्चतः । बभौ प्रतिभयं रूपं तदा रुद्रस्य भारत ॥
data.md: He uttered loud roars and awful was the sound of his laughter. Indeed, O Bharata, then Rudra assumed exceedingly terrible appearance.

data.v: तद्रूपधारिणं रुद्रं रौद्रकर्म चिकीर्षवः । निशम्य दानवाः सर्वे हृष्टाः समभिदुद्रुवुः ॥
data.md: Hearing that Rudra had assumed that form for performing dreadful deeds, the Danavas, filled with joy, began to come towards him quickly, showering huge rocks upon him as they came, and burning brands of wood, and various kinds of terrible weapons made of iron cach sharp as of a razor.

data.v: अश्मभिश्चाप्यवर्षन्त प्रदीप्तैश्च तथोल्मुकैः । घोरैः प्रहरणैश्चान्यैः शितधारैरयोमुखैः ॥
ततस्तद्दानवानीकं संप्रणेतारमच्युतम् । रुद्रखड्गबलोद्धूतं प्रचचाल मुमोह च ॥
चित्रं शीघ्रतरत्वाच्च चरन्तमसिधारिणम् । तमेकमसुराः सर्वे सहस्रमिति मेनिरे ॥
data.md: Although Rudra was alone and singlehanded, yet so quickly did he move about on the field of battle with the sword in his hand that the Asuras thought there were a thousand Rudras fighting with them.

data.v: छिन्दन्भिन्दन्रुजन्कृन्तन्दारयन्प्रमथन्नपि । अचरद्दैत्यसंघेषु रुद्रोऽग्निरिव कक्षगः ॥
data.md: Tearing and piercing and assailing and cutting and lopping off and grinding down, the great god moved about quickly among the large number of his enemies like a forest-fire amid heaps of dry grass spread around.

data.v: असिवेगप्ररुग्णास्ते छिन्नबाहूरुवक्षसः । संप्रकृत्तोत्तमाङ्गाश्च पेतुरुर्व्यां महासुराः ॥
data.md: Assailed by the god with his sword, with arms and thighs and chests cut off and pierced, and with heads cut off, the powerful Asuras began to drop down on the Earth.

data.v: अपरे दानवा भग्ना रुद्रघातावपीडिताः । अन्योन्यमभिनर्दन्तो दिशः संप्रतिपेदिरे ॥
data.md: Stricken with strokes of the sword, other Danavas broke and fled in all directions, cheering up one another as they fled.

data.v: भूमिं केचित्प्रविविशुः पर्वतानपरे तथा । अपरे जग्मुराकाशमपरेऽम्भः समाविशन् ॥
data.md: Some entered into the bowels of the Earth; others got into the caves of mountains. Some went upwards; others entered into the sea.

data.v: तस्मिन्महति संवृत्ते समरे भृशदारुणे । बभौ भूमिः प्रतिभया तदा रुधिरकर्दमा ॥
data.md: During that dreadful and fierce battle, the Earth was covered with flesh and blood, and dreadful spectacles appeared on all sides.

data.v: दानवानां शरीरैश्च महद्भिः शोणितोक्षितैः । समाकीर्णा महाबाहो शैलैरिव सकिंशुकैः ॥
data.md: Covered with the fallen bodies of Danavas bathed in blood, the Earth looked as if overspread with mountain summits filled with Kinshukas.

data.v: रुधिरेण परिक्लिन्ना प्रबभौ वसुधा तदा । रक्तार्द्रवसना श्यामा नारीव मदविह्वला ॥
स रुद्रो दानवान्हत्वा कृत्वा धर्मोत्तरं जगत् । रौद्रं रूपं विहायाशु चक्रे रूपं शिवं शिवः ॥
data.md: Having killed the Danavas and reestablished virtue on Earth, the auspicious Rudra cast off his dreadful form and put on his beneficient shape.

data.v: ततो महर्षयः सर्वे सर्वे देवगणास्तथा । जयेनाद्भुतकल्पेन देवदेवमथार्चयन् ॥
data.md: Then all the Rishis and all the gods adored that god of gods with loud cries of his victory.

data.v: ततः स भगवान्रुद्रो दानवक्षतजोक्षितम् । असिं धर्मस्य गोप्तारं ददौ सत्कृत्य विष्णवे ॥
data.md: After this the divine Rudra gave the sword, that protector of religion, covered with the blood of Danavas, to Vishnu with proper adorations.

data.v: विष्णुर्मरीचये प्रादान्मरीचिर्भगवांश्च तम् । महर्षिभ्यो ददौ खड्गमृषयो वासवाय तु ॥
data.md: Vishnu gave it to Marichi. The divine Marichi gave it to all the great Rishis. the latter gave it to Vasava.

data.v: महेन्द्रो लोकपालेभ्यो लोकपालास्तु पुत्रक । मनवे सूर्यपुत्राय ददुः खड्गं सुविस्तरम् ॥
data.md: Vasava gave it to the Regents of the quarters. The Regents, O son, gave that large sword to Manu the son of the Sun-god.

data.v: ऊचुश्चैनं तथैवाद्यं मानुषाणां त्वमीश्वरः । असिना धर्मगर्भेण पालयस्व प्रजा इति ॥
data.md: At the time of giving it to Manu, they said-You are the lord of all men. Protect all creatures with this sword having religion within its womb.

data.v: धर्मसेतुमतिक्रान्ताः सूक्ष्मस्थूलार्थकारणात् । विभज्य दण्डं रक्ष्याः स्युर्धर्मतो न यदृच्छया ॥
data.md: Properly punishing those who have disregarded the restraints of virtue for the sake of the body or the mind, they should be protected according to the ordinances but never according to caprice.

data.v: दुर्वाचा निग्रहो दण्डो हिरण्यबहुलस्तथा । व्यङ्गनं च शरीरस्य वधो वानल्पकारणात् ॥
data.md: Some should be punished with rebukes, fines and forfeitures. Loss of limb or death should never be inflicted for slight offences.

data.v: असेरेतानि रूपाणि दुर्वाचादीनि निर्दिशेत् । असेरेव प्रमाणानि परिमाणव्यतिक्रमात् ॥
data.md: These punishments, having rebukes as their first, are considered as so many forms of the sword. They are the forms that the sword assumes for the sins of persons under the protection (of the king).

data.v: अधिसृज्याथ पुत्रं स्वं प्रजानामधिपं ततः । मनुः प्रजानां रक्षार्थं क्षुपाय प्रददावसिम् ॥
data.md: In time Manu installed his own son Kshupa as the king of all creatures, and gave him the sword for their protection.

data.v: क्षुपाज्जग्राह चेक्ष्वाकुरिक्ष्वाकोश्च पुरूरवाः । आयुश्च तस्माल्लेभे तं नहुषश्च ततो भुवि ॥
data.md: Kshupa gave it to Ikshaku, and Ikshaku to Pururavas. Pururavas gave it to Ayus, and Ayus to Nahusha.

data.v: ययातिर्नहुषाच्चापि पूरुस्तस्माच्च लब्धवान् । आमूर्तरयसस्तस्मात्ततो भूमिशयो नृपः ॥
data.md: Nahusha gave it to Yayati, and Yayati to Puru. Puru gave it to Amurttaraya. From Amurttaraya it went to the royal Bhumishaya.

data.v: भरतश्चापि दौःषन्तिर्लेभे भूमिशयादसिम् । तस्माच्च लेभे धर्मज्ञो राजन्नैडबिडस्तथा ॥
data.md: Bhumishaya gave it to Dhushmanta's son Bharata. Bharata, O king, gave it to the righteous Ailavila.

data.v: ततश्चैडबिडाल्लेभे धुन्धुमारो जनेश्वरः । धुन्धुमाराच्च काम्बोजो मुचुकुन्दस्ततोऽलभत् ॥
data.md: Ailavila gave it to king Dhundumara. Dhundumara gave it to Kamvoja, and Kamvoja to Muchukunda.

data.v: मुचुकुन्दान्मरुत्तश्च मरुत्तादपि रैवतः । रैवताद्युवनाश्वश्च युवनाश्वात्ततो रघुः ॥
data.md: Muchukunda gave it to Marutta, and Marutta to Raivata. Raivata gave it to Yuvanashva, and Yuvanashva to Raghu.

data.v: इक्ष्वाकुवंशजस्तस्माद्धरिणाश्वः प्रतापवान् । हरिणाश्वादसिं लेभे शुनकः शुनकादपि ॥
data.md: Raghu gave it to the valiant Harinashva. Harinashva gave the sword to Sunaka, and Sunaka to the righteous-souled Ushinara. From the last it was taken by the Bhojas and the Yadavas.

data.v: उशीनरो वै धर्मात्मा तस्माद्भोजाः सयादवाः । यदुभ्यश्च शिबिर्लेभे शिबेश्चापि प्रतर्दनः ॥
प्रतर्दनादष्टकश्च रुशदश्वोऽष्टकादपि । रुशदश्वाद्भरद्वाजो द्रोणस्तस्मात्कृपस्ततः । ततस्त्वं भ्रातृभिः सार्धं परमासिमवाप्तवान् ॥
data.md: Prishadashva gave it to Bharadwaja, and Bharadwaja to Drona. Drona gave it to Kripa. Kripa gave that best of swords to you and your brothers.

data.v: कृत्तिकाश्चास्य नक्षत्रमसेरग्निश्च दैवतम् । रोहिण्यो गोत्रमस्याथ रुद्रश्च गुरुरुत्तमः ॥
data.md: The constellation under which the sword was born in Kritika. Agni is its god, and Rohini is its Gotra. Rudra is its great preceptor.

data.v: असेरष्टौ च नामानि रहस्यानि निबोध मे । पाण्डवेय सदा यानि कीर्तयँल्लभते जयम् ॥
data.md: The sword has eight names which are not generally known. Hear as I name them to you. If one mentions these names, O son of Pandu, one may always acquire victory.

data.v: असिर्विशसनः खड्गस्तीक्ष्णवर्त्मा दुरासदः । श्रीगर्भो विजयश्चैव धर्मपालस्तथैव च ॥
data.md: Those names then are Asi, Vaishasana, Khadga, Sharp-edged, hard of acquisition, Shrigarbha, victory and protector of virtue.

data.v: अग्र्यः प्रहरणानां च खड्गो माद्रवतीसुत । महेश्वरप्रणीतश्च पुराणे निश्चयं गतः ॥
data.md: Of all weapons, O son of Madravati, the sword is the greatest. The Puranas truly say that it was first held by Mahadeva.

data.v: पृथुस्तूत्पादयामास धनुराद्यमरिंदम । तेनेयं पृथिवी पूर्वं वैन्येन परिरक्षिता ॥
data.md: Regarding the bow, again, O chastiser of enemies, it was Prithu who first created it. It was with the help of this weapon that that son of Vena, while he ruled the Earth virtuously for many years, milked her profusely of crops and grain.

data.v: तदेतदार्षं माद्रेय प्रमाणं कर्तुमर्हसि । असेश्च पूजा कर्तव्या सदा युद्धविशारदैः ॥
data.md: You should, O son of Madri, consider what the Rishis have said as sufficient proof. All persons skilled in battle should adore the sword.

data.v: इत्येष प्रथमः कल्पो व्याख्यातस्ते सुविस्तरः । असेरुत्पत्तिसंसर्गो यथावद्भरतर्षभ ॥
data.md: I have now told you truly the first portion of your question fully, about the origin and creation of the sword, O foremost of Bharata's family.

data.v: सर्वथैतदिह श्रुत्वा खड्गसाधनमुत्तमम् । लभते पुरुषः कीर्तिं प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते ॥
data.md: By hearing of this excellent story of the origin of the sword, a man acquires fame in this world and eternal happiness in the next.'

data.v: इत्युक्तवति भीष्मे तु तूष्णींभूते युधिष्ठिरः । पप्रच्छावसरं गत्वा भ्रातॄन्विदुरपञ्चमान् ॥
data.md: Vaishampayana said When after having said this, Bhishma became silent, Yudhishthira (and the others) returned home. Addressing his brothers with Vidura forming the fifth, the king said,-'The course of the world depends upon Virtue, Profit and Desire. Amongst these three, which is the foremost, which the second, and which the last, in importance.

data.v: धर्मे चार्थे च कामे च लोकवृत्तिः समाहिता । तेषां गरीयान्कतमो मध्यमः को लघुश्च कः ॥
कस्मिंश्चात्मा नियन्तव्यस्त्रिवर्गविजयाय वै । संतुष्टा नैष्ठिकं वाक्यं यथावद्वक्तुमर्हथ ॥
data.md: For suppressing the three vices, viz., lust, anger and covetousness), upon which of the first three (viz., Virtue, Profit and Desire) should the mind be fixed? You should all cheerfully answer this question in true words.

data.v: ततोऽर्थगतितत्त्वज्ञः प्रथमं प्रतिभानवान् । जगाद विदुरो वाक्यं धर्मशास्त्रमनुस्मरन् ॥
data.md: Thus addressed by the Kuru chief, Vidura, who was conversant with the science of Profit, with the course of the world and with the real nature of thing, and endued with great intellect, spoke first these words, remembering the contents of the scriptures.

data.v: बाहुश्रुत्यं तपस्त्यागः श्रद्धा यज्ञक्रिया क्षमा । भावशुद्धिर्दया सत्यं संयमश्चात्मसंपदः ॥
data.md: Vidura said Study of the various scriptures, asceticism, gift, faith, celebration of sacrifices, forgiveness, sincerity of purpose, mercy, truth, self-control,-these form the possessions of Virtue.

data.v: एतदेवाभिपद्यस्व मा ते भूच्चलितं मनः । एतन्मूलौ हि धर्मार्थावेतदेकपदं हितम् ॥
data.md: Do you adopt Virtue. Let not your heart go away from it. Both virtue and worldly profit originate from these. I think that all these may be signified by one term.

data.v: धर्मेणैवर्षयस्तीर्णा धर्मे लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः । धर्मेण देवा दिविगा धर्मे चार्थः समाहितः ॥
data.md: It is by virtue that the Rishis have crossed the world. All the worlds depend upon virtue. It is by virtue that the gods acquired their superior position. Upon Virtue, Profit or Wealth depends.

data.v: धर्मो राजन्गुणश्रेष्ठो मध्यमो ह्यर्थ उच्यते । कामो यवीयानिति च प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः । तस्माद्धर्मप्रधानेन भवितव्यं यतात्मना ॥
data.md: Virtue, O king, is foremost of all. Profit is said to be middling. Desire it is said by the wise, is the lowest of the three.

data.v: समाप्तवचने तस्मिन्नर्थशास्त्रविशारदः । पार्थो वाक्यार्थतत्त्वज्ञो जगौ वाक्यमतन्द्रितः ॥
data.md: After Vidura had finished his say, Pritha's son Arjuna, well-skilled in the science of Profit, and conversant also with the truths of both Virtue and Profit, urged urged on (by Yudhishthira's question), said.

data.v: कर्मभूमिरियं राजन्निह वार्त्ता प्रशस्यते । कृषिवाणिज्यगोरक्ष्यं शिल्पानि विविधानि च ॥
अर्थ इत्येव सर्वेषां कर्मणामव्यतिक्रमः । न ऋतेऽर्थेन वर्तेते धर्मकामाविति श्रुतिः ॥
data.md: Arjuna said This world O king, is the field of work. Action, therefore, is spoken highly of here. Agriculture, trade, tending of cattle, and various kinds of arts, form what is called profit. Profit, again, is the end of all such acts. Without profit or wealth, both virtue and desire cannot be acquired. This is the injunction of the Shruti.

data.v: विजयी ह्यर्थवान्धर्ममाराधयितुमुत्तमम् । कामं च चरितुं शक्तो दुष्प्रापमकृतात्मभिः ॥
data.md: Even persons of impure souls, if possessed of various sorts of wealth, can perform the highest acts of virtue and gratify desires that cannot be easily satisfied.

data.v: अर्थस्यावयवावेतौ धर्मकामाविति श्रुतिः । अर्थसिद्ध्या हि निर्वृत्तावुभावेतौ भविष्यतः ॥
data.md: Virtue and Desire are the limbs of Wealth as the Shruti says. With the acquisition of Wealth, both Virtue and the objects of desire may be acquired.

data.v: उद्भूतार्थं हि पुरुषं विशिष्टतरयोनयः । ब्रह्माणमिव भूतानि सततं पर्युपासते ॥
data.md: Like all creatures adoring Brahman, even persons of superior birth adore man possessed of Wealth.

data.v: जटाजिनधरा दान्ताः पङ्कदिग्धा जितेन्द्रियाः । मुण्डा निस्तन्तवश्चापि वसन्त्यर्थार्थिनः पृथक् ॥
data.md: Even they who are clad in deerskins and bear matted locks on their heads, who are selfcontrolled, who smear their bodies with mire, who have their senses under complete control, even they who have bald heads and that are devoted Brahmacharins, and ad who live separated from one another, cherish a desire for Wealth.

data.v: काषायवसनाश्चान्ये श्मश्रुला ह्रीसुसंवृताः । विद्वांसश्चैव शान्ताश्च मुक्ताः सर्वपरिग्रहैः ॥
अर्थार्थिनः सन्ति केचिदपरे स्वर्गकाङ्क्षिणः । कुलप्रत्यागमाश्चैके स्वं स्वं मार्गमनुष्ठिताः ॥
data.md: Other clad in yellow robes, bearing long beards endued with modesty, and learning, contented, and freed from all attachments seek Wealth. Others, following the conduct of their ancestors, and observing their respective duties, and others desirous of heaven, do the same.

data.v: आस्तिका नास्तिकाश्चैव नियताः संयमे परे । अप्रज्ञानं तमोभूतं प्रज्ञानं तु प्रकाशता ॥
data.md: Believers and unbelievers, and those who practise the highest Yoga all speak of the excellence of Wealth.

data.v: भृत्यान्भोगैर्द्विषो दण्डैर्यो योजयति सोऽर्थवान् । एतन्मतिमतां श्रेष्ठ मतं मम यथातथम् । अनयोस्तु निबोध त्वं वचनं वाक्यकण्ठयोः ॥
data.md: He, indeed, is said to be truly possessed of Wealth who pleases his dependants with objects of enjoyment, and punishes his enemies. This, O foremost of intelligent men, is my opinion. Hear now Nakula and Sahadeva, who are about to speak.

data.v: ततो धर्मार्थकुशलौ माद्रीपुत्रावनन्तरम् । नकुलः सहदेवश्च वाक्यं जगदतुः परम् ॥
data.md: After Arjuna had ceased, the two sons of Madri, viz., Nakula and Sahadeva, said these words of high import.

data.v: आसीनश्च शयानश्च विचरन्नपि च स्थितः । अर्थयोगं दृढं कुर्याद्योगैरुच्चावचैरपि ॥
data.md: Sitting or lying, walking or standing, one should try to acquire Wealth even by the most difficult means.

data.v: अस्मिंस्तु वै सुसंवृत्ते दुर्लभे परमप्रिये । इह कामानवाप्नोति प्रत्यक्षं नात्र संशयः ॥
data.md: If Wealth, which is difficult of acquisition and highly agreeable, be acquired, the person who has acquired it, forsooth, is seen to earn all the objects of Desire.

data.v: योऽर्थो धर्मेण संयुक्तो धर्मो यश्चार्थसंयुतः । मध्विवामृतसंयुक्तं तस्मादेतौ मताविह ॥
data.md: That Wealth which is connected with Virtue, as also that Virtue which is connected with Wealth, is certainly like ambrosia. For this reason we hold these opinions.

data.v: अनर्थस्य न कामोऽस्ति तथार्थोऽधर्मिणः कुतः । तस्मादुद्विजते लोको धर्मार्थाद्यो बहिष्कृतः ॥
data.md: A person without wealth cannot satisfy any desire; likewise, there can be no Wealth in one who is destitute of virtue. He, therefore, who has no virtue, or wealth, is feared by the world.

data.v: तस्माद्धर्मप्रधानेन साध्योऽर्थः संयतात्मना । विश्वस्तेषु च भूतेषु कल्पते सर्व एव हि ॥
data.md: One should, therefore, try to acquire Wealth with a devoted mind, without neglecting the requirements of Virtue. They who have faith in this injunction succeed in gaining whatever they desire.

data.v: धर्मं समाचरेत्पूर्वं तथार्थं धर्मसंयुतम् । ततः कामं चरेत्पश्चात्सिद्धार्थस्य हि तत्फलम् ॥
data.md: One should first practise Virtue; next amass Wealth without sacrificing virtue; and then seek the gratification of Desire; for this should be the last act of one who has successfully acquired Wealth.

data.v: विरेमतुस्तु तद्वाक्यमुक्त्वा तावश्विनोः सुतौ । भीमसेनस्तदा वाक्यमिदं वक्तुं प्रचक्रमे ॥
data.md: Vaishampayana continued After having said these words, the twin son of the Ashvins remained silent. Then Bhimasena began to say.

data.v: नाकामः कामयत्यर्थं नाकामो धर्ममिच्छति । नाकामः कामयानोऽस्ति तस्मात्कामो विशिष्यते ॥
data.md: Bhimasena said One without Desire never seeks Wealth. One without Desire never seeks Virtue. One who is destitute of Desire has no wish. Desire, therefore, is the foremost of all the three.

data.v: कामेन युक्ता ऋषयस्तपस्येव समाहिताः । पलाशफलमूलाशा वायुभक्षाः सुसंयताः ॥
data.md: It is under the influence of Desire that the very Rishis practise penances, living upon fruits, or living upon roots or air only.

data.v: वेदोपवादेष्वपरे युक्ताः स्वाध्यायपारगाः । श्राद्धयज्ञक्रियायां च तथा दानप्रतिग्रहे ॥
data.md: Others endued with Vedic learning always read the Vedas and their auxiliaries or perform rites of faith and sacrificial acts, or make gifts or accept them.

data.v: वणिजः कर्षका गोपाः कारवः शिल्पिनस्तथा । दैवकर्मकृतश्चैव युक्ताः कामेन कर्मसु ॥
data.md: Traders, agriculturists, cattle-keepers, artists and artisans, and those who are engaged in rites of propitiation, all act from Desire.

data.v: समुद्रं चाविशन्त्यन्ये नराः कामेन संयुताः । कामो हि विविधाकारः सर्वं कामेन संततम् ॥
data.md: There are some who go into the depths of the ocean, actuated by Desire. Desire, indeed, assumes various forms. Everything is permeated by the principle of Desire.

data.v: नास्ति नासीन्नाभविष्यद्भूतं कामात्मकात्परम् । एतत्सारं महाराज धर्मार्थावत्र संश्रितौ ॥
data.md: A man who has no Desire never is, was, or will be, seen in this world. This, O king, is the truth. Both Virtue and Wealth depend upon Desire.

data.v: नवनीतं यथा दध्नस्तथा कामोऽर्थधर्मतः । श्रेयस्तैलं च पिण्याकाद्घृतं श्रेय उदश्वितः ॥
data.md: As butter is the essence of curds, so is Desire the essence of Profit and Virtue. Oil is better than oil-seeds. Clarified butter is better than sour milk.

data.v: श्रेयः पुष्पफलं काष्ठात्कामो धर्मार्थयोर्वरः । पुष्पतो मध्विव रसः कामात्संजायते सुखम् ॥
data.md: Flowers and fruits are better than wood. Likewise, Desire is better than Virtue and Profit. As honey is extracted from flowers, so is desire from these two. Desire is the father of Virtue and profit. Desire is the soul of these two.

data.v: सुचारुवेषाभिरलंकृताभि;र्मदोत्कटाभिः प्रियवादिनीभिः । रमस्व योषाभिरुपेत्य कामं; कामो हि राजंस्तरसाभिपाती ॥
data.md: Approaching beautiful women clad in excellent robes, decorated with ornaments and up with sweet wines, do you sport with them. Desire, O king, is the foremost of the three with us.

data.v: बुद्धिर्ममैषा परिषत्स्थितस्य; मा भूद्विचारस्तव धर्मपुत्र । स्यात्संहितं सद्भिरफल्गुसारं; समेत्य वाक्यं परमानृशंस्यम् ॥
data.md: Thinking upon the question to its very roots, I have arrived at this conclusion. Do not hesitate to accept this conclusion, O son of Dharma! These words of mine are not shallow. Fair as they are, they will be acceptable to all good men.

data.v: धर्मार्थकामाः सममेव सेव्या; यस्त्वेकसेवी स नरो जघन्यः । द्वयोस्तु दक्षं प्रवदन्ति मध्यं; स उत्तमो यो निरतस्त्रिवर्गे ॥
data.md: Virtue, Profit, and Desire should all be equally pursued. That man who follows only one of them is certainly not a superior person. He is middling who follows only two of them. He, on the other hand, is the best who follows all the three.

data.v: प्राज्ञः सुहृच्चन्दनसारलिप्तो; विचित्रमाल्याभरणैरुपेतः । ततो वचः संग्रहविग्रहेण; प्रोक्त्वा यवीयान्विरराम भीमः ॥
data.md: Having said these words both briefly and fully, to those heroes, Bhima endued with wisdom, surrounded by friends smeared with sandal-paste, and decorated with beautiful garlands and ornaments, remained silent.

data.v: ततो मुहूर्तादथ धर्मराजो; वाक्यानि तेषामनुचिन्त्य सम्यक् । उवाच वाचावितथं स्मयन्वै; बहुश्रुतो धर्मभृतां वरिष्ठः ॥
data.md: Then the just king Yudhishthira, that foremost of virtuous men, endued with great of you learning, thinking only for some time upon the words spoken by all of them, and thinking all those speeches to be false philosophy himself spoken as follows:

data.v: निःसंशयं निश्चितधर्मशास्त्राः; सर्वे भवन्तो विदितप्रमाणाः । विज्ञातुकामस्य ममेह वाक्य;मुक्तं यद्वै नैष्ठिकं तच्छ्रुतं मे । इह त्ववश्यं गदतो ममापि; वाक्यं निबोधध्वमनन्यभावाः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Forsooth, all have settled conclusions regarding the scriptures, and all of you know well the authorities. I have heard these words.

data.v: यो वै न पापे निरतो न पुण्ये; नार्थे न धर्मे मनुजो न कामे । विमुक्तदोषः समलोष्टकाञ्चनः; स मुच्यते दुःखसुखार्थसिद्धेः ॥
data.md: Listen now, with rapt attention, to what I say to you. He who is not employed in virtue or in sin, he who does not attend to Profit, or Virtue, or Desire, who is above all shortcomings, who regards gold and a clod of Earth with equal eyes, becomes freed from pleasure and pain and the necessity of accomplishing his purposes.

data.v: भूतानि जातीमरणान्वितानि; जराविकारैश्च समन्वितानि । भूयश्च तैस्तैः प्रतिबोधितानि; मोक्षं प्रशंसन्ति न तं च विद्मः ॥
data.md: All creatures are subject to birth and death. All are liable to decay and change. Risen to their senses by the various benefits and evils of life, all of them speak highly of liberation. We do not know, however, what liberation is.

data.v: स्नेहे नबद्धस्य न सन्ति तानी;त्येवं स्वयंभूर्भगवानुवाच । बुधाश्च निर्वाणपरा वदन्ति; तस्मान्न कुर्यात्प्रियमप्रियं च ॥
data.md: The Self-sprung and divine Brahman has said that there is no liberation for him who is fettered with ties of attachment and love. The learned, however, seek Extinction. Therefore, one should never regard anything as either pleasant or unpleasant.

data.v: एतत्प्रधानं न तु कामकारो; यथा नियुक्तोऽस्मि तथा चरामि । भूतानि सर्वाणि विधिर्नियुङ्क्ते; विधिर्बलीयानिति वित्त सर्वे ॥
data.md: This view seems to be the best. Not one in this world can act as he likes. I act precisely as I am made to do. The great Creator makes all creatures move as He wills. The Creator is Supreme. Know this, all of you.

data.v: न कर्मणाप्नोत्यनवाप्यमर्थं; यद्भावि सर्वं भवतीति वित्त । त्रिवर्गहीनोऽपि हि विन्दतेऽर्थं; तस्मादिदं लोकहिताय गुह्यम् ॥
data.md: No one can, by his deed, acquire what is unobtainable. That which is to be, occurs. Know this. And since one who has withdrawn himself from the three-fold objects may acquire liberation, it seems, therefore, that liberation yields the highest good,

data.v: ततस्तदग्र्यं वचनं मनोनुगं; समस्तमाज्ञाय ततोऽतिहेतुमत् । तदा प्रणेदुश्च जहर्षिरे च ते; कुरुप्रवीराय च चक्रुरञ्जलीन् ॥
data.md: Having heard all these most significant reasonable and pleasant words, Bhima and others were filled with joy and joining their hands, bowed to that prince of Kuru's race.

data.v: सुचारुवर्णाक्षरशब्दभूषितां; मनोनुगां निर्धुतवाक्यकण्टकाम् । निशम्य तां पार्थिव पार्थभाषितां; गिरं नरेन्द्राः प्रशशंसुरेव ते । पुनश्च पप्रच्छ सरिद्वरासुतं; ततः परं धर्ममहीनसत्त्वः ॥
data.md: O king, having heard those sweet words of the king, acceptable to the heart, and divested of dissonant sounds and words, indeed, those foremost of men began to speak highly of Yudhishthira.

data.v: पितामह महाप्राज्ञ कुरूणां कीर्तिवर्धन । प्रश्नं कंचित्प्रवक्ष्यामि तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: O grandfather, you of great wisdom, I shall ask you a question. You should, O enhancer of the joy of the Kurus, to describe it fully to me.

data.v: कीदृशा मानवाः सौम्याः कैः प्रीतिः परमा भवेत् । आयत्यां च तदात्वे च के क्षमास्तान्वदस्व मे ॥
data.md: What kind of man are gentle by nature? With whom may the best friendship exists? Tell us also who are able to do good now and in the future.

data.v: न हि तत्र धनं स्फीतं न च संबन्धिबान्धवाः । तिष्ठन्ति यत्र सुहृदस्तिष्ठन्तीति मतिर्मम ॥
data.md: I think that neither increasing wealth, nor relatives, nor kinsmen occupy that place which well-meaning friends do.

data.v: दुर्लभो हि सुहृच्छ्रोता दुर्लभश्च हितः सुहृत् । एतद्धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ सर्वं व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: A friend capable of hearing beneficial advice, and also of doing good, is highly rare! You should foremost of virtuous men, describe fully those subjects.

data.v: संधेयान्पुरुषान्राजन्नसंधेयांश्च तत्त्वतः । वदतो मे निबोध त्वं निखिलेन युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Hear, O Yudhishthira, as I speak to you fully of those men with whom friendships may be contracted and those with whom friendships should not be made.

data.v: लुब्धः क्रूरस्त्यक्तधर्मा निकृतः शठ एव च । क्षुद्रः पापसमाचारः सर्वशङ्की तथालसः ॥
दीर्घसूत्रोऽनृजुः कष्टो गुरुदारप्रधर्षकः । व्यसने यः परित्यागी दुरात्मा निरपत्रपः ॥
सर्वतः पापदर्शी च नास्तिको वेदनिन्दकः । संप्रकीर्णेन्द्रियो लोके यः कामनिरतश्चरेत् ॥
असत्यो लोकविद्विष्टः समये चानवस्थितः । पिशुनोऽथाकृतप्रज्ञो मत्सरी पापनिश्चयः ॥
दुःशीलोऽथाकृतात्मा च नृशंसः कितवस्तथा । मित्रैरर्थकृती नित्यमिच्छत्यर्थपरश्च यः ॥
वहतश्च यथाशक्ति यो न तुष्यति मन्दधीः । अमित्रमिव यो भुङ्क्ते सदा मित्रं नरर्षभ ॥
अस्थानक्रोधनो यश्च अकस्माच्च विरज्यते । सुहृदश्चैव कल्याणानाशु त्यजति किल्बिषी ॥
अल्पेऽप्यपकृते मूढस्तथाज्ञानात्कृतेऽपि च । कार्योपसेवी मित्रेषु मित्रद्वेषी नराधिप ॥
शत्रुर्मित्रमुखो यश्च जिह्मप्रेक्षी विलोभनः । न रज्यति च कल्याणे यस्त्यजेत्तादृशं नरम् ॥
पानपो द्वेषणः क्रूरो निर्घृणः परुषस्तथा । परोपतापी मित्रध्रुक्तथा प्राणिवधे रतः ॥
data.md: One who drinks wine, one who hates others, one who is angry, one who is merciless, one who feels pain on seeing other's happiness, one who injures friends, one who always kills living creatures, one who is ungrateful, one who is vile, should be shunned. Friendship should never be contracted with any of them. Likewise, no friendship should be made with him who is always busy with seeing the faults of others. Listen now to me as I mention the persons, with whom friendship may be contracted.

data.v: कृतघ्नश्चाधमो लोके न संधेयः कथंचन । छिद्रान्वेषी न संधेयः संधेयानपि मे शृणु ॥
data.md: One who drinks wine, one who hates others, one who is angry, one who is merciless, one who feels pain on seeing other's happiness, one who injures friends, one who always kills living creatures, one who is ungrateful, one who is vile, should be shunned. Friendship should never be contracted with any of them. Likewise, no friendship should be made with him who is always busy with seeing the faults of others. Listen now to me as I mention the persons, with whom friendship may be contracted.

data.v: कुलीना वाक्यसंपन्ना ज्ञानविज्ञानकोविदाः । मित्रज्ञाश्च कृतज्ञाश्च सर्वज्ञाः शोकवर्जिताः ॥
माधुर्यगुणसंपन्नाः सत्यसंधा जितेन्द्रियाः । व्यायामशीलाः सततं भृतपुत्राः कुलोद्गताः ॥
रूपवन्तो गुणोपेतास्तथालुब्धा जितश्रमाः । दोषैर्वियुक्ताः प्रथितैस्ते ग्राह्याः पार्थिवेन ह ॥
यथाशक्तिसमाचाराः सन्तस्तुष्यन्ति हि प्रभो । नास्थाने क्रोधवन्तश्च न चाकस्माद्विरागिणः ॥
विरक्ताश्च न रुष्यन्ति मनसाप्यर्थकोविदाः । आत्मानं पीडयित्वापि सुहृत्कार्यपरायणाः । न विरज्यन्ति मित्रेभ्यो वासो रक्तमिवाविकम् ॥
दोषांश्च लोभमोहादीनर्थेषु युवतिष्वथ । न दर्शयन्ति सुहृदां विश्वस्ता बन्धुवत्सलाः ॥
लोष्टकाञ्चनतुल्यार्थाः सुहृत्स्वशठबुद्धयः । ये चरन्त्यनभीमाना निसृष्टार्थविभूषणाः । संगृह्णन्तः परिजनं स्वाम्यर्थपरमाः सदा ॥
ईदृशैः पुरुषश्रेष्ठैः संधिं यः कुरुते नृपः । तस्य विस्तीर्यते राष्ट्रं ज्योत्स्ना ग्रहपतेरिव ॥
शास्त्रनित्या जितक्रोधा बलवन्तो रणप्रियाः । क्षान्ताः शीलगुणोपेताः संधेयाः पुरुषोत्तमाः ॥
data.md: Friendship should be formed with men who are well-practised in weapons, who have completely subjugated their anger, who are always strong in battle and are highly born, and are of good behaviour, and varied accomplishments.

data.v: ये च दोषसमायुक्ता नराः प्रोक्ता मयानघ । तेषामप्यधमो राजन्कृतघ्नो मित्रघातकः । त्यक्तव्यः स दुराचारः सर्वेषामिति निश्चयः ॥
data.md: Amongst the vicious men, O sinless one, that I have mentioned, the vilest, o king, are those who are ungrateful and who injure friends. Those wicked persons should be shunned by all. This, indeed, is a settled injunction.'

data.v: विस्तरेणार्थसंबन्धं श्रोतुमिच्छामि पार्थिव । मित्रद्रोही कृतघ्नश्च यः प्रोक्तस्तं च मे वद ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said I wish to hear fully this description. Tell me who they are who injure friends and ungrateful persons.

data.v: हन्त ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम् । उदीच्यां दिशि यद्वृत्तं म्लेच्छेषु मनुजाधिप ॥
data.md: I shall recite to you an old story the incidents of which took place in the country, O king, of the Mlecchas that lies to the north.

data.v: ब्राह्मणो मध्यदेशीयः कृष्णाङ्गो ब्रह्मवर्जितः । ग्रामं प्रेक्ष्य जनाकीर्णं प्राविशद्भैक्षकाङ्क्षया ॥
data.md: There was a certain Brahmana of the middle country. He had no Vedic learning. (One day), seeing a prosperous village, the man entered it from desire of getting alms.

data.v: तत्र दस्युर्धनयुतः सर्ववर्णविशेषवित् । ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यसंधश्च दाने च निरतोऽभवत् ॥
data.md: In that village lived a very rich robber conversant with the characteristics of all the castes, devoted to the Brahmanas, firm in truth, and always engaged in making gifts.

data.v: तस्य क्षयमुपागम्य ततो भिक्षामयाचत । प्रतिश्रयं च वासार्थं भिक्षां चैवाथ वार्षिकीम् ॥
data.md: Going to the house of that robber, the Brahmana begged for alms. Indeed, he prayed for a house to live in and the necessaries of life lasting for a year.

data.v: प्रादात्तस्मै स विप्राय वस्त्रं च सदृशं नवम् । नारीं चापि वयोपेतां भर्त्रा विरहितां तदा ॥
data.md: Thus begged by the Brahmana, the robber gave him a piece of new cloth with its ends complete, and a young widow.

data.v: एतत्संप्राप्य हृष्टात्मा दस्योः सर्वं द्विजस्तदा । तस्मिन्गृहवरे राजंस्तया रेमे स गौतमः ॥
data.md: Getting all those things from the robber, the Brahmana become filled with joy. Gautama began to live happily in that big house given to him by the robber.

data.v: कुटुम्बार्थेषु दस्योः स साहाय्यं चाप्यथाकरोत् । तत्रावसत्सोऽथ वर्षाः समृद्धे शबरालये । बाणवेध्ये परं यत्नमकरोच्चैव गौतमः ॥
data.md: He began to help the relatives and kinsmen of the female slave the robber-chief gave him. Thus he lived for many years in that prosperous village of hunters.

data.v: वक्राङ्गांस्तु स नित्यं वै सर्वतो बाणगोचरे । जघान गौतमो राजन्यथा दस्युगणस्तथा ॥
हिंसापरो घृणाहीनः सदा प्राणिवधे रतः । गौतमः संनिकर्षेण दस्युभिः समतामियात् ॥
तथा तु वसतस्तस्य दस्युग्रामे सुखं तदा । अगच्छन्बहवो मासा निघ्नतः पक्षिणो बहून् ॥
data.md: Living happily in that robber village for many months, he killed a number of wild cranes.

data.v: ततः कदाचिदपरो द्विजस्तं देशमागमत् । जटी चीराजिनधरः स्वाध्यायपरमः शुचिः ॥
data.md: One day another Brahmana came to that village. He was clad in rags and deer-skins and bore matted locks on his head. Of highly pure conduct, he was devoted to the study of the Vedas.

data.v: विनीतो नियताहारो ब्रह्मण्यो वेदपारगः । सब्रह्मचारी तद्देश्यः सखा तस्यैव सुप्रियम् । तं दस्युग्राममगमद्यत्रासौ गौतमोऽभवत् ॥
data.md: Of a humble disposition, of restricted diet, devoted to the Brahmanas, well-read in ihe Vedas, and observant of Brahmacharya vows, that Brahmana had been a dear friend of Gautama and belonged to that part of the country from which Gautama had come.

data.v: स तु विप्रगृहान्वेषी शूद्रान्नपरिवर्जकः । ग्रामे दस्युजनाकीर्णे व्यचरत्सर्वतोदिशम् ॥
ततः स गौतमगृहं प्रविवेश द्विजोत्तमः । गौतमश्चापि संप्राप्तस्तावन्योन्येन संगतौ ॥
वक्राङ्गभारहस्तं तं धनुष्पाणिं कृतागसम् । रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गं गृहद्वारमुपागतम् ॥
तं दृष्ट्वा पुरुषादाभमपध्वस्तं क्षयागतम् । अभिज्ञाय द्विजो व्रीडामगमद्वाक्यमाह च ॥
data.md: Seeing that man who looked like a cannibal and who had fallen away from the pure practices of his caste, and entering his house, the newly-arrived guest, recognising him, O king, said these words

data.v: किमिदं कुरुषे मौढ्याद्विप्रस्त्वं हि कुलोद्गतः । मध्यदेशपरिज्ञातो दस्युभावं गतः कथम् ॥
पूर्वान्स्मर द्विजाग्र्यांस्तान्प्रख्यातान्वेदपारगान् । येषां वंशेऽभिजातस्त्वमीदृशः कुलपांसनः ॥
अवबुध्यात्मनात्मानं सत्यं शीलं श्रुतं दमम् । अनुक्रोशं च संस्मृत्य त्यज वासमिमं द्विज ॥
data.md: Recollect, O twice-born one, your famous kinsmen of former times, all of whom were well-read in the Vedas. Born in their family, alas, you have sullied it.

data.v: एवमुक्तः स सुहृदा तदा तेन हितैषिणा । प्रत्युवाच ततो राजन्विनिश्चित्य तदार्तवत् ॥
data.md: Awake yourself by your own exertions. Remembering the power, the conduct, the learning, the self-control, the mercy (which belong to your caste), leave this your present house, O twice-born one.

data.v: अधनोऽस्मि द्विजश्रेष्ठ न च वेदविदप्यहम् । वृत्त्यर्थमिह संप्राप्तं विद्धि मां द्विजसत्तम ॥
data.md: Thus spoken to by that well-meaning friend of his, O king, Gautama answered him in great distress of heart, saying,-O foremost of twiceborn ones, I am poor. I have no knowledge of the Vedas. Know, O best of Brahmanas, that I have taken up my quarters here for the sake of money only.

data.v: त्वद्दर्शनात्तु विप्रर्षे कृतार्थं वेद्म्यहं द्विज । आत्मानं सह यास्यावः श्वो वसाद्येह शर्वरीम् ॥
