data.md: There is no resort of cither Intelligence or Soul. The understanding creates the mind, but never the qualities.

data.v: रश्मींस्तेषां स मनसा यदा सम्यङ्नियच्छति । तदा प्रकाशतेऽस्यात्मा घटे दीपो ज्वलन्निव ॥
data.md: When the Soul, by means of the mind, sufficiently controls the rays that proved from the senses, it is then that it becomes visible (10 the Understanding) like a lamp burning within a cover.

data.v: त्यक्त्वा यः प्राकृतं कर्म नित्यमात्मरतिर्मुनिः । सर्वभूतात्मभूतः स्यात्स गच्छेत्परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: That person who renounces all ordinary acts, practises penances, devotes himself to Study the Soul, taking a delight in it, and regards himself as the Soul of all creatures, acquires a supreme end.

data.v: यथा वारिचरः पक्षी लिप्यमानो न लिप्यते । एवमेव कृतप्रज्ञो भूतेषु परिवर्तते ॥
data.md: As an aquatic bird while moving over the waters, is never welted, so does a wise person move among creatures.

data.v: एवंस्वभावमेवैतत्स्वबुद्ध्या विहरेन्नरः । अशोचन्नप्रहृष्यंश्च चरेद्विगतमत्सरः ॥
data.md: One should act in the world, by the help of his intelligence, in this way, without grief, without joy, without distinction of personality, for all, and shorn of malice and envy,

data.v: स्वभावसिद्ध्या संसिद्धान्स नित्यं सृजते गुणान् । ऊर्णनाभिर्यथा स्रष्टा विज्ञेयास्तन्तुवद्गुणाः ॥
data.md: One living in this way creates the qualities (i.e. transcends them), like a spider creating threads. The qualities should indeed, be considered as the threads of the spider.

data.v: प्रध्वस्ता न निवर्तन्ते निवृत्तिर्नोपलभ्यते । प्रत्यक्षेण परोक्षं तदनुमानेन सिध्यति ॥
data.md: Some say that the qualities of such men are not lost. Some say that they are all lost. Those who say that they are not lost rely upon the Shrutis, which do not contain any declaration to the contrary. They, however, who say, that the qualities are all lost rely on the Smritis. One should taking into consideration both these opinions, judge as to which of them is right.

data.v: एवमेके व्यवस्यन्ति निवृत्तिरिति चापरे । उभयं संप्रधार्यैतदध्यवस्येद्यथामति ॥
इतीमं हृदयग्रन्थिं बुद्धिभेदमयं दृढम् । विमुच्य सुखमासीत न शोचेच्छिन्नसंशयः ॥
data.md: One should thus solve the knotty question which is capable of shaking the understanding by doubt, and thereby acquire happiness. When that doubt will be removed, one will no longer : have to grieve.

data.v: मलिनाः प्राप्नुयुः शुद्धिं यथा पूर्णां नदीं नराः । अवगाह्य सुविद्वंसो विद्धि ज्ञानमिदं तथा ॥
data.md: Men of impure hearts may by knowledge acquire success like persons plunging in a full river purifying themselves of all dirts.

data.v: महानदीं हि पारज्ञस्तप्यते न तरन्यथा । एवं ये विदुरध्यात्मं कैवल्यं ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥
एतां बुद्ध्वा नरः सर्वां भूतानामागतिं गतिम् । अवेक्ष्य च शनैर्बुद्ध्या लभते शं परं ततः ॥
data.md: Man, by understanding with the help of his intelligence, the manner in which creatures come and leave the world, is sure to attain by and by to steadfast peace.

data.v: त्रिवर्गो यस्य विदितः प्राग्ज्योतिः स विमुच्यते । अन्विष्य मनसा युक्तस्तत्त्वदर्शी निरुत्सुकः ॥
data.md: The Soul cannot be seen unless the senses, which are set on various objects and are difficult of being controlled, be all duly restrained.

data.v: न चात्मा शक्यते द्रष्टुमिन्द्रियेषु विभागशः । तत्र तत्र विसृष्टेषु दुर्जयेष्वकृतात्मभिः ॥
data.md: He who knows this, is really wise. What other mark is there of a wise man? Acquiring this knowledge, intelligent men considered themselves to be crowned with success.

data.v: एतद्बुद्ध्वा भवेद्बुद्धः किमन्यद्बुद्धलक्षणम् । विज्ञाय तद्धि मन्यन्ते कृतकृत्या मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: That which strikes the Ignorant with fear can never create fear in persons of Knowledge. There is no higher and for anybody than Liberation. The sages say that on account of the excess or otherwise of good qualities, differences are seen regarding the degree of Liberation.

data.v: न भवति विदुषां ततो भयं; यदविदुषां सुमहद्भयं भवेत् । न हि गतिरधिकास्ति कस्यचि;त्सति हि गुणे प्रवदन्त्यतुल्यताम् ॥
data.md: A person succeeds, by acting without expecting fruits, (by those acts) in destroying his pristine sinful acts. To a wise man, the acts of a former life and those of this life also, do not yield any disagreeable result. But how can acts, if he continues to be engaged in them, bring about what is agreeable (viz., Liberation.)

data.v: यत्करोत्यनभिसंधिपूर्वकं; तच्च निर्णुदति यत्पुरा कृतम् । नाप्रियं तदुभयं कुतः प्रियं; तस्य तज्जनयतीह कुर्वतः ॥
data.md: People blame a person who is possessed of lust, envy, and other evil passions). Those vices draw the person down in his next life into various sorts of inferior births.

data.v: लोक आतुरजनान्विराविण;स्तत्तदेव बहु पश्य शोचतः । तत्र पश्य कुशलानशोचतो; ये विदुस्तदुभयं पदं सदा ॥
data.md: Mark attentively the vicious in this world who grieve exceedingly for the loss of their possessions. See also those who are gifted with judgement and who never grieve when placed in similar circumstances! Those who are conversant with both, deserve to be called truly wise..

data.v: हन्त वक्ष्यामि ते पार्थ ध्यानयोगं चतुर्विधम् । यं ज्ञात्वा शाश्वतीं सिद्धिं गच्छन्ति परमर्षयः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said 'I shall not, O son of Pritha, describe to you for four kinds of Yoga meditation. Obtaining a knowledge of the same, the great Rishis, attain to eternal success even in this world. Pleased with knowledge, with hearts engaged in Liberation, and conversant with Yoga, great Rishis, act in such a way that their Yoga meditation may get on properly.

data.v: यथा स्वनुष्ठितं ध्यानं तथा कुर्वन्ति योगिनः । महर्षयो ज्ञानतृप्ता निर्वाणगतमानसाः ॥
नावर्तन्ते पुनः पार्थ मुक्ताः संसारदोषतः । जन्मदोषपरिक्षीणाः स्वभावे पर्यवस्थिताः ॥
data.md: O son of Pritha, being freed from the faults of the world, these are not born again. Freed from liability to re-birth, they live in their state of original purity.

data.v: निर्द्वंद्वा नित्यसत्त्वस्था विमुक्ता नित्यमाश्रिताः । असङ्गीन्यविवादीनि मनःशान्तिकराणि च ॥
data.md: Freed from the influence of all pairs of opposite (such as heat and cold, joy and sorrow, etc.), ever existing in their own (pure) state, freed (from attachments), never accepting anything (in gift), they live in places separated from their wives and children, without others with whom disputes may arise, and favourable to perfect tranquillity of hearts.

data.v: तत्र स्वाध्यायसंश्लिष्टमेकाग्रं धारयेन्मनः । पिण्डीकृत्येन्द्रियग्राममासीनः काष्ठवन्मुनिः ॥
data.md: There restraining speech, such a person sits like a piece of wood, killing all the senses, and with mind immersed in the Supreme Self by the help of meditation.

data.v: शब्दं न विन्देच्छ्रोत्रेण स्पर्शं त्वचा न वेदयेत् । रूपं न चक्षुषा विद्याज्जिह्वया न रसांस्तथा ॥
data.md: He has no perception of sound through the car; no perception of touch through the skin no perception of from through the eye; no perception of taste through the tongue.

data.v: घ्रेयाण्यपि च सर्वाणि जह्याद्ध्यानेन योगवित् । पञ्चवर्गप्रमाथीनि नेच्छेच्चैतानि वीर्यवान् ॥
data.md: He has no perception also of scents through the organ of smell. He would, immersed in Yoga and meditation, renounce all things.

data.v: ततो मनसि संसज्य पञ्चवर्गं विचक्षणः । समादध्यान्मनो भ्रान्तमिन्द्रियैः सह पञ्चभिः ॥
data.md: Possessed of great energy of mind, he has no desire for anything that works up the five senses. The wise man, then should, withdrawing his five senses into the mind, fix the unstable mind with the five senses (into the Intellect).

data.v: विसंचारि निरालम्बं पञ्चद्वारं चलाचलम् । पूर्वे ध्यानपथे धीरः समादध्यान्मनोऽन्तरम् ॥
data.md: The Yogin should possessed of patience, fix his mind which always wanders, so that his five gates may be made firm regarding things that are themselves unstable. He should, in this sky of the heart, fix his mind into the path of meditation, making it independent of the body or any other refuge.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणि मनश्चैव यदा पिण्डीकरोत्ययम् । एष ध्यानपथः पूर्वो मया समनुवर्णितः ॥
data.md: I have spoken of the path of meditation as the first, since the Yogin has first to destroy his senses and the mind.

data.v: तस्य तत्पूर्वसंरुद्धं मनःषष्ठमनन्तरम् । स्फुरिष्यति समुद्भ्रान्तं विद्युदम्बुधरे यथा ॥
data.md: The mind, which constitutes the sixth, when thus controlled, tries of flash out like the capricious and fickle lightning playing among the clouds.

data.v: जलबिन्दुर्यथा लोलः पर्णस्थः सर्वतश्चलः । एवमेवास्य तच्चित्तं भवति ध्यानवर्त्मनि ॥
data.md: As a drop of water on a leaf in unstable and moves about on all sides, so becomes the Yogin's mind when first fix on the path of meditation.

data.v: समाहितं क्षणं किंचिद्ध्यानवर्त्मनि तिष्ठति । पुनर्वायुपथं भ्रान्तं मनो भवति वायुवत् ॥
data.md: When fixed, for some time the inind stays in that path. When, however, it goes astray again into the path of the wind, it becomes as fleet as the wind.

data.v: अनिर्वेदो गतक्लेशो गततन्द्रीरमत्सरः । समादध्यात्पुनश्चेतो ध्यानेन ध्यानयोगवित् ॥
data.md: The person who has mastered the science of Yoga,-without losing his heart by this, never regarding the loss of the toil undergone, shaking off idleness and malice,-should, again, direct his mind to meditation.

data.v: विचारश्च वितर्कश्च विवेकश्चोपजायते । मुनेः समादधानस्य प्रथमं ध्यानमादितः ॥
data.md: When one observing the vow of silence, begins to set his mind of Yoga, then discrimination, knowledge, and power to avoid cvil follow him in the trail.

data.v: मनसा क्लिश्यमानस्तु समाधानं च कारयेत् । न निर्वेदं मुनिर्गच्छेत्कुर्यादेवात्मनो हितम् ॥
data.md: He should, though disturbed by the fickleness of his mind, fix it in meditation. The Yogin should never despair, but seek own his well-being.

data.v: पांसुभस्मकरीषाणां यथा वै राशयश्चिताः । सहसा वारिणा सिक्ता न यान्ति परिभावनाम् ॥
किंचित्स्निग्धं यथा च स्याच्छुष्कचूर्णमभावितम् । क्रमशस्तु शनैर्गच्छेत्सर्वं तत्परिभावनम् ॥
एवमेवेन्द्रियग्रामं शनैः संपरिभावयेत् । संहरेत्क्रमशश्चैव स सम्यक्प्रशमिष्यति ॥
स्वयमेव मनश्चैव पञ्चवर्गश्च भारत । पूर्वं ध्यानपथं प्राप्य नित्ययोगेन शाम्यति ॥
data.md: One succeeds, O Bharata, by directing one's mind and to the path of senses meditation, in controlling them perfectly by steadfast Yoga.

data.v: न तत्पुरुषकारेण न च दैवेन केनचित् । सुखमेष्यति तत्तस्य यदेवं संयतात्मनः ॥
data.md: The happiness that he fells who has succeeded in controlling his mind and senses is such that its like can never be experienced through exertion or Destiny.

data.v: सुखेन तेन संयुक्तो रंस्यते ध्यानकर्मणि । गच्छन्ति योगिनो ह्येवं निर्वाणं तन्निरामयम् ॥
data.md: Enjoying such felicity, be continues to find pleasure in the act of meditation. Yogins attain, in this way, to the highly blessed state of Nirvana.'

data.v: चातुराश्रम्यमुक्तं ते राजधर्मास्तथैव च । नानाश्रयाश्च बहव इतिहासाः पृथग्विधाः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said You have described the four modes of life and their duties. You have also spoken of the duties of kings. You have recounted many histories of various kinds and on various subjects.

data.v: श्रुतास्त्वत्तः कथाश्चैव धर्मयुक्ता महामते । संदेहोऽस्ति तु कश्चिन्मे तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
data.md: I have also heard from you, O you of great intelligence, many discourses about morality. I have, however, one doubt. You should remove it.

data.v: जापकानां फलावाप्तिं श्रोतुमिच्छामि भारत । किं फलं जपतामुक्तं क्व वा तिष्ठन्ति जापकाः ॥
data.md: I wish, O Bharata, to hear of the fruits which silent Reciters of sacred Mantras acquire. what are the fruits that have been shorn for such men? What is that region to which they repair after death?

data.v: जपस्य च विधिं कृत्स्नं वक्तुमर्हसि मेऽनघ । जापका इति किं चैतत्सांख्ययोगक्रियाविधिः ॥
data.md: You should, also, O sinless one, tell me all the rules that have been laid down regarding such silent recitation? When the word Reciter is uttered, what shall I understand by it? Is such a man to be considered as following the ordinances of Vedanta or Yoga or Work.

data.v: किं यज्ञविधिरेवैष किमेतज्जप्यमुच्यते । एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व सर्वज्ञो ह्यसि मे मतः ॥
data.md: Or, it such a man to be considered as following the ordinances of (mental) sacrifices? How is the path of the Reciters to be called? You posses universal knowledge. Tell me all this.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । यमस्य यत्पुरा वृत्तं कालस्य ब्राह्मणस्य च ॥
data.md: Bhishma said 'Regarding it is cited the old history of Yama, Time and a certain Brahmana.

data.v: संन्यास एव वेदान्ते वर्तते जपनं प्रति । वेदवादाभिनिर्वृत्ता शान्तिर्ब्रह्मण्यवस्थितौ । मार्गौ तावप्युभावेतौ संश्रितौ न च संश्रितौ ॥
यथा संश्रूयते राजन्कारणं चात्र वक्ष्यते । मनःसमाधिरत्रापि तथेन्द्रियजयः स्मृतः ॥
सत्यमग्निपरीचारो विविक्तानां च सेवनम् । ध्यानं तपो दमः क्षान्तिरनसूया मिताशनम् ॥
विषयप्रतिसंहारो मितजल्पस्तथा शमः । एष प्रवृत्तको धर्मो निवृत्तकमथो शृणु ॥
यथा निवर्तते कर्म जपतो ब्रह्मचारिणः । एतत्सर्वमशेषेण यथोक्तं परिवर्जयेत् । त्रिविधं मार्गमासाद्य व्यक्ताव्यक्तमनाश्रयम् ॥
data.md: Follow the path of abstention, he should try to do away with his dependence on both the External and the Internal.

data.v: कुशोच्चयनिषण्णः सन्कुशहस्तः कुशैः शिखी । चीरैः परिवृतस्तस्मिन्मध्ये छन्नः कुशैस्तथा ॥
data.md: Sitting on Kusha grass, with Kusha in hand, and binding his hairs with Kusha, he should surround himself with Kusha and have Kusha for robes.

data.v: विषयेभ्यो नमस्कुर्याद्विषयान्न च भावयेत् । साम्यमुत्पाद्य मनसो मनस्येव मनो दधत् ॥
data.md: He should, bowing to all earthly matters, take leave of them and never think of them. He should, acquiring equanimity of, mind, fix his mind on the mind itself.

data.v: तद्धिया ध्यायति ब्रह्म जपन्वै संहितां हिताम् । संन्यस्यत्यथ वा तां वै समाधौ पर्यवस्थितः ॥
data.md: He should, reciting the highly beneficial verse (viz., the Gayatri), meditate with the help of his intellect on Brahma alone. Afterwards he should even leave off that, being then absolutely immersed in contemplation.

data.v: ध्यानमुत्पादयत्यत्र संहिताबलसंश्रयात् । शुद्धात्मा तपसा दान्तो निवृत्तद्वेषकामवान् ॥
data.md: His dependence on the Gayatri which he recites, will give him this concentered contemplation. He attains by penances to purity of soul, and self-control, and cessation of hatred and desire.

data.v: अरागमोहो निर्द्वंद्वो न शोचति न सज्जते । न कर्ताकरणीयानां न कार्याणामिति स्थितिः ॥
data.md: Freed from attachment and delusion, being above the influence of all pairs of opposites, he ever grieves and never suffers himself to be attracted towards worldly objects. He does not consider himself as the actor nor as the enjoyer of sufferer of the fruits of his acts.

data.v: न चाहंकारयोगेन मनः प्रस्थापयेत्क्वचित् । न चात्मग्रहणे युक्तो नावमानी न चाक्रियः ॥
data.md: He never, out of selfishness, fixes his mind on anything. Without being engaged in the acquisition of wealth, he abstains also from disregarding or insulting others, but not from work.

data.v: ध्यानक्रियापरो युक्तो ध्यानवान्ध्याननिश्चयः । ध्याने समाधिमुत्पाद्य तदपि त्यजति क्रमात् ॥
data.md: The work in which he is engaged is that of meditation; he is devoted to meditation, and seeks meditation. By meditation he acquires concentered contemplation, and then gradually leaves off meditation itself.

data.v: स वै तस्यामवस्थायां सर्वत्यागकृतः सुखी । निरीहस्त्यजति प्राणान्ब्राह्मीं संश्रयते तनुम् ॥
data.md: He enjoys, in that state, the happiness which follows Renunciation. Having thoroughly controlled his desires, he casts off his life-breaths and merges into the Brahmic body.

data.v: अथ वा नेच्छते तत्र ब्रह्मकायनिषेवणम् । उत्क्रामति च मार्गस्थो नैव क्वचन जायते ॥
data.md: Or, if he does not desire to merge into the Brahmic body, he at once goes upwards into the region of Brahma and is never born again.

data.v: आत्मबुद्धिं समास्थाय शान्तीभूतो निरामयः । अमृतं विरजःशुद्धमात्मानं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Having become tranquillity's self, and being freed from all sorts of calamity, such a person, by depending upon his own intelligence, attains to that Soul which is pure and immortal and which is without a stain.'

data.v: गतीनामुत्तमा प्राप्तिः कथिता जापकेष्विह । एकैवैषा गतिस्तेषामुत यान्त्यपरामपि ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said You have described the very high end to which the Reciters attain. I beg to enquire whether this is their only end or there any other to which they attain.

data.v: शृणुष्वावहितो राजञ्जापकानां गतिं विभो । यथा गच्छन्ति निरयमनेकं पुरुषर्षभ ॥
data.md: Bhishma said-Listen with rapt attention, O powerful king, to the end that silent Reciters attain, and to the various kinds of hell into which they sink, O foremost of men.

data.v: यथोक्तमेतत्पूर्वं यो नानुतिष्ठति जापकः । एकदेशक्रियश्चात्र निरयं स निगच्छति ॥
data.md: That Reciter who does not. at first act according to the rules which have been laid down, and who cannot complete the ritual or course of discipline laid down, has to go to hell.

data.v: अवज्ञानेन कुरुते न तुष्यति न शोचति । ईदृशो जापको याति निरयं नात्र संशयः ॥
data.md: That Reciter who work without faith, who is not contented with his work, and who takes no pleasure in it, forsooth, goes to hell.

data.v: अहंकारकृतश्चैव सर्वे निरयगामिनः । परावमानी पुरुषो भविता निरयोपगः ॥
data.md: They who follow the ritual with pride in their hearts, all go to hell. That Reciter who insults and disregards others has to go to hell.

data.v: अभिध्यापूर्वकं जप्यं कुरुते यश्च मोहितः । यत्राभिध्यां स कुरुते तं वै निरयमृच्छति ॥
data.md: That man who makes silent recitation under the influence of stupefaction and from desire of fruit, acquires all those things which he seeks at heart.

data.v: अथैश्वर्यप्रवृत्तः सञ्जापकस्तत्र रज्यते । स एव निरयस्तस्य नासौ तस्मात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
data.md: That Reciter who seeks at heart the supreme power of Yoga, has to go to hell and never becomes freed from it.

data.v: रागेण जापको जप्यं कुरुते तत्र मोहितः । यत्रास्य रागः पतति तत्र तत्रोपजायते ॥
data.md: That Reciter who makes recitation under the influence of attachments, obtain those objects which he seeks for.

data.v: दुर्बुद्धिरकृतप्रज्ञश्चले मनसि तिष्ठति । चलामेव गतिं याति निरयं वाधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: That Reciter of wicked understanding and uncleaned soul who engages in work with an unstable mind, obtains an unstable end or goes into hell.

data.v: अकृतप्रज्ञको बालो मोहं गच्छति जापकः । स मोहान्निरयं याति तत्र गत्वानुशोचति ॥
data.md: The Reciter who is not gifted with wisdom and who is foolish, becomes stupefied or deluded; and for such delusion has to go to hell where he is obliged to grieve.

data.v: दृढग्राही करोमीति जप्यं जपति जापकः । न संपूर्णो न वा युक्तो निरयं सोऽधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: If a person even of fixed heart, determining in to complete the discipline, makes, recitation, but fails to come to the end, for his having freed himself from attachments by a violent stretch without genuine conviction of their worthlessness of harmful character, he also has to go to hell.

data.v: अनिमित्तं परं यत्तदव्यक्तं ब्रह्मणि स्थितम् । सद्भूतो जापकः कस्मात्स शरीरमथाविशेत् ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said When the Reciter attains to the essence of that which exists in its own nature, which is Supreme, which is beyond description and comprehension, and which dwells in the syllable. OM forming the subject of both recitation and meditation, why is it that they have a gain to take birth in embodied forms?

data.v: दुष्प्रज्ञानेन निरया बहवः समुदाहृताः । प्रशस्तं जापकत्वं च दोषाश्चैते तदात्मकाः ॥
data.md: Reciters, for want of true knowledge and wisdom, go to various descriptions of hell. The discipline followed by Reciters is surely very superior. These, however, that I have spoken o! are their weak points.

data.v: कीदृशो जापको याति निरयं वर्णयस्व मे । कौतूहलं हि मे जातं तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Tell me what sort of hell is obtained by a Reciter? I am curious, O king, to know this. You should describe this subject to me.'

data.v: धर्मस्यांशः प्रसूतोऽसि धर्मिष्ठोऽसि स्वभावतः । धर्ममूलाश्रयं वाक्यं शृणुष्वावहितोऽनघ ॥
data.md: Bhishma said “You have originated from a portion of the good of righteousness. You are by nature observant of righteousness. Listen, O sinless one, with undivided attention, to these words having righteousness for their root.

data.v: अमूनि यानि स्थानानि देवानां परमात्मनाम् । नानासंस्थानवर्णानि नानारूपफलानि च ॥
दिव्यानि कामचारीणि विमानानि सभास्तथा । आक्रीडा विविधा राजन्पद्मिन्यश्चामलोदकाः ॥
चतुर्णां लोकपालानां शुक्रस्याथ बृहस्पतेः । मरुतां विश्वदेवानां साध्यानामश्विनोरपि ॥
रुद्रादित्यवसूनां च तथान्येषां दिवौकसाम् । एते वै निरयास्तात स्थानस्य परमात्मनः ॥
अभयं चानिमित्तं च न च क्लेशभयावृतम् । द्वाभ्यां मुक्तं त्रिभिर्मुक्तमष्टाभिस्त्रिभिरेव च ॥
data.md: The region last spoken of it shorn of fear, increate, without pain of any sort, without any agreeable or disagreeable element, beyond the reach of the three qualities, freed from the eight things (viz., the five primal elements, the senses, the mind, and the intellect), without the three (distinctions between the knower, the known, and act knowing); freed also from the four attributes (seeing, hearing, thinking, and knowing), without the fourfold causes (of knowledge) without joy and delight ard sorrow and disease.

data.v: चतुर्लक्षणवर्जं तु चतुष्कारणवर्जितम् । अप्रहर्षमनानन्दमशोकं विगतक्लमम् ॥
कालः संपच्यते तत्र न कालस्तत्र वै प्रभुः । स कालस्य प्रभू राजन्स्वर्गस्यापि तथेश्वरः ॥
data.md: Time makes it appearance there for usc. Time is not the ruler there. That supreme region is the ruler of Time as also of Heaven.

data.v: आत्मकेवलतां प्राप्तस्तत्र गत्वा न शोचति । ईदृशं परमं स्थानं निरयास्ते च तादृशाः ॥
data.md: That Reciter who becomes identified with his Soul (by withdrawing everything into it) goes there. He has, after this, never to experience any sorrow. This region is called Supreme. The other regions are hell.

data.v: एते ते निरयाः प्रोक्ताः सर्व एव यथातथम् । तस्य स्थानवरस्येह सर्वे निरयसंज्ञिताः ॥
data.md: I have not told you of all those regions that are called hell. Indeed, as compared with that foremost of regions all the others are called hell.'

data.v: कालमृत्युयमानां च ब्राह्मणस्य च सत्तम । विवादो व्याहृतः पूर्वं तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said You had mentioned the dispute between Time, Mrityu, Yama, Ikshvaku, and a Brahmana. You should describe the story in full.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । इक्ष्वाकोः सूर्यपुत्रस्य यद्वृत्तं ब्राह्मणस्य च ॥
data.md: Bhishma said 'Regarding it is cited the old history of Yama, Time and a certain Brahmana.

data.v: कालस्य मृत्योश्च तथा यद्वृत्तं तन्निबोध मे । यथा स तेषां संवादो यस्मिन्स्थानेऽपि चाभवत् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding this subject that I am describing, is cited the old story of what too place between Surya's son Ikshvaku and a certain Brahmana, and Tiine and Mrityu. Listen to me as to what happened, and what was the conversation that took place between them and the place where it happened.

data.v: ब्राह्मणो जापकः कश्चिद्धर्मवृत्तो महायशाः । षडङ्गविन्महाप्राज्ञः पैप्पलादिः स कौशिकः ॥
data.md: There was a certain the highly famous and pious Brahınana. He was a Reciter. Greatly wise, he was conversant with the six branches (of the Vedas). He was of the Kushika race and son of Pippalada.

data.v: तस्यापरोक्षं विज्ञानं षडङ्गेषु तथैव च । वेदेषु चैव निष्णातो हिमवत्पादसंश्रयः ॥
data.md: He acquired (by his austerities) spiritual insight into the various branches of the Vedas. Residing at the foot of Himavat, he was devoted to the Vedas,

data.v: सोऽन्त्यं ब्राह्मं तपस्तेपे संहितां संयतो जपन् । तस्य वर्षसहस्रं तु नियमेन तथा गतम् ॥
data.md: He practised, silently reciting the Gayatri, severe austerities for attaining to Brahma. A thousand years passed away while he was engaged in the observance of vows and fasts.

data.v: स देव्या दर्शितः साक्षात्प्रीतास्मीति तदा किल । जप्यमावर्तयंस्तूष्णीं न च तां किंचिदब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: The goddess (of Gayatri or Savitri) appeared before him and said,-I am pleased with you.-Continuing to recite the sacred Mantra, the Brahmana remained silent and spoke not a word to the goddess.

data.v: तस्यानुकम्पया देवी प्रीता समभवत्तदा । वेदमाता ततस्तस्य तज्जप्यं समपूजयत् ॥
data.md: The goddess felt mercy for him and became highly pleased. Then the mother of the Vedas spoke highly of that recitation in which the Brahmana had been engaged.

data.v: समाप्तजप्यस्तूत्थाय शिरसा पादयोस्तथा । पपात देव्या धर्मात्मा वचनं चेदमब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: After finishing his recitation the Brahmana stood up and, lowering his head, laid himself down before the goddess's feet. The pious Reciter, addressing the goddess, said,-By good luck, O goddess, you have been pleased with me and shown yourself to me. If, indeed, you are pleased with me, the boon I ask is that my heart may find pleasure in the act of recitation.

data.v: दिष्ट्या देवि प्रसन्ना त्वं दर्शनं चागता मम । यदि वापि प्रसन्नासि जप्ये मे रमतां मनः ॥
data.md: After finishing his recitation the Brahmana stood up and, lowering his head, laid himself down before the goddess's feet. The pious Reciter, addressing the goddess, said,-By good luck, O goddess, you have been pleased with me and shown yourself to me. If, indeed, you are pleased with me, the boon I ask is that my heart may find pleasure in the act of recitation.

data.v: किं प्रार्थयसि विप्रर्षे किं चेष्टं करवाणि ते । प्रब्रूहि जपतां श्रेष्ठ सर्वं तत्ते भविष्यति ॥
data.md: What do you ask, O twice-born Rishi? What wish of yours shall I make good? Tell me, O foremost of Reciters, everything will be as you wish.

data.v: इत्युक्तः स तदा देव्या विप्रः प्रोवाच धर्मवित् । जप्यं प्रति ममेच्छेयं वर्धत्विति पुनः पुनः ॥
data.md: Thus addressed by the goddess, the Brahmana, conversant with duties, replied, saying,-Let me wish about continuing my recitation s go on increasing every day.

data.v: मनसश्च समाधिर्मे वर्धेताहरहः शुभे । तत्तथेति ततो देवी मधुरं प्रत्यभाषत ॥
data.md: Let also, O auspicious goddess, my Samadhi be more complete!-The goddess sweetly said,-Let it be as you wish.

data.v: इदं चैवापरं प्राह देवी तत्प्रियकाम्यया । निरयं नैव यातासि यत्र याता द्विजर्षभाः ॥
data.md: Desiring to do good to the Brahmana, the goddess once again said to him-You shall not have to go to hell, i.e., there where great Brahmanas go.

data.v: यास्यसि ब्रह्मणः स्थानमनिमित्तमनिन्दितम् । साधये भविता चैतद्यत्त्वयाहमिहार्थिता ॥
data.md: You shall go to the region of Brahma which is incrcate and free from every fault. I go hence, but that which you have asked me shall take place.

data.v: नियतो जप चैकाग्रो धर्मस्त्वां समुपैष्यति । कालो मृत्युर्यमश्चैव समायास्यन्ति तेऽन्तिकम् । भविता च विवादोऽत्र तव तेषां च धर्मतः ॥
data.md: Go on reciting with controlled soul and rapt attention. The god Dharma will in person come lo you. Time, Mrityu, and Yama also will come to you. There will be a dispute of morality.'

data.v: एवमुक्त्वा भगवती जगाम भवनं स्वकम् । ब्राह्मणोऽपि जपन्नास्ते दिव्यं वर्षशतं तदा ॥
data.md: The goddess, having said these words returned to her own house. The Brahimana continued in recitation for a thousand divine years. Restraining anger, and always controlling self, he passed his time firmly devoting himself to truth and shorn of malice.

data.v: समाप्ते नियमे तस्मिन्नथ विप्रस्य धीमतः । साक्षात्प्रीतस्तदा धर्मो दर्शयामास तं द्विजम् ॥
data.md: Upon the completion of the observance by the intelligent Brahmana, Dharma, pleased with him, appeared before that twice-born one.

data.v: द्विजाते पश्य मां धर्ममहं त्वां द्रष्टुमागतः । जप्यस्य च फलं यत्ते संप्राप्तं तच्च मे शृणु ॥
data.md: Dharma said O twice-born one, see me who am Dharma. I have come here for seeing you. You have acquired the meed of this recitation in which you had been engaged. Listen to me as to what that rewards is.

data.v: जिता लोकास्त्वया सर्वे ये दिव्या ये च मानुषाः । देवानां निरयान्साधो सर्वानुत्क्रम्य यास्यसि ॥
data.md: You have acquired all the regions of felicity which belong to either gods or men. O good man, you shall ascend above all the abodes of the gods.

data.v: प्राणत्यागं कुरु मुने गच्छ लोकान्यथेप्सितान् । त्यक्त्वात्मनः शरीरं च ततो लोकानवाप्स्यसि ॥
data.md: O ascetic, cast off your vital breaths then, and to go whatever regions you please. By casting off your body you will acquire many regions of felicity.

data.v: कृतं लोकैर्हि मे धर्म गच्छ च त्वं यथासुखम् । बहुदुःखसुखं देहं नोत्सृजेयमहं विभो ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said What have I to do which those regions of felicity of which you speak. O Dharma, go wherever you like. I will not, O powerful lord, cast off this body which is subject to much happiness and misery.

data.v: अवश्यं भोः शरीरं ते त्यक्तव्यं मुनिपुंगव । स्वर्ग आरोह्यतां विप्र किं वा ते रोचतेऽनघ ॥
data.md: Your body, O foremost of ascetics, should certainly be cast off. Do you ascend to heaven, O Brahmana. Or, tell us what else would please you, O sinless one.

data.v: न रोचये स्वर्गवासं विना देहादहं विभो । गच्छ धर्म न मे श्रद्धा स्वर्गं गन्तुं विनात्मना ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said I do not, O powerful lord, wish to live in heaven itself without this body of mine. Leave, me, O Dharma. I have no desire to go. to heaven itself without my own body.

data.v: अलं देहे मनः कृत्वा त्यक्त्वा देहं सुखी भव । गच्छ लोकानरजसो यत्र गत्वा न शोचसि ॥
data.md: Dharma said Without setting your heart on your body, cast it off and be happy. Go into regions that are free from the quality of Ignorance. Indeed, going there, you shall never have to experience any misery.

data.v: रमे जपन्महाभाग कृतं लोकैः सनातनैः । सशरीरेण गन्तव्यो मया स्वर्गो न वा विभो ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said O highly-blessed one, I take great pleasure in recitation. What necessity have I for those eternal regions of which you speak? Indeed, O powerful lord, I do not wish to go to heaven even with this body of mine.

data.v: यदि त्वं नेच्छसि त्यक्तुं शरीरं पश्य वै द्विज । एष कालस्तथा मृत्युर्यमश्च त्वामुपागताः ॥
data.md: Dharma said If you do not wish to cast off your body, behold O twice-born one, there is Time, and there is Mrityu, and there is Yama, who are all approaching you.

data.v: अथ वैवस्वतः कालो मृत्युश्च त्रितयं विभो । ब्राह्मणं तं महाभागमुपागम्येदमब्रुवन् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said After Dharma has said this, the three Vivasvat's son (Yama), Time and Mrityu, approached that Brahmana, 0 blessed king, and addressed him thus.

data.v: तपसोऽस्य सुतप्तस्य तथा सुचरितस्य च । फलप्राप्तिस्तव श्रेष्ठा यमोऽहं त्वामुपब्रुवे ॥
data.md: Yama said I am Yama. I say to you that a high reward awaits you for these well-performed penances of yours and for this your pious conduct.

data.v: यथावदस्य जप्यस्य फलं प्राप्तस्त्वमुत्तमम् । कालस्ते स्वर्गमारोढुं कालोऽहं त्वामुपागतः ॥
data.md: Time said You have acquired a high reward which is, indeed, commensurate with the recitation that you have finished. The time is come for you to ascent to heaven. I am Time and I have come to you.

data.v: मृत्युं मा विद्धि धर्मज्ञ रूपिणं स्वयमागतम् । कालेन चोदितं विप्र त्वामितो नेतुमद्य वै ॥
data.md: Mrityu said — You who are conversant with righteousness, know me for Mrityu herself in her own proper form! I have come to you in person, urged by Time, for taking you hence, O Brahmana.

data.v: स्वागतं सूर्यपुत्राय कालाय च महात्मने । मृत्यवे चाथ धर्माय किं कार्यं करवाणि वः ॥
data.md: 'Welcome to Surya's son, to great time, to Mrityu, and to Dharma. What shall I do for you all.

data.v: अर्घ्यं पाद्यं च दत्त्वा स तेभ्यस्तत्र समागमे । अब्रवीत्परमप्रीतः स्वशक्त्या किं करोमि वः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said In that meeting, the Brahmana gave them water to wash their feet, and the usual articles of the Arghya. Highly pleased, he then addressed them, saying,—What shall I do for you all to the best of my power.

data.v: तस्मिन्नेवाथ काले तु तीर्थयात्रामुपागतः । इक्ष्वाकुरगमत्तत्र समेता यत्र ते विभो ॥
data.md: Just at that time, O monarch, (king) Ikshvaku, who had started on a pilgrimage to holy waters and shrines, came there where those gods had been assembled together. are

data.v: सर्वानेव तु राजर्षिः संपूज्याभिप्रणम्य च । कुशलप्रश्नमकरोत्सर्वेषां राजसत्तमः ॥
data.md: The royal sage Ikshvaku bowed his head and adored them all. That best of king then enquired after the welfare of all of them.

data.v: तस्मै सोऽथासनं दत्त्वा पाद्यमर्घ्यं तथैव च । अब्रवीद्ब्राह्मणो वाक्यं कृत्वा कुशलसंविदम् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana offered the king a seat, as also water to wash his feet, and the usual Arghya. Having next made the usual enquiries of courtesy, he said,-

data.v: स्वागतं ते महाराज ब्रूहि यद्यदिहेच्छसि । स्वशक्त्या किं करोमीह तद्भवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे ॥
data.md: You welcome, 0 great king. communicate to me all your wishes. Let your noble self tell me what I shall have to do for you by putting forth my might,

data.v: राजाहं ब्राह्मणश्च त्वं यदि षट्कर्मसंस्थितः । ददामि वसु किंचित्ते प्रार्थितं तद्वदस्व मे ॥
data.md: The king said I am a king. You are a Brahmana observing the six well-known duties. I will give you some wealth. That is well-known. Tell me how much I shall give you.

data.v: द्विविधा ब्राह्मणा राजन्धर्मश्च द्विविधः स्मृतः । प्रवृत्तश्च निवृत्तश्च निवृत्तोऽस्मि प्रतिग्रहात् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said There are two kinds of Brahmanas, O king, Morality or righteousness also is of two sorts : devotion to work, and abstention from work. As regards myself, I do not accept gifts.

data.v: तेभ्यः प्रयच्छ दानानि ये प्रवृत्ता नराधिप । अहं न प्रतिगृह्णामि किमिष्टं किं ददानि ते । ब्रूहि त्वं नृपतिश्रेष्ठ तपसा साधयामि किम् ॥
data.md: Give presents to them, O king, who. are given to the duty of work and acceptance. I shall not, therefore, accept any gift. On the other hand, I ask you, what is for your wellbeing. What, indeed, shall I give you? Tell me, O foremost of kings, and I shall do it with the help of my penances.

data.v: क्षत्रियोऽहं न जानामि देहीति वचनं क्वचित् । प्रयच्छ युद्धमित्येवं वादिनः स्मो द्विजोत्तम ॥
data.md: The king Said I am a Kshatriya. I do not know how to say the word-Give. The only thing, O best of twice-born ones, that we can say is-Give (us)

data.v: तुष्यसि त्वं स्वधर्मेण तथा तुष्टा वयं नृप । अन्योन्यस्योत्तरं नास्ति यदिष्टं तत्समाचर ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said You are content with the observance of the duties of your order. Likewise, I am content with the duties of mine, O king. there is, therefore, little difference between us. Do what you please.

data.v: स्वशक्त्याहं ददानीति त्वया पूर्वं प्रभाषितम् । याचे त्वां दीयतां मह्यं जप्यस्यास्य फलं द्विज ॥
data.md: You gave vent to these words first, viz., I shall give you according to my might.-I, therefore, pray, O twice-born one,-Give me the fruits of this your recitation.

data.v: युद्धं मम सदा वाणी याचतीति विकत्थसे । न च युद्धं मया सार्धं किमर्थं याचसे पुनः ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said You boasted that your words always pray for battle. Why then do you not pray for a battle with me.

data.v: वाग्वज्रा ब्राह्मणाः प्रोक्ताः क्षत्रिया बाहुजीविनः । वाग्युद्धं तदिदं तीव्रं मम विप्र त्वया सह ॥
data.md: The king said It is said that Brahinanas are armed with the thunder of speech, and that Kshatriyas have might of arms. hence, O learned Brahmana, this wordy warfare has taken place between you and me.

data.v: सैवाद्यापि प्रतिज्ञा मे स्वशक्त्या किं प्रदीयताम् । ब्रूहि दास्यामि राजेन्द्र विभवे सति माचिरम् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said As regards myself, this is my resolution today. What shall I give you according to my might? Tell me, O king of kings, and I shall give you. Do not delay.

data.v: यत्तद्वर्षशतं पूर्णं जप्यं वै जपता त्वया । फलं प्राप्तं तत्प्रयच्छ मम दित्सुर्भवान्यदि ॥
data.md: If, indeed, you wish to give me anything, then give me the fruits you have acquired by practising recitation for these thousand years.

data.v: परमं गृह्यतां तस्य फलं यज्जपितं मया । अर्धं त्वमविचारेण फलं तस्य समाप्नुहि ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said Take the greatest fruit of the recitations I have practised. Indeed, take half, without any hesitation the entire fruits of that recitation.

data.v: अथ वा सर्वमेवेह जप्यकं मामकं फलम् । राजन्प्राप्नुहि कामं त्वं यदि सर्वमिहेच्छसि ॥
data.md: Or, O king, if you desire, take without any hesitation the entire fruits of my recitations.

data.v: कृतं सर्वेण भद्रं ते जप्यं यद्याचितं मया । स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि किं च तस्य फलं वद ॥
data.md: The king said Blessed be you, I have no necessity for the fruits of your recitations which I have begged. Blessings on your head. I am about to leave you. Tell me, however, what those fruits are.

data.v: फलप्राप्तिं न जानामि दत्तं यज्जपितं मया । अयं धर्मश्च कालश्च यमो मृत्युश्च साक्षिणः ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said I have no knowledge of the fruits I have acquired. I have, however, given you those fruits that I have acquired by recitation. These, viz., Dharma and time and Yama, and Mrityu, are witnesses.

data.v: अज्ञातमस्य धर्मस्य फलं मे किं करिष्यति । प्राप्नोतु तत्फलं विप्रो नाहमिच्छे ससंशयम् ॥
data.md: The king said I will not accept any other word (from you). I have given you the fruits of my recitations. Let, O royal sage, both your words and mine prove true.

data.v: नाददेऽपरवक्तव्यं दत्तं वाचा फलं मया । वाक्यं प्रमाणं राजर्षे ममापि तव चैव हि ॥
data.md: never I will not accept any words, as I have given the frut of recitations. O king of sages, these words only are considered as authoritative.

data.v: नाभिसंधिर्मया जप्ये कृतपूर्वः कथंचन । जप्यस्य राजशार्दूल कथं ज्ञास्याम्यहं फलम् ॥
data.md: As regards my recitations, I entertained any particular desire to do. How then, O foremost of kings, should I have any knowledge of what are the fruits of those recitations?

data.v: ददस्वेति त्वया चोक्तं ददामीति तथा मया । न वाचं दूषयिष्यामि सत्यं रक्ष स्थिरो भव ॥
data.md: You said-Give! I said, I give!-I shall not falsify these words. Keep the truth. Be calm.

data.v: अथैवं वदतो मेऽद्य वचनं न करिष्यसि । महानधर्मो भविता तव राजन्मृषाकृतः ॥
data.md: If you refuge to keep my word, O king, great sin of untruth will visit you.

data.v: न युक्तं तु मृषा वाणी त्वया वक्तुमरिंदम । तथा मयाप्यभ्यधिकं मृषा वक्तुं न शक्यते ॥
data.md: O chastiser of foes, you should not utter what is untrue. Likewise, I dare not falsify what I have said.

data.v: संश्रुतं च मया पूर्वं ददानीत्यविचारितम् । तद्गृह्णीष्वाविचारेण यदि सत्ये स्थितो भवान् ॥
data.md: I have, before this, unhesitatingly said, I give! If, therefore, you are firm in truth, accept my gift.

data.v: इहागम्य हि मां राजञ्जाप्यं फलमयाचिथाः । तन्मन्निसृष्टं गृह्णीष्व भव सत्ये स्थिरोऽपि च ॥
data.md: Coming here, O king, you begged of me the fruits of my recitations. Therefore, take what I have given away, if, indeed, you are truthful.

data.v: नायं लोकोऽस्ति न परो न च पूर्वान्स तारयेत् । कुत एवावरान्राजन्मृषावादपरायणः ॥
data.md: He who is given to falsehood has neither this world nor the next. Such a person cannot rescue his departed manes. How again shall he succeed in doing good to progeny?

data.v: न यज्ञाध्ययने दानं नियमास्तारयन्ति हि । तथा सत्यं परे लोके यथा वै पुरुषर्षभ ॥
data.md: The rewards of sacrifices and gifts, as also of fasts and religious observances, are not so powerful in rescuing as truth, O foremost of men, in both this and the next world.

data.v: तपांसि यानि चीर्णानि चरिष्यसि च यत्तपः । समाः शतैः सहस्रैश्च तत्सत्यान्न विशिष्यते ॥
data.md: All the penances that have been practised by you and all those that you will practised in the future of hundreds and thousands of years are more cfficacious than truth.

data.v: सत्यमेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म सत्यमेकाक्षरं तपः । सत्यमेकाक्षरो यज्ञः सत्यमेकाक्षरं श्रुतम् ॥
data.md: Truth is the one undecaying Brahma. Truth is the one undecaying Penance. Truth is the one undecaying Sacrifice. Truth is the one undecaying Veda.

data.v: सत्यं वेदेषु जागर्ति फलं सत्ये परं स्मृतम् । सत्याद्धर्मो दमश्चैव सर्वं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
data.md: Truth is awake in the Vedas. The fruits attached to truth have been described as the highest. From truth originate Righteousness and Self-control. Everything depends on truth.

data.v: सत्यं वेदास्तथाङ्गानि सत्यं यज्ञस्तथा विधिः । व्रतचर्यास्तथा सत्यमोंकारः सत्यमेव च ॥
data.md: Truth is the Vedas and their branches. Truth is knowledge. Truth is the Ordinance. Truth is the observance of vows and fasts. Truth is the Prime Syllable OM.

data.v: प्राणिनां जननं सत्यं सत्यं संततिरेव च । सत्येन वायुरभ्येति सत्येन तपते रविः ॥
data.md: Truth is the origin of creatures. Truth is their progeny. It is by truth that the Wind moves. It is by truth that the Sun gives heat.

data.v: सत्येन चाग्निर्दहति स्वर्गः सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः । सत्यं यज्ञस्तपो वेदाः स्तोभा मन्त्राः सरस्वती ॥
data.md: It is by truth that Fire burns. It is on truth that Heaven rests. Truth is Sacrifice. Penance, Vedas, the verses of Samans, Mantras, and Sarasvati.

data.v: तुलामारोपितो धर्मः सत्यं चैवेति नः श्रुतम् । समां कक्षां धारयतो यतः सत्यं ततोऽधिकम् ॥
data.md: We have heard that once on a time truth and all religious observances were weighted in a scale. When both were weighted, that scale on which truth was, proved heavier.

data.v: यतो धर्मस्ततः सत्यं सर्वं सत्येन वर्धते । किमर्थमनृतं कर्म कर्तुं राजंस्त्वमिच्छसि ॥
data.md: There is truth where Righteousness is. Everything multiplies through truth. Why, O king, do you wish to do false act.

data.v: सत्ये कुरु स्थिरं भावं मा राजन्ननृतं कृथाः । कस्मात्त्वमनृतं वाक्यं देहीति कुरुषेऽशुभम् ॥
data.md: Be firm in truth. Do not fact falsely, O king. Why do you falsify the falsify the words-Give (me)!-which you have said?

data.v: यदि जप्यफलं दत्तं मया नेषिष्यसे नृप । स्वधर्मेभ्यः परिभ्रष्टो लोकाननुचरिष्यसि ॥
data.md: If you refuse, O king, to accept the fruits that I have given you of my recitations, you shall then have to wander over the world, fallen away from Righteousness.

data.v: संश्रुत्य यो न दित्सेत याचित्वा यश्च नेच्छति । उभावानृतिकावेतौ न मृषा कर्तुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: That person who does not give after having promised, and he also that does not accept after having begged, are both stained with falsehood. You should not, therefore, falsify your own words.

data.v: योद्धव्यं रक्षितव्यं च क्षत्रधर्मः किल द्विज । दातारः क्षत्रियाः प्रोक्ता गृह्णीयां भवतः कथम् ॥
data.md: The king said To fight and to protect from the duties of Kshatriyas. It is said that Kshatriyas are givers. How then shall I take anything from you.

data.v: न छन्दयामि ते राजन्नापि ते गृहमाव्रजम् । इहागम्य तु याचित्वा न गृह्णीषे पुनः कथम् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said I never pressed you, O king. I did not seek your house. Yourself, coming here, coming here, you yourself begged of me, Why then do you not take?

data.v: अविवादोऽस्तु युवयोर्वित्तं मां धर्ममागतम् । द्विजो दानफलैर्युक्तो राजा सत्यफलेन च ॥
data.md: Dharma said Know you both that I am Dharma himself, Let there be no dispute between you. Let the Brahmana possess the reward of gift, and let the king also obtain the merit of truth.

data.v: स्वर्गं मां विद्धि राजेन्द्र रूपिणं स्वयमागतम् । अविवादोऽस्तु युवयोरुभौ तुल्यफलौ युवाम् ॥
data.md: Heaven said Know, O great king, that I am Heaven's self-incarnate, come here in person. Let this dispute between you cease. You are both equal in respect of the merit or rewards that you have acquired.

data.v: कृतं स्वर्गेण मे कार्यं गच्छ स्वर्ग यथासुखम् । विप्रो यदीच्छते दातुं प्रतीच्छतु च मे धनम् ॥
data.md: The king said I have no use with heaven. Go, O Heaven, to the place you have come from. If this learned Brahmana wishes to go to you, let him take the rewards that I have acquired.

data.v: बाल्ये यदि स्यादज्ञानान्मया हस्तः प्रसारितः । निवृत्तिलक्षणं धर्ममुपासे संहितां जपन् ॥
data.md: Thc Brahmana said In the boyhood I had, through Ignorance, stretched my hand for accepting gifts. Now, however, I recite the Gayatri, observing the duty of abstention.

data.v: निवृत्तं मां चिरं राजन्विप्रं लोभयसे कथम् । स्वेन कार्यं करिष्यामि त्वत्तो नेच्छे फलं नृप । तपःस्वाध्यायशीलोऽहं निवृत्तश्च प्रतिग्रहात् ॥
data.md: Why do you, O king, tempt me thus, me who have for a long time followed duty of abstention? I shall myself do what my duty is. I do not wish to participate in the rewards acquired by you, O king. I am given too penances and to the study of the Vedas, and I have abstained from acceptance.

data.v: यदि विप्र निसृष्टं ते जप्यस्य फलमुत्तमम् । आवयोर्यत्फलं किंचित्सहितं नौ तदस्त्विह ॥
data.md: The king said If, O Brahmana, you are really prepared to give me the excellent reward of your recitation, then let half that reward be mine, you also take at the same time half the reward that I myself have gained by my acts.

data.v: द्विजाः प्रतिग्रहे युक्ता दातारो राजवंशजाः । यदि धर्मः श्रुतो विप्र सहैव फलमस्तु नौ ॥
data.md: Brahmanas follows the duty of acceptance. Persons born in the royal order follow the duty of giving. If you are not unaware of the duties, let our fruits be equal.

data.v: मा वा भूत्सहभोज्यं नौ मदीयं फलमाप्नुहि । प्रतीच्छ मत्कृतं धर्मं यदि ते मय्यनुग्रहः ॥
data.md: Or, if you do not wish to be my equal regarding our rewards, that I may have gained. Do take the merit I have gained if you wish to show me favour.'

data.v: ततो विकृतचेष्टौ द्वौ पुरुषौ समुपस्थितौ । गृहीत्वान्योन्यमावेष्ट्य कुचेलावूचतुर्वचः ॥
data.md: Bhishma continued 'At this time two very ugly persons came there. Each had his arm upon the other's shoulder; both were ill-dressed. They said these

data.v: न मे धारयसीत्येको धारयामीति चापरः । इहास्ति नौ विवादोऽयमयं राजानुशासकः ॥
data.md: You owe me nothing!-I really owe you!-If we dispute in this way, here is the king, who governs men.

data.v: सत्यं ब्रवीम्यहमिदं न मे धारयते भवान् । अनृतं वदसीह त्वमृणं ते धारयाम्यहम् ॥
data.md: I say truly, you owe me nothing!-You speak falsely. I owe you a debt!

data.v: तावुभौ भृशसंतप्तौ राजानमिदमूचतुः । परीक्ष्यतां यथा स्याव नावामिह विगर्हितौ ॥
data.md: Both of them, greatly exercises in dispute, then addressed the king, saying,-See, O king, that none of us may be visited by sin!

data.v: धारयामि नरव्याघ्र विकृतस्येह गोः फलम् । ददतश्च न गृह्णाति विकृतो मे महीपते ॥
data.md: Virupa said I owe my companion Vikrita, O king, the merits of the gift of a cow. I am willing to satisfy that debt. This Vikrita, however, refuses to accept repayment.

data.v: न मे धारयते किंचिद्विरूपोऽयं नराधिप । मिथ्या ब्रवीत्ययं हि त्वा मिथ्याभासं नराधिप ॥
data.md: Vikrita said This Virupa, O king, owes me nothing. He speaks an untruth under the appearance of truth, O King.

data.v: विरूप किं धारयते भवानस्य वदस्व मे । श्रुत्वा तथा करिष्यामीत्येवं मे धीयते मतिः ॥
data.md: The king said Tell me, O Virupa, what is that which you owe your friend here. I wish to first hear you and then do what is proper.

data.v: शृणुष्वावहितो राजन्यथैतद्धारयाम्यहम् । विकृतस्यास्य राजर्षे निखिलेन नरर्षभ ॥
data.md: Virupa said Hear attentively, 0 king, all the circumstances fully about how I owe my companion, viz., this Vikrita, O king.

data.v: अनेन धर्मप्राप्त्यर्थं शुभा दत्ता पुरानघ । धेनुर्विप्राय राजर्षे तपःस्वाध्यायशीलिने ॥
data.md: This Vikrita had, in days gone by, for the sake of acquiring merit, O sinless onc, given away an auspicious cow, O royal sage, to a Brahmana given to penances and the study of the Vedas.

data.v: तस्याश्चायं मया राजन्फलमभ्येत्य याचितः । विकृतेन च मे दत्तं विशूद्धेनान्तरात्मना ॥
data.md: Going to him, O king, I begged of him the reward of that act. With a pure heart, Vikrita made a gift to me of that reward.

data.v: ततो मे सुकृतं कर्म कृतमात्मविशुद्धये । गावौ हि कपिले क्रीत्वा वत्सले बहुदोहने ॥
data.md: I then, for my purification, did some good acts. I also bought two Kapila cows with calves, both of which used to give large quantities of milk.

data.v: ते चोञ्छवृत्तये राजन्मया समपवर्जिते । यथाविधि यथाश्रद्धं तदस्याहं पुनः प्रभो ॥
इहाद्य वै गृहीत्वा तत्प्रयच्छे द्विगुणं फलम् । एकस्याः पुरुषव्याघ्र कः शुद्धः कोऽत्र दोषवान् ॥
data.md: I then presented according to due rites and with proper devotion, those two cows to a poor Brahmana living by picking solitary grains. Having formerly accepted the gift from my companion, I wish, O lord, even here, to give him in return twice the reward. The circumstances being such, O foremost of men, who amongst us two shall be innocent and who guilty?

data.v: एवं विवदमानौ स्वस्त्वामिहाभ्यागतौ नृप । कुरु धर्ममधर्मं वा विनये नौ समाधय ॥
data.md: Disputing with each other about this, we have both come to you, O King, Whether you judge rightly or wrongly, settle our dispute and put us in peace.

data.v: यदि नेच्छति मे दानं यथा दत्तमनेन वै । भवानत्र स्थिरो भूत्वा मार्गे स्थापयतु प्रभुः ॥
data.md: If this my companion does not wish to take from me in return a gift equal to what he gave me, you shall have to judge patiently and put us both on the right road.

data.v: दीयमानं न गृह्णासि ऋणं कस्मात्त्वमद्य वै । यथैव तेऽभ्यनुज्ञातं तथा गृह्णीष्व माचिरम् ॥
data.md: The king said, Why do you not accept payment that is sought lo be made for the debt that he owes to you? Do not delay, but accept payment of what you know, to be your due!

data.v: दीयतामित्यनेनोक्तं ददानीति तथा मया । नायं मे धारयत्यत्र गम्यतां यत्र वाञ्छति ॥
data.md: Vikrita said-This one says that he owes me. tell him that what I gave I give away. He does not, therefore, owe me anything, Let him go wherever he likes.

data.v: ददतोऽस्य न गृह्णासि विषमं प्रतिभाति मे । दण्ड्यो हि त्वं मम मतो नास्त्यत्र खलु संशयः ॥
data.md: He is ready to give.you. You are, however, reluctant to take. It does not appear proper to me! I think you should be punished for this. There is little doubt in this.

data.v: मयास्य दत्तं राजर्षे गृह्णीयां तत्कथं पुनः । काममत्रापराधो मे दण्ड्यमाज्ञापय प्रभो ॥
data.md: I made a gift to him, O royal sage! How can I take it back? If I am guilty in this, do you declare the punishment, O powerful one.

data.v: दीयमानं यदि मया नेषिष्यसि कथंचन । नियंस्यति त्वा नृपतिरयं धर्मानुशासकः ॥
data.md: Virupa said If you refuge to take when I am ready to give, this king will, forsooth, punish you, for he is an upholder of justice. Vikrita said,

data.v: स्वं मया याचितेनेह दत्तं कथमिहाद्य तत् । गृह्णीयां गच्छतु भवानभ्यनुज्ञां ददानि ते ॥
data.md: Vikrita said Begged by him I gave him what was my own. How shall I now take it back. You may go away. I permit you.

data.v: श्रुतमेतत्त्वया राजन्ननयोः कथितं द्वयोः । प्रतिज्ञातं मया यत्ते तद्गृहाणाविचारितम् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said You have heard, O king, the words of these two. Do you take unhesitatingly what I have promised to give you.

data.v: प्रस्तुतं सुमहत्कार्यमावयोर्गह्वरं यथा । जापकस्य दृढीकारः कथमेतद्भविष्यति ॥
data.md: This subject is, indeed, as deep as an unfathomable pit. How will the tenaciousness of this Reciter end.

data.v: यदि तावन्न गृह्णामि ब्राह्मणेनापवर्जितम् । कथं न लिप्येयमहं दोषेण महताद्य वै ॥
data.md: If I do not take what has been given by this Brahmana, how shall I avoid being polluted with a great sin?

data.v: तौ चोवाच स राजर्षिः कृतकार्यौ गमिष्यथः । नेदानीं मामिहासाद्य राजधर्मो भवेन्मृषा ॥
data.md: The royal sage then said to the two disputants,-having acquired your respective objects, go you both. I should see that kingly duties, which are in me, may not become useless.

data.v: स्वधर्मः परिपाल्यश्च राज्ञामेष विनिश्चयः । विप्रधर्मश्च सुगुरुर्मामनात्मानमाविशत् ॥
data.md: It is settled that kings should follow the duties sanctioned for them. To my misfortune, however, the course of duties laid down for Brahmanas has affected my wretched self.

data.v: गृहाण धारयेऽहं ते याचितं ते श्रुतं मया । न चेद्ग्रहीष्यसे राजञ्शपिष्ये त्वां न संशयः ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said Accept, O king! I owe you, You begged it of me, and I also have promised! If, however, you refuse to take, O king, I shall forsooth curse you.

data.v: धिग्राजधर्मं यस्यायं कार्यस्येह विनिश्चयः । इत्यर्थं मे ग्रहीतव्यं कथं तुल्यं भवेदिति ॥
data.md: Fie on royal duties, the fixed action of which is even such! I should, however, take what you give only for making the two sorts of duty exactly equal.

data.v: एष पाणिरपूर्वं भो निक्षेपार्थं प्रसारितः । यन्मे धारयसे विप्र तदिदानीं प्रदीयताम् ॥
data.md: This my hand, that was never before expanded, is not stretched forth. Give me what you owe me.

data.v: संहितां जपता यावान्मया कश्चिद्गुणः कृतः । तत्सर्वं प्रतिगृह्णीष्व यदि किंचिदिहास्ति मे ॥
data.md: If I have acquired any fruits by reciting the Gayatri, accept them all.

data.v: जलमेतन्निपतितं मम पाणौ द्विजोत्तम । सममस्तु सहैवास्तु प्रतिगृह्णातु वै भवान् ॥
data.md: The king said-These drops of water, see, O foremost of Brahmanas, have fallen upon my hand. I also wish to give you. Accept my gift. Let us both stand equal.

data.v: कामक्रोधौ विद्धि नौ त्वमावाभ्यां कारितो भवान् । समेति च यदुक्तं ते समा लोकास्तवास्य च ॥
data.md: Virupa said Know, O king, that we two are Desire and Anger. We have induced you to act thus! You have made a gift in return to the Brahmana. Let there be equality between you and this twiceborn one regarding blessed regions in the next world.

data.v: नायं धारयते किंचिज्जिज्ञासा त्वत्कृते कृता । कालो धर्मस्तथा मृत्युः कामक्रोधौ तथा युवाम् ॥
data.md: This Vikrita really does not owe me anything. We appealed to you for your own sake. Time, Dharma, Mrityu, and we two, have cxamined everything about you, here in your very presence, by creating this quarrel between you and that Brahmana. go now, as you like, to those regions of happiness which you have acquired by means of your deeds.

data.v: सर्वमन्योन्यनिकषे निघृष्टं पश्यतस्तव । गच्छ लोकाञ्जितान्स्वेन कर्मणा यत्र वाञ्छसि ॥
जापकानां फलावाप्तिर्मया ते संप्रकीर्तिता । गतिः स्थानं च लोकाश्च जापकेन यथा जिताः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said I have now told you how Reciters win the fruits (of their recitation) and what, indeed, is their object, what the place, and what the region of surya.

data.v: प्रयाति संहिताध्यायी ब्रह्माणं परमेष्ठिनम् । अथ वाग्निं समायाति सूर्यमाविशतेऽपि वा ॥
data.md: A Reciter of Gayatri goes to the supreme god Brahiman, or to Agni or enters the regions, that a Reciter may acquire.

data.v: स तैजसेन भावेन यदि तत्राश्नुते रतिम् । गुणांस्तेषां समादत्ते रागेण प्रतिमोहितः ॥
data.md: If he plays there in his new form, then stupefied by such attachment, he is affected by the attributes of those particular regions.

data.v: एवं सोमे तथा वायौ भूम्याकाशशरीरगः । सरागस्तत्र वसति गुणांस्तेषां समाचरन् ॥
data.md: He is equally affected if he goes to Soma, or Vayu, or Earth, or Space. The fact is, he lives in all these, with attachment, and shows the attributes peculiar to those regions.

data.v: अथ तत्र विरागी स गच्छति त्वथ संशयम् । परमव्ययमिच्छन्स तमेवाविशते पुनः ॥
data.md: If, however, after having freed himself from attachments, he goes to those regions and does not trust the happiness he enjoys) and wishes for That Which is Supreme and Immutable, he then enters even That.

data.v: अमृताच्चामृतं प्राप्तः शीतीभूतो निरात्मवान् । ब्रह्मभूतः स निर्द्वंद्वः सुखी शान्तो निरामयः ॥
data.md: In that case he acquires the ambrosia of ambrosia, to a state free from desire and individual consciousness. He becomes Brahma's self, freed from the influence of the pairs of opposites, happy, tranquil, the without pain.

data.v: ब्रह्मस्थानमनावर्तमेकमक्षरसंज्ञकम् । अदुःखमजरं शान्तं स्थानं तत्प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Indeed, he acquires that state which is free from pain, which is tranquil, which is called Brahma, whence there is no return, and which is called the One and Jummutable.

data.v: चतुर्भिर्लक्षणैर्हीनं तथा षड्भिः सषोडशैः । पुरुषं समतिक्रम्य आकाशं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: He becomes freed from the four means of perception, viz., Direct knowledge (through the senses), Revelation, Inference, and Intuition, the six conditions, (Hunger, Trust, Grief, Delusion, Disease, and Death), and also the other six and ten senses, attributes, viz., five breaths, the ten senses, and the mind. Transcending the Creator (Brahiman), he becomes at one with the One Supreme Soul.

data.v: अथ वेच्छति रागात्मा सर्वं तदधितिष्ठति । यच्च प्रार्थयते तच्च मनसा प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Or, if moved by attachments, he does not wish for such absorption, but wishes to have a separate existence depending on that Supreme Cause of everything, then he gets the fruition of all his desires.

data.v: अथ वा वीक्षते लोकान्सर्वान्निरयसंस्थितान् । निःस्पृहः सर्वतो मुक्तस्तत्रैव रमते सुखी ॥
data.md: Or, if he hates all regions of happiness, which have been called hells, he then, driving off desire and freed from everything, enjoys supreme happiness even in those very regions.

data.v: एवमेषा महाराज जापकस्य गतिर्यथा । एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
data.md: Thus, O king, I have described to you about the end acquired by Reciters. I have told you everything. What else do you wish to hear from me?

data.v: किमुत्तरं तदा तौ स्म चक्रतुस्तेन भाषिते । ब्राह्मणो वाथ वा राजा तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, what reply was given by either the Brahmana or the king to Virupa after he had finished his speech.

data.v: अथ वा तौ गतौ तत्र यदेतत्कीर्तितं त्वया । संवादो वा तयोः कोऽभूत्किं वा तौ तत्र चक्रतुः ॥
data.md: What king of end was it, amongst those described by you, that they acquired? What, indeed, was the conversation that took place between them, and what did they do there?"

data.v: तथेत्येवं प्रतिश्रुत्य धर्मं संपूज्य चाभिभो । यमं कालं च मृत्युं च स्वर्गं संपूज्य चार्हतः ॥
data.md: Saying,-Let it be as you have said, the Brahmana, adored Dharma and Yama and Time and Mrityu and Heaven all of whom deserved adorations.

data.v: पूर्वं ये चापरे तत्र समेता ब्राह्मणर्षभाः । सर्वान्संपूज्य शिरसा राजानं सोऽब्रवीद्वचः ॥
data.md: He also adored all those foremost of Brahmanas that had come there by bending his head to them. Addressing the king then, he said,-Gifted with the reward of my recitation, O royal sage, acquire an eminent position. With your permission I shall set myself to my recitations again.

data.v: फलेनानेन संयुक्तो राजर्षे गच्छ पुण्यताम् । भवता चाभ्यनुज्ञातो जपेयं भूय एव हि ॥
वरश्च मम पूर्वं हि देव्या दत्तो महाबल । श्रद्धा ते जपतो नित्यं भवितेति विशां पते ॥
data.md: O you of great power, the goddess Savitri gave me a boon, saying,-Let, your devotion to recitation be continuous.

data.v: यद्येवमफला सिद्धिः श्रद्धा च जपितुं तव । गच्छ विप्र मया सार्धं जापकं फलमाप्नुहि ॥
data.md: If your success has become futile, and if your heart is bent upon practising again, go, O learned Brahmana, half and half with me, and you alone enjoy the reward of the recitations.

data.v: कृतः प्रयत्नः सुमहान्सर्वेषां संनिधाविह । सह तुल्यफलौ चावां गच्छावो यत्र नौ गतिः ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said You have exerted your best before all these men. Let us then become equal regarding our rewards, and let us go to receive our end.

data.v: व्यवसायं तयोस्तत्र विदित्वा त्रिदशेश्वरः । सह देवैरुपययौ लोकपालैस्तथैव च ॥
data.md: Apprised of these determination, the king of the celestials came there, accompanied by the gods and the Regents of the world.

data.v: साध्या विश्वेऽथ मरुतो ज्योतींषि सुमहान्ति च । नद्यः शैलाः समुद्राश्च तीर्थानि विविधानि च ॥
तपांसि संयोगविधिर्वेदाः स्तोभाः सरस्वती । नारदः पर्वतश्चैव विश्वावसुर्हहा हुहूः ॥
गन्धर्वश्चित्रसेनश्च परिवारगणैर्युतः । नागाः सिद्धाश्च मुनयो देवदेवः प्रजापतिः । विष्णुः सहस्रशीर्षश्च देवोऽचिन्त्यः समागमत् ॥
अवाद्यन्तान्तरिक्षे च भेर्यस्तूर्याणि चाभिभो । पुष्पवर्षाणि दिव्यानि तत्र तेषां महात्मनाम् । ननृतुश्चाप्सरःसंघास्तत्र तत्र समन्ततः ॥
data.md: Celestial flowers were poured upon those great beings. Bevies of Apsaras danced all around.

data.v: अथ स्वर्गस्तथा रूपी ब्राह्मणं वाक्यमब्रवीत् । संसिद्धस्त्वं महाभाग त्वं च सिद्धस्तथा नृप ॥
data.md: Heaven, in his embodied form, came there. Addressing the Brahmana, he said,-You have acquired Success. You highly blessed.-Then addressing the king, said,-You have also, O king acquired success.

data.v: अथ तौ सहितौ राजन्नन्योन्येन विधानतः । विषयप्रतिसंहारमुभावेव प्रचक्रतुः ॥
data.md: O king having done good to each other, the king and the Brahmana, withdrew their senses from the objects of the world.

data.v: प्राणापानौ तथोदानं समानं व्यानमेव च । एवं तान्मनसि स्थाप्य दधतुः प्राणयोर्मनः ॥
data.md: Fixing the vital airs Prana, Apana Samana, Udana, and Vyana in the heart, they fixed the mind in Prana and Apana united together.

data.v: उपस्थितकृतौ तत्र नासिकाग्रमधो भ्रुवौ । कुङ्कुण्यां चैव मनसा शनैर्धारयतः स्म तौ ॥
data.md: They then placed the two united airs in the abdomen, and fixed their eyes on the tip of the nose and then immediately below the nose and then immediately below the two eye-brows. They next saw the two airs, with the help of the mind, in the interstice between the two eyebrows, bringing them there by and by.

data.v: निश्चेष्टाभ्यां शरीराभ्यां स्थिरदृष्टी समाहितौ । जितासनौ तथाधाय मूर्धन्यात्मानमेव च ॥
data.md: With bodies perfectly motionless they were absorbed with fixed gaze. Having controlled their souls, they then placed the soul within the brain.

data.v: तालुदेशमथोद्दाल्य ब्राह्मणस्य महात्मनः । ज्योतिर्ज्वाला सुमहती जगाम त्रिदिवं तदा ॥
data.md: Then passing the crown of the great Brahmana a fiery flame of great effulgence went up to heaven,

data.v: हाहाकारस्ततो दिक्षु सर्वासु सुमहानभूत् । तज्ज्योतिः स्तूयमानं स्म ब्रह्माणं प्राविशत्तदा ॥
data.md: Loud exclamations of sorrow, uttered by all creatures, were then heard on all sides. Lauded by all, that splendour then entered Brahmana's self.

data.v: ततः स्वागतमित्याह तत्तेजः स पितामहः । प्रादेशमात्रं पुरुषं प्रत्युद्गम्य विशां पते ॥
data.md: Coming forward, the great grandfather addressed that splendour which had become like a span in size saying,-Welcome.

data.v: भूयश्चैवापरं प्राह वचनं मधुरं स्म सः । जापकैस्तुल्यफलता योगानां नात्र संशयः ॥
data.md: And again he uttered these sweet words: Verily, Reciters acquire the same end with the Yogins.

data.v: योगस्य तावदेतेभ्यः फलं प्रत्यक्षदर्शनम् । जापकानां विशिष्टं तु प्रत्युत्थानं समाधिकम् ॥
data.md: When the Yogins attains his end he gets a direct vision unto all these (here assembled). Regarding Reciters, however, there is this distinction, that they are honoured by Brahmana's advancing forward to receive them.

data.v: उष्यतां मयि चेत्युक्त्वाचेतयत्स ततः पुनः । अथास्य प्रविवेशास्यं ब्राह्मणो विगतज्वरः ॥
data.md: Live you in me,-Thus spoke Brahman and once more gave consciousness to that splendour. Indeed, then, freed from all anxieties, the Brahmana entered the mouth of the Creator.

data.v: राजाप्येतेन विधिना भगवन्तं पितामहम् । यथैव द्विजशार्दूलस्तथैव प्राविशत्तदा ॥
data.md: The king Ikshvaku, too, in the same way, entered the divine Grandfather like that best of Brahmanas.

data.v: स्वयंभुवमथो देवा अभिवाद्य ततोऽब्रुवन् । जापकार्थमयं यत्नस्तदर्थं वयमागताः ॥
data.md: The deities saluted the self-create and said, A very superior end is, indeed, laid down for Reciters.

data.v: कृतपूजाविमौ तुल्यं त्वया तुल्यफलाविमौ । योगजापकयोर्दृष्टं फलं सुमहदद्य वै । सर्वाँल्लोकानतीत्यैतौ गच्छेतां यत्र वाञ्छितम् ॥
data.md: We have seen to-day the high end that is reserved for both. Yogins and Reciters. Transcending all happy regions, these two are capable of going wherever they like.

data.v: महास्मृतिं पठेद्यस्तु तथैवानुस्मृतिं शुभाम् । तावप्येतेन विधिना गच्छेतां मत्सलोकताम् ॥
data.md: Brahmana said-He also who would read the great Smriti (viz., the Vedas) and he too who would read the other sacred Smritis that follow the former, (viz., Manu's and the rest), would, similarly allain to the same region with me.

data.v: यश्च योगे भवेद्भक्तः सोऽपि नास्त्यत्र संशयः । विधिनानेन देहान्ते मम लोकानवाप्नुयात् । गम्यतां साधयिष्यामि यथास्थानानि सिद्धये ॥
data.md: He also, who is devoted to Yoga, will, forsooth, acquire likewise, after death, my own regions. I go hence. Go ye all to your respective abodes for the accomplishment of your ends.

data.v: इत्युक्त्वा स तदा देवस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत । आमन्त्र्य तं ततो देवा ययुः स्वं स्वं निवेशनम् ॥
data.md: Having said so that foremost of gods disappeared there and then. Having obtained a leave from him beforehand the gods returned to their respective quarters.

data.v: ते च सर्वे महात्मानो धर्मं सत्कृत्य तत्र वै । पृष्ठतोऽनुययू राजन्सर्वे सुप्रीतमानसाः ॥
data.md: Having honoured Dharma, all those great beings proceeded with well-pleased hearts, O king, walking behind that great god.

data.v: एतत्फलं जापकानां गतिश्चैव प्रकीर्तिता । यथाश्रुतं महाराज किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
data.md: These are the rewards of reciters and this their end. I have described them to you as ] myself had heard of them. What else, O king, do you wish to hear of?

data.v: किं फलं ज्ञानयोगस्य वेदानां नियमस्य च । भूतात्मा वा कथं ज्ञेयस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said What are the fruits of the Jnana Yoga, of all the Vedas, and of the (various) observances and vows? How also may the individual soul be known? Tell me this, O grand father.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । मनोः प्रजापतेर्वादं महर्षेश्च बृहस्पतेः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old narrative of the conversation between that lord of creatures, viz., Manu, and the great Rishi Brihaspati.

data.v: प्रजापतिं श्रेष्ठतमं पृथिव्यां; देवर्षिसंघप्रवरो महर्षिः । बृहस्पतिः प्रश्नमिमं पुराणं; पप्रच्छ शिष्योऽथ गुरुं प्रणम्य ॥
data.md: In days of yore, the foremost of celestial Rishis, viz., Brihaspati, who was a disciple of Manu bowed to his preceptor and addressing that king and first of all creatures, said,-What is the origin of the universe? Whence have the ordinances originated? What are those fruits attributed by the learned to Knowledge? Tell me also truly, O illustrious one, what is that which the Vedas have not been able to show?

data.v: यत्कारणं मन्त्रविधिः प्रवृत्तो; ज्ञाने फलं यत्प्रवदन्ति विप्राः । यन्मन्त्रशब्दैरकृतप्रकाशं; तदुच्यतां मे भगवन्यथावत् ॥
यदर्थशास्त्रागममन्त्रविद्भि;र्यज्ञैरनेकैर्वरगोप्रदानैः । फलं महद्भिर्यदुपास्यते च; तत्किं कथं वा भविता क्व वा तत् ॥
data.md: What are those fruits which are respected by eminent sages conversant with the science of Artha, with the Vedas, and with the mantras, through sacrifices and profuse gifts of kine? Whence do those fruits originate? Where are they do be found?

data.v: मही महीजाः पवनोऽन्तरिक्षं; जलौकसश्चैव जलं दिवं च । दिवौकसश्चैव यतः प्रसूता;स्तदुच्यतां मे भगवन्पुराणम् ॥
data.md: Tell me also this old history, viz., whence have the Earth, all earthly objects, wind, sky aquatic animals, water, heaven, and the dwellers of heaven, all originated.

data.v: ज्ञानं यतः प्रार्थयते नरो वै; ततस्तदर्था भवति प्रवृत्तिः । न चाप्यहं वेद परं पुराणं; मिथ्याप्रवृत्तिं च कथं नु कुर्याम् ॥
data.md: Man is inclined towards that object which he seeks to know. I have no knowledge of that Ancient and Supreme Being. How shall I free myself from a false display of my leaning towards Him?

data.v: ऋक्सामसंघांश्च यजूंषि चाहं; छन्दांसि नक्षत्रगतिं निरुक्तम् । अधीत्य च व्याकरणं सकल्पं; शिक्षां च भूतप्रकृतिं न वेद्मि ॥
data.md: I have read the Riks, all the Samans, all the Yajuses, the Chhandas, Astronomy, Nirukta, Grammar, Sankalpa, and Shiksha. But I have no knowledge of the nature of the five principal elements which forin everything.

data.v: स मे भवाञ्शंसतु सर्वमेत;ज्ज्ञाने फलं कर्मणि वा यदस्ति । यथा च देहाच्च्यवते शरीरी; पुनः शरीरं च यथाभ्युपैति ॥
यद्यत्प्रियं यस्य सुखं तदाहु;स्तदेव दुःखं प्रवदन्त्यनिष्टम् । इष्टं च मे स्यादितरच्च न स्या;देतत्कृते कर्मविधिः प्रवृत्तः । इष्टं त्वनिष्टं च न मां भजेते;त्येतत्कृते ज्ञानविधिः प्रवृत्तः ॥
कामात्मकाश्छन्दसि कर्मयोगा; एभिर्विमुक्तः परमश्नुवीत । नानाविधे कर्मपथे सुखार्थी; नरः प्रवृत्तो न परं प्रयाति । परं हि तत्कर्मपथादपेतं; निराशिषं ब्रह्मपरं ह्यवश्यम् ॥
data.md: The ordinances about sacrifices and other observances, which are in the Vedas, all originate from desire. He, however, who frees himself from desire of acquiring happiness, performs various acts is constrained to go to hell.

data.v: प्रजाः सृष्टा मनसा कर्मणा च; द्वावप्येतौ सत्पथौ लोकजुष्टौ । दृष्ट्वा कर्म शाश्वतं चान्तवच्च; मनस्त्यागः कारणं नान्यदस्ति ॥
data.md: Creatures have all been engendered by Mind and Act. These are the two best paths adored of all. External acts yields fruits that are both transitory as also eternal. For acquiring the latter there is no other means than relinquishing the desire for fruits by the mind,

data.v: स्वेनात्मना चक्षुरिव प्रणेता; निशात्यये तमसा संवृतात्मा । ज्ञानं तु विज्ञानगुणेन युक्तं; कर्माशुभं पश्यति वर्जनीयम् ॥
data.md: As the eye, when night passes away and the veil of darkness is gone, leads its possessor by its own power, so the Understanding, when it becomes endued with Knowledge, sees all evils which should be shunned.

data.v: सर्पान्कुशाग्राणि तथोदपानं; ज्ञात्वा मनुष्याः परिवर्जयन्ति । अज्ञानतस्तत्र पतन्ति मूढा; ज्ञाने फलं पश्य यथा विशिष्टम् ॥
data.md: Men avoid snakes, sharp blades, of Kusha and pits, when they find them on their way. If some tread upon or fall into them, they do so by ignorance. Mark the superiority of the fruits of knowledge.

data.v: कृत्स्नस्तु मन्त्रो विधिवत्प्रयुक्तो; यज्ञा यथोक्तास्त्वथ दक्षिणाश्च । अन्नप्रदानं मनसः समाधिः; पञ्चात्मकं कर्मफलं वदन्ति ॥
data.md: Duly administered Mantras, sacrifices, the presents called Dakshina, gift of food and concentration of the mind are the five acts which yield fruits, there being none else.

data.v: गुणात्मकं कर्म वदन्ति वेदा;स्तस्मान्मन्त्रा मन्त्रमूलं हि कर्म । विधिर्विधेयं मनसोपपत्तिः; फलस्य भोक्ता तु यथा शरीरी ॥
data.md: Acts have the three Gunas (of Satva Rajas, and Tamas) for their soul. The Vedas say this. The Mantras, therefore, have the same three qualities, since it is with Mantras that acts are performed. The ritual also is possessed by the same three qualities. The fruits of action depend upon the mind. It is the embodied creature who enjoys those fruits.

data.v: शब्दाश्च रूपाणि रसाश्च पुण्याः; स्पर्शाश्च गन्धाश्च शुभास्तथैव । नरो नसंस्थानगतः प्रभुः स्या;देतत्फलं सिध्यति कर्मलोके ॥
data.md: All excellent sorts of sound, form, tastes, touch, and scent, are the fruits of acts, being acquired in the region of acts. As for, however, the fruits of knowledge, man acquires them even here before death.

data.v: यद्यच्छरीरेण करोति कर्म; शरीरयुक्तः समुपाश्नुते तत् । शरीरमेवायतनं सुखस्य; दुःखस्य चाप्यायतनं शरीरम् ॥
data.md: Whatever acts are perforined by means of the body, one enjoys the fruits thereof in this body. The body is, indeed, the structure to which adhere both happiness and misery.

data.v: वाचा तु यत्कर्म करोति किंचि;द्वाचैव सर्वं समुपाश्नुते तत् । मनस्तु यत्कर्म करोति किंचि;न्मनःस्थ एवायमुपाश्नुते तत् ॥
data.md: Whatever acts are performed by means of words, their fruits are enjoyed in a state in which words can be spoken. Likewise, whatever acts are performed by the mind, their fruits are enjoyed in a state in which one is not treed from the mind.

data.v: यथागुणं कर्मगणं फलार्थी; करोत्ययं कर्मफले निविष्टः । तथा तथायं गुणसंप्रयुक्तः; शुभाशुभं कर्मफलं भुनक्ति ॥
data.md: Seeking the fruits of acts, whatever acts (Satvika or Rajasika or Tamasika) a person performs, the fruits, good or bad, that he actually enjoys are permeated by their nature.

data.v: मत्स्यो यथा स्रोत इवाभिपाती; तथा कृतं पूर्वमुपैति कर्म । शुभे त्वसौ तुष्यति दुष्कृते तु; न तुष्यते वै परमः शरीरी ॥
data.md: Like fishes going against a current of water, pristine acts visit the actor. The embodied creature enjoys happiness for his good acts, and suffers misery for his evil ones.

data.v: यतो जगत्सर्वमिदं प्रसूतं; ज्ञात्वात्मवन्तो व्यतियान्ति यत्तत् । यन्मन्त्रशब्दैरकृतप्रकाशं; तदुच्यमानं शृणु मे परं यत् ॥
data.md: I will now describe Him from whom this universe has originated, Him by knowing whom persons of purified souls cross this world, Him who has not been expressed by Vedic Mantras and Words. Listen to me as I speak of that greatest of the grcat.

data.v: रसैर्वियुक्तं विविधैश्च गन्धै;रशब्दमस्पर्शमरूपवच्च । अग्राह्यमव्यक्तमवर्णमेकं; पञ्चप्रकारं ससृजे प्रजानाम् ॥
data.md: Himself freed from the several sorts of tasto and scent, and sound and touch and forin, He is incapable of being comprehended by the senses, unmanifest, without colour, the One, and He has created the five kinds of objects for His creatures.

data.v: न स्त्री पुमान्वापि नपुंसकं च; न सन्न चासत्सदसच्च तन्न । पश्यन्ति यद्ब्रह्मविदो मनुष्या;स्तदक्षरं न क्षरतीति विद्धि ॥
data.md: He is neither female, nor male, nor of the neuter sex. He is neither existent, nor nonexistent, nor existent-non-existent. Only those that are acquainted with Bralıma see Him. He knows no deterioration.

data.v: अक्षरात्खं ततो वायुर्वायोर्ज्योतिस्ततो जलम् । जलात्प्रसूता जगती जगत्यां जायते जगत् ॥
data.md: From that eternal and undecaying. One first originated Space; from space came Wind; from wind came Light; from light came Water. From water originated the Universe; and from the universe, all things that exist in it.

data.v: इमे शरीरैर्जलमेव गत्वा; जलाच्च तेजः पवनोऽन्तरिक्षम् । खाद्वै निवर्तन्ति नभाविनस्ते; ये भाविनस्ते परमाप्नुवन्ति ॥
data.md: The bodies of all (earthly) objects, thence to light or heat, thence to the wind, and thence to space. The who seek liberation have not to return from space. On the other hand, they attain to Brahma.

data.v: नोष्णं न शीतं मृदु नापि तीक्ष्णं; नाम्लं कषायं मधुरं न तिक्तम् । न शब्दवन्नापि च गन्धवत्त;न्न रूपवत्तत्परमस्वभावम् ॥
data.md: The refuge of liberation, viz., Brahma, is neither hot, nor cold, neither mild nor fierce, neither sour nor astringent, neither sweet nor bitter. He is not endued with sound, or scent, or form. He transcends all these and everything, and is without size.

data.v: स्पर्शं तनुर्वेद रसं तु जिह्वा; घ्राणं च गन्धाञ्श्रवणे च शब्दान् । रूपाणि चक्षुर्न च तत्परं य;द्गृह्णन्त्यनध्यात्मविदो मनुष्याः ॥
data.md: The skin perceives touch; the tongue, taste; the nose, scent; the ears, sounds; and the eye, forms. Men not conversant with Adhyatma succeed not in seeing what is above these.

data.v: निवर्तयित्वा रसनं रसेभ्यो; घ्राणं च गन्धाच्छ्रवणे च शब्दात् । स्पर्शात्तनुं रूपगुणात्तु चक्षु;स्ततः परं पश्यति स्वं स्वभावम् ॥
data.md: Having withdrawn the tongue from tastes, the nose from scents, the ears from sounds, and the eye from forms, one sees his ownself.

data.v: यतो गृहीत्वा हि करोति यच्च; यस्मिंश्च तामारभते प्रवृत्तिम् । यस्मिंश्च यद्येन च यश्च कर्ता; तत्कारणं तं समुपायमाहुः ॥
data.md: It has been said that which is the Cause of the actor, the act, the material with which the act is done, the place and the time of the act, and the inclinations and propensities about happiness and misery, is called the Self (or Soul).

data.v: यच्चाभिभूः साधकं व्यापकं च; यन्मन्त्रवच्छंस्यते चैव लोके । यः सर्वहेतुः परमार्थकारी; तत्कारणं कार्यमतो यदन्यत् ॥
data.md: That which permeates everything which does everything, that which exists in the universe even as the Mantras say, that which is the cause of all, that which is the highest of the high, and that which is One without a second and does all things, is the Cause. Every thing clse is effect.

data.v: यथा च कश्चित्सुकृतैर्मनुष्यः; शुभाशुभं प्राप्नुतेऽथाविरोधात् । एवं शरीरेषु शुभाशुभेषु; स्वकर्मजैर्ज्ञानमिदं निबद्धम् ॥
data.md: It is seen that person, on account of the acts performed by him, reaps fruits both good and evil, which exist harmoniously. Indeed, as the good and evil fruits begotten by their own acts live together in the bodies of creatures which are their refuge, so Knowledge lives in the .body.

data.v: यथा प्रदीपः पुरतः प्रदीप्तः; प्रकाशमन्यस्य करोति दीप्यन् । तथेह पञ्चेन्द्रियदीपवृक्षा; ज्ञानप्रदीप्ताः परवन्त एव ॥
data.md: As a lighted lamp, while burning, sees other objects before it, so the five senses which are like lamps fixed on high trees, find out their respective objects when lighted by Knowledge.

data.v: यथा हि राज्ञो बहवो ह्यमात्याः; पृथक्प्रमानं प्रवदन्ति युक्ताः । तद्वच्छरीरेषु भवन्ति पञ्च; ज्ञानैकदेशः परमः स तेभ्यः ॥
data.md: As the various ministers of a king, in a body, give him advice so the five senses which exist in the body all obey Knowledge. The latter is superior to all of them.

data.v: यथार्चिषोऽग्नेः पवनस्य वेगा; मरीचयोऽर्कस्य नदीषु चापः । गच्छन्ति चायान्ति च तन्यमाना;स्तद्वच्छरीराणि शरीरिणां तु ॥
data.md: As the flames of fire, the current of the wind, the rays of the sun, and the waters of rivers, go and come, again and again, so the bodies of embodied creatures are going and coming repeatedly.

data.v: यथा च कश्चित्परशुं गृहीत्वा; धूमं न पश्येज्ज्वलनं च काष्ठे । तद्वच्छरीरोदरपाणिपादं; छित्त्वा न पश्यन्ति ततो यदन्यत् ॥
data.md: As a person by taking up an axe cannot, by cutting open a piece of wood, see either smoke or fire in it, so one cannot, by cutting open the arms, feet and stomach of a person, cannot see the principle of knowledge, which, does not partake of the nature of stomach, the arms, and feet.

data.v: तान्येव काष्ठानि यथा विमथ्य; धूमं च पश्येज्ज्वलनं च योगात् । तद्वत्सुबुद्धिः सममिन्द्रियत्वा;द्बुधः परं पश्यति स्वं स्वभावम् ॥
data.md: As again one sees both smoke and fire in wood by rubbing it against another piece, só a person endued with true intelligence and wisdom, by uniting the senses and the soul, may see the Supreme Soul which, of course, exists in its own nature.

data.v: यथात्मनोऽङ्गं पतितं पृथिव्यां; स्वप्नान्तरे पश्यति चात्मनोऽन्यत् । श्रोत्रादियुक्तः सुमनाः सुबुद्धि;र्लिङ्गात्तथा गच्छति लिङ्गमन्यत् ॥
data.md: As in the midst of a dream one sees his own body lying on the ground s something distinct from one's own self, so a person, having the five senses, the mind, and the understanding, sees (after death) his own body and then goes from one into another form.

data.v: उत्पत्तिवृद्धिक्षयसंनिपातै;र्न युज्यतेऽसौ परमः शरीरी । अनेन लिङ्गेन तु लिङ्गमन्य;द्गच्छत्यदृष्टः प्रतिसंधियोगात् ॥
data.md: The Soul does not undergo birth, growth, decay, and destruction. Acts of life being followed by effects, the Soul, clothed in body into another, unseen by others.

data.v: न चक्षुषा पश्यति रूपमात्मनो; न चापि संस्पर्शमुपैति किंचित् । न चापि तैः साधयतेऽथ कार्यं; ते तं न पश्यन्ति स पश्यते तान् ॥
data.md: No one can see with the eye the form of the Soul. The Soul again, is not touched by another. With the senses, the Soul performs no act. The senses do not approach the Soul. The Soul, however, apprehends them all.

data.v: यथा प्रदीपे ज्वलतोऽनलस्य; संतापजं रूपमुपैति किंचित् । न चान्तरं रूपगुणं बिभर्ति; तथैव तद्दृश्यते रूपमस्य ॥
data.md: As anything, placed in a burning fire before a spectator, assumes a certain colour on account of the light and heat that acts upon it, without taking any other colour or attribute, even so the Soul's form is seen to take its colour from the body.

data.v: यथा मनुष्यः परिमुच्य काय;मदृश्यमन्यद्विशते शरीरम् । विसृज्य भूतेषु महत्सु देहं; तदाश्रयं चैव बिभर्ति रूपम् ॥
data.md: Likewise, men, renouncing one body, enters another, unseen by all. Indeed, casting off his body to the five great principal elements, he assumes a form that is likewise made of the same elements.

data.v: खं वायुमग्निं सलिलं तथोर्वीं; समन्ततोऽभ्याविशते शरीरी । नानाश्रयाः कर्मसु वर्तमानाः; श्रोत्रादयः पञ्च गुणाञ्श्रयन्ते ॥
data.md: Upon the destruction of his body the embodied creature enters space, wind, fire, water, and earth in such a way that each particular element in his body mingles with the particular element (out of his body) partaking of its nature. The senses also, which are engaged in various occupations and depend on the five elements enter their five elements what call forth their functions.

data.v: श्रोत्रं खतो घ्राणमथो पृथिव्या;स्तेजोमयं रूपमथो विपाकः । जलाश्रयः स्वेद उक्तो रसश्च; वाय्वात्मकः स्पर्शकृतो गुणश्च ॥
data.md: The ear derives its power from space; and the smell from the earth. From, which is the property of the eye, is the outcome of light or fire. Fire or heat depends on water. The tongue which has for its property taste, is merged in water. The skin which has touch for its property, is lost in the wind whose nature it partakes.

data.v: महत्सु भूतेषु वसन्ति पञ्च; पञ्चेन्द्रियार्थाश्च तथेन्द्रियेषु । सर्वाणि चैतानि मनोनुगानि; बुद्धिं मनोऽन्वेति मनः स्वभावम् ॥
data.md: The fivefold attributes, (viz., sound, etc.) dwell in the five principal elements. Those fivefold objects of the senses (viz., space, etc.,) live in the (five) senses, All these again follow the mind. The mind follows the Understanding, and the Understanding follows That which exists in its true and pure nature, viz., the Supreme Self.

data.v: शुभाशुभं कर्म कृतं यदस्य; तदेव प्रत्याददते स्वदेहे । मनोऽनुवर्तन्ति परावराणि; जलौकसः स्रोत इवानुकूलम् ॥
data.md: The actor in his new body receives all the good and bad acts done by him here, as also all acts done by him in his pristine existence. All these acts done in this life and the next ones follow the mind even as aquatic animals pass along a current.

data.v: चलं यथा दृष्टिपथं परैति; सूक्ष्मं महद्रूपमिवाभिपाति । स्वरूपमालोचयते च रूपं; परं तथा बुद्धिपथं परैति ॥
data.md: As a quickly-moving restless object comes in view, as a minute object appears huge (when seen through spectacles), as a mirror shows a person his own face, so the soul becomes an object of the Understanding's apprehension.
