data.v: ये वै शुक्रगतिं विद्युर्भूतसंकरकारिकाम् । विरागा दग्धदोषास्ते नाप्नुयुर्देहसंभवम् ॥
data.md: Those persons, who know that the course of seminal fluid is the cause of intermixture of castes, are men of controlled passions. Their sins are considered to have been consumed, and they are never subjected to re-birth.

data.md: He who performs action simply for the purpose of maintaining his body, reducing with the help of the mind the qualities into a state of equilibrium, and brings at his last moments the vital airs to the channel called Manovaha, is freed from re-birth.

data.v: भविता मनसो ज्ञानं मन एव प्रतायते । ज्योतिष्मद्विरजो दिव्यमत्र सिद्धं महात्मनाम् ॥
data.md: The Mind is sure to acquire Knowledge. It is the Mind which assumes the form of all things. Acquiring success through meditation, the minds of all great persons, become freed from desire, eternal, and shining.

data.md: Therefore, for destroying the mind, one should perform only pure deeds, and frecing himself from the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance, one is sure to acquire a very desirable end.

data.md: Knowledge (ordinarily) acquired in younger days becomes weakened with decrepitude. Through the good effects of past lives, a person, however, of ripe understanding succeeds in killing his desires.

data.md: Such a person, by getting over the fetters of the body and the senses like a traveller crossing a path full of impediments, and transgressing all faults he sees, succeeds in testing the ambrosia (of Liberation.)

data.md: Bhishma said By being attached to objects of the senses which are always imbued with evil, living creatures become helpless. Those great persons, however, who are not attached to them, acquire the greatest end.

data.md: Seeing the world beset with the evils formed by birth, death, decrepitude, sorrow, disease, and anxieties, the man of intelligence should try for the attainment of Liberation.

data.md: He should be pure in words, thought and body; he should be shorn of pride. Of tranquil soul and endued with knowledge, he should live like a mendicant, and pursue happiness without being attached to any wordły object.

data.v: अथ वा मनसः सङ्गं पश्येद्भूतानुकम्पया । अत्राप्युपेक्षां कुर्वीत ज्ञात्वा कर्मफलं जगत् ॥
data.md: Again, if his mind is filled with attachment for mercy to creatures, he should, seeing that the universe is the result of acts, one should show indifference even to mercy itself.

data.md: Whatever good acts are done, or whatever sin is committed, the actor reaps the points thereof. Hence, one should, in words, thought, and deed, do only good acts.

data.md: He enjoys happiness who practises abstention from injuring (others), truthfulness of speech, honesty towards all creatures, and forgiveness, and who is never careless.

data.md: Hence one, exercising his intelligence, should fix his mind, after training it, on peace towards all creatures.

data.md: That man who considers the practice of the virtues mentioned above as the greatest duty as securing the happiness of all creatures, and as destroying all sorts of sorrow, is possessed of the greatest knowledge, and succeeds in acquiring happiness. data.md: Forsooth, a person who is shorn of desire, free from the fetters of the world, contented to live in solitude, abstemious in diet, devoted to penances, and with senses under restraint, who has consumed all his sorrows by knowledge, who finds pleasure in practising Yoga and who has a cleansed soul, succeeds, on account of his mind being withdrawn into itself, in attaining to Brahina or Liberation.

data.md: One endued with patience and a pure soul should, forsooth, control his understanding. With the understanding, one should next restrain mind, and then with the mind overpower the objects of the senses.

data.md: When one's senses are withdrawn into the mind, the result becomes that Brahma becomes manifested in it. Indeed, when the senses are destroyed, and the soul returns to the quality of pure existence, it is regarded as being transformed into Brahma.

data.md: Then again, one should never show his Yoga power. On the other hand, one should always try to restrain his senses by practising the rules of Yoga. Indeed, one engaged in the practice of Yoga should do all those acts by which his conduct and nature may become pure.

data.md: As the imagination of a person who is awake and engaged in acts, is due only to the creative power of the mind, similarly, the impressions in a dream belong only to the mind.

data.md: A person with desire and attachment receives those imaginations based upon the impressions of numberless pristine lives. Nothing, that impresses the mind once is ever lost, and the Soul being cognisant of all those impressions makes them appear.

data.md: Whichever among the three qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance is caused by the influence of pristine acts and by whichever amongst them the mind is affected for the time being in whatever way, the elements in their subtile forms) or indicate accordingly (in the way of images).

data.md: After images have thus been created the particular quality of Goodness Darkness or Ignorance that inay have been brought by pristine acts rises in the mind and produces its last result, viz., happiness or misery.

data.v: ततः पश्यत्यसंबद्धान्वातपित्तकफोत्तरान् । रजस्तमोभवैर्भावैस्तदप्याहुर्दुरन्वयम् ॥
data.md: Those images originating principally wind, bile, and phlegm, which men apprehend through ignorance and in consequence of tendency pervaded by Darkness and Ignorance, cannot, it has been said, be easily discarded.

data.v: प्रसन्नैरिन्द्रियैर्यद्यत्संकल्पयति मानसम् । तत्तत्स्वप्नेऽप्युपरते मनोदृष्टिर्निरीक्षते ॥
data.md: (When one is awake) whatever objects a person perceives in the mind through the senses in a clear state are apprehended by the mind in dreams while the senses are inactive.

data.v: व्यापकं सर्वभूतेषु वर्ततेऽप्रतिघं मनः । मनस्यन्तर्हितं द्वारं देहमास्थाय मानसम् ॥
यत्तत्सदसदव्यक्तं स्वपित्यस्मिन्निदर्शनम् । सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्थं तदध्यात्मगुणं विदुः ॥
data.md: In the state called dreamless sleep the manifest human body which, of course, is the door of dreams, disappears in the mind. Possessing the body the mind enters the Soul which is unmanifest and upon which all existent and non-existent things depend, and becomes a wakeful witness with certainly of apprehension. Thus living in pure Consciousness which is the soul of all things, it is considered by the learned as transcending both Consciousness and all things in the universe.

data.v: लिप्सेत मनसा यश्च संकल्पादैश्वरं गुणम् । आत्मप्रभावात्तं विद्यात्सर्वा ह्यात्मनि देवताः ॥
data.md: That Yogin who by desire covets any of the divine qualities (of Knowledge or renunciation, etc.,) should regard a pure mind to be at one with the object of his desire. All things exist in a pure mind or soul.

data.v: एवं हि तपसा युक्तमर्कवत्तमसः परम् । त्रैलोक्यप्रकृतिर्देही तपसा तं महेश्वरम् ॥
data.md: This is the result acquired by one who practises penances. That Yogin, however, who has got over Darkness or ignorance, is endued with transcending effulgence. When Darkness or Ignorance has been got over, the embodied Soul becomes Supreme Brahma, the cause of the universe.

data.v: तपो ह्यधिष्ठितं देवैस्तपोघ्नमसुरैस्तमः । एतद्देवासुरैर्गुप्तं तदाहुर्ज्ञानलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: The deities have penances and Vedic rites. Darkness (or pride and cruelty), which destroys the former, has been adopted by the Asuras. This viz., Brahma, which has been said to have knowledge only for its quality, is difficult of attainment by either the gods or the Asuras.

data.v: सत्त्वं रजस्तमश्चेति देवासुरगुणान्विदुः । सत्त्वं देवगुणं विद्यादितरावासुरौ गुणौ ॥
data.md: It should be known that the qualities of Goodness, Darkness, and Ignorance belong to the gods and the Asuras. Goodness is the quality of the gods; while the two others belong to the Asuras.

data.v: ब्रह्म तत्परमं वेद्यममृतं ज्योतिरक्षरम् । ये विदुर्भावितात्मानस्ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: Brahma transcends all those qualities. It is pure Knowledge. It is immortality. It is pure effulgence. it is undecaying. Those persons of pure souls who know Brahma attain to the highest end.

data.v: हेतुमच्छक्यमाख्यातुमेतावज्ज्ञानचक्षुषा । प्रत्याहारेण वा शक्यमव्यक्तं ब्रह्म वेदितुम् ॥
data.md: One having knowledge for his eye can say this much with the help of reason and analogy. Brahma which is indestructible can be comprehended by only withdrawing the senses and the mind.

data.v: न स वेद परं धर्मं यो न वेद चतुष्टयम् । व्यक्ताव्यक्ते च यत्तत्त्वं संप्राप्तं परमर्षिणा ॥
data.md: Bhishma said 'He does not know Brahma who does not know the four topics, namely, dreams, dreamless sleep, immanent, and transcendent Brahma, as also what is Manifest (viz., the body), and what is Unmanifest (the intelligence-soul), which the great Rishi (Narayana) has described as Tattvam (pure principle).

data.v: व्यक्तं मृत्युमुखं विद्यादव्यक्तममृतं पदम् । प्रवृत्तिलक्षणं धर्ममृषिर्नारायणोऽब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: That which is manifest is subject to death. That which is unmanifest transcends, death. The Rishi Narayana has described the religion of inclination.

data.v: अत्रैवावस्थितं सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् । निवृत्तिलक्षणं धर्ममव्यक्तं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् ॥
data.md: Upon that depends the entire universe with its mobile and immobile creatures. The religion of disinclination again leads to the unmanifest and eternal Brahma.

data.v: प्रवृत्तिलक्षणं धर्मं प्रजापतिरथाब्रवीत् । प्रवृत्तिः पुनरावृत्तिर्निवृत्तिः परमा गतिः ॥
data.md: The Creator (Brahman) has described the religion of inclination. Inclination indicates rebirth or return. Disinclination on the other hand, indicates the highest end.

data.v: तां गतिं परमामेति निवृत्तिपरमो मुनिः । ज्ञानतत्त्वपरो नित्यं शुभाशुभनिदर्शकः ॥
data.md: The ascetic who wish to discriminate exactly between good and evil, who is always bent on conceiving the nature of the Soul, and who devotes himself to the religion of disinclination, attains to that high end.

data.v: तदेवमेतौ विज्ञेयावव्यक्तपुरुषावुभौ । अव्यक्तपुरुषाभ्यां तु यत्स्यादन्यन्महत्तरम् ॥
data.md: One who wishes to accomplish this, should know both the Unmanifest and Purusha of which I shall speak now. That, again, which is different from both the Unmanifest and Purusha, and which transcends them both, and which is distinguished from all beings, should be particularly seen by an intelligent man. Both, Prakriti and Purusha are without beginning and without end. Both are incapable of being known by their likes.

data.v: तं विशेषमवेक्षेत विशेषेण विचक्षणः । अनाद्यन्तावुभावेतावलिङ्गौ चाप्युभावपि ॥
data.md: One who wishes to accomplish this, should know both the Unmanifest and Purusha of which I shall speak now. That, again, which is different from both the Unmanifest and Purusha, and which transcends them both, and which is distinguished from all beings, should be particularly seen by an intelligent man. Both, Prakriti and Purusha are without beginning and without end. Both are incapable of being known by their likes.

data.v: उभौ नित्यौ सूक्ष्मतरौ महद्भ्यश्च महत्तरौ । सामान्यमेतदुभयोरेवं ह्यन्यद्विशेषणम् ॥
data.md: Both are eternal and indestructible. Both are greater than the greatest. They are similar in these. There are point of dissimilarity again between them.

data.v: प्रकृत्या सर्गधर्मिण्या तथा त्रिविधसत्त्वया । विपरीतमतो विद्यात्क्षेत्रज्ञस्य च लक्षणम् ॥
data.md: Prakriti is endued with the three qualities. It is also engaged in creation. The true attributes of Kshetrajna (Purusha or the Soul) are different.

data.v: प्रकृतेश्च विकाराणां द्रष्टारमगुणान्वितम् । अग्राह्यौ पुरुषावेतावलिङ्गत्वादसंहितौ ॥
data.md: Purusha apprehends all the changes of Prakriti (but cannot be apprehended himself.) He transcends all qualities. As regards Purusha and the Supreme Soul again, both of them cannot be comprehended. Again for their both being without qualities by which they can be distinguished, both are greatly distinguished froin all else.

data.v: संयोगलक्षणोत्पत्तिः कर्मजा गृह्यते यया । करणैः कर्मनिर्वृत्तैः कर्ता यद्यद्विचेष्टते । कीर्त्यते शब्दसंज्ञाभिः कोऽहमेषोऽप्यसाविति ॥
data.md: The creation is the result of relation between Prakriti and Purusha (the soul), but we understand it by action. All movements come through the senses by person. "Who, I, This" etc. are only wordily statements.

data.v: उष्णीषवान्यथा वस्त्रैस्त्रिभिर्भवति संवृतः । संवृतोऽयं तथा देही सत्त्वराजसतामसैः ॥
data.md: A person putting on a turban has his head circled with three folds of a piece of cloth. Similarly the embodied Soul is invested with the three qualities of Goodness, and Ignorance. But though thus invested, the Soul is not identical with those qualities.

data.v: तस्माच्चतुष्टयं वेद्यमेतैर्हेतुभिराचितम् । यथासंज्ञो ह्ययं सम्यगन्तकाले न मुह्यति ॥
data.md: Hence these four topics, which are covered by these four considerations, should be understood. One who understands all this is never stupefied when he tries to form conclusions.

data.v: श्रियं दिव्यामभिप्रेप्सुर्ब्रह्म वाङ्मनसा शुचिः । शारीरैर्नियमैरुग्रैश्चरेन्निष्कल्मषं तपः ॥
data.md: He who wishes to secure high prosperity should become pure in mind, and practising austere practices regarding the body and the senses, should devote himself to yoga without seeking for fruits.

data.v: त्रैलोक्यं तपसा व्याप्तमन्तर्भूतेन भास्वता । सूर्यश्च चन्द्रमाश्चैव भासतस्तपसा दिवि ॥
data.md: The universe is permeated by yoga power secretly passing through every part of it and lighting it up brightly. The sun and the moon shine in the sky of the heart on account of yoga power.

data.v: प्रतापस्तपसो ज्ञानं लोके संशब्दितं तपः । रजस्तमोघ्नं यत्कर्म तपसस्तत्स्वलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: The result of yoga is Knowledge. Yoga is spoken of highly in the world. Whatever acts destroy Darkness and Ignorance form yoga of the in respect of its real character.

data.v: ब्रह्मचर्यमहिंसा च शारीरं तप उच्यते । वाङ्मनोनियमः साम्यं मानसं तप उच्यते ॥
data.md: Brahmacharya and abstention from injury form yoga of the body; while restraining of mind and words form yoga of the mind.

data.v: विधिज्ञेभ्यो द्विजातिभ्यो ग्राह्यमन्नं विशिष्यते । आहारनियमेनास्य पाप्मा नश्यति राजसः ॥
data.md: The food which is acquired by begging from twice-born persons conversant with the ritual is distinguished from all other food. By taking that food abstemiously, one's sins begotten of Darkness are dissipated.

data.v: वैमनस्यं च विषये यान्त्यस्य करणानि च । तस्मात्तन्मात्रमादद्याद्यावदत्र प्रयोजनम् ॥
data.md: Living upon such food a Yogin finds his senses gradually withdrawn from their objects. Hence, he should take only that quality of food which is barely necessary for the support of his body.

data.v: अन्तकाले वयोत्कर्षाच्छनैः कुर्यादनातुरः । एवं युक्तेन मनसा ज्ञानं तदुपपद्यते ॥
data.md: Knowledge which one acquires gradually by mind devoted to yoga should be made one's own on the verge of death by a forcible stretch of power.

data.v: रजसा चाप्ययं देही देहवाञ्शब्दवच्चरेत् । कार्यैरव्याहतमतिर्वैराग्यात्प्रकृतौ स्थितः । आ देहादप्रमादाच्च देहान्ताद्विप्रमुच्यते ॥
data.md: The embodied Soul, when divested of Darkness, assumes a subtile form with all the senses of perception and moves about in space. When his mind becomes untouched by acts, he, on account of such renunciation, becomes merged in Prakriti.

data.v: हेतुयुक्तः सदोत्सर्गो भूतानां प्रलयस्तथा । परप्रत्ययसर्गे तु नियतं नातिवर्तते ॥
भवान्तप्रभवप्रज्ञा आसते ये विपर्ययम् । धृत्या देहान्धारयन्तो बुद्धिसंक्षिप्तमानसाः । स्थानेभ्यो ध्वंसमानाश्च सूक्ष्मत्वात्तानुपासते ॥
data.md: Keeping their bodies by the help of patience, withdrawing their hearts by the help of their understanding, and withdrawing are men themselves from the world of senses, some Yogins worship the senses for their subtility.

data.v: यथागमं च तत्सर्वं बुद्ध्या तन्नैव बुध्यते । देहान्तं कश्चिदन्वास्ते भावितात्मा निराश्रयः । युक्तो धारणया कश्चित्सत्तां केचिदुपासते ॥
data.md: Some of them, with mind purified by yoga, proceeding according to the scriptures and reaching the highest, succeed in knowing it by help of the understanding and live in that which is the highest and which without resting on any other thing rests on itself.

data.v: अभ्यस्यन्ति परं देवं विद्युत्संशब्दिताक्षरम् । अन्तकाले ह्युपासन्नास्तपसा दग्धकिल्बिषाः ॥
सर्व एते महात्मानो गच्छन्ति परमां गतिम् । सूक्ष्मं विशेषणं तेषामवेक्षेच्छास्त्रचक्षुषा ॥
देहं तु परमं विद्याद्विमुक्तमपरिग्रहम् । अन्तरिक्षादन्यतरं धारणासक्तमानसम् ॥
data.md: With the eye of scriptures one should mark the subtile attributes of these several forms, as distinguished by attributes, of Brahma that are adored by men. The Yogin who has gone above the necessity, as the Supreme Divinity, or as that which is Unmanifest.

data.v: मर्त्यलोकाद्विमुच्यन्ते विद्यासंयुक्तमानसाः । ब्रह्मभूता विरजसस्ततो यान्ति परां गतिम् ॥
data.md: They whose hearts are given to the acquisition of knowledge succeed first in disassociating themselves for the world of mortals. Afterwards, by renouncing attachments they partake of the nature of Brahma and at last attain to the highest end.

data.v: कषायवर्जितं ज्ञानं येषामुत्पद्यतेऽचलम् । ते यान्ति परमाँल्लोकान्विशुध्यन्तो यथाबलम् ॥
data.md: Those persons who can acquire a knowledge which is incapable of being shaken and which makes its possessors shorn of all sorts of attachments acquire different high regions after death and become emancipate according to the extent of their knowledge.

data.v: भगवन्तमजं दिव्यं विष्णुमव्यक्तसंज्ञितम् । भावेन यान्ति शुद्धा ये ज्ञानतृप्ता निराशिषः ॥
data.md: Those pure-hearted persons who have acquired contentment from knowledge, and who have contentment from knowledge, and who have renounced all desires and attachments, gradually approach in respect of their nature nearer Brahma which is unmanifest by nature, which is divine, and without birth and death.

data.v: ज्ञात्वात्मस्थं हरिं चैव निवर्तन्ते न तेऽव्ययाः । प्राप्य तत्परमं स्थानं मोदन्तेऽक्षरमव्ययम् ॥
data.md: Realising that Brahma lives in their souls, they become themselves immutable and have never to come back to the Earth). Acquiring that supreme, indestructible and eternal state they live in happiness.

data.v: एतावदेतद्विज्ञानमेतदस्ति च नास्ति च । तृष्णाबद्धं जगत्सर्वं चक्रवत्परिवर्तते ॥
data.md: The knowledge of this world is this: (Persons who have overcome ignorance think that) it does not exist. The whole universe, feltered by desire, is revolving like a wheel.

data.v: बिसतन्तुर्यथैवायमन्तःस्थः सर्वतो बिसे । तृष्णातन्तुरनाद्यन्तस्तथा देहगतः सदा ॥
data.md: As the fibres of a lotus-stalk overspread themselves into every part of the stalk, likewise the fibres of desire, which are without beginning or end, spread themselves over every part of the body.

data.v: सूच्या सूत्रं यथा वस्त्रे संसारयति वायकः । तद्वत्संसारसूत्रं हि तृष्णासूच्या निबध्यते ॥
data.md: As a weaver drives his threads into a cloth by means of his shuttle, similarly the threads that constitute the fabric of the universe are woven by the shuttle of Desire.

data.v: विकारं प्रकृतिं चैव पुरुषं च सनातनम् । यो यथावद्विजानाति स वितृष्णो विमुच्यते ॥
data.md: He who understands the changes of Nature, Nature herself, and Purusha, becomes freed from Desire and acquires Liberation.

data.v: प्रकाशं भगवानेतदृषिर्नारायणोऽमृतम् । भूतानामनुकम्पार्थं जगाद जगतो हितम् ॥
data.md: The divine Rishi Narayana, that refuge of the universe, for the sake of mercy towards all creatures, distinctly laid down these means for the acquisition of immortality.

data.v: केन वृत्तेन वृत्तज्ञो जनको मिथिलाधिपः । जगाम मोक्षं धर्मज्ञो भोगानुत्सृज्य मानुषान् ॥
data.md: By acting how, O you who are conversant with all courses of conduct, did Janaka the king of Mithila, versed in the religion of Liberation, succeed in acquiring Liberation, after casting off all worldly enjoyments?

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । येन वृत्तेन वृत्तज्ञः स जगाम महत्सुखम् ॥
data.md: “Regarding it is cited the following old narrative of the particular conduct by which that king, a master of all courses of conduct, succeeded in acquiring the highest happiness.

data.v: जनको जनदेवस्तु मिथिलायां जनाधिपः । और्ध्वदेहिकधर्माणामासीद्युक्तो विचिन्तने ॥
data.md: There was a king in Mithila of the name of Janadeva of Janaka's race. He was ever engaged in thinking of the courses of conduct that might lead to the attainment of Brahma.

data.v: तस्य स्म शतमाचार्या वसन्ति सततं गृहे । दर्शयन्तः पृथग्धर्मान्नानापाषण्डवादिनः ॥
data.md: One hundred preceptors always used to live in his palace, describing to him the various courses of duty followed by people who had adopted the various modes of life.

data.v: स तेषां प्रेत्यभावे च प्रेत्यजातौ विनिश्चये । आगमस्थः स भूयिष्ठमात्मतत्त्वे न तुष्यति ॥
data.md: Well read in the Vedas, he was not very well satisfied with the speculations of his instructors on the nature of the Soul, and in their teachings of his extinction upon the dissolution of the body or of re-birth after death.

data.v: तत्र पञ्चशिखो नाम कापिलेयो महामुनिः । परिधावन्महीं कृत्स्नां जगाम मिथिलामपि ॥
data.md: Once upon a time a great ascetic named Panchashikha the son of Kapila, having roamed over the whole world, arrived at Mithila.

data.v: सर्वसंन्यासधर्माणां तत्त्वज्ञानविनिश्चये । सुपर्यवसितार्थश्च निर्द्वंद्वो नष्टसंशयः ॥
data.md: Having made conclusions about the diverse duties connected with renunciation, he was above all pairs of opposites, and had no doubts.

data.v: ऋषीणामाहुरेकं यं कामादवसितं नृषु । शाश्वतं सुखमत्यन्तमन्विच्छन्स सुदुर्लभम् ॥
data.md: He was considered as the foremost of Rishis. Living wherever he pleased, he wished to place before the reach of all men eternal happiness that is so difficult of attainment.

data.v: यमाहुः कपिलं सांख्याः परमर्षिं प्रजापतिम् । स मन्ये तेन रूपेण विस्मापयति हि स्वयम् ॥
data.md: It appeared that he roamed, amazing the world, having put on the form of none else then that great Rishi, that lord of creatures, whom the followers of the Sankhya doctrine knew by the name of Kapila.

data.v: आसुरेः प्रथमं शिष्यं यमाहुश्चिरजीविनम् । पञ्चस्रोतसि यः सत्रमास्ते वर्षसहस्रिकम् ॥
data.md: He was the greatest of all the disciples of Asuri and was called the undying. He had performed a mental Sacrifice lasting for a thousand years.

data.v: तं समासीनमागम्य मण्डलं कापिलं महत् । पुरुषावस्थमव्यक्तं परमार्थं निबोधयत् ॥
इष्टिसत्रेण संसिद्धो भूयश्च तपसा मुनिः । क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोर्व्यक्तिं बुबुधे देवदर्शनः ॥
data.md: For acquiring a knowledge of the Soul, Asuri had enquired of his preceptor. On account of the latter's instructions and of his own penances, Asuri understood the distinction between the body and the Soul and had gained celestial vision.

data.v: यत्तदेकाक्षरं ब्रह्म नानारूपं प्रदृश्यते । आसुरिर्मण्डले तस्मिन्प्रतिपेदे तदव्ययम् ॥
data.md: In that assembly of ascetics, Asuri described the Immutable, One, and Indestructible Brahma which is seen in various forms.

data.v: तस्य पञ्चशिखः शिष्यो मानुष्या पयसा भृतः । ब्राह्मणी कपिला नाम काचिदासीत्कुटुम्बिनी ॥
data.md: Panchashikha became a disciple of Asuri. He lived on human milk. There was a certain Brahman lady named Kapila. She was Asuri's wife.

data.v: तस्याः पुत्रत्वमागम्य स्त्रियाः स पिबति स्तनौ । ततः स कापिलेयत्वं लेभे बुद्धिं च नैष्ठिकीम् ॥
data.md: Panchashikha was accepted by her as a son and he used to suck her breasts. For this, he came to be known as the son of Kapila and his understanding became fixed on Brahma.

data.v: एतन्मे भगवानाह कापिलेयाय संभवम् । तस्य तत्कापिलेयत्वं सर्ववित्त्वमनुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: The divine Rishi said to me, all this, regarding the circumstances of his birth and those about his becoming the son of Kapila. The latter also told me about the omniscience of Panchashikha.

data.v: सामान्यं कपिलो ज्ञात्वा धर्मज्ञानामनुत्तमम् । उपेत्य शतमाचार्यान्मोहयामास हेतुभिः ॥
data.md: Knowing fully all the forms of duty, Panchashikha, after having himself gained high knowledge, (came to Janaka) and knowing that that king had equal reverence for all his preceptors, began to startle those hundred preceptors (by a very sensible exposition of his doctrine).

data.v: जनकस्त्वभिसंरक्तः कापिलेयानुदर्शनात् । उत्सृज्य शतमाचार्यान्पृष्ठतोऽनुजगाम तम् ॥
data.md: Marking the genius of the son of Kapila, Janaka became exceedingly attacked to him, and abandoning his hundred preceptors, began to follow him.

data.v: तस्मै परमकल्याय प्रणताय च धर्मतः । अब्रवीत्परमं मोक्षं यत्तत्सांख्यं विधीयते ॥
data.md: Then Kapila's son began to discourse to Janaka, who had according to the ordinance bent his head to him and who was fully competent to understand the sage's instructions, upon that great religion of Liberation which is explained in Sankhya treatises.

data.v: जातिनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा हि कर्मनिर्वेदमब्रवीत् । कर्मनिर्वेदमुक्त्वा च सर्वनिर्वेदमब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Describing first of all the miseries of birth, he spoke next of the miseries of (religious) acts. Having finished that topic he explained the miseries of all states of existence ending even with that in the high region of the Creator.

data.v: यदर्थं कर्मसंसर्गः कर्मणां च फलोदयः । तदनाश्वासिकं मोघं विनाशि चलमध्रुवम् ॥
data.md: He also described that Delusion which beget the practice of religion, and acts, and their fruits, and which is highly untrustworthy, destructible, unsteady, and uncertain.

data.v: दृश्यमाने विनाशे च प्रत्यक्षे लोकसाक्षिके । आगमात्परमस्तीति ब्रुवन्नपि पराजितः ॥
data.md: Sceptics say that when death is seen directly by all, they who hold, on account of their faith in the scriptures, that something distinct from the body, called the Soul, exists, are necessarily defeated in argument.

data.v: अनात्मा ह्यात्मनो मृत्युः क्लेशो मृत्युर्जरामयः । आत्मानं मन्यते मोहात्तदसम्यक्परं मतम् ॥
data.md: They also hold that one's Soul, and that sorrow, decrepitude, and disease indicate (partial) death of the Soul. He who holds owing to error, that the Soul is distinct from the body and exists after the loss of body, entertains an unreasonable opinion.

data.v: अथ चेदेवमप्यस्ति यल्लोके नोपपद्यते । अजरोऽयममृत्युश्च राजासौ मन्यते तथा ॥
data.md: If that is considered as existent which does not really exist in the world, then it may be mentioned that the king, being known so, is really never subject to decrepitude or death. But is he, therefore, to be really believed to be beyond decrepitude and death?

data.v: अस्ति नास्तीति चाप्येतत्तस्मिन्नसति लक्षणे । किमधिष्ठाय तद्ब्रूयाल्लोकयात्राविनिश्चयम् ॥
data.md: When the question arises whether an object exists or not, and when that whose existence in asserted presents all the signs of non-existence, what is that upon which ordinary people depend in settling the affairs of life?

data.v: प्रत्यक्षं ह्येतयोर्मूलं कृतान्तैतिह्ययोरपि । प्रत्यक्षो ह्यागमोऽभिन्नः कृतान्तो वा न किंचन ॥
data.md: Direct evidence is the basis of both inference and the scriptures. The scriptures can be contradicted by direct evidence. As to inference its evidence is not much.

data.v: यत्र तत्रानुमानेऽस्ति कृतं भावयतेऽपि वा । अन्यो जीवः शरीरस्य नास्तिकानां मते स्मृतः ॥
data.md: Do not reason on inference only whatever may be the subject. There is nothing else called individual soul than this body.

data.v: रेतो वटकणीकायां घृतपाकाधिवासनम् । जातिस्मृतिरयस्कान्तः सूर्यकान्तोऽम्बुभक्षणम् ॥
data.md: The capacity to produce leaves, flowers, fruits, roots and bark lies in a banian seed. The grass and water that is taken by a cow produce milk and butter, substances differing in nature from that of the causes. Various substances when allowed to decompose in water for sometime produce spirituous liquors whose nature is quite different from that of those substances producing them. Likewise, from the vital seed in produced the body and its attributes with the understanding, consciousness, wood, and other qualities. Two pieces of wood, rubbed together, beget fire. Coming in contact with the rays of the Sun, the stone called Suryakanta begets fire. Any solid metal, heated in fire, dries up water when coming in contact with it. Likewise, the material body produces the mind and its attributes of perception, memory, imagination, etc. As the loadstone moves iron, likewise the . senses are controlled by the mind.

data.v: प्रेत्य भूतात्ययश्चैव देवताभ्युपयाचनम् । मृते कर्मनिवृत्तिश्च प्रमाणमिति निश्चयः ॥
data.md: Thus do the sceptics reason, who are, however, mistaken. The disappearance (of animation) upon the body becoming lifeless means death. The supplication of the gods by the very men who deny the separate existence of the Soul is another good argument (for the proposition that the Soul is separate from the body). Another argument against the sceptic is that his proposition argues a destruction of acts.

data.v: न त्वेते हेतवः सन्ति ये केचिन्मूर्तिसंस्थिताः । अमर्त्यस्य हि मर्त्येन सामान्यं नोपपद्यते ॥
data.md: These that have been mentioned and have material forms, cannot possible be the causes (of the immaterial Soul and its immaterial accompaniments). The identity of immaterial things with objects that are material cannot be comprehended.

data.v: अविद्याकर्मचेष्टानां केचिदाहुः पुनर्भवम् । कारणं लोभमोहौ तु दोषाणां च निषेवणम् ॥
data.md: Some hold that there is re-birth which is caused by Ignorance, the desire for acts, cupidity, carelessness, and bent towards other vices.

data.v: अविद्यां क्षेत्रमाहुर्हि कर्म बीजं तथा कृतम् । तृष्णासंजननं स्नेह एष तेषां पुनर्भवः ॥
data.md: They say that Ignorance is the soil. Acts form the seed that is placed in that soil. Desire is the water that causes that seed to grow. In this manner they explained re-birth.

data.v: तस्मिन्व्यूढे च दग्धे च चित्ते मरणधर्मिणि । अन्योऽन्याज्जायते देहस्तमाहुः सत्त्वसंक्षयम् ॥
data.md: They hold that ignorance being ingrained in an imperceptible way, one mortal body being destroyed, another originates at once from it; and that when it is consumed by the help of knowledge, the destruction of existence itself follows, or the person attains to what is called annihilation.

data.v: यदा स रूपतश्चान्यो जातितः श्रुतितोऽर्थतः । कथमस्मिन्स इत्येव संबन्धः स्यादसंहितः ॥
data.md: This opinion also is mistaken, It may be asked that when the being that is thus re-bom is a different one in its nature, birth, and objects of virtue and vice, why should it then be considered to be identical with the being that was? Indeed, the only inference that can be made is that the entire chain of existences of a particular being is not really one of connected links.

data.v: एवं सति च का प्रीतिर्दानविद्यातपोबलैः । यदन्याचरितं कर्म सर्वमन्यः प्रपद्यते ॥
data.md: Then, again, if the being that is the outcome of a re-birth be really different from what it was in a pristine existence, it may be asked what satisfaction is to a person from the exercise of the spirit of charity, or from the acquisition of knowledge or of ascetic power, since the acts perforined by one are to bear fruits upon another person in another state of existence.

data.v: यदा ह्ययमिहैवान्यैः प्राकृतैर्दुःखितो भवेत् । सुखितैर्दुःखितैर्वापि दृश्योऽप्यस्य विनिर्णयः ॥
data.md: Another refutation of the doctrine would be that one in this life may rendered miserable by the acts of another in a pristine life, or having become miserable may again become happy. By witnessing however, what actually takes place in the world, a proper conclusion may be drawn regarding the unseen.

data.v: तथा हि मुसलैर्हन्युः शरीरं तत्पुनर्भवेत् । पृथग्ज्ञानं यदन्यच्च येनैतन्नोपलभ्यते ॥
data.md: The separate Consciousness that is the outcome of re-birth is different from the Consciousness that had preceded it in a pristine existence. The way, however, in which the appearance of that separate Consciousness is explained by that theory is not at all consistent or reasonable. The Consciousness was the very opposite of eternal, being only transitory, extending as it did till dissolution of the body. That which had an end cannot be considered as the cause for the production of a second Consciousness appearing after the end. If again, the very very loss of of the previous Consciousness be considered as the cause of the production of the second Consciousness, then when the death of a human body is caused by a heavy bludgeon, a second body would originate from the body that is thus deprived of animation.

data.v: ऋतुः संवत्सरस्तिथ्यः शीतोष्णे च प्रियाप्रिये । यथातीतानि पश्यन्ति तादृशः सत्त्वसंक्षयः ॥
data.md: Again, their doctrine of annihilation is subject to the objection that extinction will become a revolving phenomenon like that of the seasons, or the year, or the Yuga, or heat, or cold, or agreeable or disagreeable objects.

data.v: जरया हि परीतस्य मृत्युना वा विनाशिना । दुर्बलं दुर्बलं पूर्वं गृहस्येव विनश्यति ॥
data.md: If for avoiding these objections, the followers of this doctrine hold the existence of a Soul that is permanent and with which cach new Consciousness is attached, they again subject themselves to the new objection that that permanent substance, by being overcome with decrepitude, and with death that causes destruction, may in time be itself weakened and destroyed. If the supports of a palace are weakened by time, the mansion itself is sure to fall down in the end.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणि मनो वायुः शोणितं मांसमस्थि च । आनुपूर्व्या विनश्यन्ति स्वं धातुमुपयान्ति च ॥
data.md: The senses, the mind, wind, blood, flesh, bones, one after another, meet with destruction and enter each into its own productive causes.

data.v: लोकयात्राविधानं च दानधर्मफलागमः । यदर्थं वेदशब्दाश्च व्यवहाराश्च लौकिकाः ॥
data.md: If again the existence of an eternal Soul is held which is immutable, which is the refuge of the understanding, consciousness, and other similar attributes, and which is dissociated from all these, such an assertion is subject to a serious objection for then all that is usually done in the world would be meaningless, especially with reference to the attaininent of the fruits of charity and other religious acts. All the injunctions in the Shrutis regarding those acts, and all acts connected with the conduct of in the world, would be equally men meaningless, for the Soul being dissociated form, the understanding and the mind, there is no one to enjoy the fruits of good acts and Vedic rites.

data.v: इति सम्यङ्मनस्येते बहवः सन्ति हेतवः । एतदस्तीदमस्तीति न किंचित्प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Thus various sorts of speculations arise in the mind. Nothing can settle whether this opinion is right or that is right.

data.v: तेषां विमृशतामेवं तत्तत्समभिधावताम् । क्वचिन्निविशते बुद्धिस्तत्र जीर्यति वृक्षवत् ॥
data.md: Reflecting on these opinions, particular persons follow particular lines of speculation. The understanding of these, directed to particular theories become immersed and are at last entirely lost in them.

data.v: एवमर्थैरनर्थैश्च दुःखिताः सर्वजन्तवः । आगमैरपकृष्यन्ते हस्तिपैर्हस्तिनो यथा ॥
data.md: Thus all men are made miserable by pursuits good or bad. Bringing them back to the right path, the Vedas alone, guide them along it, like grooms conducting their elephants.

data.v: अर्थांस्तथात्यन्तसुखावहांश्च; लिप्सन्त एते बहवो विशुल्काः । महत्तरं दुःखमभिप्रपन्ना; हित्वामिषं मृत्युवशं प्रयान्ति ॥
data.md: Many men, with weakened minds, seek objects of great happiness. These, however, have soon to meet with a larger quantity of SOITow, and then, alienated by force from their coveted mcat, they subject themselves to the sway of death.

data.v: विनाशिनो ह्यध्रुवजीवितस्य; किं बन्धुभिर्मित्रपरिग्रहैश्च । विहाय यो गच्छति सर्वमेव; क्षणेन गत्वा न निवर्तते च ॥
data.md: What has one, who is subject to destruction and whose life is fickle, to do with kinsmen and friends and wives and other like possessions? He who meets death after having relinquished all these, passes easily out of the world and has never to return.

data.v: भूव्योमतोयानलवायवो हि; सदा शरीरं परिपालयन्ति । इतीदमालक्ष्य कुतो रतिर्भवे;द्विनाशिनो ह्यस्य न शर्म विद्यते ॥
इदमनुपधि वाक्यमच्छलं; परमनिरामयमात्मसाक्षिकम् । नरपतिरभिवीक्ष्य विस्मितः; पुनरनुयोक्तुमिदं प्रचक्रमे ॥
जनको जनदेवस्तु ज्ञापितः परमर्षिणा । पुनरेवानुपप्रच्छ सांपराये भवाभवौ ॥
data.md: Bhishma said "Thus instructed by the great Rishi Panchashikha, Janadeva of the family of Janaka, once more asked him about the subject of existence or non-existence after death.

data.v: भगवन्यदिदं प्रेत्य संज्ञा भवति कस्यचित् । एवं सति किमज्ञानं ज्ञानं वा किं करिष्यति ॥
data.md: O illustrious one, if no person, retains any knowledge after departing from this state of existence, if, indeed, this is true, what then is the difference between Ignorance and Knowledge? What do we gain then by knowledge and what do we lose by ignorance?

data.v: सर्वमुच्छेदनिष्ठं स्यात्पश्य चैतद्द्विजोत्तम । अप्रमत्तः प्रमत्तो वा किं विशेषं करिष्यति ॥
data.md: See, O foremost of the twice-born, that if liberation be such, then all religious acts and vows terminate only in annihilation? Of what use would then the distinction be between heedfulness and heedlessness.

data.v: असंसर्गो हि भूतेषु संसर्गो वा विनाशिषु । कस्मै क्रियेत कल्पेन निश्चयः कोऽत्र तत्त्वतः ॥
data.md: If Liberation means dissociation from all objects of pleasure or an association with objects that are not lasting, why should then men cherish a desire for action or having set themselves to action, continue to find out the necessary means for the accomplishment of desired ends? What then is the truth.

data.v: तमसा हि प्रतिच्छन्नं विभ्रान्तमिव चातुरम् । पुनः प्रशमयन्वाक्यैः कविः पञ्चशिखोऽब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Seeing the king enveloped in thick darkness, stupefied by error, and become helpless, the learned Panchashikha put his mind at rest by once more addressing him thus.

data.v: उच्छेदनिष्ठा नेहास्ति भावनिष्ठा न विद्यते । अयं ह्यपि समाहारः शरीरेन्द्रियचेतसाम् । वर्तते पृथगन्योन्यमप्यपाश्रित्य कर्मसु ॥
data.md: In Liberation the consummation is not Extinction. Nur is that consummation any kind of Existence. What we see is a union of body senses, and mind. Existing independently as also depending on one another, these go on acting.

data.v: धातवः पञ्चशाखोऽयं खं वायुर्ज्योतिरम्बु भूः । ते स्वभावेन तिष्ठन्ति वियुज्यन्ते स्वभावतः ॥
data.md: The ingredients that form the body are water, ether, wind, heat, and earth. These exisi together according to their own nature. They become separated again according to their own nature.

data.v: आकाशं वायुरूष्मा च स्नेहो यच्चापि पार्थिवम् । एष पञ्चसमाहारः शरीरमिति नैकधा । ज्ञानमूष्मा च वायुश्च त्रिविधः कर्मसंग्रहः ॥
data.md: Ether, wind, heat, water and earth,-these five objects in a state of union form the body. The body is not one element.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थाश्च स्वभावश्चेतना मनः । प्राणापानौ विकारश्च धातवश्चात्र निःसृताः ॥
data.md: Intelligence, stomachic heat, and the vital airs, called Prana, etc., that are all wind, three are the organs of action. The senses, the objects of the senses, the power by which they become capable of being perceived the faculties by which they succeed in perceiving them, the mind, the vital airs called Prana. Apana and the rest, and the various juices and humours that are the results of the digestive organs, flow from the three organs already named.

data.v: श्रवणं स्पर्शनं जिह्वा दृष्टिर्नासा तथैव च । इन्द्रियाणीति पञ्चैते चित्तपूर्वंगमा गुणाः ॥
data.md: Hearing, touch, taste, vision, and scent,-these are the five senses. They have derived their attributes from the mind which is their cause.

data.md: In the act of hearing, three causes must exist simultaneously, viz., the two ears, sound, and the mind. The same is the case with the perception of touch; the same with that of form; the same with that of taste and smell.

data.v: एवं पञ्चत्रिका ह्येते गुणास्तदुपलब्धये । येन यस्त्रिविधो भावः पर्यायात्समुपस्थितः ॥
data.md: These fifteen attributes are necessary for the several kinds of perception. In consequence of them, every man becomes conscious of three separate things regarding those perceptions.

data.v: सात्त्विको राजसश्चैव तामसश्चैव ते त्रयः । त्रिविधा वेदना येषु प्रसूता सर्वसाधना ॥
data.md: There are again three classes (of mental perception, viz., those that appertain to Goodness, those that belong of Darkness, and those that belong to Ignorance. With them are connected three kinds of consciousness, including all feelings and emotions.

data.v: प्रहर्षः प्रीतिरानन्दः सुखं संशान्तचित्तता । अकुतश्चित्कुतश्चिद्वा चित्ततः सात्त्विको गुणः ॥
data.md: Pleasure, satisfaction, joy, happiness, and tranquillity, originating in the mind from any perceptible cause or in the absence of any apparent cause, appertain to the quality of Goodness.

data.v: अतुष्टिः परितापश्च शोको लोभस्तथाक्षमा । लिङ्गानि रजसस्तानि दृश्यन्ते हेत्वहेतुतः ॥
data.md: Discontent, regret, grief, cupidity, and vindictiveness, having no cause or occasioned by any perceptible cause, are the marks of the quality of Darkness.

data.v: अविवेकस्तथा मोहः प्रमादः स्वप्नतन्द्रिता । कथंचिदपि वर्तन्ते विविधास्तामसा गुणाः ॥
data.md: Wrong judgement, stupefaction, carelessness, dreams, and sleepiness, however, caused, appertain to the quality of Ignorance.

data.v: तत्र यत्प्रीतिसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत् । वर्तते सात्त्विको भाव इत्यपेक्षेत तत्तथा ॥
data.md: Whatever state of consciousness exists, regarding either the body or the mind, united with joy or satisfaction, should be considered as due to the quality of Goodness.

data.v: यत्तु संतापसंयुक्तमप्रीतिकरमात्मनः । प्रवृत्तं रज इत्येव ततस्तदभिचिन्तयेत् ॥
data.md: Whatever state of consciousness exists united with any feeling of discontent or depression should be considered as the outcome of the quality of Darkness.

data.v: अथ यन्मोहसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत् । अप्रतर्क्यमविज्ञेयं तमस्तदुपधारयेत् ॥
data.md: Whatever state, of the body or the body or the mind, exists with error or carelessness, is the outcome of Ignorance which is incomprehensible and inexplicable.

data.md: The organ of hearing rests on either; it is either itself (under limitations); Sound has that organ for its refuge. In perceiving sound, one may not immediately acquire a knowledge of the organ of hearing and of ether. But when sound is perceived, the organ of hearing and ether do not long remain unknown.

data.v: एवं त्वक्चक्षुषी जिह्वा नासिका चैव पञ्चमी । स्पर्शे रूपे रसे गन्धे तानि चेतो मनश्च तत् ॥
data.md: The same is the case with the skin, the eyes, the tongue, and the nose forming the fifth. They exist in touch, form, taste, and smell. They form the faculty of perception and they are the mind.

data.v: स्वकर्मयुगपद्भावो दशस्वेतेषु तिष्ठति । चित्तमेकादशं विद्धि बुद्धिर्द्वादशमी भवेत् ॥
data.md: Each doing its own particular function, all the five organs of action and the five others of knowledge exist simultaneously, and upon the union of the ten dwells the mind as the eleventh and upon the mind the understanding as the twelfth.

data.v: तेषामयुगपद्भाव उच्छेदो नास्ति तामसः । आस्थितो युगपद्भावे व्यवहारः स लौकिकः ॥
data.md: It is be said that these twelve do not exist simultaneously, then the consequence would be that there would be death in dreamless sleep. But as there is no death in dreamless sleep, it must be admitted that these twelve exist simultaneously as regards themselves but of past separately from the Soul. The co-existence of those twelve with the Soul that is ordinarily spoken is only a common form of speech with the vulgar for ordinary purposes of the world.

data.v: इन्द्रियाण्यवसृज्यापि दृष्ट्वा पूर्वं श्रुतागमम् । चिन्तयन्नानुपर्येति त्रिभिरेवान्वितो गुणैः ॥
data.md: The dreamer, on account of the appearance sensual impressions, becomes conscious of his senses in their subtile forms, and endued as he already is with the three qualities, he considers his senses as existing with their respective objects and, therefore, acts and moves about with an imaginary body after the manner of his own self while awake.

data.v: यत्तमोपहतं चित्तमाशु संचारमध्रुवम् । करोत्युपरमं काले तदाहुस्तामसं सुखम् ॥
data.md: That dissociation of the Soul from the understanding and the mind with the senses, which speedily disappears, which has no stability, and which the mind causes to arise only when influenced by Ignorance is happiness that partakes as the learned say, of the nature of Ignorance and is experienced in this gross body only.

data.v: यद्यदागमसंयुक्तं न कृत्स्नमुपशाम्यति । अथ तत्राप्युपादत्ते तमो व्यक्तमिवानृतम् ॥
data.md: Over the felicity of Liberation also, the felicity, viz., which is created by the inspired teaching of Vedas and in which no one sees the slightest mark of sorrow,-the same indescribable and truth-concealing darkness seems to spread itself.

data.md: Like to what occurs in dreamless sleep, in liberation also, subjective and objective existences, which have their origin in one's : acts, are all discarded. data.md: When such is the case, and when all creatures, on account of the well-known cause, exist, due to a state of union between Soul and body, which of these two then is destructible and how can that which is said to be eternal, suffer destruction?

data.v: यथार्णवगता नद्यो व्यक्तीर्जहति नाम च । न च स्वतां नियच्छन्ति तादृशः सत्त्वसंक्षयः ॥
data.md: As small rivers falling into larger ones lose their forms and names, and the larger ones falling into the ocean lose their forms and names too, similarly called Liberation.

data.md: Likewise, the individual Soul which is characterised by qualities, is received into the Universal Soul, and when all its attributes disappear, how can it be differently mentioned?

data.v: क्षीणे च पुण्ये विगते च पापे; ततोनिमित्ते च फले विनष्टे । अलेपमाकाशमलिङ्गमेव;मास्थाय पश्यन्ति महद्ध्यसक्ताः ॥

data.md: As a bird leaves a tree that is about to fall down upon a water and sits on a (new) resting place, similarly similarly the person freed from attachinents renounces both joy and sorrow and dissociated even from his subtile and subtler forms attains to that end which is full of the highest prosperty.

data.md: Bhishma said The ancients who had there minds, directed to the Shrutis, spoke highly of the duty of selfcontrol for all the castes in general, but for the Brahmanas in especial.

data.v: नादान्तस्य क्रियासिद्धिर्यथावदुपलभ्यते । क्रिया तपश्च वेदाश्च दमे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
data.md: One who is not self-controlled never enjoys success in religious rites. Religious rites, penances, truth, all these depend upon selfcontrol.

data.v: दमस्तेजो वर्धयति पवित्रं दम उच्यते । विपाप्मा निर्भयो दान्तः पुरुषो विन्दते महत् ॥
data.md: Self-control increases one's energy. Self-। control is said to be sacred. The man of selfcontrol becomes sinless and fearless and acquires great results.

data.v: सुखं दान्तः प्रस्वपिति सुखं च प्रतिबुध्यते । सुखं लोके विपर्येति मनश्चास्य प्रसीदति ॥
data.md: One who is self-controlled sleeps happily and wakes happily. He lives happily in the world and his mind always remains cheerful

data.md: Every sort of excitement is quietly controlled by self-control. One who is not selfcontrolled fails in a similar endeavour. The self-controlled man sees his numberless focs (such as lust, desire, and anger, etc.') as if these dwell in a separate body.

data.v: क्रव्याद्भ्य इव भूतानामदान्तेभ्यः सदा भयम् । तेषां विप्रतिषेधार्थं राजा सृष्टः स्वयंभुवा ॥
data.md: Like tigers and other carnivorous animals, persons shorn of self-control always strike all creatures with fear. For controlling these men, the Self-create (Brahma) created kings.

data.v: आश्रमेषु च सर्वेषु दम एव विशिष्यते । यच्च तेषु फलं धर्मे भूयो दान्ते तदुच्यते ॥
data.md: In all the modes of life, the practice of selfcontrol is distinguished above all other virtues. The fruits of self-control are much greater than those obtainable in all the modes of life.

data.v: तेषां लिङ्गानि वक्ष्यामि येषां समुदयो दमः । अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः संतोषः श्रद्दधानता ॥
अक्रोध आर्जवं नित्यं नातिवादो न मानिता । गुरुपूजानसूया च दया भूतेष्वपैशुनम् ॥
जनवादमृषावादस्तुतिनिन्दाविवर्जनम् । साधुकामश्चास्पृहयन्नायाति प्रत्ययं नृषु ॥
अवैरकृत्सूपचारः समो निन्दाप्रशंसयोः । सुवृत्तः शीलसंपन्नः प्रसन्नात्मात्मवान्बुधः । प्राप्य लोके च सत्कारं स्वर्गं वै प्रेत्य गच्छति ॥
data.md: Shom of vindictiveness and all sorts of guile, and unaffected by praise and censure, such a man is well-behaved, has good manners is pure of soul, had fortitude, and is a complete master of his passions.

data.v: सर्वभूतहिते युक्तो न स्मयाद्द्वेष्टि वै जनम् । महाह्रद इवाक्षोभ्य प्रज्ञातृप्तः प्रसीदति ॥
data.md: Devoted to universal benevolence, such a man never feels animosity for any one. Tranquil like a calm ocean, wisdom feels his soul and he is ever cheerful.

data.v: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यः सर्वेषामभयं यतः । नमस्यः सर्वभूतानां दान्तो भवति ज्ञानवान् ॥
data.md: Endued with intelligence, and deserving of universal reverence, the self-controlled man never fears any creature and is feared by no creature in return.

data.v: न हृष्यति महत्यर्थे व्यसने च न शोचति । स वै परिमितप्रज्ञः स दान्तो द्विज उच्यते ॥
data.md: That man who never rejoices even at large accessions and never feels sorrow when overtaken by misfortune, is said to be endued with contented wisdom. Such a man is said to he self-controlled. Indeed, such a man is said to be a twice-born man.

data.v: कर्मभिः श्रुतसंपन्नः सद्भिराचरितैः शुभैः । सदैव दमसंयुक्तस्तस्य भुङ्क्ते महत्फलम् ॥
data.md: Well-read in the scriptures and gifted with a pure soul, the man of self-controi, performing all those acts that are done by the good, enjoys their high fruits.

data.v: अनसूया क्षमा शान्तिः संतोषः प्रियवादिता । सत्यं दानमनायासो नैष मार्गो दुरात्मनाम् ॥
data.md: The wicked men, however, never follow the path of benevolence, forgiveness, tranquillity, contentment, sweetness of speech, trutli, liberality, and comfort.

data.v: कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा ब्रह्मचारी जितेन्द्रियः । विक्रम्य घोरे तपसि ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः । कालाकाङ्क्षी चरेल्लोकान्निरपाय इवात्मवान् ॥
data.md: They follow the path of lust, anger, cupidity, envy of others, and boastfulness. Overcoming lust and anger, practising the vow of Brahmacharya and becoming a complete master of his senses, the Brahman practising patiently the austerest penances, and observing the most rigid restraints, should live in this world, calmly waiting for his time like one seeming to have a body through fully knowing that he is not subject to destruction.

data.v: द्विजातयो व्रतोपेता यदिदं भुञ्जते हविः । अन्नं ब्राह्मणकामाय कथमेतत्पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said The three twice-born classes, who perform sacrifices and other rites, some times eat the remnants, consisting of meat and wine, of sacrifices in honour of the gods, from motives of obtaining children and heaven. What, O grandfather, is the nature of this act?

data.v: अवेदोक्तव्रतोपेता भुञ्जानाः कार्यकारिणः । वेदोक्तेषु च भुञ्जाना व्रतलुप्ता युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Those who eat forbidden food without performing the sacrifices and vows ordained in the Vedas are known as wilful men. Those, on the other hand, who eat such food in the observance of Vedic sacrifices and vows and actuated by the desire of fruits in the shape of heaven and children, ascend to heaven but drop down on the termination of their merits.

data.v: यदिदं तप इत्याहुरुपवासं पृथग्जनाः । एतत्तपो महाराज उताहो किं तपो भवेत् ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Common people say that fasting is penance. Is fasting, however, really so, or is penance somethings different?

data.v: मासपक्षोपवासेन मन्यन्ते यत्तपो जनाः । आत्मतन्त्रोपघातः स न तपस्तत्सतां मतम् । त्यागश्च सन्नतिश्चैव शिष्यते तप उत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said People really consider fast, measured by months or fortnights or days, as penance. The good, however, hold that such is not penance. On the other hand, fast is an obstacle to the acquirement of the knowledge of the Soul.

data.v: सदोपवासी च भवेद्ब्रह्मचारी सदैव च । मुनिश्च स्यात्सदा विप्रो दैवतं च सदा भजेत् ॥
कुटुम्बिको धर्मकामः सदास्वप्नश्च भारत । अमांसाशी सदा च स्यात्पवित्रं च सदा जपेत् ॥
अमृताशी सदा च स्यान्न च स्याद्विषभोजनः । विघसाशी सदा च स्यात्सदा चैवातिथिप्रियः ॥
कथं सदोपवासी स्याद्ब्रह्मचारी कथं भवेत् । विघसाशी कथं च स्यात्सदा चैवातिथिप्रियः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said one ever How can one practising such penance come to be known as one who is always fasting or as who follows the VOW of Brahmacharya, or as one who always lives upon sacrificial residue, or as one who always worships guests.

data.v: अन्तरा प्रातराशं च सायमाशं तथैव च । सदोपवासी च भवेद्यो न भुङ्क्ते कथंचन ॥
data.md: Bhishma said He will be considered as one who is always fasting if he eats once during the day and once during the night at the fixed hours without eating anything in the interim.

data.v: भार्यां गच्छन्ब्रह्मचारी ऋतौ भवति ब्राह्मणः । ऋतवादी सदा च स्याज्ज्ञाननित्यश्च यो नरः ॥
data.md: Such a Brahman, by always speaking the truth and by following always wisdom, and by going to his wife only in her season and never at other times, becomes a Brahmacharin.

data.v: अभक्षयन्वृथामांसममांसाशी भवत्युत । दाननित्यः पवित्रश्च अस्वप्नश्च दिवास्वपन् ॥
data.md: By never cating meat of animals not killed for sacrifice, he will become a strict vegetarian. By always becoming charitable he will become ever pure, and by abstaining from sleep during De day he will become one who is always awake.

data.v: भृत्यातिथिषु यो भुङ्क्ते भुक्तवत्सु सदा स ह । अमृतं सकलं भुङ्क्त इति विद्धि युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Know, O Yudhisthira, that the man who eats only after having fed his servants and guests becomes an eater always of ambrosia.

data.v: अभुक्तवत्सु नाश्नानः सततं यस्तु वै द्विजः । अभोजनेन तेनास्य जितः स्वर्गो भवत्युत ॥
देवताभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च भृत्येभ्योऽतिथिभिः सह । अवशिष्टं तु योऽश्नाति तमाहुर्विघसाशिनम् ॥
data.md: He is said to live upon sacrificial residue who eats only what remains after feeding the gods, the Pitris, servants and guests.

data.v: तेषां लोका ह्यपर्यन्ताः सदने ब्रह्मणा सह । उपस्थिताश्चाप्सरोभिः परियान्ति दिवौकसः ॥
data.md: Such men acquires numberless blessed regions in next life. The gods and the Apsaras with Brahman himself, come to their homes.

data.v: देवताभिश्च ये सार्धं पितृभिश्चोपभुञ्जते । रमन्ते पुत्रपौत्रैश्च तेषां गतिरनुत्तमा ॥
data.md: They who share their food with the gods and the Pitris pass their days always happily with their sons and grandsons, and at last, leaving off this body, acquire a very high end.

data.v: यदिदं कर्म लोकेऽस्मिञ्शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् । पुरुषं योजयत्येव फलयोगेन भारत ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said In this world, O Bharata, good and bad acts attach themselves to man for the purpose of producing fruits for enjoyment or endurance.

data.v: कर्ता स्वित्तस्य पुरुष उताहो नेति संशयः । एतदिच्छामि तत्त्वेन त्वत्तः श्रोतुं पितामह ॥
data.md: Is man, however, to be regarded as their doer or is he not to be considered so? My mind is full of doubts regarding this question. I wish to hear this fully from you, O grandfather.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । प्रह्रादस्य च संवादमिन्द्रस्य च युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it, О Yudhisthira, is cited the old discourse between Prahlada and Indra.

data.v: असक्तं धूतपाप्मानं कुले जातं बहुश्रुतम् । अस्तम्भमनहंकारं सत्त्वस्थं समये रतम् ॥
तुल्यनिन्दास्तुतिं दान्तं शून्यागारनिवेशनम् । चराचराणां भूतानां विदितप्रभवाप्ययम् ॥
अक्रुध्यन्तमहृष्यन्तमप्रियेषु प्रियेषु च । काञ्चने वाथ लोष्टे वा उभयोः समदर्शनम् ॥
आत्मनिःश्रेयसज्ञाने धीरं निश्चितनिश्चयम् । परावरज्ञं भूतानां सर्वज्ञं समदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: Earnestly studying the Soul and acquiring Emancipation, and firm in knowledge, he had acquired firm conclusions about truth.

data.v: शक्रः प्रह्रादमासीनमेकान्ते संयतेन्द्रियम् । बुभुत्समानस्तत्प्रज्ञामभिगम्येदमब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Acquainted with what is supreme and what is not so among all things, omniscient and of universal sight, as he was seated on day in a solitary room with his senses under complete control, Shakra approached him, and desirous

data.v: यैः कैश्चित्संमतो लोके गुणैः स्यात्पुरुषो नृषु । भवत्यनपगान्सर्वांस्तान्गुणाँल्लक्षयामहे ॥
data.md: O king, I see all those qualities permanently living in you by which a person acquires the esteem of all.

data.v: अथ ते लक्ष्यते बुद्धिः समा बालजनैरिह । आत्मानं मन्यमानः सञ्श्रेयः किमिह मन्यसे ॥
data.md: Your understanding seems to be like that of a child, free from attachment and aversion. You know the soul. What, do you think, is the best means by which a knowledge of the Soul may be acquired.

data.v: बद्धः पाशैश्च्युतः स्थानाद्द्विषतां वशमागतः । श्रिया विहीनः प्रह्राद शोचितव्ये न शोचसि ॥
data.md: You are now bound in fetters, fallen off from your former position, brought under the sway of your foes, and divested of prosperity. Your present circumstances are such as may well give room to grief. Yet how is it, O Prahlada, that you do not grieve.

data.v: प्रज्ञालाभात्तु दैतेय उताहो धृतिमत्तया । प्रह्राद स्वस्थरूपोऽसि पश्यन्व्यसनमात्मनः ॥
data.md: Is this owing, O son of Diti, to the acquisition of wisdom or is it on account of your fortitude? Behold your calamities, O Prahlada, and yet you appear like one that is happy and tranquil.

data.v: इति संचोदितस्तेन धीरो निश्चितनिश्चयः । उवाच श्लक्ष्णया वाचा स्वां प्रज्ञामनुवर्णयन् ॥
data.md: Thus urged by Indra, the king of the Daityas, endued with firinness and with fixed conclusions about truth, replied in these sweet words showing great wisdom.

data.v: प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च भूतानां यो न बुध्यते । तस्य स्तम्भो भवेद्बाल्यान्नास्ति स्तम्भोऽनुपश्यतः ॥
data.md: Prahlada said “He who does not know the origin and the destruction of all created objects, is, on account of such ignorance, stupefied. He, however, who knows these two things, is never stupefied.

data.v: स्वभावात्संप्रवर्तन्ते निवर्तन्ते तथैव च । सर्वे भावास्तथाभावाः पुरुषार्थो न विद्यते ॥
data.md: All kinds of entities and non-entities come into being or cease on account of their own nature. No kind of personal exertion is necessary (for their production). In the absence of personal exertion it is clear that no personal agent exists for the production of all this that we perceive. But though the person never does anything, yet through the influence of Ignorance a consciousness regarding agency over spreads itself on it.

data.v: पुरुषार्थस्य चाभावे नास्ति कश्चित्स्वकारकः । स्वयं तु कुर्वतस्तस्य जातु मानो भवेदिह ॥
यस्तु कर्तारमात्मानं मन्यते साध्वसाधुनोः । तस्य दोषवती प्रज्ञा स्वमूर्त्यज्ञेति मे मतिः ॥
data.md: He who regards himself as the doer of good or bad acts possesses a vile wisdom. Such a person is, in my opinion, does not know the truth.

data.v: यदि स्यात्पुरुषः कर्ता शक्रात्मश्रेयसे ध्रुवम् । आरम्भास्तस्य सिध्येरन्न च जातु पराभवेत् ॥
data.md: If, O Shakra, the being known as person were really the actor, then all acts undertaken for his own benefit would certainly be successful. None of those acts would be futile. Persons struggling their utmost to avoid what is not desired and to bring about what is desired are not to be seen. What becomes then of personal exertion?

data.v: अनिष्टस्य हि निर्वृत्तिरनिवृत्तिः प्रियस्य च । लक्ष्यते यतमानानां पुरुषार्थस्ततः कुतः ॥
data.md: If, O Shakra, the being known as person were really the actor, then all acts undertaken for his own benefit would certainly be successful. None of those acts would be futile. Persons struggling their utmost to avoid what is not desired and to bring about what is desired are not to be seen. What becomes then of personal exertion?

data.v: अनिष्टस्याभिनिर्वृत्तिमिष्टसंवृत्तिमेव च । अप्रयत्नेन पश्यामः केषांचित्तत्स्वभावतः ॥
data.md: In the case of some, we see that without any exertion on their part, what is not desired is not brought about and what is desired, is done. This then must be the result of Nature.

data.v: प्रतिरूपधराः केचिद्दृश्यन्ते बुद्धिसत्तमाः । विरूपेभ्योऽल्पबुद्धिभ्यो लिप्समाना धनागमम् ॥
data.md: Some extraordinary persons again are seen, for though possessed of superior intelligence they have to seek wealth from others that are vulgar in features and gifted with little intelligence.

data.v: स्वभावप्रेरिताः सर्वे निविशन्ते गुणा यदा । शुभाशुभास्तदा तत्र तस्य किं मानकारणम् ॥
data.md: Indeed, when all qualities, good or bad, enter a person impelled by Nature, what is there for one to boast (of his superior possessions)?

data.v: स्वभावादेव तत्सर्वमिति मे निश्चिता मतिः । आत्मप्रतिष्ठिता प्रज्ञा मम नास्ति ततोऽन्यथा ॥
data.md: All these come from Nature. This is my seitled belief. Even Liberation and knowledge of self, in my view, originate from the same Source.

data.v: कर्मजं त्विह मन्येऽहं फलयोगं शुभाशुभम् । कर्मणां विषयं कृत्स्नमहं वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु ॥
data.md: In this world all fruits, good or bad, that attach themselves to persons, are considered as the outcome of acts. I shall now describe fully the subject of acts. Hear me.

data.v: यथा वेदयते कश्चिदोदनं वायसो वदन् । एवं सर्वाणि कर्माणि स्वभावस्यैव लक्षणम् ॥
data.md: As a crow, while eating some food, announces the presences of that food by its repeated cawing, similarly all our acts only proclaim the indications of Nature.

data.v: विकारानेव यो वेद न वेद प्रकृतिं पराम् । तस्य स्तम्भो भवेद्बाल्यान्नास्ति स्तम्भोऽनुपश्यतः ॥
data.md: He who is acquainted with only the metamorphoses of Nature but not with Nature which is supreme and exist by herself, feels stupefication on account of his ignorance. He, however, who understands the difference between Nature and her metamorphoses is never stupefied.

data.v: स्वभावभाविनो भावान्सर्वानेवेह निश्चये । बुध्यमानस्य दर्पो वा मानो वा किं करिष्यति ॥
data.md: All things originate from Nature. On account of one's certain conviction about it, he would never be affected by pride or arrogance.

data.v: वेद धर्मविधिं कृत्स्नं भूतानां चाप्यनित्यताम् । तस्माच्छक्र न शोचामि सर्वं ह्येवेदमन्तवत् ॥
data.md: When I know the origin of all the ordinances of mortality and when I ain acquainted with the instability of all objects, I can not, O Shakra, indulge in grief. All this is endued with an end.

data.v: निर्ममो निरहंकारो निरीहो मुक्तबन्धनः । स्वस्थोऽव्यपेतः पश्यामि भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययौ ॥
data.md: Without attachments, without pride, without desire and hope, freed from all fetters, and dissociated from everything, I am passing my time happily, seeing that appearance and disappearance of all created objects.

data.v: कृतप्रज्ञस्य दान्तस्य वितृष्णस्य निराशिषः । नायासो विद्यते शक्र पश्यतो लोकविद्यया ॥
data.md: For one who is wise, who is self-controlled, who is contented, who is without desire and hope, and who sees all things with the light of self-knowledge, on trouble or anxiety exists, O Shakra.

data.md: One that burns anything burns a thing that has been already burnt. One who kills, only kills, a victim already killed. One who is destroyed, has been before destroyed. A thing that is acquired by a person is what is already arrived and intended for his acquirement.

data.v: नास्य द्वीपः कुतः पारं नावारः संप्रदृश्यते । नान्तमस्य प्रपश्यामि विधेर्दिव्यस्य चिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: This Time is like an ocean. There is no island in it. Its other shore is beyond reach. Its boundary cannot be seen. Thinking even deeply, I do not see the end of this continuous steam that is the great ordainer of all things and that is, forsooth celestial.

data.v: यदि मे पश्यतः कालो भूतानि न विनाशयेत् । स्यान्मे हर्षश्च दर्पश्च क्रोधश्चैव शचीपते ॥
data.md: If I did not know that it is Time which destroys all creatures, then, perhaps, I would have experienced the emotions of joy, pride and anger, O husband of Shachi.

data.v: तुषभक्षं तु मां ज्ञात्वा प्रविविक्तजने गृहे । बिभ्रतं गार्दभं रूपमादिश्य परिगर्हसे ॥
data.md: Have you come here to condemn me, having come to know that I am now assuming the form of an ass that lives upon chaff and that is now passing his days in a lonely spot remote from the dwellings of men.

data.v: इच्छन्नहं विकुर्यां हि रूपाणि बहुधात्मनः । विभीषणानि यानीक्ष्य पलायेथास्त्वमेव मे ॥
data.md: If I wish, even now I can assume various dreadful forms, seeing any one of which you would immediately fly away from my presence.

data.v: कालः सर्वं समादत्ते कालः सर्वं प्रयच्छति । कालेन विधृतं सर्वं मा कृथाः शक्र पौरुषम् ॥
data.md: It is Time that gives every thing and again takes away everything. It is Time that ordains all things. Do not, O Shakra, brag of your manliness.

data.v: पुरा सर्वं प्रव्यथते मयि क्रुद्धे पुरंदर । अवैमि त्वस्य लोकस्य धर्मं शक्र सनातनम् ॥
data.md: Formerly, O Purandara, whenever, I used to be angry everything used to become agitated. I know, however, O Shakra, that eternal attributes of all things in the world.

data.v: त्वमप्येवमपेक्षस्व मात्मना विस्मयं गमः । प्रभवश्च प्रभावश्च नात्मसंस्थः कदाचन ॥
data.md: Do you also know the truth. Do not allow yourself to be filled with wonder. Prosperity and its origin are not under one's control.

data.v: कौमारमेव ते चित्तं तथैवाद्य यथा पुरा । समवेक्षस्व मघवन्बुद्धिं विन्दस्व नैष्ठिकीम् ॥
data.md: Your mind is like that of a child. It is the same as it was before. Open your eyes, O Maghavat and acquire an understanding which is sure and true.

data.v: देवा मनुष्याः पितरो गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः । आसन्सर्वे मम वशे तत्सर्वं वेत्थ वासव ॥
data.md: In days gone by, that gods, men, the Pitris, the Gandharvas, the Nagas, and the Rakshasas, were all under my control. You know this, O Vasava.

data.v: नमस्तस्यै दिशेऽप्यस्तु यस्यां वैरोचनो बलिः । इति मामभ्यपद्यन्त बुद्धिमात्सर्यमोहिताः ॥
data.md: Having their understandings overcome by ignorance, all creatures used to flatter me, saying,-Salutations to that cardinal point where Virochana's son Vali may now be living, O husband of Sachi, I do not at all grieve when I think of that honour. I am not sorry for this fall of mine. My understanding is very strong here, viz., that I will abide by the sway of the Ordainer.

data.v: नाहं तदनुशोचामि नात्मभ्रंशं शचीपते । एवं मे निश्चिता बुद्धिः शास्तुस्तिष्ठाम्यहं वशे ॥
data.md: Having their understandings overcome by ignorance, all creatures used to flatter me, saying,-Salutations to that cardinal point where Virochana's son Vali may now be living, O husband of Sachi, I do not at all grieve when I think of that honour. I am not sorry for this fall of mine. My understanding is very strong here, viz., that I will abide by the sway of the Ordainer.

data.v: दृश्यते हि कुले जातो दर्शनीयः प्रतापवान् । दुःखं जीवन्सहामात्यो भवितव्यं हि तत्तथा ॥
data.md: It is seen that some one of nobly born highly beautiful and powerful, lives in misery, with all his counsellors and friends. This happens because it has been so ordained.

data.v: दौष्कुलेयस्तथा मूढो दुर्जातः शक्र दृश्यते । सुखं जीवन्सहामात्यो भवितव्यं हि तत्तथा ॥
data.md: Likewise, some one born in an ignoble race, devoid of knowledge, and with even a stain on his birth, is seen, O Shakra, to live happily with all his counsellors and friends. This also happens because it has been so oridained.

data.v: कल्याणी रूपसंपन्ना दुर्भगा शक्र दृश्यते । अलक्षणा विरूपा च सुभगा शक्र दृश्यते ॥
data.md: An auspicious and beautiful woman, O Shakra, is seen to pass her life miserably. Likewise, ugly woman with every inauspicious mark is seen to live in great happiness.

data.v: नैतदस्मत्कृतं शक्र नैतच्छक्र त्वया कृतम् । यत्त्वमेवंगतो वज्रिन्यद्वाप्येवंगता वयम् ॥
data.md: That we have now become so is not owing to any act of ours, O Shakra. That you are now so is not owing, O holder of the thunderbolt, to any act of yours?

data.v: न कर्म तव नान्येषां कुतो मम शतक्रतो । ऋद्धिर्वाप्यथ वा नर्द्धिः पर्यायकृतमेव तत् ॥
data.md: You have not done anything, O you of a hundred sacrifices, for which you are now an enjoying this prosperity. Nor have I done anything for which I have now been shorn of prosperity. Prosperity and adversity come in succession.

data.v: पश्यामि त्वा विराजन्तं देवराजमवस्थितम् । श्रीमन्तं द्युतिमन्तं च गर्जन्तं च ममोपरि ॥
data.md: I now see you blazing with splendour, endued with prosperity, possessed of beauty, placed at the head of all the gods, and thus roaring at me.

data.v: एतच्चैवं न चेत्कालो मामाक्रम्य स्थितो भवेत् । पातयेयमहं त्वाद्य सवज्रमपि मुष्टिना ॥
data.md: This would never be but for the Time standing near after having attacked me. Indeed, if Time had not attacked me I would have today slain you with only a blow of my fists albeit you are armed with the thunder.

data.v: न तु विक्रमकालोऽयं क्षमाकालोऽयमागतः । कालः स्थापयते सर्वं कालः पचति वै तथा ॥
data.md: This, however, is not the time for displaying my prowess. On the other hand, the time that has come when I should conduct myself with peace and tranquillity. It is Time which establishes all things. Time acts upon all things and brings about their final consummation.

data.v: मां चेदभ्यागतः कालो दानवेश्वरमूर्जितम् । गर्जन्तं प्रतपन्तं च कमन्यं नागमिष्यति ॥
data.md: I was the adored king of the Danavas. Consuming all with my energy, I used to roar in strength and pride. When Time has attacked even myself, who is there whom he will not attack.

data.v: द्वादशानां हि भवतामादित्यानां महात्मनाम् । तेजांस्येकेन सर्वेषां देवराज हृतानि मे ॥
data.md: Formerly, O king of the gods, singly I bore the energy of all the twelve illustrious Adityas with yourself amongst them.

data.v: अहमेवोद्वहाम्यापो विसृजामि च वासव । तपामि चैव त्रैलोक्यं विद्योताम्यहमेव च ॥
data.md: It was I that used to bear up water and then to shower it as rain. O Vasava! It was I who used to give both light and heat to the three worlds.

data.v: संरक्षामि विलुम्पामि ददाम्यहमथाददे । संयच्छामि नियच्छामि लोकेषु प्रभुरीश्वरः ॥
data.md: It was I who used to protect and it was I that used to destroy. It was I who gave and it was I who took. It was I who used to bind and it was I who used to unbind. In all the worlds I was the one powerful master.

data.v: तदद्य विनिवृत्तं मे प्रभुत्वममराधिप । कालसैन्यावगाढस्य सर्वं न प्रतिभाति मे ॥
data.md: That sovereign control which I had, O king of the gods, is now gone. I am now attacked by the foreces of Time. Those things, therefore, are no longer seen to shine in me.

data.v: नाहं कर्ता न चैव त्वं नान्यः कर्ता शचीपते । पर्यायेण हि भुज्यन्ते लोकाः शक्र यदृच्छया ॥
data.md: I am not the actor. You are not the actor. None else, O husband of Sachi, is the doer. It is Time, O Shakra, that protects or destroys all things.

data.v: मासार्धमासवेश्मानमहोरात्राभिसंवृतम् । ऋतुद्वारं वर्षमुखमाहुर्वेदविदो जनाः ॥
data.md: Persons well-read in the Vedas say that me is Brahma. The fortnights and months are his body. That body is clothed with days and nights as its dresses. The seasons are his senses. The year is his mouth.

data.v: आहुः सर्वमिदं चिन्त्यं जनाः केचिन्मनीषया । अस्याः पञ्चैव चिन्तायाः पर्येष्यामि च पञ्चधा ॥
data.md: Some people, on account of their superior intelligence, say that the entire universe should be conceived as Brahma. The Vedas, however, teach, that the five sacs that cover the Soul should be known as Brahma.

data.v: गम्भीरं गहनं ब्रह्म महत्तोयार्णवं यथा । अनादिनिधनं चाहुरक्षरं परमेव च ॥
data.md: Brahma is deep and inaccessible like a deep ocean. It is said that it has neither beginning nor end, and that it is both indestructible and destructible.

data.v: सत्त्वेषु लिङ्गमावेश्य नलिङ्गमपि तत्स्वयम् । मन्यन्ते ध्रुवमेवैनं ये नरास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: Though it is by nature without attributes yet it enters all existent objects and as such is clothed with attributes. Those persons who know truth consider Brahma as eternal.

data.v: भूतानां तु विपर्यासं मन्यते गतवानिति । न ह्येतावद्भवेद्गम्यं न यस्मात्प्रकृतेः परः ॥
data.md: Through the force of Ignorance, Brahma makes the attribute of materiality to invest the Chit or Soul which is immaterial spirit. Materiality, however, is not the true attribute of the Soul.

data.v: गतिं हि सर्वभूतानामगत्वा क्व गमिष्यसि । यो धावता न हातव्यस्तिष्ठन्नपि न हीयते । तमिन्द्रियाणि सर्वाणि नानुपश्यन्ति पञ्चधा ॥
data.md: Brahma in the form of Time is the refuge of all creatures. Where can you go transcending that Time? Time or Brahma, indeed, cannot be shunned by running nor by standing still.

data.v: आहुश्चैनं केचिदग्निं केचिदाहुः प्रजापतिम् । ऋतुमासार्धमासांश्च दिवसांस्तु क्षणांस्तथा ॥
पूर्वाह्णमपराह्णं च मध्याह्नमपि चापरे । मुहूर्तमपि चैवाहुरेकं सन्तमनेकधा । तं कालमवजानीहि यस्य सर्वमिदं वशे ॥
बहूनीन्द्रसहस्राणि समतीतानि वासव । बलवीर्योपपन्नानि यथैव त्वं शचीपते ॥
data.md: Many thousands of Indras have gone away, O Vasava, cach of whom was endued with great strength and prowess. Similarly you also, O lord of Shachi, shall have to pass away.

data.v: त्वामप्यतिबलं शक्रं देवराजं बलोत्कटम् । प्राप्ते काले महावीर्यः कालः संशमयिष्यति ॥
data.md: The omnipotent Time will destroy you too, O Shakra, who are endued with swelling might and that are the chief of the deities, when your hour comes.

data.v: य इदं सर्वमादत्ते तस्माच्छक्र स्थिरो भव । मया त्वया च पूर्वैश्च न स शक्योऽतिवर्तितुम् ॥
data.md: Time carries away all things. Therefore, O Indra, do not brag! Time cannot be quieted by either you or me or by those gone before us.

data.v: यामेतां प्राप्य जानीषे राजश्रियमनुत्तमाम् । स्थिता मयीति तन्मिथ्या नैषा ह्येकत्र तिष्ठति ॥
data.md: This kingly prosperity which you have acquired and which you consider incomparable, had formerly been possessed by me. It is unsubstantial and unreal. She does not live long in one place.

data.v: स्थिता हीन्द्रसहस्रेषु त्वद्विशिष्टतमेष्वियम् । मां च लोला परित्यज्य त्वामगाद्विबुधाधिप ॥
data.md: Indeed, she had lived in thousands of Indras before you, all of whom, again, were, very much superior to you! Unstable as she is, leaving me she has now approached you, O king of the gods.

data.v: मैवं शक्र पुनः कार्षीः शान्तो भवितुमर्हसि । त्वामप्येवंगतं त्यक्त्वा क्षिप्रमन्यं गमिष्यति ॥
data.md: Do not, O Shakra, brag again! You should become tranquil! Knowing you to be full of vanity, she will very soon leave you.'

data.v: शतक्रतुरथापश्यद्बलेर्दीप्तां महात्मनः । स्वरूपिणीं शरीराद्धि तदा निष्क्रामतीं श्रियम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said “After this, the god of a hundred sacrifices saw the goddess of Prosperity, in her own embodied, but shining, form, issue out of the body of the great Vali.

data.v: तां दीप्तां प्रभया दृष्ट्वा भगवान्पाकशासनः । विस्मयोत्फुल्लनयनो बलिं पप्रच्छ वासवः ॥
data.md: Beholding the goddess blazing with radiance, the illustrious chastiser of Paka, addressed Vali thus with eyes expanded in wonder.

data.v: बले केयमपक्रान्ता रोचमाना शिखण्डिनी । त्वत्तः स्थिता सकेयूरा दीप्यमाना स्वतेजसा ॥
data.md: Shakra said 'O Vali, who is this one, thus shining effulgently, thus adorned with a crown, thus adorned with golden bracelets on her upper arms, and thus emitting a halo on all sides on account of her energy that is issuing out of your body.'

data.v: न हीमामासुरीं वेद्मि न दैवीं न च मानुषीम् । त्वमेवैनां पृच्छ मा वा यथेष्टं कुरु वासव ॥
data.md: Vali said I do not know whether she is an Asura woman or a celestial one, or a human one. You may or may not ask her yourself. Do what pleases you."

data.v: का त्वं बलेरपक्रान्ता रोचमाना शिखण्डिनी । अजानतो ममाचक्ष्व नामधेयं शुचिस्मिते ॥
data.md: Shakra said 'O You of sweet smiles, who are you who are so effulgent and adorned with plumes that thus issue from the body of Vali! I do not know you, kindly tell me your name.

data.v: का त्वं तिष्ठसि मायेव दीप्यमाना स्वतेजसा । हित्वा दैत्येश्वरं सुभ्रु तन्ममाचक्ष्व तत्त्वतः ॥
data.md: Who, indeed, are you that thus stand here as Maya herself, shining with your own splendour, after having left the lord of the Daityas? O, tell me this as I ask you.'

data.v: न मा विरोचनो वेद न मा वैरोचनो बलिः । आहुर्मां दुःसहेत्येवं विधित्सेति च मां विदुः ॥
data.md: Virochana did not know, me, His son this Vali knows me not. The learned called me by the name of Dusshaha (born with difficulty). Some knew me by the name of Vidhitsa (desire for action).

data.v: भूतिर्लक्ष्मीति मामाहुः श्रीरित्येवं च वासव । त्वं मां शक्र न जानीषे सर्वे देवा न मां विदुः ॥
data.md: I have other names also, O Vasava! They are Bhuti, Lakshmi, and Shree (prosperity). You know me not, O Shakra, nor does any one among the gods know me.'

data.v: किमिदं त्वं मम कृते उताहो बलिनः कृते । दुःसहे विजहास्येनं चिरसंवासिनी सती ॥
data.md: Shakra said-'O lady who is difficult of being borne, why do you leave Vali now after having lived in him for a long time? It is owing to any act of mine or is it owing to any act of Vali's.'

data.v: न धाता न विधाता मां विदधाति कथंचन । कालस्तु शक्र पर्यायान्मैनं शक्रावमन्यथाः ॥
data.md: Shree said 'Neither the Creator nor the Ordainer governs me. It is Time that takes me from one place to another. Do not, O Shakra, disrespect Vali.'

data.v: कथं त्वया बलिस्त्यक्तः किमर्थं वा शिखण्डिनि । कथं च मां न जह्यास्त्वं तन्मे ब्रूहि शुचिस्मिते ॥
data.md: Shakra said 'Why O goddess adorned with plumes, do you leave Vali? Why also do you approach me? Tell me this, O you of sweet smiles!

data.v: सत्ये स्थितास्मि दाने च व्रते तपसि चैव हि । पराक्रमे च धर्मे च पराचीनस्ततो बलिः ॥
data.md: Shree said 'I reside in truth, in gifts, in good vows, in penances in prowess, and in virtue! Vali has fallen off from all these.

data.v: ब्रह्मण्योऽयं सदा भूत्वा सत्यवादी जितेन्द्रियः । अभ्यसूयद्ब्राह्मणान्वै उच्छिष्टश्चास्पृशद्घृतम् ॥
data.md: Formerly he was devoted to the Brahmanas. He was truthful and had mastered his passions. Latterly, however, he began to entertain feelings of animosity towards the Brahmanas and touched clarified butter with impure hands.

data.v: यज्ञशीलः पुरा भूत्वा मामेव यजतेत्ययम् । प्रोवाच लोकान्मूढात्मा कालेनोपनिपीडितः ॥
data.md: Formerly he was always used to perform sacrifices. At last, blinded by ignorance and possessed by Time he began to brag before all persons, saying that his adorations towards me were ceaseless.

data.v: अपाकृता ततः शक्र त्वयि वत्स्यामि वासव । अप्रमत्तेन धार्यास्मि तपसा विक्रमेण च ॥
data.md: Leaving him I shall henceforth, O Shakra, live in you! You should bear me vigilantly, and with penances and prowess.

data.v: अस्ति देवमनुष्येषु सर्वभूतेषु वा पुमान् । यस्त्वामेको विषहितुं शक्नुयात्कमलालये ॥
data.md: Shakra said O you who live in lotuses, there is not a single person among gods, men, and all creatures, that can bear you for ever!

data.v: नैव देवो न गन्धर्वो नासुरो न च राक्षसः । यो मामेको विषहितुं शक्तः कश्चित्पुरंदर ॥
data.md: 'Truly, O Purandara, there is none among gods, Gandharvas, Asuras, or Rakshasas, who can bear me for ever!'

data.v: तिष्ठेथा मयि नित्यं त्वं यथा तद्ब्रूहि मे शुभे । तत्करिष्यामि ते वाक्यमृतं त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Shakra said O auspicious lady, tell me how I should behave so that you may live in me perpetually. I shall, forsooth, obey your commands. You should answer me truly.'

data.v: स्थास्यामि नित्यं देवेन्द्र यथा त्वयि निबोध तत् । विधिना वेददृष्टेन चतुर्धा विभजस्व माम् ॥
data.md: Shree said four parts 'O King of the deities, I shall tell you as to how I may be entitled to live in you perpetually. Divide me into four according to the Vedic injunction.'

data.v: अहं वै त्वा निधास्यामि यथाशक्ति यथाबलम् । न तु मेऽतिक्रमः स्याद्वै सदा लक्ष्मि तवान्तिके ॥
data.md: Shakra said I shall give you habitations according to their strength and power in bearing you. As regards myself, I shall always take care, O Lakshmi, that I may not offend you in any way.

data.v: भूमिरेव मनुष्येषु धारणी भूतभाविनी । सा ते पादं तितिक्षेत समर्था हीति मे मतिः ॥
data.md: Amongst men, the Earth, that mother of all things, bears them all. She shall bear a fourth part of yourself. I think she has the strength to do so.

data.v: एष मे निहितः पादो योऽयं भूमौ प्रतिष्ठितः । द्वितीयं शक्र पादं मे तस्मात्सुनिहितं कुरु ॥
data.md: Shree said-Here, I give up a quarter of myself. Let it be placed on the Earth. Do you, next, make a proper distribution, O Shakra, for my second quarter.

data.v: आप एव मनुष्येषु द्रवन्त्यः परिचारिकाः । तास्ते पादं तितिक्षन्तामलमापस्तितिक्षितुम् ॥
data.md: Shakra said 'The waters, among men, in their liquid form, do various services to men. Let the waters bear a fourth part of your person. They have the strength to bear a fourth part of you person. They have the strength to bear a portion of yours.'

data.v: एष मे निहितः पादो योऽयमप्सु प्रतिष्ठितः । तृतीयं शक्र पादं मे तस्मात्सुनिहितं कुरु ॥
data.md: Shree said-Here, I give up a quarter of myself. Let it be placed on the Earth. Do you, next, make a proper distribution, O Shakra, for my second quarter.

data.v: यस्मिन्देवाश्च यज्ञाश्च यस्मिन्वेदाः प्रतिष्ठिताः । तृतीयं पादमग्निस्ते सुधृतं धारयिष्यति ॥
data.md: Shakra said 'The Vedas, the sacrifices, and the gods are all established in Fire. Fire will bear your third quarter, when it is placed therein.'

data.v: एष मे निहितः पादो योऽयमग्नौ प्रतिष्ठितः । चतुर्थं शक्र पादं मे तस्मात्सुनिहितं कुरु ॥
