data.md: I wish, O Kuru hero, to know what origin and what the end is of all creatures; what the nature of their meditation is and what their acts; what the divisions of time are, and what is the spare of human existence in the respective cycles.

data.v: लोकतत्त्वं च कार्त्स्न्येन भूतानामागतिं गतिम् । सर्गश्च निधनं चैव कुत एतत्प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: I wish also to know fully the truth about the genesis and the conduct of the world; the you. coming of creatures into the world and their exit. Indeed; whence their creation and destruction?

data.v: यदि तेऽनुग्रहे बुद्धिरस्मास्विह सतां वर । एतद्भवन्तं पृच्छामि तद्भवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे ॥
data.md: O best of virtuous persons, if you wish to favour us, do tell this about which I ask

data.v: पूर्वं हि कथितं श्रुत्वा भृगुभाषितमुत्तमम् । भरद्वाजस्य विप्रर्षेस्ततो मे बुद्धिरुत्तमा ॥
data.md: Having heard before this the excellent discourse of Bhrigu to the twice-born sage Bharadvaja, which you did recite, my understanding, shorn of ignorance, has become greatly attached to yoga, and withdrawn from worldly objects rests upon heavenly purity. I ask you about the subject, therefore, once more. You should describe it to me fully.

data.v: जाता परमधर्मिष्ठा दिव्यसंस्थानसंस्थिता । ततो भूयस्तु पृच्छामि तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
data.md: Having heard before this the excellent discourse of Bhrigu to the twice-born sage Bharadvaja, which you did recite, my understanding, shorn of ignorance, has become greatly attached to yoga, and withdrawn from worldly objects rests upon heavenly purity. I ask you about the subject, therefore, once more. You should describe it to me fully.

data.v: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम् । जगौ यद्भगवान्व्यासः पुत्राय परिपृच्छते ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it I shall recite to you an old narrative of what the divine Vyasa said to his son Shuka when the latter had asked the former.

data.v: अधीत्य वेदानखिलान्साङ्गोपनिषदस्तथा । अन्विच्छन्नैष्ठिकं कर्म धर्मनैपुणदर्शनात् ॥
data.md: Having studied the measureless Vedas with all their branches and the Upanishads, and desirous of leading a life of celibacy on account of his having acquired excellence of religious merit, Shuka put these very questions, about which his doubts had not been removed, to his father Dvipayana, who had removed (by study and contemplation) all doubt regarding true duties.

data.v: कृष्णद्वैपायनं व्यासं पुत्रो वैयासकिः शुकः । पप्रच्छ संदेहमिमं छिन्नधर्मार्थसंशयम् ॥
data.md: Having studied the measureless Vedas with all their branches and the Upanishads, and desirous of leading a life of celibacy on account of his having acquired excellence of religious merit, Shuka put these very questions, about which his doubts had not been removed, to his father Dvipayana, who had removed (by study and contemplation) all doubt regarding true duties.

data.v: भूतग्रामस्य कर्तारं कालज्ञाने च निश्चयम् । ब्राह्मणस्य च यत्कृत्यं तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
data.md: Shuka said You should tell me who the Creator is of all beings, as fixed by a knowledge of time, and what the duties are of a Brahmana!

data.v: तस्मै प्रोवाच तत्सर्वं पिता पुत्राय पृच्छते । अतीतानागते विद्वान्सर्वज्ञः सर्वधर्मवित् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said The father, having a knowledge of both the past and the future, conversant with all duties and gifted with omniscience, thus described the subject to his son, who had questioned him.

data.v: अनाद्यन्तमजं दिव्यमजरं ध्रुवमव्ययम् । अप्रतर्क्यमविज्ञेयं ब्रह्माग्रे समवर्तत ॥
data.md: Vyasa said Only Brahma, who is without beginning without end, unborn, effulgent, above decay, immutable, indestructible, inconceivable and transcending knowledge, exists before the Creation.

data.v: काष्ठा निमेषा दश पञ्च चैव; त्रिंशत्तु काष्ठा गणयेत्कलां ताम् । त्रिंशत्कलाश्चापि भवेन्मुहूर्तो; भागः कलाया दशमश्च यः स्यात् ॥
त्रिंशन्मुहूर्तश्च भवेदहश्च; रात्रिश्च संख्या मुनिभिः प्रणीता । मासः स्मृतो रात्र्यहनी च त्रिंश;त्संवत्सरो द्वादशमास उक्तः । संवत्सरं द्वे अयने वदन्ति; संख्याविदो दक्षिणमुत्तरं च ॥
अहोरात्रे विभजते सूर्यो मानुषलौकिके । रात्रिः स्वप्नाय भूतानां चेष्टायै कर्मणामहः ॥
data.md: The sun makes the day and the night for men. The night is for the sleep of all living creatures, and the day is for work.

data.v: पित्र्ये रात्र्यहनी मासः प्रविभागस्तयोः पुनः । कृष्णोऽहः कर्मचेष्टायां शुक्लः स्वप्नाय शर्वरी ॥
data.md: A month of human beings is equal to a day and night of the departed manes. That division consists in this: the light half of the month is their day which is for work; and the dark fortnight is their night for sleep.

data.v: दैवे रात्र्यहनी वर्षं प्रविभागस्तयोः पुनः । अहस्तत्रोदगयनं रात्रिः स्याद्दक्षिणायनम् ॥
data.md: A year (of men) is equal to a day and night to the gods. This division consists in this: the half year for which the sun travels from the vernal to the autumnal equinox is the day of the gods, and the half year for which the sun moves from the latter to the former is their night.

data.v: ये ते रात्र्यहनी पूर्वे कीर्तिते दैवलौकिके । तयोः संख्याय वर्षाग्रं ब्राह्मे वक्ष्याम्यहःक्षपे ॥
data.md: Calculating by the days and nights of human beings about which I have told you, I shall speak of the day and night of Brahman and his years also.

data.v: तेषां संवत्सराग्राणि प्रवक्ष्याम्यनुपूर्वशः । कृते त्रेतायुगे चैव द्वापरे च कलौ तथा ॥
data.md: I shall, in their order, tell you the number of years, that are for different purposes calculated differently, in the Krita, the Treta, the Dvapara, and the Kali Yugas.

data.v: चत्वार्याहुः सहस्राणि वर्षाणां तत्कृतं युगम् । तस्य तावच्छती संध्या संध्यांशश्च तथाविधः ॥
data.md: Four thousand celestial years is the duration of the first or Krita age. The morning of that cycle consists of four hundred years and its evening is of four hundred years.

data.v: इतरेषु ससंध्येषु ससंध्यांशेषु च त्रिषु । एकापायेन संयान्ति सहस्राणि शतानि च ॥
data.md: Regarding the other cycles, the duration of each gradually decreases by a quarter in respect of both the principal period with the minor portion and the conjoining portion itself.

data.v: एतानि शाश्वताँल्लोकान्धारयन्ति सनातनान् । एतद्ब्रह्मविदां तात विदितं ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् ॥
data.md: These periods always keep up the neverending and eternal worlds. They who know Brahma, O child, regard this as Immutable Brahma.

data.v: चतुष्पात्सकलो धर्मः सत्यं चैव कृते युगे । नाधर्मेणागमः कश्चित्परस्तस्य प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: In the Krita age all the duties exist in full, along with Truth. Men of that age never acquired knowledge or object through unrighteous or forbidden means.

data.v: इतरेष्वागमाद्धर्मः पादशस्त्ववरोप्यते । चौरिकानृतमायाभिरधर्मश्चोपचीयते ॥
data.md: In the other cycles duty, as laid down in the Vedas, is seen to gradually decline by a quarter in each. Sinfulness multiplies by theft, untruth, and deception.

data.v: अरोगाः सर्वसिद्धार्थाश्चतुर्वर्षशतायुषः । कृते त्रेतादिष्वेतेषां पादशो ह्रसते वयः ॥
data.md: In the Krita age, all persons are free from disease and achieve their objects, and all live for four hundred years. In the Treta, the period of life decreases by a quarter.

data.v: वेदवादाश्चानुयुगं ह्रसन्तीति च नः श्रुतम् । आयूंषि चाशिषश्चैव वेदस्यैव च यत्फलम् ॥
data.md: We have heard that, in the succeeding Yugas, the words of the Vedas, the periods of life, the blessings and the fruits of Vedic rites, all decrease gradually.

data.v: अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास्त्रेतायां द्वापरेऽपरे । अन्ये कलियुगे धर्मा यथाशक्तिकृता इव ॥
data.md: The duties set down for the Krita Yuga are of one kind. Those for the Treta are otherwise. Those for the Dwapara are different. And those for the Kali are otherwise. This is in accordance with the decline which marks every succeeding cycle.

data.v: तपः परं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां ज्ञानमुत्तमम् । द्वापरे यज्ञमेवाहुर्दानमेव कलौ युगे ॥
data.md: In the Krita, Penance is the foremost. In the Treta, Knowledge is foremost. In Dvapara, Sacrifice has been said to be the foremost. In the Kali Yuga, only gift is sanctioned.

data.v: एतां द्वादशसाहस्रीं युगाख्यां कवयो विदुः । सहस्रं परिवृत्तं तद्ब्राह्मं दिवसमुच्यते ॥
data.md: The learned say that these twelve thousand celestial years from what is celled a cycle. A thousand such cycles form a single day of Brahman.

data.v: रात्रिस्तावत्तिथी ब्राह्मी तदादौ विश्वमीश्वरः । प्रलयेऽध्यात्ममाविश्य सुप्त्वा सोऽन्ते विबुध्यते ॥
data.md: The same is the duration of Brahman's night. With the beginning of Brahman's day the universe begins to come into being. During the period of universal dissolution the Creator sleeps, in Yoga-meditation. When the period of sleep expires, He awakes.

data.v: सहस्रयुगपर्यन्तमहर्यद्ब्रह्मणो विदुः । रात्रिं युगसहस्रान्तां तेऽहोरात्रविदो जनाः ॥
data.md: What is Brahman's day covers a thousand such cycles. His night also covers a thousand similar cycles. They who know this are said to know the day and the night.

data.v: प्रतिबुद्धो विकुरुते ब्रह्माक्षय्यं क्षपाक्षये । सृजते च महद्भूतं तस्माद्व्यक्तात्मकं मनः ॥
data.md: On the expiry of His night, Brahman, waking up modifies the indestructible intelligence by causing it to be overlaid with ignorance. He then causes Consciousness to spring up, whence originates Mind which is at one with the Manifest.

data.v: ब्रह्म तेजोमयं शुक्रं यस्य सर्वमिदं जगत् । एकस्य भूतं भूतस्य द्वयं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
data.md: Vyasa said Brahma is the effulgent seed from which existing as it does by itself, has originated the entire universe consisting of two kinds of being, viz., the mobile and the immobile,

data.v: अहर्मुखे विबुद्धः सन्सृजते विद्यया जगत् । अग्र एव महाभूतमाशु व्यक्तात्मकं मनः ॥
data.md: At the dawn of His day, waking up, He creates with the aid of Avidya this universe. Mahat or the principle of Greatness at first springs up. That Mahat is speedily changed into Mind which is the soul of the Manifest.

data.v: अभिभूयेह चार्चिष्मद्व्यसृजत्सप्त मानसान् । दूरगं बहुधागामि प्रार्थनासंशयात्मकम् ॥
data.md: Overwhelming the Intelligence, which is effulgent, with Ignorance, Mind creates seven great entities. Urged by the desire of creating, Mind, which is far-reaching, which has many courses, and which had desire and doubt for its leading signs, beings to create various kinds of objects by modifications of itself. Ether first originates from it. Know that its property is Sound.

data.v: मनः सृष्टिं विकुरुते चोद्यमानं सिसृक्षया । आकाशं जायते तस्मात्तस्य शब्दो गुणो मतः ॥
आकाशात्तु विकुर्वाणात्सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिः । बलवाञ्जायते वायुस्तस्य स्पर्शो गुणो मतः ॥
data.md: From Ether, by modification, originates the bearer of all scents, viz., the pure, and powerful Wind. It is said to possess the property of Touch.

data.v: वायोरपि विकुर्वाणाज्ज्योतिर्भूतं तमोनुदम् । रोचिष्णु जायते तत्र तद्रूपगुणमुच्यते ॥
data.md: From Wind also, by modification, originates Light endued with effulgence. Beautiful and called also Shukram, it is thus created, possessing the attribute of Form.

data.v: ज्योतिषोऽपि विकुर्वाणाद्भवन्त्यापो रसात्मिकाः । अद्भ्यो गन्धगुणा भूमिः पूर्वैषा सृष्टिरुच्यते ॥
data.md: From light, by modification, originates Water having taste for its attribute. From Water originates Earth having Scent for its attribute. These are said to represent primary creation.

data.v: गुणाः पूर्वस्य पूर्वस्य प्राप्नुवन्त्युत्तरोत्तरम् । तेषां यावत्तिथं यद्यत्तत्तत्तावद्गुणं स्मृतम् ॥
data.md: These, in succession, acquire the attributes of the immediately preceding ones from which they have originated. Each has not only its own special attribute but each succeeding one has the attributes of all the previous ones.

data.v: उपलभ्याप्सु चेद्गन्धं केचिद्ब्रूयुरनैपुणात् । पृथिव्यामेव तं विद्यादापो वायुं च संश्रितम् ॥
data.md: If anybody, perceiving Scent in Water, were from ignorance to say that it belongs to Water, he would make a mistake, for Scent is the attribute of Earth though it may exist in Water and also Wind.

data.v: एते तु सप्त पुरुषा नानाविर्याः पृथक्पृथक् । नाशक्नुवन्प्रजाः स्रष्टुमसमागम्य सर्वतः ॥
data.md: These seven kinds of entities, possessing various kinds of energy, at first existed separately from one another. They could not create objects without all of them acting in a body.

data.v: ते समेत्य महात्मानमन्योन्यमभिसंश्रिताः । शरीराश्रयणं प्राप्तास्ततः पुरुष उच्यते ॥
data.md: All these great entities coming together, and mixing with one another, form the constituent parts of the body which are called limbs.

data.v: श्रयणाच्छरीरं भवति मूर्तिमत्षोडशात्मकम् । तदाविशन्ति भूतानि महान्ति सह कर्मणा ॥
data.md: On account of the combination of those limbs,-the sum-total, invested with form and having sixteen constituent parts, becomes what is called the body, (When the gross body is thus forined), the subtile principle of greatness, with the unexhausted remnant of acts, then enters that combination called the gross body.

data.v: सर्वभूतानि चादाय तपसश्चरणाय च । आदिकर्ता महाभूतं तमेवाहुः प्रजापतिम् ॥
data.md: The original Creator of all beings, then having by His Maya divided Himself, enters that subtile form for overloO king everything. And because he is the original Creator of all beings he is called the lord of all beings.

data.v: स वै सृजति भूतानि स एव पुरुषः परः । अजो जनयते ब्रह्मा देवर्षिपितृमानवान् ॥
लोकान्नदीः समुद्रांश्च दिशः शैलान्वनस्पतीन् । नरकिंनररक्षांसि वयःपशुमृगोरगान् । अव्ययं च व्ययं चैव द्वयं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
तेषां ये यानि कर्माणि प्राक्सृष्ट्यां प्रतिपेदिरे । तान्येव प्रतिपद्यन्ते सृज्यमानाः पुनः पुनः ॥
हिंस्राहिंस्रे मृदुक्रूरे धर्माधर्मे ऋतानृते । अतो यन्मन्यते धाता तस्मात्तत्तस्य रोचते ॥
महाभूतेषु नानात्वमिन्द्रियार्थेषु मूर्तिषु । विनियोगं च भूतानां धातैव विदधात्युत ॥
data.md: It is the Ordained himself who attaches variety to the great entities to the objects of the senses and to size or bulk of existent matter, and settles the relations of creatures with those various entities.

data.v: केचित्पुरुषकारं तु प्राहुः कर्मविदो जनाः । दैवमित्यपरे विप्राः स्वभावं भूतचिन्तकाः ॥
data.md: Of men who had devoted themselves to the science of things, there are some who say that, in the production of effects, Exertion is supreme. Some learned persons hold that Destiny is supreme, and some that it is Nature which is the agent.

data.v: पौरुषं कर्म दैवं च फलवृत्तिस्वभावतः । त्रय एतेऽपृथग्भूता नविवेकं तु केचन ॥
data.md: Others hold that Acts flowing from Exertion and Destiny, produce effects, helped by Nature. Instead of considering any of these as alone powerful for the production of effects, they say that it is the union of all three that produces all effects.

data.v: एवमेतच्च नैवं च यद्भूतं सृजते जगत् । कर्मस्था विषमं ब्रूयुः सत्त्वस्थाः समदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: About this subject, some say that such is the case; some, that such is not the case; some, that both of these are not the case; and some that it is not that the reverse of both are not. These, of course, are the contentions of those who depend on Acts, with reference to objects. They, however, whose see the truth consider Brahma as the causes.

data.v: तपो निःश्रेयसं जन्तोस्तस्य मूलं दमः शमः । तेन सर्वानवाप्नोति यान्कामान्मनसेच्छति ॥
data.md: Penance is the greatest good for living creatures. The roots of penance are tranquillity and self-control. By penance one acquires all things that he longs for in his mind.

data.v: तपसा तदवाप्नोति यद्भूतं सृजते जगत् । स तद्भूतश्च सर्वेषां भूतानां भवति प्रभुः ॥
data.md: By penance one attains to that Being who creates the universe. He who thus succeeds in attaining to that Being becomes the powerful lord of all beings.

data.v: ऋषयस्तपसा वेदानध्यैषन्त दिवानिशम् । अनादिनिधना नित्या वागुत्सृष्टा स्वयंभुवा ॥
data.md: it is by penance that the Rishis can read the Vedas without interruption. In the beginning the self-create caused those excellent Vedic sounds, that are embodiments of knowledge and that have neither beginning nor end. From those sounds have sprung all sorts of actions.

data.v: ऋषीणां नामधेयानि याश्च वेदेषु सृष्टयः । शर्वर्यन्तेषु जातानां तान्येवैभ्यो ददाति सः ॥
नामभेदस्तपःकर्मयज्ञाख्या लोकसिद्धयः । आत्मसिद्धिस्तु वेदेषु प्रोच्यते दशभिः क्रमैः ॥
data.md: in the Vedas has been described the subject of the Soul's Liberation, along with the ten means formed by study of the Vedas, adoption of the domestic mode of life. penances, observance of all duties, common to all the modes of life, sacrifices, performance of all acts leading to pure fame meditation which is of three kinds, and that kind of Liberation called success (Siddhi) attainable in this life.

data.v: यदुक्तं वेदवादेषु गहनं वेददृष्टिभिः । तदन्तेषु यथायुक्तं क्रमयोगेन लक्ष्यते ॥
data.md: That incomprehensible Brahma which has been described in the words of the Vedas, and which has been described more clearly in the Upanishads by those who have an insight into the Vedas, can be realised by gradually following the practices referred to above.

data.v: कर्मजोऽयं पृथग्भावो द्वंद्वयुक्तो वियोगिनः । आत्मसिद्धिस्तु विज्ञाता जहाति प्रायशो बलम् ॥
data.md: This consciousness of duality, fraught again with that of pairs opposites, is born only of acts in which he is engaged to a person who thinks he has a body. That person, however, who has attained to Liberation aided by his knowledge, drives off by force that consciousness of duality.

data.v: द्वे ब्रह्मणी वेदितव्ये शब्दब्रह्म परं च यत् । शब्दब्रह्मणि निष्णातः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: Two Brahmas should be known viz., the Brahma represented by the Vedas and that which is beyond the Vedas and is supreme. One who is conversant with Brahma represented by sound succeeds in attaining to Brahma that is Supreme.

data.v: आरम्भयज्ञाः क्षत्रस्य हविर्यज्ञा विशस्तथा । परिचारयज्ञाः शूद्रास्तु तपोयज्ञा द्विजातयः ॥
data.md: The destruction of animals is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Kshatriyas. The growing of corn is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Vaisshyas. Serving the three other orders is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Shudras. Penance is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Brahmanas.

data.v: त्रेतायुगे विधिस्त्वेषां यज्ञानां न कृते युगे । द्वापरे विप्लवं यान्ति यज्ञाः कलियुगे तथा ॥
data.md: In the Krita age the perforinance of sacrifices was not required. Such performance became necessary in the Treta age. In the Dvapara, sacrifices have begun to fall off. In the Kali, the same is the case with them,

data.v: अपृथग्धर्मिणो मर्त्या ऋक्सामानि यजूंषि च । काम्यां पुष्टिं पृथग्दृष्ट्वा तपोभिस्तप एव च ॥
data.md: In the Krita age, worshipping only one Brahma, men regarded the Richs, the Samans, the Yajushas, and the rites and sacrifices that are performed from motives of advantage, as all different from the object of their worship, and practised only Yoga by means of penances.

data.v: त्रेतायां तु समस्तास्ते प्रादुरासन्महाबलाः । संयन्तारः स्थावराणां जङ्गमानां च सर्वशः ॥
data.md: In the Treta age, many powerful men flourished who governed all mobile and immobile objects.

data.v: त्रेतायां संहता ह्येते यज्ञा वर्णास्तथैव च । संरोधादायुषस्त्वेते व्यस्यन्ते द्वापरे युगे ॥
data.md: Accordingly, in that age, the Vedas, and sacrifices, and the distinctions between the several orders, and the four modes of life, existed in a body. On account, however, of the decrease in the period of life in Dvapara, all these, it that age, fall off from that compact condition.

data.v: दृश्यन्ते नापि दृश्यन्ते वेदाः कलियुगेऽखिलाः । उत्सीदन्ते सयज्ञाश्च केवला धर्मसेतवः ॥
data.md: In the Kali age, all the Vedas become so scarce that they are not seen by men. Afflicted by iniquity, they become extinct along with the rites and sacrifices laid down in them.

data.v: कृते युगे यस्तु धर्मो ब्राह्मणेषु प्रदृश्यते । आत्मवत्सु तपोवत्सु श्रुतवत्सु प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
data.md: The righteousness which is seen in the Krita age is now seen in such Brahmanas as are of purified souls and as are devoted to penances and the study of the scriptures.

data.v: अधर्मव्रतसंयोगं यथाधर्मं युगे युगे । विक्रियन्ते स्वधर्मस्था वेदवादा यथायुगम् ॥
data.md: As regards the other cycles, it is seen that without at once giving up the duties and acts that are consistent with righteousness, men, observing the practices of their respective orders, and conversant with the ordinances of the Vedas, are led, by the authority of the scriptures, and from motives of advantage and interest to perform sacrifices and vows and sojourns to sacred waters and places.

data.v: यथा विश्वानि भूतानि वृष्ट्या भूयांसि प्रावृषि । सृज्यन्ते जङ्गमस्थानि तथा धर्मा युगे युगे ॥
data.md: As in the rainy reason a large variety of new objets of the immobile order are caused to come into being by the showers that fall from the clouds, so many new kinds of duty or religious observances are brought about in each new cycle.

data.v: यथर्तुष्वृतुलिङ्गानि नानारूपाणि पर्यये । दृश्यन्ते तानि तान्येव तथा ब्रह्माहरात्रिषु ॥
data.md: As the same phenomena reappear with the reappearance of the seasons, so, at each new Creation of the same attributes appear in each new Brahman and Hara.

data.v: विहितं कालनानात्वमनादिनिधनं तथा । कीर्तितं यत्पुरस्तात्ते तत्सूते चात्ति च प्रजाः ॥
data.md: I have, before this, spoken to you of Time which is without beginning and without end, which ordains this variety in the universe. It is that Time which creates and destroys all creatures.

data.v: दधाति प्रभवे स्थानं भूतानां संयमो यमः । स्वभावेनैव वर्तन्ते द्वंद्वयुक्तानि भूरिशः ॥
data.md: All the numberless creatures which exist subject to pairs of opposites and according to their respective natures, have Time for their refuge. It is Time that puts on those forms and it is Time which upholds them.]

data.v: सर्गः कालः क्रिया वेदाः कर्ता कार्यं क्रिया फलम् । प्रोक्तं ते पुत्र सर्वं वै यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥
data.md: I have thus described to you, O son, the topics about which you had asked, viz., Creation, Time, Sacrifices and other rites, the Vedas, the real actor in the universe, action, and the results of action.

data.v: प्रत्याहारं तु वक्ष्यामि शर्वर्यादौ गतेऽहनि । यथेदं कुरुतेऽध्यात्मं सुसूक्ष्मं विश्वमीश्वरः ॥
data.md: Vyasa said I shall now tell you how, when his day is gone and his night comes, he withdraws ali things to himself, or how the Supreme Master, making this gross universe exceedingly subtile, inerges every thing into his Soul.

data.v: दिवि सूर्यास्तथा सप्त दहन्ति शिखिनोऽर्चिषा । सर्वमेतत्तदार्चिर्भिः पूर्णं जाज्वल्यते जगत् ॥
data.md: When the time for universal dissolution comes twelve Suns, and Agni with his seven flames, begin to burn. Wrapt by those flames, the entire universe begins to blaze forth in a huge fire.

data.v: पृथिव्यां यानि भूतानि जङ्गमानि ध्रुवाणि च । तान्येवाग्रे प्रलीयन्ते भूमित्वमुपयान्ति च ॥
data.md: All things mobile and immobile that are on the Earth first disappear and merge into the substance of which this planet is formed.

data.v: ततः प्रलीने सर्वस्मिन्स्थावरे जङ्गमे तथा । अकाष्ठा निस्तृणा भूमिर्दृश्यते कूर्मपृष्ठवत् ॥
data.md: After all mobile and immobile objects have thus disappeared, the Earth, shorn of trees and herbs, looks nude like a tortoise shell.

data.v: भूमेरपि गुणं गन्धमाप आददते यदा । आत्तगन्धा तदा भूमिः प्रलयत्वाय कल्पते ॥
data.md: Then water takes up the attribute of earth, viz., scent. When earth becomes shorn of its principal attribute, that element is about to be destroyed.

data.v: आपस्ततः प्रतिष्ठन्ति ऊर्मिमत्यो महास्वनाः । सर्वमेवेदमापूर्य तिष्ठन्ति च चरन्ति च ॥
data.md: Water then prevails. Surging into big billows and roaring dreadfully only water fills this space and moves about or stands still.

data.v: अपामपि गुणांस्तात ज्योतिराददते यदा । आपस्तदा आत्तगुणा ज्योतिष्युपरमन्ति च ॥
data.md: Then the attribute of water is taken by Heat, and losing its own attribute, water emerges in that element.

data.v: यदादित्यं स्थितं मध्ये गूहन्ति शिखिनोऽर्चिषः । सर्वमेवेदमर्चिर्भिः पूर्णं जाज्वल्यते नभः ॥
data.md: When the time for universal dissolution comes twelve Suns, and Agni with his seven flames, begin to burn. Wrapt by those flames, the entire universe begins to blaze forth in a huge fire.

data.v: ज्योतिषोऽपि गुणं रूपं वायुराददते यदा । प्रशाम्यति तदा ज्योतिर्वायुर्दोधूयते महान् ॥
data.md: Then Wind comes and takes the attribute, viz., form, of Heat of Light, which, possessed of great power, begins to be awfully agitated.

data.v: ततस्तु मूलमासाद्य वायुः संभवमात्मनः । अधश्चोर्ध्वं च तिर्यक्च दोधवीति दिशो दश ॥
data.md: Obtaining its own attribute, viz., sound the Wind begins to move upwards and downwards and transversely along all the ten points.

data.v: वायोरपि गुणं स्पर्शमाकाशं ग्रसते यदा । प्रशाम्यति तदा वायुः खं तु तिष्ठति नानदत् ॥
data.md: Then Space takes the attribute, viz., sound, of Wind, upon which the latter is extinguished and enters into a state of existence resembling that of unheard or unuttered sound.

data.v: आकाशस्य गुणं शब्दमभिव्यक्तात्मकं मनः । मनसो व्यक्तमव्यक्तं ब्राह्मः स प्रतिसंचरः ॥
data.md: Then sound, which is the attribute of space, is swallowed up by Mind which is the essence of all manifest things. Thus Mind which in itself is unmanifest withdraws all that is manifested by Mind. This withdrawal of manifest Mind into unmanifest Mind, is called the destruction of the external universe.

data.v: तदात्मगुणमाविश्य मनो ग्रसति चन्द्रमाः । मनस्युपरतेऽध्यात्मा चन्द्रमस्यवतिष्ठते ॥
data.md: Then the Moon having made Mind withdraw its attribute into itself, swallows it up. When Mind, ceasing to exist, thus enters into the Moon, the other attributes of Creator are all that remain.

data.v: तं तु कालेन महता संकल्पः कुरुते वशे । चित्तं ग्रसति संकल्पस्तच्च ज्ञानमनुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: This Moon which is called also determination, is then, after a very long time, brought under Creator's sway, the reason being that determination has to perform a very difficult work, viz., the destruction of the faculties that are employed in the process of judgement. When this has been done, the condition reached is said to be of high knowledge.

data.v: कालो गिरति विज्ञानं कालो बलमिति श्रुतिः । बलं कालो ग्रसति तु तं विद्वान्कुरुते वशे ॥
data.md: Then time swallows up this Knowledge, and as the Shruti says, Time itself in its turn is devoured by Might or Energy. Might or cnergy, however, is (again) devoured by time, which last is then brought under her sway by kilowledge.

data.v: आकाशस्य तदा घोषं तं विद्वान्कुरुतेऽऽत्मनि । तदव्यक्तं परं ब्रह्म तच्छाश्वतमनुत्तमम् । एवं सर्वाणि भूतानि ब्रह्मैव प्रतिसंचरः ॥
data.md: Possessed of Knowledge, the Creator then swallows up non-existence itself into his Soui. That is Unmanifest and Supreme Brahma. That is Eternal, and that is the Highest of the High. Thus all existent creatures are withdrawn into Brahma.

data.v: यथावत्कीर्तितं सम्यगेवमेतदसंशयम् । बोध्यं विद्यामयं दृष्ट्वा योगिभिः परमात्मभिः ॥
data.md: Truly has this, which should be conceived (with the aid of the scriptures) and which is a topic of Science, been thus said by Yogins endued with Supreme Souls, after actual experience.

data.v: एवं विस्तारसंक्षेपौ ब्रह्माव्यक्ते पुनः पुनः । युगसाहस्रयोरादावह्नो रात्र्यास्तथैव च ॥
data.md: Even thus does Unmanifest Brahma repeatedly practise the processes of Creation and Destruction, and even thus are Brahman's Day and Night each consisting of a thousand Yugas.

data.v: भूतग्रामे नियुक्तं यत्तदेतत्कीर्तितं मया । ब्राह्मणस्य तु यत्कृत्यं तत्ते वक्ष्यामि पृच्छते ॥
data.md: Vyasa said-I have described to you fully that which you had asked me about the Creation of all beings. Listen to me as I tell you now what the duties are of a Brahmana.

data.v: जातकर्मप्रभृत्यस्य कर्मणां दक्षिणावताम् । क्रिया स्यादा समावृत्तेराचार्ये वेदपारगे ॥
data.md: The rituals of all ceremonies for which sacrificial fees are sanctioned, beginning with birth-rite and ending with Sama-vartana (return from preceptor's house) depend for their performance upon a preceptor well-versed in the Vedas.

data.v: अधीत्य वेदानखिलान्गुरुशुश्रूषणे रतः । गुरूणामनृणो भूत्वा समावर्तेत यज्ञवित् ॥
data.md: Having read all the Vedas and having showed submission towards his preceptor while living with him, and having paid the preceptor's fee, the youth should return home with a perfect knowledge of all sacrifices.

data.v: आचार्येणाभ्यनुज्ञातश्चतुर्णामेकमाश्रमम् । आ विमोक्षाच्छरीरस्य सोऽनुतिष्ठेद्यथाविधि ॥
data.md: Obtaining the permission of his preceptor, he should follow one of the four modes of life and live in it duly satisfying its duties till he renounces his body.

data.v: प्रजासर्गेण दारैश्च ब्रह्मचर्येण वा पुनः । वने गुरुसकाशे वा यतिधर्मेण वा पुनः ॥
data.md: He should either live like a house-holder with wives and engaged in creating offspring, or live the life of celibacy or in the forest in the company of his preceptor, or follow the duties of a Yati.

data.v: गृहस्थस्त्वेव सर्वेषां चतुर्णां मूलमुच्यते । तत्र पक्वकषायो हि दान्तः सर्वत्र सिध्यति ॥
data.md: A house-holder's life is said to be the root of all the other modes of life. A self-controlled house-holder who has mastered all his attachments of worldly objects always becomes successful.

data.v: प्रजावाञ्श्रोत्रियो यज्वा मुक्तो दिव्यैस्त्रिभिरृणैः । अथान्यानाश्रमान्पश्चात्पूतो गच्छति कर्मभिः ॥
data.md: By procreating children, by gaining a knowledge of the Vedas, and by celebrating sacrifices, a Brahmana satisfies the three debts he owes. He should then enter the other inodes of life, having purified himself by his acts.

data.v: यत्पृथिव्यां पुण्यतमं विद्यास्थानं तदावसेत् । यतेत तस्मिन्प्रामाण्यं गन्तुं यशसि चोत्तमे ॥
data.md: He should live for good in that place which he may ascertain to be the most sacred spot on earth, and he should try, in all matters leading to fame, for attaining to an eminent position.

data.v: तपसा वा सुमहता विद्यानां पारणेन वा । इज्यया वा प्रदानैर्वा विप्राणां वर्धते यशः ॥
data.md: The fame of Brahmanas increases through austere penances, through mastery of the various branches of knowledge, through sacrifices, and through gifts.

data.v: यावदस्य भवत्यस्मिँल्लोके कीर्तिर्यशस्करी । तावत्पुण्यकृताँल्लोकाननन्तान्पुरुषोऽश्नुते ॥
data.md: Truly, a person enjoys endless regions of the righteous as long as his deeds or the memory thereof exists in this world.

data.v: अध्यापयेदधीयीत याजयेत यजेत च । न वृथा प्रतिगृह्णीयान्न च दद्यात्कथंचन ॥
data.md: A Brahmana should teach, study, officiate at other people's sacrifices, and offer sacrifices himself. He should not give away uselessly or accept other people's gifts uselessly.

data.v: याज्यतः शिष्यतो वापि कन्यया वा धनं महत् । यद्यागच्छेद्यजेद्दद्यान्नैकोऽश्नीयात्कथंचन ॥
data.md: Profuse wealth, that may come from one who is assisted in a sacrifice, from a pupil, or from marriage of a daughter, should be spent in the celebration of a sacrifice, or in making gifts. Wealth coming from any of these sources should never be enjoyed by a Brahmana alone.

data.v: गृहमावसतो ह्यस्य नान्यत्तीर्थं प्रतिग्रहात् । देवर्षिपितृगुर्वर्थं वृद्धातुरबुभुक्षताम् ॥
data.md: For a Brahmana living like a house-holder, there is no means save the acceptance of gifts for the sake of the gods, or the Rishis, or the Pitris, or the preceptor, or the aged, or the diseased, or the hungry.

data.v: अन्तर्हिताभितप्तानां यथाशक्ति बुभूषताम् । द्रव्याणामतिशक्त्यापि देयमेषां कृतादपि ॥
data.md: One should make gifts from his own siock, including even cooked food, more than he can fairly afford, to those who are persecuted by unseen foes, or those who are trying to the best of their power to acquire Knowledge.

data.v: अर्हतामनुरूपाणां नादेयं ह्यस्ति किंचन । उच्चैःश्रवसमप्यश्वं प्रापणीयं सतां विदुः ॥
data.md: There is nothing that cannot be given to a deserving person. The good and the wise deserve to have even the best of horses, called Uchchaishravas, belonging to Indra himself.

data.v: अनुनीय तथा काव्यः सत्यसंधो महाव्रतः । स्वैः प्राणैर्ब्राह्मणप्राणान्परित्राय दिवं गतः ॥
data.md: Of high vows, Satyasanaha, having, with due humility, offered his own life for saving a Brahmana, ascended to heaven.

data.v: रन्तिदेवश्च सांकृत्यो वसिष्ठाय महात्मने । अपः प्रदाय शीतोष्णा नाकपृष्ठे महीयते ॥
data.md: Sankriti's son Rantideva, having given only lukewarm water to the great Vasistha, ascended to heaven and received great honours there.

data.v: आत्रेयश्चन्द्रदमयोरर्हतोर्विविधं धनम् । दत्त्वा लोकान्ययौ धीमाननन्तान्स महीपतिः ॥
data.md: Aftri's royal and highly intelligent son Indradamana, having given various kinds of wealth to a deserving person, acquired various regions of felicity in the next world,

data.v: शिबिरौशीनरोऽङ्गानि सुतं च प्रियमौरसम् । ब्राह्मणार्थमुपाकृत्य नाकपृष्ठमितो गतः ॥
data.md: Ushinara's son Shivi, having given away his own limbs and his dear son for the sake of a Brahmana, ascended to heaven from this world.

data.v: प्रतर्दनः काशिपतिः प्रदाय नयने स्वके । ब्राह्मणायातुलां कीर्तिमिह चामुत्र चाश्नुते ॥
data.md: Having given away his very eyes to a Brahmana, Pratarddana, the king of Kasi, enjoyed great fame both here and hereafter.

data.v: दिव्यं मृष्टशलाकं तु सौवर्णं परमर्द्धिमत् । छत्रं देवावृधो दत्त्वा सराष्ट्रोऽभ्यपतद्दिवम् ॥
data.md: Having given away a very beautiful and costly umbrella, with eight golden ribs, King Devavriddha proceeded to heaven with all the denizens of his kingdom.

data.v: सांकृतिश्च तथात्रेयः शिष्येभ्यो ब्रह्म निर्गुणम् । उपदिश्य महातेजा गतो लोकाननुत्तमान् ॥
data.md: Having given instruction to his disciples on the subject of Impersonal Brahma, Sanskriti of Atri's race, endued with great energy, proceeded to the regions of great felicity.

data.v: अम्बरीषो गवां दत्त्वा ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रतापवान् । अर्बुदानि दशैकं च सराष्ट्रोऽभ्यपतद्दिवम् ॥
data.md: Having given to the Brahmanas eleven Arvudas of kine, Amvarisha of great prowess, proceeded to heaven with all the denizens of his kingdom.

data.v: सावित्री कुण्डले दिव्ये शरीरं जनमेजयः । ब्राह्मणार्थे परित्यज्य जग्मतुर्लोकमुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: By giving away her ear-rings, Savitri, and, by giving away his own body, king Janamejaya both proceeded to high regions of felicity.

data.v: सर्वरत्नं वृषादर्भो युवनाश्वः प्रियाः स्त्रियः । रम्यमावसथं चैव दत्त्वामुं लोकमास्थितः ॥
data.md: By giving away various kinds of gems, a fine palace, and inany beautiful women, Yuvanashva the son of Vrishadabha ascended to heaven.

data.v: निमी राष्ट्रं च वैदेहो जामदग्न्यो वसुंधराम् । ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ चापि गयश्चोर्वीं सपत्तनाम् ॥
data.md: Nimi, the king the Videhas, gave away his kingdom, Jamadagni's son (Rama) gave away the whole Earth; and Gaya gave away the Earth with all her towns and cities, to the Brahmanas.

data.v: अवर्षति च पर्जन्ये सर्वभूतानि चासकृत् । वसिष्ठो जीवयामास प्रजापतिरिव प्रजाः ॥
data.md: Once when the clouds ceased to pour, Vashishtha, resembling Brahman himself, kept alive all creatures like Prajapati (by his power and kindness).

data.v: करंधमस्य पुत्रस्तु मरुत्तो नृपतिस्तथा । कन्यामङ्गिरसे दत्त्वा दिवमाशु जगाम ह ॥
data.md: By giving away his daughter to Angiras, Karandha's son Marutta of purified soul, quickly ascended to heaven.

data.v: ब्रह्मदत्तश्च पाञ्चाल्यो राजा बुद्धिमतां वरः । निधिं शङ्खं द्विजाग्र्येभ्यो दत्त्वा लोकानवाप्तवान् ॥
data.md: Brahmadatta, the king of the Panchalas, possessed of great intelligence, by giving away two costly jewels called Nidhi and Shankha to some of the foremost of the Brahmanas, acquired many regions of felicity.

data.v: राजा मित्रसहश्चापि वसिष्ठाय महात्मने । मदयन्तीं प्रियां दत्त्वा तया सह दिवं गतः ॥
data.md: Having given his own dear wife Mayadanti to the great Vasistha, King Mitrasaha ascenued to heaven with that wife of his.

data.v: सहस्रजिच्च राजर्षिः प्राणानिष्टान्महायशाः । ब्राह्मणार्थे परित्यज्य गतो लोकाननुत्तमान् ॥
data.md: The royal and highly illustrious sage Shasrajit, having cast off his own dear life for the sake of a Brahmana, ascended to regions of great happiness.

data.v: सर्वकामैश्च संपूर्णं दत्त्वा वेश्म हिरण्मयम् । मुद्गलाय गतः स्वर्गं शतद्युम्नो महीपतिः ॥
data.md: Having given to Mudgala a golden palace furnished with every object of comfort and use, king shatadyumna ascended to heaven.

data.v: नाम्ना च द्युतिमान्नाम शाल्वराजः प्रतापवान् । दत्त्वा राज्यमृचीकाय गतो लोकाननुत्तमान् ॥
data.md: The king of the Shalvas, named Dyatimat, endued with great prowess gave to Richika his entire kingdom and ascended to heaven.

data.v: मदिराश्वश्च राजर्षिर्दत्त्वा कन्यां सुमध्यमाम् । हिरण्यहस्ताय गतो लोकान्देवैरभिष्टुतान् ॥
data.md: By giving away daughter Shanta to Rishyarshringa, the highly powerful royal sage Lomapada obtained the fruition of all his wishes. By giving away his slender waisted daughter of Hiranyahasta, the royal sage Madirashva, ascended to regions esteemed of the very gods.

data.v: लोमपादश्च राजर्षिः शान्तां दत्त्वा सुतां प्रभुः । ऋश्यशृङ्गाय विपुलैः सर्वकामैरयुज्यत ॥
data.md: By giving away daughter Shanta to Rishyarshringa, the highly powerful royal sage Lomapada obtained the fruition of all his wishes. By giving away his slender waisted daughter of Hiranyahasta, the royal sage Madirashva, ascended to regions esteemed of the very gods.

data.v: दत्त्वा शतसहस्रं तु गवां राजा प्रसेनजित् । सवत्सानां महातेजा गतो लोकाननुत्तमान् ॥
data.md: By giving away a hundred thousand kine with calves, the highly energetic king Prasenajit ascended to excellent regions of happiness.

data.v: एते चान्ये च बहवो दानेन तपसा च ह । महात्मानो गताः स्वर्गं शिष्टात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः ॥
data.md: These and many others, endued with great and well-ordered souls, and having their senses under control, ascended, by means of gifts and penances, to heaven.

data.v: तेषां प्रतिष्ठिता कीर्तिर्यावत्स्थास्यति मेदिनी । दानयज्ञप्रजासर्गैरेते हि दिवमाप्नुवन् ॥
data.md: Their fame will last as long as the Earth lierself will exist. All of them have, by gifts and sacrifices and procreation of children proceeded to heaven.

data.v: त्रयीविद्यामवेक्षेत वेदेषूक्तामथाङ्गतः । ऋक्सामवर्णाक्षरतो यजुषोऽथर्वणस्तथा ॥
data.md: Vyasa said The three-fold knowledge which occurs in the Vedas and their branches should be required. That knowledge is to be got from the Richs, the Samans, and the sciences called Varna and Akshara. There are besides, the Yajushas and the Atharvans. The Divine Being lives in the six sorts of acts indicated in these.

data.v: वेदवादेषु कुशला ह्यध्यात्मकुशलाश्च ये । सत्त्ववन्तो महाभागाः पश्यन्ति प्रभवाप्ययौ ॥
data.md: They who are well-read in the injunctions of the Vedas, who have knowledge of the Soul, who are attached to the quality of Goodness, and who are highly blessed, succeed in understanding the origin and the end of all things.

data.v: एवं धर्मेण वर्तेत क्रियाः शिष्टवदाचरेत् । असंरोधेन भूतानां वृत्तिं लिप्सेत वै द्विजः ॥
data.md: A Brahmana should follow the duties laid down in the Vedas. He should do all his works like a good man of controlled soul. He should acquire his livelihood without injuring any creature.

data.v: सद्भ्य आगतविज्ञानः शिष्टः शास्त्रविचक्षणः । स्वधर्मेण क्रिया लोके कुर्वाणः सत्यसंगरः ॥
data.md: Having derived knowledge from the good and wise, he should govern his passions and desires. Well-versed in the scriptures, he should follow those duties which have been laid down for him, and do all works in this world guided by the qualities of goodness. Living even like a house-holder, the Brahmana should perform the six acts already spoken of.

data.v: तिष्ठत्येतेषु गृहवान्षट्सु कर्मसु स द्विजः । पञ्चभिः सततं यज्ञैः श्रद्दधानो यजेत च ॥
धृतिमानप्रमत्तश्च दान्तो धर्मविदात्मवान् । वीतहर्षभयक्रोधो ब्राह्मणो नावसीदति ॥
data.md: With his heart full of faith, he should adore the deities in the five well-known sacrifices. Possessed of patience, ever vigilant, having self-control, conversant with duties, with a purified soul, divested of joy, pride, and anger, the Brahmana should never sink in langour.

data.v: दानमध्ययनं यज्ञस्तपो ह्रीरार्जवं दमः । एतैर्वर्धयते तेजः पाप्मानं चापकर्षति ॥
data.md: Gifts, study of the Vedas, sacrifices, penances, modesty, guilelessness and selfcontrol,-these increase one's energy and dissipate one's sins.

data.v: धूतपाप्मा तु मेधावी लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः । कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा निनीषेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥
data.md: One gifted with intelligence should be abstemious in diet and should conquer his senses. Indeed, having subdued both lust and anger and having dissipated all his sins, he should try to attain Brahina.

data.v: अग्नींश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चार्चेद्देवताः प्रणमेत च । वर्जयेद्रुषतीं वाचं हिंसां चाधर्मसंहिताम् ॥
data.md: He should adore the Fire and Brahmanas, and bow to the gods. He should avoid all sorts of inauspicious talk, and all acts of unrighteous talk, and all acts of unrighteous injury.

data.v: एषा पूर्वतरा वृत्तिर्ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते । ज्ञानागमेन कर्माणि कुर्वन्कर्मसु सिध्यति ॥
data.md: This preliminary course of conduct is first sanctioned for a Brahmana. Subsequently, when knowledge comes, he should begin work, for success lies in works.

data.v: पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां घोरां लोभकूलां सुदुस्तराम् । मन्युपङ्कामनाधृष्यां नदीं तरति बुद्धिमान् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana who is gifted with intelligence succeeds in crossing over the river of life that is so difficult to cross and so furious a and terrible, having the five senses for its waters, cupidity for its origin, and anger for its mire.

data.v: काममन्यूद्धतं यत्स्यान्नित्यमत्यन्तमोहितम् । महता विधिदृष्टेन बलेनाप्रतिघातिना । स्वभावस्रोतसा वृत्तमुह्यते सततं जगत् ॥
data.md: He should never overlook the fact that Time stands behind him in threatening mien,-Time who is the great stupefier of all things, and who is armed with a very great and irresistible force issuing from the great Creator himself.

data.v: कालोदकेन महता वर्षावर्तेन संततम् । मासोर्मिणर्तुवेगेन पक्षोलपतृणेन च ॥
निमेषोन्मेषफेनेन अहोरात्रजवेन च । कामग्राहेण घोरेण वेदयज्ञप्लवेन च ॥
धर्मद्वीपेन भूतानां चार्थकामरवेण च । ऋतसोपानतीरेण विहिंसातरुवाहिना ॥
युगह्रदौघमध्येन ब्रह्मप्रायभवेन च । धात्रा सृष्टानि भूतानि कृष्यन्ते यमसादनम् ॥
एतत्प्रज्ञामयैर्धीरा निस्तरन्ति मनीषिणः । प्लवैरप्लववन्तो हि किं करिष्यन्त्यचेतसः ॥
data.md: Wise and patient persons always succeed in crossing over this dreadful river by engaging the rafts of knowledge and wisdom. What, however, can insensiate fools, destitute of similar rafts, do?

data.v: उपपन्नं हि यत्प्राज्ञो निस्तरेन्नेतरो जनः । दूरतो गुणदोषौ हि प्राज्ञः सर्वत्र पश्यति ॥
data.md: It is reasonable that only he that is wise should succeed in crossing this river and not the man of little understanding. The former sees from a distance the merits and faults of everything.

data.v: संशयात्मा स कामात्मा चलचित्तोऽल्पचेतनः । अप्राज्ञो न तरत्येव यो ह्यास्ते न स गच्छति ॥
data.md: The man, however, of weak and little understanding, and whose soul is full of desire and cupidity, is always stricken with doubt. Hence, the man shorn of wisdom never succeeds in crossing over that stream. He also who sits inactively, can never cross it over.

data.v: अप्लवो हि महादोषमुह्यमानोऽधिगच्छति । कामग्राहगृहीतस्य ज्ञानमप्यस्य न प्लवः ॥
data.md: The man shorn of the raft of wisdom in consequence of his having to bear the heavy burden of great faults, sinks down. One that is seized by the crocodile of desire, even if endued with knowledge, can never make knowledge his raft.

data.v: तस्मादुन्मज्जनस्यार्थे प्रयतेत विचक्षणः । एतदुन्मज्जनं तस्य यदयं ब्राह्मणो भवेत् ॥
data.md: For these reasons the wise and intelligent {}}en should try to float over the stream of Time. He indeed, succeeds in keeping himself afloat who knows Brahma.

data.v: त्र्यवदाते कुले जातस्त्रिसंदेहस्त्रिकर्मकृत् । तस्मादुन्मज्जनस्तिष्ठेन्निस्तरेत्प्रज्ञया यथा ॥
data.md: One born in a noble family, abstaining from the three duties of teaching, officiating at other's sacrifices, and accepting gifts, and doing only the three other acts, viz., studying, Sacrificing, and giving, should, for those reasons, try to float over the river. Such a man is sure to cross it over helped by the raft of wisdom.

data.v: संस्कृतस्य हि दान्तस्य नियतस्य कृतात्मनः । प्राज्ञस्यानन्तरा सिद्धिरिह लोके परत्र च ॥
data.md: One who is pure in conduct, who is selfcontrolled and observant of good vows, whose soul is under restraint, and who is endued with wisdom, certainly gains success in this and the other world.

data.v: वर्तते तेषु गृहवानक्रुध्यन्ननसूयकः । पञ्चभिः सततं यज्ञैर्विघसाशी यजेत च ॥
data.md: The Brahmana living like a house-holder should conquer anger and envy, practise the virtues already named, and adoring the gods in the five sacrifices, eat after having fed the gods, Pitris, and guests.

data.v: सतां वृत्तेन वर्तेत क्रियाः शिष्टवदाचरेत् । असंरोधेन धर्मस्य वृत्तिं लिप्सेदगर्हिताम् ॥
data.md: A Brahmana should follow the duties laid down in the Vedas. He should do all his works like a good man of controlled soul. He should acquire his livelihood without injuring any creature.

data.v: श्रुतिविज्ञानतत्त्वज्ञः शिष्टाचारो विचक्षणः । स्वधर्मेण क्रियावांश्च कर्मणा सोऽप्यसंकरः ॥
data.md: One who is well-read in the truths of the Vedas and the other branches of knowledge, whose conduct is like that of a person of wellgoverned soul, who is gifted with a clear vision, who follows the duties of his order, who does not by his acts make an intermixture of duties, who follows the observances laid down in the scriptures, who is endued with wisdom, who is shorn of envy and malice, and who is well conversant with the differences between righteous and iniquity, succeeds in overcoming all his difficulties.

data.v: क्रियावाञ्श्रद्दधानश्च दाता प्राज्ञोऽनसूयकः । धर्माधर्मविशेषज्ञः सर्वं तरति दुस्तरम् ॥
धृतिमानप्रमत्तश्च दान्तो धर्मविदात्मवान् । वीतहर्षभयक्रोधो ब्राह्मणो नावसीदति ॥
data.md: With his heart full of faith, he should adore the deities in the five well-known sacrifices. Possessed of patience, ever vigilant, having self-control, conversant with duties, with a purified soul, divested of joy, pride, and anger, the Brahmana should never sink in langour.

data.v: एषा पूर्वतरा वृत्तिर्ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते । ज्ञानवित्त्वेन कर्माणि कुर्वन्सर्वत्र सिध्यति ॥
data.md: This preliminary course of conduct is first sanctioned for a Brahmana. Subsequently, when knowledge comes, he should begin work, for success lies in works.

data.v: अधर्मं धर्मकामो हि करोतीहाविचक्षणः । धर्मं चाधर्मसंकाशं शोचन्निव करोति सः ॥
data.md: One who is not gifted with clear vision, does wrong even when one wishes to do right. By even exercising his judgement, such a person, does such acts of virtue as are wrong.

data.v: धर्मं करोमीति करोत्यधर्म;मधर्मकामश्च करोति धर्मम् । उभे बालः कर्मणी न प्रजान;न्स जायते म्रियते चापि देही ॥
data.md: Desiring to do what is right one does what is wrong. Likewise desiring to do what is wrong, one does what is right. Such a person is a fool. Not knowing the two kinds of acts, one has to go through repeated re-births and deaths.

data.v: अथ चेद्रोचयेदेतद्द्रुह्येत मनसा तथा । उन्मज्जंश्च निमज्जंश्च ज्ञानवान्प्लववान्भवेत् ॥
data.md: Vyasa said If Liberation is sought for, then knowledge should be acquired. For a person who is carried up and down along the stream of Time or life, Knowledge is the raft by which he can reach the shore.

data.v: प्रज्ञया निर्मितैर्धीरास्तारयन्त्यबुधान्प्लवैः । नाबुधास्तारयन्त्यन्यानात्मानं वा कथंचन ॥
data.md: Those wise men who have acquired fixed conclusions of the nature of the soul by the help of wisdom, are able of assist the ignorant in crossing the river of time or life with the raft of knowledge. The ignorant, are unable to save either themselves or others.

data.v: छिन्नदोषो मुनिर्योगान्युक्तो युञ्जीत द्वादश । दशकर्मसुखानर्थानुपायापायनिर्भयः ॥
data.md: He who has freed himself from desire and all other faults, and who has freed himself from all attachments, should attend to these twelve requirements of Yoga, viz., place, acts, affection, objects, means, destruction, certainty, eyes, food, suppression, mind and survey.

data.v: चक्षुराचारवित्प्राज्ञो मनसा दर्शनेन च । यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी बुद्ध्या य इच्छेज्ज्ञानमुत्तमम् । ज्ञानेन यच्छेदात्मानं य इच्छेच्छान्तिमात्मनः ॥
data.md: He who wishes to acquire superior Knowledge, should, by the help of his understanding, restrain both speech and mind. He who wishes to have tranquillity, should, by the help of his knowledge, govern his soul.

data.v: एतेषां चेदनुद्रष्टा पुरुषोऽपि सुदारुणः । यदि वा सर्ववेदज्ञो यदि वाप्यनृचोऽजपः ॥
यदि वा धार्मिको यज्वा यदि वा पापकृत्तमः । यदि वा पुरुषव्याघ्रो यदि वा क्लैब्यधारिता ॥
तरत्येव महादुर्गं जरामरणसागरम् । एवं ह्येतेन योगेन युञ्जानोऽप्येकमन्ततः । अपि जिज्ञासमानो हि शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
data.md: Without speaking of the results of the attainment of Brahma by Yoga, it may be said that he who engages himself to only enquire after the Soul rises above the necessity of observing the acts laid down in the Vedas.

data.v: धर्मोपस्थो ह्रीवरूथ उपायापायकूबरः । अपानाक्षः प्राणयुगः प्रज्ञायुर्जीवबन्धनः ॥
चेतनाबन्धुरश्चारुराचारग्रहनेमिवान् । दर्शनस्पर्शनवहो घ्राणश्रवणवाहनः ॥
प्रज्ञानाभिः सर्वतन्त्रप्रतोदो ज्ञानसारथिः । क्षेत्रज्ञाधिष्ठितो धीरः श्रद्धादमपुरःसरः ॥
त्यागवर्त्मानुगः क्षेम्यः शौचगो ध्यानगोचरः । जीवयुक्तो रथो दिव्यो ब्रह्मलोके विराजते ॥
अथ संत्वरमाणस्य रथमेतं युयुक्षतः । अक्षरं गन्तुमनसो विधिं वक्ष्यामि शीघ्रगम् ॥
data.md: I shall now tell you the speedy means that should be followed by the person who would get ready his car in such a way for passing through this forest of the world in order to reach the goal formed by Brahma that is above decrepitude and destruction.

data.v: सप्त यो धारणाः कृत्स्ना वाग्यतः प्रतिपद्यते । पृष्ठतः पार्श्वतश्चान्या यावत्यस्ताः प्रधारणाः ॥
data.md: To fix the mind upon one thing at a time is called Dharana, following proper vows and restraints, the Yogin practises in all seven kinds of Dharana. There are, again, as many sorts of Dharanas originating out of these, upon subjects which are near or distant.

data.v: क्रमशः पार्थिवं यच्च वायव्यं खं तथा पयः । ज्योतिषो यत्तदैश्वर्यमहंकारस्य बुद्धितः ॥
data.md: Through these the Yogin by and by, lords Earth, Wind, Ether, Water, Fire, Consciousness, and Understanding. After this he gradually lords over the Unmanifest.

data.v: अव्यक्तस्य तथैश्वर्यं क्रमशः प्रतिपद्यते । विक्रमाश्चापि यस्यैते तथा युङ्क्ते स योगतः ॥
अथास्य योगयुक्तस्य सिद्धिमात्मनि पश्यतः । निर्मथ्यमानः सूक्ष्मत्वाद्रूपाणीमानि दर्शयेत् ॥
शैशिरस्तु यथा धूमः सूक्ष्मः संश्रयते नभः । तथा देहाद्विमुक्तस्य पूर्वरूपं भवत्युत ॥
अथ धूमस्य विरमे द्वितीयं रूपदर्शनम् । जलरूपमिवाकाशे तत्रैवात्मनि पश्यति ॥
अपां व्यतिक्रमे चापि वह्निरूपं प्रकाशते । तस्मिन्नुपरते चास्य पीतवस्त्रवदिष्यते । ऊर्णारूपसवर्णं च तस्य रूपं प्रकाशते ॥
अथ श्वेतां गतिं गत्वा वायव्यं सूक्ष्ममप्यजः । अशुक्लं चेतसः सौक्ष्म्यमव्यक्तं ब्रह्मणोऽस्य वै ॥
data.md: Then having gained whiteness, and the subtility of air, the Brahman's soul attains the supreme whiteness and subtilety of Ether.

data.v: एतेष्वपि हि जातेषु फलजातानि मे शृणु । जातस्य पार्थिवैश्वर्ये सृष्टिरिष्टा विधीयते ॥
data.md: Listen to me, as I tell you the results of these various conditions when they take place. That Yogin who has been able to conquer the element of Earth, acquires by such mastery the power of Creation.

data.v: प्रजापतिरिवाक्षोभ्यः शरीरात्सृजति प्रजाः । अङ्गुल्यङ्गुष्ठमात्रेण हस्तपादेन वा तथा ॥
data.md: Like a second Prajapati possessed of a nature which knows no disturbances he can, from his own body, create all sorts of creatures. With only his foe, or with his hand or fcet, that person can, alone, make the entire Earth tremble who has conquered the Wind. Even this is the attribute of the Wind as said in the Shruti. The Yogin who has conquered count of his having attained to uniformity with that element, and can also disappear at will.

data.v: पृथिवीं कम्पयत्येको गुणो वायोरिति स्मृतः । आकाशभूतश्चाकाशे सवर्णत्वात्प्रणश्यति ॥
वर्णतो गृह्यते चापि कामात्पिबति चाशयान् । न चास्य तेजसा रूपं दृश्यते शाम्यते तथा ॥
data.md: By mastering over Water, one can drink up rivers, lakes, and oceans. By mastering over Fire, the Yogin becomes so effulgent that his form cannot be spied. He becomes visible only when he puts out the fire within him. When the Yogin succeeds in destroying the consciousness of Ego, these five elements come within his control.

data.v: अहंकारस्य विजितेः पञ्चैते स्युर्वशानुगाः । षण्णामात्मनि बुद्धौ च जितायां प्रभवत्यथ ॥
निर्दोषा प्रतिभा ह्येनं कृत्स्ना समभिवर्तते । तथैव व्यक्तमात्मानमव्यक्तं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
यतो निःसरते लोको भवति व्यक्तसंज्ञकः । तत्राव्यक्तमयीं व्याख्यां शृणु त्वं विस्तरेण मे । तथा व्यक्तमयीं चैव संख्यां पूर्वं निबोध मे ॥
data.md: Listen now to me fully as I explain the science of Unmanifest. But first of all listen to me about all that is Manifest as explained in the Sankhya system of philosophy.

data.v: पञ्चविंशतितत्त्वानि तुल्यान्युभयतः समम् । योगे सांख्येऽपि च तथा विशेषांस्तत्र मे शृणु ॥
data.md: In both the Yoga and the Sankhya systems, twenty-five subjects of knowledge have been treated in nearly the same way. Here me as I describe their chief characteristics.

data.v: प्रोक्तं तद्व्यक्तमित्येव जायते वर्धते च यत् । जीर्यते म्रियते चैव चतुर्भिर्लक्षणैर्युतम् ॥
data.md: What is Manifest is possessed of those four attributes, viz., birth, growth, decay and death.

data.v: विपरीतमतो यत्तु तदव्यक्तमुदाहृतम् । द्वावात्मानौ च वेदेषु सिद्धान्तेष्वप्युदाहृतौ ॥
data.md: What does not possess these attributes is said to to be Unmanifest. Two Souls are mentioned in the Vedas and in their auxiliary sciences.

data.v: चतुर्लक्षणजं त्वन्यं चतुर्वर्गं प्रचक्षते । व्यक्तमव्यक्तजं चैव तथा बुद्धमथेतरत् । सत्त्वं क्षेत्रज्ञ इत्येतद्द्वयमप्यनुदर्शितम् ॥
data.md: The first is endued with the four attributes already mentioned, and has a longing for the four-fold objects of life. This soul is called Manifest, and it is born of the Unmanifest. It is both Intelligent and non-Intelligent.

data.v: द्वावात्मानौ च वेदेषु विषयेषु च रज्यतः । विषयात्प्रतिसंहारः सांख्यानां सिद्धिलक्षणम् ॥
निर्ममश्चानहंकारो निर्द्वंद्वश्छिन्नसंशयः । नैव क्रुध्यति न द्वेष्टि नानृता भाषते गिरः ॥
आक्रुष्टस्ताडितश्चैव मैत्रेण ध्याति नाशुभम् । वाग्दण्डकर्ममनसां त्रयाणां च निवर्तकः ॥
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु ब्रह्माणमभिवर्तते । नैवेच्छति न चानिच्छो यात्रामात्रव्यवस्थितः ॥
अलोलुपोऽव्यथो दान्तो न कृती न निराकृतिः । नास्येन्द्रियमनेकाग्रं नातिक्षिप्तमनोरथः । अहिंस्रः सर्वभूतानामीदृक्सांख्यो विमुच्यते ॥
अथ योगाद्विमुच्यन्ते कारणैर्यैर्निबोध मे । योगैश्वर्यमतिक्रान्तो योऽतिक्रामति मुच्यते ॥
इत्येषा भावजा बुद्धिः कथिता ते न संशयः । एवं भवति निर्द्वंद्वो ब्रह्माणं चाधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: I have thus described to you those topics, viz., Liberation according to the Yoga system which are dissimilar if the speaker be disposed to treat them as such. Thus can one get over all pairs of opposites. thus can one attain to Brahma.

data.v: अथ ज्ञानप्लवं धीरो गृहीत्वा शान्तिमास्थितः । उन्मज्जंश्च निमज्जंश्च ज्ञानमेवाभिसंश्रयेत् ॥
data.md: Vyasa said Carried up and down in life's ocean, he that is capable of meditation catches the raft of Knowledge, and for achieving his Liberation adheres to Knowledge itself.

data.v: किं तज्ज्ञानमथो विद्या यया निस्तरति द्वयम् । प्रवृत्तिलक्षणो धर्मो निवृत्तिरिति चैव हि ॥
data.md: Shuka said What is that Knowledge? Is it that learning by which, when error is gone, the truth reveals itselt? Or, is it those duties consisting of acts to be done or achieved, by the help of which the object sought for, may be understood or attained? Or, is it those duties, called absention from acts by which an extinction of the Soul is to be sought? Do tell me what it is, so that by its help the two, viz., birth and death, may be avoided.

data.v: यस्तु पश्येत्स्वभावेन विना भावमचेतनः । पुष्यते च पुनः सर्वान्प्रज्ञया मुक्तहेतुकः ॥
data.md: Vyasa said That fool who, believing that all this exists by its own Nature without, in sooth, an eternal foundation, satisfies by such instruction the aspirations of disciples, defeating by his dialectical ingenuity the reasons the latter might urge to the contrary, succeeds not in acquiring any truth.

data.v: येषां चैकान्तभावेन स्वभावः कारणं मतम् । पूत्वा तृणबुसीकां वै ते लभन्ते न किंचन ॥
data.md: They again, who firinly believe that all Cause is due to the Nature of things, cannot acquire any truth by even listening to learned 17en or the Rishis.

data.v: ये चैनं पक्षमाश्रित्य वर्तयन्त्यल्पचेतसः । स्वभावं कारणं ज्ञात्वा न श्रेयः प्राप्नुवन्ति ते ॥
data.md: Those little-witted men who stop (in their speculations), having adopted either of these doctrines, those men who regard Nature as the Cause never succeed in acquiring any benefit for themselves.

data.v: स्वभावो हि विनाशाय मोहकर्ममनोभवः । निरुक्तमेतयोरेतत्स्वभावपरभावयोः ॥
data.md: This belief in Nature (as the producing and the sustaining Cause), originating as it does from a mind labouring under the influence of error, causes the destruction of the person who cherishes it. Hear of the truth regarding these two doctrines which hold (1) that things exist by their own Nature and (2) that they flow accordingly from others that are different form, and that precede, them.

data.v: कृष्यादीनि हि कर्माणि सस्यसंहरणानि च । प्रज्ञावद्भिः प्रकॢप्तानि यानासनगृहाणि च ॥
data.md: Wise men take to agriculture and tillage, and the acquisition of crops and of vehicles, seats, carpets and houses.

data.v: आक्रीडानां गृहाणां च गदानामगदस्य च । प्रज्ञावन्तः प्रवक्तारो ज्ञानवद्भिरनुष्ठिताः ॥
data.md: They also look to the laying of pleasuregardens, the construction of spacious palaces and the preparation of medicines for all sorts of diseases.

data.v: प्रज्ञा संयोजयत्यर्थैः प्रज्ञा श्रेयोऽधिगच्छति । राजानो भुञ्जते राज्यं प्रज्ञया तुल्यलक्षणाः ॥
data.md: It is wisdom (which consists in the application of means) which brings about the fruition of objects. It is wisdom which gains beneficial results. It is wisdom which enables kings to exercise and enjoy sovereignty although they are endued with attributes equal to those of persons over whom they rule.

data.v: पारावर्यं तु भूतानां ज्ञानेनैवोपलभ्यते । विद्यया तात सृष्टानां विद्यैव परमा गतिः ॥
data.md: It is by wisdom that the difference is made between the high and the low among beings. It is by wisdom that the superior and the inferior ones among created objects are made out. It is wisdom or knowledge which is greatest refuge of all things.

data.v: भूतानां जन्म सर्वेषां विविधानां चतुर्विधम् । जराय्वण्डमथोद्भेदं स्वेदं चाप्युपलक्षयेत् ॥
data.md: All the sorts of created things have four kinds of birth. They are viviparous, oviparous, vegetables, and those born of filth.

data.v: स्थावरेभ्यो विशिष्टानि जङ्गमान्युपलक्षयेत् । उपपन्नं हि यच्चेष्टा विशिष्येत विशेष्ययोः ॥
data.md: Mobile creatures should be regarded superior to the immobile. It is reasonable that intelligence which differentiates (all nonintelligent matter), should be considered superior to (non-intelligent) matter.

data.v: आहुर्द्विबहुपादानि जङ्गमानि द्वयानि च । बहुपाद्भ्यो विशिष्टानि द्विपादानि बहून्यपि ॥
data.md: Mobile creatures, whose number is legion, are of two sorts, viz., those that are many legs and those that have two. The latter, however, are superior to the former.

data.v: द्विपदानि द्वयान्याहुः पार्थिवानीतराणि च । पार्थिवानि विशिष्टानि तानि ह्यन्नानि भुञ्जते ॥
data.md: Bipeds, again, are of two sorts, viz., those that live on land and those that are otherwise. Of these, the former are superior to the latter. The superior ones eat various sorts of cooked food.

data.v: पार्थिवानि द्वयान्याहुर्मध्यमान्युत्तमानि च । मध्यमानि विशिष्टानि जातिधर्मोपधारणात् ॥
data.md: Bipeds moving on land are of two sorts, viz., middling or intermediate, and those that are foremost. Of these, the middling or intermediate are considered as superior (to the foriner) for their observing the duties of caste.

data.v: मध्यमानि द्वयान्याहुर्धर्मज्ञानीतराणि च । धर्मज्ञानि विशिष्टानि कार्याकार्योपधारणात् ॥
data.md: Bipeds moving on land are of two sorts, viz., middling or intermediate, and those that are foremost. Of these, the middling or intermediate are considered as superior (to the foriner) for their observing the duties of caste.

data.v: धर्मज्ञानि द्वयान्याहुर्वेदज्ञानीतराणि च । वेदज्ञानि विशिष्टानि वेदो ह्येषु प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
data.md: The middling or intermediate ones are said to be of two sorts, viz., those who are conversant with duties, and those who are otherwise. Of those, the former are superior for they can discriminate between what should be done and what should not.

data.v: वेदज्ञानि द्वयान्याहुः प्रवक्तॄणीतराणि च । प्रवक्तॄणि विशिष्टानि सर्वधर्मोपधारणात् ॥
data.md: Bipeds, again, are of two sorts, viz., those that live on land and those that are otherwise. Of these, the former are superior to the latter. The superior ones eat various sorts of cooked food.

data.v: विज्ञायन्ते हि यैर्वेदाः सर्वधर्मक्रियाफलाः । सयज्ञाः सखिला वेदाः प्रवक्तृभ्यो विनिःसृताः ॥
प्रवक्तॄणि द्वयान्याहुरात्मज्ञानीतराणि च । आत्मज्ञानि विशिष्टानि जन्माजन्मोपधारणात् ॥
data.md: Bipeds moving on land are of two sorts, viz., middling or intermediate, and those that are foremost. Of these, the middling or intermediate are considered as superior (to the foriner) for their observing the duties of caste.

data.v: धर्मद्वयं हि यो वेद स सर्वः सर्वधर्मविद् । स त्यागी सत्यसंकल्पः स तु क्षान्तः स ईश्वरः ॥
data.md: Duties, again, are of two kinds (viz., Pravritti and Nivritti). He who is conversant with duties is said to be omniscient or endued with universal knowledge. Such a man is a Renouncer. Such a man is firin in the fulfilment of his objects. Such a man is truthful, pure and endued with prowess.

data.v: धर्मज्ञानप्रतिष्ठं हि तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः । शब्दब्रह्मणि निष्णातं परे च कृतनिश्चयम् ॥
data.md: The gods know him as a Brahmana who is devoted to knowledge of Brahma. Such a man is versed also in the Vedas are earnestly given to the study of the Self.

data.v: अन्तःस्थं च बहिष्ठं च येऽऽधियज्ञाधिदैवतम् । जानन्ति तान्नमस्यामस्ते देवास्तात ते द्विजाः ॥
data.md: They who have true knowledge see their own self as existing both in and out. Such men, O child, are truly twice-born and such men are gods.

data.v: तेषु विश्वमिदं भूतं साग्रं च जगदाहितम् । तेषां माहात्म्यभावस्य सदृशं नास्ति किंचन ॥
data.md: This world of beings depends upon these, and in them exist this whole universe. There is nothing equal to their greatness.

data.v: आदिं ते निधनं चैव कर्म चातीत्य सर्वशः । चतुर्विधस्य भूतस्य सर्वस्येशाः स्वयंभुवः ॥
data.md: Transcending birth, and death, and distinctions and all acts, they are the lords of the four kinds of creatures, and are the equals of Self-create himself.

data.v: एषा पूर्वतरा वृत्तिर्ब्राह्मणस्य विधीयते । ज्ञानवानेव कर्माणि कुर्वन्सर्वत्र सिध्यति ॥
data.md: This preliminary course of conduct is first sanctioned for a Brahmana. Subsequently, when knowledge comes, he should begin work, for success lies in works.

data.v: तत्र चेन्न भवेदेवं संशयः कर्मनिश्चये । किं नु कर्म स्वभावोऽयं ज्ञानं कर्मेति वा पुनः ॥
data.md: If no doubt is entertained about acts, then acis done are sure to lead to success. The doubt we speak of is whether acts are obligatory or optional.

data.v: तत्र चेह विवित्सा स्याज्ज्ञानं चेत्पुरुषं प्रति । उपपत्त्युपलब्धिभ्यां वर्णयिष्यामि तच्छृणु ॥
data.md: About this if acts, are ordained for man for gaining knowledge, they should be considered as obligatory. I shall now describe them by the light of inferences and experience. Here me. some

data.v: पौरुषं कारणं केचिदाहुः कर्मसु मानवाः । दैवमेके प्रशंसन्ति स्वभावं चापरे जनाः ॥
data.md: Regarding acts men hold that Exertion is their root. Others say that Necessity is their cause. Others, again, hold that Nature is the cause.

data.v: पौरुषं कर्म दैवं च फलवृत्तिस्वभावतः । त्रयमेतत्पृथग्भूतमविवेकं तु केचन ॥
data.md: Others hold that Acts flowing from Exertion and Destiny, produce effects, helped by Nature. Instead of considering any of these as alone powerful for the production of effects, they say that it is the union of all three that produces all effects.

data.v: एवमेतन्न चाप्येवमुभे चापि न चाप्युभे । कर्मस्था विषमं ब्रूयुः सत्त्वस्थाः समदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: About this subject, some say that such is the case; some, that such is not the case; some, that both of these are not the case; and some that it is not that the reverse of both are not. These, of course, are the contentions of those who depend on Acts, with reference to objects. They, however, whose see the truth consider Brahma as the causes.

data.v: त्रेतायां द्वापरे चैव कलिजाश्च ससंशयाः । तपस्विनः प्रशान्ताश्च सत्त्वस्थाश्च कृते युगे ॥
data.md: The men of the Treta, the Dvapara, and the Kali Yugas, are filled with doubts. The men, however, the Krita Yuga, are given to penances, endued with tranquil souls, and observant of righteousness,

data.v: अपृथग्दर्शिनः सर्वे ऋक्सामसु यजुःषु च । कामद्वेषौ पृथग्दृष्ट्वा तपः कृत उपासते ॥
data.md: In that age all men consider the Richs, the Samans, and the Yajushes as Identical, despite their seeming diversity. Analysing desire and hatred, they adore only penance.

data.v: तपोधर्मेण संयुक्तस्तपोनित्यः सुसंशितः । तेन सर्वानवाप्नोति कामान्यान्मनसेच्छति ॥
data.md: Given to the practice of penances, firm in them, and rigid in their observance, one acquires the fruition of all desires by penances alone.

data.v: तपसा तदवाप्नोति यद्भूत्वा सृजते जगत् । तद्भूतश्च ततः सर्वो भूतानां भवति प्रभुः ॥
data.md: By penance one attains to that Being who creates the universe. He who thus succeeds in attaining to that Being becomes the powerful lord of all beings.

data.v: तदुक्तं वेदवादेषु गहनं वेददर्शिभिः । वेदान्तेषु पुनर्व्यक्तं क्रमयोगेन लक्ष्यते ॥
data.md: That incomprehensible Brahma which has been described in the words of the Vedas, and which has been described more clearly in the Upanishads by those who have an insight into the Vedas, can be realised by gradually following the practices referred to above.

data.v: आरम्भयज्ञाः क्षत्रस्य हविर्यज्ञा विशः स्मृताः । परिचारयज्ञाः शूद्राश्च जपयज्ञा द्विजातयः ॥
data.md: The destruction of animals is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Kshatriyas. The growing of corn is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Vaisshyas. Serving the three other orders is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Shudras. Penance is the sacrifice sanctioned for the Brahmanas.

data.v: परिनिष्ठितकार्यो हि स्वाध्यायेन द्विजो भवेत् । कुर्यादन्यन्न वा कुर्यान्मैत्रो ब्राह्मण उच्यते ॥
data.md: By observing the duties sanctioned for him, and by studying the Vedas and other scriptures, one becomes a twice-born one whether one does any other deed or not, he becomes a Brahmana by becoming the friend of all creatures.

data.v: त्रेतादौ सकला वेदा यज्ञा वर्णाश्रमास्तथा । संरोधादायुषस्त्वेते व्यस्यन्ते द्वापरे युगे ॥
data.md: Accordingly, in that age, the Vedas, and sacrifices, and the distinctions between the several orders, and the four modes of life, existed in a body. On account, however, of the decrease in the period of life in Dvapara, all these, it that age, fall off from that compact condition.

data.v: द्वापरे विप्लवं यान्ति वेदाः कलियुगे तथा । दृश्यन्ते नापि दृश्यन्ते कलेरन्ते पुनः पुनः ॥
data.md: In Dvapara age as also in the Kali, the Vedas become of doubtful interpretation. Towards the close of Kali again, it is doubtful if they ever can be seen by the eye.

data.v: उत्सीदन्ति स्वधर्माश्च तत्राधर्मेण पीडिताः । गवां भूमेश्च ये चापामोषधीनां च ये रसाः ॥
data.md: In that age, the duties of the respective castes disappear, and men become possessed by sin, the juicy attributes of kine, of the earth, of water, and of herbs, disappear.

data.v: अधर्मान्तर्हिता वेदा वेदधर्मास्तथाश्रमाः । विक्रियन्ते स्वधर्मस्थाः स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥
data.md: Through (universal) sin the Vedas disappear, and with them all the duties laid down in them, as also the duties of the four imodes of life. They who follow the duties, of their own order become afflicted, and all mobile and immobile objects suffer a change for the worse.

data.v: यथा सर्वाणि भूतानि वृष्टिर्भौमानि वर्षति । सृजते सर्वतोऽङ्गानि तथा वेदा युगे युगे ॥
data.md: As the rain from the sky causes all products of the Earth to grow, likewise the Veda develops all its auxilliaries.

data.v: विसृतं कालनानात्वमनादिनिधनं च यत् । कीर्तितं तत्पुरस्तान्मे यतः संयान्ति यान्ति च ॥
data.md: I have, before this, spoken to you of Time which is without beginning and without end, which ordains this variety in the universe. It is that Time which creates and destroys all creatures.

data.v: धातेदं प्रभवस्थानं भूतानां संयमो यमः । स्वभावेन प्रवर्तन्ते द्वंद्वसृष्टानि भूरिशः ॥
data.md: All the numberless creatures which exist subject to pairs of opposites and according to their respective natures, have Time for their refuge. It is Time that puts on those forms and it is Time which upholds them.]

data.v: सर्गः कालो धृतिर्वेदाः कर्ता कार्यं क्रिया फलम् । एतत्ते कथितं तात यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥
data.md: Time is the origin of all creatures; it is Time which makes them grow; Time is their destroyer; and lastly it is Time which is their ruler. Subject to pairs of opposites, innumerable sorts of creatures rest on Time, according to their own natures.

data.v: इत्युक्तोऽभिप्रशस्यैतत्परमर्षेस्तु शासनम् । मोक्षधर्मार्थसंयुक्तमिदं प्रष्टुं प्रचक्रमे ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Thus addressed by his father, Shuka, highly praising these instructions of the great Rishi, began to ask the following questions regarding the import of duties which brings on Liberation.

data.v: प्रजावाञ्श्रोत्रियो यज्वा वृद्धः प्रज्ञोऽनसूयकः । अनागतमनैतिह्यं कथं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: Shuka said By what means does a wise man well-read in the Vedas, observant of sacrifices, and shorn of malice attains to Brahma which is incapable of being apprehended by either direct evidence or inference, and incapable of being described by the Vedas.

data.v: तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण सर्वत्यागेन मेधया । सांख्ये वा यदि वा योगे एतत्पृष्टोऽभिधत्स्व मे ॥
data.md: Asked by me, tell me by what means can Brahma be known. Is it by penance, by Brahmacharya, by renunciation of everything, by intelligence, by help of the Sankhya philosophy, or by the Yoga?

data.v: मनसश्चेन्द्रियाणां चाप्यैकाग्र्यं समवाप्यते । येनोपायेन पुरुषैस्तच्च व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: What are the means and what sort of singleness of purpose may inen acquire regarding both, viz., the mind and the senses? You should explain all this to me!

data.v: नान्यत्र विद्यातपसोर्नान्यत्रेन्द्रियनिग्रहात् । नान्यत्र सर्वसंत्यागात्सिद्धिं विन्दति कश्चन ॥
data.md: Vyasa said No man achieves success by any other means save the acquisition of knowledge, the practice of penances, the control of the senses, and renunciation of everything.

data.v: महाभूतानि सर्वाणि पूर्वसृष्टिः स्वयंभुवः । भूयिष्ठं प्राणभृद्ग्रामे निविष्टानि शरीरिषु ॥
data.md: The great elements (five in number) represent the first creation of the Self-create. They have been very largely put in embodied creatures living in the world of life.

data.v: भूमेर्देहो जलात्सारो ज्योतिषश्चक्षुषी स्मृते । प्राणापानाश्रयो वायुः खेष्वाकाशं शरीरिणाम् ॥
data.md: The bodies of all embodied creatures are originated from earth. Their humours originate from water. Their eyes originate from light. Prana, Apana (and other vital breaths), depend on the wind. And, lastly, all unoccupied apertures within them originate from Space.

data.v: क्रान्ते विष्णुर्बले शक्रः कोष्ठेऽग्निर्भुक्तमर्छति । कर्णयोः प्रदिशः श्रोत्रे जिह्वायां वाक्सरस्वती ॥
data.md: Vishnu is in the feet (of living creatures). Indra is in their arms. Within the stomach lies Agni, desirous of eating. The points of the horizon are in the ears, the organ of hearing. Speech, which is the goddess of learning, is in the tongue.

data.v: कर्णौ त्वक्चक्षुषी जिह्वा नासिका चैव पञ्चमी । दर्शनानीन्द्रियोक्तानि द्वाराण्याहारसिद्धये ॥
data.md: The ears, skin, eyes, tongue, and nose forming the fifth, are the senses of knowledge. These exist for apprehending their respective objects.

data.v: शब्दं स्पर्शं तथा रूपं रसं गन्धं च पञ्चमम् । इन्द्रियाणि पृथक्त्वर्थान्मनसो दर्शयन्त्युत ॥
data.md: Sound, touch, from, taste, and scent for the fifth, are the objects of the (five) senses. These should always be considered as distinct from the senses.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणि मनो युङ्क्ते वश्यान्यन्तेव वाजिनः । मनश्चापि सदा युङ्क्ते भूतात्मा हृदयाश्रितः ॥
data.md: Like the charioteer driving his well trained horses along the paths he likes, the mind, imoves the senses. The mind, in its turn, is inoved by the Understanding sitting in the heart.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणां तथैवेषां सर्वेषामीश्वरं मनः । नियमे च विसर्गे च भूतात्मा मनसस्तथा ॥
data.md: The mind is the lord of all these senses employing them in their functions and guiding controlling them. Likewise, the Understanding is the lord of the mind.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थाश्च स्वभावश्चेतना मनः । प्राणापानौ च जीवश्च नित्यं देहेषु देहिनाम् ॥
data.md: The senses, the objects of the senses, the attributes of the objects of Nature, understanding, mind, the vital our and individual soul dwell in the bodies of all embodied creatures.

data.v: आश्रयो नास्ति सत्त्वस्य गुणशब्दो न चेतना । सत्त्वं हि तेजः सृजति न गुणान्वै कदाचन ॥
data.md: The body within which the Understanding lives, has no real existence. The body, therefore, is not the seat of the Understanding. Nature (Prakriti), endued with three qualities, is the refuge of the Understanding which exists only in the form of a sound. The Soul also is not the refuge of the Understanding. It is Desire which creates the Understanding. Desire, however, never creates the three qualities.

data.v: एवं सप्तदशं देहे वृतं षोडशभिर्गुणैः । मनीषी मनसा विप्रः पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि ॥
data.md: The wise man, capable of controlling his senses, sees the seventeenth, viz., the Soul as surrounded by six and ten qualities, in his own Understanding by the help of the mind.

data.v: न ह्ययं चक्षुषा दृश्यो न च सर्वैरपीन्द्रियैः । मनसा संप्रदीप्तेन महानात्मा प्रकाशते ॥
data.md: The Soul cannot be seen with the help of the eye, or with that of all the senses. Getting over all, the Soul can be seen by only the light of the mind's lamp.

data.v: अशब्दस्पर्शरूपं तदरसागन्धमव्ययम् । अशरीरं शरीरे स्वे निरीक्षेत निरिन्द्रियम् ॥
data.md: Shorn of the properties of sound and touch and form, without taste and smell, indestructible and without a body and without senses, it is nevertheless seen within the body.

data.v: अव्यक्तं व्यक्तदेहेषु मर्त्येष्वमरमाश्रितम् । योऽनुपश्यति स प्रेत्य कल्पते ब्रह्मभूयसे ॥
data.md: Unmanifest and supreme, it lives in all mortal frames, Guided by the preceptor and the Vedas, he who sees it hereafter becomes Brahma's self.

data.v: विद्याभिजनसंपन्ने ब्राह्मणे गवि हस्तिनि । शुनि चैव श्वपाके च पण्डिताः समदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: The wise see impartially a Brahmana gifted with knowledge and disciples, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and a Chandala.

data.v: स हि सर्वेषु भूतेषु जङ्गमेषु ध्रुवेषु च । वसत्येको महानात्मा येन सर्वमिदं ततम् ॥
data.md: Transcending all things, the Soul lives in all creatures, mobile and immobile.

data.v: सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । यदा पश्यति भूतात्मा ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
data.md: When a living creature sees his own Soul in all things, and all things in his own Soul, he is said to attain to Brahma.

data.v: यावानात्मनि वेदात्मा तावानात्मा परात्मनि । य एवं सततं वेद सोऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
data.md: One occupies the Supreme Soul proportionate to what is occupied in one's own soul by Vedic sound. He who can always realise the identity of all things with his own self, forsooth, acquires immortality.

data.v: सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्य सर्वभूतहितस्य च । देवापि मार्गे मुह्यन्ति अपदस्य पदैषिणः ॥
data.md: Even the gods are stupefied in the path of that trackless man who forms the soul of all creatures, who is engaged in the well being of all creatures and who wishes to attain to the final refuge (of all things).

data.v: शकुनीनामिवाकाशे जले वारिचरस्य वा । यथा गतिर्न दृश्येत तथैव सुमहात्मनः ॥
data.md: Indeed, the road which is followed by men of knowledge is as invisible as that of birds in the sky or of fish in water.

data.v: कालः पचति भूतानि सर्वाण्येवात्मनात्मनि । यस्मिंस्तु पच्यते कालस्तं न वेदेह कश्चन ॥
data.md: Time, by its own power, cooks all entities within itself. No one, however, knows That in which Time, again, is itself cooked.

data.v: न तदूर्ध्वं न तिर्यक्च नाधो न च तिरः पुनः । न मध्ये प्रतिगृह्णीते नैव कश्चित्कुतश्चन ॥
data.md: That does not take place above, or in the middle or below, or in transverse or in any Other direction. That is no tangible thing and cannot be found in any placc.

data.v: सर्वेऽन्तःस्था इमे लोका बाह्यमेषां न किंचन । यः सहस्रं समागच्छेद्यथा बाणो गुणच्युतः ॥
नैवान्तं कारणस्येयाद्यद्यपि स्यान्मनोजवः । तस्मात्सूक्ष्मात्सूक्ष्मतरं नास्ति स्थूलतरं ततः ॥
data.md: All these worlds exists within That. There is nothing in these worlds which exists out of That. Even if one goes on ceaselessly with the motion of arrow shot off the bow-string, even if one goes on with the speed of the mind itself, one would not still get at the end of that which is the cause of all this. There is nothing grosser than that.

data.v: सर्वतःपाणिपादान्तं सर्वतोक्षिशिरोमुखम् । सर्वतःश्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
data.md: His hands and feet are everywhere. His cyes, head, and face are everywhere. His ears are everywhere in the universe. He exists Occupying all things.

data.v: तदेवाणोरणुतरं तन्महद्भ्यो महत्तरम् । तदन्तः सर्वभूतानां ध्रुवं तिष्ठन्न दृश्यते ॥
data.md: That is minuter than the minutest, and is the heart of all things. Though existing, that is still imperceptible.

data.v: अक्षरं च क्षरं चैव द्वैधीभावोऽयमात्मनः । क्षरः सर्वेषु भूतेषु दिव्यं ह्यमृतमक्षरम् ॥
data.md: Indestructible and destructible,-these are the dual forms of the (Supreme) Self. The existence it shows in all mobile and immobile entities is destructible; while the existence in shows in Chaitanya is celestial, immortal, and indestructible.

data.v: नवद्वारं पुरं गत्वा हंसो हि नियतो वशी । ईशः सर्वस्य भूतस्य स्थावरस्य चरस्य च ॥
data.md: Though the master of all existent beings both mobile and immobile, though inactive and shorn of attributes, it enters nevertheless the well-known house of nine doors and becomes engaged in action.

data.v: हानिभङ्गविकल्पानां नवानां संश्रयेण च । शरीराणामजस्याहुर्हंसत्वं पारदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: Wise men who can see the other shore hold that the Supreme Soul becomes endued with the attribute of action on account of motion, pleasure and pain, variety of form, and the nine well-known possessions.

data.v: हंसोक्तं चाक्षरं चैव कूटस्थं यत्तदक्षरम् । तद्विद्वानक्षरं प्राप्य जहाति प्राणजन्मनी ॥
data.md: That indestructible Soul which is said to be endued with the attribute or action is nothing else than the indestructible Soul which is said to be inactive. A learned person, by attaining to that indestructible essence, gives up for ever both life and birth.

data.v: पृच्छतस्तव सत्पुत्र यथावदिह तत्त्वतः । सांख्यन्यायेन संयुक्तं यदेतत्कीर्तितं मया ॥
data.md: Vyasa said O excellent son, accosted by you. I have told you truly what the answer to your question should be according to the doctrine of Knowledge as explained in the Sankhya system.

data.v: योगकृत्यं तु ते कृत्स्नं वर्तयिष्यामि तच्छृणु । एकत्वं बुद्धिमनसोरिन्द्रियाणां च सर्वशः । आत्मनो ध्यायिनस्तात ज्ञानमेतदनुत्तमम् ॥
तदेतदुपशान्तेन दान्तेनाध्यात्मशीलिना । आत्मारामेण बुद्धेन बोद्धव्यं शुचिकर्मणा ॥
योगदोषान्समुच्छिद्य पञ्च यान्कवयो विदुः । कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च भयं स्वप्नं च पञ्चमम् ॥
क्रोधं शमेन जयति कामं संकल्पवर्जनात् । सत्त्वसंसेवनाद्धीरो निद्रामुच्छेत्तुमर्हति ॥
धृत्या शिश्नोदरं रक्षेत्पाणिपादं च चक्षुषा । चक्षुः श्रोत्रे च मनसा मनो वाचं च कर्मणा ॥
अप्रमादाद्भयं जह्याल्लोभं प्राज्ञोपसेवनात् । एवमेतान्योगदोषाञ्जयेन्नित्यमतन्द्रितः ॥
अग्नींश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चार्चेद्देवताः प्रणमेत च । वर्जयेद्रुषितां वाचं हिंसायुक्तां मनोनुगाम् ॥
data.md: He should adore the Fire and Brahmanas, and bow to the gods. He should avoid all sorts of inauspicious talk, and all acts of unrighteous talk, and all acts of unrighteous injury.

data.v: ब्रह्म तेजोमयं शुक्रं यस्य सर्वमिदं रसः । एकस्य भूतं भूतस्य द्वयं स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
data.md: Vyasa said Brahma is the effulgent seed from which existing as it does by itself, has originated the entire universe consisting of two kinds of being, viz., the mobile and the immobile,

data.v: ध्यानमध्ययनं दानं सत्यं ह्रीरार्जवं क्षमा । शौचमाहारसंशुद्धिरिन्द्रियाणां च निग्रहः ॥
data.md: Brahma became the eye, in the form of this mobile and immobile universe, of all elements that were born. Meditation, study, gift, truth, modesty, simplicity, forgiveness, purity of body, purity of conduct, and subjugation of the senses, these increase one's energy which dissipates his sins.

data.v: एतैर्विवर्धते तेजः पाप्मानं चापकर्षति । सिध्यन्ति चास्य सर्वार्था विज्ञानं च प्रवर्तते ॥
समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु लब्धालब्धेन वर्तयन् । धुतपाप्मा तु तेजस्वी लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः । कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा निनीषेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥
