data.md: One gifted with intelligence should be abstemious in diet and should conquer his senses. Indeed, having subdued both lust and anger and having dissipated all his sins, he should try to attain Brahina.

data.v: मनसश्चेन्द्रियाणां च कृत्वैकाग्र्यं समाहितः । प्राग्रात्रापररात्रेषु धारयेन्मन आत्मना ॥
data.md: Uniting firmly the senses and the mind with gaze fixed inwards, one should, in the silent hours of evening or those before dawn, fix his mind upon the understanding.

data.v: जन्तोः पञ्चेन्द्रियस्यास्य यदेकं छिद्रमिन्द्रियम् । ततोऽस्य स्रवति प्रज्ञा दृतेः पादादिवोदकम् ॥
data.md: If even one of the five senses of a human being be kept ungoverned all his wisdom escapes through it like water through a hole not made up at the bottom of a leather bag.

data.v: मनस्तु पूर्वमादद्यात्कुमीनानिव मत्स्यहा । ततः श्रोत्रं ततश्चक्षुर्जिह्वां घ्राणं च योगवित् ॥
data.md: The mind in the first instance should be controlled by the Yogin like a fisherman trying at the commencement to make that one among the fish powerless from which he auticipates the greatest danger to his nets. Having first governed the mind, the Yogin should then proceed to subdue his ears, then his tongue, and then his nose.

data.v: तत एतानि संयम्य मनसि स्थापयेद्यतिः । तथैवापोह्य संकल्पान्मनो ह्यात्मनि धारयेत् ॥
data.md: Having controlled these, he should fix there on the mind. Then withdrawing the mind from all purposes. He should settle it on the understanding.

data.v: पञ्च ज्ञानेन संधाय मनसि स्थापयेद्यतिः । यदैतान्यवतिष्ठन्ते मनःषष्ठानि चात्मनि । प्रसीदन्ति च संस्थाय तदा ब्रह्म प्रकाशते ॥
data.md: Indeed having governed the five senses, the Yati should fix them on the mind. When these with the mind for the sixth become concentrated in the understanding, and thus centred remain steady and firm then Brahma becomes perceptible like a smokeless blazing fire or the effulgent Sun.

data.v: विधूम इव दीप्तार्चिरादित्य इव दीप्तिमान् । वैद्युतोऽग्निरिवाकाशे पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मना । सर्वं च तत्र सर्वत्र व्यापकत्वाच्च दृश्यते ॥
data.md: Indeed, one then beholds in himself his own soul like lightning in the firmament. Everything then appears in it and it appears in cverything on account of its infinitude.

data.v: तं पश्यन्ति महात्मानो ब्राह्मणा ये मनीषिणः । धृतिमन्तो महाप्राज्ञाः सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
data.md: Those great Brahmanas, who are possessed of wisdom, who are endued with fortitude, who are possessed of high knowledge and who are cngaged in the well being of all creatures, succeed in saying it.

data.v: एवं परिमितं कालमाचरन्संशितव्रतः । आसीनो हि रहस्येको गच्छेदक्षरसात्म्यताम् ॥
data.md: Practising austere vows, the Yogin, who acts thus for six months seated by himself on a lonely spot, becomes at one with the Indestructible.

data.v: प्रमोहो भ्रम आवर्तो घ्राणश्रवणदर्शने । अद्भुतानि रसस्पर्शे शीतोष्णे मारुताकृतिः ॥
data.md: Acquiring by Yoga annihilation, extension, power to present different shapes in the same person or body, celestial scents, and sounds, and sights, the most agreeable sensations of taste and touch, pleasurable sensations of coolness and warmth, equality with the wind, power to understanding the meaning of scriptures and every work of genius, living with celestial damsels, the Yogin should not care for them and merge them all in the Understanding.

data.v: प्रतिभामुपसर्गांश्चाप्युपसंगृह्य योगतः । तांस्तत्त्वविदनादृत्य स्वात्मनैव निवर्तयेत् ॥
data.md: Acquiring by Yoga annihilation, extension, power to present different shapes in the same person or body, celestial scents, and sounds, and sights, the most agreeable sensations of taste and touch, pleasurable sensations of coolness and warmth, equality with the wind, power to understanding the meaning of scriptures and every work of genius, living with celestial damsels, the Yogin should not care for them and merge them all in the Understanding.

data.v: कुर्यात्परिचयं योगे त्रैकाल्यं नियतो मुनिः । गिरिशृङ्गे तथा चैत्ये वृक्षाग्रेषु च योजजेत् ॥
data.md: Restraining words and the senses should practise Yoga after dusk and before dawn seated on a mountain summit, or at the foot of a huge tree or with a tree before him.

data.v: संनियम्येन्द्रियग्रामं गोष्ठे भाण्डमना इव । एकाग्रश्चिन्तयेन्नित्यं योगान्नोद्वेजयेन्मनः ॥
data.md: Controlling all the senses within the heart, one should, with faculties concentrated, think on the Eternal and Indestructible like a man of the world thinking of wealth and other valuable properties. One should never, while practising Yoga, with draw his mind from it. one

data.v: येनोपायेन शक्येत संनियन्तुं चलं मनः । तं तं युक्तो निषेवेत न चैव विचलेत्ततः ॥
data.md: One should with devotion pursue those mcans by which he may control the restive mind. One should never suffer himself to fall away from it.

data.v: शून्या गिरिगुहाश्चैव देवतायतनानि च । शून्यागाराणि चैकाग्रो निवासार्थमुपक्रमेत् ॥
data.md: With the senses and the mind withdrawn from everything else, the Yogin should repair 10 empty caves of mountains, to temples consecrated to the gods and to empty houses or apartiments, for living there.

data.v: नाभिष्वजेत्परं वाचा कर्मणा मनसापि वा । उपेक्षको यताहारो लब्धालब्धे समो भवेत् ॥
data.md: One should not mix with another in either speech, act or thought. Disregarding all things and eating very sparingly the Yogin should regard equally objects acquired or lost.

data.v: यश्चैनमभिनन्देत यश्चैनमपवादयेत् । समस्तयोश्चाप्युभयोर्नाभिध्यायेच्छुभाशुभम् ॥
data.md: He should treat equally one who praises and one who censures him. He should not seek the good or the evil of one or the other.

data.v: न प्रहृष्येत लाभेषु नालाभेषु च चिन्तयेत् । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु सधर्मा मातरिश्वनः ॥
data.md: He should not rejoice at an acquisition or be sorry at a failure or loss. Treating all beings equally he should imitate the wind.

data.v: एवं सर्वात्मनः साधोः सर्वत्र समदर्शिनः । षण्मासान्नित्ययुक्तस्य शब्दब्रह्मातिवर्तते ॥
data.md: Brahma, represented by sound, appcars very clearly unto one whose mind is thus turned to itself, who leads a pure life, and who sees all things equally, indeed unto one who is ever engaged in Yoga thus for even six months.

data.v: वेदनार्ताः प्रजा दृष्ट्वा समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः । एतस्मिन्निरतो मार्गे विरमेन्न विमोहितः ॥
data.md: Seeing all men stricken with anxiety the Yogin should regard a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and a lump of gold with an equal eye. Indeed, he should withdraw himself from this path, cherishing a hatred for it, and never allow himself to be stupefied.

data.v: अपि वर्णावकृष्टस्तु नारी वा धर्मकाङ्क्षिणी । तावप्येतेन मार्गेण गच्छेतां परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: By following the path indicated above, even a person of an inferior caste, or a woman, will surely acquire the highest end.

data.v: अजं पुराणमजरं सनातनं; यदिन्द्रियैरुपलभते नरोऽचलः । अणोरणीयो महतो महत्तरं; तदात्मना पश्यति युक्त आत्मवान् ॥
data.md: He who has subdued his mind sees in his own self, by the help of his own understanding the Increate, Ancient, Undeteriorating, and Eternal Brahma,-That which cannot be attained to except by controlled senses,-That which is subtler than the most subtile, and grosser than the most gross, and which is Emancipation's self.

data.v: इदं महर्षेर्वचनं महात्मनो; यथावदुक्तं मनसानुदृश्य च । अवेक्ष्य चेयात्परमेष्ठिसात्म्यतां; प्रयान्ति यां भूतगतिं मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said By ascertaining from the preceptors and by themselves reflecting with their minds upon these words of the great Rishi spoken so properly wise persons become at one with Brahima himself, till, indeed, the time when the universal dissolution sets in that swallows up all existent beings.

data.v: यदिदं वेदवचनं कुरु कर्म त्यजेति च । कां दिशं विद्यया यान्ति कां च गच्छन्ति कर्मणा ॥
data.md: Shuka said The injunctions of the Vedas are twofold. They once lay down the command,Do all acts. They again declare renounce acts.-I ask-where do persons go by the help of Knowledge and where by the help of acts.

data.v: एतद्वै श्रोतुमिच्छामि तद्भवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे । एतत्त्वन्योन्यवैरूप्ये वर्तते प्रतिकूलतः ॥
data.md: I wish to hear this. Do tell me this. Indeed, these injunctions about knowledge and acts are dissimilar and even contradictory.

data.v: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं पराशरसुतः सुतम् । कर्मविद्यामयावेतौ व्याख्यास्यामि क्षराक्षरौ ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Thus addressed, the son of Parasara said to his son,-I shall explain to you the two paths, viz., the destructible and the indestructible, resting respectively upon acts and knowledge. Listen with rapt attention, O child, to me as I point out to you the place which is reached by one with the help of knowledge, and that other place which is reached with the help of acts. The difference between these two places is as great as the endless firmament.

data.v: यां दिशं विद्यया यान्ति यां च गच्छन्ति कर्मणा । शृणुष्वैकमनाः पुत्र गह्वरं ह्येतदन्तरम् ॥
अस्ति धर्म इति प्रोक्तं नास्तीत्यत्रैव यो वदेत् । तस्य पक्षस्य सदृशमिदं मम भवेदथ ॥
data.md: The question which you have asked me has given me such pain as an athestic talk gives to a religious man.

data.v: द्वाविमावथ पन्थानौ यत्र वेदाः प्रतिष्ठिताः । प्रवृत्तिलक्षणो धर्मो निवृत्तौ च सुभाषितः ॥
data.md: These are the two paths upon which the Vedas are settled: the duties (Acts) indicated by action and those based on renunciation described so beautifully.By acts a living creature is destroyed. By knowledge, whoever, he becomes free. Therefore, Yogins, who see the other sides of the ocean of life, never perform acts.

data.v: कर्मणा बध्यते जन्तुर्विद्यया तु प्रमुच्यते । तस्मात्कर्म न कुर्वन्ति यतयः पारदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: These are the two paths upon which the Vedas are settled: the duties (Acts) indicated by action and those based on renunciation described so beautifully.By acts a living creature is destroyed. By knowledge, whoever, he becomes free. Therefore, Yogins, who see the other sides of the ocean of life, never perform acts.

data.v: कर्मणा जायते प्रेत्य मूर्तिमान्षोडशात्मकः । विद्यया जायते नित्यमव्ययो ह्यव्ययात्मकः ॥
data.md: Through acts one is compelled to take rebirth, after death which a body composed of the sixteen ingredients. Through knowledge, however, one becomes metamorphosed into that which is Eternal, is Eternal, Unmanifest, and Immutable.

data.v: कर्म त्वेके प्रशंसन्ति स्वल्पबुद्धितरा नराः । तेन ते देहजालानि रमयन्त उपासते ॥
data.md: Little-witted persons speak highly of acts. On account of this they have to assume bodies ceaselessly.

data.v: ये तु बुद्धिं परां प्राप्ता धर्मनैपुण्यदर्शिनः । न ते कर्म प्रशंसन्ति कूपं नद्यां पिबन्निव ॥
data.md: Those men, who have keen perceptions about duties and who have attained to that high understanding, never speak highly of acts even as persons, who depend for their drinking water upon the supply of streams never speak highly of wells and tanks.

data.v: कर्मणः फलमाप्नोति सुखदुःखे भवाभवौ । विद्यया तदवाप्नोति यत्र गत्वा न शोचति ॥
यत्र गत्वा न म्रियते यत्र गत्वा न जायते । न जीर्यते यत्र गत्वा यत्र गत्वा न वर्धते ॥
यत्र तद्ब्रह्म परममव्यक्तमजरं ध्रुवम् । अव्याहतमनायासममृतं चावियोगि च ॥
द्वंद्वैर्यत्र न बाध्यन्ते मानसेन च कर्मणा । समाः सर्वत्र मैत्राश्च सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
विद्यामयोऽन्यः पुरुषस्तात कर्ममयोऽपरः । विद्धि चन्द्रमसं दर्शे सूक्ष्मया कलया स्थितम् ॥
data.md: Know that without suffering destruction, the man of knowledge exists for ever like the moon on the last day of the dark fortnight existing in a subtile form.

data.v: तदेतदृषिणा प्रोक्तं विस्तरेणानुमीयते । नवजं शशिनं दृष्ट्वा वक्रं तन्तुमिवाम्बरे ॥
data.md: The great Rishi had described this more fully. Regarding the man given to acts his nature may be inferred from seeing the new moon which appears like a bent thread in the sky.

data.v: एकादशविकारात्मा कलासंभारसंभृतः । मूर्तिमानिति तं विद्धि तात कर्मगुणात्मकम् ॥
data.md: Know, O son, that the man of acts is born again with a body with eleven elements for its component parts which are the results of modification, and with a subtile form which represents a total of sixteen.

data.v: देवो यः संश्रितस्तस्मिन्नब्बिन्दुरिव पुष्करे । क्षेत्रज्ञं तं विजानीयान्नित्यं त्यागजितात्मकम् ॥
data.md: The god who resides in that (material) form, like a drop of water on a lotus leaf, should be known as Kshetrajna (Soul) which is Eternal and which gets over by Yoga both the mind and the understanding.

data.v: तमो रजश्च सत्त्वं च विद्धि जीवगुणानिमान् । जीवमात्मगुणं विद्यादात्मानं परमात्मनः ॥
data.md: Goodness, darkness, and ignorance are the qualities of the Understanding. The understanding is the attribute of the individual soul living within the body. The individual soul, in its turn, emanates froin the Supreme Soul.

data.v: सचेतनं जीवगुणं वदन्ति; स चेष्टते चेष्टयते च सर्वम् । ततः परं क्षेत्रविदो वदन्ति; प्रावर्तयद्यो भुवनानि सप्त ॥
data.md: The body with the soul is said to be the attribute of individual soul. It is individual soul which acts and causes all bodies to live. He who has created the seven worlds is said by those who are acquainted with what is Kshatra to be above individual soul.

data.v: क्षरात्प्रभृति यः सर्गः सगुणानीन्द्रियाणि च । बुद्ध्यैश्वर्याभिसर्गार्थं यद्ध्यानं चात्मनः शुभम् ॥
data.md: Shuka said I have now understood that there are two kinds of creation, viz., one universal emanating from the (universal) Soul. The other consisting of the senses with their objects, originates from the power of the Understanding. This last transcends the other and is considered to be the foremost.

data.v: भूय एव तु लोकेऽस्मिन्सद्वृत्तिं वृत्तिहैतुकीम् । यया सन्तः प्रवर्तन्ते तदिच्छाम्यनुवर्णितम् ॥
data.md: I wish however, to once more hear of that path of righteousness which runs in this world, regulated by the virtue of Time and according to which all good men form their conduct.

data.v: वेदे वचनमुक्तं तु कुरु कर्म त्यजेति च । कथमेतद्विजानीयां तच्च व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: In the Vedas there are both kinds of saying, do acts and avoid acts. How shall I succeed in determining which of the two is right? You should explain this clearly.

data.v: लोकवृत्तान्ततत्त्वज्ञः पूतोऽहं गुरुशासनात् । कृत्वा बुद्धिं वियुक्तात्मा त्यक्ष्याम्यात्मानमव्यथः ॥
data.md: Having acquired through your instructions, a thorough knowledge of the course of conduct of human beings, having purified myself by the practice of only righteousness, and having cleansed my understanding, I shall, after renouncing my body, see the indestructible Soul.

data.v: यैषा वै विहिता वृत्तिः पुरस्ताद्ब्रह्मणा स्वयम् । एषा पूर्वतरैः सद्भिराचीर्णा परमर्षिभिः ॥
data.md: The course of conduct that was fist laid down by Brahman himself was duly followed by the wise and pious persons of yore viz., the great Rishis of ancient times.

data.v: ब्रह्मचर्येण वै लोकाञ्जयन्ति परमर्षयः । आत्मनश्च हृदि श्रेयस्त्वन्विच्छ मनसात्मनि ॥
वने मूलफलाशी च तप्यन्सुविपुलं तपः । पुण्यायतनचारी च भूतानामविहिंसकः ॥
विधूमे सन्नमुसले वानप्रस्थप्रतिश्रये । काले प्राप्ते चरन्भैक्षं कल्पते ब्रह्मभूयसे ॥
निःस्तुतिर्निर्नमस्कारः परित्यज्य शुभाशुभे । अरण्ये विचरैकाकी येन केनचिदाशितः ॥
data.md: Abstaining from flattery and from bowing your head to others, and avoiding both good and evil, live in the forest alone appeasing hunger by any means that presents itself before you.

data.v: यदिदं वेदवचनं लोकवादे विरुध्यते । प्रमाणे चाप्रमाणे च विरुद्धे शास्त्रता कुतः ॥
data.md: The saying of the Vedas are, in the opinion of the ordinary person, contradictory. Whether on severe ! this is authoritative or that is so, when there is this conflict, how can they be considered to be spiritual.

data.v: इत्येतच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि भगवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे । कर्मणामविरोधेन कथमेतत्प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: I wish to hear this; how can both be considered as authoritative. How indeed, can liberation be obtained without violating the ordinance regarding the obligatory character of acts.

data.v: इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाचेदं गन्धवत्याः सुतः सुतम् । ऋषिस्तत्पूजयन्वाक्यं पुत्रस्यामिततेजसः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Thus addressed the son of Gandhavati, viz., the Rishi, praising these words of his highly energetic son, replied to him as follows.

data.v: गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारी च वानप्रस्थोऽथ भिक्षुकः । यथोक्तकारिणः सर्वे गच्छन्ति परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: Vyasa said One who is a Brahmacharin, one who lives like a house-holder, one who is a herinit and one who lives like a mendicant, all reach the same high end by duly satisfying the duties of their respective modes of life.

data.v: एको य आश्रमानेताननुतिष्ठेद्यथाविधि । अकामद्वेषसंयुक्तः स परत्र महीयते ॥
data.md: Or if one, and the same person, shorn of desire and aversion, follows (one after another) all these four modes of life according to the ordinances that have been laid down, he is certainly gratified (by such conduct) to understand Brahma.

data.v: चतुष्पदी हि निःश्रेणी ब्रह्मण्येषा प्रतिष्ठिता । एतामाश्रित्य निःश्रेणीं ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
data.md: The four modes of life form a ladder or flight of steps. That fight attaches to Brahma. By ascending that flight one reaches the region of Brahma.

data.v: आयुषस्तु चतुर्भागं ब्रह्मचार्यनसूयकः । गुरौ वा गुरुपुत्रे वा वसेद्धर्मार्थकोविदः ॥
data.md: For following the fourth mode of life the Brahmacharya, conversant with the distinctions of duty and shorn of malice, should live with the preceptor or his preceptor's son.

data.v: कर्मातिरेकेण गुरोरध्येतव्यं बुभूषता । दक्षिणो नापवादी स्यादाहूतो गुरुमाश्रयेत् ॥
data.md: Having performed all acts, he should study, sitting at the feet of his preceptor, with anxious desire to learn. He should always behave with simplicity, avoid evil speech, and take lessons only when his preceptor asks him for it.

data.v: जघन्यशायी पूर्वं स्यादुत्थायी गुरुवेश्मनि । यच्च शिष्येण कर्तव्यं कार्यं दासेन वा पुनः ॥
data.md: While living in the preceptor's house, he should seek bed after the preceptor has gone to his and rise therefrom before the preceptor rises from his. He should do all such acts again which a disciple as also a menial servant should do. Doing these he should humbly stand by his preceptor. Skilled in every kind of work, he should act like a menial servant, doing every act for his preceptor.

data.v: कृतमित्येव तत्सर्वं कृत्वा तिष्ठेत पार्श्वतः । किंकरः सर्वकारी च सर्वकर्मसु कोविदः ॥
data.md: While living in the preceptor's house, he should seek bed after the preceptor has gone to his and rise therefrom before the preceptor rises from his. He should do all such acts again which a disciple as also a menial servant should do. Doing these he should humbly stand by his preceptor. Skilled in every kind of work, he should act like a menial servant, doing every act for his preceptor.

data.v: शुचिर्दक्षो गुणोपेतो ब्रूयादिषुरिवात्वरः । चक्षुषा गुरुमव्यग्रो निरीक्षेत जितेन्द्रियः ॥
data.md: Becoming pure in body and mind, and acquiring cleverness and other virtues he should now and then speak what is pleasant, Controlling his senses he should look at his preceptor without curiosity.

data.v: नाभुक्तवति चाश्नीयादपीतवति नो पिबेत् । न तिष्ठति तथासीत नासुप्ते प्रस्वपेत च ॥
data.md: He should never eat before his preceptor has eaten; never drink before his preceptor has drunk; never sit down before is preceptor has sat down; and never go to bed before his preceptor has gone.

data.v: उत्तानाभ्यां च पाणिभ्यां पादावस्य मृदु स्पृशेत् । दक्षिणं दक्षिणेनैव सव्यं सव्येन पीडयेत् ॥
data.md: He should gently touch his preceptor's feet with palms, the right foot with the right hand and the left foot with the left.

data.v: अभिवाद्य गुरुं ब्रूयादधीष्व भगवन्निति । इदं करिष्ये भगवन्निदं चापि कृतं मया ॥
data.md: Reverentially saluting the preceptor, he should say to him:-O illustrious one, teach me! I shall do this, O illustrious one! This ] have already done, O twice born one. I am ready to do whatever else your reverend self may be pleased to command.

data.v: इति सर्वमनुज्ञाप्य निवेद्य गुरवे धनम् । कुर्यात्कृत्वा च तत्सर्वमाख्येयं गुरवे पुनः ॥
data.md: Having said all this, and having duły offered himself (thus), he should perform whatever acts of his preceptor wait for doing and having completed them inform the preceptor once more that they have been done.

data.v: यांस्तु गन्धान्रसान्वापि ब्रह्मचारी न सेवते । सेवेत तान्समावृत्त इति धर्मेषु निश्चयः ॥
data.md: What scents or tastes the Brahmacharin may abstain from while actually leading a life of celebacy may be used by him after his return from the preceptor's house. This is according to the ordinance.

data.v: ये केचिद्विस्तरेणोक्ता नियमा ब्रह्मचारिणः । तान्सर्वाननुगृह्णीयाद्भवेच्चानपगो गुरोः ॥
data.md: Whatever observances have been laid down in full for Brahmacharins should all be regularly practised by him. He should all be regularly practised by him. He should be always at the beck and call of his preceptor.

data.v: स एवं गुरवे प्रीतिमुपहृत्य यथाबलम् । आश्रमेष्वाश्रमेष्वेवं शिष्यो वर्तेत कर्मणा ॥
data.md: Having pleased his preceptor in this way to the best of his powers, the disciple should, from that mode of life, enter into the others and practise the duties of each.

data.v: वेदव्रतोपवासेन चतुर्थे चायुषो गते । गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा समावर्तेद्यथाविधि ॥
data.md: Having (thus) spent a fourth part of his life in the study of the Vedas, and observance of vows and fasts, and given the preceptor his fee, the disciple should, according to the ordinance, bidadicu and return home for becoming a house-holder.

data.v: धर्मलब्धैर्युतो दारैरग्नीनुत्पाद्य धर्मतः । द्वितीयमायुषो भागं गृहमेधिव्रती भवेत् ॥
data.md: Then, having married according to the ordinances, and having carefully established the domestic fire, he should, observing all the Vows and fasts, become a house-holder and pass the second period of life.

data.v: द्वितीयमायुषो भागं गृहमेधी गृहे वसेत् । धर्मलब्धैर्युतो दारैरग्नीनुत्पाद्य सुव्रतः ॥
data.md: Vayasa said Performing meritorious vows, ihe house holder, for the second period of his life, should live in his house, having married according to the ordinance and having established a fire.

data.v: गृहस्थवृत्तयश्चैव चतस्रः कविभिः स्मृताः । कुसूलधान्यः प्रथमः कुम्भीधान्यस्त्वनन्तरम् ॥
data.md: Four kinds of conduct have been enunciated by the learned for the domestic mode of life. The first consists of keeping grain in store sufficient to last for three years. The second is of keeping a store to last for one year.

data.v: अश्वस्तनोऽथ कापोतीमाश्रितो वृत्तिमाहरेत् । तेषां परः परो ज्यायान्धर्मतो लोकजित्तमः ॥
data.md: The thirds is of providing for the day without thinking of the borrow. The fourth consists of collecting grain like a pegion. Of these cach one is superior in merit to its predecessor as has been laid down by the scriptures.

data.v: षट्कर्मा वर्तयत्येकस्त्रिभिरन्यः प्रवर्तते । द्वाभ्यामेकश्चतुर्थस्तु ब्रह्मसत्रे व्यवस्थितः । गृहमेधिव्रतान्यत्र महान्तीह प्रचक्षते ॥
data.md: Observing the first kind of conduct a householder may practise all the six well as known duties. He who observes the second kind of conduct should perform three only of these duties, namely learning, giving and taking. He who follows the third kind of conduct should practise only two of the duties (viz., learning, and giving and taking. He who follows the third kind of conduct should practise only two of duties (viz., learning, and giving). The householder practising the fourth mode of life should observe only one duty (viz., reading the scriptures).

data.v: नात्मार्थं पाचयेदन्नं न वृथा घातयेत्पशून् । प्राणी वा यदि वाप्राणी संस्कारं यजुषार्हति ॥
न दिवा प्रस्वपेज्जातु न पूर्वापररात्रयोः । न भुञ्जीतान्तराकाले नानृतावाह्वयेत्स्त्रियम् ॥
नास्यानश्नन्वसेद्विप्रो गृहे कश्चिदपूजितः । तथास्यातिथयः पूज्या हव्यकव्यवहाः सदा ॥
वेदविद्याव्रतस्नाताः श्रोत्रिया वेदपारगाः । स्वधर्मजीविनो दान्ताः क्रियावन्तस्तपस्विनः । तेषां हव्यं च कव्यं चाप्यर्हणार्थं विधीयते ॥
data.md: He should always adore such guests who present sacrificial offerings, who are cleansed by Vedic learning, who observe excellent vows, who are high-born and conversant with the scriptures, who are self-controlled, mindful of all religious acts, and devoted to penances. The scriptures hold that what is offered to the gods and the departed manes in sacrifices and religious rites, is meant for the service of guests like these.

data.v: न खरैः संप्रयातस्य स्वधर्माज्ञानकस्य च । अपविद्धाग्निहोत्रस्य गुरोर्वालीककारिणः ॥
data.md: In this mode of life. the scriptures hold that a portion of food, should be given to every creature, to one, who for the sake of show, keeps his nails and beard, to one who from pride shows what his own (religious) practises are, to one who has unduly abandoned his sacred fire, and even to one who has injured his preceptor. A house holder should give (food) to Brahmacharins and Sanyasins.

data.v: संविभागोऽत्र भूतानां सर्वेषामेव शिष्यते । तथैवापचमानेभ्यः प्रदेयं गृहमेधिना ॥
data.md: In this mode of life. the scriptures hold that a portion of food, should be given to every creature, to one, who for the sake of show, keeps his nails and beard, to one who from pride shows what his own (religious) practises are, to one who has unduly abandoned his sacred fire, and even to one who has injured his preceptor. A house holder should give (food) to Brahmacharins and Sanyasins.

data.v: विघसाशी भवेन्नित्यं नित्यं चामृतभोजनः । अमृतं यज्ञशेषं स्याद्भोजनं हविषा समम् । भृत्यशेषं तु योऽश्नाति तमाहुर्विघसाशिनम् ॥
data.md: The house-holder, should every day eat Vighasa and ambrosia. Mixed with clarified butter, the remains of the food, which is offered in sacrifices, make ambrosia. That householder who eats after having fed his servants, is said to eat Vighasa. The food, which remains after the servants have been fed, is called Vighasa, and that which is left after the presentation of sacrificial offerings, is called Amrita.

data.v: स्वदारनिरतो दान्तो ह्यनसूयुर्जितेन्द्रियः । ऋत्विक्पुरोहिताचार्यैर्मातुलातिथिसंश्रितैः ॥
वृद्धबालातुरैर्वैद्यैर्ज्ञातिसंबन्धिबान्धवैः । मातापितृभ्यां जामीभिर्भ्रात्रा पुत्रेण भार्यया ॥
data.md: He should never fall out with his sacrificial priest, ordinary, and preceptor, with his maternal uncle and guests and dependants, with the aged and the young, with those who suffer from diseases, with those who practise as physicians, with kinsmen, relatives, and friends, with his parents, with women who belong to his own paternal family, with his brother and son and wife, with his daughter, and with his servants.

data.v: दुहित्रा दासवर्गेण विवादं न समाचरेत् । एतान्विमुच्य संवादान्सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
एतैर्जितैस्तु जयति सर्वाँल्लोकान्न संशयः । आचार्यो ब्रह्मलोकेशः प्राजापत्ये पिता प्रभुः ॥
अतिथिस्त्विन्द्रलोकेशो देवलोकस्य चर्त्विजः । जामयोऽप्सरसां लोके वैश्वदेवे तु ज्ञातयः ॥
data.md: The preceptor is able to take one to the regions of Brahman. The father can take to the regions of Prajapati. The guest is powerful enough to lead to the region of Indra. The priest has the power to take to the regions of the celestials. Female relatives on the father's side have power over the regions of the Apsaras, and blood relatives over the regions of the Vishvedevas.

data.v: संबन्धिबान्धवा दिक्षु पृथिव्यां मातृमातुलौ । वृद्धबालातुरकृशास्त्वाकाशे प्रभविष्णवः ॥
data.md: Relation by marriage and collateral kinsmen have power over the several quarters of the horizon (viz., north, etc.) and the mother and the maternal uncle have power over the Earth. The old, the young, the afflicted, the worn out have power over the firmament.

data.v: भ्राता ज्येष्ठः समः पित्रा भार्या पुत्रः स्वका तनुः । छाया स्वा दाशवर्गस्तु दुहिता कृपणं परम् ॥
data.md: The eldest brother is like a father to all his younger brother). The wife and the son are one's own body. One's menial servants are his shadow. The daughter is an object of great love.

data.v: तस्मादेतैरधिक्षिप्तः सहेन्नित्यमसंज्वरः । गृहधर्मरतो विद्वान्धर्मनित्यो जितक्लमः ॥
data.md: Therefore a householder, gifted with learning, observant of duties and endued with endurance, should hear without excitement or anxiety every sort of annoyance and even censure from the last-named relatives.

data.v: न चार्थबद्धः कर्माणि धर्मं वा कंचिदाचरेत् । गृहस्थवृत्तयस्तिस्रस्तासां निःश्रेयसं परम् ॥
data.md: No pious householder should do any act, out of consideration for money. There are three courses of duly attached to the domestic mode of a life. Of these every succeeding one is more meritorious than the preceding one.

data.v: परस्परं तथैवाहुश्चातुराश्रम्यमेव तत् । ये चोक्ता नियमास्तेषां सर्वं कार्यं बुभूषता ॥
data.md: The same rule of merit holds good regarding the four modes of life also viz., every succeeding one is superior to the one preceding it.

data.v: कुम्भीधान्यैरुञ्छशिलैः कापोतीं चास्थितैस्तथा । यस्मिंश्चैते वसन्त्यर्हास्तद्राष्ट्रमभिवर्धते ॥
data.md: That kingdom becomes prosperous where these highly deserving persons dwell viz., those who live like householders according to the Kumbhadhanya method, they who live according to the Uncha method, and they who live according to the Kapoti method.

data.v: दश पूर्वान्दश परान्पुनाति च पितामहान् । गृहस्थवृत्तयस्त्वेता वर्तयेद्यो गतव्यथः ॥
data.md: That man, who cheerfully lives like a householder, observing those duties, succeeds in sanctifying ten generations of his ancestors above and ten generations below.

data.v: स चक्रचरलोकानां सदृशीं प्राप्नुयाद्गतिम् । यतेन्द्रियाणामथ वा गतिरेषा विधीयते ॥
data.md: A householder, duly observing the duties of domestic life, acquires what gives in the end happiness, equal to what takes place in the regions attained by great kings and emperors. Even such is the end of those who have controlled their senses.

data.v: स्वर्गलोको गृहस्थानामुदारमनसां हितः । स्वर्गो विमानसंयुक्तो वेददृष्टः सुपुष्पितः ॥
data.md: Heaven has been ordained for all great householders. That heaven is filled with charming cars for each. Even that is the charming heaven described in the Vedas.

data.v: स्वर्गलोके गृहस्थानां प्रतिष्ठा नियतात्मनाम् । ब्रह्मणा विहिता श्रेणिरेषा यस्मात्प्रमुच्यते । द्वितीयं क्रमशः प्राप्य स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
data.md: The regions of heaven form the high mead for all householders of controlled minds. The Self-born Brahma ordained that the domestic life, should secure heaven, and since it has been so ordained, a person, by gradually following the second mode of life, obtains happiness in heaven.

data.v: अतः परं परममुदारमाश्रमं; तृतीयमाहुस्त्यजतां कलेवरम् । वनौकसां गृहपतिनामनुत्तमं; शृणुष्वैतत्क्लिष्टशरीरकारिणाम् ॥
data.md: After this comes that high and superior mode of life, called the third, for those that are desirous of renouncing their bodies. Superior to that of householders is the life of hermits,-who reduce their bodies into skeletons overlaid with dried skins. Listen as I describe to this subject to you further more.

data.v: प्रोक्ता गृहस्थवृत्तिस्ते विहिता या मनीषिणाम् । तदनन्तरमुक्तं यत्तन्निबोध युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Bhishma said You have been told what the duties of a householders are as ordained by the wise. Listen now, O Yudhisthira, to the next class of duties.

data.v: क्रमशस्त्ववधूयैनां तृतीयां वृत्तिमुत्तमाम् । संयोगव्रतखिन्नानां वानप्रस्थाश्रमौकसाम् ॥
data.md: Gradually leading off the domestic mode, one should enter the third mode which is good. It is the mode which is followed by persons who living with their wives pain themselves by means of austerities. It is the mode followed by those who live in forest as hermits.

data.v: श्रूयतां पार्थ भद्रं ते सर्वलोकाश्रयात्मनाम् । प्रेक्षापूर्वं प्रवृत्तानां पुण्यदेशनिवासिनाम् ॥
data.md: Blessed be you, O son, listen to the duties observed by those who follow this mode of life in which are set forth the practices of all men and all modes of life. Listen, indeed, to the duties of those who live in sacred spots and who have adopted this mode after proper consideration.

data.v: गृहस्थस्तु यदा पश्येद्वलीपलितमात्मनः । अपत्यस्यैव चापत्यं वनमेव तदाश्रयेत् ॥
data.md: Vyasa said When the householder sees his body wrinkled and hair white on his head, and children of his children, he should then retire into the forest.

data.v: तृतीयमायुषो भागं वानप्रस्थाश्रमे वसेत् । तानेवाग्नीन्परिचरेद्यजमानो दिवौकसः ॥
data.md: He should pass the third portion of his life as Vanaprastha. He should worship those sacred fires to which he had attended while a householder. Desirous of performing sacrifices, he should also worship the gods.

data.v: नियतो नियताहारः षष्ठभक्तोऽप्रमादवान् । तदग्निहोत्रं ता गावो यज्ञाङ्गानि च सर्वशः ॥
data.md: Observing vows and being sparing in diet, he should eat only once, during the sixth part of the day. He should be always careful. Adoring his fires, he should keep some kine, serving them dutifully. He should perform all the rituals of a sacrifice.

data.v: अकृष्टं वै व्रीहियवं नीवारं विघसानि च । हवींषि संप्रयच्छेत मखेष्वत्रापि पञ्चसु ॥
data.md: He should live upon rice and wheat which grows indigenously, and upon other sorts of grains, growing wildly. He should eat the remnant after feeding guests. In the third mode of life, he should make offerings of clarified butter in the five celebrated Sacrifices.

data.v: वानप्रस्थाश्रमेऽप्येताश्चतस्रो वृत्तयः स्मृताः । सद्यःप्रक्षालकाः केचित्केचिन्मासिकसंचयाः ॥
data.md: Four courses of conduct have been laid down for the Vanaprastha mode of life. Some gather only what is necessary for the day. Some store up things for a month.

data.v: वार्षिकं संचयं केचित्केचिद्द्वादशवार्षिकम् । कुर्वन्त्यतिथिपूजार्थं यज्ञतन्त्रार्थसिद्धये ॥
data.md: Some collect grain and other necessaries sufficient to last for twelve years. Hermits may act thus for adoring guests and performning sacrifices.

data.v: अभ्रावकाशा वर्षासु हेमन्ते जलसंश्रयाः । ग्रीष्मे च पञ्चतपसः शश्वच्च मितभोजनाः ॥
data.md: They should during the rains, expose themselves to rain and go to water during the autumn. In summer, they should sit in the midst of four fires with the sun burning overhead. Throughout the year, however, they should be sparing in deit.

data.v: भूमौ विपरिवर्तन्ते तिष्ठेद्वा प्रपदैरपि । स्थानासनैर्वर्तयन्ति सवनेष्वभिषिञ्चते ॥
data.md: They should sit and sleep on the naked earth. They stand on only their toes. They should be satisfied with the bare earth and with small mats of grass. They perform their ablutions morning, noon, and evening.

data.v: दन्तोलूखलिनः केचिदश्मकुट्टास्तथापरे । शुक्लपक्षे पिबन्त्येके यवागूं क्वथितां सकृत् ॥
data.md: Some amongst them use only their teeth for cleaning grain. Others use only stones for the same, Some amongst them drink, only during the light fortnight, boiled very lightly, gruel of wheat (or other, grain).

data.v: कृष्णपक्षे पिबन्त्येके भुञ्जते च यथाक्रमम् । मूलैरेके फलैरेके पुष्पैरेके दृढव्रताः ॥
data.md: Others drink similar gruel only during the dark fortnight. Some eat what only comes of itself. Some practising rigid vows, live upon only roots, some upon only fruits, some upon only flowers, duly following the method followed by the Vaikhanashas.

data.v: वर्तयन्ति यथान्यायं वैखानसमतं श्रिताः । एताश्चान्याश्च विविधा दीक्षास्तेषां मनीषिणाम् ॥
चतुर्थश्चौपनिषदो धर्मः साधारणः स्मृतः । वानप्रस्थो गृहस्थश्च ततोऽन्यः संप्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: These and various other observances are practised by those wise and pious men. The fourth mode of life is based upon the Upanishads. The duties prescribed for it may be observed in all the modes of life equally. Differing from the others this mode comes afler domestic and forest life.

data.v: अस्मिन्नेव युगे तात विप्रैः सर्वार्थदर्शिभिः । अगस्त्यः सप्त ऋषयो मधुच्छन्दोऽघमर्षणः ॥
सांकृतिः सुदिवा तण्डिर्यवान्नोऽथ कृतश्रमः । अहोवीर्यस्तथा काव्यस्ताण्ड्यो मेधातिथिर्बुधः ॥
शलो वाकश्च निर्वाकः शून्यपालः कृतश्रमः । एवंधर्मसु विद्वांसस्ततः स्वर्गमुपागमन् ॥
तात प्रत्यक्षधर्माणस्तथा यायावरा गणाः । ऋषीणामुग्रतपसां धर्मनैपुणदर्शिनाम् ॥
अवाच्यापरिमेयाश्च ब्राह्मणा वनमाश्रिताः । वैखानसा वालखिल्याः सिकताश्च तथापरे ॥
कर्मभिस्ते निरानन्दा धर्मनित्या जितेन्द्रियाः । गताः प्रत्यक्षधर्माणस्ते सर्वे वनमाश्रिताः । अनक्षत्रा अनाधृष्या दृश्यन्ते ज्योतिषां गणाः ॥
जरया च परिद्यूनो व्याधिना च प्रपीडितः । चतुर्थे चायुषः शेषे वानप्रस्थाश्रमं त्यजेत् । सद्यस्कारां निरूप्येष्टिं सर्ववेदसदक्षिणाम् ॥
आत्मयाजी सोऽऽत्मरतिरात्मक्रीडात्मसंश्रयः । आत्मन्यग्नीन्समारोप्य त्यक्त्वा सर्वपरिग्रहान् ॥
सद्यस्क्रांश्च यजेद्यज्ञानिष्टीश्चैवेह सर्वदा । सदैव याजिनां यज्ञादात्मनीज्या निवर्तते ॥
त्रींश्चैवाग्नीन्यजेत्सम्यगात्मन्येवात्ममोक्षणात् । प्राणेभ्यो यजुषा पञ्च षट्प्राश्नीयादकुत्सयन् ॥
data.md: He should always celebrate such sacrifices and rites as are completed in a single day. When, however, from performance of the (ordinary) sacrifices of sacrificers, the Sacrifice in Self begins, then for liberation he should sacrifice his own self in the three fires. Without linding fault with his food he should take five or six mouthfuls, offering them duly to the five vital airs uttering Mantras of the Yajurveda.

data.v: केशलोमनखान्वाप्य वानप्रस्थो मुनिस्ततः । आश्रमादाश्रमं सद्यः पूतो गच्छति कर्मभिः ॥
data.md: Practising austerities while living like a forest recluse, one should shave off and having purified himself by acts, pass into the fourth and the last holy mode of life.

data.v: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो यो दत्त्वा प्रव्रजेद्द्विजः । लोकास्तेजोमयास्तस्य प्रेत्य चानन्त्यमश्नुते ॥
data.md: That twice-born one who enters the fourth mode of life, giving pledges of assurance to all creatures, succeeds in acquiring many effulgent regions hereafter and ultimately attains to the Infinite.

data.v: सुशीलवृत्तो व्यपनीतकल्मषो; न चेह नामुत्र च कर्तुमीहते । अरोषमोहो गतसंधिविग्रहो; भवेदुदासीनवदात्मविन्नरः ॥
data.md: Of excellent disposition and conduct, with sins all purged off the person who is conversant with his own self never wished to perform any act for either this or the other world. Shorn of anger, error, anxiety and without friendship, such a person live in this world like one having nothing to do with it.

data.v: यमेषु चैवात्मगतेषु न व्यथे;त्स्वशास्त्रसूत्राहुतिमन्त्रविक्रमः । भवेद्यथेष्टा गतिरात्मयाजिनो; न संशयो धर्मपरे जितेन्द्रिये ॥
data.md: One in the (observance of Sannyasa) should not be unwilling in satisfying the duties included in Yama and those also that walk behind them. Such a person should live energetically according to the ordinances laid down his own mode, and leave off Vedic study and the sacred thread which marks his birth. Given to righteousness and having his senses under complete control, such a person endued with knowledge of self, attains forsooth, to the end for which he tries.

data.v: ततः परं श्रेष्ठमतीव सद्गुणै;रधिष्ठितं त्रीनधिवृत्तमुत्तमम् । चतुर्थमुक्तं परमाश्रमं शृणु; प्रकीर्त्यमानं परमं परायणम् ॥
data.md: After the third is the fourth mode of life. It is very superior, and has numberless high virtues. In merit it reigns supreme over the three other modes of life. It is said to occupy the very highest place. Listen to me as I describe the duties belonging to that mode which is very supreme and which is the high refuge of all.

data.v: वर्तमानस्तथैवात्र वानप्रस्थाश्रमे यथा । योक्तव्योऽऽत्मा यथा शक्त्या परं वै काङ्क्षता पदम् ॥
data.md: Shuka said While living satisfying duly the duties of the forest life, how should one, who tries to attain to that which is the highest object of knowledge, set his soul on Yoga according to be best of his power?

data.v: प्राप्य संस्कारमेताभ्यामाश्रमाभ्यां ततः परम् । यत्कार्यं परमार्थार्थं तदिहैकमनाः शृणु ॥
data.md: Vyasa said Having acquired purity by the practice of the first two modes of life, viz., Brahmacharya and domesticity, one should, thereafter, set his mind on Yoga in the third mode of life. Listen now with rapt attention to what should be done for attaining to the highest object of acquisition.

data.v: कषायं पाचयित्वा तु श्रेणिस्थानेषु च त्रिषु । प्रव्रजेच्च परं स्थानं परिव्रज्यामनुत्तमाम् ॥
data.md: Having conquered all shortcomings of the mind of heart by easy means in the practice of the first three modes of life, one should pass into the best and the highest of all the modes, viz., Sannyasa or Renunciation.

data.v: तद्भवानेवमभ्यस्य वर्ततां श्रूयतां तथा । एक एव चरेन्नित्यं सिद्ध्यर्थमसहायवान् ॥
data.md: Do you then pass your days, having acquired the purity. Listen also to me. One should, alone and without anybody to help him or bear him company, practise Yoga for achieving success.

data.v: एकश्चरति यः पश्यन्न जहाति न हीयते । अनग्निरनिकेतः स्याद्ग्राममन्नार्थमाश्रयेत् ॥
data.md: One who practises Yoga without any one in his company, who sees everything as repetition of his own self, and who never discard anything, never falls away from Liberation. Without keeping the sacrificial fires and without a fixed dwelling, such a person should enter a village for only begging his food.

data.v: अश्वस्तनविधानः स्यान्मुनिर्भावसमन्वितः । लघ्वाशी नियताहारः सकृदन्ननिषेविता ॥
data.md: He should provide himself for the day without keeping any thing in store for the morrow. He should practise penances, with heat fixed on the Supreme. Eating little and that even under proper restrictions, he should not take more than one meal in a day.

data.v: कपालं वृक्षमूलानि कुचेलमसहायता । उपेक्षा सर्वभूतानामेतावद्भिक्षुलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: The other marks of a mendicant are the human skull, protection under trees, rags for wearing, companionless solitude, and indifference to all creatures.

data.v: यस्मिन्वाचः प्रविशन्ति कूपे प्राप्ताः शिला इव । न वक्तारं पुनर्यान्ति स कैवल्याश्रमे वसेत् ॥
data.md: That person into whom words enter like terrified elephants into a well, and from whom they never return to the speaker, is fit to lead this mode of life which had Libcration for its end.

data.v: नैव पश्येन्न शृणुयादवाच्यं जातु कस्यचित् । ब्राह्मणानां विशेषेण नैव ब्रूयात्कथंचन ॥
data.md: The mendicant should never mind the evil deeds of any person. He should never hear vilifications of others. He should especially guard against reviling a Brahmana.

data.v: यद्ब्राह्मणस्य कुशलं तदेव सततं वदेत् । तूष्णीमासीत निन्दायां कुर्वन्भेषजमात्मनः ॥
data.md: He should always say only what is pleasant to the Brahmanas. When anything is said against him, he should remain perfectly silent. Such silence is the medical treatment prescribed for him.

data.v: येन पूर्णमिवाकाशं भवत्येकेन सर्वदा । शून्यं येन जनाकीर्णं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः ॥
data.md: That person for whose single self the spot he occupies becomes like the eastern sky, and who can regard as perfectly lonely a spot teeming with thousands of men and things, is considered by the gods to be a true Brahmana.

data.v: येन केनचिदाच्छन्नो येन केनचिदाशितः । यत्रक्वचनशायी च तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः ॥
data.md: The gods know him for a Brahmana who puts on whatever comes by the way, who lives upon whatever he gets, and who sleeps on what ever spot he finds.

data.v: अहेरिव गणाद्भीतः सौहित्यान्नरकादिव । कुणपादिव च स्त्रीभ्यस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः ॥
data.md: The gods regard him as a Brahmana who fears company like a snake; the full measure of gratification (from foods and drinks) as of hell; and women as a corpse.

data.v: न क्रुध्येन्न प्रहृष्येच्च मानितोऽमानितश्च यः । सर्वभूतेष्वभयदस्तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः ॥
data.md: The gods know him as a Brahmana who is never glad when honoured and never angry when insulted, and who has given assurances of mercy to all creatures.

data.v: नाभिनन्देत मरणं नाभिनन्देत जीवितम् । कालमेव प्रतीक्षेत निदेशं भृतको यथा ॥
data.md: One following the last mode of life should not regard death with joy. Nor should he regard life with joy. He should only wait for his hour like a servant waiting for his master's command.

data.v: अनभ्याहतचित्तः स्यादनभ्याहतवाक्तथा । निर्मुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यो निरमित्रस्य किं भयम् ॥
data.md: He should purify his heart of all shortcomings. He should purify his speech of all faults. He should purge himself of all sins. Shorn as he is of enemies what fear can attack him.

data.v: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो भूतानामभयं यतः । तस्य देहाद्विमुक्तस्य भयं नास्ति कुतश्चन ॥
data.md: He who fears no creature and whom no creature fears, can have no fear from any quarter, freed as he is from every form of mistake.

data.v: यथा नागपदेऽन्यानि पदानि पदगामिनाम् । सर्वाण्येवापिधीयन्ते पदजातानि कौञ्जरे ॥
data.md: As the foot-prints of all other creatures moving upon legs are engulfed within those of elephants, likewise all ranks and conditions are absorbed within Yoga.

data.v: एवं सर्वमहिंसायां धर्मार्थमपिधीयते । अमृतः स नित्यं वसति योऽहिंसां प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Similarly, every other duty and observance is encompassed within the one duty of abstention froin injury. He who avoids injuring other creatures, lives an eternal life of joy.

data.v: अहिंसकः समः सत्यो धृतिमान्नियतेन्द्रियः । शरण्यः सर्वभूतानां गतिमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥
data.md: One who abstains from injury, who regards all creatures impartially, who is devoted to truth, who is gifted with fortitude, who has his senses under restraints, and who extends protection to all beings, attains to a peerless end.

data.v: एवं प्रज्ञानतृप्तस्य निर्भयस्य मनीषिणः । न मृत्युरतिगो भावः स मृत्युमधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: The state of death cannot with selfknowledge, who is shorn of fear, desire and expectancy. On the other hand, such a person conquers death.

data.v: विमुक्तं सर्वसङ्गेभ्यो मुनिमाकाशवत्स्थितम् । अस्वमेकचरं शान्तं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः ॥
data.md: The gods know him for a Brahmana who is freed from attachments of every kind, who practises penances, who lives like space which while containing everything is yet unattached to all things, who has nothing which he can call his own, who reads a lonely life, and who possesses equanimity of soul.

data.v: जीवितं यस्य धर्मार्थं धर्मोऽरत्यर्थमेव च । अहोरात्राश्च पुण्यार्थं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः ॥
data.md: The gods regard him as a Brahmana whose life is for the practice of righteousness, whose righteousness is for the behoof of them who wait dutifully upon him, and whose days and nights exist only for acquiring religious merit.

data.v: निराशिषमनारम्भं निर्नमस्कारमस्तुतिम् । अक्षीणं क्षीणकर्माणं तं देवा ब्राह्मणं विदुः ॥
data.md: The gods regard him as a Brahmana who is shorn of desire, who never struggles (for worldly emoluments), who never lowers his head to any one, who never flatters another, and who is shorn of all sorts of attachment.

data.v: सर्वाणि भूतानि सुखे रमन्ते; सर्वाणि दुःखस्य भृशं त्रसन्ति । तेषां भयोत्पादनजातखेदः; कुर्यान्न कर्माणि हि श्रद्दधानः ॥
data.md: All creatures are filled with pleasure at the prospect of happiness or miserable at the prospect of grief. The man of faith, therefore who should feel sorry at the prospect of afflicting other other creatures, must abstain absolutely from all acts.

data.v: दानं हि भूताभयदक्षिणायाः; सर्वाणि दानान्यधितिष्ठतीह । तीक्ष्णां तनुं यः प्रथमं जहाति; सोऽनन्तमाप्नोत्यभयं प्रजाभ्यः ॥
data.md: The gift of assurances of harmlessness to all creatures is superior in point of merit all other gifts. He who, at the beginning, promises abstention from injury, acquires Liberation whence is the assurance of harınlessness to all creatures.

data.v: उत्तान आस्येन हविर्जुहोति; लोकस्य नाभिर्जगतः प्रतिष्ठा । तस्याङ्गमङ्गानि कृताकृतं च; वैश्वानरः सर्वमेव प्रपेदे ॥
data.md: That man who does not put into his open mouth even the five or six inouthfuls which are sanctioned for the forest recluse, is said to be the navel of the world, and the refuge of the universe. The fire occupies the head and other limbs, as also the acts good and bad.

data.v: प्रादेशमात्रे हृदि निश्रितं य;त्तस्मिन्प्राणानात्मयाजी जुहोति । तस्याग्निहोत्रं हुतमात्मसंस्थं; सर्वेषु लोकेषु सदैवतेषु ॥
data.md: Such a man, who performs a sacrifice in his own self, makes a libation of his senses and mind into the fire which lives within the limited space of his own heart. On account again of his pouring such a libation into such a fire within his own self, the universe with all creatures including the very celestials, becomes pleased.

data.v: दैवं त्रिधातुं त्रिवृतं सुपर्णं; ये विद्युरग्र्यं परमार्थतां च । ते सर्वलोकेषु महीयमाना; देवाः समर्थाः सुकृतं व्रजन्ति ॥
data.md: They, who know the Sentiency which is endued with effulgence, which is covered with T: three sheaths, which has three qualities for its characteristics, to be Ishvara partaking of that which is highest, viz., the nature of the Supreme Soul, are respected of all the worlds. They very gods with all human beings applaud their merits.

data.v: वेदांश्च वेद्यं च विधिं च कृत्स्न;मथो निरुक्तं परमार्थतां च । सर्वं शरीरात्मनि यः प्रवेद; तस्मै स्म देवाः स्पृहयन्ति नित्यम् ॥
data.md: He who succeeds is seeing in the Soul which lives in his own body all the Vedas, ether and the other objects of perception, the rituals of the scriptures, all those entities which are perceptible in sound only, and the superior nature of the Supreme Soul, adored of the very gods as the foremost of all beings.

data.v: भूमावसक्तं दिवि चाप्रमेयं; हिरण्मयं योऽण्डजमण्डमध्ये । पतत्रिणं पक्षिणमन्तरिक्षे; यो वेद भोग्यात्मनि दीप्तरश्मिः ॥
data.md: He who sees in the Soul which lives within his body that foremost of beings which is not attached to the Earth, which is not attached to the Earth, which is immeasurable in even the limitless sky, which is made of gold, which is begotten of the egg and lives within the egg, which is equipped with many feathers, and which has two wings like a bird, and which is rendered effulgent by many rays of light is adored of the very gods as the foremost of all beings.

data.v: आवर्तमानमजरं विवर्तनं; षण्णेमिकं द्वादशारं सुपर्व । यस्येदमास्ये परियाति विश्वं; तत्कालचक्रं निहितं गुहायाम् ॥
data.md: The very gods adore him in whose understanding is set the wheel of Time, which is constantly revolving, which knows no deterioration, which devours the span of existence of every creature, which has the six seasons for its naves, which is equipped with twelve radii consisting of the twelve months, which has excellent joints, and towards whose gaping mouth goes on this universe.

data.v: यः संप्रसादं जगतः शरीरं; सर्वान्स लोकानधिगच्छतीह । तस्मिन्हुतं तर्पयतीह देवां;स्ते वै तृप्तास्तर्पयन्त्यास्यमस्य ॥
data.md: The Supreme Soul is the huge unconsciousness of dreamless sleep. That Unconsciousness form the body of the universe. It pervades all created things. Sentiency occupying a portion of that capacious unconsciousness, pleases the gods. These last, being pleased, gratify the open mouth of the unconsciousness.

data.v: तेजोमयो नित्यतनुः पुराणो; लोकाननन्तानभयानुपैति । भूतानि यस्मान्न त्रसन्ते कदाचि;त्स भूतेभ्यो न त्रसते कदाचित् ॥
data.md: Endued with effulgence as also with the principle of eternity, Sentiency is without a beginning. It wins infinite regions of eternal happiness. He whom no creature fears, has never to fear any creature.

data.v: अगर्हणीयो न च गर्हतेऽन्या;न्स वै विप्रः परमात्मानमीक्षेत् । विनीतमोहो व्यपनीतकल्मषो; न चेह नामुत्र च योऽर्थमृच्छति ॥
data.md: He who never does anything blameable and who never censures another, is said to be a truly twice-born one. Such a man succeeds in seeing the Supreme Soul. He whose ignorance has been removed and whose sins have been washed away, never enjoys either here or hereafter the happiness that is enjoyed by others.

data.v: अरोषमोहः समलोष्टकाञ्चनः; प्रहीणशोको गतसंधिविग्रहः । अपेतनिन्दास्तुतिरप्रियाप्रिय;श्चरन्नुदासीनवदेष भिक्षुकः ॥
data.md: A person following the fourth mode of life wanders on the Earth like one not attached to anything. Such a person is shorn of anger and crror. Such a person regards equally a clod of earth and a lump of gold. such a man never keeps anything in store for his use. Such a person has no friends and enemies. Such a person does not care praise or blame, and the agreeable and the disagreeable.

data.v: प्रकृतेस्तु विकारा ये क्षेत्रज्ञस्तैः परिश्रितः । ते चैनं न प्रजानन्ति स तु जानाति तानपि ॥
data.md: Vyasa said The Sentiency is endued with all thse entities which are modifications of Nature. These do not know the Soul but the Soul knows them all.

data.v: तैश्चैष कुरुते कार्यं मनःषष्ठैरिहेन्द्रियैः । सुदान्तैरिव संयन्ता दृढैः परमवाजिभिः ॥
data.md: Like a good driver going on with the help of strong, well-trained, and very good horses along the paths he chooses, thc Soul acts with the help of these, called the senses, having the mind for their sixth.

data.v: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यः परमं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा महान्परः ॥
data.md: The objects of the senses are superior to the senses themselves. The mind is superior to those objects. The understanding is superior to the mind. Mahat or the principle of greatness is superior to the understanding.

data.v: महतः परमव्यक्तमव्यक्तात्परतोऽमृतम् । अमृतान्न परं किंचित्सा काष्ठा सा परा गतिः ॥
data.md: Superior to Mahat is the Prakriti. Superior to the Prakriti is Brahma. There is nothing superior to Brahma. That is the highest limit of goodness and the highest end.

data.v: एवं सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोऽऽत्मा न प्रकाशते । दृश्यते त्वग्र्यया बुद्ध्या सूक्ष्मया तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
data.md: The Supreme Soul is hidden in every creature. It is not so manifest that ordinary men can see. Only Yogins with subtile vision see the Supreme Soul with the help of their keen and subtile understandings.

data.v: अन्तरात्मनि संलीय मनःषष्ठानि मेधया । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थांश्च बहु चिन्त्यमचिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: Merging the senses having the mind for their sixth and all the objects of the senses into the inner self by the help of the understanding, and meditating upon the three states of consciousness, viz., the object thought, the act of thinking, and the thinker, and abstaining by contemplation from every kind of enjoyment, replenishing his mind with the knowledge that he is Brahma's self, laying aside at the same time all consciousness of power, and there by making his Soul perfectly tranquil, the Yogin attains to immortality.

data.v: ध्यानोपरमणं कृत्वा विद्यासंपादितं मनः । अनीश्वरः प्रशान्तात्मा ततोऽर्छत्यमृतं पदम् ॥
data.md: Merging the senses having the mind for their sixth and all the objects of the senses into the inner self by the help of the understanding, and meditating upon the three states of consciousness, viz., the object thought, the act of thinking, and the thinker, and abstaining by contemplation from every kind of enjoyment, replenishing his mind with the knowledge that he is Brahma's self, laying aside at the same time all consciousness of power, and there by making his Soul perfectly tranquil, the Yogin attains to immortality.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणां तु सर्वेषां वश्यात्मा चलितस्मृतिः । आत्मनः संप्रदानेन मर्त्यो मृत्युमुपाश्नुते ॥
data.md: That person, however, who becomes the slave of all his senses and whose ideas of right and wrong have been confounded, already subject as he is to death, actually meets with death by such surrender of self.

data.v: हित्वा तु सर्वसंकल्पान्सत्त्वे चित्तं निवेशयेत् । सत्त्वे चित्तं समावेश्य ततः कालंजरो भवेत् ॥
data.md: Destroying all desires, one should drown the gross understanding into one's subtile Understanding. Having thus drowned the gross into the subtile Understanding, one is sure to become a second Kalanjara mountain.

data.v: चित्तप्रसादेन यतिर्जहाति हि शुभाशुभम् । प्रसन्नात्मात्मनि स्थित्वा सुखमानन्त्यमश्नुते ॥
data.md: By purifying his heart, the Yogin gets over both righteousness and its opposite. By purifying his hcart and by living in his own true nature, he acquires the highest happiness.

data.v: लक्षणं तु प्रसादस्य यथा तृप्तः सुखं स्वपेत् । निवाते वा यथा दीपो दीप्यमानो न कम्पते ॥
data.md: The sign of that purity of heart is that one who has acquired it experiences that state of unconsciousness which is similar to that of dreamless slumber. The Yogin who has acquired that state lives like the steady flame of a lamp which burns in a place where the atmosphere is perfectly still.

data.v: एवं पूर्वापरे रात्रे युञ्जन्नात्मानमात्मना । सत्त्वाहारविशुद्धात्मा पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मनि ॥
data.md: Being sparing in diet, and having purified his heart, that Yogin who applies his Soul to the Soul, sees the Soul in the Soul.

data.v: रहस्यं सर्ववेदानामनैतिह्यमनागमम् । आत्मप्रत्ययिकं शास्त्रमिदं पुत्रानुशासनम् ॥
data.md: This topic, O son, intended for your instruction, is the essence of all the Vedas. The truths expounded in it cannot be understood by the help of inference alone or by that of mere study of the scriptures. One must understand in himself by the help of faith.

data.v: धर्माख्यानेषु सर्वेषु सत्याख्यानेषु यद्वसु । दशेदमृक्सहस्राणि निर्मथ्यामृतमुद्धृतम् ॥
data.md: By churning the riches contained in all religious works and in all topics based on truth, as also the ten thousand Riches, this ambrosia has been acquired.

data.v: नवनीतं यथा दध्नः काष्ठादग्निर्यथैव च । तथैव विदुषां ज्ञानं पुत्रहेतोः समुद्धृतम् । स्नातकानामिदं शास्त्रं वाच्यं पुत्रानुशासनम् ॥
data.md: As butter from curds and fire from wood, so this has been raised for the sake of my son,-this which forms the knowledge of all truly wise men.

data.v: तदिदं नाप्रशान्ताय नादान्तायातपस्विने । नावेदविदुषे वाच्यं तथा नानुगताय च ॥
नासूयकायानृजवे न चानिर्दिष्टकारिणे । न तर्कशास्त्रदग्धाय तथैव पिशुनाय च ॥
श्लाघते श्लाघनीयाय प्रशान्ताय तपस्विने । इदं प्रियाय पुत्राय शिष्यायानुगताय च । रहस्यधर्मं वक्तव्यं नान्यस्मै तु कथंचन ॥
data.md: It should never be delivered to one whose intellect has been consumed by disputation, or one who is vile or low. This topic containing the quintessence of duties, should be communicated to that person, however, who is possessed of fame, or who deserves praise, or who is of tranquil soul, or possessed of ascetic merit, to a Brahimana who is such to one's son or dutiful disciple, but on no account should it be delivered to others.

data.v: यद्यप्यस्य महीं दद्याद्रत्नपूर्णामिमां नरः । इदमेव ततः श्रेय इति मन्येत तत्त्ववित् ॥
data.md: If any person gives away the entire Earth with all her treasures, to one conversant with truth, the latter should still consider the gifts of This knowledge as very much superior to that gift.

data.v: अतो गुह्यतरार्थं तदध्यात्ममतिमानुषम् । यत्तन्महर्षिभिर्दृष्टं वेदान्तेषु च गीयते । तत्तेऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥
data.md: I shall now describe to you a subject which is a greater mystery than this, a subject connected with the Soul, which is above the ordinary understandings of human beings, which has been seen by the foremost of Rishis, what has been treated in the Upanishads, and which forms the topic of your inquiry.

data.v: अध्यात्मं विस्तरेणेह पुनरेव वदस्व मे । यदध्यात्मं यथा चेदं भगवन्नृषिसत्तम ॥
data.md: Shuka said O illustrious one, O foremost of Rishis, once again describe to me fully the subject bearing on soul. Tell me what, in deed, is spiritual topic and whence does it come?

data.v: अध्यात्मं यदिदं तात पुरुषस्येह विद्यते । तत्तेऽहं संप्रवक्ष्यामि तस्य व्याख्यामिमां शृणु ॥
data.md: Vyasa said That, O son, which is considered as spiritual with reference to human beings, I shall now mention to you, and listen to the explanation I give.

data.v: भूमिरापस्तथा ज्योतिर्वायुराकाशमेव च । महाभूतानि भूतानां सागरस्योर्मयो यथा ॥
data.md: Earth, water, light, wind, and entities are the great principles which form the component parts of all creatures, and though really one are yet considered different like the waves of the Ocean.

data.v: प्रसार्येह यथाङ्गानि कूर्मः संहरते पुनः । तद्वन्महान्ति भूतानि यवीयःसु विकुर्वते ॥
data.md: Like a tortoise extending out its limbs and withdrawing then again, the great elements, by living in innumerable small forms, go through transformations.

data.v: इति तन्मयमेवेदं सर्वं स्थावरजङ्गमम् । सर्गे च प्रलये चैव तस्मान्निर्दिश्यते तथा ॥
data.md: All this universe of mobile and immobile objects has for its component parts these five elements. Everything, regarding creation and destruction, is referable to this fivefold elements.

data.v: महाभूतानि पञ्चैव सर्वभूतेषु भूतकृत् । अकरोत्तात वैषम्यं यस्मिन्यदनुपश्यति ॥
data.md: These five elements are in all existent things. The Creator of all things, however, has made an unequal distribution of those elements for serving different ends.

data.v: अकरोद्यच्छरीरेषु कथं तदुपलक्षयेत् । इन्द्रियाणि गुणाः केचित्कथं तानुपलक्षयेत् ॥
data.md: How can one understand that unequal distribution in the various objects of the universe? Which amongst them are the senses and which the attributes? How may this be understood?

data.v: एतत्ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथावदिह दर्शनम् । शृणु तत्त्वमिहैकाग्रो यथातत्त्वं यथा च तत् ॥
data.md: Vyasa said I shall explain this to you properly, one after another. Listen with rapt attention to the subject as I explain how what I have said actually takes place.

data.v: शब्दः श्रोत्रं तथा खानि त्रयमाकाशसंभवम् । प्राणश्चेष्टा तथा स्पर्श एते वायुगुणास्त्रयः ॥
data.md: Sound, the sense of hearing, and all the cavities within the body,-these three Originate-from ether. The vital airs, the action of the limbs, and touch are the attributes of the wind.

data.v: रूपं चक्षुर्विपाकश्च त्रिधा ज्योतिर्विधीयते । रसोऽथ रसनं स्नेहो गुणास्त्वेते त्रयोऽम्भसाम् ॥
data.md: From eyes and the digestive fire within the stomach, originate from light. Taste, tongue, and all the humours,—these three originate from water.

data.v: घ्रेयं घ्राणं शरीरं च भूमेरेते गुणास्त्रयः । एतावानिन्द्रियग्रामो व्याख्यातः पाञ्चभौतिकः ॥
data.md: Scent, nose, and the body,-these three,-form the attributes of earth. These then, as I have explained to you, are the changes of the five (great) elements in connection with the senses.

data.v: वायोः स्पर्शो रसोऽद्भ्यश्च ज्योतिषो रूपमुच्यते । आकाशप्रभवः शब्दो गन्धो भूमिगुणः स्मृतः ॥
data.md: Touch is said to be attribute of the wind; taste of water; form of light. Sound originate from ether, and scent is the property of earth.

data.v: मनो बुद्धिश्च भावश्च त्रय एतेऽऽत्मयोनिजाः । न गुणानतिवर्तन्ते गुणेभ्यः परमा मताः ॥
data.md: Mind, Understanding, and Nature,—these three, originate from their own previous states, and acquiring a position higher than the attributes, do not get over those attributes.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणि नरे पञ्च षष्ठं तु मन उच्यते । सप्तमीं बुद्धिमेवाहुः क्षेत्रज्ञं पुनरष्टमम् ॥
data.md: There are five senses in man. The mind is called the sixth. The Understanding is called the seventh. The Soul is the eighth.

data.v: चक्षुरालोचनायैव संशयं कुरुते मनः । बुद्धिरध्यवसानाय साक्षी क्षेत्रज्ञ उच्यते ॥
data.md: The eyes and the other senses are for only receiving impressions of form, etc. The mind exists for doubting. The Understanding determines those doubts. The Soul is said to only see every work without mingling with them.

data.v: रजस्तमश्च सत्त्वं च त्रय एते स्वयोनिजाः । समाः सर्वेषु भूतेषु तद्गुणेषूपलक्षयेत् ॥
data.md: The qualities of goodness, darkness and ignorance originate from their counterparts. These exist equally in all creatures. These are called qualities and should be known by the actions they produce.

data.v: यथा कूर्म इहाङ्गानि प्रसार्य विनियच्छति । एवमेवेन्द्रियग्रामं बुद्धिः सृष्ट्वा नियच्छति ॥
data.md: As the tortoise extends its limbs and withdraws them once again within itself, so the Understanding creates the senses and once again withdraws them into itself. The consciousness of ego which arises about what is above the soles of the feet and below the crown of the head, is mainly due to the action of the Understanding.

data.v: यदूर्ध्वं पादतलयोरवाङ्मूर्ध्नश्च पश्यति । एतस्मिन्नेव कृत्ये वै वर्तते बुद्धिरुत्तमा ॥
गुणान्नेनीयते बुद्धिर्बुद्धिरेवेन्द्रियाण्यपि । मनःषष्ठानि सर्वाणि बुद्ध्यभावे कुतो गुणाः ॥
data.md: It is the Understanding which is transformed into the (five) attributes. It is the Understanding also which is transformed into the (five) senses with the mind for the sixth. Where the attributes when the Understanding is nowhere? are Own

data.v: तत्र यत्प्रीतिसंयुक्तं किंचिदात्मनि लक्षयेत् । प्रशान्तमिव संशुद्धं सत्त्वं तदुपधारयेत् ॥
data.md: Regarding those actions, all such states of cheerfulness or joy, of tranquillity and purity which one becomes conscious of in one self, should be known as due to the quality of goodness.

data.v: यत्तु संतापसंयुक्तं काये मनसि वा भवेत् । रजः प्रवर्तकं तत्स्यात्सततं हारि देहिनाम् ॥
data.md: All such states of sorrow in either the body or the mind, should be considered as due to the influence of the quality of darkness.

data.v: यत्तु संमोहसंयुक्तमव्यक्तविषयं भवेत् । अप्रतर्क्यमविज्ञेयं तमस्तदुपधार्यताम् ॥
data.md: All such states of stupefaction whose cause cannot be deterinined (by either reason or inward light), should be known as due to the action of Ignorance.

data.v: प्रहर्षः प्रीतिरानन्दः साम्यं स्वस्थात्मचित्तता । अकस्माद्यदि वा कस्माद्वर्तते सात्त्विको गुणः ॥
data.md: Delight, cheerfulness, joy, equanimity, contentment of heart, due to any known cause or originating otherwise, are all effects of the quality of goodness.

data.v: अभिमानो मृषावादो लोभो मोहस्तथाक्षमा । लिङ्गानि रजसस्तानि वर्तन्ते हेत्वहेतुतः ॥
data.md: Pride, false speech, cupidity, stupefaction, vindictiveness, whether originating from any known cause or otherwise, are characteristics of the quality of darkness.

data.v: तथा मोहः प्रमादश्च तन्द्री निद्राप्रबोधिता । कथंचिदभिवर्तन्ते विज्ञेयास्तामसा गुणाः ॥
data.md: Stupefaction of judgement, carelessness, sleep, lethargy, and indolence, from whatever cause these may originate, are to be regarded as the characteristics of the quality of Ignorance.

data.v: मनः प्रसृजते भावं बुद्धिरध्यवसायिनी । हृदयं प्रियाप्रिये वेद त्रिविधा कर्मचोदना ॥
data.md: Vyasa said The mind creates innumerable ideas. The Understanding, differentiates things and ascertains their true nature. The heart discriminates which is pleasant and which unpleasant. There are the three forces which produce acts.

data.v: इन्द्रियेभ्यः परा ह्यर्था अर्थेभ्यः परमं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्बुद्धेरात्मा परो मतः ॥
data.md: The objects of the senses are superior to the senses themselves. The mind is superior to those objects. The understanding is superior to the mind. Mahat or the principle of greatness is superior to the understanding.

data.v: बुद्धिरात्मा मनुष्यस्य बुद्धिरेवात्मनोऽऽत्मिका । यदा विकुरुते भावं तदा भवति सा मनः ॥
data.md: as on Ordinarily the Understanding is a man's Soul. When the Understanding, by itself, forms ideas (of objects) within itself, it is then called Mind.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणां पृथग्भावाद्बुद्धिर्विक्रियते ह्यणु । शृण्वती भवति श्रोत्रं स्पृशती स्पर्श उच्यते ॥
data.md: The senses being different from one another, the Understanding presents different aspects account of its different modifications. When it hears, it becomes the organ of hearing, and when it touches, it becomes the organ of touch.

data.v: पश्यन्ती भवते दृष्टी रसती रसनं भवेत् । जिघ्रती भवति घ्राणं बुद्धिर्विक्रियते पृथक् ॥
data.md: Likewise, when it sees, it becomes the organ of vision, and when it tastes, it becomes the organ of taste and when it smells, it becomes the organs of scent. It is the Understanding which appears under different guises by modification.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणीति तान्याहुस्तेष्वदृश्याधितिष्ठति । तिष्ठती पुरुषे बुद्धिस्त्रिषु भावेषु वर्तते ॥
data.md: These modifications of the Understanding are called the senses. The invisible Soul is placed over them as their presiding chief. Living in the body, the Understanding exists in the three states (of qualities).

data.v: कदाचिल्लभते प्रीतिं कदाचिदपि शोचते । न सुखेन न दुःखेन कदाचिदिह युज्यते ॥
data.md: Sometimes it acquires cheerfulness, sometimes it yields to grief and sometimes its condition becomes such that it is united with neither joy nor sorrow.

data.v: सेयं भावात्मिका भावांस्त्रीनेतानतिवर्तते । सरितां सागरो भर्ता महावेलामिवोर्मिमान् ॥
data.md: The Understanding, however, whose chief function is to create elements, transcends those three states as the ocean, the king of rivers, stands against the powerful currents of the rivers that fall into it.

data.v: यदा प्रार्थयते किंचित्तदा भवति सा मनः । अधिष्ठानानि वै बुद्ध्या पृथगेतानि संस्मरेत् । इन्द्रियाण्येव मेध्यानि विजेतव्यानि कृत्स्नशः ॥
data.md: When the Understanding desires anything, it is called by the name of Mind. The senses, again, should all be considered as contained within the Understanding. The senses, which are engaged in bearing impressions of form, scent, etc., should all be controlled.

data.v: सर्वाण्येवानुपूर्व्येण यद्यन्नानुविधीयते । अविभागगता बुद्धिर्भावे मनसि वर्तते । प्रवर्तमानं तु रजः सत्त्वमप्यनुवर्तते ॥
data.md: When one sense becomes subordinate to the Understanding, the latter, though really not different, enters the Mind in the form of existent things. Such is the case with the senses one after another with reference to the ideas that are said to be apprehended by them.

data.v: ये चैव भावा वर्तन्ते सर्व एष्वेव ते त्रिषु । अन्वर्थाः संप्रवर्तन्ते रथनेमिमरा इव ॥
data.md: All the three states which exist, viz., Sativa, Rajas, and Tamas, attach to those three (viz., Mind, Understanding, and Consciousness), and like the spokes of a car-wheel acting for their attachment, to the circumference of the wheel, they follow the various objects.

data.v: प्रदीपार्थं नरः कुर्यादिन्द्रियैर्बुद्धिसत्तमैः । निश्चरद्भिर्यथायोगमुदासीनैर्यदृच्छया ॥
data.md: The mind must covert the senses into a lamp for removing the darkness which obstructs the knowledge of the Supreme Self. This knowledge which is gained by Yogins with the help of the especial instruments of Yoga, is acquired without any particular exertion by men who abstain from worldly objects.

data.v: एवंस्वभावमेवेदमिति विद्वान्न मुह्यति । अशोचन्नप्रहृष्यंश्च नित्यं विगतमत्सरः ॥
data.md: The universe is of the nature. The man of knowledge, therefore, become never stupefied. Such a man never grieves, never rejoices, and is shorn of envy.

data.v: न ह्यात्मा शक्यते द्रष्टुमिन्द्रियैः कामगोचरैः । प्रवर्तमानैरनये दुर्धरैरकृतात्मभिः ॥
data.md: The soul cannot be seen with the help of the senses whose nature is to roam about among all objects of desire. Even pious men, whose senses are pure, cannot see the soul with their help what then should be said of the vicious whose senses are impure.

data.v: तेषां तु मनसा रश्मीन्यदा सम्यङ्नियच्छति । तदा प्रकाशते ह्यात्मा घटे दीप इव ज्वलन् । सर्वेषामेव भूतानां तमस्यपगते यथा ॥
data.md: When, however, a person, with the help of his mind, firmly holds their reins, it is then that his Soul sees itself like an object coming in view on account of the light of a lamp.

data.v: यथा वारिचरः पक्षी न लिप्यति जले चरन् । एवमेव कृतप्रज्ञो न दोषैर्विषयांश्चरन् । असज्जमानः सर्वेषु न कथंचन लिप्यते ॥
data.md: Likewise, a wise man by even enjoying all earthly objects without being attached to any of them, is never affected by shortcomings of any kind.

data.v: त्यक्त्वा पूर्वकृतं कर्म रतिर्यस्य सदात्मनि । सर्वभूतात्मभूतस्य गुणमार्गेष्वसज्जतः ॥
data.md: He who avoids acts after having performed them properly, and takes delight in the one really existent, viz., the Soul who has formed hinself the soul of all created beings, and who keeps himself understanding and senses which are created by the soul. The qualities can not apprehend the Soul. The Soul, however, apprehends them always.

data.v: सत्त्वमात्मा प्रसवति गुणान्वापि कदा च न । न गुणा विदुरात्मानं गुणान्वेद स सर्वदा ॥
data.md: He who avoids acts after having performed them properly, and takes delight in the one really existent, viz., the Soul who has formed hinself the soul of all created beings, and who keeps himself understanding and senses which are created by the soul. The qualities can not apprehend the Soul. The Soul, however, apprehends them always.

data.v: परिद्रष्टा गुणानां स स्रष्टा चैव यथातथम् । सत्त्वक्षेत्रज्ञयोरेतदन्तरं विद्धि सूक्ष्मयोः ॥
data.md: The Soul is the witness which sees the qualities and duly works them up. Mark this difference between the Understanding and the Soul both which are highly subtile.

data.v: सृजते तु गुणानेक एको न सृजते गुणान् । पृथग्भूतौ प्रकृत्या तौ संप्रयुक्तौ च सर्वदा ॥
data.md: One of them creates the qualities. The other does not create them. Though they are different from each other by nature, they are, however, always united.

data.v: यथा मत्स्योऽद्भिरन्यः सन्संप्रयुक्तौ तथैव तौ । मशकोदुम्बरौ चापि संप्रयुक्तौ यथा सह ॥
data.md: The fish residing in the water is different from the element in which it resides. But as the fish and the water forming its residence are always united, likewise the quality of goodness and the individual soul exist in a state of union. The gnat begotten of a rotten fig is really not the fig but different from it. As the gnat and the fig are seen to be united with each other, so are the qualities of goodness and the individual Soul.

data.v: इषीका वा यथा मुञ्जे पृथक्च सह चैव च । तथैव सहितावेतावन्योन्यस्मिन्प्रतिष्ठितौ ॥
data.md: As the blade in a clump of grass though distinct from the clump, exists in a state of union with it, so these two, though different from each other and each exists in its own self, are to be seen in a state of perpetual union.

data.v: सृजते तु गुणान्सत्त्वं क्षेत्रज्ञस्त्वनुतिष्ठति । गुणान्विक्रियतः सर्वानुदासीनवदीश्वरः ॥
data.md: The objects by which one is encircled are created by the Understanding. Without being connected with them, the Soul stands aloof, lording over them. The Understanding creates all objects. The three principal qualities are continually being transformed. The Soul, gifled with power, lords over them all, without, however, mingling with them.

data.v: स्वभावयुक्तं तत्सर्वं यदिमान्सृजते गुणान् । ऊर्णनाभिर्यथा सूत्रं सृजते तन्तुवद्गुणान् ॥
data.md: The objects created by the Understanding partake of its own nature. Like the threads created by the spider, the objects created by the Understanding partake of the nature of Understanding.

data.v: प्रध्वस्ता न निवर्तन्ते प्रवृत्तिर्नोपलभ्यते । एवमेके व्यवस्यन्ति निवृत्तिरिति चापरे ॥
data.md: When destroyed, the qualities do not cease to exist; only, their existence becomes invisible. When, however, a thing is beyond the range of the senses, its existence (or otherwise) is understood by inference. This is the opinion of some persons. Others hold that with destruction the qualities cease to be. are

data.v: उभयं संप्रधार्यैतदध्यवस्येद्यथामति । अनेनैव विधानेन भवेद्गर्भशयो महान् ॥
data.md: Meditating duly upon these two opinions, one should try his best according to the way one thinks proper. It is by this way that one should acquire eminence and take refuge in his own Soul alone.

data.v: अनादिनिधनं नित्यमासाद्य विचरेन्नरः । अक्रुध्यन्नप्रहृष्यंश्च नित्यं विगतमत्सरः ॥
data.md: The Soul is without beginning and without end. Understanding his Soul properly man should move and act, without yielding to anger, without indulging in joy, and always shorn of envy.

data.v: इत्येवं हृदयग्रन्थिं बुद्धिचिन्तामयं दृढम् । अतीत्य सुखमासीत अशोचंश्छिन्नसंशयः ॥
data.md: Cutting by this means the knot that is in his heart, created by the faculties of the Understanding, which is hard (to cut), but which can be destroyed by knowledge, one should live happily, without yielding to grief, and with his doubts removed.

data.v: तप्येयुः प्रच्युताः पृथ्व्या यथा पूर्णां नदीं नराः । अवगाढा ह्यविद्वांसो विद्धि लोकमिमं तथा ॥
data.md: Know that they who mix in worldly affairs, are as distressed in body and mind as persons ignorant of the art of swimming when they fall from the land into a vast and deep river.

data.v: न तु ताम्यति वै विद्वान्स्थले चरति तत्त्ववित् । एवं यो विन्दतेऽऽत्मानं केवलं ज्ञानमात्मनः ॥
data.md: Being conversant with the truth, the learned man, however, is never distressed, for he feels like one walking over firm land. Indeed, he who perceives his Soul to be such, viz., as full of consciousness which has knowledge alone for its mark, is never distressed.

data.v: एवं बुद्ध्वा नरः सर्वां भूतानामागतिं गतिम् । समवेक्ष्य शनैः सम्यग्लभते शममुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: By thus knowing the origin and end of all creatures, and by thus apprehending their distinctions, a person succeeds in acquiring high felicity.

data.v: एतद्वै जन्मसामर्थ्यं ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषतः । आत्मज्ञानं शमश्चैव पर्याप्तं तत्परायणम् ॥
data.md: This knowledge is the possession of a Brahmana in particular by virtue of his birth. Knowledge of the Soul, and happiness like above, are each fully sufficient to lead to Liberation.

data.v: एतद्बुद्ध्वा भवेद्बुद्धः किमन्यद्बुद्धलक्षणम् । विज्ञायैतद्विमुच्यन्ते कृतकृत्या मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: By gaining such knowledge one really becomes learned. What else is the mark of a person of knowledge? Having gained such knowledge, the wise men consider themselves successful and become liberated. Those things which produce fear to men shorn of knowledge do not do so to those who are gifted with knowledge. There is no end higher than the eternal end which is acquired by a learned person.

data.v: न भवति विदुषां महद्भयं; यदविदुषां सुमहद्भयं भवेत् । न हि गतिरधिकास्ति कस्यचि;द्भवति हि या विदुषः सनातनी ॥
data.md: By gaining such knowledge one really becomes learned. What else is the mark of a person of knowledge? Having gained such knowledge, the wise men consider themselves successful and become liberated. Those things which produce fear to men shorn of knowledge do not do so to those who are gifted with knowledge. There is no end higher than the eternal end which is acquired by a learned person.

data.v: लोकमातुरमसूयते जन;स्तत्तदेव च निरीक्ष्य शोचते । तत्र पश्य कुशलानशोचतो; ये विदुस्तदुभयं कृताकृतम् ॥
data.md: One sees with aversion all earthly objects of enjoyment which are, of course, full of shortcomings. Again seeing others pursue such objects with pleasure, another is filled with sorrow. But they who are conversant with both objects, viz., that which is fictitious and that which is not so, are never grieved and are truly happy.

data.v: यत्करोत्यनभिसंधिपूर्वकं; तच्च निर्णुदति यत्पुरा कृतम् । न प्रियं तदुभयं न चाप्रियं; तस्य तज्जनयतीह कुर्वतः ॥
data.md: What a man does without expectation of fruits dissipates his acts of a pristine life. The acts, however, of such a person both of this end and his pristine life cannot lead to Liberation. On the other hand, such destruction of former acts and such acts of this life cannot bring what is disagreeable (viz., hell), even if the wise man engages in acts.

data.v: यस्माद्धर्मात्परो धर्मो विद्यते नेह कश्चन । यो विशिष्टश्च धर्मेभ्यस्तं भवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे ॥
data.md: Shuka said May your reverend self describe what is the foremost of all duties, indeed, of that duty then which no higher one exists in this world.

data.v: धर्मं ते संप्रवक्ष्यामि पुराणमृषिसंस्तुतम् । विशिष्टं सर्वधर्मेभ्यस्तमिहैकमनाः शृणु ॥
data.md: Vyasa said I shall now describe to you duties having a very ancient origin and laid down by the Rishis, duties which are superior to all others. Listen to me with rapt attention.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणि प्रमाथीनि बुद्ध्या संयम्य यत्नतः । सर्वतो निष्पतिष्णूनि पिता बालानिवात्मजान् ॥
data.md: The maddening senses should carefully be governed by the understanding like a father checking his own in experienced children liable to fall into various evil habits.

data.v: मनसश्चेन्द्रियाणां च ह्यैकाग्र्यं परमं तपः । तज्ज्यायः सर्वधर्मेभ्यः स धर्मः पर उच्यते ॥
data.md: To withdraw the mind and the senses from all unworthy objects and their duc concentration (upon higher objects) is the highest penance. That is the highest of all duties. Indeed, that is said to be the highest duty.

data.v: तानि सर्वाणि संधाय मनःषष्ठानि मेधया । आत्मतृप्त इवासीत बहु चिन्त्यमचिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: Directing, by the help of the understanding, the senses having the mind for their sixth, and without, thinking of worldly objects which create innumerablc kinds of thought, one should live contented with his own self.

data.v: गोचरेभ्यो निवृत्तानि यदा स्थास्यन्ति वेश्मनि । तदा त्वमात्मनात्मानं परं द्रक्ष्यसि शाश्वतम् ॥
data.md: When withdrawn from the fields where they generally run loose, senses and the mind return for living in their proper abode, it is then that you will see in your own self the Eternal and Supreme Soul.

data.v: सर्वात्मानं महात्मानं विधूममिव पावकम् । तं पश्यन्ति महात्मानो ब्राह्मणा ये मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: Those great Brahmanas who are endud with wisdom succeed in seeing that Supreme and Universal Soul which resembles a blazing fire in effulgence.

data.v: यथा पुष्पफलोपेतो बहुशाखो महाद्रुमः । आत्मनो नाभिजानीते क्व मे पुष्पं क्व मे फलम् ॥
data.md: As a large tree enveloped with numberless branches and filled with many flowers and fruits, does not know in which part it has flowers and in which it has fruits, similarly the Soul, as modified by birth and other qualities, does not know whence it has come and whither it is to go. There is, however, an inner Soul, which sees every thing.

data.v: एवमात्मा न जानीते क्व गमिष्ये कुतो न्वहम् । अन्यो ह्यत्रान्तरात्मास्ति यः सर्वमनुपश्यति ॥
