data.md: As a large tree enveloped with numberless branches and filled with many flowers and fruits, does not know in which part it has flowers and in which it has fruits, similarly the Soul, as modified by birth and other qualities, does not know whence it has come and whither it is to go. There is, however, an inner Soul, which sees every thing.

data.v: ज्ञानदीपेन दीप्तेन पश्यत्यात्मानमात्मना । दृष्ट्वा त्वमात्मनात्मानं निरात्मा भव सर्ववित् ॥
data.md: One sees the Soul with the help of the lamp of knowledge. Seeing, therefore, yourself with you ownself, cease to regard your body as yourself and acquire omniscience.

data.v: विमुक्तः सर्वपापेभ्यो मुक्तत्वच इवोरगः । परां बुद्धिमवाप्येह विपाप्मा विगतज्वरः ॥
data.md: Purged of all sins, like a snake that has cast off its slough, one acquires high intelligence here and becomes free from every anxiety and the obligation of acquiring a new body.

data.v: सर्वतःस्रोतसं घोरां नदीं लोकप्रवाहिनीम् । पञ्चेन्द्रियग्राहवतीं मनःसंकल्परोधसम् ॥
data.md: Having its current spread in various directions, dreadful is this river of life carrying the world onward in its course. The five senses are its crocodiles. The mind and its objects are the shores.

data.v: लोभमोहतृणच्छन्नां कामक्रोधसरीसृपाम् । सत्यतीर्थानृतक्षोभां क्रोधपङ्कां सरिद्वराम् ॥
data.md: Cupidity and bewilderment of judgement are the grass and straw and anger are the dreadful reptiles which live in it. Truth forms the landing stage by its miry banks. Falsehood forms its surges, and anger its mire.

data.v: अव्यक्तप्रभवां शीघ्रां दुस्तरामकृतात्मभिः । प्रतरस्व नदीं बुद्ध्या कामग्राहसमाकुलाम् ॥
data.md: Originating from the Unmanifest, rapid is its current, and incapable of being crossed by persons of impure souls. Do you, with the help of the understanding, cross that river having desires for its alligators.

data.v: संसारसागरगमां योनिपातालदुस्तराम् । आत्मजन्मोद्भवां तात जिह्वावर्तां दुरासदाम् ॥
data.md: The worldly concerns form the ocean towards which that river runs. Genus and species form its unfathomable depth that none can understand. One's birth, O child, is the source from which that stream originates. Speech forms its eddies.

data.v: यां तरन्ति कृतप्रज्ञा धृतिमन्तो मनीषिणः । तां तीर्णः सर्वतोमुक्तो विपूतात्मात्मविच्छुचिः ॥
data.md: Only men endued with learning wisdom, and understanding succeed in crossing it which is so difficult to cross. Crossing it, you will free yourself from every attachment, acquiring a tranquil heart, knowing the Soul, and becoming pure in every way.

data.v: उत्तमां बुद्धिमास्थाय ब्रह्मभूयं गमिष्यसि । संतीर्णः सर्वसंक्लेशान्प्रसन्नात्मा विकल्मषः ॥
भूमिष्ठानीव भूतानि पर्वतस्थो निशामय । अक्रुध्यन्नप्रहृष्यंश्च ननृशंसमतिस्तथा । ततो द्रक्ष्यसि भूतानां सर्वेषां प्रभवाप्ययौ ॥
एवं वै सर्वधर्मेभ्यो विशिष्टं मेनिरे बुधाः । धर्मं धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ मुनयस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: Wise men consider such an act to be the foremost of all things. Indeed, this act of crossing the river of life is considered by the foremost of pious persons, by ascetics conversant with the truth, to be the greatest of all acts that one can perform.

data.v: आत्मनोऽव्ययिनो ज्ञात्वा इदं पुत्रानुशासनम् । प्रयताय प्रवक्तव्यं हितायानुगताय च ॥
data.md: This knowledge of the all-pervading Soul should be delivered to one's son. It should be inculcated upto one who is of controlled Senses, who is honest in conduct, and. that is docile or submissive.

data.v: आत्मज्ञानमिदं गुह्यं सर्वगुह्यतमं महत् । अब्रुवं यदहं तात आत्मसाक्षिकमञ्जसा ॥
data.md: This knowledge of Soul, which I have just explained to you, O child, and the evidence of whose truth is supplied by the Soul itself, is, indeed, the greatest of all mysteries, and the very highest knowledge which one can acquire.

data.v: नैव स्त्री न पुमानेतन्नैव चेदं नपुंसकम् । अदुःखमसुखं ब्रह्म भूतभव्यभवात्मकम् ॥
data.md: Brahma has no sex,-inale, a female, or neuter. It is neither sorrow nor happiness. Its essence the past, the future, and the present.

data.v: नैतज्ज्ञात्वा पुमान्स्त्री वा पुनर्भवमवाप्नुयात् । अभवप्रतिपत्त्यर्थमेतद्वर्त्म विधीयते ॥
data.md: Whatever the sex may be, male or female, the person who acquires the knowledge of Brahma hath never to go through re-births. This duty (of Yoga) has been described for acquiring Liberation from re-birth.

data.v: यथा मतानि सर्वाणि न चैतानि यथा तथा । कथितानि मया पुत्र भवन्ति न भवन्ति च ॥
data.md: These words which I have used for answering your question lead to Liberation in the same way as the various other opinions held by various other sages who have described this subject. I have explained the subject to you in the manner in which it should be explained. Those opinions sometimes yield fruit and sometimes not.

data.v: तत्प्रीतियुक्तेन गुणान्वितेन; पुत्रेण सत्पुत्रगुणान्वितेन । पृष्टो हीदं प्रीतिमता हितार्थं; ब्रूयात्सुतस्येह यदुक्तमेतत् ॥
data.md: Therefore, good child, when asked by a contented, meritorious, and self-controlled son or disciple, a preceptor should, with a delighted hcart, explain, according to their true import, these instructions which I have delivered for your benefit my son.

data.v: गन्धान्रसान्नानुरुन्ध्यात्सुखं वा; नालंकारांश्चाप्नुयात्तस्य तस्य । मानं च कीर्तिं च यशश्च नेच्छे;त्स वै प्रचारः पश्यतो ब्राह्मणस्य ॥
data.md: Vyasa said One should not show any liking for scents and tastes and other sorts of enjoyment. Nor should one accept ornaments and other articles giving the enjoyment of the senses of scent and taste. One should not seek honour and achievements and fame. Even this is the conduct of a Brahmana endued with vision.

data.v: सर्वान्वेदानधीयीत शुश्रूषुर्ब्रह्मचर्यवान् । ऋचो यजूंषि सामानि न तेन न स ब्राह्मणः ॥
data.md: He who has mastered all the Vedas, having served dutifully his preceptor and practised the vow of celibacy, he who knows all the Richs, Yajushes, and Samans, is not a twice-born one.

data.v: ज्ञातिवत्सर्वभूतानां सर्ववित्सर्ववेदवित् । नाकामो म्रियते जातु न तेन न च ब्राह्मणः ॥
data.md: One who treats all creatures like his kinsman, and one who is acquainted with Brahma, is said to be the master of all the Vedas. One who is shorn of desire, never dies. It is by such a conduct and such a bent of mind that one becomes a truly twice-born one.

data.v: इष्टीश्च विविधाः प्राप्य क्रतूंश्चैवाप्तदक्षिणान् । नैव प्राप्नोति ब्राह्मण्यमभिध्यानात्कथंचन ॥
data.md: Having performed only various sorts or religious rights and various sacrifices completed with sacrificial presents, one does not gain the dignity of a Brahmana if he is devoid of mercy and has not renounced desire.

data.v: यदा चायं न बिभेति यदा चास्मान्न बिभ्यति । यदा नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
data.md: When one ceases to fear all creatures and when all creatures cease to fear him, when one never desires for anything nor entertains hatred for anything, then he is said to acquire the dignity of Brahma.

data.v: यदा न कुरुते भावं सर्वभूतेषु पापकम् । कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
data.md: Then only a person attains to Brahma when he does not behave sinfully towards any creature in thought, word, or deed.

data.v: कामबन्धनमेवैकं नान्यदस्तीह बन्धनम् । कामबन्धनमुक्तो हि ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥
data.md: There is only one kind of fetter in this world, viz., the chain of desire, and no other. One who is freed from the chain of desire acquires the dignity of Brahma.

data.v: कामतो मुच्यमानस्तु धूम्राभ्रादिव चन्द्रमाः । विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन्धीरो धैर्येण वर्तते ॥
data.md: Shorn of desire like the Moon emerged from clouds, the wise man, purged of all stains, live patiently expecting his time.

data.v: आपूर्यमाणमचलप्रतिष्ठं; समुद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत् । स कामकान्तो न तु कामकामः; स वै लोकात्स्वर्गमुपैति देही ॥
data.md: That person into whose mind all sorts of desire enter like various rivers falling into the ocean without being able to increase its limits by their discharge, acquires equaniinity, but not he who cherishes desire for all worldly objects.

data.v: वेदस्योपनिषत्सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः । दमस्योपनिषद्दानं दानस्योपनिषत्तपः ॥
data.md: The Vedas have truth for their object. Truth has the mastering of the senses for its object. The subjugation of the senses has charity for its object. Charity has penance for its object.

data.v: तपसोपनिषत्त्यागस्त्यागस्योपनिषत्सुखम् । सुखस्योपनिषत्स्वर्गः स्वर्गस्योपनिषच्छमः ॥
data.md: Penance has renunciation for its recondite object. Renunciation has happiness for its object. Happiness has heaven for its object. Heaven has tranquillity for its object.

data.v: क्लेदनं शोकमनसोः संतापं तृष्णया सह । सत्त्वमिच्छसि संतोषाच्छान्तिलक्षणमुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: For the sake of contentment you should desire to acquire a serene understanding which is a valuable possession, indicating Liberation, and which, scorching sorrow and all objects or doubts together with thirst, destroys them entirely in the long run.

data.v: विशोको निर्ममः शान्तः प्रसन्नात्मात्मवित्तमः । षड्भिर्लक्षणवानेतैः समग्रः पुनरेष्यति ॥
data.md: One endued with those six qualities, viz., contentment, sorrowlessness, freedom from fetters, peacefulness, cheerfulness, and freedom from envy, is sure to become full or complete.

data.v: षड्भिः सत्त्वगुणोपेतैः प्राज्ञैरधिकमन्त्रिभिः । ये विदुः प्रेत्य चात्मानमिहस्थांस्तांस्तथा विदुः ॥
data.md: They who, transcending all consciousness of body, know the Soul which lives within the body and which is understood by only wise persons with the help of the six entities when endowed with only the quality of goodness, and with the help also of the other three, succeed in attaining to Liberation.

data.v: अकृत्रिममसंहार्यं प्राकृतं निरुपस्कृतम् । अध्यात्मं सुकृतप्रज्ञः सुखमव्ययमश्नुते ॥
data.md: The wise man enjoys endless beatitude by understanding the Soul which reigns within the body, which is shorn of the attributes of birth and death, which exists in its own true nature, which being uninvested with attributes requires no acts of purification, and which is identical with Brahma.

data.v: निष्प्रचारं मनः कृत्वा प्रतिष्ठाप्य च सर्वतः । यामयं लभते तुष्टिं सा न शक्यमतोऽन्यथा ॥
data.md: The pleasure which a man enjoys by governing his mind from roving in all directions and fixing it entirely on the Soul is such that its like cannot be acquired by one through any other means.

data.v: येन तृप्यत्यभुञ्जानो येन तुष्यत्यवित्तवान् । येनास्नेहो बलं धत्ते यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥
data.md: He is said to be a qualified master of the Vedas who is conversant with what gratifies one whose stomach is empty, which pleases one who is angry, and which invigorates one whose limbs are dry.

data.v: संगोप्य ह्यात्मनो द्वाराण्यपिधाय विचिन्तयन् । यो ह्यास्ते ब्राह्मणः शिष्टः स आत्मरतिरुच्यते ॥
data.md: Suspending his senses that have been properly checked from unworthy indulgence, he who lives in Yoga meditation, is said to be a Brahma. Such a person is said to acquire his joys from the Soul.

data.v: समाहितं परे तत्त्वे क्षीणकाममवस्थितम् । सर्वतः सुखमन्वेति वपुश्चान्द्रमसं यथा ॥
data.md: Regarding one who lives after having destroyed desire and devoting himself to the highest subject of existence, it should be said that his happiness is continuously increased like the lunar disc.

data.v: सविशेषाणि भूतानि गुणांश्चाभजतो मुनेः । सुखेनापोह्यते दुःखं भास्करेण तमो यथा ॥
data.md: Like the Sun removing darkness, happiness removes the sorrows of that Yogin who gets over both the gross and the subtile elements, as also the intellectual principle and the Unmanifest.

data.v: तमतिक्रान्तकर्माणमतिक्रान्तगुणक्षयम् । ब्राह्मणं विषयाश्लिष्टं जरामृत्यू न विन्दतः ॥
data.md: Decrepitude and death cannot attack that Brahma who has got beyond the sphere of acts, who has gone the destruction of the qualities themselves, and who is no longer attached to earthly objects.

data.v: स यदा सर्वतो मुक्तः समः पर्यवतिष्ठते । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थांश्च शरीरस्थोऽतिवर्तते ॥
data.md: Indeed, when freed from everything, the Yogin, lives in a state transcending both attachment and hatred, he is said to be, even ill this life, above his senses and all their objects.

data.v: कारणं परमं प्राप्य अतिक्रान्तस्य कार्यताम् । पुनरावर्तनं नास्ति संप्राप्तस्य परात्परम् ॥
data.md: That Yogin, who having gone above Prakriti attains to the Highest Cause, becomes freed from the obligation of a re-birth on account of his having attained 10 that which is the highest.

data.v: द्वंद्वानि मोक्षजिज्ञासुरर्थधर्मावनुष्ठितः । वक्त्रा गुणवता शिष्यः श्राव्यः पूर्वमिदं महत् ॥
data.md: Vyasa said A qualified preceptor should, first of all, describe the most capacious subject of spirituality, that has been explained in the previous chapter, to a disciple who wishes to enquire after Liberation after having transcended all pairs of opposites and performed the concerns of both profit and religion.

data.v: आकाशं मारुतो ज्योतिरापः पृथ्वी च पञ्चमी । भावाभावौ च कालश्च सर्वभूतेषु पञ्चसु ॥
data.md: Ether, wind, light, water, and earth as the fifth, and existence and non-existence and time, exist in all living creatures having the five for their component ingredients.

data.v: अन्तरात्मकमाकाशं तन्मयं श्रोत्रमिन्द्रियम् । तस्य शब्दं गुणं विद्यान्मूर्तिशास्त्रविधानवित् ॥
data.md: Space is unoccupied interstice. The organs of hearing consist of space. One knowing the science of elements endued with form should know that ether has sound for its attribute.

data.v: चरणं मारुतात्मेति प्राणापानौ च तन्मयौ । स्पर्शनं चेन्द्रियं विद्यात्तथा स्पर्शं च तन्मयम् ॥
data.md: Wind is essence of the feet. The vital airs are made of wind. Wind is the essence of the sense of touch, and touch is the attribute of wind.

data.v: ततः पाकः प्रकाशश्च ज्योतिश्चक्षुश्च तन्मयम् । तस्य रूपं गुणं विद्यात्तमोऽन्ववसितात्मकम् ॥
data.md: Heat, the digestive fire in the stomach, light that manifests all things, the heat of the body, and eye as the fifth, are all of light which has forin of various colours for its attribute.

data.v: प्रक्लेदः क्षुद्रता स्नेह इत्यापो ह्युपदिश्यते । रसनं चेन्द्रियं जिह्वा रसश्चापां गुणो मतः ॥
संघातः पार्थिवो धातुरस्थिदन्तनखानि च । श्मश्रु लोम च केशाश्च सिराः स्नायु च चर्म च ॥
इन्द्रियं घ्राणसंज्ञानं नासिकेत्यभिधीयते । गन्धश्चैवेन्द्रियार्थोऽयं विज्ञेयः पृथिवीमयः ॥
उत्तरेषु गुणाः सन्ति सर्वे सर्वेषु चोत्तराः । पञ्चानां भूतसंघानां संततिं मुनयो विदुः ॥
data.md: Each subsequent element partakes of the attribute or attributes of the preceding one in addition to its own. The (three) supplementary entities exist in all living creatures. The Rishis thus described the five elements and the effects and qualities emanating from or belonging to them.

data.v: मनो नवममेषां तु बुद्धिस्तु दशमी स्मृता । एकादशोऽन्तरात्मा च सर्वतः पर उच्यते ॥
data.md: The mind is the ninth, and the understanding is the tenth. The Soul, which is infinite, is the eleventh. It is considered as the highest of all.

data.v: व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिर्मनो व्याकरणात्मकम् । कर्मानुमानाद्विज्ञेयः स जीवः क्षेत्रसंज्ञकः ॥
data.md: The mind has doubt or its essence. The understanding discriminates and produces certainty. The Soul becomes known as Jiva or individual soul when invested with body through the consequences of acts.

data.v: एभिः कालाष्टमैर्भावैर्यः सर्वैः सर्वमन्वितम् । पश्यत्यकलुषं प्राज्ञः स मोहं नानुवर्तते ॥
data.md: That man who regards all living creatures as unsullied though endued with all these entities having time for their essence, has never to perform acts moved on by error.

data.v: शरीराद्विप्रमुक्तं हि सूक्ष्मभूतं शरीरिणम् । कर्मभिः परिपश्यन्ति शास्त्रोक्तैः शास्त्रचेतसः ॥
data.md: Vyasa said Those who are well-read in the scriptures see, with the help of acts laid down in the scriptures, the Soul which is encased in a subtile body and is highly subtile and which is dissociated from the gross body in which it lives.

data.v: यथा मरीच्यः सहिताश्चरन्ति; गच्छन्ति तिष्ठन्ति च दृश्यमानाः । देहैर्विमुक्ता विचरन्ति लोकां;स्तथैव सत्त्वान्यतिमानुषाणि ॥
data.md: As the rays of the Sun which move in dense masses through every part of the sky, cannot be seen by the naked eye though their existence can be perceived by reason, likewise, existent beings freed from gross bodies and moving in universe are above the reach of human vision,

data.v: प्रतिरूपं यथैवाप्सु तापः सूर्यस्य लक्ष्यते । सत्त्ववांस्तु तथा सत्त्वं प्रतिरूपं प्रपश्यति ॥
data.md: As the shining solar disc is seen reflected in the reflected water so the Yogin sees reflected within gross bodies the existent self.

data.v: तानि सूक्ष्माणि सत्त्वस्था विमुक्तानि शरीरतः । स्वेन तत्त्वेन तत्त्वज्ञाः पश्यन्ति नियतेन्द्रियाः ॥
data.md: All those souls again that are encased in subtile forins after being alienated from the gross bodies in which they lived, are perceptible to Yogins, who have controlled their senses and who are gifted with knowledge of the soul. Indeed, helped by their own souls, Yogins see those invisible beings,

data.v: स्वपतां जाग्रतां चैव सर्वेषामात्मचिन्तितम् । प्रधानद्वैधयुक्तानां जहतां कर्मजं रजः ॥
data.md: Whether asleep or awake, during the day or in the night, and during the night or in the day, they who practise Yoga after renouncing all the creations of the understanding the passion engendered by acts, and the power which Yoga begets, succeed in keeping their subtile form under complete control.

data.v: यथाहनि तथा रात्रौ यथा रात्रौ तथाहनि । वशे तिष्ठति सत्त्वात्मा सततं योगयोगिनाम् ॥
data.md: Whether asleep or awake, during the day or in the night, and during the night or in the day, they who practise Yoga after renouncing all the creations of the understanding the passion engendered by acts, and the power which Yoga begets, succeed in keeping their subtile form under complete control.

data.v: तेषां नित्यं सदानित्यो भूतात्मा सततं गुणैः । सप्तभिस्त्वन्वितः सूक्ष्मैश्चरिष्णुरजरामरः ॥
data.md: The individual soul which lives in such Yogins, always endued with the seven subtile principles, moves in all blissful regions, freed from decrepitude and death. I say “always,' and 'freed from death, as in common parlance, for, in sooth, that subtile form is also terininable.

data.v: मनोबुद्धिपराभूतः स्वदेहपरदेहवित् । स्वप्नेष्वपि भवत्येष विज्ञाता सुखदुःखयोः ॥
data.md: That man, however, who is under the influence of his mind and understanding, differentiates, even in his dreams, his own body from that of another and experiences both pleasure and pain.

data.v: तत्रापि लभते दुःखं तत्रापि लभते सुखम् । क्रोधलोभौ तु तत्रापि कृत्वा व्यसनमर्छति ॥
data.md: Really, even in his dreams he enjoys happiness and suffers misery; and yielding to anger and cupidity, suffers all sorts of calamities.

data.v: प्रीणितश्चापि भवति महतोऽर्थानवाप्य च । करोति पुण्यं तत्रापि जाग्रन्निव च पश्यति ॥
data.md: In his dreams he acquires great riches and feels highly satisfied: performs meritorious acts, and sees as he does when he is awake.

data.v: तमेवमतितेजोंशं भूतात्मानं हृदि स्थितम् । तमोरजोभ्यामाविष्टा नानुपश्यन्ति मूर्तिषु ॥
data.md: Men possessed by the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance never succeed in sceing within the gross body the sentiency which is a portion of the Supreme Soul to transcendent effulgence and which lies within the heart of every creature.

data.v: शास्त्रयोगपरा भूत्वा स्वमात्मानं परीप्सवः । अनुच्छ्वासान्यमूर्तीनि यानि वज्रोपमान्यपि ॥
data.md: They who learn Yoga for the purpose of obtaining a knowledge of Self succeed in getting over the inanimate and gross body, the imperceptible subtile body, and the casual body which is not destroyed on the occasion of even the universal destruction.

data.v: पृथग्भूतेषु सृष्टेषु चतुर्ष्वाश्रमकर्मसु । समाधौ योगमेवैतच्छाण्डिल्यः शममब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Of the duties laid down for the various modes of life including the fourth mode, these which I have described, which have Yoga for their foremost, and which indicate a complete stoppage of all operations of the Mind and the Understanding, have been laid down by Shandilya.

data.v: विदित्वा सप्त सूक्ष्माणि षडङ्गं च महेश्वरम् । प्रधानविनियोगस्थः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: Having comprehended the seven subtile principles, having comprehended also the Supreme Cause of the universe with the six attributes, and lastly having understood that the universe so only a modification of nescience endued with the three qualities, one succeeds in seeing high Brahina,

data.v: हृदि कामद्रुमश्चित्रो मोहसंचयसंभवः । क्रोधमानमहास्कन्धो विवित्सापरिमोचनः ॥
data.md: Vyasa said There is a wonderful tree in the heart of man, called Desire. It is born of the seed called Error. Anger and Pride from its large trunk. The desire for work is the hollow ground around its foot.

data.v: तस्य चाज्ञानमाधारः प्रमादः परिषेचनम् । सोऽभ्यसूयापलाशो हि पुरादुष्कृतसारवान् ॥
data.md: Ignorance is the root of that tree, and carelessness is the water which nourishes it. Envy forms its leaves. The evil acts of pristine lives supply it with vigour.

data.v: संमोहचिन्ताविटपः शोकशाखो भयंकरः । मोहनीभिः पिपासाभिर्लताभिः परिवेष्टितः ॥
data.md: Loss of judgement and anxiety are its twigs; grief forms its huge branches; and fear it is sprout. Thirst which seems agreeable, forms the creepers which twine round it on all sides.

data.v: उपासते महावृक्षं सुलुब्धास्तं फलेप्सवः । आयासैः संयतः पाशैः फलानि परिवेष्टयन् ॥
data.md: Avaricious men, fettered in chains of iron, sitting around that fruit-producing tree, worship it, in expectation of its fruit.

data.v: यस्तान्पाशान्वशे कृत्वा तं वृक्षमपकर्षति । गतः स दुःखयोरन्तं यतमानस्तयोर्द्वयोः ॥
data.md: He who, subduing those chains, cuts down that tree and seeks to renounce both sorrow and joy, succeeds in attaining to the end of both.

data.v: संरोहत्यकृतप्रज्ञः संतापेन हि पादपम् । स तमेव ततो हन्ति विषं ग्रस्तमिवातुरम् ॥
data.md: That foolish wight who nourishes this tree by enjoying the objects of the senses is destroyed by those very objects like a poisonous pill destroying the patient to whom it is given.

data.v: तस्यानुशयमूलस्य मूलमुद्ध्रियते बलात् । त्यागाप्रमादाकृतिना साम्येन परमासिना ॥
data.md: However, by the help of Yoga, a clever man forcibly cuts off with the sword of concentration, the far-reaching root of this tree.

data.v: एवं यो वेद कामस्य केवलं परिकर्षणम् । वधं वै कामशास्त्रस्य स दुःखान्यतिवर्तते ॥
data.md: One who understands that the end of all acts performed from the desire of fruit is rebirth or chains that bind, succeeds in getting over all sorrow.

data.v: शरीरं पुरमित्याहुः स्वामिनी बुद्धिरिष्यते । तत्र बुद्धेः शरीरस्थं मनो नामार्थचिन्तकम् ॥
data.md: The body is compared to a city. The understanding is its mistress. The mind living within the body is the minister of that mistress whose chief duty is to decide.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणि जनाः पौरास्तदर्थं तु परा कृतिः । तत्र द्वौ दारुणौ दोषौ तमो नाम रजस्तथा ॥
data.md: The senses are the citizens who are employed by the mind. For maintaining those citizens the mind shows a strong inclination for various sorts of acts. Two great faults are seen in those acts, namely, Darkness and ignorance.

data.v: यदर्थमुपजीवन्ति पौराः सहपुरेश्वराः । अद्वारेण तमेवार्थं द्वौ दोषावुपजीवतः ॥
data.md: Upon the fruits of those acts depend those citizens along with the chiefs of the city. The two faults live upon the fruits of those acts which are done by forbidden means.

data.v: तत्र बुद्धिर्हि दुर्धर्षा मनः साधर्म्यमुच्यते । पौराश्चापि मनस्त्रस्तास्तेषामपि चला स्थितिः ॥
data.md: Such being the case, the understanding, which of itself is unconquerable, goes down to a state of equality with the mind. Then again the senses, moved by the stained mind, lose their own firmness.

data.v: यदर्थं बुद्धिरध्यास्ते न सोऽर्थः परिषीदति । यदर्थं पृथगध्यास्ते मनस्तत्परिषीदति ॥
data.md: Those objects again to acquire which the understanding tries, tries, produce grief and ultimately meet with destruction. Those objects, after destruction, are remembered by the mind, and accordingly they afflict the mind even after they are lost.

data.v: पृथग्भूतं यदा बुद्ध्या मनो भवति केवलम् । तत्रैनं विवृतं शून्यं रजः पर्यवतिष्ठते ॥
data.md: The understanding is also afflicted, for the mind is said to be different from the understanding only when the mind is viewed regarding its chief function of getting impressions about whose certainty it is no judge. In sooth, however, the mind is identical with the understanding. The quality of Darkness which is in the understanding then overwhelms the Soul itself that lies over that understanding sullied by Darkness like an image upon a mirror.

data.v: तन्मनः कुरुते सख्यं रजसा सह संगतम् । तं चादाय जनं पौरं रजसे संप्रयच्छति ॥
data.md: It is the mind that first becomes united with darkness. Having united itself, it attacks the soul, the understanding, and the senses, and surrenders them to Rajas."

data.v: भूतानां गुणसंख्यानं भूयः पुत्र निशामय । द्वैपायनमुखाद्भ्रष्टं श्लाघया परयानघ ॥
दीप्तानलनिभः प्राह भगवान्धूम्रवर्चसे । ततोऽहमपि वक्ष्यामि भूयः पुत्र निदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Do you, O son, O sinless one, listen once more, with feeling of great pride, to the words given vent to by the Island-born Rishi on the subject of the enumeration of the principles. Like a blazing fire, the great Rishi said these words to his son who took after a fire wrapped in smoke. Instructed by what he said, I also, O son, shall again explain to you that certain knowledge.

data.v: भूमेः स्थैर्यं पृथुत्वं च काठिन्यं प्रसवात्मता । गन्धो गुरुत्वं शक्तिश्च संघातः स्थापना धृतिः ॥
data.md: The properties of earth are immobility, weight, hardness, productiveness, scent, density, capacity to absorb all sorts of scents, cohesion, habitableness, and that attribute of the mind which is called patience.

data.v: अपां शैत्यं रसः क्लेदो द्रवत्वं स्नेहसौम्यता । जिह्वा विष्यन्दिनी चैव भौमाप्यास्रवणं तथा ॥
data.md: The properties of water are coolness, taste, moisture, liquidity, softness, agreeableness, tongue, fluidity, capacity to the congealed, and power to melt all earthy products.

data.v: अग्नेर्दुर्धर्षता तेजस्तापः पाकः प्रकाशनम् । शौचं रागो लघुस्तैक्ष्ण्यं दशमं चोर्ध्वभागिता ॥
data.md: The properties of fire are irresistible energy, inflammability, heat, capacity to soften, light, sorrow, disease, speed, fury, and upward motion.

data.v: वायोरनियमः स्पर्शो वादस्थानं स्वतन्त्रता । बलं शैघ्र्यं च मोहश्च चेष्टा कर्मकृता भवः ॥
data.md: The properties of the wind are touch that is neither hot nor cool, power to help the organs of speech, independence, strength, celerity, power to help all kinds of discharge, power to raise other objects, breaths inhaled and exhaled, life, and birth.

data.v: आकाशस्य गुणः शब्दो व्यापित्वं छिद्रतापि च । अनाश्रयमनालम्बमव्यक्तमविकारिता ॥
data.md: The properties of space are sound, extension, capacity of being enclosed, absence of refuge, power of being unmanifest, capacity for modification, incapacity for resistance, material cause for producing the sense of hearing, and the unoccupied parts of the human body. These are the fifty properties, as declared, which form the essences of the five elementary entities.

data.v: अप्रतीघातता चैव भूतत्वं विकृतानि च । गुणाः पञ्चाशतं प्रोक्ताः पञ्चभूतात्मभाविताः ॥
data.md: The properties of space are sound, extension, capacity of being enclosed, absence of refuge, power of being unmanifest, capacity for modification, incapacity for resistance, material cause for producing the sense of hearing, and the unoccupied parts of the human body. These are the fifty properties, as declared, which form the essences of the five elementary entities.

data.v: चलोपपत्तिर्व्यक्तिश्च विसर्गः कल्पना क्षमा । सदसच्चाशुता चैव मनसो नव वै गुणाः ॥
data.md: Patience, reasoning, remembrance, forgetfulness or error, imagination, endurance, inclination towards good, inclination towards evil, and restlessness,-are the properties of the mind.

data.v: इष्टानिष्टविकल्पश्च व्यवसायः समाधिता । संशयः प्रतिपत्तिश्च बुद्धौ पञ्चेह ये गुणाः ॥
data.md: Destruction of both good and evil thoughts, perseverance, concentration, decision, and ascertainment of all things depending upon direct evidence, form the five properties of the understanding.

data.v: कथं पञ्चगुणा बुद्धिः कथं पञ्चेन्द्रिया गुणाः । एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व सूक्ष्मज्ञानं पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said How can the understanding be said to have five properties? How again, can the five senses be described as properties. Explain to me, O grandfather, all this abstruse topic.

data.v: आहुः षष्टिं भूतगुणान्वै; भूतविशिष्टा नित्यविषक्ताः । भूतविषक्ताश्चाक्षरसृष्टाः; पुत्र न नित्यं तदिह वदन्ति ॥
data.md: Bhishma said The understanding is said to possess altogether sixty properties, for the understanding includes the five clements. All those properties exist in the Soul. The Vedas say, O son, that the elements, their properties, are all created by Him who is above all decay. These entities, therefore, are not eternal.

data.v: तत्पुत्र चिन्ताकलितं यदुक्त;मनागतं वै तव संप्रतीह । भूतार्थतत्त्वं तदवाप्य सर्वं; भूतप्रभावाद्भव शान्तबुद्धिः ॥
data.md: The theories contradicting the Revelation which have in the previous Verses, O son, been placed before you, are all defective in the eye of reason. Minding, however, in this world all that I have said to you about the Supreme Brahma, do you after acquiring the power which the knowledge of Brahma offers, seek to acquire tranquillity of heart.

data.v: य इमे पृथिवीपालाः शेरते पृथिवीतले । पृतनामध्य एते हि गतसत्त्वा महाबलाः ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said These kings who lie on the Earth's surface amid their respective armies, these princes of great power, are now all deprived of life.

data.v: एकैकशो भीमबला नागायुतबलास्तथा । एते हि निहताः संख्ये तुल्यतेजोबलैर्नरैः ॥
data.md: Every one of these powerful kings was endued with strength equal to that of ten thousand elephants. Alas! these have all have killed by men equally powerful and strong.

data.v: नैषां पश्यामि हन्तारं प्राणिनां संयुगे पुरा । विक्रमेणोपसंपन्नास्तेजोबलसमन्विताः ॥
data.md: I do not see any one else that could kill any of these men in battle. All of them were gifted with great prowess, great energy, and great strength.

data.v: अथ चेमे महाप्राज्ञ शेरते हि गतासवः । मृता इति च शब्दोऽयं वर्तत्येषु गतासुषु ॥
data.md: Highly wise, they are now lying dead on the naked earth. about them, however, that are deprived of life, the word that is used is that they are dead.

data.v: इमे मृता नृपतयः प्रायशो भीमविक्रमाः । तत्र मे संशयो जातः कुतः संज्ञा मृता इति ॥
data.md: All these highly powerful kings are said to be dead. On this subject a doubt lies in my mind. Whence is life and whence is death.

data.v: कस्य मृत्युः कुतो मृत्युः केन मृत्युरिह प्रजाः । हरत्यमरसंकाश तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Who is it that dies? whence is death? Whence is death? Why does death take away living creatures. O grandfather, tell me this, O you who are like a god.

data.v: पुरा कृतयुगे तात राजासीदविकम्पकः । स शत्रुवशमापन्नः संग्रामे क्षीणवाहनः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said In days of yore, in the Krita age, O son, there was a king of the name of Anukampaka. His cars, elephants, horse and men having been reduced in number, he succumbed to the power of his enemies in battle.

data.v: तत्र पुत्रो हरिर्नाम नारायणसमो बले । स शत्रुभिर्हतः संख्ये सबलः सपदानुगः ॥
data.md: His son, named Hari, who was like Narayana himself in strength, was in that battle killed by his enemies along with all his followers and troops.

data.v: स राजा शत्रुवशगः पुत्रशोकसमन्वितः । यदृच्छयाशान्तिपरो ददर्श भुवि नारदम् ॥
data.md: Stricken with grief consequent on the death of his son, and himself brought under the control of enemies, the king devoted himself thence to a life of peacefulness. One day, while wandering listlessly he met the sage Narada on the Earth.

data.v: स तस्मै सर्वमाचष्ट यथा वृत्तं जनेश्वरः । शत्रुभिर्ग्रहणं संख्ये पुत्रस्य मरणं तथा ॥
data.md: The king told Narada all that had taken place, viz., the death of his son in battle and his own capture by his enemies.

data.v: तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा नारदोऽथ तपोधनः । आख्यानमिदमाचष्ट पुत्रशोकापहं तदा ॥
data.md: Having heard him Narada, endued with wealth of penances, then recited to him the following narrative for removing his grief consequent on the death of his son.

data.v: राजञ्शृणु समाख्यानमद्येदं बहुविस्तरम् । यथा वृत्तं श्रुतं चैव मयापि वसुधाधिप ॥
data.md: Narada said Listen now, O king, to the following long narrative which had taken place. I myself heard it formerly, O king!

data.v: प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा महातेजाः प्रजासर्गे पितामहः । अतीव वृद्धा बहुला नामृष्यत पुनः प्रजाः ॥
data.md: Endued with great energy, the Grandfather, at the time of the creation of the universe, created a large number of living beings. These multiplied greatly, and none of them died.

data.v: न ह्यन्तरमभूत्किंचित्क्वचिज्जन्तुभिरच्युत । निरुच्छ्वासमिवोन्नद्धं त्रैलोक्यमभवन्नृप ॥
data.md: There was not a part of the universe which was not overcrowded with living creatures, O you of great glory! Indeed, O king, the three worlds appeared to swell with living beings, and became, as it were, breathless.

data.v: तस्य चिन्ता समुत्पन्ना संहारं प्रति भूपते । चिन्तयन्नाध्यगच्छच्च संहारे हेतुकारणम् ॥
data.md: Then, O king, the Grandfather thought as to how he should destroy the surplus population. Thinking of the matter, the Self-create, however, could not decide by what means the destruction of life was to be performed.

data.v: तस्य रोषान्महाराज खेभ्योऽग्निरुदतिष्ठत । तेन सर्वा दिशो राजन्ददाह स पितामहः ॥
data.md: Thereupon, O king, Brahman gave way to anger and in consequence of his anger a fire issued out of his body. With that fire born of his anger, the Grandfather burnt all the quarters of the universe, O king.

data.v: ततो दिवं भुवं खं च जगच्च सचराचरम् । ददाह पावको राजन्भगवत्कोपसंभवः ॥
data.md: Indeed, that fire begotten of the Divine Lord's anger, O king, burnt Heaven and Earth and the Sky and the whole Universe with all its mobile and immobile beings.

data.v: तत्रादह्यन्त भूतानि जङ्गमानि ध्रुवाणि च । महता कोपवेगेन कुपिते प्रपितामहे ॥
data.md: Truly, when the Grandfather thus became angry, all mobile and immobile beings began to be consumed by the irresistible power of that anger.

data.v: ततो हरिजटः स्थाणुर्वेदाध्वरपतिः शिवः । जगाद शरणं देवो ब्रह्माणं परवीरहा ॥
data.md: Then the divine and sacred Sthanu, that destroyer of hostile heroes, that lord of the Vedas and the scriptures, filled with pity, tried to please Brahma.

data.v: तस्मिन्नभिगते स्थाणौ प्रजानां हितकाम्यया । अब्रवीद्वरदो देवो ज्वलन्निव तदा शिवम् ॥
data.md: When Sthanu came to Brahma out of feelings of benevolence, the great God addressed him, saying,-you deserved boons at my hands! What desire of yours shall I fulfil? I shall do you good by doing whatever you wish.

data.v: करवाण्यद्य कं कामं वरार्होऽसि मतो मम । कर्ता ह्यस्मि प्रियं शंभो तव यद्धृदि वर्तते ॥
data.md: When Sthanu came to Brahma out of feelings of benevolence, the great God addressed him, saying,-you deserved boons at my hands! What desire of yours shall I fulfil? I shall do you good by doing whatever you wish.

data.v: प्रजासर्गनिमित्तं मे कार्यवत्तामिमां प्रभो । विद्धि सृष्टास्त्वया हीमा मा कुप्यासां पितामह ॥
data.md: Sthanu said Know, O lord, that my prayer to you is in behalf of the created beings of the universe! These beings have been created by you. Do not be angry with them, O Grandfather.

data.v: तव तेजोग्निना देव प्रजा दह्यन्ति सर्वशः । ता दृष्ट्वा मम कारुण्यं मा कुप्यासां जगत्प्रभो ॥
data.md: By the fire born of your anger, illustrious one, all the created beings are being burnt. Seeing them placed in such a condition, I am filled with compassion. Do not be angry with them, O maker of the universe.

data.v: न कुप्ये न च मे कामो न भवेरन्प्रजा इति । लाघवार्थं धरण्यास्तु ततः संहार इष्यते ॥
data.md: The lord of all created beings said, I am not angry, nor is it my desire that all the create beings should perish. It is only for lightening the lord of the Earth that destruction is desirable.

data.v: इयं हि मां सदा देवी भारार्ता समचोदयत् । संहारार्थं महादेव भारेणाप्सु निमज्जति ॥
data.md: The godess Earth, suffering from the load of creatures, requested me, O Mahadeva, for destroying them, especially as she appeared to sink under their load into the water.

data.v: यदाहं नाधिगच्छामि बुद्ध्या बहु विचारयन् । संहारमासां वृद्धानां ततो मां क्रोध आविशत् ॥
data.md: When after exercising my intelligence even for a long time I could not find out the means by which to bring about the destruction of this overgrown population, it was then that I was possessed by ire.

data.v: संहारान्तं प्रसीदस्व मा क्रुधस्त्रिदशेश्वर । मा प्रजाः स्थावरं चैव जङ्गमं च विनीनशः ॥
data.md: Do not give way to anger, O lord of the celestials, about the destruction of living creatures! Be-pleased! Let not these mobile and immobile beings be destroyed.

data.v: पल्वलानि च सर्वाणि सर्वं चैव तृणोलपम् । स्थावरं जङ्गमं चैव भूतग्रामं चतुर्विधम् ॥
data.md: All tanks, all sorts of grass and herbs, all immobile beings, and all the four divisions of mobile creatures, are being consumed. The whole universe is about to be shorn of beings. Be pleased, O divine Lord! O you of pious soul this is the boon that I seek at your hands.

data.v: तदेतद्भस्मसाद्भूतं जगत्सर्वमुपप्लुतम् । प्रसीद भगवन्साधो वर एष वृतो मया ॥
data.md: All tanks, all sorts of grass and herbs, all immobile beings, and all the four divisions of mobile creatures, are being consumed. The whole universe is about to be shorn of beings. Be pleased, O divine Lord! O you of pious soul this is the boon that I seek at your hands.

data.v: नष्टा न पुनरेष्यन्ति प्रजा ह्येताः कथंचन । तस्मान्निवर्त्यतामेतत्तेजः स्वेनैव तेजसा ॥
data.md: If destroyed, these creatures would not return. Therefore, let this energy of yours be neutralised by your own energy.

data.v: उपायमन्यं संपश्य प्रजानां हितकाम्यया । यथेमे जन्तवः सर्वे निवर्तेरन्परंतप ॥
अभावमभिगच्छेयुरुत्सन्नप्रजनाः प्रजाः । अधिदैवनियुक्तोऽस्मि त्वया लोकेष्विहेश्वर ॥
त्वद्भवं हि जगन्नाथ जगत्स्थावरजङ्गमम् । प्रसाद्य त्वां महादेव याचाम्यावृत्तिजाः प्रजाः ॥
data.md: All this inobile and immobile creatures, O lord of the universe, originated from you. Pacifying you, O god of gods, I beg of you that living creatures may repeatedly come back into the world, undergoing repeated deaths!

data.v: श्रुत्वा तु वचनं देवः स्थाणोर्नियतवाङ्मनाः । तेजस्तत्स्वं निजग्राह पुनरेवान्तरात्मना ॥
data.md: Narada continued Hearing these words of Sthanu, the divine Brahma of controlled speech and mind himself suppressed that energy of his within his own heart.

data.v: ततोऽग्निमुपसंगृह्य भगवाँल्लोकपूजितः । प्रवृत्तिं च निवृत्तिं च कल्पयामास वै प्रभुः ॥
data.md: Suppressing that fire that had been destroying the universe, the illustrious Brahma, worshipped of all, and endued with illimitable power, then arranged for both birth and death of all living creatures.

data.v: उपसंहरतस्तस्य तमग्निं रोषजं तदा । प्रादुर्बभूव विश्वेभ्यः खेभ्यो नारी महात्मनः ॥
data.md: After the Self-create had withdrawn and suppressed that fire, there came out, from all the pores of his body, a lady dressed in robes of black and red, with black eyes, black palms, wearing a pair of charming ear-rings and bedecked with celestial ornaments.

data.v: कृष्णा रक्ताम्बरधरा रक्तनेत्रतलान्तरा । दिव्यकुण्डलसंपन्ना दिव्याभरणभूषिता ॥
सा विनिःसृत्य वै खेभ्यो दक्षिणामाश्रिता दिशम् । ददृशातेऽथ तौ कन्यां देवौ विश्वेश्वरावुभौ ॥
data.md: Having originated from Brahman's body, the lady sat on his right. The two foremost of gods thereupon espied her.

data.v: तामाहूय तदा देवो लोकानामादिरीश्वरः । मृत्यो इति महीपाल जहि चेमाः प्रजा इति ॥
data.md: Then, O king, the powerful Self-create, the prime Cause of all the worlds, saluted her and said, O Death, kill these creatures of the universe.

data.v: त्वं हि संहारबुद्ध्या मे चिन्तिता रुषितेन च । तस्मात्संहर सर्वास्त्वं प्रजाः सजडपण्डिताः ॥
data.md: Filled with ire and resolved to encompass the destruction of created beings, I have called you. Do you, there, begin to destroy all creatures foolish or learned.

data.v: अविशेषेण चैव त्वं प्रजाः संहर भामिनि । मम त्वं हि नियोगेन श्रेयः परमवाप्स्यसि ॥
data.md: O lady, kill all created beings without any exception. At my command you will acquire great prosperity.

data.v: एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी मृत्युः कमलमालिनी । प्रदध्यौ दुःखिता बाला साश्रुपातमतीव हि ॥
data.md: Thus addressed, the the goddess Death, adorned with a garland of lotuses, began to think sorrowfully and shed profuse tears.

data.v: पाणिभ्यां चैव जग्राह तान्यश्रूणि जनेश्वरः । मानवानां हितार्थाय ययाचे पुनरेव च ॥
data.md: Without suffering her tears, however, to fall down, she held them, O king, in her joinedhands. She then solicited the Self-born, moved by the desire of doing good to mankind.

data.v: विनीय दुःखमबला सा त्वतीवायतेक्षणा । उवाच प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा लतेवावर्जिता तदा ॥
data.md: Narada said The lady having large eyes, controlling her grief by self-exertion, addressed the Grandfather, with joined hands and bending low like a creeper.

data.v: त्वया सृष्टा कथं नारी मादृशी वदतां वर । रौद्रकर्माभिजायेत सर्वप्राणिभयंकरी ॥
data.md: And she said, How, O foremost of speakers, shall a lady like me who has sprung from you proceed to perform such a terrible feat-a feat, which is sure to terrorize all living creatures.

data.v: बिभेम्यहमधर्मस्य धर्म्यमादिश कर्म मे । त्वं मां भीतामवेक्षस्व शिवेनेश्वर चक्षुषा ॥
data.md: I fear to do any thing that is iniquitious! Do you find out a holy work for me. You see that I am frightened. Oh, look upon me mercifully.

data.v: बालान्वृद्धान्वयःस्थांश्च न हरेयमनागसः । प्राणिनः प्राणिनामीश नमस्तेऽभिप्रसीद मे ॥
data.md: I shall not be able to cut off living creatures,-infants, youths, and elderly ones,-who have done me no injury! O lord of all creatures, I bow to you, be pleased with me.

data.v: प्रियान्पुत्रान्वयस्यांश्च भ्रातॄन्मातॄः पितॄनपि । अपध्यास्यन्ति यद्देव मृतांस्तेषां बिभेम्यहम् ॥
data.md: I shall not be able to cut off dear sons, loved friends and brothers and mothers and fathers! If these perish their surviving relatives will surely curse me. Thinking of this I am filled with fear.

data.v: कृपणाश्रुपरिक्लेदो दहेन्मां शाश्वतीः समाः । तेभ्योऽहं बलवद्भीता शरणं त्वामुपागता ॥
data.md: The tears of the sorrow-stricken survivors will burn me for good. I am very much afraid of them. I seek your protection.

data.v: यमस्य भवने देव यात्यन्ते पापकर्मिणः । प्रसादये त्वा वरद प्रसादं कुरु मे प्रभो ॥
data.md: All sinful creatures will have to sink into hell. I seek to please you, O boon-giving god! Extend to me your favour, O powerful lord.

data.v: एतमिच्छाम्यहं कामं त्वत्तो लोकपितामह । इच्छेयं त्वत्प्रसादाच्च तपस्तप्तुं सुरेश्वर ॥
data.md: I seek the satisfaction of this wish, O Grandfather, of all the worlds. O foremost of all the gods, I seek, through your grace, permission to practise austere penances.

data.v: मृत्यो संकल्पिता मे त्वं प्रजासंहारहेतुना । गच्छ संहर सर्वास्त्वं प्रजा मा च विचारय ॥
data.md: The Grandfather said O Death, I have selected you for the destruction of all creatures! Go, and begin the task of killing all. Do not think thus.

data.v: एतदेवमवश्यं हि भविता नैतदन्यथा । क्रियतामनवद्याङ्गि यथोक्तं मद्वचोऽनघे ॥
data.md: This must surely take place. It cannot be otherwise. O sinless one, O fair lady do you satisfy the order I have given.

data.v: एवमुक्ता महाबाहो मृत्युः परपुरंजय । न व्याजहार तस्थौ च प्रह्वा भगवदुन्मुखी ॥
data.md: Thus addressed, O you of mighty arms, the lady called Death, O conqueror of hostile cities, did not utter a word, but humbly stood there with her eyes turned towards the powerful Lord of all creatures.

data.v: पुनः पुनरथोक्ता सा गतसत्त्वेव भामिनी । तूष्णीमासीत्ततो देवो देवानामीश्वरेश्वरः ॥
data.md: Brahma addressed her again and again, but the lady appeared to be herself deprived of life. Seeing her thus, the god of gods, that lords of lords, became silent.

data.v: प्रससाद किल ब्रह्मा स्वयमेवात्मनात्मवान् । स्मयमानश्च लोकेशो लोकान्सर्वानवैक्षत ॥
data.md: Indeed, the Self-create by an effort of his will, became pleased. Smiling the lord of all the worlds then looked at the universe.

data.v: निवृत्तरोषे तस्मिंस्तु भगवत्यपराजिते । सा कन्यापजगामास्य समीपादिति नः श्रुतम् ॥
data.md: We have heard that when that unconquered and illustrious lord controlled his anger, the lady (called Death) went away from his side.

data.v: अपसृत्याप्रतिश्रुत्य प्रजासंहरणं तदा । त्वरमाणेव राजेन्द्र मृत्युर्धेनुकमभ्ययात् ॥
data.md: Leaving Brahma's side without having promised to bring about the destruction of living creatures, Death speedily went, O king, 10 the sacred spot known by the name of Dhenuka.

data.v: सा तत्र परमं देवी तपोऽचरत दुश्चरम् । समा ह्येकपदे तस्थौ दश पद्मानि पञ्च च ॥
data.md: There the goddess performed austere penances for fifteen billions of years, standing upon one foot.

data.v: तां तथा कुर्वतीं तत्र तपः परमदुश्चरम् । पुनरेव महातेजा ब्रह्मा वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
कुरुष्व मे वचो मृत्यो तदनादृत्य सत्वरा । तथैवैकपदे तात पुनरन्यानि सप्त सा ॥
तस्थौ पद्मानि षट्चैव पञ्च द्वे चैव मानद । भूयः पद्मायुतं तात मृगैः सह चचार सा ॥
पुनर्गत्वा ततो राजन्मौनमातिष्ठदुत्तमम् । अप्सु वर्षसहस्राणि सप्त चैकं च पार्थिव ॥
data.md: And once more, O foremost of men, she passed twenty thousand years living upon air only. Once again, O king she observed the excellent vow of silence for eight thousand years passing the whole period in water. Then that maiden, O best of kings, went to river Kaushiki.

data.v: ततो जगाम सा कन्या कौशिकीं भरतर्षभ । तत्र वायुजलाहारा चचार नियमं पुनः ॥
ततो ययौ महाभागा गङ्गां मेरुं च केवलम् । तस्थौ दार्विव निश्चेष्टा भूतानां हितकाम्यया ॥
ततो हिमवतो मूर्ध्नि यत्र देवाः समीजिरे । तत्राङ्गुष्ठेन राजेन्द्र निखर्वमपरं ततः । तस्थौ पितामहं चैव तोषयामास यत्नतः ॥
data.md: Actuated by the desire of doing good to all living creatures, she stood perfectly motionless there like a piece of wood. Going thence to the summit of Himavat where the gods had celebrated their great sacrifice, she stood there for another hundred billions of years, standing upon only the toes of her feet, with the object of pleasing the Grandfather with such an act of austerity.

data.v: ततस्तामब्रवीत्तत्र लोकानां प्रभवाप्ययः । किमिदं वर्तते पुत्रि क्रियतां तद्वचो मम ॥
data.md: Going there the Creator and Destroyer of the universe again addressed her saying,-What are you doing, O daughter! Satisfy those words of mine!

data.v: ततोऽब्रवीत्पुनर्मृत्युर्भगवन्तं पितामहम् । न हरेयं प्रजा देव पुनस्त्वाहं प्रसादये ॥
data.md: Addressing the divine Grandfather, the maiden once more said, I am unable to destroy living creatures, O god! I seek to please you.

data.v: तामधर्मभयत्रस्तां पुनरेव च याचतीम् । तदाब्रवीद्देवदेवो निगृह्येदं वचस्ततः ॥
data.md: Frightened at doing the prospect of iniquity as she then was and employed in soliciting the Grandfather to excuse her for disobedience the Grandsire silenced her, and once more said to her',-

data.v: अधर्मो नास्ति ते मृत्यो संयच्छेमाः प्रजाः शुभे । मया ह्युक्तं मृषा भद्रे भविता नेह किंचन ॥
data.md: No sin shall visit you, O Death,! Do you, O auspicious maiden, begin the task of destroying living creatures! What I have said, O amiable girl, cannot be falsified.

data.v: धर्मः सनातनश्च त्वामिहैवानुप्रवेक्ष्यते । अहं च विबुधाश्चैव त्वद्धिते निरताः सदा ॥
data.md: Eternal virtue shall now live in you. Myself and all the gods shall always be busy with secking your well-being.

data.v: इममन्यं च ते कामं ददामि मनसेप्सितम् । न त्वा दोषेण यास्यन्ति व्याधिसंपीडिताः प्रजाः ॥
data.md: I grant you this other wish that is in your heart! Living creatures shall be possessed by disease, and shall not censure you.

data.v: पुरुषेषु च रूपेण पुरुषस्त्वं भविष्यसि । स्त्रीषु स्त्रीरूपिणी चैव तृतीयेषु नपुंसकम् ॥
data.md: You will become a male in all male beings, a female in all female beings, and a eunuch in all those who are so.

data.v: सैवमुक्ता महाराज कृताञ्जलिरुवाच ह । पुनरेव महात्मानं नेति देवेशमव्ययम् ॥
data.md: Thus addressed by Brahma, O king, the maiden at last said, with joined hands to that great and undecaying lord of all the gods-I am unable to satisfy your order. The great God again said to her, O Death, do you kill men!

data.v: तामब्रवीत्तदा देवो मृत्यो संहर मानवान् । अधर्मस्ते न भविता तथा ध्यास्याम्यहं शुभे ॥
यानश्रुबिन्दून्पतितानपश्यं; ये पाणिभ्यां धारितास्ते पुरस्तात् । ते व्याधयो मानवान्घोररूपाः; प्राप्ते काले पीडयिष्यन्ति मृत्यो ॥
data.md: I shall so ordain that you will not commit any sin by doing this, O auspicious lady. The tears that I see fall from your eyes, and which you still hold in joined hands, shall take the form of terrible diseases and even they shall destroy men when their time comes.

data.v: सर्वेषां त्वं प्राणिनामन्तकाले; कामक्रोधौ सहितौ योजयेथाः । एवं धर्मस्त्वामुपैष्यत्यमेयो; न चाधर्मं लप्स्यसे तुल्यवृत्तिः ॥
data.md: When the end of living creatures arrives you will send Desire and Anger together against them. You shall reap immeasurable merit. You will not commit sin, being yourself perfectly equal in your conduct.

data.v: एवं धर्मं पालयिष्यस्यथोक्तं; न चात्मानं मज्जयिष्यस्यधर्मे । तस्मात्कामं रोचयाभ्यागतं त्वं; संयोज्याथो संहरस्वेह जन्तून् ॥
data.md: By doing this you will only observe righteousness instead of committing sin. Do you, therefore, mind the work in hand, and addressing Desire and Anger begin to kill all living creatures.

data.v: सा वै तदा मृत्युसंज्ञापदेशा;च्छापाद्भीता बाढमित्यब्रवीत्तम् । अथो प्राणान्प्राणिनामन्तकाले; कामक्रोधौ प्राप्य निर्मोह्य हन्ति ॥
data.md: Thus addressed, that lady, Death, became afraid of Brahma's curse and answered him, saying,-Yes! Thence-forward she began to send Desire and Anger at the last hours of living creatures, and through their agency to kill them.

data.v: मृत्योर्ये ते व्याधयश्चाश्रुपाता; मनुष्याणां रुज्यते यैः शरीरम् । सर्वेषां वै प्राणिनां प्राणनान्ते; तस्माच्छोकं मा कृथा बुध्य बुद्ध्या ॥
data.md: Those tears that Death had shed are the diseases by which the bodies of men are possessed. At the destruction, therefore, of living creatures, one should not, understanding with the help of the intelligence, give way to grief.

data.v: सर्वे देवाः प्राणिनां प्राणनान्ते; गत्वा वृत्ताः संनिवृत्तास्तथैव । एवं सर्वे मानवाः प्राणनान्ते; गत्वावृत्ता देववद्राजसिंह ॥
data.md: As the senses of all creatures disappear when they are in dreamless slumber and return once more when they awake, similarly, upon the dissolution of their bodies, all human beings have to go into the other world and return thence to this, O foremost of kings.

data.v: वायुर्भीमो भीमनादो महौजाः; सर्वेषां च प्राणिनां प्राणभूतः । नानावृत्तिर्देहिनां देहभेदे; तस्माद्वायुर्देवदेवो विशिष्टः ॥
data.md: The element called wind, which has terrible energy and mighty prowess and dealening roars, acts as the life in all living creatures. When the bodies of living creatures are destroyed, that wind, passing from the old performs various functions in various new bodies. Therefore the wind is called the lord of senses and is superior to all other elements forming the gross body.

data.v: सर्वे देवा मर्त्यसंज्ञाविशिष्टाः; सर्वे मर्त्या देवसंज्ञाविशिष्टाः । तस्मात्पुत्रं मा शुचो राजसिंह; पुत्रः स्वर्गं प्राप्य ते मोदते ह ॥
data.md: The gods, without any exception, have to take birth as mortal creatures on Earth. Likewise, all mortal creatures also, succeed in acquiring the dignity to gods. Therefore, O foremost of kings, do not grieve for you son. Your son has gone to heaven, and is enjoying great happiness there.

data.v: एवं मृत्युर्देवसृष्टा प्रजानां; प्राप्ते काले संहरन्ती यथावत् । तस्याश्चैव व्याधयस्तेऽश्रुपाताः; प्राप्ते काले संहरन्तीह जन्तून् ॥
data.md: It was thus, O king, that Death was created by the Self-Create and it is in this way that she kills duly all living creatures when their time comes. the tears she had shed became diseases, which when their last hours come, snatch away all beings gifted with life.

data.v: इमे वै मानवाः सर्वे धर्मं प्रति विशङ्किताः । कोऽयं धर्मः कुतो धर्मस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said All men who live on this Earth, are filled with doubts regarding the nature .or righteousness. Who is this that is called Righteousness? Whence also does Righteousness come? come? Tell me this, O Grandfather! Is Righteousness for this world or for the next world? Or, is it for both here and hereafter? Tell me this, O grandfather?"

data.v: धर्मो न्वयमिहार्थः किममुत्रार्थोऽपि वा भवेत् । उभयार्थोऽपि वा धर्मस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
सदाचारः स्मृतिर्वेदास्त्रिविधं धर्मलक्षणम् । चतुर्थमर्थमित्याहुः कवयो धर्मलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: The practices of the good, the Smritis and the Vedas, are the three marks of righteousness. Besides these, the learned have said that the object (of doing works) is the fourth mark.

data.v: अपि ह्युक्तानि कर्माणि व्यवस्यन्त्युत्तरावरे । लोकयात्रार्थमेवेह धर्मस्य नियमः कृतः । उभयत्र सुखोदर्क इह चैव परत्र च ॥
data.md: The Rishis of old have said what acts are righteous and also classificd them as superior or inferior in point of merit. The rules of righteousness have been sanctioned for the conduct of the affairs of the world.

data.v: अलब्ध्वा निपुणं धर्मं पापः पापे प्रसज्जति । न च पापकृतः पापान्मुच्यन्ते केचिदापदि ॥
अपापवादी भवति यदा भवति धर्मवित् । धर्मस्य निष्ठा स्वाचारस्तमेवाश्रित्य भोत्स्यसे ॥
data.md: Some hold that sinful wights can never be purged of their sins. In times of difficulty a person by even speaking an untruth acquires the merit of speaking the truth. So a person who performs a sinful act acquires by that very means the merit of having done a pious act. Conduct is the refuge of righteousness. Helped by it you should know what righteousness is.

data.v: यदाधर्मसमाविष्टो धनं गृह्णाति तस्करः । रमते निर्हरन्स्तेनः परवित्तमराजके ॥
data.md: The very thief, stealing others things, spends them in acts of seeming virtue. During anarchy, the thief takes great pleasure in approaching what belongs to others.

data.v: यदास्य तद्धरन्त्यन्ये तदा राजानमिच्छति । तदा तेषां स्पृहयते ये वै तुष्टाः स्वकैर्धनैः ॥
data.md: When others, however, rob him of what he has gained by robbery, he then seeks a king. At even such a time, when he is highly indignant for his rights of property being violated, he secretly hankers after the riches of those who are contented with their own.

data.v: अभीतः शुचिरभ्येति राजद्वारमशङ्कितः । न हि दुश्चरितं किंचिदन्तरात्मनि पश्यति ॥
data.md: Fearlessly and without a doubt in his mind he goes to the king's palace, with a mind purged of every sin. Within even his own heart he does not see mark of any evil act.

data.v: सत्यस्य वचनं साधु न सत्याद्विद्यते परम् । सत्येन विधृतं सर्वं सर्वं सत्ये प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
data.md: To speak the truth is meritorious. There is nothing superior to truth. Everything is supported by truth, and everything depends upon truth.

data.v: अपि पापकृतो रौद्राः सत्यं कृत्वा पृथक्पृथक् । अद्रोहमविसंवादं प्रवर्तन्ते तदाश्रयाः । ते चेन्मिथोऽधृतिं कुर्युर्विनश्येयुरसंशयम् ॥
data.md: Even the sinful and dreadful persons swearing to keep the truth amongst themselves, do away with all grounds of quarrel and in a body perform their (sinful) deeds, depending upon truth. If they behaved falsely towards one another, they would, forsooth, he destroyed.

data.v: न हर्तव्यं परधनमिति धर्मः सनातनः । मन्यन्ते बलवन्तस्तं दुर्बलैः संप्रवर्तितम् । यदा नियतिदौर्बल्यमथैषामेव रोचते ॥
data.md: One should not take other's properties. That is an eternal duty. Powerful men consider it as one that has been introduced by the weak.

data.v: न ह्यत्यन्तं बलयुता भवन्ति सुखिनोऽपि वा । तस्मादनार्जवे बुद्धिर्न कार्या ते कथंचन ॥
असाधुभ्योऽस्य न भयं न चोरेभ्यो न राजतः । न किंचित्कस्यचित्कुर्वन्निर्भयः शुचिरावसेत् ॥
data.md: Therefore, do not ever think of doing a wrong act. One behaving in this way has no fear of dishonest men or thieves, or the king. Not having injured any one, such a man lives fearlessly and with a pure heart.

data.v: सर्वतः शङ्कते स्तेनो मृगो ग्राममिवेयिवान् । बहुधाचरितं पापमन्यत्रैवानुपश्यति ॥
data.md: A thief fears every body, like a deer driven from the forest into the midst of an inhabited village. He considers other people as sinful as himself.

data.v: मुदितः शुचिरभ्येति सर्वतो निर्भयः सदा । न हि दुश्चरितं किंचिदात्मनोऽन्येषु पश्यति ॥
data.md: Fearlessly and without a doubt in his mind he goes to the king's palace, with a mind purged of every sin. Within even his own heart he does not see mark of any evil act.

data.v: दातव्यमित्ययं धर्म उक्तो भूतहिते रतैः । तं मन्यन्ते धनयुताः कृपणैः संप्रवर्तितम् ॥
data.md: Persons who do good to all creatures have said that charity is another high duty. The rich people think that this duty has been laid down by the poor.

data.v: यदा नियतिकार्पण्यमथैषामेव रोचते । न ह्यत्यन्तं धनवन्तो भवन्ति सुखिनोऽपि वा ॥
data.md: When, however, ill luck overtakes, these men they the approve of this injunction. Again, they who surpass others in strength or power do not necessarily become happy.

data.v: यदन्यैर्विहितं नेच्छेदात्मनः कर्म पूरुषः । न तत्परेषु कुर्वीत जानन्नप्रियमात्मनः ॥
data.md: A person should never do that to others which he does not like to be done to him by others, knowing how painful it is to himself.

data.v: योऽन्यस्य स्यादुपपतिः स कं किं वक्तुमर्हति । यदन्यस्तस्य तत्कुर्यान्न मृष्येदिति मे मतिः ॥
data.md: What can a man seeking another man's wife say to another man? It is seen, however, that even such a man, when he sees his wife with another person, becomes unable to forgive the act.

data.v: जीवितुं यः स्वयं चेच्छेत्कथं सोऽन्यं प्रघातयेत् । यद्यदात्मन इच्छेत तत्परस्यापि चिन्तयेत् ॥
data.md: How can a person who wishes to himself take breath think of preventing another by a murderous act from doing the same? Whatever wishes one cherishes about his own self, one should certainly cherish regarding another.

data.v: अतिरिक्तैः संविभजेद्भोगैरन्यानकिंचनान् । एतस्मात्कारणाद्धात्रा कुसीदं संप्रवर्तितम् ॥
data.md: With his surplus riches he should remove the wants of the poor. Therefore the Creator ordained the practice of multiplying one's wealth.

data.v: यस्मिंस्तु देवाः समये संतिष्ठेरंस्तथा भवेत् । अथ चेल्लाभसमये स्थितिर्धर्मेऽपि शोभना ॥
data.md: One should walk along that road by proceeding along which he may hope to meet with the gods; or, at such times when wealth is acquired, the duties of sacrifice and gift are highly spoken of.

data.v: सर्वं प्रियाभ्युपगतं धर्ममाहुर्मनीषिणः । पश्यैतं लक्षणोद्देशं धर्माधर्मे युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: The sages have said that righteousness consists in the performance of objects by means of agreeable means. See, O Yudhisthira, that this is the standard that has been upheld in pointing out the marks of virtue and sin.

data.v: लोकसंग्रहसंयुक्तं विधात्रा विहितं पुरा । सूक्ष्मधर्मार्थनियतं सतां चरितमुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: In days of yore the Creator ordained virtue gifting it with the power of holding the world together. The excellent conduct of the good, is subjected to restraints for acquiring virtue which depends upon many delicate considerations.

data.v: धर्मलक्षणमाख्यातमेतत्ते कुरुसत्तम । तस्मादनार्जवे बुद्धिर्न कार्या ते कथंचन ॥
data.md: The marks of virtue have now been described to you, O best of Kuru's race? Do not, therefore, at any time think of doing a wrong act.

data.v: सूक्ष्मं साधु समादिष्टं भवता धर्मलक्षणम् । प्रतिभा त्वस्ति मे काचित्तां ब्रूयामनुमानतः ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said You say that virtue or duty depends upon delicate consideration, that it is marked out by the conduct of the good, that it is fraught with restraints, and that its characteristics are also contained in the Vedas. It appears to me, however, that I have a certain inward light by virtue of which I can differentiate between right and wrong by inferences.

data.v: भूयांसो हृदये ये मे प्रश्नास्ते व्याहृतास्त्वया । इममन्यं प्रवक्ष्यामि न राजन्विग्रहादिव ॥
data.md: Numberless questions which I had wished to ask you have all been answered by you. There is one question, however, that I shall just now put. It is not prompted, O king, by desire of mere discussion.

data.v: इमानि हि प्रापयन्ति सृजन्त्युत्तारयन्ति च । न धर्मः परिपाठेन शक्यो भारत वेदितुम् ॥
data.md: All these embodied creatures, it seems, take birth, exist, and renounce their bodies, of their own nature. Duty and its opposite, therefore, cannot be determined, O Bharata, by study of the scriptures alone.

data.v: अन्यो धर्मः समस्थस्य विषमस्थस्य चापरः । आपदस्तु कथं शक्याः परिपाठेन वेदितुम् ॥
data.md: The duties of a rich person are of one sort. Those of a person who has fallen into distress are of another sort. How can duty in the time of poverty be determined by reading the scriptures alone?

data.v: सदाचारो मतो धर्मः सन्तस्त्वाचारलक्षणाः । साध्यासाध्यं कथं शक्यं सदाचारो ह्यलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: The acts of the good, as you have said, form virtue. The good, however, are to be known by their acts. The definition, therefore, has at the bottom a begging of the question, and the result is that what is meant by conduct of the good remains unsettled.

data.v: दृश्यते धर्मरूपेण अधर्मं प्राकृतश्चरन् । धर्मं चाधर्मरूपेण कश्चिदप्राकृतश्चरन् ॥
data.md: It is seen that some ordinary man commits sin while apparently achieving virtue. Some extraordinary person again may be seen who achieves virtue by committing acts which are seemingly sinful.

data.v: पुनरस्य प्रमाणं हि निर्दिष्टं शास्त्रकोविदैः । वेदवादाश्चानुयुगं ह्रसन्तीति ह नः श्रुतम् ॥
data.md: Then, again, the proof has been given by even those who are well-conversant with the scriptures themselves, for we have heard that the ordinances of the Vedas disappear gradually in every successive cycle. The duties in the Krita age are of one sort. Those in the Treta are of another sort, and those in the Dvapara are of a different sort. The duties in the Kali age, again, are entirely of a different character. It seems, therefore, that duties have been sanctioned for the respective cycles according to the powers of human beings in the different ages.

data.v: अन्ये कृतयुगे धर्मास्त्रेतायां द्वापरेऽपरे । अन्ये कलियुगे धर्मा यथाशक्तिकृता इव ॥
data.md: Then, again, the proof has been given by even those who are well-conversant with the scriptures themselves, for we have heard that the ordinances of the Vedas disappear gradually in every successive cycle. The duties in the Krita age are of one sort. Those in the Treta are of another sort, and those in the Dvapara are of a different sort. The duties in the Kali age, again, are entirely of a different character. It seems, therefore, that duties have been sanctioned for the respective cycles according to the powers of human beings in the different ages.

data.v: आम्नायवचनं सत्यमित्ययं लोकसंग्रहः । आम्नायेभ्यः परं वेदाः प्रसृता विश्वतोमुखाः ॥
data.md: When, therefore, all the declarations in the Vedas do not suit equally all the ages, the saying that the Vedas are true is only a popular parlance given vent to for popular satisfaction. whose range From the Shrutis have originated the Smritis is very wide.

data.v: ते चेत्सर्वे प्रमाणं वै प्रमाणं तन्न विद्यते । प्रमाणे चाप्रमाणे च विरुद्धे शास्त्रता कुतः ॥
data.md: The saying of the Vedas are, in the opinion of the ordinary person, contradictory. Whether on severe ! this is authoritative or that is so, when there is this conflict, how can they be considered to be spiritual.

data.v: धर्मस्य ह्रियमाणस्य बलवद्भिर्दुरात्मभिः । या या विक्रियते संस्था ततः सापि प्रणश्यति ॥
data.md: Then, again, it is seen, that when some wicked wights of great power cause certain portions of religious acts to be stopped, these are destroyed for ever.

data.v: विद्म चैवं न वा विद्म शक्यं वा वेदितुं न वा । अणीयान्क्षुरधाराया गरीयान्पर्वतादपि ॥
data.md: Whether we know it or not, whether we are able to determine it or not, the course of duty is sharper than the edge of a razor and grosser than even a mountain.

data.v: गन्धर्वनगराकारः प्रथमं संप्रदृश्यते । अन्वीक्ष्यमाणः कविभिः पुनर्गच्छत्यदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: Virtue at first appears in the form of the romantic house of vapour seen in the distant sky. When, however, it is examined by the ! learned, it disappears.

data.v: निपानानीव गोभ्याशे क्षेत्रे कुल्येव भारत । स्मृतोऽपि शाश्वतो धर्मो विप्रहीणो न दृश्यते ॥
data.md: Like the small ponds at which cattle drink or the shallow canals along cultivated fields, that dry up very soon, the eternal practices laid down in the Smrities, falling into discontinuance, at last disappear for good.

data.v: कामादन्ये क्षयादन्ये कारणैरपरैस्तथा । असन्तो हि वृथाचारं भजन्ते बहवोऽपरे ॥
data.md: Amongst good men, some are seen to become hypocrites by allowing themselves to be moved by desire. Some become so, desiring by others. Many others tread in the same path, moved by various other motives of a similar nature.

data.v: धर्मो भवति स क्षिप्रं विलीनस्त्वेव साधुषु । अन्ये तानाहुरुन्मत्तानपि चावहसन्त्युत ॥
data.md: It cannot be gainsaid that such acts are righteous. Fools, again, hold that virtue is an empty sound among those called good. They ridicule such persons and consider them as men bereft of reason.

data.v: महाजना ह्युपावृत्ता राजधर्मं समाश्रिताः । न हि सर्वहितः कश्चिदाचारः संप्रदृश्यते ॥
data.md: Many great men, again, neglecting the duties of their own order, follow those of the Kshatriyas. No such conduct, therefore, is to be seen, which is for universal benevolence.

data.v: तेनैवान्यः प्रभवति सोऽपरं बाधते पुनः । दृश्यते चैव स पुनस्तुल्यरूपो यदृच्छया ॥
data.md: By a certain action, one becomes really meritorious. The same actions prevent another from the acquisition of merit. Another, by performing those actions at his pleasure, it is seen, remains unchanged.

data.v: येनैवान्यः प्रभवति सोऽपरानपि बाधते । आचाराणामनैकाग्र्यं सर्वेषामेव लक्षयेत् ॥
data.md: Thus that action by which one reaps merit, obstructs another in the acquisition of merit. One may thus seen that all actions are not peculiar in motive and character.

data.v: चिराभिपन्नः कविभिः पूर्वं धर्म उदाहृतः । तेनाचारेण पूर्वेण संस्था भवति शाश्वती ॥
data.md: It seems, therefore, that only that which the learned of old denominated righteousness is righteousness to this day; and through that course of conduct the distinctions and limitations have become eternal.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । तुलाधारस्य वाक्यानि धर्मे जाजलिना सह ॥
data.md: Regarding it is cited the old conversation of Tuladhara with Jajali on the subject of virtue. There was once a Brahmana named Jajali who lived in a certain forest, like a forest-recluse.

data.v: वने वनचरः कश्चिज्जाजलिर्नाम वै द्विजः । सागरोद्देशमागम्य तपस्तेपे महातपाः ॥
data.md: Practising austere penances, he proceeded at a certain time towards the sea-shore, and arrived there began to practise the most austere penances.

data.v: नियतो नियताहारश्चीराजिनजटाधरः । मलपङ्कधरो धीमान्बहून्वर्षगणान्मुनिः ॥
data.md: Observing many vows and restraints his food restricted by fast, his body clad in rags and skins, bearing matted locks on his head, his entire body smeared with filth and clay, the intelligent Brahmana passed many years there, speechless.

data.v: स कदाचिन्महातेजा जलवासो महीपते । चचार लोकान्विप्रर्षिः प्रेक्षमाणो मनोजवः ॥
data.md: Highly energetic that regenerate ascetic, O king, while living within the waters, travelled through all the worlds with the speed of the mind, desirous of seeing all things.

data.v: स चिन्तयामास मुनिर्जलमध्ये कदाचन । विप्रेक्ष्य सागरान्तां वै महीं सवनकाननाम् ॥
data.md: Having seen the whole Earth bounded by the ocean and adorned with rivers and lakes and forests, the ascetic one day, while sitting under the water, began to think thus:न मया सदृशोऽस्तीह लोके स्थावरजङ्गमे।

data.v: न मया सदृशोऽस्तीह लोके स्थावरजङ्गमे । अप्सु वैहायसं गच्छेन्मया योऽन्यः सहेति वै ॥
data.md: In this world of mobile and immobile creatures there is none who can equal me! Who can travel with me among the stars and planets in the sky and live again within the waters!

data.v: स दृश्यमानो रक्षोभिर्जलमध्येऽवदत्ततः । अब्रुवंश्च पिशाचास्तं नैवं त्वं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Unseen by the Rakshasas while he said this to himself, the Pishachas said to him,-You should not say so!

data.v: तुलाधारो वणिग्धर्मा वाराणस्यां महायशाः । सोऽप्येवं नार्हते वक्तुं यथा त्वं द्विजसत्तम ॥
data.md: There is a man named Tuladhara highly illustrious and doing the business of buying and selling, Even he, O best of twice-born ones, is not worthy of saying such words as you say!

data.v: इत्युक्तो जाजलिर्भूतैः प्रत्युवाच महातपाः । पश्येयं तमहं प्राज्ञं तुलाधारं यशस्विनम् ॥
data.md: Thus addressed by those beings, Jajali of austere penances replied to them, saying,-I shall see that famous Tuladhara who is endued with such wisdom!

data.v: इति ब्रुवाणं तमृषिं रक्षांस्युद्धृत्य सागरात् । अब्रुवन्गच्छ पन्थानमास्थायेमं द्विजोत्तम ॥
data.md: When the Rishi said this, those superhuman beings raised him from the sea, and said to him,-best of twice-born one, go along this road!

data.v: इत्युक्तो जाजलिर्भूतैर्जगाम विमनास्तदा । वाराणस्यां तुलाधारं समासाद्याब्रवीद्वचः ॥
data.md: Thus addressed by those beings, Jajali went onwards with a depressed heart. Arrived at Baranasi he met Tuladhara whom he addressed thus.

data.v: किं कृतं सुकृतं कर्म तात जाजलिना पुरा । येन सिद्धिं परां प्राप्तस्तन्नो व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said What, O sire, are those difficult feats which Jajali had performed before for which he had acquired such great success? You should describe them to me.

data.v: अतीव तपसा युक्तो घोरेण स बभूव ह । नद्युपस्पर्शनरतः सायं प्रातर्महातपाः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Jajali had practised penances of the severest austerities. He used to perform ablutions morning and cvening.

data.v: अग्नीन्परिचरन्सम्यक्स्वाध्यायपरमो द्विजः । वानप्रस्थविधानज्ञो जाजलिर्ज्वलितः श्रिया ॥
data.md: Carefully serving his fires, he was given to the study of the Vedas. Well conversant with the duties laid down for hermits, Jajali, seemed to shine with effulgence.

data.v: सत्ये तपसि तिष्ठन्स न च धर्ममवैक्षत । वर्षास्वाकाशशायी स हेमन्ते जलसंश्रयः ॥
data.md: He continued to live in the forest, performing penances, But he never took himself for one who had acquired any merit by his acts. During the rains he slept under the open sky. In auturnn he sat in water.

data.v: वातातपसहो ग्रीष्मे न च धर्ममविन्दत । दुःखशय्याश्च विविधा भूमौ च परिवर्तनम् ॥
data.md: In summer he exposed himself to the sun and the wind. Still he never took himself for one who had acquired any merit by such acts. He used to sleep on various sorts of painful beds and also on the naked earth.

data.v: ततः कदाचित्स मुनिर्वर्षास्वाकाशमास्थितः । अन्तरिक्षाज्जलं मूर्ध्ना प्रत्यगृह्णान्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
data.md: On one occasion that ascetic, while standing under the sky during the rainy season, received on his head repeated showers froin the clouds.

data.v: अथ तस्य जटाः क्लिन्ना बभूवुर्ग्रथिताः प्रभो । अरण्यगमनान्नित्यं मलिनो मलसंयुताः ॥
data.md: He had to pass through the forests again and again. Partly with exposure to the rains and partly with the filth they caught, the locks of that pure Rishi became entangled and intertwined with one another.

data.v: स कदाचिन्निराहारो वायुभक्षो महातपाः । तस्थौ काष्ठवदव्यग्रो न चचाल च कर्हिचित् ॥
data.md: At one time abstaining entirely from food and living upon air alone, that great ascetic, stood in the forest like a wooden post Unmoved at heart, he stood there, without once moving an inch.

data.v: तस्य स्म स्थाणुभूतस्य निर्विचेष्टस्य भारत । कुलिङ्गशकुनौ राजन्नीडं शिरसि चक्रतुः ॥
data.md: While he stood there unmoved like a wooden post, О Bharata, a pair of Kulinga birds, O king, built their nest on his head.

data.v: स तौ दयावान्विप्रर्षिरुपप्रैक्षत दम्पती । कुर्वाणं नीडकं तत्र जटासु तृणतन्तुभिः ॥
data.md: Filled with pity, the great Rishis allowed those birds in building their nest among his matted locks with pieces of grass.

data.v: यदा स न चलत्येव स्थाणुभूतो महातपाः । ततस्तौ परिविश्वस्तौ सुखं तत्रोषतुस्तदा ॥
data.md: And as the ascetic stood there like a wooden post, the two birds lived on his head happily and confidingly.

data.v: अतीतास्वथ वर्षासु शरत्काल उपस्थिते । प्राजापत्येन विधिना विश्वासात्काममोहितौ ॥
data.md: The rainy season passed away and autumn set in. Actuated by desire, the couple approached each other according to the law of the Creator, and with perfect confidence laid their eggs, O king, on the head of that Rishi.

data.v: तत्रापातयतां राजञ्शिरस्यण्डानि खेचरौ । तान्यबुध्यत तेजस्वी स विप्रः संशितव्रतः ॥
बुद्ध्वा च स महातेजा न चचालैव जाजलिः । धर्मे धृतमना नित्यं नाधर्मं स त्वरोचयत् ॥
data.md: Of rigid vows and endued with energy, the ascetic knew it. Knowing even what the birds had done, Jajali did not move. Bent strongly upon acquiring merit, no act involving the slightest injury to others could meet with his approval.

data.v: अहन्यहनि चागम्य ततस्तौ तस्य मूर्धनि । आश्वासितौ वै वसतः संप्रहृष्टौ तदा विभो ॥
data.md: Going away and returning every day from, and to his head, the birds happily and trustfully lived there, O powerful king.

data.v: अण्डेभ्यस्त्वथ पुष्टेभ्यः प्रजायन्त शकुन्तकाः । व्यवर्धन्त च तत्रैव न चाकम्पत जाजलिः ॥
data.md: When in the course of time the eggs became mature and young ones came out, they began to grow up in that nest, for Jajali moved not in the least.

data.v: स रक्षमाणस्त्वण्डानि कुलिङ्गानां यतव्रतः । तथैव तस्थौ धर्मात्मा निर्विचेष्टः समाहितः ॥
data.md: Firmly observing his vows, the righteous Rishi continued to hold and protect those eggs by standing on that very spot perfectly motionless and immersed in Yoga meditation.

data.v: ततस्तु कालसमये बभूवुस्तेऽथ पक्षिणः । बुबुधे तांश्च स मुनिर्जातपक्षाञ्शकुन्तकान् ॥
data.md: In course of time the young ones grew and became endued with wings. The Muni knew that the young Kulingas had grown up so.

data.v: ततः कदाचित्तांस्तत्र पश्यन्पक्षीन्यतव्रतः । बभूव परमप्रीतस्तदा मतिमतां वरः ॥
data.md: That foremost of intelligent men, of austere VOWS, one day saw those young ones and became filled with pleasure.

data.v: तथा तानभिसंवृद्धान्दृष्ट्वा चाप्नुवतां मुदम् । शकुनौ निर्भयौ तत्र ऊषतुश्चात्मजैः सह ॥
data.md: Seeing their young ones endued with wings, the parent birds became very happy and continued to live in the Rishi's head with them in perfect confidence.

data.v: जातपक्षांश्च सोऽपश्यदुड्डीनान्पुनरागतान् । सायं सायं द्विजान्विप्रो न चाकम्पत जाजलिः ॥
data.md: The learned Jajali saw that when the young birds had wings they flew to the air every evening and came back to his head without having gone far. He still stood motionless there.

data.v: कदाचित्पुनरभ्येत्य पुनर्गच्छन्ति संततम् । त्यक्ता मातृपितृभ्यां ते न चाकम्पत जाजलिः ॥
data.md: Sometime after he saw that, left by their parents, they went out alone and came back again alone, Jajali did not still move.

data.v: अथ ते दिवसं चारीं गत्वा सायं पुनर्नृप । उपावर्तन्त तत्रैव निवासार्थं शकुन्तकाः ॥
data.md: Sometime after, the young birds going away in the morning spent the whole day out of his sight but returned in the evening for living in the nest.

data.v: कदाचिद्दिवसान्पञ्च समुत्पत्य विहंगमाः । षष्ठेऽहनि समाजग्मुर्न चाकम्पत जाजलिः ॥
data.md: Sometime after, leaving their nest for five days at a time, they returned on the sixth day. Jajali still did not move.

data.v: क्रमेण च पुनः सर्वे दिवसानि बहून्यपि । नोपावर्तन्त शकुना जातप्राणाः स्म ते यदा ॥
data.md: Subsequently, when they gained their full strength, they left him and did not return at all even after many days.

data.v: कदाचिन्मासमात्रेण समुत्पत्य विहंगमाः । नैवागच्छंस्ततो राजन्प्रातिष्ठत स जाजलिः ॥
data.md: At last, at another time, leaving him, they did not come even after a month. Then, O king, Jajali left that place.

data.v: ततस्तेषु प्रलीनेषु जाजलिर्जातविस्मयः । सिद्धोऽस्मीति मतिं चक्रे ततस्तं मान आविशत् ॥
data.md: When they had thus gone away for ever, Jajali wondered much and thought that he had gained ascetic success. Then pride entered his heart.

data.v: स तथा निर्गतान्दृष्ट्वा शकुन्तान्नियतव्रतः । संभावितात्मा संभाव्य भृशं प्रीतस्तदाभवन् ॥
data.md: Ever observing vows, the great ascetic, seeing the birds thus leave him. After having been brought up on his head, thought highly of himself, and became filled with joy.

data.v: स नद्यां समुपस्पृश्य तर्पयित्वा हुताशनम् । उदयन्तमथादित्यमभ्यगच्छन्महातपाः ॥
data.md: He then bathed in a river and poured libations on the sacred fire, and worshipped the rising Sun.

data.v: संभाव्य चटकान्मूर्ध्नि जाजलिर्जपतां वरः । आस्फोटयत्तदाकाशे धर्मः प्राप्तो मयेति वै ॥
data.md: Having thus made those chataka birds, grow on his head, Jajali that foremost of ascetics, began to strike his armpits and cry loudly through the sky, I have acquired great merit.

data.v: अथान्तरिक्षे वागासीत्तां स शुश्राव जाजलिः । धर्मेण न समस्त्वं वै तुलाधारस्य जाजले ॥
data.md: Then an unseen voice arose in the sky and Jajali heard these words:-You are not equal, O Jajali, to Tuladhara in righteousness.

data.v: वाराणस्यां महाप्राज्ञस्तुलाधारः प्रतिष्ठितः । सोऽप्येवं नार्हते वक्तुं यथा त्वं भाषसे द्विज ॥
data.md: There is a man named Tuladhara highly illustrious and doing the business of buying and selling, Even he, O best of twice-born ones, is not worthy of saying such words as you say!

data.v: सोऽमर्षवशमापन्नस्तुलाधारदिदृक्षया । पृथिवीमचरद्राजन्यत्रसायंगृहो मुनिः ॥
data.md: Hearing these words, Jajali became possessed by anger and desirous of meeting with Tuladhara, O king, began to roam over the whole Earth, observing the vow of silence and passing the night where he met with evening.

data.v: कालेन महतागच्छत्स तु वाराणसीं पुरीम् । विक्रीणन्तं च पण्यानि तुलाधारं ददर्श सः ॥
data.md: As soon as the shop-keeper Tuladhara saw the Brahmana arrived at his place, he cheerfully stood up and adored the guest with proper salutations.

data.v: सोऽपि दृष्ट्वैव तं विप्रमायान्तं भाण्डजीवनः । समुत्थाय सुसंहृष्टः स्वागतेनाभ्यपूजयत् ॥
data.md: After a long time he reached the city of Baranasi, and saw Tuladhara engaged in selling miscellaneous articles.

data.v: आयानेवासि विदितो मम ब्रह्मन्न संशयः । ब्रवीमि यत्तु वचनं तच्छृणुष्व द्विजोत्तम ॥
data.md: Tuladhara said For tsooth, O Brahmana, I know that you have come to me. Listen, however, Oforemost of twice-born ones, to what I say!

data.v: सागरानूपमाश्रित्य तपस्तप्तं त्वया महत् । न च धर्मस्य संज्ञां त्वं पुरा वेत्थ कथंचन ॥
data.md: Living on a low land near the sea-shore you had practised very hard penancces. But you had no consciousness of having acquired religious merit.

data.v: ततः सिद्धस्य तपसा तव विप्र शकुन्तकाः । क्षिप्रं शिरस्यजायन्त ते च संभावितास्त्वया ॥
data.md: When you had at last acquired ascetic success, certain birds were born on your head. You took great care of the little creatures:

data.v: जातपक्षा यदा ते च गताश्चारीमितस्ततः । मन्यमानस्ततो धर्मं चटकप्रभवं द्विज । खे वाचं त्वमथाश्रौषीर्मां प्रति द्विजसत्तम ॥
data.md: When at last those birds came winged and when they began to leave your head for going here and there in search of food, it was then that, for your having thus assisted at the birth of those Chatakas, you began to feel pride, O Brahmana, thinking you had acquired great merit.

data.v: अमर्षवशमापन्नस्ततः प्राप्तो भवानिह । करवाणि प्रियं किं ते तद्ब्रूहि द्विजसत्तम ॥
data.md: Then, O foremost of twice-born ones, you heard in the sky a voice that spoke of me. The words you had heard filled you with anger and for that you have come here! Tell me, what wish of yours shall I fulfil, O best of Brahmanas.

data.v: इत्युक्तः स तदा तेन तुलाधारेण धीमता । प्रोवाच वचनं धीमाञ्जाजलिर्जपतां वरः ॥
data.md: Thus accosted by the intelligent Tuladhara on that occasion, the highly intelligent Jajali, that foremost of ascetics, said these words to him:

data.v: विक्रीणानः सर्वरसान्सर्वगन्धांश्च वाणिज । वनस्पतीनोषधीश्च तेषां मूलफलानि च ॥
data.md: You sell all sorts of juices and scents, O son of a trader, as also (barks and leaves of) huge trees and herbs and their fruits and roots.

data.v: अध्यगा नैष्ठिकीं बुद्धिं कुतस्त्वामिदमागतम् । एतदाचक्ष्व मे सर्वं निखिलेन महामते ॥
data.md: But how have you gained this stability of understanding? How have you gained this knowledge? O you of great intelligence, tell me all this fully.

data.v: एवमुक्तस्तुलाधारो ब्राह्मणेन यशस्विना । उवाच धर्मसूक्ष्माणि वैश्यो धर्मार्थतत्त्ववित् । जाजलिं कष्टतपसं ज्ञानतृप्तस्तदा नृप ॥
data.md: Thus accosted by that highly famous Brahmana, Tuladhara of the Vaishya caste, well acquatinted with the truths of morality and contented with knowledge, described to Jajali who had practised severe penances, the ways of morality.

data.v: वेदाहं जाजले धर्मं सरहस्यं सनातनम् । सर्वभूतहितं मैत्रं पुराणं यं जना विदुः ॥
data.md: Tuladhara said a O Jajali, I know, with all its mysteries, morality, which is eternal. It is nothing else but that ancient morality which every body knows, and which consists of universal friendliness, and beneficence to all creatures.

data.v: अद्रोहेणैव भूतानामल्पद्रोहेण वा पुनः । या वृत्तिः स परो धर्मस्तेन जीवामि जाजले ॥
