data.v: वैगुण्यमेव पश्यन्ति न गुणाननुयुञ्जते । तेषां तमःशरीराणां तम एव परायणम् ॥
data.md: These men see fruitlessness on every side, and if they succeed in acquiring the power of knowledge they never give it to others for rescuing them. Made up entirely of the quality of ignorance, they have ignorance only for their refuge.

data.v: यो यथाप्रकृतिर्जन्तुः प्रकृतेः स्याद्वशानुगः । तस्य द्वेषश्च कामश्च क्रोधो दम्भोऽनृतं मदः । नित्यमेवाभिवर्तन्ते गुणाः प्रकृतिसंभवाः ॥
data.md: One becomes subject to all the characteristics of that nature which one imbibes. Accordingly, of him who has ignorance for his refuge, the passions of envy, lust, anger, pride, falsehood, and vanity, continually grow, for one's qualities have one's nature for their root.

data.v: एतद्बुद्ध्यानुपश्यन्तः संत्यजेयुः शुभाशुभम् । परां गतिमभीप्सन्तो यतयः संयमे रताः ॥
data.md: Thinking in this way and seeing these faults, Yatis, who seek the highest end, follow Yoga, leaving both good and ill.

data.v: सर्वमेतन्मया ब्रह्मञ्शास्त्रतः परिकीर्तितम् । न ह्यविज्ञाय शास्त्रार्थं प्रवर्तन्ते प्रवृत्तयः ॥
data.md: O Brahmana, all that I have said is strictly according to the scriptures. It is, however, very true that without a correct understanding of the meaning of the scriptures, one does not feel inclined to obey what the scriptures really say.

data.v: यः कश्चिन्न्याय्य आचारः सर्वं शास्त्रमिति श्रुतिः । यदन्याय्यमशास्त्रं तदित्येषा श्रूयते श्रुतिः ॥
data.md: Whatever conduct is consistent with equity, is conformable with the scriptures. Even that is what the Shruti says, Likewise, whatever conduct is inconsistent with equity in incompatible with the scriptures. This also is held by the Shruti.

data.v: न प्रवृत्तिरृते शास्त्रात्काचिदस्तीति निश्चयः । यदन्यद्वेदवादेभ्यस्तदशास्त्रमिति श्रुतिः ॥
data.md: It is certain that no one can do a scriptural act by violating the scriptures. That which is against the Vedas is unscriptural. The Shruti says this. are

data.v: शास्त्रादपेतं पश्यन्ति बहवो व्यक्तमानिनः । शास्त्रदोषान्न पश्यन्ति इह चामुत्र चापरे । अविज्ञानहतप्रज्ञा हीनप्रज्ञास्तमोवृताः ॥
data.md: Many men, who believe only what directly appeals to their senses, see only this world. They do not see what the scriptures declare to be faults. They have, accordingly, like ourselves, to yield to grief. Those objects of the sense which concern men like you are the same with which other living creatures concerned.

data.v: शक्यं त्वेकेन मुक्तेन कृतकृत्येन सर्वशः । पिण्डमात्रं व्यपाश्रित्य चरितुं सर्वतोदिशम् । वेदवादं व्यपाश्रित्य मोक्षोऽस्तीति प्रभाषितुम् ॥
data.md: Only he who is given to Yoga, who has satisfied all his duties, who is capable of roving everywhere depending only on his own body, who has brought his soul under perfect restraint, who has gone above the requirements of the science of morality and who disregards the whole world, can transgress the declarations of the Vedas regarding acts, and say that there is Liberation,

data.v: इदं तु दुष्करं कर्म कुटुम्बमभिसंश्रितम् । दानमध्ययनं यज्ञः प्रजासंतानमार्जवम् ॥
data.md: For one, however, who lives in the midst of relatives, this course of conduct is highly difficult to follow. Gift, study of the Vedas, sacrifices begetting children, simplicity of conduct, when by doing even these no one attains to Liberation, fie on him who seeks to altain to it. and on Liberation itself that is sought! It appears that the labour spent upon acquiring it is all fruitless.

data.v: यद्येतदेवं कृत्वापि न विमोक्षोऽस्ति कस्यचित् । धिक्कर्तारं च कार्यं च श्रमश्चायं निरर्थकः ॥
data.md: For one, however, who lives in the midst of relatives, this course of conduct is highly difficult to follow. Gift, study of the Vedas, sacrifices begetting children, simplicity of conduct, when by doing even these no one attains to Liberation, fie on him who seeks to altain to it. and on Liberation itself that is sought! It appears that the labour spent upon acquiring it is all fruitless.

data.v: नास्तिक्यमन्यथा च स्याद्वेदानां पृष्ठतःक्रिया । एतस्यानन्त्यमिच्छामि भगवञ्श्रोतुमञ्जसा ॥
data.md: One is charged with atheism if he disregards the Vedas by not doing the acts they declare. O illustrious one, I wish to hear forthwith about that which comes in the Vedas after the injunctions about acts.

data.v: तथ्यं वदस्व मे ब्रह्मन्नुपसन्नोऽस्म्यधीहि भोः । यथा ते विदितो मोक्षस्तथेच्छाम्युपशिक्षितुम् ॥
data.md: Do tell me the truth, O Brahmana! I sit at your feet as a disciple. Teach me kindly! I wish to know as much about Liberation as is known to you, O learned one!

data.v: वेदाः प्रमाणं लोकानां न वेदाः पृष्ठतःकृताः । द्वे ब्रह्मणी वेदितव्ये शब्दब्रह्म परं च यत् । शब्दब्रह्मणि निष्णातः परं ब्रह्माधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: Kapila said The Vedas are considered as an authority by all. People never disobey them. Brahma is of two kinds, viz., Brahma is represented by sound, and Brahma as Supreme.

data.v: शरीरमेतत्कुरुते यद्वेदे कुरुते तनुम् । कृतशुद्धशरीरो हि पात्रं भवति ब्राह्मणः ॥
आनन्त्यमनुयुङ्क्ते यः कर्मणा तद्ब्रवीमि ते । निरागममनैतिह्यं प्रत्यक्षं लोकसाक्षिकम् ॥
धर्म इत्येव ये यज्ञान्वितन्वन्ति निराशिषः । उत्पन्नत्यागिनोऽलुब्धाः कृपासूयाविवर्जिताः । धनानामेष वै पन्थास्तीर्थेषु प्रतिपादनम् ॥
data.md: Whether purity of heart has been acquired or not, is what can be known to the person himself who has acquired it. It can never be known with the help of either the Vedas or inference. They who have no expectations, who discard every sort of riches by not keeping anything for future use, who are not covetous, and who are free from every sort of affection and aversion, celebrate sacrifices believing only that their performance is a duty. To make gifts to deserving persons is the end of all riches.

data.v: अनाश्रिताः पापकृत्याः कदाचित्कर्मयोनितः । मनःसंकल्पसंसिद्धा विशुद्धज्ञाननिश्चयाः ॥
अक्रुध्यन्तोऽनसूयन्तो निरहंकारमत्सराः । ज्ञाननिष्ठास्त्रिशुक्लाश्च सर्वभूतहिते रताः ॥
आसन्गृहस्था भूयिष्ठमव्युत्क्रान्ताः स्वकर्मसु । राजानश्च तथा युक्ता ब्राह्मणाश्च यथाविधि ॥
समा ह्यार्जवसंपन्नाः संतुष्टा ज्ञाननिश्चयाः । प्रत्यक्षधर्माः शुचयः श्रद्दधानाः परावरे ॥
data.md: They treated all creatures equally and were gifted with perfect sincerity. They had contentiment, certainty of knowledge. The rewards of their righteousness were apparent, and they were pure in conduct and heart. They were endued with faith in Brahma of both forms.

data.v: पुरस्ताद्भावितात्मानो यथावच्चरितव्रताः । चरन्ति धर्मं कृच्छ्रेऽपि दुर्गे चैवाधिसंहताः ॥
data.md: At first making their hearts pure, they duly observed all vows. They observed the duties of righteousness on even occasions of distress and great difficulty, without deviating in any particular.

data.v: संहत्य धर्मं चरतां पुरासीत्सुखमेव तत् । तेषां नासीद्विधातव्यं प्रायश्चित्तं कदाचन ॥
data.md: Uniting together they used to celebrate meritorious acts. In this they found great happiness. And inasmuch as they never transgressed, they had never to perform any expiatory rite.

data.v: सत्यं हि धर्ममास्थाय दुराधर्षतमा मताः । न मात्रामनुरुध्यन्ते न धर्मच्छलमन्ततः ॥
data.md: Depending upon the true course of virtue, they became gifted with irresistible energy. They never followed their own understandings while acquiring merit but followed the injunctions of the scriptures along for that end. Accordingly they were never guilty of guile in performing acts of righteousness.

data.v: य एव प्रथमः कल्पस्तमेवाभ्याचरन्सह । अस्यां स्थितौ स्थितानां हि प्रायश्चित्तं न विद्यते । दुर्बलात्मन उत्पन्नं प्रायश्चित्तमिति श्रुतिः ॥
data.md: There is no expiation for men who follow the ordinances laid down in the scriptures. The Shruti says that expiation exists for only men who are weak and unable to follow the absolute provisions of the sacred law.

data.v: यत एवंविधा विप्राः पुराणा यज्ञवाहनाः । त्रैविद्यवृद्धाः शुचयो वृत्तवन्तो यशस्विनः । यजन्तोऽहरहर्यज्ञैर्निराशीर्बन्धना बुधाः ॥
data.md: Many Brahmanas of this kind in days of yore, devoted to the celebration of Vedas, endued with purity, good conduct and fame.

data.v: तेषां यज्ञाश्च वेदाश्च कर्माणि च यथागमम् । आगमाश्च यथाकालं संकल्पाश्च यथाव्रतम् ॥
अपेतकामक्रोधानां प्रकृत्या संशितात्मनाम् । ऋजूनां शमनित्यानां स्थितानां स्वेषु कर्मसु । सर्वमानन्त्यमेवासीदिति नः शाश्वती श्रुतिः ॥
तेषामदीनसत्त्वानां दुश्चराचारकर्मणाम् । स्वकर्मभिः संवृतानां तपो घोरत्वमागतम् ॥
तं सदाचारमाश्चर्यं पुराणं शाश्वतं ध्रुवम् । अशक्नुवद्भिश्चरितुं किंचिद्धर्मेषु सूचितम् ॥
निरापद्धर्म आचारस्त्वप्रमादोऽपराभवः । सर्ववर्णेषु यत्तेषु नासीत्कश्चिद्व्यतिक्रमः ॥
धर्ममेकं चतुष्पादमाश्रितास्ते नरर्षभाः । तं सन्तो विधिवत्प्राप्य गच्छन्ति परमां गतिम् ॥
गृहेभ्य एव निष्क्रम्य वनमन्ये समाश्रिताः । गृहमेवाभिसंश्रित्य ततोऽन्ये ब्रह्मचारिणः ॥
धर्ममेतं चतुष्पादमाश्रमं ब्राह्मणा विदुः । आनन्त्यं ब्रह्मणः स्थानं ब्राह्मणा नाम निश्चयः ॥
अत एवंविधा विप्राः पुराणा धर्मचारिणः । त एते दिवि दृश्यन्ते ज्योतिर्भूता द्विजातयः ॥
data.md: They also who observe the domestic mode of life, attain to the highest end; and lastly, those who lead the Brahmacharya mode, attain to the same end. Those Brahmanas are seen to shine in the sky as luminaries shedding beneficent rays of light all around.

data.v: नक्षत्राणीव धिष्ण्येषु बहवस्तारकागणाः । आनन्त्यमुपसंप्राप्ताः संतोषादिति वैदिकम् ॥
data.md: Those countless Brahmanas have become stars and constellations set in their fixed roads. By virtue of contentment they have all acquired Infinity as the Vedas say.

data.v: यद्यागच्छन्ति संसारं पुनर्योनिषु तादृशाः । न लिप्यन्ते पापकृत्यैः कदाचित्कर्मयोनितः ॥
data.md: If such men have to return to the world through the wombs of living creatures, they are never sullied by sins which have the unexhausted remnant of pristine deeds for their originating cause.

data.v: एवं युक्तो ब्राह्मणः स्यादन्यो ब्राह्मणको भवेत् । कर्मैव पुरुषस्याह शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् ॥
एवं पक्वकषायाणामानन्त्येन श्रुतेन च । सर्वमानन्त्यमेवासीदेवं नः शाश्वती श्रुतिः ॥
तेषामपेततृष्णानां निर्णिक्तानां शुभात्मनाम् । चतुर्थ औपनिषदो धर्मः साधारणः स्मृतः ॥
स सिद्धैः साध्यते नित्यं ब्राह्मणैर्नियतात्मभिः । संतोषमूलस्त्यागात्मा ज्ञानाधिष्ठानमुच्यते ॥
अपवर्गगतिर्नित्यो यतिधर्मः सनातनः । साधारणः केवलो वा यथाबलमुपास्यते ॥
गच्छतो गच्छतः क्षेमं दुर्बलोऽत्रावसीदति । ब्रह्मणः पदमन्विच्छन्संसारान्मुच्यते शुचिः ॥
data.md: Renunciation is sometimes found mixed with the duties of other modes. But whether existing in that state or by itself, one practises it according to his power. Renunciation is the root of great benefit to every sort of person. Only he who is weak, fails to pursue it. That pure-hearted man who seeks to attain to Brahma becomes saved from the world.

data.v: ये भुञ्जते ये ददते यजन्तेऽधीयते च ये । मात्राभिर्धर्मलब्धाभिर्ये वा त्यागं समाश्रिताः ॥
एतेषां प्रेत्यभावे तु कतमः स्वर्गजित्तमः । एतदाचक्ष्व मे ब्रह्मन्यथातथ्येन पृच्छतः ॥
परिग्रहाः शुभाः सर्वे गुणतोऽभ्युदयाश्च ये । न तु त्यागसुखं प्राप्ता एतत्त्वमपि पश्यसि ॥
data.md: Those who live like householders are surely auspicious and gain every sort of excellence. They are unable, however, to enjoy the happiness of Renunciation. Even you may see this.

data.v: भवन्तो ज्ञाननिष्ठा वै गृहस्थाः कर्मनिश्चयाः । आश्रमाणां च सर्वेषां निष्ठायामैक्यमुच्यते ॥
data.md: You depend upon knowledge as the means. Those who live like householders, have placed their faith in acts. It has, however, been said that the end of all modes of life is Liberation.

data.v: एकत्वे च पृथक्त्वे च विशेषो नान्य उच्यते । तद्यथावद्यथान्यायं भगवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे ॥
data.md: No difference, therefore, is seen between them about either their superiority or inferiority of power. O illustrious one do you, then, clear out the mystery and enlighten me.

data.v: शरीरपक्तिः कर्माणि ज्ञानं तु परमा गतिः । पक्वे कषाये वमनै रसज्ञाने न तिष्ठति ॥
आनृशंस्यं क्षमा शान्तिरहिंसा सत्यमार्जवम् । अद्रोहो नाभिमानश्च ह्रीस्तितिक्षा शमस्तथा ॥
data.md: Kapila said-Acts only purify the body, Knowledge, however, is the highest end. When all defects of the heart are cured, and when the happiness of Brahma becomes established in knowledge. benevolence, forgiveness, tranquillity, mercy, truthfulness, and open-mindedness, abstention from injury, absence of pride, modestry, renunciation, and abstention from work are acquired.

data.v: पन्थानो ब्रह्मणस्त्वेते एतैः प्राप्नोति यत्परम् । तद्विद्वाननुबुध्येत मनसा कर्मनिश्चयम् ॥
data.md: These form the path of Brahma. By those one acquires the Highest. A wise man when he acquires these qualities, understands that the cure of all defects of the heart is the result of acts.

data.v: यां विप्राः सर्वतः शान्ता विशुद्धा ज्ञाननिश्चयाः । गतिं गच्छन्ति संतुष्टास्तामाहुः परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: That, indeed, is considered as the highest end which is acquired by Brahmanas gifted with wisdom, withdrawn from all acts, possessed of purity and the surety of knowledge.

data.v: वेदांश्च वेदितव्यं च विदित्वा च यथास्थिति । एवं वेदविदित्याहुरतोऽन्यो वातरेटकः ॥
data.md: One who acquires a knowledge of the Vedas, of that which is taught by the Vedas, and the details of acts, is said to be conversant with the Vedas. Any other man is only a bag of wind.

data.v: सर्वं विदुर्वेदविदो वेदे सर्वं प्रतिष्ठितम् । वेदे हि निष्ठा सर्वस्य यद्यदस्ति च नास्ति च ॥
data.md: One who is master of the Vedas, knows everything, for everything is established on the Veda. The present, past, and future all exist in the Vedas.

data.v: एषैव निष्ठा सर्वस्य यद्यदस्ति च नास्ति च । एतदन्तं च मध्यं च सच्चासच्च विजानतः ॥
data.md: This is the one conclusion of all the scriptures viz., that this universe exists and does not exist. To the man of knowledge this is both existent and non-existent. To him this all is both the end and the middle.

data.v: समस्तत्याग इत्येव शम इत्येव निष्ठितः । संतोष इत्यत्र शुभमपवर्गे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
ऋतं सत्यं विदितं वेदितव्यं; सर्वस्यात्मा जङ्गमं स्थावरं च । सर्वं सुखं यच्छिवमुत्तमं च; ब्रह्माव्यक्तं प्रभवश्चाव्ययश्च ॥
data.md: This truth depends upon all the Vedas, viz., that when complete Renunciation takes place one acquires what is sufficient. Then, again, the highest contentment follows and depends upon Liberation, which is absolute, which exists as the soul of all moral and immortal things, which is well-known as such universal soul, which is the highest object of knowledge as being at one with all mobile and immobile objects, which is full, which is perfect happiness, which is without duality, which is the foremost of all things, which is Brahma, which is Unmanifest and the cause also of the Unmanifest, and which is without any sort of decay.

data.v: तेजः क्षमा शान्तिरनामयं शुभं; तथाविधं व्योम सनातनं ध्रुवम् । एतैः शब्दैर्गम्यते बुद्धिनेत्रै;स्तस्मै नमो ब्रह्मणे ब्राह्मणाय ॥
data.md: Power to control the senses, forgiveness and abstention from work owing to the absence of desire,-these three are the cause of perfect happiness. With the help of these three qualities, men having understanding for their eyes, succeed in reaching that Brahma which is increate, which is the supreme cause of the universe, which is unchangeable, and which is beyond destruction. I bow to that Brahma, which is at one with him that knows it.

data.v: धर्ममर्थं च कामं च वेदाः शंसन्ति भारत । कस्य लाभो विशिष्टोऽत्र तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said The Vedas, O Bharata, describe Religion, Profit, and Pleasure. Tell me, however, O grand-father, the attainment of which is considered as superior.

data.v: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम् । कुण्डधारेण यत्प्रीत्या भक्तायोपकृतं पुरा ॥
data.md: Bhishma said About it I shall recite to you the ancient discourse of the benefit which Kundadhara in days of yore had conferred upon one who was devoted to him.

data.v: अधनो ब्राह्मणः कश्चित्कामाद्धर्ममवैक्षत । यज्ञार्थं स ततोऽर्थार्थी तपोऽतप्यत दारुणम् ॥
data.md: Once on a time a Brahmana shorn of riches tried to win virtue, actuated by the desire of fruit. He continually thought of riches for employing it in the celebration of sacrifices. For gaining his end he engaged in the practice of the austerest penances.

data.v: स निश्चयमथो कृत्वा पूजयामास देवताः । भक्त्या न चैवाध्यगच्छद्धनं संपूज्य देवताः ॥
data.md: Determined to achieve his object, he began to adore the gods with great devotion. But he failed to acquire riches by such adoration of the gods.

data.v: ततश्चिन्तां पुनः प्राप्तः कतमद्दैवतं नु तत् । यन्मे द्रुतं प्रसीदेत मानुषैरजडीकृतम् ॥
data.md: He thereupon began to think aside, What is that god, hitherto not worshipped by men, who may be forthwith favourably disposed towards me?

data.v: अथ सौम्येन वपुषा देवानुचरमन्तिके । प्रत्यपश्यज्जलधरं कुण्डधारमवस्थितम् ॥
data.md: While thinking thus with a cool mind, he saw stationed before him that retainer of the gods, viz., the Cloud called Kundadhara.

data.v: दृष्ट्वैव तं महात्मानं तस्य भक्तिरजायत । अयं मे धास्यति श्रेयो वपुरेतद्धि तादृशम् ॥
data.md: As soon as he saw that mighty-armed being, the Brahmana's feelings of devotion were excited, and he said to himself,-This one will surely give me prosperity! Indeed, his form indicates it.

data.v: संनिकृष्टश्च देवस्य न चान्यैर्मानुषैर्वृतः । एष मे दास्यति धनं प्रभूतं शीघ्रमेव च ॥
data.md: He lives near the gods. He has not as yet been worshipped by other man. He will surely give me profuse riches without any delay!

data.v: ततो धूपैश्च गन्धैश्च माल्यैरुच्चावचैरपि । बलिभिर्विविधैश्चापि पूजयामास तं द्विजः ॥
data.md: The Brahmana then, having determined thus, adored that Cloud with incense, perfumes and garlands of flowers of the most superior kind, and with various sorts of offerings.

data.v: ततः स्वल्पेन कालेन तुष्टो जलधरस्तदा । तस्योपकारे नियतामिमां वाचमुवाच ह ॥
data.md: Thus adored, the Cloud became very soon pleased with his worshipper, and uttered these words of benefit to that Brahmana:

data.v: ब्रह्मघ्ने च सुरापे च चोरे भग्नव्रते तथा । निष्कृतिर्विहिता सद्भिः कृतघ्ने नास्ति निष्कृतिः ॥
data.md: The wise have laid down expiation for one guilty of Brahmanicide, or of drinking alcohol, or of stealing, or of neglecting all meritorious vows. There is no expiation, however, for one who is ungrateful.

data.v: आशायास्तनयोऽधर्मः क्रोधोऽसूयासुतः स्मृतः । पुत्रो लोभो निकृत्यास्तु कृतघ्नो नार्हति प्रजाम् ॥
data.md: Expectation has a child named Sin. Anger, again, is considered to be a child of Envy. Cupidity is the child of Deceit. Ingratitude, however, is barnen.

data.v: ततः स ब्राह्मणः स्वप्ने कुण्डधारस्य तेजसा । अपश्यत्सर्वभूतानि कुशेषु शयितस्तदा ॥
data.md: After this, that Brahmana, stretched on a bed of Kusha grass, and penetrated with the energy of Kundadhara, saw all living beings in a dream.

data.v: शमेन तपसा चैव भक्त्या च निरुपस्कृतः । शुद्धात्मा ब्राह्मणो रात्रौ निदर्शनमपश्यत ॥
data.md: Indeed, on account of his absence of passion, penances, and devotion, that Brahmana of purified soul and standing aloof from all enjoyments saw in the night that effect of his devotion to Kundadhara.

data.v: मणिभद्रं स तत्रस्थं देवतानां महाद्युतिम् । अपश्यत महात्मानं व्यादिशन्तं युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Indeed, O Yudhishthira, he saw the great and highly effulgent Manibhadra stationed in the midst of the gods, engaged in giving his orders.

data.v: तत्र देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति राज्यानि च धनानि च । शुभैः कर्मभिरारब्धाः प्रच्छिदन्त्यशुभेषु च ॥
data.md: There the gods seemed to be engaged in granting kingdoms and riches to men, induced by their good deeds, and in taking them away when men deviated from goodness.

data.v: पश्यतामथ यक्षाणां कुण्डधारो महाद्युतिः । निष्पत्य पतितो भूमौ देवानां भरतर्षभ ॥
data.md: Then, O foremost of Bharata's race, the highly effulgent Kundadhara, bending himself low, laid himself down on the ground before the gods in the presences of all the Yakshas.

data.v: ततस्तु देववचनान्मणिभद्रो महायशाः । उवाच पतितं भूमौ कुण्डधार किमिष्यते ॥
data.md: At the command of the gods the Manibhadra said to the prostrate Kundadhara,-What does Kundadhara want?

data.v: यदि प्रसन्ना देवा मे भक्तोऽयं ब्राह्मणो मम । अस्यानुग्रहमिच्छामि कृतं किंचित्सुखोदयम् ॥
data.md: Thereupon Kundadhara replied,-If, indeed, the gods are gratified with me, there, that Brahmana respects me greatly. I pray for some favour being shown to him, something, that may bring him happiness.

data.v: ततस्तं मणिभद्रस्तु पुनर्वचनमब्रवीत् । देवानामेव वचनात्कुण्डधारं महाद्युतिम् ॥
data.md: Hearing this, Manibhadra, ordered by the gods, once more said to the highly intelligent Kundadhara.

data.v: उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते कृतकार्यः सुखी भव । यावद्धनं प्रार्थयते ब्राह्मणोऽयं सखा तव । देवानां शासनात्तावदसंख्येयं ददाम्यहम् ॥
data.md: Rise, Rise up, O Kundadhara; Your prayer has borne success! Be you happy! If this Brahmana seeks riches, let as much wealth be given to him, as he wishes. at the command of the gods I shall give him immeasurable riches.

data.v: विचार्य कुण्डधारस्तु मानुष्यं चलमध्रुवम् । तपसे मतिमाधत्त ब्राह्मणस्य यशस्विनः ॥
data.md: Then, thinking upon the fieeting and unreal character of the humanity, Kundadhara set his heart, O Yudhisthira, upon inclining the Brahmana to penances.

data.v: नाहं धनानि याचामि ब्राह्मणाय धनप्रद । अन्यमेवाहमिच्छामि भक्तायानुग्रहं कृतम् ॥
data.md: Indeed, Kundadhara said,-I do not, O giver of riches, beg for wealth on behalf of this Brahmana. I desire the bestowed of another favour upon him.

data.v: पृथिवीं रत्नपूर्णां वा महद्वा धनसंचयम् । भक्ताय नाहमिच्छामि भवेदेष तु धार्मिकः ॥
data.md: I do not pray for this devotee of mine mountains of pearls and gems, or even the whole Earth with all her riches. I wish, however, that he should be virtuous.

data.v: धर्मेऽस्य रमतां बुद्धिर्धर्मं चैवोपजीवतु । धर्मप्रधानो भवतु ममैषोऽनुग्रहो मतः ॥
data.md: Let his heart find pleasure in virtue! Let him have virtue for his support. Let virtue be the foremost of all his objects. This is the favour which I am inclined to give my support. Manibhadra said

data.v: यदा धर्मफलं राज्यं सुखानि विविधानि च । फलान्येवायमश्नातु कायक्लेशविवर्जितः ॥
data.md: The fruits of virtue are always kingdom and happiness of various sorts. Let this one enjoy those fruits, always freed from all sorts of physical sufferings.

data.v: ततस्तदेव बहुशः कुण्डधारो महायशाः । अभ्यासमकरोद्धर्मे ततस्तुष्टास्य देवताः ॥
data.md: Thus addressed, the highly illustrious Kundadhara, repeatedly prayed for virtue alone for that Brahmana. The gods were highly pleased at it.

data.v: प्रीतास्ते देवताः सर्वा द्विजस्यास्य तथैव च । भविष्यत्येष धर्मात्मा धर्मे चाधास्यते मतिः ॥
data.md: Then Manibhadra said The gods are all pleased with you as also with this Brahmana. This one shall become a virtuous man. He shall devote his mind to virtue.

data.v: ततः प्रीतो जलधरः कृतकार्यो युधिष्ठिर । ईप्सितं मनसो लब्ध्वा वरमन्यैः सुदुर्लभम् ॥
data.md: The Cloud, Kundadhara, became pleased,O Yudhishthira, at thus having been successful in gaining his wish. The boon that he had got was one that could not be acquired by anybody else.

data.v: ततोऽपश्यत चीराणि सूक्ष्माणि द्विजसत्तमः । पार्श्वतोऽभ्यागतो न्यस्तान्यथ निर्वेदमागतः ॥
data.md: The Brahinana then saw scattered around him many fine fabrics of cloth. Without caring for them at all, the Brahmana came to disrelish the world.

data.v: अयं न सुकृतं वेत्ति को न्वन्यो वेत्स्यते कृतम् । गच्छामि वनमेवाहं वरं धर्मेण जीवितुम् ॥
data.md: When this one does not attach any value to good deeds, who else will? I had better go to the forest for leading a life of righteousness.

data.v: निर्वेदाद्देवतानां च प्रसादात्स द्विजोत्तमः । वनं प्रविश्य सुमहत्तप आरब्धवांस्तदा ॥
data.md: Bhishma said as Cherishing a distaste for the world, and through the grace also of the gods, that foremost of Brahmanas entered the forest and began to practise the austerest of penances.

data.v: देवतातिथिशेषेण फलमूलाशनो द्विजः । धर्मे चापि महाराज रतिरस्याभ्यजायत ॥
data.md: Living upon such fruits and roots remained after serving the gods and guests, the mind of that twice-born one, O king, was firmly set upon virtue.

data.v: त्यक्त्वा मूलफलं सर्वं पर्णाहारोऽभवद्द्विजः । पर्णं त्यक्त्वा जलाहारस्तदासीद्द्विजसत्तमः ॥
data.md: By and bye the Brahmana, leaving off fruits and roots, began to use leaves of trees as his food. Then leaving off leaves, he took to water only as his subsistence.

data.v: वायुभक्षस्ततः पश्चाद्बहून्वर्षगणानभूत् । न चास्य क्षीयते प्राणस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥
data.md: Thereafter he passed many years by living upon air only. All this time, however, his strength did not decrease. This seemed highly wonderful.

data.v: धर्मे च श्रद्दधानस्य तपस्युग्रे च वर्ततः । कालेन महता तस्य दिव्या दृष्टिरजायत ॥
data.md: Devoted to virtue and engaged in the practice of the severest austerities, after a long time he gained spiritual vision.

data.v: तस्य बुद्धिः प्रादुरासीद्यदि दद्यां महद्धनम् । तुष्टः कस्मैचिदेवाहं न मिथ्या वाग्भवेन्मम ॥
data.md: He then thought, saying to himself,-If, being pleased with anybody I give him riches, my speech would never be untrue.

data.v: ततः प्रहृष्टवदनो भूय आरब्धवांस्तपः । भूयश्चाचिन्तयत्सिद्धो यत्परं सोऽभ्यपद्यत ॥
data.md: With a face lighted up by smiles, he once more began to practise severer austerities.

data.v: यदि दद्यामहं राज्यं तुष्टो वै यस्य कस्यचित् । स भवेदचिराद्राजा न मिथ्या वाग्भवेन्मम ॥
data.md: And once more, having gained (higher) success, he thought that he could by his-will force, then create the very highest objects. If, pleased with any person whatsoever I give him even sovereignty, he will immediately become a king, for my words will never be falsified.

data.v: तस्य साक्षात्कुण्डधारो दर्शयामास भारत । ब्राह्मणस्य तपोयोगात्सौहृदेनाभिचोदितः ॥
data.md: While he was thinking thus, kundadhara, actuated by his friendship for the Brahmana and no less by the ascetic success which the Brahmana had gained, appeared before him, O Bharata.

data.v: समागम्य स तेनाथ पूजां चक्रे यथाविधि । ब्राह्मणः कुण्डधारस्य विस्मितश्चाभवन्नृप ॥
data.md: Meeting with him the Brahmana offered him adorations according to the observances ordained. The Brahmana, however, felt some surprise, O king.

data.v: ततोऽब्रवीत्कुण्डधारो दिव्यं ते चक्षुरुत्तमम् । पश्य राज्ञां गतिं विप्र लोकांश्चावेक्ष चक्षुषा ॥
data.md: Then Kundadhara addressed the Brahmana, saying, you have now got an excellent and spiritual eye! See with this vision of yours the end which is attained by kings, and see all the worlds besides.

data.v: ततो राज्ञां सहस्राणि मग्नानि निरये तदा । दूरादपश्यद्विप्रः स दिव्ययुक्तेन चक्षुषा ॥
data.md: The Brahmana then, then, his spiritual vision, saw from a distance thousands of kings sunk in hell.

data.v: मां पूजयित्वा भावेन यदि त्वं दुःखमाप्नुयाः । कृतं मया भवेत्किं ते कश्च तेऽनुग्रहो भवेत् ॥
data.md: Kundadhara said After having adored me with devotion you had got sorrow for your share, what then would have been the good done to you by me, and what the value of my favour.

data.v: पश्य पश्य च भूयस्त्वं कामानिच्छेत्कथं नरः । स्वर्गद्वारं हि संरुद्धं मानुषेषु विशेषतः ॥
data.md: Look, look, for what end do men seek the gratification of carnal enjoyments! The door of heaven is closed to men.

data.v: ततोऽपश्यत्स कामं च क्रोधं लोभं भयं मदम् । निद्रां तन्द्रीं तथालस्यमावृत्य पुरुषान्स्थितान् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said The Brahmana then saw many men living in this world, embracing lust, anger, avarice, fear, pride, sheep, procrastination, and activity.

data.v: एतैर्लोकाः सुसंरुद्धा देवानां मानुषाद्भयम् । तथैव देववचनाद्विघ्नं कुर्वन्ति सर्वशः ॥
data.md: All human beings are enchained with these. The gods are afraid of men. These vices, at the order of the gods, mar and disconcert on all sides.

data.v: न देवैरननुज्ञातः कश्चिद्भवति धार्मिकः । एष शक्तोऽसि तपसा राज्यं दातुं धनानि च ॥
data.md: No man can become virtuous unless allowed by the gods. You have become competent to give away kingdoms and riches through your penances!

data.v: ततः पपात शिरसा ब्राह्मणस्तोयधारिणे । उवाच चैनं धर्मात्मा महान्मेऽनुग्रहः कृतः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Thus addressed, the pious Brahmana, bending his head to that Cloud, laid himself low on the ground, and said,-You have, indeed, done me a great favour!

data.v: कामलोभानुबन्धेन पुरा ते यदसूयितम् । मया स्नेहमविज्ञाय तत्र मे क्षन्तुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Unconscious of the great love shown by you towards me,I through the influency of desire and avarice, could not show good will towards you.

data.v: क्षान्तमेव मयेत्युक्त्वा कुण्डधारो द्विजर्षभम् । संपरिष्वज्य बाहुभ्यां तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
data.md: Then Kundadhara said That foremost of twice-born ones,-I have forgiven you!-and having embraced him with his arms disappeared there and then.

data.v: ततः सर्वानिमाँल्लोकान्ब्राह्मणोऽनुचचार ह । कुण्डधारप्रसादेन तपसा योजितः पुरा ॥
data.md: The Brahmana then travelled through all the worlds, having acquired ascetic through the favour of Kundadhara.

data.v: विहायसा च गमनं तथा संकल्पितार्थता । धर्माच्छक्त्या तथा योगाद्या चैव परमा गतिः ॥
data.md: Through the power gained from virtue and penances, one acquires power to pass through the skies and to fructify all his wishes and purposes, and finally attain to the highest end.

data.v: देवता ब्राह्मणाः सन्तो यक्षा मानुषचारणाः । धार्मिकान्पूजयन्तीह न धनाढ्यान्न कामिनः ॥
data.md: Thë gods, Brahmanas, Yakshas, and all good men and Charanas always adore the virtuous but never the rich given up to the indulgence of their desires. success

data.v: सुप्रसन्ना हि ते देवा यत्ते धर्मे रता मतिः । धने सुखकला काचिद्धर्मे तु परमं सुखम् ॥
data.md: The gods are truly placed with you since your mind is devoted to virtue. In riches there may be a very little happiness but in virtue the extent of happiness is very great.

data.v: बहूनां यज्ञतपसामेकार्थानां पितामह । धर्मार्थं न सुखार्थार्थं कथं यज्ञः समाहितः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Of all sorts of sacrifices, all of which, of course, are said to have but one object, tell me, O grandfather, what that sacrifice is which has been ordained for only the sake of virtue and not for the acquisition of either heaven or riches.

data.v: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि नारदेनानुकीर्तितम् । उञ्छवृत्तेः पुरावृत्तं यज्ञार्थे ब्राह्मणस्य ह ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it I shall relate to you the history, formerly recited by Narada, of a Brahmana who for celebrating sacrifices, lived like a beggar.

data.v: राष्ट्रे धर्मोत्तरे श्रेष्ठे विदर्भेष्वभवद्द्विजः । उञ्छवृत्तिरृषिः कश्चिद्यज्ञे यज्ञं समादधे ॥
data.md: Narada said In one of the foremost of kingdins that was known for virtue, there lived a Brahmana. Devoted to penances and living like a wretched beggar, that Brahmana was earnestly engaged in worshipping Vishnu in sacrifices.

data.v: श्यामाकमशनं तत्र सूर्यपत्नी सुवर्चला । तिक्तं च विरसं शाकं तपसा स्वादुतां गतम् ॥
data.md: He had Shyamaka for his food, as also Suryaparni and Suvarchala and other kinds of potherbs that were bitter and distasteful. for his penances, all these tasted sweet.

data.v: उपगम्य वने पृथ्वीं सर्वभूतविहिंसया । अपि मूलफलैरिज्यो यज्ञः स्वर्ग्यः परंतप ॥
data.md: Not injuring any creature, and leading the life of a forest recluse, he acquired ascetic success. With roots and fruits, O scorcher of foes, he used to worship Vishnu in sacrifices that were intended to bestow heaven upon him.

data.v: तस्य भार्या व्रतकृशा शुचिः पुष्करचारिणी । यज्ञपत्नीत्वमानीता सत्येनानुविधीयते । सा तु शापपरित्रस्ता न स्वभावानुवर्तिनी ॥
data.md: The Brahmana, whose name was Satya, had a wife namely Pushkaradharini. She was pureminded, and had emaciated herself by practising many austere vows. She did not, however, approve of the conduct of her husband. Summoned, however, to sit by him as his wife (in a sacrifice), she feared to incur his curse and, therefore, comported herself with his conduct. The garments that covered her body consisted of the plumes of peacocks.

data.v: मयूरजीर्णपर्णानां वस्त्रं तस्याश्च पर्णिनाम् । अकामायाः कृतं तत्र यज्ञे होत्रानुमार्गतः ॥
शुक्रस्य पुनराजातिरपध्यानादधर्मवित् । तस्मिन्वने समीपस्थो मृगोऽभूत्सहचारिकः । वचोभिरब्रवीत्सत्यं त्वया दुष्कृतकं कृतम् ॥
यदि मन्त्राङ्गहीनोऽयं यज्ञो भवति वैकृतः । मां भोः प्रक्षिप होत्रे त्वं गच्छ स्वर्गमतन्द्रितः ॥
ततस्तु यज्ञे सावित्री साक्षात्तं संन्यमन्त्रयत् । निमन्त्रयन्ती प्रत्युक्ता न हन्यां सहवासिनम् ॥
data.md: Then the presiding goddess of the solar disc, viz., Savitri, came to that sacrifice in her incarnate form and insisted upon that Brahmana in doing what he was desired by that deer to do. The Brahmana said to that goddess, however, who thus insisted,-I shall not kill this deer who lives with me in this same neighbourhood!

data.v: एवमुक्ता निवृत्ता सा प्रविष्टा यज्ञपावकम् । किं नु दुश्चरितं यज्ञे दिदृक्षुः सा रसातलम् ॥
data.md: Thus addressed by the Brahmana, the goddess Savitri desisted and entered the sacrificial fire from desire of seeing the nether world, and wishing to avoid the sight of other short-comings in that sacrifice.

data.v: सा तु बद्धाञ्जलिं सत्यमयाचद्धरिणं पुनः । सत्येन संपरिष्वज्य संदिष्टो गम्यतामिति ॥
data.md: The deer then, with joined hands, again begged of Satya for that. Satya, however, embraced him in friendship and sent him away,-Go!

data.v: ततः स हरिणो गत्वा पदान्यष्टौ न्यवर्तत । साधु हिंसय मां सत्य हतो यास्यामि सद्गतिम् ॥
data.md: At this, the deer seemed to leave that place. But after he had gone eight steps he came back and said,-Verily, do you kill me! Truly do I say, killed by you I am sure to attain to a pious end!

data.v: पश्य ह्यप्सरसो दिव्या मया दत्तेन चक्षुषा । विमानानि विचित्राणि गन्धर्वाणां महात्मनाम् ॥
data.md: I give you (spiritual) vision. Behold the celestial Apsaras and the handsome cars of the great Gandharvas!

data.v: ततः सुरुचिरं दृष्ट्वा स्पृहालग्नेन चक्षुषा । मृगमालोक्य हिंसायां स्वर्गवासं समर्थयत् ॥
data.md: Seeing (that spectacle) for a long time, with longing eyes, and seeing the deer and thinking that living in heaven can be acquired by only slaughter, he approved (of it).

data.v: स तु धर्मो मृगो भूत्वा बहुवर्षोषितो वने । तस्य निष्कृतिमाधत्त न ह्यसौ यज्ञसंविधिः ॥
data.md: It was Dharına himself who had become a deer that lived in that forest for many years. Dharma provided for his salvation and advised him, saying,-This (destruction of living creatures) is not according to the ordinances about Sacrifice..

data.v: तस्य तेन तु भावेन मृगहिंसात्मनस्तदा । तपो महत्समुच्छिन्नं तस्माद्धिंसा न यज्ञिया ॥
data.md: The penances, which had been of very great measure, of that Brahmana whose mind had cherished the desire of killing the deer, diminished greatly on account of that thought itself. The injuring of living creatures, therefore, is no part of sacrifice.

data.v: ततस्तं भगवान्धर्मो यज्ञं याजयत स्वयम् । समाधानं च भार्याया लेभे स तपसा परम् ॥
data.md: Then the illustrious Dharma, himself assisted that Brahmana, by acting as the priest, to perforin a sacrifice. The Brahmana, after this, on account of his penances, attained to the same state of mind with his wife.

data.v: अहिंसा सकलो धर्मो हिंसा यज्ञेऽसमाहिता । सत्यं तेऽहं प्रवक्ष्यामि यो धर्मः सत्यवादिनाम् ॥
data.md: Abstention from injury is the religion which is perfect about its rewards. The religion of cruelty is only so far beneficial that it leads to heaven. I have described to you the religion of Truth which, indeed, is the religion of those who utter Brahma.

data.v: कथं भवति पापात्मा कथं धर्मं करोति वा । केन निर्वेदमादत्ते मोक्षं वा केन गच्छति ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said By what means does a man become sinful, by what does he acquire virtue, by what does he acquire renunciation, and by what does he acquire Liberation.

data.v: विदिताः सर्वधर्मास्ते स्थित्यर्थमनुपृच्छसि । शृणु मोक्षं सनिर्वेदं पापं धर्मं च मूलतः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said now You know all duties. This question which you have put to me is only for confirmation of your conclusions. Listen fully to Liberation, and Renunciation, and Sin, and Virtue.

data.v: विज्ञानार्थं हि पञ्चानामिच्छा पूर्वं प्रवर्तते । प्राप्य ताञ्जायते कामो द्वेषो वा भरतर्षभ ॥
data.md: Perceiving any one of the five objects, desire runs after it at first. Indeed, obtaining them within the pale of the senses, O foremost of Bharata's family, desire or hatred originates.

data.v: ततस्तदर्थं यतते कर्म चारभते पुनः । इष्टानां रूपगन्धानामभ्यासं च चिकीर्षति ॥
data.md: One then, for the sake of that object, trics and begins acts that require much labour. One tries his best for enjoying again and again those forms and scents that appear very sweet.

data.v: ततो रागः प्रभवति द्वेषश्च तदनन्तरम् । ततो लोभः प्रभवति मोहश्च तदनन्तरम् ॥
data.md: The mind of one possessed by greed and mistake and affected by attachment and hatred is never bent to virtue. One then begins with hypocrisy to do deeds which are good.

data.v: लोभमोहाभिभूतस्य रागद्वेषान्वितस्य च । न धर्मे जायते बुद्धिर्व्याजाद्धर्मं करोति च ॥
व्याजेन चरतो धर्ममर्थव्याजोऽपि रोचते । व्याजेन सिध्यमानेषु धनेषु कुरुनन्दन ॥
तत्रैव कुरुते बुद्धिं ततः पापं चिकीर्षति । सुहृद्भिर्वार्यमाणोऽपि पण्डितैश्चापि भारत ॥
उत्तरं न्यायसंबद्धं ब्रवीति विधियोजितम् । अधर्मस्त्रिविधस्तस्य वर्धते रागमोहजः ॥
पापं चिन्तयते चैव प्रब्रवीति करोति च । तस्याधर्मप्रवृत्तस्य दोषान्पश्यन्ति साधवः ॥
एकशीलाश्च मित्रत्वं भजन्ते पापकर्मिणः । स नेह सुखमाप्नोति कुत एव परत्र वै ॥
एवं भवति पापात्मा धर्मात्मानं तु मे शृणु । यथा कुशलधर्मा स कुशलं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
य एतान्प्रज्ञया दोषान्पूर्वमेवानुपश्यति । कुशलः सुखदुःखानां साधूंश्चाप्युपसेवते ॥
data.md: He who, helped by his wisdom, succeeds beforehand seeing the faults referred to above, who is skilled in determining what is happiness and what is sorrow and how each is engendered, and who waits respectfully upon the good, makes progress in acquiring virtue, both on account of his habit and such companionship of the good. The mind of such a person finds pleasure in virtue, and he live on, making virtue his stay.

data.v: तस्य साधुसमाचारादभ्यासाच्चैव वर्धते । प्रज्ञा धर्मे च रमते धर्मं चैवोपजीवति ॥
सोऽथ धर्मादवाप्तेषु धनेषु कुरुते मनः । तस्यैव सिञ्चते मूलं गुणान्पश्यति यत्र वै ॥
धर्मात्मा भवति ह्येवं मित्रं च लभते शुभम् । स मित्रधनलाभात्तु प्रेत्य चेह च नन्दति ॥
शब्दे स्पर्शे तथा रूपे रसे गन्धे च भारत । प्रभुत्वं लभते जन्तुर्धर्मस्यैतत्फलं विदुः ॥
स धर्मस्य फलं लब्ध्वा न तृप्यति युधिष्ठिर । अतृप्यमाणो निर्वेदमादत्ते ज्ञानचक्षुषा ॥
प्रज्ञाचक्षुर्यदा कामे दोषमेवानुपश्यति । विरज्यते तदा कामान्न च धर्मं विमुञ्चति ॥
सर्वत्यागे च यतते दृष्ट्वा लोकं क्षयात्मकम् । ततो मोक्षाय यतते नानुपायादुपायतः ॥
data.md: Seeing then all the worlds as being subject top destruction, he tries to renounce virtue and tries to attain to Liberation by the (well-known) means.

data.v: शनैर्निर्वेदमादत्ते पापं कर्म जहाति च । धर्मात्मा चैव भवति मोक्षं च लभते परम् ॥
data.md: Gradually renouncing all sinful deeds he follows Renunciation, and becoming righteoussouled succeeds at last in acquiring Liberation.

data.v: एतत्ते कथितं तात यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि । पापं धर्मं तथा मोक्षं निर्वेदं चैव भारत ॥
data.md: I have now told you, O Son, of that about which you had asked me, viz., the topics of Sin, Righteousness, Renunciation, and Liberation, O Bharata.

data.v: तस्माद्धर्मे प्रवर्तेथाः सर्वावस्थं युधिष्ठिर । धर्मे स्थितानां कौन्तेय सिद्धिर्भवति शाश्वती ॥
data.md: You should, therefore, O Yudhishthira, follow virtue under all circumstances. Eternal is the success, O son of Kunti, of you who follow righteousness.

data.v: मोक्षः पितामहेनोक्त उपायान्नानुपायतः । तमुपायं यथान्यायं श्रोतुमिच्छामि भारत ॥
data.md: Yudhisthira said You have said, O grand-father, that Liberation is to be acquired by means and not otherwise. I wish to hear duly what those means are.

data.v: त्वय्येवैतन्महाप्राज्ञ युक्तं निपुणदर्शनम् । यदुपायेन सर्वार्थान्नित्यं मृगयसेऽनघ ॥
data.md: Bhishma said O you of great wisdom, this enquiry which you have made me and which is connected with a subtle topic, is really worthy of you, since you, O sinless one, always try to accomplish all your objects by the application of means.

data.v: करणे घटस्य या बुद्धिर्घटोत्पत्तौ न सानघ । एवं धर्माभ्युपायेषु नान्यद्धर्मेषु कारणम् ॥
data.md: That state of mind which one feels when he makes an earthen jar for his use, disappears after the jar has been completed. Likewise, that cause which makes persons who regard virtue as the root of advancement and prosperity ceases to act with them who seek to acquire Liberation.

data.v: पूर्वे समुद्रे यः पन्था न स गच्छति पश्चिमम् । एकः पन्था हि मोक्षस्य तन्मे विस्तरतः शृणु ॥
data.md: That path which leads to the Eastern Ocean is not the path by which one can go to the Western Ocean. There is only one path which leads to Liberation. Listen to me as I describe it to you in detail.

data.v: क्षमया क्रोधमुच्छिन्द्यात्कामं संकल्पवर्जनात् । सत्त्वसंसेवनाद्धीरो निद्रामुच्छेतुमर्हति ॥
data.md: One should, by practising forgiveness, root out anger and by renouncing all purposes, root out desire. By practising the quality of goodness one should conquer sleep.

data.v: अप्रमादाद्भयं रक्षेच्छ्वासं क्षेत्रज्ञशीलनात् । इच्छां द्वेषं च कामं च धैर्येण विनिवर्तयेत् ॥
data.md: By carefulness one should keep off fear, and by contemplation of the Soul one should conquer vital airs. One should remove by patience desire, hatred, and lust; and error, ignorance, and doubt, by study of truth. By pursuit of knowledge one should avoid inquiry after uninteresting things.

data.v: भ्रमं प्रमोहमावर्तमभ्यासाद्विनिवर्तयेत् । निद्रां च प्रतिभां चैव ज्ञानाभ्यासेन तत्त्ववित् ॥
data.md: By carefulness one should keep off fear, and by contemplation of the Soul one should conquer vital airs. One should remove by patience desire, hatred, and lust; and error, ignorance, and doubt, by study of truth. By pursuit of knowledge one should avoid inquiry after uninteresting things.

data.v: उपद्रवांस्तथा रोगान्हितजीर्णमिताशनात् । लोभं मोहं च संतोषाद्विषयांस्तत्त्वदर्शनात् ॥
data.md: By frugal and easily digestible food one should dispell all disorders and diseases. By contentment one should remove greed and stupefaction of judgement, and all earthly concerns should be avoided by a knowledge of the truth.

data.v: अनुक्रोशादधर्मं च जयेद्धर्ममुपेक्षया । आयत्या च जयेदाशामर्थं सङ्गविवर्जनात् ॥
data.md: By practising benevolence one should conquer sin, and by regard for all creatures one should gain virtue. One should avoid expectation by thinking that it is connected with the future; and one should renounce riches by abandoning desire itself.

data.v: अनित्यत्वेन च स्नेहं क्षुधं योगेन पण्डितः । कारुण्येनात्मनो मानं तृष्णां च परितोषतः ॥
data.md: The intelligent man should cast off affection by thinking that everything is fickle. He should control hunger by practising Yoga. By practising benevolence one should keep off all ideas of ego, and remove all sorts of craving by adopting contentment.

data.v: उत्थानेन जयेत्तन्द्रीं वितर्कं निश्चयाज्जयेत् । मौनेन बहुभाष्यं च शौर्येण च भयं जयेत् ॥
data.md: By exertion should subdue procrastination, by certainty all kinds of doubt, one by taciturnity, loquaciousness, and by courage every sort of fear.

data.v: यच्छेद्वाङ्मनसी बुद्ध्या तां यच्छेज्ज्ञानचक्षुषा । ज्ञानमात्मा महान्यच्छेत्तं यच्छेच्छान्तिरात्मनः ॥
data.md: Speech and mind are to be controlled by the Understanding, and the Understanding, in its turn, by the eye of knowledge. Knowledge, again, is to be controlled by the knowledge of the Soul, and finally the Soul it to be controlled by the Soul.

data.v: तदेतदुपशान्तेन बोद्धव्यं शुचिकर्मणा । योगदोषान्समुच्छिद्य पञ्च यान्कवयो विदुः ॥
data.md: This last is acquired by those who are of pure acts and endued with tranquillity of soul, the means being the subjugation of those five obstacles of Yoga of which the learned speak.

data.v: कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च भयं स्वप्नं च पञ्चमम् । परित्यज्य निषेवेत तथेमान्योगसाधनान् ॥
data.md: By renouncing desire, anger covetousness, fear and sleep, one should controlling speech, practise the observances favourable to Yoga, viz., contemplation, study, gift, truth, modesty, candour, forgiveness, purity of heart, purity of food, and the subjugation of the senses.

data.v: ध्यानमध्ययनं दानं सत्यं ह्रीरार्जवं क्षमा । शौचमाहारतः शुद्धिरिन्द्रियाणां च संयमः ॥
data.md: By renouncing desire, anger covetousness, fear and sleep, one should controlling speech, practise the observances favourable to Yoga, viz., contemplation, study, gift, truth, modesty, candour, forgiveness, purity of heart, purity of food, and the subjugation of the senses.

data.v: एतैर्विवर्धते तेजः पाप्मानमपहन्ति च । सिध्यन्ति चास्य संकल्पा विज्ञानं च प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: By these one's energy is increased, sins are removed, wishes crowned with success, and knowledge gained.

data.v: धूतपापः स तेजस्वी लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः । कामक्रोधौ वशे कृत्वा निनीषेद्ब्रह्मणः पदम् ॥
data.md: When one becomes purged of sins and possessed of energy and abstemious in diet and the master of his senses, one then, having conquered both desire and anger, seeks to attain to Brahma.

data.v: अमूढत्वमसङ्गित्वं कामक्रोधविवर्जनम् । अदैन्यमनुदीर्णत्वमनुद्वेगो व्यवस्थितिः ॥
data.md: The avoidance of ignorance, the absence of attachment, freedom from desire and anger, the power that is acquired by Yoga, the absence of pride and haughtiness, freedom from anxiety, absence of attachment to anything like home and family,—these forin the path of Liberation. That path is delightful, stainless, and pure. Likewise, the control of speech, of body, and of mind, when practised from the absence of desire, forms also the path of Liberation.

data.v: एष मार्गो हि मोक्षस्य प्रसन्नो विमलः शुचिः । तथा वाक्कायमनसां नियमः कामतोऽन्यथा ॥
data.md: The avoidance of ignorance, the absence of attachment, freedom from desire and anger, the power that is acquired by Yoga, the absence of pride and haughtiness, freedom from anxiety, absence of attachment to anything like home and family,—these forin the path of Liberation. That path is delightful, stainless, and pure. Likewise, the control of speech, of body, and of mind, when practised from the absence of desire, forms also the path of Liberation.

data.v: अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । नारदस्य च संवादं देवलस्यासितस्य च ॥
data.md: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Kapila and the cow. Listen to it, O Yudhishthira.

data.v: आसीनं देवलं वृद्धं बुद्ध्वा बुद्धिमतां वरः । नारदः परिपप्रच्छ भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययम् ॥
data.md: Once on a time Narada, seeing that foremost of intelligent men, viz., Devala of venerable years, seated at his ease, asked him about the origin and the destruction of all creatures.

data.v: कुतः सृष्टमिदं विश्वं ब्रह्मन्स्थावरजङ्गमम् । प्रलये च कमभ्येति तद्भवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे ॥
data.md: Narada said Whence, O Brahmana, has this universe, consisting of mobile and iminobile objects, been created? When, again, the all-embracing destruction sets in, into whom does it merge! Let your learned self describe this to me.

data.v: येभ्यः सृजति भूतानि कालो भावप्रचोदितः । महाभूतानि पञ्चेति तान्याहुर्भूतचिन्तकाः ॥
data.md: are Those from which the Supreme Self, when the time comes, actuated by the desire of existence in various forms, creates all creatures, and said by persons conversant with objects to be the five essential principles.

data.v: तेभ्यः सृजति भूतानि काल आत्मप्रचोदितः । एतेभ्यो यः परं ब्रूयादसद्ब्रूयादसंशयम् ॥
data.md: Time, moved by the Understanding, created other objects from them. He who says that there is anything else save these, says the untruth.

data.v: विद्धि नारद पञ्चैताञ्शाश्वतानचलान्ध्रुवान् । महतस्तेजसो राशीन्कालषष्ठान्स्वभावतः ॥
data.md: Know, O Narada, that these five are eternal, indestructible, and without beginning and without end. With Kala as their sixth, these five essential ingredients naturally possessed of great power.

data.v: आपश्चैवान्तरिक्षं च पृथिवी वायुपावकौ । असिद्धिः परमेतेभ्यो भूतेभ्यो मुक्तसंशयम् ॥
data.md: Water, Ether, Earth, Air, and Fire,—these are those five principal elements. Forsooth, there is nothing higher or superior to these.

data.v: नोपपत्त्या न वा युक्त्या त्वसद्ब्रूयादसंशयम् । वेत्थ तानभिनिर्वृत्तान्षडेते यस्य राशयः ॥
data.md: The existence of nothing else can is inferred by any one agreeably to the conclusions of the Shrutis or arguments drawn from reason. If any one does hold the existence of anything else, then his assertion would, in sooth, be useless. Know that these six form all others. That of which are all these is called non-existent.

data.v: पञ्चैव तानि कालश्च भावाभावौ च केवलौ । अष्टौ भूतानि भूतानां शाश्वतानि भवाप्ययौ ॥
data.md: These five, and Kala (or Jiva), the effects of past acts, and Ignorance,-these eight eternal essences are the causes of the birth and destruction of creatures.

data.v: अभावाद्भावितेष्वेव तेभ्यश्च प्रभवन्त्यपि । विनष्टोऽपि च तान्येव जन्तुर्भवति पञ्चधा ॥
data.md: When creatures are destroyed it is into these that they merge; and when they are born, it is again from them that they do so. Indeed, after destruction, a creature resolves itself into those five elements.

data.v: तस्य भूमिमयो देहः श्रोत्रमाकाशसंभवम् । सूर्यश्चक्षुरसुर्वायुरद्भ्यस्तु खलु शोणितम् ॥
data.md: His body is made of earth; his ear is made of ether; his eye has light for it cause, his life is of air, and his blood is of water.

data.v: चक्षुषी नासिकाकर्णौ त्वग्जिह्वेति च पञ्चमी । इन्द्रियाणीन्द्रियार्थानां ज्ञानानि कवयो विदुः ॥
data.md: The two eyes, the nose, the two ears, the skin, and the tongue, are the senses. These, the learned hold, exist for perception of their various objects.

data.v: दर्शनं श्रवणं घ्राणं स्पर्शनं रसनं तथा । उपपत्त्या गुणान्विद्धि पञ्च पञ्चसु पञ्चधा ॥
data.md: Seeing, hearing, smelling, touching and tasting are the actions of the senses. The five senses, are connected with five objects in five ways. Know, by the inference of reason, their similitude of attributes.

data.v: रूपं गन्धो रसः स्पर्शः शब्दश्चैवाथ तद्गुणाः । इन्द्रियैरुपलभ्यन्ते पञ्चधा पञ्च पञ्चभिः ॥
data.md: Form, scent, taste, touch, and sound, are the five properties that are perceived by the five senses in five different ways.

data.v: रूपं गन्धं रसं स्पर्शं शब्दं चैतांस्तु तद्गुणान् । इन्द्रियाणि न बुध्यन्ते क्षेत्रज्ञस्तैस्तु बुध्यते ॥
data.md: These five properties, viz., form scent, taste, touch, and sound, are not really perceived by the senses, but it is the Soul that apprehends them through the senses.

data.v: चित्तमिन्द्रियसंघातात्परं तस्मात्परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिः क्षेत्रज्ञो बुद्धितः परः ॥
data.md: That which is called Faculty is superior to all the Superior to Mind is Understanding, and superior to Understanding is Soul. senses.

data.v: पूर्वं चेतयते जन्तुरिन्द्रियैर्विषयान्पृथक् । विचार्य मनसा पश्चादथ बुद्ध्या व्यवस्यति । इन्द्रियैरुपलब्धार्थान्सर्वान्यस्त्वध्यवस्यति ॥
data.md: At first a living creature perceives various objects through the senses. With Mind he reflects over them, and then with the help of Understanding, he arrives at certainty of knowledge. Endued with Understanding, one arrives at certainty of conclusions regarding objects perceived through the senses.

data.v: चित्तमिन्द्रियसंघातं मनो बुद्धिं तथाष्टमीम् । अष्टौ ज्ञानेन्द्रियाण्याहुरेतान्यध्यात्मचिन्तकाः ॥
data.md: The five senses, Faculty, Mind, and Understanding,-these are regarded as organs of knowledge by those conversant with the spiritual science.

data.v: पाणिपादं च पायुश्च मेहनं पञ्चमं मुखम् । इति संशब्द्यमानानि शृणु कर्मेन्द्रियाण्यपि ॥
data.md: The hands, the feet, the anus, the inembrum virile, the mouth, form the five organs of actions.

data.v: जल्पनाभ्यवहारार्थं मुखमिन्द्रियमुच्यते । गमनेन्द्रियं तथा पादौ कर्मणः करणे करौ ॥
data.md: The mouth is spoken of as an organ of action because it contains the instrument of speech, and that of eating. The feet are organs of locomotion and the hands for doing various sorts of work.

data.v: पायूपस्थौ विसर्गार्थमिन्द्रिये तुल्यकर्मणी । विसर्गे च पुरीषस्य विसर्गे चाभिकामिके ॥
data.md: The anus and the membrum virile are two organs which exist for evacuation. The first is for evacuation of stools, the second for that of urine as also of the semen when one feels the influence of desire.

data.v: बलं षष्ठं षडेतानि वाचा सम्यग्यथागमम् । ज्ञानचेष्टेन्द्रियगुणाः सर्वे संशब्दिता मया ॥
data.md: Besides these, there is a sixth organ of action. It is called muscle. These then are the names of the six organs of action according to the book written on the subject. I have now described to you the names of all the organs of knowledge and of action, and all the attributes of the five elements.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणां स्वकर्मभ्यः श्रमादुपरमो यदा । भवतीन्द्रियसंन्यासादथ स्वपिति वै नरः ॥
data.md: When on account of the organs being fatigued, they cease to discharge their respective functions, the owner of those organs, their action being suspended is said to sleep.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणां व्युपरमे मनोऽनुपरतं यदि । सेवते विषयानेव तद्विद्यात्स्वप्नदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: If when the action of these organs is stopped, the action of the mind, does not cease, but on the other hand the mind continues to act, that state of Consciousness is called Dream.

data.v: सात्त्विकाश्चैव ये भावास्तथा राजसतामसाः । कर्मयुक्तान्प्रशंसन्ति सात्त्विकानितरांस्तथा ॥
data.md: During wakefulness there are three states of the mind viz., that connected with Goodness, that with Darkness, and that with Ignorance. In dream also the mind is connected with the same three states. Those very states, when they appear is dreams, connected with pleasurable actions, are spoken highly of.

data.v: आनन्दः कर्मणां सिद्धिः प्रतिपत्तिः परा गतिः । सात्त्विकस्य निमित्तानि भावान्संश्रयते स्मृतिः ॥
data.md: Happiness, success, knowledge, and absence of attachment are the marks of the quality of Goodness. Whatever states are experienced by living creatures, as shown in acts, during their hours of wakefulness, reappear in memory during their hours of sleep when they dream. The passage of our ideas as they exist during wakefulness into those of dreams, and that of ideas as they exist in dreams into those of wakefulness, become directly perceptible in that state of consciousness which is called dreamless sleep. That is eternal, and that is desirable.

data.v: जन्तुष्वेकतमेष्वेवं भावा ये विधिमास्थिताः । भावयोरीप्सितं नित्यं प्रत्यक्षगमनं द्वयोः ॥
data.md: Happiness, success, knowledge, and absence of attachment are the marks of the quality of Goodness. Whatever states are experienced by living creatures, as shown in acts, during their hours of wakefulness, reappear in memory during their hours of sleep when they dream. The passage of our ideas as they exist during wakefulness into those of dreams, and that of ideas as they exist in dreams into those of wakefulness, become directly perceptible in that state of consciousness which is called dreamless sleep. That is eternal, and that is desirable.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणि च भावाश्च गुणाः सप्तदश स्मृताः । तेषामष्टादशो देही यः शरीरे स शाश्वतः ॥
data.md: There are five organs of knowledge, and five of action; with muscular power, mind, understanding, and faculty, and with also the three qualities of goodness, darkness and ignorance, the number, it has been said, comes up to seventeen. The eighteenth in the calculation is he who owns the body. Indeed, he who lives in this body is eternal.

data.v: अथ वा सशरीरास्ते गुणाः सर्वे शरीरिणाम् । संश्रितास्तद्वियोगे हि सशरीरा न सन्ति ते ॥
data.md: All those seventeen (with Avidya or nesciene as eighteenth) living in the body, exist attached to him who owns the body. When the owner disappear from the body, those eighteen cease to live together in the body.

data.v: अथ वा संनिपातोऽयं शरीरं पाञ्चभौतिकम् । एकश्च दश चाष्टौ च गुणाः सह शरीरिणाम् । ऊष्मणा सह विंशो वा संघातः पाञ्चभौतिकः ॥
data.md: Or, this body made up the five principal elements only a combination. The eighteen attributes, with him that owns the body, and counting stomachic heat numbering twentieth, form that which is known as the Combination of the Five.

data.v: महान्संधारयत्येतच्छरीरं वायुना सह । तस्यास्य भावयुक्तस्य निमित्तं देहभेदने ॥
यथैवोत्पद्यते किंचित्पञ्चत्वं गच्छते तथा । पुण्यपापविनाशान्ते पुण्यपापसमीरितम् । देहं विशति कालेन ततोऽयं कर्मसंभवम् ॥
data.md: Whatever creature is born is resolved once more into the five principal elements upon the exhaustion of his merits and demerits; and moved again by the merits and demerits acquired in that life enters into another body resulting from his deeds.

data.v: हित्वा हित्वा ह्ययं प्रैति देहाद्देहं कृताश्रयः । कालसंचोदितः क्षेत्री विशीर्णाद्वा गृहाद्गृहम् ॥
data.md: His habitation always resulting from nescience, desire, and acts, he migrates from body to body, leaving off one after another repeatedly, urged on by Time, like a person leaving house after in succession.

data.v: तत्र नैवानुतप्यन्ते प्राज्ञा निश्चितनिश्चयाः । कृपणास्त्वनुतप्यन्ते जनाः संबन्धिमानिनः ॥
data.md: The wise, wise, gifted with certainty of knowledge, do not yield to grief upon seeing this. Only the foolish, erroneously supposing relationships indulge in grief on seeing such changes of habitation.

data.v: न ह्ययं कस्यचित्कश्चिन्नास्य कश्चन विद्यते । भवत्येको ह्ययं नित्यं शरीरे सुखदुःखभाक् ॥
data.md: This individual soul is no one's relation; there is none again that may be said to belong to him. He is always alone, and he is himself the creator of his own body and his own happiness and misery.

data.v: नैव संजायते जन्तुर्न च जातु विपद्यते । याति देहमयं भुक्त्वा कदाचित्परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: This individual is never born, nor does he ever die. Freed from the fetters of body, he succeeds sometimes in acquiring the highest end.

data.v: पुण्यपापमयं देहं क्षपयन्कर्मसंचयात् । क्षीणदेहः पुनर्देही ब्रह्मत्वमुपगच्छति ॥
data.md: Deprived of body, because freed through the dissipation of acts from bodies that are the outcome of merits and demerits, individual at last attains to Brahma.

data.v: पुण्यपापक्षयार्थं च सांख्यं ज्ञानं विधीयते । तत्क्षये ह्यस्य पश्यन्ति ब्रह्मभावे परां गतिम् ॥
data.md: For the dissipation of both merits and demerits, Knowledge has been described as the cause in the Sankhya school. Upon the dissipation of merit and demerit, when individual soul attains to the status of Brahma, the learned behold the attainment of individual soul to the highest end.

data.v: भ्रातरः पितरः पुत्रा ज्ञातयः सुहृदस्तथा । अर्थहेतोर्हताः क्रूरैरस्माभिः पापबुद्धिभिः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Cruel and sinful as we are, alas, we have killed brothers and fathers and grandsons and relatives and friends and sons.

data.v: येयमर्थोद्भवा तृष्णा कथमेतां पितामह । निवर्तयेम पापं हि तृष्णया कारिता वयम् ॥
data.md: How, O grandfather, shall we remove this thirst for riches. Alas, through that thirst we have committed many sinful deeds.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । गीतं विदेहराजेन माण्डव्यायानुपृच्छते ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old narrative of what was said by the king of the Videhas to the enquiring Mandavya.

data.v: सुसुखं बत जीवामि यस्य मे नास्ति किंचन । मिथिलायां प्रदीप्तायां न मे दह्यति किंचन ॥
data.md: The king of the Videhas said, I have nothing, yet I live in great happiness. If the whole of Mithila be reduced to ashes nothing of mine will be burnt down.

data.v: अर्थाः खलु समृद्धा हि बाढं दुःखं विजानताम् । असमृद्धास्त्वपि सदा मोहयन्त्यविचक्षणान् ॥
data.md: Tangible possessions of what value they may be, are a source of sorrow to men of knowledge; while properties of cven little value attract the foolish. one

data.v: यच्च कामसुखं लोके यच्च दिव्यं महत्सुखम् । तृष्णाक्षयसुखस्यैते नार्हतः षोडशीं कलाम् ॥
data.md: Whatever happiness is in this world, owing to the gratification of desire, and whatever celestial happiness exists of high value, do not form even a sixteenth part of the felicity that accrues from the disappearance of desire.

data.v: यथैव शृङ्गं गोः काले वर्धमानस्य वर्धते । तथैव तृष्णा वित्तेन वर्धमानेन वर्धते ॥
data.md: As the horns of a cow grow with the growth of the cow itself, similarly the thirst for riches multiplies with increasing acquisitions of wealth.

data.v: किंचिदेव ममत्वेन यदा भवति कल्पितम् । तदेव परितापाय नाशे संपद्यते पुनः ॥
data.md: The object for which feels an attachment, becomes a source of pain to him when it is lost.

data.v: न कामाननुरुध्येत दुःखं कामेषु वै रतिः । प्राप्यार्थमुपयुञ्जीत धर्मे कामं विवर्जयेत् ॥
data.md: One should not entertain desire. Attachment to desire brings on sorrow. When riches have been acquired one should devote it to virtuous purposes. One should even then relinquish desire.

data.v: विद्वान्सर्वेषु भूतेषु व्याघ्रमांसोपमो भवेत् । कृतकृत्यो विशुद्धात्मा सर्वं त्यजति वै सह ॥
data.md: The man of knowledge always considers other creatures like unto himself. Having purified his soul and gained success, he casts off everything here.

data.v: उभे सत्यानृते त्यक्त्वा शोकानन्दौ प्रियाप्रिये । भयाभये च संत्यज्य संप्रशान्तो निरामयः ॥
data.md: By shaking off both truth and falsehood, grief and joy, the agreeable and disagreeable, fearlessness and fear, one acquires tranquillity, and becomes free from anxiety.

data.v: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः । योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम् ॥
data.md: That thirst which cannot be shaken off by men of foolish understanding, which does not decrease with the decline of the body, and which is considered as dreadful disease, one who succeeds in shaking off is sure to find happiress.

data.v: चारित्रमात्मनः पश्यंश्चन्द्रशुद्धमनामयम् । धर्मात्मा लभते कीर्तिं प्रेत्य चेह यथासुखम् ॥
data.md: The virtuous man by seeing his own conduct has become bright as the moon and free from every sort of evil, succeeds in happily acquiring great fame both here and hereafter.

data.v: राज्ञस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रीतिमानभवद्द्विजः । पूजयित्वा च तद्वाक्यं माण्डव्यो मोक्षमाश्रितः ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of the king, the Brahmana became filled with joy, and speaking highly of what he heard, Mandavya followed the path of Liberation.

data.v: किंशीलः किंसमाचारः किंविद्यः किंपरायणः । प्राप्नोति ब्रह्मणः स्थानं यत्परं प्रकृतेर्ध्रुवम् ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said "What should be a man's conduct, what his acts, what his knowledge, and to what must he be devoted, for attaining to Brahma's place which is above Nature and which is unchangeable?”

data.v: मोक्षधर्मेषु निरतो लघ्वाहारो जितेन्द्रियः । प्राप्नोति परमं स्थानं यत्परं प्रकृतेर्ध्रुवम् ॥
data.md: One who is devoted to the religion of Liberation, abstemious in diet, and the master of his senses, attains to that high place which is above Prakriti and is unchangeable.

data.v: स्वगृहादभिनिःसृत्य लाभालाभे समो मुनिः । समुपोढेषु कामेषु निरपेक्षः परिव्रजेत् ॥
न चक्षुषा न मनसा न वाचा दूषयेदपि । न प्रत्यक्षं परोक्षं वा दूषणं व्याहरेत्क्वचित् ॥
data.md: Neither with eye, nor with word, nor in thought, should one disparage another. Nor should one speak ill of any person either in or out of his hearing.

data.v: न हिंस्यात्सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायणगतिश्चरेत् । नेदं जीवितमासाद्य वैरं कुर्वीत केनचित् ॥
data.md: One should refrain from injuring any creature, and fact observing the course of the Sun. Having come into this life, one should not treat with unfriendliness any creature.

data.v: अतिवादांस्तितिक्षेत नाभिमन्येत्कथंचन । क्रोध्यमानः प्रियं ब्रूयादाक्रुष्टः कुशलं वदेत् ॥
data.md: One should disregard disgraceful speeches, and never in pride consider himself as superior to another. When sought to be angered by another, one should still give vent to agreeable speeches. Even when spoken ill of one should not calumniate in return.

data.v: प्रदक्षिणं प्रसव्यं च ग्राममध्ये न चाचरेत् । भैक्षचर्यामनापन्नो न गच्छेत्पूर्वकेतितः ॥
data.md: One should not act in a friendly or an unfriendly manner in the midst of human beings. One should not go about many houses in this round of mendicancy. Nor should one go to any house having obtained a previous invitation.

data.v: अवकीर्णः सुगुप्तश्च न वाचा ह्यप्रियं वदेत् । मृदुः स्यादप्रतिक्रूरो विस्रब्धः स्यादरोषणः ॥
data.md: Even when filled with filth, one should, firmly following his duties, refrain from addressing unpleasant words to such men. One should be merciful. One should not return an injury. One should be fearless; one should not speak highly of himself.

data.v: विधूमे न्यस्तमुसले व्यङ्गारे भुक्तवज्जने । अतीते पात्रसंचारे भिक्षां लिप्सेत वै मुनिः ॥
data.md: The man of controlled senses should beg alms in a householder's house when the smoke has ceased to rise from it, when the sound of the husking rod is heard no more, when the hearth-fire is gone, when all the inmates have taken their food, or when the hour for setting the dishes is over.

data.v: अनुयात्रिकमर्थस्य मात्रालाभेष्वनादृतः । अलाभे न विहन्येत लाभश्चैनं न हर्षयेत् ॥
लाभं साधारणं नेच्छेन्न भुञ्जीताभिपूजितः । अभिपूजितलाभं हि जुगुप्सेतैव तादृशः ॥
data.md: He should be satisfied with only as much as is hardly necessary for keeping the body and soul together. Even that much of food which yields gratification should not be sought by him. When he fails to get what he wants, he should not cherish discontent. Success, again, in obtaining what he wants, should not elate him. He should never wish for such things as are sought by ordinary men. He should never take his meals at any body's house when respectfully invited thereto. One like him should hate any thing that is presented with honour.

data.v: न चान्नदोषान्निन्देत न गुणानभिपूजयेत् । शय्यासने विविक्ते च नित्यमेवाभिपूजयेत् ॥
data.md: He should never find fault with the food put before him, nor should he speak highly of its merits. He should seek a bed and a seat that are removed from human habitations.

data.v: शून्यागारं वृक्षमूलमरण्यमथ वा गुहाम् । अज्ञातचर्यां गत्वान्यां ततोऽन्यत्रैव संविशेत् ॥
data.md: The places he should seek should be such as an abandoned house, the foot of a tree, a forest, or a cave. Without making his practices to be known by others, or concealing their real nature by appearing to adopt others, he should enter his own Self.

data.v: अनुरोधविरोधाभ्यां समः स्यादचलो ध्रुवः । सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चोभे नानुरुध्येत कर्मणि ॥
data.md: By association with Yoga and dissociation from company, he should be perfectly calm, steadily fixed, and uniform. He should not acquire either merit or demerit by means of acts.

data.v: वाचो वेगं मनसः क्रोधवेगं; विवित्सावेगमुदरोपस्थवेगम् । एतान्वेगान्विनयेद्वै तपस्वी; निन्दा चास्य हृदयं नोपहन्यात् ॥
data.md: One should govern the impulses of words, of the mind, of anger of envy, of hunger, and of lust. Given to penances for purifying his heart, he should never allow the censures (of others) to pain his heart.

data.v: मध्यस्थ एव तिष्ठेत प्रशंसानिन्दयोः समः । एतत्पवित्रं परमं परिव्राजक आश्रमे ॥
data.md: Becoming neutral, should live, regarding praise and censure as equal. This, indeed, is the holiest and the highest path of Renunciation.

data.v: महात्मा सुव्रतो दान्तः सर्वत्रैवानपाश्रितः । अपूर्वचारकः सौम्यो अनिकेतः समाहितः ॥
data.md: Endued with great soul, the Sannyasin should control his senses from all things and stand aloof from all attachments. He should never go to the places visited by him and the men known to him while he lived otherwise, Agreeable to all creatures, and without a fixed dwelling, he should be given to the contemplation of Self. one

data.v: वानप्रस्थगृहस्थाभ्यां न संसृज्येत कर्हिचित् । अज्ञातलिप्सां लिप्सेत न चैनं हर्ष आविशेत् ॥
data.md: He should never mingle with house-holders and hermits. He should eat such food as he may get without effort. He should never allow joy to possess his heart.

data.v: विजानतां मोक्ष एष श्रमः स्यादविजानताम् । मोक्षयानमिदं कृत्स्नं विदुषां हारितोऽब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Such a life of Renunciation brings on Liberation to those that are wise. The practice of these duties is a great burden to those, however, that are fools, The sage Harita declared all this to be the path by which Liberation can be acquired.

data.v: अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो दत्त्वा यः प्रव्रजेद्गृहात् । लोकास्तेजोमयास्तस्य तथानन्त्याय कल्पते ॥
data.md: He who leaves his home, having assured all creatures of his perfect harmlessness, acquires many bright and eternal regions of felicity.

data.v: धन्या धन्या इति जनाः सर्वेऽस्मान्प्रवदन्त्युत । न दुःखिततरः कश्चित्पुमानस्माभिरस्ति ह ॥
data.md: All men describe ourselves as highly fortunate. In sooth, however, there is no person more wretched than ourselves.

data.v: लोकसंभावितैर्दुःखं यत्प्राप्तं कुरुसत्तम । प्राप्य जातिं मनुष्येषु देवैरपि पितामह ॥
data.md: Though respected of all the world, O best of the Kurus, and though we have been born among men, O grandfather, having been begotten by the very gods, yet when so much sorrow has come to us, it appears, O reverened chief, that birth in an embodied form is the root of all sorrow! Alas, when shall we adopt a life of Renunciation which dissipates sorrow?

data.v: कदा वयं करिष्यामः संन्यासं दुःखसंज्ञकम् । दुःखमेतच्छरीराणां धारणं कुरुसत्तम ॥
data.md: Though respected of all the world, O best of the Kurus, and though we have been born among men, O grandfather, having been begotten by the very gods, yet when so much sorrow has come to us, it appears, O reverened chief, that birth in an embodied form is the root of all sorrow! Alas, when shall we adopt a life of Renunciation which dissipates sorrow?

data.v: विमुक्ताः सप्तदशभिर्हेतुभूतैश्च पञ्चभिः । इन्द्रियार्थैर्गुणैश्चैव अष्टाभिः प्रपितामह ॥
data.md: Sages of rigid vows freed from the seventeen (i.e., the five vital airs, mind, understanding, and the ten organs of knowledge and action), from the five shortcomings of Yoga (viz., desire, anger, covetousness, fear, and sleep), which form the chief causes (for subjugating man to repeated re-birth), and from the other eight, (viz., the five objects of the senses and the three qualities), have never to incur rebirth. When, O scorcher of enemies, shall we succeed in renouncing sovereignty for adopting a life of Renunciation.

data.v: न गच्छन्ति पुनर्भावं मुनयः संशितव्रताः । कदा वयं भविष्यामो राज्यं हित्वा परंतप ॥
data.md: Sages of rigid vows freed from the seventeen (i.e., the five vital airs, mind, understanding, and the ten organs of knowledge and action), from the five shortcomings of Yoga (viz., desire, anger, covetousness, fear, and sleep), which form the chief causes (for subjugating man to repeated re-birth), and from the other eight, (viz., the five objects of the senses and the three qualities), have never to incur rebirth. When, O scorcher of enemies, shall we succeed in renouncing sovereignty for adopting a life of Renunciation.

data.v: नास्त्यनन्तं महाराज सर्वं संख्यानगोचरम् । पुनर्भावोऽपि संख्यातो नास्ति किंचिदिहाचलम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Everything, O great king, has an end. Everything has limits assigned to it! Even rebirth, it is well known, has an end. In this world there is nothing unchangeable.

data.v: न चापि गम्यते राजन्नैष दोषः प्रसङ्गतः । उद्योगादेव धर्मज्ञ कालेनैव गमिष्यथ ॥
data.md: You think, O king, that this portion is a fault. that it is not true, regarding our present subject of discussion. You, however, know virtue, and have readiness. It is certain, therefore, that you will go to the end of your sorrow in time.

data.v: ईशोऽयं सततं देही नृपते पुण्यपापयोः । तत एव समुत्थेन तमसा रुध्यतेऽपि च ॥
data.md: Individual with body, O king, is not the author of his merits and demerits. On the other hand, he becomes covered with the Darkness that is begotten by his merits and demerits.

data.v: यथाञ्जनमयो वायुः पुनर्मानःशिलं रजः । अनुप्रविश्य तद्वर्णो दृश्यते रञ्जयन्दिशः ॥
data.md: As the wind (having no colour of its own) assumes the colour of the substances which it has seized and tinges the different points of the horizon, similarly Individual Soul, though himself colourless, assumes a colour on account of its being enveloped by Darkness and variegated by the fruits of action, and passes from body to body.

data.v: तथा कर्मफलैर्देही रञ्जितस्तमसावृतः । विवर्णो वर्णमाश्रित्य देहेषु परिवर्तते ॥
data.md: As the wind (having no colour of its own) assumes the colour of the substances which it has seized and tinges the different points of the horizon, similarly Individual Soul, though himself colourless, assumes a colour on account of its being enveloped by Darkness and variegated by the fruits of action, and passes from body to body.

data.v: ज्ञानेन हि यदा जन्तुरज्ञानप्रभवं तमः । व्यपोहति तदा ब्रह्म प्रकाशेत सनातनम् ॥
data.md: When Individual Soul succeeds in removing by means of Knowledge the Darkness which covers him in consequence of Ignorance, then immutable Brahma becomes manifest.

data.v: अयत्नसाध्यं मुनयो वदन्ति; ये चापि मुक्तास्त उपासितव्याः । त्वया च लोकेन च सामरेण; तस्मान्न शाम्यन्ति महर्षिसंघाः ॥
data.md: The Sages say that return to Immutable Brahma cannot be attained by Acts. Yourself, others in the world, and the gods too, should respect them who have acquired Liberation. All the great Rishis never desist from culture of Brahma.

data.v: अस्मिन्नर्थे पुरा गीतं शृणुष्वैकमना नृप । यथा दैत्येन वृत्रेण भ्रष्टैश्वर्येण चेष्टितम् ॥
data.md: Regarding it is cited that discourse which was recited (by Shukra) in days of old. Listen, O king, with rapt attention to the course of conduct that was followed by the Daitya Vritra after he was shorn of all his prosperity.

data.v: निर्जितेनासहायेन हृतराज्येन भारत । अशोचता शत्रुमध्ये बुद्धिमास्थाय केवलाम् ॥
data.md: Depending only upon his intelligence, he did not grieve in the midst of his enemies, although he had been defeated, although he was friendless, and although he was deprived of sovereignty, O Bharata!

data.v: भ्रष्टैश्वर्यं पुरा वृत्रमुशना वाक्यमब्रवीत् । कच्चित्पराजितस्याद्य न व्यथा तेऽस्ति दानव ॥
data.md: When in days of old Vritra was reft of sovereignty, (his preceptor) Ushanas said to him, I hope, O Danava, that on account of your defeat your cherish no grief.

data.v: सत्येन तपसा चैव विदित्वा संक्षयं ह्यहम् । न शोचामि न हृष्यामि भूतानामागतिं गतिम् ॥
data.md: Vritra said Forsooth, having understood, by the help of truth and penances, the coming and going of all living creatures, I have ceased to grieve or joy.

data.v: कालसंचोदिता जीवा मज्जन्ति नरकेऽवशाः । परिदृष्टानि सर्वाणि दिव्यान्याहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: Urged by Times creatures sink helplessly in hell. Some again, the sages hold, go to heaven. All these pass their time happily.

data.v: क्षपयित्वा तु तं कालं गणितं कालचोदिताः । सावशेषेण कालेन संभवन्ति पुनः पुनः ॥
data.md: Passing their fixed time in heaven and hell, and with some portion of their merits and demerits unexhausted, they again and again take birth, moved by Time.

data.v: तिर्यग्योनिसहस्राणि गत्वा नरकमेव च । निर्गच्छन्त्यवशा जीवाः कालबन्धनबन्धनाः ॥
data.md: Fettered by the bonds of Desire, creatures pass through numberless intermediate lives and fall helplessly into hell.

data.v: एवं संसरमाणानि जीवान्यहमदृष्टवान् । यथा कर्म तथा लाभ इति शास्त्रनिदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: I have seen that creatures come and go even thus. The lesson taught in the Scriptures is that one's acquisitions tally with his acts.

data.v: तिर्यग्गच्छन्ति नरकं मानुष्यं दैवमेव च । सुखदुःखे प्रियद्वेष्ये चरित्वा पूर्वमेव च ॥
कृतान्तविधिसंयुक्तं सर्वलोकः प्रपद्यते । गतं गच्छन्ति चाध्वानं सर्वभूतानि सर्वदा ॥
कालसंख्यानसंख्यातं सृष्टिस्थितिपरायणम् । तं भाषमाणं भगवानुशना प्रत्यभाषत । भीमान्दुष्टप्रलापांस्त्वं तात कस्मात्प्रभाषसे ॥
प्रत्यक्षमेतद्भवतस्तथान्येषां मनीषिणाम् । मया यज्जयलुब्धेन पुरा तप्तं महत्तपः ॥
data.md: Vritra said You and also other sages know full well the severe penances which I practised from greed of victory.

data.v: गन्धानादाय भूतानां रसांश्च विविधानपि । अवर्धं त्रीन्समाक्रम्य लोकान्वै स्वेन तेजसा ॥
data.md: Appropriating various scents and various sorts of tastes that other creatures had for enjoying, I swelled up with my own energy, assailing the three worlds.

data.v: ज्वालामालापरिक्षिप्तो वैहायसचरस्तथा । अजेयः सर्वभूतानामासं नित्यमपेतभीः ॥
data.md: Decked with numberless effulgent rays I used to pass through the skies incapable of being defeated by any creature and fearing none.

data.v: ऐश्वर्यं तपसा प्राप्तं भ्रष्टं तच्च स्वकर्मभिः । धृतिमास्थाय भगवन्न शोचामि ततस्त्वहम् ॥
data.md: I acquired great prosperity through my penenaces and lost it again through my own deeds. Depending on my fortitude, however, I do not grieve for this change.

data.v: युयुत्सता महेन्द्रेण पुरा सार्धं महात्मना । ततो मे भगवान्दृष्टो हरिर्नारायणः प्रभुः ॥
data.md: Desirous of fighting the great Indra, the great ruler of the celestial region, I beheld in that battle the illustrious Hari, the powerful Narayana, He who is called Vaikuntha, Purusha, Ananta, Shukla, Vishnu, Sanatana, Munjakesha, Harishmashru, and the Grandsire of all creatures.

data.v: वैकुण्ठः पुरुषो विष्णुः शुक्लोऽनन्तः सनातनः । मुञ्जकेशो हरिश्मश्रुः सर्वभूतपितामहः ॥
नूनं तु तस्य तपसः सावशेषं ममास्ति वै । यदहं प्रष्टुमिच्छामि भवन्तं कर्मणः फलम् ॥
data.md: Forsooth, there is still a residue of the rewards of that penance represented by a sight of the great Hari! On account of this unspent residue that I have become desirous of asking you, O illustrious one, about the fruits of action.

data.v: ऐश्वर्यं वै महद्ब्रह्मन्कस्मिन्वर्णे प्रतिष्ठितम् । निवर्तते चापि पुनः कथमैश्वर्यमुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Upon which order (of men) has been placed high Brahma prosperity? In what manner, again, does high prosperity fall off?

data.v: कस्माद्भूतानि जीवन्ति प्रवर्तन्तेऽथ वा पुनः । किं वा फलं परं प्राप्य जीवस्तिष्ठति शाश्वतः ॥
data.md: From whom do creatures originate and live? Through whom again do they act? What is that great Fruit by acquiring which a creature succeeds in living for good as Brahma?

data.v: केन वा कर्मणा शक्यमथ ज्ञानेन केन वा । ब्रह्मर्षे तत्फलं प्राप्तुं तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: By what Act or by what Knowledge can that fruit be acquired? You should, O learned Brahmana, expound these to me!

data.v: इतीदमुक्तः स मुनिस्तदानीं; प्रत्याह यत्तच्छृणु राजसिंह । मयोच्यमानं पुरुषर्षभ त्व;मनन्यचित्तः सह सोदरीयैः ॥
data.md: Described by me, O foremost of kings, listen, with rapt attention, O best of men, with all your brothers, to what the sage Ushanas then said after he had been thus addressed by that king of Danavas.

data.v: नमस्तस्मै भगवते देवाय प्रभविष्णवे । यस्य पृथ्वीतलं तात साकाशं बाहुगोचरम् ॥
data.md: Ushana said I bow to that divine and illustrious and powerful Being who holds this Earth with the sky in his arms.

data.v: मूर्धा यस्य त्वनन्तं च स्थानं दानवसत्तम । तस्याहं ते प्रवक्ष्यामि विष्णोर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: I shall speak to you of the pre-eminent greatness of that Vishnu whose head, O best of the Danavas, is that Infinite place.

data.v: तयोः संवदतोरेवमाजगाम महामुनिः । सनत्कुमारो धर्मात्मा संशयच्छेदनाय वै ॥
data.md: While they were thus talking with each other there came to them the great sage Sanatkumara of pious soul for the purpose of removing their doubts.

data.v: स पूजितोऽसुरेन्द्रेण मुनिनोशनसा तथा । निषसादासने राजन्महार्हे मुनिपुंगवः ॥
data.md: Adored of the king of Asuras and the sage Ushanas, that foremost of sages sat down on a rich seat.

data.v: तमासीनं महाप्राज्ञमुशना वाक्यमब्रवीत् । ब्रूह्यस्मै दानवेन्द्राय विष्णोर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: After the highly wise Kumara had been seated, Ushanas said to him,-Describe to this king of the Danavas the pre-eminent greatness of Vishnu.

data.v: सनत्कुमारस्तु ततः श्रुत्वा प्राह वचोऽर्थवत् । विष्णोर्माहात्म्यसंयुक्तं दानवेन्द्राय धीमते ॥
data.md: Hearing these words, Sanatkumara said to the following, fraught with grave sense, upon the pre-cminent greatness of Vishnu to the intelligent king of the Danavas.

data.v: शृणु सर्वमिदं दैत्य विष्णोर्माहात्म्यमुत्तमम् । विष्णौ जगत्स्थितं सर्वमिति विद्धि परंतप ॥
data.md: Listen, O Daitya, to everything regarding the greatness of Vishnu. Know, O destroyer of foes, that the entire universe depends on Vishnu.

data.v: सृजत्येष महाबाहो भूतग्रामं चराचरम् । एष चाक्षिपते काले काले विसृजते पुनः । अस्मिन्गच्छन्ति विलयमस्माच्च प्रभवन्त्युत ॥
data.md: O you of mighty arms, it is He who creates all creatures mobile and immobile. In course of Time it is He, again, who withdraws all things and in Time it is He who once more sends them from Himself.

data.v: नैष दानवता शक्यस्तपसा नैव चेज्यया । संप्राप्तुमिन्द्रियाणां तु संयमेनैव शक्यते ॥
data.md: Into Hari all things merge at the universal dissolution, and from Hiin all things again come forth. Men having scriptural learning cannot get him by such lore. Nor can He be acquired by Penances, nor by Sacrifices. The only means by which He can be acquired is by controlling the Senses.

data.v: बाह्ये चाभ्यन्तरे चैव कर्मणा मनसि स्थितः । निर्मलीकुरुते बुद्ध्या सोऽमुत्रानन्त्यमश्नुते ॥
data.md: Not that sacrifices are absolutely useless towards such an end. For a person, by relying upon both external and internal acts, and upon his own mind, can purify (them) by his own understanding. By such means, one can enjoy Infinity in the world.

data.v: यथा हिरण्यकर्ता वै रूप्यमग्नौ विशोधयेत् । बहुशोऽतिप्रयत्नेन महतात्मकृतेन ह ॥
