data.v: आकाशस्था ध्रुवं यत्र दोषं ब्रूयुर्विपश्चिताम् । आत्मपूजाभिकामा वै को वसेत्तत्र पण्डितः ॥
data.md: What learned man who cares for his respect will live there where people talk about the faults of the learned even when such have no foundations to stand upon?

data.v: यत्र संलोडिता लुब्धैः प्रायशो धर्मसेतवः । प्रदीप्तमिव शैलान्तं कस्तं देशं न संत्यजेत् ॥
data.md: Who is there that will not leave that place, like a garment whose end has caught fire, where covetous men tries to break down the limits of virtue?

data.v: यत्र धर्ममनाशङ्काश्चरेयुर्वीतमत्सराः । चरेत्तत्र वसेच्चैव पुण्यशीलेषु साधुषु ॥
data.md: One should remain and live in that place, among good men of pious disposition, where persons possessed of humility are engaged in fearlessly practising the duties of religion.

data.v: धर्ममर्थनिमित्तं तु चरेयुर्यत्र मानवाः । न ताननुवसेज्जातु ते हि पापकृतो जनाः ॥
data.md: One should not dwell there where men practise the duties of religion for the sake of wealth and other worldly purposes, for the people of that place are all to be considered as sinful.

data.v: कर्मणा यत्र पापेन वर्तन्ते जीवितेस्पवः । व्यवधावेत्ततस्तूर्णं ससर्पाच्छरणादिव ॥
data.md: One should fly away quickly from that place, as if from a room which there is a snake, where the inhabitants, desirous of acquiring the means of life, are engaged in the practice of sinful deeds.

data.v: येन खट्वां समारूढः कर्मणानुशयी भवेत् । आदितस्तन्न कर्तव्यमिच्छता भवमात्मनः ॥
data.md: One desirous of what is wholesome, should, from the beginning, avoid that act for which one becomes stretched, as it were, on a bed of thorns and for which one becomes invested with the desires born of the pristine deeds.

data.v: यत्र राजा च राज्ञश्च पुरुषाः प्रत्यनन्तराः । कुटुम्बिनामग्रभुजस्त्यजेत्तद्राष्ट्रमात्मवान् ॥
data.md: The pious man should leave that kingdom where the king and the king's officers exercise equal authority and where people eat before feeding their relatives.

data.v: श्रोत्रियास्त्वग्रभोक्तारो धर्मनित्याः सनातनाः । याजनाध्यापने युक्ता यत्र तद्राष्ट्रमावसेत् ॥
data.md: One should live in that country where Brahmanas having a knowledge of the scriptures are fed first; where they always practise religious duties, and where they are engaged in teaching disciples and officiating at the sacrifices of others.

data.v: स्वाहास्वधावषट्कारा यत्र सम्यगनुष्ठिताः । अजस्रं चैव वर्तन्ते वसेत्तत्राविचारयन् ॥
data.md: One should unhesitatingly live in that country where the sounds Svaha, Svadha, and Vashat are duly and continuously uttered.

data.v: अशुचीन्यत्र पश्येत ब्राह्मणान्वृत्तिकर्शितान् । त्यजेत्तद्राष्ट्रमासन्नमुपसृष्टमिवामिषम् ॥
data.md: One should leave that kingdom, like poisoned meat, where one sees Brahmanas compelled to follow unholy practices, by want of the means of life.

data.v: प्रीयमाणा नरा यत्र प्रयच्छेयुरयाचिताः । स्वस्थचित्तो वसेत्तत्र कृतकृत्य इवात्मवान् ॥
data.md: With a contented heart and considering all his wishes as already gratified, a pious man should live in that country whose denizens gladly give away before even they are asked.

data.v: दण्डो यत्राविनीतेषु सत्कारश्च कृतात्मसु । चरेत्तत्र वसेच्चैव पुण्यशीलेषु साधुषु ॥
data.md: One should remain and live in that place, among good men of pious disposition, where persons possessed of humility are engaged in fearlessly practising the duties of religion.

data.v: उपसृष्टेष्वदान्तेषु दुराचारेष्वसाधुषु । अविनीतेषु लुब्धेषु सुमहद्दण्डधारणम् ॥
यत्र राजा धर्मनित्यो राज्यं वै पर्युपासिता । अपास्य कामान्कामेशो वसेत्तत्राविचारयन् ॥
तथाशीला हि राजानः सर्वान्विषयवासिनः । श्रेयसा योजयन्त्याशु श्रेयसि प्रत्युपस्थिते ॥
data.md: Kings endued with such a disposition, secure the prosperity of those who live in their kingdoms when prosperity is on the point of leaving them.

data.v: पृच्छतस्ते मया तात श्रेय एतदुदाहृतम् । न हि शक्यं प्रधानेन श्रेयः संख्यातुमात्मनः ॥
data.md: I have thus told you, O son, in answer to you enquiry, what is beneficial or excellent. No one can describe, on account of its exceedingly high character, what is beneficial or excellent for the Soul.

data.v: एवं प्रवर्तमानस्य वृत्तिं प्रणिहितात्मनः । तपसैवेह बहुलं श्रेयो व्यक्तं भविष्यति ॥
data.md: Many and high will the excellences be, through the performance of the duties laid down for his, of the man who for earning his livelihood during the time of his stay in this world, acts in the way indicated above and who devotes his soul to the well-being of creatures.

data.v: कथं नु मुक्तः पृथिवीं चरेदस्मद्विधो नृपः । नित्यं कैश्च गुणैर्युक्तः सङ्गपाशाद्विमुच्यते ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said How, O grandfather, should a king like us act in this world, keeping in view the great object of acquisition? What attributes, again, should he always possess so that he may be liberated from attachments.

data.v: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि इतिहासं पुरातनम् । अरिष्टनेमिना प्रोक्तं सगरायानुपृच्छते ॥
data.md: Bhishma said-I shall in this connection recite to you the old narrative that was uttered by Arishtanemi to Sagara who had sought his advice.

data.v: किं श्रेयः परमं ब्रह्मन्कृत्वेह सुखमश्नुते । कथं न शोचेन्न क्षुभ्येदेतदिच्छामि वेदितुम् ॥
data.md: Sagara said What is that good, O Brahmana, by doing which one may enjoy happiness here? How, indeed, may one avoid grief and agitation? I wish to know all this.

data.v: एवमुक्तस्तदा तार्क्ष्यः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः । विबुध्य संपदं चाग्र्यां सद्वाक्यमिदमब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Thus addressed by Sagara, Arishtanemi of Tarkshya's race, conversant with all the scriptures, considering the enquiries ad deserving fully of his instructions, said these words:सुखं मोक्षसुखं लोके न च मूढोऽवगच्छति।

data.v: सुखं मोक्षसुखं लोके न च लोकोऽवगच्छति । प्रसक्तः पुत्रपशुषु धनधान्यसमाकुलः ॥
data.md: The happiness of Liberation is true happiness in the world. The ignorant man knows is not, attached, as he is, to children and animals and possessed of riches and corn.

data.v: सक्तबुद्धिरशान्तात्मा न स शक्यश्चिकित्सितुम् । स्नेहपाशसितो मूढो न स मोक्षाय कल्पते ॥
data.md: The understanding that is attached to worldly objects and the longing mind baffle all skilful treatment. The ignorant man who is bound is the fetters of affection cannot acquire Liberation.

data.v: स्नेहजानिह ते पाशान्वक्ष्यामि शृणु तान्मम । सकर्णकेन शिरसा शक्याश्छेत्तुं विजानता ॥
data.md: I shall now describe to you all the fetters which originate from the affections. Hear them with attention. Indeed, they can be heard with profit by one who is endued with knowledge.

data.v: संभाव्य पुत्रान्कालेन यौवनस्थान्निवेश्य च । समर्थाञ्जीवने ज्ञात्वा मुक्तश्चर यथासुखम् ॥
data.md: Having procreated children in due time and married them when they become young men, and having found them to be competent for earning their livelihood, do you free youself from all attachments and rove about happily.

data.v: भार्यां पुत्रवतीं वृद्धां लालितां पुत्रवत्सलाम् । ज्ञात्वा प्रजहि काले त्वं परार्थमनुदृश्य च ॥
data.md: When you find you dear consort grown old in years and attached to the son she has given birth to, do you leave her in time, keeping in view the highest object of acquisition.

data.v: सापत्यो निरपत्यो वा मुक्तश्चर यथासुखम् । इन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियार्थांस्त्वमनुभूय यथाविधि ॥
data.md: Whether you get a son or not, having, during the first years of your life, duly enjoyed with your senses the objects thereof, liberate yourself from attachments and rove about in happiness.

data.v: कृतकौतूहलस्तेषु मुक्तश्चर यथासुखम् । उपपत्त्योपलब्धेषु लाभेषु च समो भव ॥
data.md: Having satisfied the senses with their objects, you should suppress the desire of further indulging them. Liberating yourself from attachments, you should rove in happiness, contenting yourself with what is got without exertion and previous calculation, and loO king impartially towards all creatures and objects.

data.v: एष तावत्समासेन तव संकीर्तितो मया । मोक्षार्थो विस्तरेणापि भूयो वक्ष्यामि तच्छृणु ॥
data.md: Thus, O son, have I told you briefly. Hear me now, for I shall tell you fully, the desirability of the acquisition of Liberation.

data.v: मुक्ता वीतभया लोके चरन्ति सुखिनो नराः । सक्तभावा विनश्यन्ति नरास्तत्र न संशयः ॥
data.md: Those persons who live in this world shorn of attachments and fear, succeed in acquiring happiness. Those persons, however, who are attached to worldly objects, forsooth, meet with destruction,

data.v: आहारसंचयाश्चैव तथा कीटपिपीलिकाः । असक्ताः सुखिनो लोके सक्ताश्चैव विनाशिनः ॥
data.md: Worms and ants are engaged in the acquisition of food and are seen to die in the search. They who are shorn or attachments are happy, while they who are attached to worldly objects meet with destruction.

data.v: स्वजने न च ते चिन्ता कर्तव्या मोक्षबुद्धिना । इमे मया विनाभूता भविष्यन्ति कथं त्विति ॥
data.md: If you wish to acquire Liberation you should never place your thoughts on your relatives, thinking, How shall these live without me?

data.v: स्वयमुत्पद्यते जन्तुः स्वयमेव विवर्धते । सुखदुःखे तथा मृत्युं स्वयमेवाधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: A living creature takes birth by himself, and, grow by himself, and acquires happiness and misery, and death by himself.

data.v: भोजनाच्छादने चैव मात्रा पित्रा च संग्रहम् । स्वकृतेनाधिगच्छन्ति लोके नास्त्यकृतं पुरा ॥
data.md: In this world people enjoy and obtain good and cloth and other acquisitions acquired by either their parents or themselves. This is the result of the acts of pristine lives, for nothing can be had in this life which is not the result of the past.

data.v: धात्रा विहितभक्ष्याणि सर्वभूतानि मेदिनीम् । लोके विपरिधावन्ति रक्षितानि स्वकर्मभिः ॥
data.md: All creatures live on the Earth, protected by their own acts, and acquiring their food as the result of what is ordained by Him who allots the fruits of acts.

data.v: स्वयं मृत्पिण्डभूतस्य परतन्त्रस्य सर्वदा । को हेतुः स्वजनं पोष्टुं रक्षितुं वादृढात्मनः ॥
data.md: A man is but a lump of clay, and always depends completely on their forces. A man, being thus so weak, what rational motive can one have for protecting and feeding his relatives?

data.v: स्वजनं हि यदा मृत्युर्हन्त्येव तव पश्यतः । कृतेऽपि यत्ने महति तत्र बोद्धव्यमात्मना ॥
data.md: When your relatives are carried away by Death in your very presence and despite you utmost efforts to save them, that circumstance alone should awaken you.

data.v: जीवन्तमपि चैवैनं भरणे रक्षणे तथा । असमाप्ते परित्यज्य पश्चादपि मरिष्यसि ॥
data.md: In the very life-time of your relatives and before own duty is completed of feeding and protecting them, you may yourself die and leave them.

data.v: यदा मृतश्च स्वजनं न ज्ञास्यसि कथंचन । सुखितं दुःखितं वापि ननु बोद्धव्यमात्मना ॥
data.md: After your relatives have been carried away from this world by death, you cannot know what becomes of them there,—that is, whether they are happy or miserable. This fact ought to awaken you.

data.v: मृते वा त्वयि जीवे वा यदि भोक्ष्यति वै जनः । स्वकृतं ननु बुद्ध्वैवं कर्तव्यं हितमात्मनः ॥
data.md: When on account of the fruits of their own acts your relatives can maintain themselves in this world whether you live or die, thinking of this you should do what is for your own wellbeing.

data.v: एवं विजानँल्लोकेऽस्मिन्कः कस्येत्यभिनिश्चितः । मोक्षे निवेशय मनो भूयश्चाप्युपधारय ॥
data.md: When such is the case, who is the world is to be considered as whose? Do you, therefore, think of acquiring Liberation. Hear now what more I shall say to you.

data.v: क्षुत्पिपासादयो भावा जिता यस्येह देहिनः । क्रोधो लोभस्तथा मोहः सत्त्ववान्मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: That man of firm Soul, forsooth, liberated who has conquered hunger and thirst and such other states of the body, as also anger and cupidity and error.

data.v: द्यूते पाने तथा स्त्रीषु मृगयायां च यो नरः । न प्रमाद्यति संमोहात्सततं मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: That man is always liberated who does not forget himself, through folly, by indulging in gambling and drinking and concubinage and the chase.

data.v: दिवसे दिवसे नाम रात्रौ रात्रौ सदा सदा । भोक्तव्यमिति यः खिन्नो दोषबुद्धिः स उच्यते ॥
data.md: That man who is really affected by sorrow for being compelled to eat every day and every night for maintaining life, is said to be congnisant of the faults of life.

data.v: आत्मभावं तथा स्त्रीषु मुक्तमेव पुनः पुनः । यः पश्यति सदा युक्तो यथावन्मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: Once who, as the outcome of careful reflection, considers his repeated births as due to sexual congress with women, is held to be freed from attachments.

data.v: संभवं च विनाशं च भूतानां चेष्टितं तथा । यस्तत्त्वतो विजानाति लोकेऽस्मिन्मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: That man is certainly Liberated who knows truly the nature of the birth, the destruction, and the acts of living creatures.

data.v: प्रस्थं वाहसहस्रेषु यात्रार्थं चैव कोटिषु । प्रासादे मञ्चकस्थानं यः पश्यति स मुच्यते ॥
data.md: That man becomes certainly freed who seeks only a handful of corn, for the support of life, from amidst millions upon millions of carts loaded with gain, and who finds no difference between a shad of bamboo and reeds and a palace.

data.v: मृत्युनाभ्याहतं लोकं व्याधिभिश्चोपपीडितम् । अवृत्तिकर्शितं चैव यः पश्यति स मुच्यते ॥
data.md: That man becomes certainly freed who seeks the world as afflicted by death, disease and famine.

data.v: यः पश्यति सुखी तुष्टो नपश्यंश्च विहन्यते । यश्चाप्यल्पेन संतुष्टो लोकेऽस्मिन्मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: Indeed, one who sees the world to consist of eaters and edibles, and who is never affected by pleasure and pain begotten by illusion, is considered as liberated.

data.v: अग्नीषोमाविदं सर्वमिति यश्चानुपश्यति । न च संस्पृश्यते भावैरद्भुतैर्मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: One, who sees all the objects in the form of Fire and Soma, he is never affected by wonderful pleasures and is considered as liberated.

data.v: पर्यङ्कशय्या भूमिश्च समाने यस्य देहिनः । शालयश्च कदन्नं च यस्य स्यान्मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: That man who considers a soft bed on a fine bed-stead and the hard ground as equal, and who considers good shali rice and hard thick rice as equal, is liberated.

data.v: क्षौमं च कुशचीरं च कौशेयं वल्कलानि च । आविकं चर्म च समं यस्य स्यान्मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: That man who considers linen and cloth made of grass as equal, and who considers cloth of silk and barks of trees as the same, and who sees no difference between cleans sheepskin and unclean leather, is liberated.

data.v: पञ्चभूतसमुद्भूतं लोकं यश्चानुपश्यति । तथा च वर्तते दृष्ट्वा लोकेऽस्मिन्मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: That man who considers this world as the result of the combination of the five principal elements, and who acts in this world, keeping this notion foremost, is liberated.

data.v: सुखदुःखे समे यस्य लाभालाभौ जयाजयौ । इच्छाद्वेषौ भयोद्वेगौ सर्वथा मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: That man who considers pleasure and pain in the same light and gain and loss as equal, and victory and defeat as the same to whom like and dislike are the same, and who is unmoved under fear and anxiety, is perfectly liberated.

data.v: रक्तमूत्रपुरीषाणां दोषाणां संचयं तथा । शरीरं दोषबहुलं दृष्ट्वा चेदं विमुच्यते ॥
data.md: That man who considers his body which had so many inperfections, to be only a mass of blood, urine and excreta, as also of disorders and diseases, is liberated,

data.v: वलीपलितसंयोगं कार्श्यं वैवर्ण्यमेव च । कुब्जभावं च जरया यः पश्यति स मुच्यते ॥
data.md: That man becomes liberated who always recollects that this body, when possessed by decrepitude, becomes assailed by wrinkless and white hairs and leanness and paleness of complexion and a bending of the form.

data.v: पुंस्त्वोपघातं कालेन दर्शनोपरमं तथा । बाधिर्यं प्राणमन्दत्वं यः पश्यति स मुच्यते ॥
data.md: That man who considers his body as subject to loss of power, weakness of sight, deafness, and loss of strength, is liberated.

data.v: गतानृषींस्तथा देवानसुरांश्च तथा गतान् । लोकादस्मात्परं लोकं यः पश्यति स मुच्यते ॥
data.md: That man who knows that the very Rishis, the gods, and the Asuras are beings that have to depart form their respective spheres to other regions, is liberated.

data.v: प्रभावैरन्वितास्तैस्तैः पार्थिवेन्द्राः सहस्रशः । ये गताः पृथिवीं त्यक्त्वा इति ज्ञात्वा विमुच्यते ॥
data.md: That man who knows that thousands of kings possessed of even great power have dies, succeeds in becoming liberated.

data.v: अर्थांश्च दुर्लभाँल्लोके क्लेशांश्च सुलभांस्तथा । दुःखं चैव कुटुम्बार्थे यः पश्यति स मुच्यते ॥
data.md: That man who knows that in this world the acquisition of objects is always hard, that pain of profuse, and that the maintenance of relative is always painful becomes liberated.

data.v: अपत्यानां च वैगुण्यं जनं विगुणमेव च । पश्यन्भूयिष्ठशो लोके को मोक्षं नाभिपूजयेत् ॥
data.md: Seeing the abundant faults of children and of other men, who is there that would worship Liberation?

data.v: शास्त्राल्लोकाच्च यो बुद्धः सर्वं पश्यति मानवः । असारमिव मानुष्यं सर्वथा मुक्त एव सः ॥
data.md: That man who, enlightened by the scriptures and the experience of the world sees every human concern in this world to be unreal, becomes liberated.

data.v: एतच्छ्रुत्वा मम वचो भवांश्चरतु मुक्तवत् । गार्हस्थ्ये यदि ते मोक्षे कृता बुद्धिरविक्लवा ॥
data.md: Remembering these words of mine, do you act like one who has become liberated, whether it is a life of domesticity that you would lead or pursue Liberation without allowing your understanding to be confounded.

data.v: तत्तस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा सम्यक्स पृथिवीपतिः । मोक्षजैश्च गुणैर्युक्तः पालयामास च प्रजाः ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of his with attention, king Sagara, acquired those virtues which yield liberation and continued, with their help to rule his subjects.

data.v: तिष्ठते मे सदा तात कौतूहलमिदं हृदि । तदहं श्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तः कुरुपितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said This curiosity, O sire, is always living in my mind. O grandfather to the Kurus, I wish to hear everything about it form you!

data.v: कथं देवर्षिरुशना सदा काव्यो महामतिः । असुराणां प्रियकरः सुराणामप्रिये रतः ॥
data.md: Why was the celestial Rishi, the great Ushanas, called also Kavi, engaged in doing what was agreeable to the Asuras and disagreeable to the gods.

data.v: वर्धयामास तेजश्च किमर्थममितौजसाम् । नित्यं वैरनिबद्धाश्च दानवाः सुरसत्तमैः ॥
data.md: Why was he engaged in diminishing the energy of the gods? Why the Danavas always fought with the foremost of the gods.

data.v: कथं चाप्युशना प्राप शुक्रत्वममरद्युतिः । ऋद्धिं च स कथं प्राप्तः सर्वमेतद्ब्रवीहि मे ॥
data.md: Endued with the effulgence of an immortal, why did Ushanas obtain the name of Shukra? How also did he acquire such superior excellence? Tell me all about these things.

data.v: न याति च स तेजस्वी मध्येन नभसः कथम् । एतदिच्छामि विज्ञातुं निखिलेन पितामह ॥
data.md: Though highly energetic, why can he not go to the centre of the sky? I wish, O grandfather, to learn everything about all these matters.

data.v: शृणु राजन्नवहितः सर्वमेतद्यथातथम् । यथामति यथा चैतच्छ्रुतपूर्वं मयानघ ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Listen, O king, attentively to all this as it actually took place, O sinless one, I shall describe these masters to you as I have heard and understood them.

data.v: एष भार्गवदायादो मुनिः सत्यो दृढव्रतः । असुराणां प्रियकरो निमित्ते करुणात्मके ॥
data.md: O firm vows and respected by all, Ushanas, that descendant of Bhrigu's race, became engaged in doing what was disagreeable to the gods for some good cause.

data.v: इन्द्रोऽथ धनदो राजा यक्षरक्षोधिपः स च । प्रभविष्णुश्च कोशस्य जगतश्च तथा प्रभुः ॥
data.md: The royal Kuvera, the chief of the Yakshas and the Rakshas, is the lord of the wealth of Indra, that master of the universe.

data.v: तस्यात्मानमथाविश्य योगसिद्धो महामुनिः । रुद्ध्वा धनपतिं देवं योगेन हृतवान्वसु ॥
data.md: The great ascetic Ushanas, crowned with Yoga-success, entered the person of Kuvera, and depriving the lord of wealth of his liberty by means of Yoga, robbed him of all his riches.

data.v: हृते धने ततः शर्म न लेभे धनदस्तथा । आपन्नमन्युः संविग्नः सोऽभ्यगात्सुरसत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Seeing his riches taken away from him, the lord of wealth became highly displeased. Filled anxiety, and his anger also being worked up, he want to that foremost of god, viz., Mahadeva.

data.v: निवेदयामास तदा शिवायामिततेजसे । देवश्रेष्ठाय रुद्राय सौम्याय बहुरूपिणे ॥
data.md: Kuvera reported the matter to Shiva of great energy, that first of gods, fierce and amiable, and endued with various forms.

data.v: योगात्मकेनोशनसा रुद्ध्वा मम हृतं वसु । योगेनात्मगतिं कृत्वा निःसृतश्च महातपाः ॥
data.md: He said Ushanas, having spiritualised himself by Yoga, entered my body and depriving myself of liberty, has taken away all my riches. Having by Yoga entered my body he has again left it.

data.v: एतच्छ्रुत्वा ततः क्रुद्धो महायोगी महेश्वरः । संरक्तनयनो राजञ्शूलमादाय तस्थिवान् ॥
data.md: Hearing these words, Maheshvara of Supreme Yoga-powers became filled with ire. His eyes, O king, became blood-red, and taking up his lance he waited.

data.v: क्वास्वौ क्वासाविति प्राह गृहीत्वा परमायुधम् । उशना दूरतस्तस्य बभौ ज्ञात्वा चिकीर्षितम् ॥
data.md: Having taken up that foremost of weapons, the great god began to say, Where is he? Where is he?—Meanwhile, Ushanas, having learnt the purpose of Mahadeva from a distance, waited silently.

data.v: स महायोगिनो बुद्ध्वा तं रोषं वै महात्मनः । गतिमागमनं वेत्ति स्थानं वेत्ति ततः प्रभुः ॥
data.md: Having learnt the fact of the anger of the great Maheshvara of superior Yoga-power, the powerful Ushanas began to think as to whether he should go to Maheshvara or fly away or remain where he was.

data.v: संचिन्त्योग्रेण तपसा महात्मानं महेश्वरम् । उशना योगसिद्धात्मा शूलाग्रे प्रत्यदृश्यत ॥
data.md: Thinking, with the help of his severe penances, of the great Mahadeva, Ushanas, of soul crowned with Yoga-success, put himself on the point of Mahadeva's lance.

data.v: विज्ञातरूपः स तदा तपःसिद्धेन धन्विना । ज्ञात्वा शूलं च देवेशः पाणिना समनामयत् ॥
data.md: Understanding that Ushanas, whose penances had been crowned with success and who had converted himself into the from of pure Knowledge, was staying at the point of his lance, the bow-armed Rudra, bent that weapon with his hand.

data.v: आनतेनाथ शूलेन पाणिनामिततेजसा । पिनाकमिति चोवाच शूलमुग्रायुधः प्रभुः ॥
data.md: When the fierce-armed and powerful Mahadeva of great energy had thus bent his lance that weapon came to be called from that time by the name of Pinaka.

data.v: पाणिमध्यगतं दृष्ट्वा भार्गवं तमुमापतिः । आस्यं विवृत्य ककुदी पाणिं संप्राक्षिपच्छनैः ॥
data.md: The lord of Uma, seeing Bhargava thus brought upon the palm of his hand, opened his mouth. The chief of the gods then threw Bhargava into his mouth and swallowed him up.

data.v: स तु प्रविष्ट उशना कोष्ठं माहेश्वरं प्रभुः । व्यचरच्चापि तत्रासौ महात्मा भृगुनन्दनः ॥
data.md: The powerful and great Ushanas of Bhrigu's race, entering the stomach of Maheshvara, began to wander there.

data.v: किमर्थं व्यचरद्राजन्नुशना तस्य धीमतः । जठरे देवदेवस्य किं चाकार्षीन्महाद्युतिः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said How, O king, could Ushanas wander within the stomach of that foremost (god) of superior intelligence? What also did that great god do while the Brahmana was within his stomach.

data.v: पुरा सोऽन्तर्जलगतः स्थाणुभूतो महाव्रतः । वर्षाणामभवद्राजन्प्रयुतान्यर्बुदानि च ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Then Mahadeva of severe vows, entered the water and remained there like an immovable wooden stake, O king, for millions of years.

data.v: उदतिष्ठत्तपस्तप्त्वा दुश्चरं स महाह्रदात् । ततो देवातिदेवस्तं ब्रह्मा समुपसर्पत ॥
data.md: His Yoga penances of the austerest type having been over, he rose from the great lake. Then that prime god of the gods, viz., the eternal Brahman, approached him, and enquired after the progress of his penances and well-being. The god having the bull for his emblem answered, saying,—My penances have been well practised.

data.v: तपोवृद्धिमपृच्छच्च कुशलं चैनमव्ययम् । तपः सुचीर्णमिति च प्रोवाच वृषभध्वजः ॥
तत्संयोगेन वृद्धिं चाप्यपश्यत्स तु शंकरः । महामतिरचिन्त्यात्मा सत्यधर्मरतः सदा ॥
data.md: Of inconceivable soul, endued with great intelligence, and ever devoted to the religion of truth, Shankara saw that Ushanas within his stomach had become greater on account of those penances of his.

data.v: स तेनाढ्यो महायोगी तपसा च धनेन च । व्यराजत महाराज त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान् ॥
data.md: That foremost of Yogins. (viz., Ushanas), rich with that wealth of penances and the wealth (of Kuvera), shone brightly in the three worlds, gifted with great energy.

data.v: ततः पिनाकी योगात्मा ध्यानयोगं समाविशत् । उशना तु समुद्विग्नो निलिल्ये जठरे ततः ॥
data.md: After this, Mahadeva armed with Pinaka, that soul of Yoga, once more began to roam within the stomach of the great god.

data.v: तुष्टाव च महायोगी देवं तत्रस्थ एव च । निःसारं काङ्क्षमाणस्तु तेजसा प्रत्यहन्यत ॥
data.md: The great ascetic began to sing the praises of the god from where he was desirous of finding on outlet for escape. But, having stopped all his outlets, Rudra, prevented him from coming out.

data.v: उशना तु तदोवाच जठरस्थो महामुनिः । प्रसादं मे कुरुष्वेति पुनः पुनररिंदम ॥
data.md: The great ascetic Ushanas, however, O chastiser of enemies, from within Mahadeva's stomach repeatedly addressed the god, saying,-Show me your kindness.

data.v: तमुवाच महादेवो गच्छ शिश्नेन मोक्षणम् । इति स्रोतांसि सर्वाणि रुद्ध्वा त्रिदशपुंगवः ॥
data.md: To him Mahadeva said,-Go out through my urethra!-He had closed up all other outlets of his body.

data.v: अपश्यमानः स द्वारं सर्वतःपिहितो मुनिः । पर्यक्रामद्दह्यमान इतश्चेतश्च तेजसा ॥
data.md: Closed on all sides and unable to find out the outlet pointed out, the asetic began to roam hither and thither. burning all the while with Mahadeva's energy.

data.v: स विनिष्क्रम्य शिश्नेन शुक्रत्वमभिपेदिवान् । कार्येण तेन नभसो नागच्छत च मध्यतः ॥
data.md: At last he found the outlet and came out through it. On account of this incident he passed by the name of Shukra, and it is for this he also became unable to attain the central point of the sky.

data.v: निष्क्रान्तमथ तं दृष्ट्वा ज्वलन्तमिव तेजसा । भवो रोषसमाविष्टः शूलोद्यतकरः स्थितः ॥
data.md: Seeing him come out of his stomach and shining bringhtly with energy, Bhava filled with anger, stood with lance uplifted in his hand.

data.v: न्यवारयत तं देवी क्रुद्धं पशुपतिं पतिम् । पुत्रत्वमगमद्देव्या वारिते शंकरे च सः ॥
data.md: The goddess Uma then interposed and forbade the angry lord of all creatures, viz., her consort, to kill the Brahmana. And on account of Uma's having thus prevented her lord from fulfilling his purpose, the ascetic Ushanas became the son of the goddess.

data.v: हिंसनीयस्त्वया नैष मम पुत्रत्वमागतः । न हि देवोदरात्कश्चिन्निःसृतो नाशमर्छति ॥
data.md: The goddess said-This Brahmana no longer deserves to be killed by you. He has become my son. O god, one who comes out of your stomach does not deserve to be killed by you.

data.v: ततः प्रीतोऽभवद्देव्याः प्रहसंश्चेदमब्रवीत् । गच्छत्वेष यथाकाममिति राजन्पुनः पुनः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Pacified by these words of his wife, Bhava smiled and said repeatedly these words, O king, viz.,-Let this one go wherever he likes.

data.v: ततः प्रणम्य वरदं देवं देवीमुमां तथा । उशना प्राप तद्धीमान्गतिमिष्टां महामुनिः ॥
data.md: Bowing to the boon-giving Mahadeva and also to his wife the goddess Uma, the great ascetic Ushanas, gifted with superior intelligence, proceeded to the place he chose.

data.v: एतत्ते कथितं तात भार्गवस्य महात्मनः । चरितं भरतश्रेष्ठ यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥
data.md: I have thus described to you, O chief of the Bharatas, the story of the great Bhargava about which you had asked me.

data.v: अतः परं महाबाहो यच्छ्रेयस्तद्वदस्व मे । न तृप्याम्यमृतस्येव वचसस्ते पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said O you of great arms, tell me, after this, what is beneficial for us, O grandfather, I am never satiated with your words which seem to me like ambrosia.

data.v: किं कर्म पुरुषः कृत्वा शुभं पुरुषसत्तम । श्रेयः परमवाप्नोति प्रेत्य चेह च तद्वद ॥
data.md: What are those good acts, O best of men, by doing which a man succeeds in obtaining what is for his greatest good, both in the world, and in the next, O giver of boons.

data.v: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि यथा पूर्वं महायशाः । पराशरं महात्मानं पप्रच्छ जनको नृपः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said-Regarding it I shall describe to you what the celebrated king Janaka had enquired, in days of great Parashara.

data.v: किं श्रेयः सर्वभूतानामस्मिँल्लोके परत्र च । यद्भवेत्प्रतिपत्तव्यं तद्भवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे ॥
data.md: What is beneficial for all creatures both in this world and the next? Do you tell me what should be known by all about it.

data.v: ततः स तपसा युक्तः सर्वधर्मविधानवित् । नृपायानुग्रहमना मुनिर्वाक्यमथाब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Thus accosted Parashara, endued with great ascetic merit and conversant with the ordinances of every religion, said these words, desirous of favouring the king.

data.v: धर्म एव कृतः श्रेयानिह लोके परत्र च । तस्माद्धि परमं नास्ति यथा प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: Parashara said Virtue acquired by acts is of supreme benefit both in this world and the next. The sages of old have said that there is nothing higher than virtue.

data.v: प्रतिपद्य नरो धर्मं स्वर्गलोके महीयते । धर्मात्मकः कर्मविधिर्देहिनां नृपसत्तम । तस्मिन्नाश्रमिणः सन्तः स्वकर्माणीह कुर्वते ॥
data.md: By accomplishing the sacred duties a man becomes honoured in heaven. The virtue, again, of embodied creatures, O best of kings, consists in the ordinances on the subject of acts. All good men belonging to the several modes of life, fixing their faith on virtue, perform their respective duties.

data.v: चतुर्विधा हि लोकस्य यात्रा तात विधीयते । मर्त्या यत्रावतिष्ठन्ते सा च कामात्प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: Four modes of life, O child, have been laid down in this world. Wherever men live the means of maintenance come to them of themselves.

data.v: सुकृतासुकृतं कर्म निषेव्य विविधैः क्रमैः । दशार्धप्रविभक्तानां भूतानां बहुधा गतिः ॥
data.md: Doing by different means virtuous or sinful acts, living creatures, when dissolved into their five constituent elements, attain to various ends.

data.v: सौवर्णं राजतं वापि यथा भाण्डं निषिच्यते । तथा निषिच्यते जन्तुः पूर्वकर्मवशानुगः ॥
data.md: As vessels of white brass, when steeped in liquified gold or silver, get the hue of these metals, so a living creature, who is entirely dependant upon the acts of his pristine lives, takes his colour from the nature of those acts.

data.v: नाबीजाज्जायते किंचिन्नाकृत्वा सुखमेधते । सुकृती विन्दति सुखं प्राप्य देहक्षयं नरः ॥
data.md: Nothing can originate without a seed. No one can acquire happiness without having performed acts capable of bringing on happiness. When one's body is dissolved, he succeeds in acquiring happiness only on account of the good acts of pristine lives.

data.v: दैवं तात न पश्यामि नास्ति दैवस्य साधनम् । स्वभावतो हि संसिद्धा देवगन्धर्वदानवाः ॥
data.md: The sceptic argues, O child, saying,-I do not see that anything in this world is the result of destiny or the virtuous and sinful deeds of pristine lives. Inference cannot settle the existence or operation of destiny. The gods, the Gandharvas and the Danavas have become what they are on account of their own nature.

data.v: प्रेत्य जातिकृतं कर्म न स्मरन्ति सदा जनाः । ते वै तस्य फलप्राप्तौ कर्म चापि चतुर्विधम् ॥
data.md: People never recollect in their next lives the acts done by them in pristine ones. For explaining the acquisition of fruits in any particular life people seldom name the four sorts of acts alleged to have been performed in pristine lives.

data.v: लोकयात्राश्रयश्चैव शब्दो वेदाश्रयः कृतः । शान्त्यर्थं मनसस्तात नैतद्वृद्धानुशासनम् ॥
data.md: The declarations have the Vedas for their authority have been made for guiding the conduct of men in his world, and for tranquillizing the minds of men. These, O child, cannot represent the saying of truly wise men.

data.v: चक्षुषा मनसा वाचा कर्मणा च चतुर्विधम् । कुरुते यादृशं कर्म तादृशं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: This opinion is wrong. In sooth, one acquires the fruits of whatever among the four sorts of acts one does with the eye, the mind, the tongue, and muscles.

data.v: निरन्तरं च मिश्रं च फलते कर्म पार्थिव । कल्याणं यदि वा पापं न तु नाशोऽस्य विद्यते ॥
data.md: As the fruit of his acts, O king, a person, sometimes acquires happiness wholly, sometimes misery in the same way, and sometimes happiness and misery united together. Whether virtuous or sinful, acts are never destroyed.

data.v: कदाचित्सुकृतं तात कूटस्थमिव तिष्ठति । मज्जमानस्य संसारे यावद्दुःखाद्विमुच्यते ॥
data.md: Sometimes, 0 child, the happiness consequent on good acts remains concealed and covered in such a way that it does not shew itself in the case of the person who is sinking in life's ocean till his sorrows disappear.

data.v: ततो दुःखक्षयं कृत्वा सुकृतं कर्म सेवते । सुकृतक्षयाद्दुष्कृतं च तद्विद्धि मनुजाधिप ॥
data.md: After sorrow has been dissipated, one begins to enjoy (the fruits of) his good acts. And know, O king, that upon the exhaustion of the fruits of good deeds, those of sinful ones begain to throw themselves.

data.v: दमः क्षमा धृतिस्तेजः संतोषः सत्यवादिता । ह्रीरहिंसाव्यसनिता दाक्ष्यं चेति सुखावहाः ॥
data.md: Self-control, forgiveness, patience, energy, contentment, truthfulness, modesty, abstention from injury, freedom from the evil practices called Vyasana, and cleverness,—these yield happiness.

data.v: दुष्कृते सुकृते वापि न जन्तुरयतो भवेत् । नित्यं मनःसमाधाने प्रयतेत विचक्षणः ॥
data.md: No creature is perpetually subject to the fruits of his good or bad acts. The wise man should always try to collect and concentrate his mind.

data.v: नायं परस्य सुकृतं दुष्कृतं वापि सेवते । करोति यादृशं कर्म तादृशं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: One never has to enjoy or endure the good and bad deeds of another. Indeed, one enjoys and endures the fruits of only those acts that he does oneself.

data.v: सुखदुःखे समाधाय पुमानन्येन गच्छति । अन्येनैव जनः सर्वः संगतो यश्च पार्थिव ॥
data.md: The person who renounces both happiness and misery walks along a particular path. Those men, however, O king, who allow themselves to be attached to all worldly objects, walk along an entirely different path.

data.v: परेषां यदसूयेत न तत्कुर्यात्स्वयं नरः । यो ह्यसूयुस्तथायुक्तः सोऽवहासं नियच्छति ॥
data.md: A person should not himself do that act which, if done by another, will bring censure on him. Indeed, by doing an act that one censures in others, one meets with ridicule.

data.v: भीरू राजन्यो ब्राह्मणः सर्वभक्षो; वैश्योऽनीहावान्हीनवर्णोऽलसश्च । विद्वांश्चाशीलो वृत्तहीनः कुलीनः; सत्याद्भ्रष्टो ब्राह्मणः स्त्री च दुष्टा ॥
रागी मुक्तः पचमानोऽऽत्महेतो;र्मूर्खो वक्ता नृपहीनं च राष्ट्रम् । एते सर्वे शोच्यतां यान्ति राज;न्यश्चायुक्तः स्नेहहीनः प्रजासु ॥
मनोरथरथं प्राप्य इन्द्रियार्थहयं नरः । रश्मिभिर्ज्ञानसंभूतैर्यो गच्छति स बुद्धिमान् ॥
data.md: Parashara said That man, who, having got this car, viz., his body endued with mind, goes on, restraining with the reins of knowledge the horses of the objects of the senses, should certainly be considered as an intelligent one.

data.v: सेवाश्रितेन मनसा वृत्तिहीनस्य शस्यते । द्विजातिहस्तान्निर्वृत्ता न तु तुल्यात्परस्परम् ॥
data.md: The homage by a person whose mind depends on itself and who has renounced the means of livelihood, is worthy of high praise, that homage, namely, O twice born one, from one who has succeeded in getting over acts, but not acquired from the mutual discussion of men in the same state of progress.

data.v: आयुर्नसुलभं लब्ध्वा नावकर्षेद्विशां पते । उत्कर्षार्थं प्रयतते नरः पुण्येन कर्मणा ॥
data.md: Having got the allotted period of life, O king, with such difficulty, one should not diminish it. On other hand, man should always try, by righteous deeds, for his gradual advancement.

data.v: वर्णेभ्योऽपि परिभ्रष्टः स वै संमानमर्हति । न तु यः सत्क्रियां प्राप्य राजसं कर्म सेवते ॥
data.md: Among the six different colours that individual Soul attains at different periods of his existence, he who falls away from a superior colour deserves blame and censure. Hence, one who has acquired the result of good decds should act in such a way as to avoid all acts sullied by the quality of Darkness.

data.v: वर्णोत्कर्षमवाप्नोति नरः पुण्येन कर्मणा । दुर्लभं तमलब्धा हि हन्यात्पापेन कर्मणा ॥
data.md: Man attains to a superior colour by pious deeds. Unable to acquire a superior colour for such acquisition is highly difficult, a person, by doing sinful deeds only kills himself.

data.v: अज्ञानाद्धि कृतं पापं तपसैवाभिनिर्णुदेत् । पापं हि कर्म फलति पापमेव स्वयं कृतम् । तस्मात्पापं न सेवेत कर्म दुःखफलोदयम् ॥
data.md: All sinful deeds that are perpetrated unconsciously or in ignorance are destroyed by penances. A sinful deed, however, that is committed knowingly, yields much sorrow.

data.v: पापानुबन्धं यत्कर्म यद्यपि स्यान्महाफलम् । न तत्सेवेत मेधावी शुचिः कुसलिलं यथा ॥
data.md: The intelligent man would never do a sinful act even if it produce the greatest advantage, just as a person who is pure would never touch a Chandala.

data.v: किंकष्टमनुपश्यामि फलं पापस्य कर्मणः । प्रत्यापन्नस्य हि सतो नात्मा तावद्विरोचते ॥
data.md: How miserable is the fruit I behold of sinful deeds. Through sin the very vision of the sinner become perverse, and he mistakes his body and its unstable accompaniments for the soul.

data.v: प्रत्यापत्तिश्च यस्येह बालिशस्य न जायते । तस्यापि सुमहांस्तापः प्रस्थितस्योपजायते ॥
data.md: That foolish man who does not succeed in following Renunciation in this world becomes stricken with great grief when he goes to the next world.

data.v: विरक्तं शोध्यते वस्त्रं न तु कृष्णोपसंहितम् । प्रयत्नेन मनुष्येन्द्र पापमेवं निबोध मे ॥
data.md: An uncoloured cloth, when dirty, can be purified, but not a piece of cloth which is dyed with black; so, O king, listen to me with care, is it the case with sin.

data.v: स्वयं कृत्वा तु यः पापं शुभमेवानुतिष्ठति । प्रायश्चित्तं नरः कर्तुमुभयं सोऽश्नुते पृथक् ॥
data.md: That man who, having knowingly perpetrated a sin, acts righteously for expiating that sin, has to enjoy and endure the fruits of his good and bad deeds separately.

data.v: अज्ञानात्तु कृतां हिंसामहिंसा व्यपकर्षति । ब्राह्मणाः शास्त्रनिर्देशादित्याहुर्ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥
data.md: The Brahmavadins hold, under the authority of what has been sanctioned in the Vedas, that all acts of injury committed in ignorance are made good by virtuous acts.

data.v: तथा कामकृतं चास्य विहिंसैवापकर्षति । इत्याहुर्धर्मशास्त्रज्ञा ब्राह्मणा वेदपारगाः ॥
data.md: A sin, however, however, that is committed knowingly is never repaired by righteousness. Thus the twice-born Brahmavadins who are conversant with the scriptures of Brahman.

data.v: अहं तु तावत्पश्यामि कर्म यद्वर्तते कृतम् । गुणयुक्तं प्रकाशं च पापेनानुपसंहितम् ॥
data.md: But I hold that whatever acts are done, be they righteous or sinful, be they done knowingly or otherwise, they remain till their fruits are enjoyed or endured.

data.v: यथा सूक्ष्माणि कर्माणि फलन्तीह यथातथम् । बुद्धियुक्तानि तानीह कृतानि मनसा सह ॥
data.md: Whatever acts are done by the mind with full deliberation, yield, according to their grossness or subtility, fruits which are gross or subtile.

data.v: भवत्यल्पफलं कर्म सेवितं नित्यमुल्बणम् । अबुद्धिपूर्वं धर्मज्ञ कृतमुग्रेण कर्मणा ॥
data.md: Those acts, however, O you of righteous soul, which are fraught with great injury, if done in ignorance do, forsooth, produce consequences which lead to hell, with this difference that are disproportionate in point of gravity to the acts that produce them.

data.v: कृतानि यानि कर्माणि दैवतैर्मुनिभिस्तथा । नाचरेत्तानि धर्मात्मा श्रुत्वा चापि न कुत्सयेत् ॥
data.md: As to those acts of the gods or repeated ascctics, a pious man should never do their like or, informed to them, should never censure them.

data.v: संचिन्त्य मनसा राजन्विदित्वा शक्तिमात्मनः । करोति यः शुभं कर्म स वै भद्राणि पश्यति ॥
data.md: That man, who, reflecting with his mind, O king, and ascertaining his own ability, performs pious deeds, forsooth, acquires what is for his well-being.

data.v: नवे कपाले सलिलं संन्यस्तं हीयते यथा । नवेतरे तथाभावं प्राप्नोति सुखभावितम् ॥
सतोयेऽन्यत्तु यत्तोयं तस्मिन्नेव प्रसिच्यते । वृद्धे वृद्धिमवाप्नोति सलिले सलिलं यथा ॥
एवं कर्माणि यानीह बुद्धियुक्तानि भूपते । नसमानीह हीनानि तानि पुण्यतमान्यपि ॥
राज्ञा जेतव्याः सायुधाश्चोन्नताश्च; सम्यक्कर्तव्यं पालनं च प्रजानाम् । अग्निश्चेयो बहुभिश्चापि यज्ञै;रन्ते मध्ये वा वनमाश्रित्य स्थेयम् ॥
data.md: A king should subjugate his enemies and all who seek to assert their superiority, and he should properly rule and protect his subjects. One should ignite his sacred fires and pour libations on them in various sacrifices, and retiring into the woods in either his middle or old age, should live there.

data.v: दमान्वितः पुरुषो धर्मशीलो; भूतानि चात्मानमिवानुपश्येत् । गरीयसः पूजयेदात्मशक्त्या; सत्येन शीलेन सुखं नरेन्द्र ॥
data.md: Gifted with self-control, and possessed of righteous conduct, one should regard all creatures as his ownself. One should again respect his superiors. By the practice of truth and of good conduct, O king one is sure to acquire happiness.

data.v: कः कस्य चोपकुरुते कश्च कस्मै प्रयच्छति । प्राणी करोत्ययं कर्म सर्वमात्मार्थमात्मना ॥
data.md: Nobody in this world does good to another. Nobody makes gifts to others. All persons are seen to act for their own selves.

data.v: गौरवेण परित्यक्तं निःस्नेहं परिवर्जयेत् । सोदर्यं भ्रातरमपि किमुतान्यं पृथग्जनम् ॥
data.md: People are seen to abandon their very parents and their uterine brothers when these cease to love them. What need be said then of relatives of other grades.

data.v: विशिष्टस्य विशिष्टाच्च तुल्यौ दानप्रतिग्रहौ । तयोः पुण्यतरं दानं तद्द्विजस्य प्रयच्छतः ॥
data.md: Gifts a distinguished person and acceptance of the gifts made by a distinguished person both produce equal merit. Of these two acts, however, the making of a gift is superior to the acceptance thereof.

data.v: न्यायागतं धनं वर्णैर्न्यायेनैव विवर्धितम् । संरक्ष्यं यत्नमास्थाय धर्मार्थमिति निश्चयः ॥
data.md: to That wealth is gained by fair means and is multiplied by fair means, should be protected with care for the sake of acquiring virtue. This is an accepted truth.

data.v: न धर्मार्थी नृशंसेन कर्मणा धनमर्जयेत् । शक्तितः सर्वकार्याणि कुर्यान्नर्द्धिमनुस्मरेत् ॥
data.md: One desirous of gaining virtue, should never gain riches by means involving injury to others. One should perform his acts according to his power, without zealously seeking riches.

data.v: अपो हि प्रयतः शीतास्तापिता ज्वलनेन वा । शक्तितोऽतिथये दत्त्वा क्षुधार्तायाश्नुते फलम् ॥
data.md: By giving water, whether cold or heated by fire, with a devoted mind, to a (thirsty) guest, according to the best of his might, one acquires the merit of the act of giving food to a hungry man.

data.v: रन्तिदेवेन लोकेष्टा सिद्धिः प्राप्ता महात्मना । फलपत्रैरथो मूलैर्मुनीनर्चितवानसौ ॥
data.md: The great Rantideva acquired success in all the worlds by adoring the ascetics with offerings of only roots and fruits and leaves.

data.v: तैरेव फलपत्रैश्च स माठरमतोषयत् । तस्माल्लेभे परं स्थानं शैब्योऽपि पृथिवीपतिः ॥
data.md: The royal son of Shaivi also acquired the highest regions of happiness by having pleased the Son-god along with his companion with offerings of the same sort.

data.v: देवतातिथिभृत्येभ्यः पितृभ्योऽथात्मनस्तथा । ऋणवाञ्जायते मर्त्यस्तस्मादनृणतां व्रजेत् ॥
data.md: All men, by being born, become indebted to gods, guests, servants, Pitris, and their own selves. Every one should, therefore do his best for satisfying those debts.

data.v: स्वाध्यायेन महर्षिभ्यो देवेभ्यो यज्ञकर्मणा । पितृभ्यः श्राद्धदानेन नृणामभ्यर्चनेन च ॥
data.md: One frees oneself from his debt to the great Rishis by studying the Vedas. One satisfies his debts to the gods by celebrating sacrifices. By performing the rites of the Shraddha one satisfies the debts to the Pitris. One satisfies the debt to his fellow men by doing good to them. son son

data.v: वाचः शेषावहार्येण पालनेनात्मनोऽपि च । यथावद्भृत्यवर्गस्य चिकीर्षेद्धर्ममादितः ॥
data.md: One satisfies the debts he owns to one's own self by listening to Vedic recitations and reflecting on their meaning, by eating the remnants of sacrifices, and by supporting his body. One should duly perform all the acts, from the beginning, that he owes to his servants.

data.v: प्रयत्नेन च संसिद्धा धनैरपि विवर्जिताः । सम्यग्घुत्वा हुतवहं मुनयः सिद्धिमागताः ॥
data.md: Through shorn of wealth, men are seen to attain to success by great exertions. Ascetics by duly adoring the gods, and by duly pouring libations of clarified butter on the sacred fire, have been seen to acquire ascetic success.

data.v: विश्वामित्रस्य पुत्रत्वमृचीकतनयोऽगमत् । ऋग्भिः स्तुत्वा महाभागो देवान्वै यज्ञभागिनः ॥
data.md: Richika's became the of Vishvamitra. By worshipping the gods who have shares in sacrificial offerings, with Riches, (he acquired success in after life).

data.v: गतः शुक्रत्वमुशना देवदेवप्रसादनात् । देवीं स्तुत्वा तु गगने मोदते तेजसा वृतः ॥
data.md: Ushanas became Shukra by having pleased the god of gods. Indeed, by singing the praises of the goddess (Uma), he sports in the sky, in the great effulgence.

data.v: असितो देवलश्चैव तथा नारदपर्वतौ । कक्षीवाञ्जामदग्न्यश्च रामस्ताण्ड्यस्तथांशुमान् ॥
वसिष्ठो जमदग्निश्च विश्वामित्रोऽत्रिरेव च । भरद्वाजो हरिश्मश्रुः कुण्डधारः श्रुतश्रवाः ॥
एते महर्षयः स्तुत्वा विष्णुमृग्भिः समाहिताः । लेभिरे तपसा सिद्धिं प्रसादात्तस्य धीमतः ॥
अनर्हाश्चार्हतां प्राप्ताः सन्तः स्तुत्वा तमेव ह । न तु वृद्धिमिहान्विच्छेत्कर्म कृत्वा जुगुप्सितम् ॥
data.md: Many undeserving men, by worshipping that good god, won great distinction. One should not seek for advancement by committing any wicked or censurable deed.

data.v: येऽर्था धर्मेण ते सत्या येऽधर्मेण धिगस्तु तान् । धर्मं वै शाश्वतं लोके न जह्याद्धनकाङ्क्षया ॥
data.md: That wealth which acquired by fair means is true wealth. Fie on that wealth however, which is acquired by unfair means. Virtue is eternal. It should never, in this world, be renounced from desire of riches.

data.v: आहिताग्निर्हि धर्मात्मा यः स पुण्यकृदुत्तमः । वेदा हि सर्वे राजेन्द्र स्थितास्त्रिष्वग्निषु प्रभो ॥
data.md: That pious person who keeps his sacred fire and offers his daily adorations to the gods is considered as the foremost of righteous persons. All the Vedas, O foremost of kings, are established on the three sacred fires.

data.v: स चाप्यग्न्याहितो विप्रः क्रिया यस्य न हीयते । श्रेयो ह्यनाहिताग्नित्वमग्निहोत्रं न निष्क्रियम् ॥
data.md: That Brahmana is said to possess the sacred fire whose acts exist in full. It is better to at once leave off the sacred fire than to keep it, abstaining from acts.

data.v: अग्निरात्मा च माता च पिता जनयिता तथा । गुरुश्च नरशार्दूल परिचर्या यथातथम् ॥
data.md: The sacred fire, the mother, the father who has begotten, and the preceptor, O foremost men, should all be duly attended and served with humility.

data.v: मानं त्यक्त्वा यो नरो वृद्धसेवी; विद्वान्क्लीबः पश्यति प्रीतियोगात् । दाक्ष्येणाहीनो धर्मयुक्तो नदान्तो; लोकेऽस्मिन्वै पूज्यते सद्भिरार्यः ॥
data.md: That man, who, renouncing all feelings of pride, humbly attends upon and serves them who are venerable for age, who is endued with learning and shorn of lust, who regains all creatures equally with an eye of love, who nas no riches, who is righteous in his acts, and who is shorn of the desire of inflicting any kind of injury, that truly respectable man is adored in this world by the good and pious.

data.v: वृत्तिः सकाशाद्वर्णेभ्यस्त्रिभ्यो हीनस्य शोभना । प्रीत्योपनीता निर्दिष्टा धर्मिष्ठान्कुरुते सदा ॥
data.md: Parashara said The lowest order, it is proper, should derive their maintenance from the three other orders. Such service, rendered with love and respect, makes them pious.

data.v: वृत्तिश्चेन्नास्ति शूद्रस्य पितृपैतामही ध्रुवा । न वृत्तिं परतो मार्गेच्छुश्रूषां तु प्रयोजयेत् ॥
data.md: If the ancestors of any Shudra were not engaged in service, he should not still engage himself in any other occupation. Truly, he should take up service as his occupation.

data.v: सद्भिस्तु सह संसर्गः शोभते धर्मदर्शिभिः । नित्यं सर्वास्ववस्थासु नासद्भिरिति मे मतिः ॥
data.md: In my opinion, it is proper for them to mix under all circumstances, with good men devoted to virtue, but never with the wicked.

data.v: यथोदयगिरौ द्रव्यं संनिकर्षेण दीप्यते । तथा सत्संनिकर्षेण हीनवर्णोऽपि दीप्यते ॥
data.md: As in the Eastern hills, jewels and metals blaze with greater effulgence on account of their nearness to the Sun, so the lowest order shines on account of their association with the good.

data.v: यादृशेन हि वर्णेन भाव्यते शुक्लमम्बरम् । तादृशं कुरुते रूपमेतदेवमवैहि मे ॥
data.md: A piece of white cloth assumes that colour with which it is dyed. Such is the case with Shudras.

data.v: तस्माद्गुणेषु रज्येथा मा दोषेषु कदाचन । अनित्यमिह मर्त्यानां जीवितं हि चलाचलम् ॥
data.md: Therefore, one should also attach him to all good qualities but never to bad qualities. The life of human beings in this world is fickle and transitory.

data.v: सुखे वा यदि वा दुःखे वर्तमानो विचक्षणः । यश्चिनोति शुभान्येव स भद्राणीह पश्यति ॥
data.md: That wise man who, in happiness as also in misery, acquire only what is good, is considered as a true observer of the scriptures.

data.v: धर्मादपेतं यत्कर्म यद्यपि स्यान्महाफलम् । न तत्सेवेत मेधावी न तद्धितमिहोच्यते ॥
data.md: The intelligent man would never do a sinful act even if it produce the greatest advantage, just as a person who is pure would never touch a Chandala.

data.v: यो हृत्वा गोसहस्राणि नृपो दद्यादरक्षिता । स शब्दमात्रफलभाग्राजा भवति तस्करः ॥
data.md: That lawless king who, taking thousands of kine from their lawful owners, gives them away acquires on fruit save an empty sound. On the other hand, he cominits the sin of theft.

data.v: स्वयंभूरसृजच्चाग्रे धातारं लोकपूजितम् । धातासृजत्पुत्रमेकं प्रजानां धारणे रतम् ॥
data.md: The Self-create at first created the Being called Dhatri held in universal esteem. Dhatri created a son who was engaged in maintaining all the worlds.

data.v: तमर्चयित्वा वैश्यस्तु कुर्यादत्यर्थमृद्धिमत् । रक्षितव्यं तु राजन्यैरुपयोज्यं द्विजातिभिः ॥
data.md: Adoring that God, the Vaishya engages for the means of his support, in agriculture and the tending of cattle. The Kshatriyas should undertake the task of protecting all the other classes. The Brahmanas should only enjoy.

data.v: अजिह्मैरशठक्रोधैर्हव्यकव्यप्रयोक्तृभिः । शूद्रैर्निर्मार्जनं कार्यमेवं धर्मो न नश्यति ॥
data.md: As regards the Shudras, they should take up the task of humbly and honestly collecting together the articles that are to be offered in sacrifices, and in cleaning altars and other places where sacrifices are to be celebrated. If each order acts in this way, virtue would not suffer any decrease.

data.v: अप्रनष्टे ततो धर्मे भवन्ति सुखिताः प्रजाः । सुखेन तासां राजेन्द्र मोदन्ते दिवि देवताः ॥
data.md: If virtue is preserved in its full, all creatures inhabiting the Earth would be happy, Seeing the happiness of all creatures on Earth, the gods in heaven become filled with gladness.

data.v: तस्माद्यो रक्षति नृपः स धर्मेणाभिपूज्यते । अधीते चापि यो विप्रो वैश्यो यश्चार्जने रतः ॥
data.md: Hence, that king, who, according to the duties laid down for his order, protects the other classes, becomes worthy of respect. similarly, the Brahmana who is employed in studying the scriptures, the Vaishya who is engaged in acquiring riches, and the Shudra who is always engaged in serving the three other classes with rapt attention, become objects of reverence. By acting in other ways, O king, each order is said to deviate from virtue.

data.v: यश्च शुश्रूषते शूद्रः सततं नियतेन्द्रियः । अतोऽन्यथा मनुष्येन्द्र स्वधर्मात्परिहीयते ॥
data.md: Hence, that king, who, according to the duties laid down for his order, protects the other classes, becomes worthy of respect. similarly, the Brahmana who is employed in studying the scriptures, the Vaishya who is engaged in acquiring riches, and the Shudra who is always engaged in serving the three other classes with rapt attention, become objects of reverence. By acting in other ways, O king, each order is said to deviate from virtue.

data.v: प्राणसंतापनिर्दिष्टाः काकिण्योऽपि महाफलाः । न्यायेनोपार्जिता दत्ताः किमुतान्याः सहस्रशः ॥
data.md: Keeping aside gifts by thousands, even twenty cowries that one may give painfully, having acquired them righteously, will yield great benefit.

data.v: सत्कृत्य तु द्विजातिभ्यो यो ददाति नराधिप । यादृशं तादृशं नित्यमश्नाति फलमूर्जितम् ॥
data.md: Those persons, O king, who make gifts to Brahmanas after respecting them duly, reap excellent fruits proportionate to those gifts.

data.v: अभिगम्य दत्तं तुष्ट्या यद्धन्यमाहुरभिष्टुतम् । याचितेन तु यद्दत्तं तदाहुर्मध्यमं बुधाः ॥
data.md: The gift is highly valued which the donor inakes after seeking out the done and respecting him properly. That gift is middling which the donor makes upon being prayed for it.

data.v: अवज्ञया दीयते यत्तथैवाश्रद्धयापि च । तदाहुरधमं दानं मुनयः सत्यवादिनः ॥
data.md: That gift, however, which is made contemptuously and without any respect, is said to be very inferior. This is what the truthful sages say.

data.v: अतिक्रमे मज्जमानो विविधेन नरः सदा । तथा प्रयत्नं कुर्वीत यथा मुच्येत संशयात् ॥
data.md: While sinking in this ocean of life, man should always try to cross that ocean by various means. Indeed, he should so exert himself that he might be released from the fetters of this world.

data.v: दमेन शोभते विप्रः क्षत्रियो विजयेन तु । धनेन वैश्यः शूद्रस्तु नित्यं दाक्ष्येण शोभते ॥
data.md: The Brahmana shines by self-control; the Kshatriya by victory; the Vaishya by riches; while the Shudra always shines in glory through clever serving.

data.v: प्रतिग्रहागता विप्रे क्षत्रिये शस्त्रनिर्जिताः । वैश्ये न्यायार्जिताश्चैव शूद्रे शुश्रूषयार्जिताः । स्वल्पाप्यर्थाः प्रशस्यन्ते धर्मस्यार्थे महाफलाः ॥
data.md: Parashara said In the Brahmana, wealth gained by acceptance of gifts, in the Kshatriya that acquired by victory in battle, in the Vaishya that acquired by performing the duties laid down for his order, and in the Shudra that acquired by serving the three other orders, however small it may be, is worthy of praise, and when spent for the acquisition of virtue yields great benefits. The Shudra is said to be the constant servitor of the three other orders.

data.v: नित्यं त्रयाणां वर्णानां शूद्रः शुश्रूषुरुच्यते । क्षत्रधर्मा वैश्यधर्मा नावृत्तिः पतति द्विजः । शूद्रकर्मा यदा तु स्यात्तदा पतति वै द्विजः ॥
data.md: If the Brahmana, when hard-pressed for a living, performs the duties of either the Kshatriya or the Vaishya, he does not fall off from virtue. When, however, the Brahmana performs the duties of the lowest order, then does he certainly fall off.

data.v: वाणिज्यं पाशुपाल्यं च तथा शिल्पोपजीवनम् । शूद्रस्यापि विधीयन्ते यदा वृत्तिर्न जायते ॥
data.md: When the Shudra is unable to secure his living by service of the three other orders, then it is lawful for him to follow trade, tending of cattle, and the practice of the mechanical arts.

data.v: रङ्गावतरणं चैव तथा रूपोपजीवनम् । मद्यमांसोपजीव्यं च विक्रयो लोहचर्मणोः ॥
data.md: Appearance on the stage and disguising oneself in various forms, exhibition of puppets, the sale of spirits and meat, and trading in iron and leather, should never be adopted for purposes of a living by one who had never before been engaged in those callings every one of which is regarded as censurable in the world. We have heard that if one engaged in them can renounce them, he acquires great merit.

data.v: अपूर्विणा न कर्तव्यं कर्म लोके विगर्हितम् । कृतपूर्विणस्तु त्यजतो महान्धर्म इति श्रुतिः ॥
संसिद्धः पुरुषो लोके यदाचरति पापकम् । मदेनाभिप्लुतमनास्तच्च नग्राह्यमुच्यते ॥
data.md: When one who has become successful in life acts sinfully on account of his mind being filled with pride, his acts under such circumstances can never pass for authority.

data.v: श्रूयन्ते हि पुराणे वै प्रजा धिग्दण्डशासनाः । दान्ता धर्मप्रधानाश्च न्यायधर्मानुवर्तकाः ॥
data.md: It is heard in the Puranas that formerly mankind were self-controlled, that they valued virtue greatly, that the practices they followed for livelihood were all agreeable to propriety and the injunctions laid down in the scriptures; and that the only punishment that was necessary for chastising them when they did wrong was merely the deprecation of their deeds.

data.v: धर्म एव सदा नॄणामिह राजन्प्रशस्यते । धर्मवृद्धा गुणानेव सेवन्ते हि नरा भुवि ॥
data.md: At the time of which we speak, O king, Virtue, and nothing else, was much praised among men. Having achieved great progress in virtue, men in those days adored only all good qualities that they saw.

data.v: तं धर्ममसुरास्तात नामृष्यन्त जनाधिप । विवर्धमानाः क्रमशस्तत्र तेऽन्वाविशन्प्रजाः ॥
data.md: The Asuras, however, O child, could not bear that virtue, which prevailed in the world. Multiplying the Asuras entered the bodies of inen.

data.v: तेषां दर्पः समभवत्प्रजानां धर्मनाशनः । दर्पात्मनां ततः क्रोधः पुनस्तेषामजायत ॥
data.md: Then was pride generated in men which is so destructive of virtue. From pride originated arrogance, and from arrogance originated anger.

data.v: ततः क्रोधाभिभूतानां वृत्तं लज्जासमन्वितम् । ह्रीश्चैवाप्यनशद्राजंस्ततो मोहो व्यजायत ॥
data.md: When men thus became overwhelmed with anger, modesty and shame disappeared from them, and then they were possessed by carelessness.

data.v: ततो मोहपरीतास्ते नापश्यन्त यथा पुरा । परस्परावमर्देन वर्तयन्ति यथासुखम् ॥
data.md: Afflicted by carelessness, they could no longer see as before, and as the consequence thereof they began to assail one another and thereby gain riches without any compunction.

data.v: तान्प्राप्य तु स धिग्दण्डो नकारणमतोऽभवत् । ततोऽभ्यगच्छन्देवांश्च ब्राह्मणांश्चावमन्य ह ॥
data.md: When men became such, the punishment of mere depreciation on transgressors could produce no effect. Men, showing no respect of either the gods or Brahmanas, began to indulge their senses to their fill.

data.v: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवा देववरं शिवम् । अगच्छञ्शरणं वीरं बहुरूपं गणाधिपम् ॥
data.md: At that time the gods repaired to that foremost of god, viz., Shiva, possessed of patience of multiform aspect and endued with the foremost of qualities and sought his protection.

data.v: तेन स्म ते गगनगाः सपुराः पातिताः क्षितौ । तिस्रोऽप्येकेन बाणेन देवाप्यायिततेजसा ॥
data.md: The gods gave him their conjoined energy, and thereupon the great god, with a single arrow killed on the Earth those three Asuras, viz., Desire, Anger, and Cupidity, who were staying in the sky, along with their very dwellers.

data.v: तेषामधिपतिस्त्वासीद्भीमो भीमपराक्रमः । देवतानां भयकरः स हतः शूलपाणिना ॥
data.md: The dreadful king those Asuras, endued with terrific prowess, who had struck the gods with terror, was also killed by Mahadeva armed with the lance.

data.v: तस्मिन्हतेऽथ स्वं भावं प्रत्यपद्यन्त मानवाः । प्रावर्तन्त च वेदा वै शास्त्राणि च यथा पुरा ॥
data.md: When this king of the Asuras was killed men once more gained their proper natures, and once more began to study the Vedas and the other scriptures as in days of yore.

data.v: ततोऽभ्यषिञ्चन्राज्येन देवानां दिवि वासवम् । सप्तर्षयश्चान्वयुञ्जन्नराणां दण्डधारणे ॥
data.md: Then the seven ancient Rishis came forward and installed Vasava as the king of the gods and the ruler of heaven. And they took upon themselves the task of holding the rod of punishment over mankind.

data.v: सप्तर्षीणामथोर्ध्वं च विपृथुर्नाम पार्थिवः । राजानः क्षत्रियाश्चैव मण्डलेषु पृथक्पृथक् ॥
data.md: After the seven Rishis came king Viprithu and many other kings, all belonging to the Kshatriya order for separately ruling separate classes of human beings.

data.v: महाकुलेषु ये जाता वृत्ताः पूर्वतराश्च ये । तेषामथासुरो भावो हृदयान्नापसर्पति ॥
data.md: There were, in those ancient times, certain clderly men from whose minds all wicked feelings did not disappear.

data.v: तस्मात्तेनैव भावेन सानुषङ्गेन पार्थिवाः । आसुराण्येव कर्माणि न्यषेवन्भीमविक्रमाः ॥
data.md: Hence, on account of that wicked state of their minds and of those incidents connected with it, there appeared many kings of dreadful prowess who began to perform only such acts as were fit for Asuras.

data.v: प्रत्यतिष्ठंश्च तेष्वेव तान्येव स्थापयन्ति च । भजन्ते तानि चाद्यापि ये बालिशतमा नराः ॥
data.md: Those human beings, who are very foolish follow those wicked acts, establish them as authorities, and practise them to this day.

data.v: तस्मादहं ब्रवीमि त्वां राजन्संचिन्त्य शास्त्रतः । संसिद्धाधिगमं कुर्यात्कर्म हिंसात्मकं त्यजेत् ॥
data.md: Therefore, O king, I say, you, have reflected properly with the help of the scriptures, that one should avoid all acts that are fraught with injury or malice and try to acquire a knowledge of the Soul.

data.v: न संकरेण द्रविणं विचिन्वीत विचक्षणः । धर्मार्थं न्यायमुत्सृज्य न तत्कल्याणमुच्यते ॥
data.md: The man endued with wisdom would not seek riches for the performance of religions rites by unfair and immoral ways. Wealth aquired by such means can never yield benefits.

data.v: स त्वमेवंविधो दान्तः क्षत्रियः प्रियबान्धवः । प्रजा भृत्यांश्च पुत्रांश्च स्वधर्मेणानुपालय ॥
data.md: Do you, then, become a Kshatriya of this kind! Do you restrain your senses, be kind to your friends, and cherish, according to the duties of your order, your subjects, servants, and children.

data.v: इष्टानिष्टसमायोगो वैरं सौहार्दमेव च । अथ जातिसहस्राणि बहूनि परिवर्तते ॥
data.md: Through the union of both prosperity and adversity, there arise friendships and enmities. Thousands and thousands of existences are continually revolving, and in every mode of individual Soul's existence these must take place.

data.v: तस्माद्गुणेषु रज्येथा मा दोषेषु कदाचन । निर्गुणो यो हि दुर्बुद्धिरात्मनः सोऽरिरुच्यते ॥
data.md: Therefore, be attached to good qualities of every sort, but never to faults. Such is the nature of good qualities that if the most foolish person, shorn of every virtue, hears himself praised for any good quality, he becomes filled with joy.

data.v: मानुषेषु महाराज धर्माधर्मौ प्रवर्ततः । न तथान्येषु भूतेषु मनुष्यरहितेष्विह ॥
data.md: Virtue and sin exist, O king, only among men. These do not exist among other creatures.

data.v: धर्मशीलो नरो विद्वानीहकोऽनीहकोऽपि वा । आत्मभूतः सदा लोके चरेद्भूतान्यहिंसयन् ॥
data.md: One should, therefore, whether in need of food and other necessaries of life or above such need, be of virtuous disposition, acquire knowledge, always consider all creatures as his own self, and abstain totally from inflicting any kind of injury.

data.v: यदा व्यपेतहृल्लेखं मनो भवति तस्य वै । नानृतं चैव भवति तदा कल्याणमृच्छति ॥
data.md: When one's mind becomes shorn of desire, and when all Darkness is removed from it, it is then that one acquires what is auspicious.

data.v: एष धर्मविधिस्तात गृहस्थस्य प्रकीर्तितः । तपोविधिं तु वक्ष्यामि तन्मे निगदतः शृणु ॥
data.md: Parashara said I have now described to you the ordained duties of a householder. I shall now describe to you the ordinances about penances. Hear me as I describe that subject.

data.v: प्रायेण हि गृहस्थस्य ममत्वं नाम जायते । सङ्गागतं नरश्रेष्ठ भावैस्तामसराजसैः ॥
data.md: It is generally seen, O king. that on account of sentiments fraught with Darkness and Ignorance, the senses of mine begotten by attachment, originates in the heart of householder.

data.v: गृहाण्याश्रित्य गावश्च क्षेत्राणि च धनानि च । दाराः पुत्राश्च भृत्याश्च भवन्तीह नरस्य वै ॥
data.md: Becoming a householder, one acquires kine, fields, wealth of diverse sorts, wives, children, and servants.

data.v: एवं तस्य प्रवृत्तस्य नित्यमेवानुपश्यतः । रागद्वेषौ विवर्धेते ह्यनित्यत्वमपश्यतः ॥
data.md: One who follows this mode of life continually casts his eye upon these objects. Under these circumstances, one's attachments and aversions multiply, and one ceases to consider unreal possessions as eternal and indestructible.

data.v: रागद्वेषाभिभूतं च नरं द्रव्यवशानुगम् । मोहजाता रतिर्नाम समुपैति नराधिप ॥
data.md: When a person becomes possessed by attachment and aversion, and gives way to the control of worldly objects, the desire of enjoyment then seizes him, originating from carelessness, O king.

data.v: कृतार्थो भोगतो भूत्वा स वै रतिपरायणः । लाभं ग्राम्यसुखादन्यं रतितो नानुपश्यति ॥
data.md: Considering that person as blessed who has the largest share of enjoyments in this world, the man devoted to enjoyment does not, on account of his attachment thereto, see that there is any other happiness save what depends upon the gratification of the senses.

data.v: ततो लोभाभिभूतात्मा सङ्गाद्वर्धयते जनम् । पुष्ट्यर्थं चैव तस्येह जनस्यार्थं चिकीर्षति ॥
data.md: Overwhelmed with cupidity that originates from such attachment, he then tries to multiply the number of his relatives and attendants, and for pleasing these latter he tries to increase his wealth by every means in his power.

data.v: स जानन्नपि चाकार्यमर्थार्थं सेवते नरः । बालस्नेहपरीतात्मा तत्क्षयाच्चानुतप्यते ॥
data.md: Filled with affection for children, such a person then commits, for the sake of acquiring riches, evil deeds, and yields to grief if his wealth belost.

data.v: ततो मानेन संपन्नो रक्षन्नात्मपराजयम् । करोति येन भोगी स्यामिति तस्माद्विनश्यति ॥
data.md: Having acquired honours and always guarding against the defeat of his plans, he follows such means as would satisfy his desire of enjoyment. At last he meets with destruction as the inevitable result of the conduct he follows.

data.v: तपो हि बुद्धियुक्तानां शाश्वतं ब्रह्मदर्शनम् । अन्विच्छतां शुभं कर्म नराणां त्यजतां सुखम् ॥
data.md: It is well known, however, that true happiness is theirs who are endued with intelligence, who are Brahmavadins, who try to perform only auspicious and beneficial acts, and who abstain from all acts which are optional and originate from desire only.

data.v: स्नेहायतननाशाच्च धननाशाच्च पार्थिव । आधिव्याधिप्रतापाच्च निर्वेदमुपगच्छति ॥
data.md: From loss of all such objects in which are centred our affections, from loss of riches, O king, and from the oppression of physical diseases and mental anguish a person falls into despair.

data.v: निर्वेदादात्मसंबोधः संबोधाच्छास्त्रदर्शनम् । शास्त्रार्थदर्शनाद्राजंस्तप एवानुपश्यति ॥
data.md: From this despair originates an awakening of the soul. From such an awakening proceeds study of the Scriptures. From contemplation of the meaning of the Scriptures, O king, one sees the value of penance.

data.v: दुर्लभो हि मनुष्येन्द्र नरः प्रत्यवमर्शवान् । यो वै प्रियसुखे क्षीणे तपः कर्तुं व्यवस्यति ॥
data.md: A person endued with the knowledge of what is essential and what accidental, O king, is very rare,-a man who tries to practise penances, under the conviction that the happiness one enjoys from the possession of such agreeable objects as wives and children brings on ultimately misery.

data.v: तपः सर्वगतं तात हीनस्यापि विधीयते । जितेन्द्रियस्य दान्तस्य स्वर्गमार्गप्रदेशकम् ॥
data.md: Penances, O child, are for all. They are ordained for even the lowest order of men, Penances lead the self-controlled man who has mastered all his senses to the way to heaven.

data.v: प्रजापतिः प्रजाः पूर्वमसृजत्तपसा विभुः । क्वचित्क्वचिद्व्रतपरो व्रतान्यास्थाय पार्थिव ॥
data.md: It was through penances that the powerful Lord of all creatures, O king, practising vows at particular intervals, created all existent objects.

data.v: आदित्या वसवो रुद्रास्तथैवाग्न्यश्विमारुताः । विश्वेदेवास्तथा साध्याः पितरोऽथ मरुद्गणाः ॥
data.md: The Aditya's, the Vasus, the Rudras, Agni, the Ashvins, the Maruts, the Vishvedevas, the Saddhyas, the Pitris, the Maruts, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the other Inhabitants of heaven, and indeed, all other celestials whatever, O child, have all become successful through their penances.

data.v: यक्षराक्षसगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्चान्ये दिवौकसः । संसिद्धास्तपसा तात ये चान्ये स्वर्गवासिनः ॥
data.md: The Aditya's, the Vasus, the Rudras, Agni, the Ashvins, the Maruts, the Vishvedevas, the Saddhyas, the Pitris, the Maruts, the Yakshas, the Rakshasas, the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the other Inhabitants of heaven, and indeed, all other celestials whatever, O child, have all become successful through their penances.

data.v: ये चादौ ब्रह्मणा सृष्टा ब्राह्मणास्तपसा पुरा । ते भावयन्तः पृथिवीं विचरन्ति दिवं तथा ॥
data.md: Those Brahmanas whom Brahman created at the beginning, succeeded through their penances in honouring not the Earth alone but the heaven also in which they moved about at pleasure.

data.v: मर्त्यलोके च राजानो ये चान्ये गृहमेधिनः । महाकुलेषु दृश्यन्ते तत्सर्वं तपसः फलम् ॥
data.md: In this world of men, they who are kings and those others who are householders born in high families, have all become what they are on account of their penances.,

data.v: कौशिकानि च वस्त्राणि शुभान्याभरणानि च । वाहनासनयानानि सर्वं तत्तपसः फलम् ॥
data.md: The silken dresses they put on the excellent ornaments that decorate their persons, the animals and vehicles they ride, and the seats they use are all the outcome of their penances.

data.v: मनोनुकूलाः प्रमदा रूपवत्यः सहस्रशः । वासः प्रासादपृष्ठे च तत्सर्वं तपसः फलम् ॥
data.md: Thousands of many charming and beautiful damsels, that they enjoy, and their residence in palaces, are all on account of their penances.

data.v: शयनानि च मुख्यानि भोज्यानि विविधानि च । अभिप्रेतानि सर्वाणि भवन्ति कृतकर्मणाम् ॥
data.md: The righteous persons enjoy various sorts of costly beds and sweet viands,

data.v: नाप्राप्यं तपसा किंचित्त्रैलोक्येऽस्मिन्परंतप । उपभोगपरित्यागः फलान्यकृतकर्मणाम् ॥
data.md: There is nothing in the three worlds, O scorcher of enemies, that penances cannot bring in. Even those who are shorn of true knowledge acquire Renunciation through their penances.

data.v: सुखितो दुःखितो वापि नरो लोभं परित्यजेत् । अवेक्ष्य मनसा शास्त्रं बुद्ध्या च नृपसत्तम ॥
data.md: Whether in rich circumstances or miserable, a person should renounce cupidity, meditating on the scriptures, with the help of his mind and understanding, O best of kings.

data.v: असंतोषोऽसुखायैव लोभादिन्द्रियविभ्रमः । ततोऽस्य नश्यति प्रज्ञा विद्येवाभ्यासवर्जिता ॥
data.md: Discontent produces misery. Cupidity brings on stupefaction of the senses. The senses being stupefied, one's wisdom is lost like knowledge not kept up by continued application.

data.v: नष्टप्रज्ञो यदा भवति तदा न्यायं न पश्यति । तस्मात्सुखक्षये प्राप्ते पुमानुग्रं तपश्चरेत् ॥
data.md: When one's wisdom is lost, he cannot discriminate what is proper from what is improper. Hence, when one's happiness is destroyed he should practise the austerest of penances.

data.v: यदिष्टं तत्सुखं प्राहुर्द्वेष्यं दुःखमिहोच्यते । कृताकृतस्य तपसः फलं पश्यस्व यादृशम् ॥
data.md: Wheat is agreeable is called happiness. What is disagreeable is called misery. Happiness is the outcome of penances practisted. When they are not practised, the outcome is misery. See the fruits of practising and abstaining from penances.

data.v: नित्यं भद्राणि पश्यन्ति विषयांश्चोपभुञ्जते । प्राकाश्यं चैव गच्छन्ति कृत्वा निष्कल्मषं तपः ॥
data.md: By practising pure penances, people always enjoy auspicious consequences of every sort, enjoy all good things, and acquire great fame.

data.v: अप्रियाण्यवमानांश्च दुःखं बहुविधात्मकम् । फलार्थी सत्पथत्यक्तः प्राप्नोति विषयात्मकम् ॥
data.md: He, however, who, by abandoning (pure penances), undertakes penances from desire of fruit, suffers from many disagreeable consequences, and disgrace and sorrow of all sorts, as the fruits thereof, all of which originate from worldly possessions.

data.v: धर्मे तपसि दाने च विचिकित्सास्य जायते । स कृत्वा पापकान्येव निरयं प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Despite the desirability of practising virtue, penances, and gifts, the desire for doing all sorts of forbidden acts originates in his mind. By thus perpetrating various sorts of sinful deeds, he goes to hell.

data.v: सुखे तु वर्तमानो वै दुःखे वापि नरोत्तम । स्ववृत्ताद्यो न चलति शास्त्रचक्षुः स मानवः ॥
data.md: That person, O best of men, who, in both happiness and misery, does deviate from the duties ordained for him, is said to have the scriptures for his eye.

data.v: इषुप्रपातमात्रं हि स्पर्शयोगे रतिः स्मृता । रसने दर्शने घ्राणे श्रवणे च विशां पते ॥
data.md: It is said that the pleasure one gets from the gratification of his senses of touch, tongue, sight, smell, and hearing, O king, lasts only so long as an arrow shot off the bow takes in falling down upon the Earth.

data.v: ततोऽस्य जायते तीव्रा वेदना तत्क्षयात्पुनः । बुधा येन प्रशंसन्ति मोक्षं सुखमनुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Upon the termination of the pleasure, which is fickle, on suffers the most acute pain. It is only the senseless that do not speak highly of happiness of Liberation which is peerless.

data.v: ततः फलार्थं चरति भवन्ति ज्यायसो गुणाः । धर्मवृत्त्या च सततं कामार्थाभ्यां न हीयते ॥
data.md: Seeing the misery consequent upon the gratification of the senses, the wise cultivate the virtues of tranquillity and self-control for the purpose of acquiring Liberation. On account of righteous conduct, riches and pleasure can never succeed in afflicting them.

data.v: अप्रयत्नागताः सेव्या गृहस्थैर्विषयाः सदा । प्रयत्नेनोपगम्यश्च स्वधर्म इति मे मतिः ॥
data.md: Householders may, without any compunction, enjoy riches and other possessions which are acquired with Exertion. About the duties of their order, I think, they should satisfy them with the help of Exertion.

data.v: मानिनां कुलजातानां नित्यं शास्त्रार्थचक्षुषाम् । धर्मक्रियावियुक्तानामशक्त्या संवृतात्मनाम् ॥
data.md: The practice of those who are honoured, who are born in high families, and who have their eyes always turned towards the meaning of the Scriptures, is incapable of being followed by those who are sinful and who have uncontrolled minds.

data.v: क्रियमाणं यदा कर्म नाशं गच्छति मानुषम् । तेषां नान्यदृते लोके तपसः कर्म विद्यते ॥
data.md: All acts that are done by man under the influence of pride, meet with destruction. Therefore, there is no other act, for the respectable and the truly righteous, in this world to do than penance.

data.v: सर्वात्मना तु कुर्वीत गृहस्थः कर्मनिश्चयम् । दाक्ष्येण हव्यकव्यार्थं स्वधर्मं विचरेन्नृप ॥
data.md: As regards, those householders, however, who are addicted to acts, they should, with their whole hearts, perform acts. Following the duties of their order, O king, they should with diligence and assiduity celebrate sacrifices and other religious rites.

data.v: यथा नदीनदाः सर्वे सागरे यान्ति संस्थितिम् । एवमाश्रमिणः सर्वे गृहस्थे यान्ति संस्थितिम् ॥
data.md: Indeed, as all rivers, male and female, go in the end to the Ocean, so men belonging to all the other orders have the householders for their refuge.

data.v: वर्णो विशेषवर्णानां महर्षे केन जायते । एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं तद्ब्रूहि वदतां वर ॥
data.md: Janaka said Whence, O great Rishi, does this difference of colour arise among men of the different orders? I wish to know this. Tell me this, O foreinost of speakers.

data.v: यदेतज्जायतेऽपत्यं स एवायमिति श्रुतिः । कथं ब्राह्मणतो जातो विशेषग्रहणं गतः ॥
data.md: The Shrutis say that the offspring one begets is his own self. Originally sprung from Brahman, all the inhabitants of the Earth should have been Brahmanas. Sprung from Brahmanas, why have men begun to perform works distinguished from those of Brahmanas.

data.v: एवमेतन्महाराज येन जातः स एव सः । तपसस्त्वपकर्षेण जातिग्रहणतां गतः ॥
सुक्षेत्राच्च सुबीजाच्च पुण्यो भवति संभवः । अतोऽन्यतरतो हीनादवरो नाम जायते ॥
data.md: Parashara said It is as you say, O king! The offspring begotten by one is none else than the begetter himself. Because men have deviated from penance, this distribution into classes of different colours has taken place. When the soil and the seed is good, the offspring produced become meritorious. If, however, the soil and seed are inferior, the offspring that will be born will be inferior.

data.v: वक्त्राद्भुजाभ्यामूरुभ्यां पद्भ्यां चैवाथ जज्ञिरे । सृजतः प्रजापतेर्लोकानिति धर्मविदो विदुः ॥
data.md: Persons well read in the scriptures know that when the Lord of all creatures began to create the worlds, some creatures originated from his mouth, some from his arms, some from his thighs, and some from his feet.

data.v: मुखजा ब्राह्मणास्तात बाहुजाः क्षत्रबन्धवः । ऊरुजा धनिनो राजन्पादजाः परिचारकाः ॥
data.md: Those who came out of his mouth, O child, were called Brahmanas. Those who originated from his arms were called Kshatriyas. Those, O king, sprang from his thighs, and some from his feet.

data.v: चतुर्णामेव वर्णानामागमः पुरुषर्षभ । अतोऽन्ये त्वतिरिक्ता ये ते वै संकरजाः स्मृताः ॥
data.md: Only these four orders of men, O king, were thus created. They who belong to classes besides these are said to have originated from an intermixture of these.

data.v: क्षत्रजातिरथाम्बष्ठा उग्रा वैदेहकास्तथा । श्वपाकाः पुल्कसाः स्तेना निषादाः सूतमागधाः ॥
data.md: The Kshatriyas called Atirathas, Amvashthas, Ugras, Vaidehas, Shvapakas, Pukasas, Stenas, Nishadas, Sutas, and Chandalas, O monarch, have all originated form the four original castes by intermixture with one another.

data.v: आयोगाः करणा व्रात्याश्चण्डालाश्च नराधिप । एते चतुर्भ्यो वर्णेभ्यो जायन्ते वै परस्परम् ॥
data.md: The Kshatriyas called Atirathas, Amvashthas, Ugras, Vaidehas, Shvapakas, Pukasas, Stenas, Nishadas, Sutas, and Chandalas, O monarch, have all originated form the four original castes by intermixture with one another.

data.v: ब्रह्मणैकेन जातानां नानात्वं गोत्रतः कथम् । बहूनीह हि लोके वै गोत्राणि मुनिसत्तम ॥
data.md: Janka said When all have originated from Brahman alone, how did human beings become divergent of race? O best of ascetics, numberless diversity of races is seen in this world.

data.v: यत्र तत्र कथं जाताः स्वयोनिं मुनयो गताः । शूद्रयोनौ समुत्पन्ना वियोनौ च तथापरे ॥
data.md: How could, men devoted to penances acquire the dignity of Brahmanas, though of indiscriminate origin? Indeed, those born in pure wombs and those in impure, all became Brahmanas.

data.v: राजन्नैतद्भवेद्ग्राह्यमपकृष्टेन जन्मना । महात्मनां समुत्पत्तिस्तपसा भावितात्मनाम् ॥
data.md: O king, that status of great persons who succeeded in purifying their souls by penances could not be regarded as affected by their low births.

data.v: उत्पाद्य पुत्रान्मुनयो नृपते यत्र तत्र ह । स्वेनैव तपसा तेषामृषित्वं विदधुः पुनः ॥
data.md: Great Rishi, O monarch, by begetting children in indiscriminate wombs, gave them the dignity of Rishis by means of their power of asceticism.

data.v: पितामहश्च मे पूर्वमृश्यशृङ्गश्च काश्यपः । वटस्ताण्ड्यः कृपश्चैव कक्षीवान्कमठादयः ॥
यवक्रीतश्च नृपते द्रोणश्च वदतां वरः । आयुर्मतङ्गो दत्तश्च द्रुपदो मत्स्य एव च ॥
एते स्वां प्रकृतिं प्राप्ता वैदेह तपसोऽऽश्रयात् । प्रतिष्ठिता वेदविदो दमे तपसि चैव हि ॥
मूलगोत्राणि चत्वारि समुत्पन्नानि पार्थिव । अङ्गिराः कश्यपश्चैव वसिष्ठो भृगुरेव च ॥
data.md: Originally only four families arose, O king viz., Angiras, Kashyapa, Vashishtha and Bhrigu.

data.v: कर्मतोऽन्यानि गोत्राणि समुत्पन्नानि पार्थिव । नामधेयानि तपसा तानि च ग्रहणं सताम् ॥
data.md: On account of acts and behaviour, O king, many other families came into existence in time. The names of those families have originated from the penances of those who have founded them. Good people use them.

data.v: विशेषधर्मान्वर्णानां प्रब्रूहि भगवन्मम । तथा सामान्यधर्मांश्च सर्वत्र कुशलो ह्यसि ॥
data.md: Janaka said Tell me, O holy one, the especial duties of the several castes. Tell me also with their common duties are. You know everything.

data.v: प्रतिग्रहो याजनं च तथैवाध्यापनं नृप । विशेषधर्मो विप्राणां रक्षा क्षत्रस्य शोभना ॥
data.md: Parashara said Taking gifts, officiating at the sacrifices of others, the teaching of pupils, O king, are the especial duties of the Brahmanas. The protection of the other castes is the special duty of the Kshatriya.

data.v: कृषिश्च पाशुपाल्यं च वाणिज्यं च विशामपि । द्विजानां परिचर्या च शूद्रकर्म नराधिप ॥
data.md: Agriculture, cattle-tending, and trade are the duties, of the Vaishyas. While service of the (three) twice-born classes is the duty, 0 king, of the Shudras.

data.v: विशेषधर्मा नृपते वर्णानां परिकीर्तिताः । धर्मान्साधारणांस्तात विस्तरेण शृणुष्व मे ॥
data.md: I have now told you what the especial duties are of the four castes, O king. Hear, now, O child as I tell you what the common duties are of all the four castes.

data.v: आनृशंस्यमहिंसा चाप्रमादः संविभागिता । श्राद्धकर्मातिथेयं च सत्यमक्रोध एव च ॥
data.md: Compassion, abstention from injury, carefulness, giving to others what is due to them, Shraddhas in honour of departed manes, hospitality to guests, truthfulness, subjugation of anger, contentedness with one's own married wives, purity, freedom from malice, knowledge of Self, and Renunciation,-these duties, O king are common to all the castes.

data.v: स्वेषु दारेषु संतोषः शौचं नित्यानसूयता । आत्मज्ञानं तितिक्षा च धर्माः साधारणा नृप ॥
