data.md: Compassion, abstention from injury, carefulness, giving to others what is due to them, Shraddhas in honour of departed manes, hospitality to guests, truthfulness, subjugation of anger, contentedness with one's own married wives, purity, freedom from malice, knowledge of Self, and Renunciation,-these duties, O king are common to all the castes.

data.v: ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्यास्त्रयो वर्णा द्विजातयः । अत्र तेषामधीकारो धर्मेषु द्विपदां वर ॥
data.md: Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas,these are the three twice-born orders, They have all an equal right to the performance of these dutics, O foremost of men.

data.v: विकर्मावस्थिता वर्णाः पतन्ति नृपते त्रयः । उन्नमन्ति यथासन्तमाश्रित्येह स्वकर्मसु ॥
data.md: These three castes following the duties Other than those sanctioned for them, suffer indignity, O king, as they go up and acquire great merit by taking for their model some righteous individual of their respective classes who duly satisfies his own duties.

data.v: न चापि शूद्रः पततीति निश्चयो; न चापि संस्कारमिहार्हतीति वा । श्रुतिप्रवृत्तं न च धर्ममाप्नुते; न चास्य धर्मे प्रतिषेधनं कृतम् ॥
data.md: The Shudra never falls down; nor is he worthy of any of the rites of regeneration. The course of duties originating from the Vedas is not his. He is not interdicted, however, from practising the thirteen duties which are common to all the castes.

data.v: वैदेहकं शूद्रमुदाहरन्ति; द्विजा महाराज श्रुतोपपन्नाः । अहं हि पश्यामि नरेन्द्र देवं; विश्वस्य विष्णुं जगतः प्रधानम् ॥
data.md: O king of the Videhas, Brahmanas learned in the Vedas, O king, regard a (virtutous) Shudra as equal to Brahman himself. I, however, O king, regard such a Shudra as the effulgent Vishnu of the universe, the foremost one in all the worlds.

data.v: सतां वृत्तमनुष्ठाय निहीना उज्जिहीर्षवः । मन्त्रवर्जं न दुष्यन्ति कुर्वाणाः पौष्टिकीः क्रियाः ॥
data.md: Persons of the lowest caste, desiring to root out the evil passions, may follow the conduct of the good; and, while so acting, they may acquire great merit by performing all rites that lead to advancement, omitting the Mantras which are to be uttered by the other castes while performing the self-same ceremonies.

data.v: यथा यथा हि सद्वृत्तमालम्बन्तीतरे जनाः । तथा तथा सुखं प्राप्य प्रेत्य चेह च शेरते ॥
data.md: Wherever persons of the lowest caste follow the conduct of the good, they succeed in acquiring happiness on account of which they are able to pass their time in happiness both in this world and the next.

data.v: किं कर्म दूषयत्येनमथ जातिर्महामुने । संदेहो मे समुत्पन्नस्तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Janaka said O great ascetic, is man sullied by his deeds or is he stained by the order or class in which he is born? A doubt has arisen in my mind. You should expound this to me.

data.v: असंशयं महाराज उभयं दोषकारकम् । कर्म चैव हि जातिश्च विशेषं तु निशामय ॥
data.md: Parashara said Forsooth, O king, both, viz., acts and birth, are sources of demerit. Listen now to their difference.

data.v: जात्या च कर्मणा चैव दुष्टं कर्म निषेवते । जात्या दुष्टश्च यः पापं न करोति स पूरुषः ॥
data.md: That man who, though sullied by birth, does not coinmit sin, abstains from sin notwithstanding birth and acts.

data.v: जात्या प्रधानं पुरुषं कुर्वाणं कर्म धिक्कृतम् । कर्म तद्दूषयत्येनं तस्मात्कर्म नशोभनम् ॥
data.md: If, however, a person of superior birth perpetrates censurable deeds, such acts pollute him. Hence, of the two, viz., acts and birth, acts pollute man.

data.v: कानि कर्माणि धर्म्याणि लोकेऽस्मिन्द्विजसत्तम । न हिंसन्तीह भूतानि क्रियमाणानि सर्वदा ॥
data.md: Janaka said What are those righteous acts in this world, 0 best of all twice-born ones, the accomplishment of which does not inflict any injury upon other creatures?

data.v: शृणु मेऽत्र महाराज यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि । यानि कर्माण्यहिंस्राणि नरं त्रायन्ति सर्वदा ॥
data.md: Parashara said Hear from me, O king, about what you ask, viz.., those acts free from injury which always rescue man.

data.v: संन्यस्याग्नीनुपासीनाः पश्यन्ति विगतज्वराः । नैःश्रेयसं धर्मपथं समारुह्य यथाक्रमम् ॥
data.md: Those who, keeping aside their domestic fires, have freed themselves from all worldly attachments, become freed from all anxieties. Gradually getting up step by step, in the path of Yoga, they at last see the stage of highest happiness. Gifted with faith and humility, always practising self-control, possessed of keen intelligence, and abstaining from all acts, they acquire eternal happiness.

data.v: प्रश्रिता विनयोपेता दमनित्याः सुसंशिताः । प्रयान्ति स्थानमजरं सर्वकर्मविवर्जिताः ॥
data.md: Those who, keeping aside their domestic fires, have freed themselves from all worldly attachments, become freed from all anxieties. Gradually getting up step by step, in the path of Yoga, they at last see the stage of highest happiness. Gifted with faith and humility, always practising self-control, possessed of keen intelligence, and abstaining from all acts, they acquire eternal happiness.

data.v: सर्वे वर्णा धर्मकार्याणि सम्य;क्कृत्वा राजन्सत्यवाक्यानि चोक्त्वा । त्यक्त्वाधर्मं दारुणं जीवलोके; यान्ति स्वर्गं नात्र कार्यो विचारः ॥
data.md: All classes of men, O king, by duly doing virtuous acts, by speaking the truth, and by abstaining from sin, in this world, go up to heaven. There is no doubt in this.

data.v: पिता सखायो गुरवः स्त्रियश्च; न निर्गुणा नाम भवन्ति लोके । अनन्यभक्ताः प्रियवादिनश्च; हिताश्च वश्याश्च तथैव राजन् ॥
data.md: Parashara said The father, the friends, the preceptors, and the wishes of the preceptors of men who are shorn of devotion, are unable to give to those men the merits derivable from devotion. Only they who are firmly devoted to such elders, who speak what is agreeable to them, who speek their well-being, and who are submissive to them in conduct, can acquire the merit to devotion.

data.v: पिता परं दैवतं मानवानां; मातुर्विशिष्टं पितरं वदन्ति । ज्ञानस्य लाभं परमं वदन्ति; जितेन्द्रियार्थाः परमाप्नुवन्ति ॥
data.md: That father is the highest of gods with his children. It is said that the father is superior to the mother. The acquirement of Knowledge is are considered as the hightest acquisition. They who have subjugating the objects of the senses, acquire what is highest.

data.v: रणाजिरे यत्र शराग्निसंस्तरे; नृपात्मजो घातमवाप्य दह्यते । प्रयाति लोकानमरैः सुदुर्लभा;न्निषेवते स्वर्गफलं यथासुखम् ॥
data.md: That Kshatriya prince, who going to the battle-field, receives wounds amid fiery arrows shooting in all directions and burns therewith, certainly goes to regions which unattainable by the very gods and, arrived there enjoys the happiness of heaven in perfect contentiment.

data.v: श्रान्तं भीतं भ्रष्टशस्त्रं रुदन्तं; पराङ्मुखं परिबर्हैश्च हीनम् । अनुद्यतं रोगिणं याचमानं; न वै हिंस्याद्बालवृद्धौ च राजन् ॥
data.md: A Kshatriya should not, O king, strike one who is fatigued, or one who is terrified, or one who has been disarmed, or one who is weeping, or one who is reluctant to fight, or one who is unequipped with mail and cars and horse and infantry, or one who has ceased to exert in the fight, or one who is ill, or one who cries for quarter. Or one who is of tender years, or one who is old.

data.v: परिबर्हैः सुसंपन्नमुद्यतं तुल्यतां गतम् । अतिक्रमेत नृपतिः संग्रामे क्षत्रियात्मजम् ॥
data.md: A Kshatriya should, in battle, fight one of his order, who is equipped with mail and cars and horse and infantry who is ready for battle, and who is a compeer.

data.v: तुल्यादिह वधः श्रेयान्विशिष्टाच्चेति निश्चयः । निहीनात्कातराच्चैव नृपाणां गर्हितो वधः ॥
data.md: Death at the hands of one who is equal or of a superior is praiseworthy, but not that at the hands of one that is low, or of one who is a coward, or of one who is a wretch. This is well known.

data.v: पापात्पापसमाचारान्निहीनाच्च नराधिप । पाप एव वधः प्रोक्तो नरकायेति निश्चयः ॥
data.md: Death at the hands of one who is sinful, or of one who is of low birth and wicked conduct, O king is infamous and leads to hell.

data.v: न कश्चित्त्राति वै राजन्दिष्टान्तवशमागतम् । सावशेषायुषं चापि कश्चिदेवापकर्षति ॥
data.md: One whose lease of life has run out, cannot be saved by any body. Likewise, one whose lease of life has not run out can never be killed by any one.

data.v: स्निग्धैश्च क्रियमाणानि कर्माणीह निवर्तयेत् । हिंसात्मकानि कर्माणि नायुरिच्छेत्परायुषा ॥
data.md: One should prevent his affectionate elders from doing to his such acts as done by menials, as also all such acts as can injure others. One should never wish to extend his own life by taking the lives of others.

data.v: गृहस्थानां तु सर्वेषां विनाशमभिकाङ्क्षताम् । निधनं शोभनं तात पुलिनेषु क्रियावताम् ॥
data.md: When they sacrifice their lives, it is laudable for all householders observing the duties of men living in sacred places to give up their lives on the banks of sacred rivers.

data.v: आयुषि क्षयमापन्ने पञ्चत्वमुपगच्छति । नाकारणात्तद्भवति कारणैरुपपादितम् ॥
data.md: When one lease of life is over, his body dissolved into the five elements. Sometimes this occurs suddenly and some times it is brought about by (natural) causes.

data.v: तथा शरीरं भवति देहाद्येनोपपादितम् । अध्वानं गतकश्चायं प्राप्तश्चायं गृहाद्गृहम् ॥
data.md: He who having obtained a body, destroys it himself becomes invested with another body of a similar nature. Though set on the path of Liberation, he yet becomes a traveller and acquires another body like a person going from one room into another.

data.v: द्वितीयं कारणं तत्र नान्यत्किंचन विद्यते । तद्देहं देहिनां युक्तं मोक्षभूतेषु वर्तते ॥
data.md: About such a man's attainment of a second body the only cause is his accidental death. There is no second cause. That new body which embodied creatures obtain, comes into existence and becomes attached to Rudras and Pishachas.

data.v: सिरास्नाय्वस्थिसंघातं बीभत्सामेध्यसंकुलम् । भूतानामिन्द्रियाणां च गुणानां च समागमम् ॥
data.md: Learned men, conversant with spiritual science say that the body is a compound of arteries and sinews and bones and much repulsive and impure matter and a compound of essences, and the senses and the objects of the senses born of desire, all having an outer cover of skin close to them. Shorn of beauty and other accomplishments, this compound, through force of the desires of a pristine life, assumes a human forin.

data.v: त्वगन्तं देहमित्याहुर्विद्वांसोऽध्यात्मचिन्तकाः । गुणैरपि परिक्षीणं शरीरं मर्त्यतां गतम् ॥
data.md: Learned men, conversant with spiritual science say that the body is a compound of arteries and sinews and bones and much repulsive and impure matter and a compound of essences, and the senses and the objects of the senses born of desire, all having an outer cover of skin close to them. Shorn of beauty and other accomplishments, this compound, through force of the desires of a pristine life, assumes a human forin.

data.v: शरीरिणा परित्यक्तं निश्चेष्टं गतचेतनम् । भूतैः प्रकृतिमापन्नैस्ततो भूमौ निमज्जति ॥
data.md: Left off by the owner, the body becomes inanimate and motionless. Indeed, when the principal ingredients return to their respective natures, the body is mixed up with the dust.

data.v: भावितं कर्मयोगेन जायते तत्र तत्र ह । इदं शरीरं वैदेह म्रियते यत्र तत्र ह । तत्स्वभावोऽपरो दृष्टो विसर्गः कर्मणस्तथा ॥
data.md: Caused by its union with deeds, this body reappears under circumstances determined by its deeds. Indeed O king of the Videhas, under whatever circumstances this body is dissolved, its next birth, determined by the these circumstances, is seen to enjoy and endure the fruits of all its pristine deeds.

data.v: न जायते तु नृपते कंचित्कालमयं पुनः । परिभ्रमति भूतात्मा द्यामिवाम्बुधरो महान् ॥
स पुनर्जायते राजन्प्राप्येहायतनं नृप । मनसः परमो ह्यात्मा इन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः ॥
द्विविधानां च भूतानां जङ्गमाः परमा नृप । जङ्गमानामपि तथा द्विपदाः परमा मताः । द्विपदानामपि तथा द्विजा वै परमाः स्मृताः ॥
data.md: Amongst mobile creatures the two legged are superior. Amongst two-legged creatures, those that are are twice-born are superior.

data.v: द्विजानामपि राजेन्द्र प्रज्ञावन्तः परा मताः । प्राज्ञानामात्मसंबुद्धाः संबुद्धानाममानिनः ॥
data.md: Amongst those that are twice-born they who are endued with wisdom are superior. Amongst them who are endued with wisdom they that have succeeded in acquiring a knowledge of the soul are superior. Amongst those who are endued with a knowledge of the soul, those who are endued with humility are superior.

data.v: जातमन्वेति मरणं नृणामिति विनिश्चयः । अन्तवन्ति हि कर्माणि सेवन्ते गुणतः प्रजाः ॥
data.md: Death follows birth in all men. This is settled. Creatures, influenced by the qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance, pursue acts which have an end.

data.v: आपन्ने तूत्तरां काष्ठां सूर्ये यो निधनं व्रजेत् । नक्षत्रे च मुहूर्ते च पुण्ये राजन्स पुण्यकृत् ॥
data.md: That man is considered as righteous who meets with dissolution when the Sun is in the northern declension, and at a time and under a constellation both of which are sacred and auspicious, He is righteous who, having purified himself of all sins and performed all his acts according to the best of his might and having abstained from giving pain to any man, meets with death when it comes.

data.v: अयोजयित्वा क्लेशेन जनं प्लाव्य च दुष्कृतम् । मृत्युनाप्राकृतेनेह कर्म कृत्वात्मशक्तितः ॥
विषमुद्बन्धनं दाहो दस्युहस्तात्तथा वधः । दंष्ट्रिभ्यश्च पशुभ्यश्च प्राकृतो वध उच्यते ॥
data.md: The death that one meets with by taking poision, by hanging, by burning, at the hands of robbers and at the teeth of animals, is said to be an infamous one.

data.v: न चैभिः पुण्यकर्माणो युज्यन्ते नाभिसंधिजैः । एवंविधैश्च बहुभिरपरैः प्राकृतैरपि ॥
data.md: Those man who are righteous never meet with such or similar deaths even if they be afflicted with mental and physical diseases of the most painful sort.

data.v: ऊर्ध्वं हित्वा प्रतिष्ठन्ते प्राणाः पुण्यकृतां नृप । मध्यतो मध्यपुण्यानामधो दुष्कृतकर्मणाम् ॥
data.md: The lives of the pious, O king, piercing through the Sun, ascend into the regions of Brahman. The lives of those who are both righteous and sinful rove in the middle regions. The lives of those who are sinful sink into the lowest depths. There is one only enemy (of man) and not another. That enemy is at one with Ignorance, O king. Overwhelmed by it, is led to perpetrate frightful and exceedingly cruel deeds.

data.v: एकः शत्रुर्न द्वितीयोऽस्ति शत्रु;रज्ञानतुल्यः पुरुषस्य राजन् । येनावृतः कुरुते संप्रयुक्तो; घोराणि कर्माणि सुदारुणानि ॥
प्रबोधनार्थं श्रुतिधर्मयुक्तं; वृद्धानुपास्यं च भवेत यस्य । प्रयत्नसाध्यो हि स राजपुत्र; प्रज्ञाशरेणोन्मथितः परैति ॥
data.md: That enemy for resisting which one should display his energy waiting upon the aged according to the duties laid down in the Shrutis,-~-that enemy which cannot be Overcome except by steady endeavours,-meets with destruction, O king, only when it is crushed by the arrows of wisdom. One

data.v: अधीत्य वेदांस्तपसा ब्रह्मचारी; यज्ञाञ्शक्त्या संनिसृज्येह पञ्च । वनं गच्छेत्पुरुषो धर्मकामः; श्रेयश्चित्वा स्थापयित्वा स्ववंशम् ॥
data.md: The man desirous of acquiring merit should at first study the Vedas and practise penances, becoming a Brahimacharin. He should next, becoming a householder, perform the usual Sacrifices. Establishing his race, he should then enter the forest, controlling his senses, and desirous of acquiring Liberation.

data.v: उपभोगैरपि त्यक्तं नात्मानमवसादयेत् । चण्डालत्वेऽपि मानुष्यं सर्वथा तात दुर्लभम् ॥
data.md: One should never emaciate himself by abstaining from every enjoyment. Of all births, that of a human being is preferable even if one has to become a Chandala.

data.v: इयं हि योनिः प्रथमा यां प्राप्य जगतीपते । आत्मा वै शक्यते त्रातुं कर्मभिः शुभलक्षणैः ॥
data.md: Indeed, O king, that order of birth (viz., humanity) is the foremost, since by becoming a human being one succeeds in rescuing his self by meritorious acts.

data.v: कथं न विप्रणश्येम योनितोऽस्या इति प्रभो । कुर्वन्ति धर्मं मनुजाः श्रुतिप्रामाण्यदर्शनात् ॥
data.md: Men always perform righteous acts, O lord, guided by the authority of the Shrutis, so that they may not deviate from the status of humanity.

data.v: यो दुर्लभतरं प्राप्य मानुष्यमिह वै नरः । धर्मावमन्ता कामात्मा भवेत्स खलु वञ्च्यते ॥
data.md: That man who, having been born as a man that is so difficult of attainment, indulges in malice, disregards righteousness and gives way :o desire, is certainly betrayed by his desires.

data.v: यस्तु प्रीतिपुरोगेण चक्षुषा तात पश्यति । दीपोपमानि भूतानि यावदर्चिर्न नश्यति ॥
data.md: That man who regards all creatures impartially guided by affection, considering them worthy of being cherished with loving, aid, who disregards all sorts of wealth, who offers them consolation, gives them food, addresses them in sweet words, and who rejoices in their happiness and grieves in their sorrows, has never to suffer misery in the next world.

data.v: सान्त्वेनानुप्रदानेन प्रियवादेन चाप्युत । समदुःखसुखो भूत्वा स परत्र महीयते ॥
data.md: That man who regards all creatures impartially guided by affection, considering them worthy of being cherished with loving, aid, who disregards all sorts of wealth, who offers them consolation, gives them food, addresses them in sweet words, and who rejoices in their happiness and grieves in their sorrows, has never to suffer misery in the next world.

data.v: दानं त्यागः शोभना मूर्तिरद्भ्यो; भूयः प्लाव्यं तपसा वै शरीरम् । सरस्वतीनैमिषपुष्करेषु; ये चाप्यन्ये पुण्यदेशाः पृथिव्याम् ॥
data.md: Repairing to the Sarasvati, the Naimisha forest, the Pushkara lake, and the other sacred spots on Earth, one should make gifts, practise renunciation, render his aspect amiable, O king, and purify his body with baths and penances.

data.v: गृहेषु येषामसवः पतन्ति; तेषामथो निर्हरणं प्रशस्तम् । यानेन वै प्रापणं च श्मशाने; शौचेन नूनं विधिना चैव दाहः ॥
data.md: Those men who meet with death within their houses should have their bodies cremated. Their bodies bodies should should be be taken to the crematorium on cars and there they should be burnt according to the rites of purification that have been laid down in the scriptures,

data.v: इष्टिः पुष्टिर्यजनं याजनं च; दानं पुण्यानां कर्मणां च प्रयोगः । शक्त्या पित्र्यं यच्च किंचित्प्रशस्तं; सर्वाण्यात्मार्थे मानवो यः करोति ॥
data.md: Religious rites, beneficial ceremonies, the performance of sacrifices, officiation at the sacrifices of others, gifts, the doing of other meritorious deeds, the performance according to the best of his power, of all that has been ordained in in the case of his deceased ancestors,-all these one does for benefiting his own self.

data.v: धर्मशास्त्राणि वेदाश्च षडङ्गानि नराधिप । श्रेयसोऽर्थे विधीयन्ते नरस्याक्लिष्टकर्मणः ॥
data.md: O king! All the scriptures of righteousness and the Vedas with six angas proceed for the welfare of sinless one.

data.v: एतद्वै सर्वमाख्यातं मुनिना सुमहात्मना । विदेहराजाय पुरा श्रेयसोऽर्थे नराधिप ॥
data.md: Bhishma continued All this was said by that great sage to the king of the Videhas, O king, in days of yore for his well-being.

data.v: पुनरेव तु पप्रच्छ जनको मिथिलाधिपः । पराशरं महात्मानं धर्मे परमनिश्चयम् ॥
data.md: Daksha said Once again Janaka, the king of Mithila, asked the great Parashara gifted with certain knowledge regarding all duties.

data.v: किं श्रेयः का गतिर्ब्रह्मन्किं कृतं न विनश्यति । क्व गतो न निवर्तेत तन्मे ब्रूहि महामुने ॥
data.md: Janaka said What yields good? What is the best path (for living creatures)? What is that which being done is never destroyed? What is that spot going where one has not to return? Tell me all this, O you of great intelligence.

data.v: असङ्गः श्रेयसो मूलं ज्ञानं ज्ञानगतिः परा । चीर्णं तपो न प्रणश्येद्वापः क्षेत्रे न नश्यति ॥
data.md: Parashara said Dissociation is the root of what is good. Knowledge is the greatest path. Penances practised are never destroyed. Gifts also, made to worthy persons, are not lost.

data.v: छित्त्वाधर्ममयं पाशं यदा धर्मेऽभिरज्यते । दत्त्वाभयकृतं दानं तदा सिद्धिमवाप्नुयात् ॥
data.md: When one, snapping the fetters of sin, begins to take pleasure in virtue, and when one makes that highest of all gifts, viz., the promise of all harmlessness to all creatures, then does one acquire success.

data.v: यो ददाति सहस्राणि गवामश्वशतानि च । अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यस्तद्दानमतिवर्तते ॥
data.md: He who gives away thousands of kine and hundreds of horses, and who promises harmlessness to all creatures receives in return the promise of harmlessness from all.

data.v: वसन्विषयमध्येऽपि न वसत्येव बुद्धिमान् । संवसत्येव दुर्बुद्धिरसत्सु विषयेष्वपि ॥
data.md: One may live in the midst of all sorts or riches and cnjoyment, yet, if blessed with intelligence, one does not live in them; while he who is shorn of intelligence lives wholly in objects of enjoyment which unsubstantial.

data.v: नाधर्मः श्लिष्यते प्राज्ञमापः पुष्करपर्णवत् । अप्राज्ञमधिकं पापं श्लिष्यते जतु काष्ठवत् ॥
data.md: Sin cannot attach to a wise man as water cannot drench the leaves of the lotus. Sin sticks more firmly to him who is without attachment as lac and wood stick firmly to each other.

data.v: नाधर्मः कारणापेक्षी कर्तारमभिमुञ्चति । कर्ता खलु यथाकालं तत्सर्वमभिपद्यते । न भिद्यन्ते कृतात्मान आत्मप्रत्ययदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: Sin, which cannot be dissipated except by endurance of its fruits, never leaves the doer. The doer, when the time comes, has to suffer the consequences thereof. They, however, who are of purified souls and who realise the cxistence of Brahma, are never afflicted by the fruits of their deeds. are even

data.v: बुद्धिकर्मेन्द्रियाणां हि प्रमत्तो यो न बुध्यते । शुभाशुभेषु सक्तात्मा प्राप्नोति सुमहद्भयम् ॥
data.md: Careless in about one's senses of knowledge and of action, one who is not conscious of his wicked deeds, and whose heart is attached to both good and bad, becomes afflicted with great fear.

data.v: वीतरागो जितक्रोधः सम्यग्भवति यः सदा । विषये वर्तमानोऽपि न स पापेन युज्यते ॥
data.md: One who at all times becomes entirely freed from attachments and who completely subdues the passion of anger, is never sullied by sin even if he lives in the enjoyment of worldly objects.

data.v: मर्यादायां धर्मसेतुर्निबद्धो नैव सीदति । पुष्टस्रोत इवायत्तः स्फीतो भवति संचयः ॥
data.md: As a dyke set across a river, if not washed away, makes the waters thereof to swell up, so the man who, without being attached to objects of pleasure, creates the dyke of virtue whose materials consist of the limitations set down in the scriptures, has never to wane away. On the other hand, his merits and penances, increase.

data.v: यथा भानुगतं तेजो मणिः शुद्धः समाधिना । आदत्ते राजशार्दूल तथा योगः प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: As the pure gem absorbs and attracts to itself, according to the natural law, the rays of the Sun, so, O foremost of kings, does Yoga proceed by help of rapt attention.

data.v: यथा तिलानामिह पुष्पसंश्रया;त्पृथक्पृथग्याति गुणोऽतिसौम्यताम् । तथा नराणां भुवि भावितात्मनां; यथाश्रयं सत्त्वगुणः प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: As sesame seeds, for being always with sweet-scented flowers, become in respect of quality very sweet, so the quality of Goodness arises in men proportionate to the extent of their association with persons of purified souls.

data.v: जहाति दारानिहते न संपदः; सदश्वयानं विविधाश्च याः क्रियाः । त्रिविष्टपे जातमतिर्यदा नर;स्तदास्य बुद्धिर्विषयेषु भिद्यते ॥
data.md: When one becomes desirous of living in heaven, he abandons his wives and riches and rank and vehicles and various sorts of good deeds. indeed, when one gets such a bent of mind, his understanding is said to be dissociated from the objects of the senses.

data.v: प्रसक्तबुद्धिर्विषयेषु यो नरो; यो बुध्यते ह्यात्महितं कदा च न । स सर्वभावानुगतेन चेतसा; नृपामिषेणेव झषो विकृष्यते ॥
data.md: That man who, with understanding attached to the objects of the senses, becomes blind to what is for his real well-beings, is dragged by his heart which runs after all earthly objects, like a fish by the bait of meat.

data.v: संघातवान्मर्त्यलोकः परस्परमपाश्रितः । कदलीगर्भनिःसारो नौरिवाप्सु निमज्जति ॥
data.md: Like the body that is made up of different limbs and organs, all mortal creatures exist depending upon one another. They are weak like the pith of the banana plant. They sink in the world's ocean like a boat.

data.v: न धर्मकालः पुरुषस्य निश्चितो; न चापि मृत्युः पुरुषं प्रतीक्षते । क्रिया हि धर्मस्य सदैव शोभना; यदा नरो मृत्युमुखेऽभिवर्तते ॥
data.md: There is no fixed time for the acquisition of virtue. Death waits for no man. When man is constantly running towards the jaws of Death, the doing of pious deeds is proper at all times.

data.v: यथान्धः स्वगृहे युक्तो ह्यभ्यासादेव गच्छति । तथा युक्तेन मनसा प्राज्ञो गच्छति तां गतिम् ॥
data.md: Like a blind man who, with attention, can move about his own house, the wise man, with mind fixed on Yoga, can proceed along the road.

data.v: मरणं जन्मनि प्रोक्तं जन्म वै मरणाश्रितम् । अविद्वान्मोक्षधर्मेषु बद्धो भ्रमति चक्रवत् ॥
data.md: It has been said that death originates from birth. Birth is subject to the control of death. One unacquainted with the course of the duties of Liberation revolves like a wheel between birth and death, unable to free himself from that fate.

data.v: यथा मृणालोऽनुगतमाशु मुञ्चति कर्दमम् । तथात्मा पुरुषस्येह मनसा परिमुच्यते । मनः प्रणयतेऽऽत्मानं स एनमभियुञ्जति ॥
data.md: As the lotus stalk quickly leaves the mire attached to it, so the Soul can quickly renounce the mind.

data.v: परार्थे वर्तमानस्तु स्वकार्यं योऽभिमन्यते । इन्द्रियार्थेषु सक्तः सन्स्वकार्यात्परिहीयते ॥
data.md: Engaged amid the objects of the senses, one who considers such engagement to be his employment falls away from his true employment on account of such devotion to those objects.

data.v: अधस्तिर्यग्गतिं चैव स्वर्गे चैव परां गतिम् । प्राप्नोति स्वकृतैरात्मा प्राज्ञस्येहेतरस्य च ॥
data.md: The soul of the wise man acquires, through its pious deeds, a state of great happiness in heaven, while that of the man who is not endued with wisdom sinks very low or is born among intermediate creatures.

data.v: मृन्मये भाजने पक्वे यथा वै न्यस्यते द्रवः । तथा शरीरं तपसा तप्तं विषयमश्नुते ॥
data.md: As a liquid substance, if kept in a baked earthen pot, does not escape therefrom but remains undiminished similarly, one's body with which one had practised penances enjoys (without rejecting) all objects of pleasure.

data.v: विषयानश्नुते यस्तु न स भोक्ष्यत्यसंशयम् । यस्तु भोगांस्त्यजेदात्मा स वै भोक्तुं व्यवस्यति ॥
data.md: Verily, that man who enjoys earthly objects can never be liberated. That man, however, who renounces such objects, succeeds in enjoying great happiness hereafter.

data.v: नीहारेण हि संवीतः शिश्नोदरपरायणः । जात्यन्ध इव पन्थानमावृतात्मा न बुध्यते ॥
data.md: Like one suffering from blindness and, therefore, incapable of seeing his way, the sensualist, with soul confined in an opaque case, seems to be surrounded by a mist and cannot see (the true object).

data.v: वणिग्यथा समुद्राद्वै यथार्थं लभते धनम् । तथा मर्त्यार्णवे जन्तोः कर्मविज्ञानतो गतिः ॥
data.md: As merchants, going across the sea, make profits according to their capital, so creatures, in this world of men, attain to ends proportionate to their respective deeds.

data.v: अहोरात्रमये लोके जरारूपेण संचरन् । मृत्युर्ग्रसति भूतानि पवनं पन्नगो यथा ॥
data.md: Like a snake devouring air, Death walks in this world made up of days and nights in the form of Decrepitude and devours all ceatures.

data.v: स्वयं कृतानि कर्माणि जातो जन्तुः प्रपद्यते । नाकृतं लभते कश्चित्किंचिदत्र प्रियाप्रियम् ॥
data.md: A creature, when born, enjoys or suffers the fruits of deeds done by him in his pristine lives. There is nothing agreeable or disagreeable which one enjoys or suffers without its being the result of the deeds one has done in his previous lives.

data.v: शयानं यान्तमासीनं प्रवृत्तं विषयेषु च । शुभाशुभानि कर्माणि प्रपद्यन्ते नरं सदा ॥
data.md: Whether lying or proceeding, whether sitting idly or engaged in his business, in whatever state a man may be, his pristine deeds good or bad, always approach him.

data.v: न ह्यन्यत्तीरमासाद्य पुनस्तर्तुं व्यवस्यति । दुर्लभो दृश्यते ह्यस्य विनिपातो महार्णवे ॥
data.md: One who has gone to the other end of the ocean, wishes not to cross the sea for returning to the bank whence he had sailed.

data.v: यथा भारावसक्ता हि नौर्महाम्भसि तन्तुना । तथा मनोऽभियोगाद्वै शरीरं प्रतिकर्षति ॥
data.md: As the fisherman, when he wishes, raises with the help of his chord his boat sunk in the waters, similarly the mind by the help of Yoga contemplation, raises individual Soul sunk in the world's ocean and unliberated from consciousness of body.

data.v: यथा समुद्रमभितः संस्यूताः सरितोऽपराः । तथाद्या प्रकृतिर्योगादभिसंस्यूयते सदा ॥
data.md: As all rivers running towards the ocean, join it, so the mind, when engaged in Yoga, becomes united with primal Nature.

data.v: स्नेहपाशैर्बहुविधैरासक्तमनसो नराः । प्रकृतिस्था विषीदन्ति जले सैकतवेश्मवत् ॥
data.md: Men whose minds become fettered by various bonds of affection, and who are sunk in ignorance, meet with destruction like houses of sand in water.

data.v: शरीरगृहसंस्थस्य शौचतीर्थस्य देहिनः । बुद्धिमार्गप्रयातस्य सुखं त्विह परत्र च ॥
data.md: That embodied creature who considers his body as only a house and purity as its sacred water, and who walks along the road of the understanding, acquires happiness both in this world and the next.

data.v: विस्तराः क्लेशसंयुक्ताः संक्षेपास्तु सुखावहाः । परार्थं विस्तराः सर्वे त्यागमात्महितं विदुः ॥
data.md: One who walks along the road recommended by the understanding acquires happiness both in this world and the next. Many of them are fraught with misery; while the Few yield happiness. Fruits represented by Nescience form the Many. Renunciation yields the soul's happiness.

data.v: संकल्पजो मित्रवर्गो ज्ञातयः कारणात्मकाः । भार्या दासाश्च पुत्राश्च स्वमर्थमनुयुञ्जते ॥
data.md: One's friends who originate from his determination, and one's kinsmen whose attachment is due to selfish reasons, one's wives and sons and servants only devour his riches.

data.v: न माता न पिता किंचित्कस्यचित्प्रतिपद्यते । दानपथ्योदनो जन्तुः स्वकर्मफलमश्नुते ॥
data.md: Neither the mother, nor the father, can confer the slightest benefit upon him in the next world. Gifts form the diet upon which he can live. Indeed, one is compelled to enjoy the fruits of his own deeds.

data.v: माता पुत्रः पिता भ्राता भार्या मित्रजनस्तथा । अष्टापदपदस्थाने त्वक्षमुद्रेव न्यस्यते ॥
data.md: The mother, the son, the father, the brother, the wife, and friends, are like lines drawn with gold by the side of gold itself.

data.v: सर्वाणि कर्माणि पुरा कृतानि; शुभाशुभान्यात्मनो यान्ति जन्तोः । उपस्थितं कर्मफलं विदित्वा; बुद्धिं तथा चोदयतेऽन्तरात्मा ॥
data.md: All acts, good and bad, done in pristine lives, visit the doer. Knowing that everything enjoys or suffers at present is the outcome of his pristine deeds, the soul makes the understanding move on different directions.

data.v: व्यवसायं समाश्रित्य सहायान्योऽधिगच्छति । न तस्य कश्चिदारम्भः कदाचिदवसीदति ॥
data.md: Depending on earnest endeavour and equipped with proper aids, he who undertakes to accomplish his tasks never meets with failure.

data.v: अद्वैधमनसं युक्तं शूरं धीरं विपश्चितम् । न श्रीः संत्यजते नित्यमादित्यमिव रश्मयः ॥
data.md: As the rays of light never abandon the Sun, so prosperity never leaves him who has firm faith.

data.v: आस्तिक्यव्यवसायाभ्यामुपायाद्विस्मयाद्धिया । यमारभत्यनिन्द्यात्मा न सोऽर्थः परिसीदति ॥
data.md: That act which a man of pure soul does with faith and earnestness, with the help of proper means, without pride, and with intelligence, becomes never lost.

data.v: सर्वः स्वानि शुभाशुभानि नियतं कर्माणि जन्तुः स्वयं; गर्भात्संप्रतिपद्यते तदुभयं यत्तेन पूर्वं कृतम् । मृत्युश्चापरिहारवान्समगतिः कालेन विच्छेदिता; दारोश्चूर्णमिवाश्मसारविहितं कर्मान्तिकं प्रापयेत् ॥
data.md: A creature obtains from the very time of his residence in the mother's womb all his own acts good and bad that were acquired by him in his pristine lives. Death, which is irresistible, helped by Time which encompasses the destruction of life, takes all creatures to their end like wind scattering the dust of sawed timber.

data.v: स्वरूपतामात्मकृतं च विस्तरं; कुलान्वयं द्रव्यसमृद्धिसंचयम् । नरो हि सर्वो लभते यथाकृतं; शुभाशुभेनात्मकृतेन कर्मणा ॥
data.md: Through acts good and bad done by himself in his pristine lives, man acquires gold and animals, and wives, and children, and honour of birth, and costly possessions, and his entire affluence.

data.v: इत्युक्तो जनको राजन्यथातथ्यं मनीषिणा । श्रुत्वा धर्मविदां श्रेष्ठः परां मुदमवाप ह ॥
data.md: Bhishma continued Thus addressed agreeably to the truth by the sage, Janaka, that foremost of pious men, O king, heard everything the Rishi said and acquired great happiness from it.

data.v: सत्यं क्षमां दमं प्रज्ञां प्रशंसन्ति पितामह । विद्वांसो मनुजा लोके कथमेतन्मतं तव ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said 0 grandfather, learmed men praise truth, self-control, forgiveness and wisdom. What is your opinion about these virtues?

data.v: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम् । साध्यानामिह संवादं हंसस्य च युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it I shall recite to you an old narrative, O Yudhishthira, of the discourse between the Sadhyas and a Swan.

data.v: हंसो भूत्वाथ सौवर्णस्त्वजो नित्यः प्रजापतिः । स वै पर्येति लोकांस्त्रीनथ साध्यानुपागमत् ॥
data.md: Once on a time the uncreate and eternal Lord of all creatures, assuming the form of a golden Swan, passed through the three worlds till in course of his ramblings he came upon the Sadhyas.

data.v: शकुने वयं स्म देवा वै साध्यास्त्वामनुयुज्महे । पृच्छामस्त्वां मोक्षधर्मं भवांश्च किल मोक्षवित् ॥
data.md: The Saddhyas said 0 lord, we are the gods called Sadhyas. We like to question you. Indeed, we would ask you about the religion of liberation. You are well acquainted with it.

data.v: श्रुतोऽसि नः पण्डितो धीरवादी; साधुशब्दः पतते ते पतत्रिन् । किं मन्यसे श्रेष्ठतमं द्विज त्वं; कस्मिन्मनस्ते रमते महात्मन् ॥
data.md: We have heard, O bird, that you are endued with great learning, and eloquent and wise of speech. O bird, what do you think is the highest of all objects? O great one, in what does your mind find pleasure?

data.v: तन्नः कार्यं पक्षिवर प्रशाधि; यत्कार्याणां मन्यसे श्रेष्ठमेकम् । यत्कृत्वा वै पुरुषः सर्वबन्धै;र्विमुच्यते विहगेन्द्रेह शीघ्रम् ॥
data.md: Do you, therefore, O foremost of birds, instruct us as to what that one act is which you consider as the foremost of all acts, and by doing which, O king of birds, one may soon be freed from all fetters.

data.v: इदं कार्यममृताशाः शृणोमि; तपो दमः सत्यमात्माभिगुप्तिः । ग्रन्थीन्विमुच्य हृदयस्य सर्वा;न्प्रियाप्रिये स्वं वशमानयीत ॥
data.md: The Swan said O nectar-drinking ones, I have heard that one should follow these, viz., penances, selfcontrol, truth, and subjugation of the mind. Losing all the knots of the heart, one should also bring under his control both what is pleasant and what is unpleasant.

data.v: नारुंतुदः स्यान्न नृशंसवादी; न हीनतः परमभ्याददीत । ययास्य वाचा पर उद्विजेत; न तां वदेद्रुशतीं पापलोक्याम् ॥
data.md: One should not cut the vitals of others. One should not utter cruel words. One should never receive scriptural lectures from a mean person. one should never utter such words as pain others, as make others miserable, and as lead to hell.

data.v: वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्पतन्ति; यैराहतः शोचति रात्र्यहानि । परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्ति; तान्पण्डितो नावसृजेत्परेषु ॥
data.md: Wordy arrows fall from the lips. Pierced therewith one burns always. Those arrows do not cut any other part than the very vitals of the person aimed. Hence he who is a learned man, should never aim them at others.

data.v: परश्चेदेनमतिवादबाणै;र्भृशं विध्येच्छम एवेह कार्यः । संरोष्यमाणः प्रतिमृष्यते यः; स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परस्य ॥
data.md: If a person deeply cuts a wise man with wordy arrows, the wise man should remain silent. The man who, though sought to be angered, rejoices without giving way to anger, takes away from the provoker all his merits,

data.v: क्षेपाभिमानादभिषङ्गव्यलीकं; निगृह्णाति ज्वलितं यश्च मन्युम् । अदुष्टचेता मुदितोऽनसूयुः; स आदत्ते सुकृतं वै परेषाम् ॥
data.md: That man of virtuous soul, who, full of joy and shom of malice, control his burning ire which, if indulged, would lead him to speak ill of others and verily become his enemy, takes away the merits of others.

data.v: आक्रुश्यमानो न वदामि किंचि;त्क्षमाम्यहं ताड्यमानश्च नित्यम् । श्रेष्ठं ह्येतत्क्षममप्याहुरार्याः; सत्यं तथैवार्जवमानृशंस्यम् ॥
data.md: As for myself, I never answer when another speaks ill of me. If attacked, I always forgive the assault. The righteous hold that forgiveness, truth, sincerity and compassion are the foremost (of all virtues).

data.v: वेदस्योपनिषत्सत्यं सत्यस्योपनिषद्दमः । दमस्योपनिषन्मोक्ष एतत्सर्वानुशासनम् ॥
data.md: Truth is the essence of the Vedas. The essence of Truth is self-control. The essence of self-control is Liberation. This is the teaching of all the scriptures.

data.v: वाचो वेगं मनसः क्रोधवेगं; विवित्सावेगमुदरोपस्थवेगम् । एतान्वेगान्यो विषहत्युदीर्णां;स्तं मन्येऽहं ब्राह्मणं वै मुनिं च ॥
data.md: I know that person as a Brahmana and Muni who governs the rising impulse of speech, the impulse of anger appearing in the mind, the impulse to thirst, and the impulses of the stomach and the organ of pleasure.

data.v: अक्रोधनः क्रुध्यतां वै विशिष्ट;स्तथा तितिक्षुरतितिक्षोर्विशिष्टः । अमानुषान्मानुषो वै विशिष्ट;स्तथाज्ञानाज्ज्ञानवान्वै प्रधानः ॥
आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः । आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति ॥
data.md: Assailed with harsh words, one should not assail in return. Indeed, one who, under such circumstances, renounces anger, succeeds in burning the assailer and taking away all his merits.

data.v: यो नात्युक्तः प्राह रूक्षं प्रियं वा; यो वा हतो न प्रतिहन्ति धैर्यात् । पापं च यो नेच्छति तस्य हन्तु;स्तस्मै देवाः स्पृहयन्ते सदैव ॥
data.md: That person who when attacked with harsh words, does not utter a harsh word in reply, who when lauded does not say what is pleasant to him who praise, who is gifted with such fortitude as not to strike in return when struck and not to even wish evil to the striker, finds his company always sought after by the gods.

data.v: पापीयसः क्षमेतैव श्रेयसः सदृशस्य च । विमानितो हतोऽऽक्रुष्ट एवं सिद्धिं गमिष्यति ॥
data.md: A sinful man should be forgiven as if he were righteous by one who is insulted, struck, and calumniated. By acting in this way one gains success.

data.v: सदाहमार्यान्निभृतोऽप्युपासे; न मे विवित्सा न च मेऽस्ति रोषः । न चाप्यहं लिप्समानः परैमि; न चैव किंचिद्विषमेण यामि ॥
data.md: Though all my objects have been fulfilled, yet I always wait respectfully on the righteous. I have no thirst. My anger has been suppressed. Seduced by covetousness I do not deviate from the path of virtue. I do not also approach any one with prayers for riches.

data.v: नाहं शप्तः प्रतिशपामि किंचि;द्दमं द्वारं ह्यमृतस्येह वेद्मि । गुह्यं ब्रह्म तदिदं वो ब्रवीमि; न मानुषाच्छ्रेष्ठतरं हि किंचित् ॥
data.md: If cursed I do not curse in return. I know that self-control is the door of immortality. I disclose to you a great mystery. There is no position that is superior to that of humanity.

data.v: विमुच्यमानः पापेभ्यो घनेभ्य इव चन्द्रमाः । विरजाः कालमाकाङ्क्षन्धीरो धैर्येण सिध्यति ॥
data.md: Freed from sin like the Moon from misty clouds, the wise man, shining in resplendence, acquires success by patiently waiting for his time.

data.v: यः सर्वेषां भवति ह्यर्चनीय; उत्सेचने स्तम्भ इवाभिजातः । यस्मै वाचं सुप्रशस्तां वदन्ति; स वै देवान्गच्छति संयतात्मा ॥
data.md: A person of controlled soul, who becomes the object of worship with all by becoming the foremost of the pillars of the universe, and to whom only agreeable words are addressed by all, acquires the companionship of the gods.

data.v: न तथा वक्तुमिच्छन्ति कल्याणान्पुरुषे गुणान् । यथैषां वक्तुमिच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यमनुयुञ्जकाः ॥
data.md: Revilers never speak of the merits of a person as readily as they speak of his demerits.

data.v: यस्य वाङ्मनसी गुप्ते सम्यक्प्रणिहिते सदा । वेदास्तपश्च त्यागश्च स इदं सर्वमाप्नुयात् ॥
data.md: That person whose speech and mind are properly controlled and always devoted to the Supreme, gets the fruits of the Vedas, Penances, and Renunciation.

data.v: आक्रोशनावमानाभ्यामबुधाद्वर्धते बुधः । तस्मान्न वर्धयेदन्यं न चात्मानं विहिंसयेत् ॥
data.md: The wise man should never revile (in return) those who have no merit, by speaking out their dispraise and by insults. He should not extol others and should never injure themselves.

data.v: अमृतस्येव संतृप्येदवमानस्य वै द्विजः । सुखं ह्यवमतः शेते योऽवमन्ता स नश्यति ॥
data.md: The wise and learned man considers revilement as nectar. Reviled, he sleeps without anxiety. The reviler, on the other hand, meets with destruction.

data.v: यत्क्रोधनो यजते यद्ददाति; यद्वा तपस्तप्यति यज्जुहोति । वैवस्वतस्तद्धरतेऽस्य सर्वं; मोघः श्रमो भवति क्रोधनस्य ॥
data.md: The sacrifices that one celebrates angrily, the gifts one makes in angrily, the penances one practices angrily, and the offerings and libations one makes to the sacred fire angrily, are such that their merits are robbed by Yama. The toil of an angry man becomes entirely frutile.

data.v: चत्वारि यस्य द्वाराणि सुगुप्तान्यमरोत्तमाः । उपस्थमुदरं हस्तौ वाक्चतुर्थी स धर्मवित् ॥
data.md: You foremost of immortals, that person is said to be conversant with virtue whose four doors, viz., the organ of generation, the stoinach, the two arms, and speech, are well governed.

data.v: सत्यं दमं ह्यार्जवमानृशंस्यं; धृतिं तितिक्षामभिसेवमानः । स्वाध्यायनित्योऽस्पृहयन्परेषा;मेकान्तशील्यूर्ध्वगतिर्भवेत्सः ॥
data.md: That person who, always practising truth and self-control and sincerity and mercy and patience and renunciation, becomes devoted to the study of the Vedas, does not covet others possession, and pursues what is good with a singleness of purpose, succeeds in going to heaven.

data.v: सर्वानेताननुचरन्वत्सवच्चतुरः स्तनान् । न पावनतमं किंचित्सत्यादध्यगमं क्वचित् ॥
data.md: Like a calf sucking all the four teets of its dam's udders, one should devote himself to the practice of all these virtues. I do not know whether anything exists more sacred than Truth.

data.v: आचक्षेऽहं मनुष्येभ्यो देवेभ्यः प्रतिसंचरन् । सत्यं स्वर्गस्य सोपानं पारावारस्य नौरिव ॥
data.md: Having walked among both human beings and the gods, I say that Truth is the only means for reaching heaven even as a ship is the only means for crossing deep.

data.v: यादृशैः संनिवसति यादृशांश्चोपसेवते । यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः ॥
data.md: A person becomes like those with whom he lives, and like those whom he respects, and like to what he wishes to be.

data.v: यदि सन्तं सेवते यद्यसन्तं; तपस्विनं यदि वा स्तेनमेव । वासो यथा रङ्गवशं प्रयाति; तथा स तेषां वशमभ्युपैति ॥
data.md: If a person waits respectfully on him who is good, or him who is otherwise, if he waits respectfully on a sage endued with ascetic merit or on a thief, passes under his control and gets his colour like a piece of cloth catching the dye in which it is washed.

data.v: सदा देवाः साधुभिः संवदन्ते; न मानुषं विषयं यान्ति द्रष्टुम् । नेन्दुः समः स्यादसमो हि वायु;रुच्चावचं विषयं यः स वेद ॥
data.md: The gods always talk with those who are good and wise. They, therefore, never entertain the desire for even seeing the enjoyments in which men take pleasure. The person who knows that all objects of enjoyment are subject to changes, has few rivals, and is superior to the very Moon and Wind.

data.v: अदुष्टं वर्तमाने तु हृदयान्तरपूरुषे । तेनैव देवाः प्रीयन्ते सतां मार्गस्थितेन वै ॥
data.md: When the Purusha that lives in one's heart is pure, and walks in the path of the righteous, the gods take a pleasure in him.

data.v: शिश्नोदरे येऽभिरताः सदैव; स्तेना नरा वाक्परुषाश्च नित्यम् । अपेतदोषानिति तान्विदित्वा; दूराद्देवाः संपरिवर्जयन्ति ॥
data.md: The gods shun from a distance those who are always devoted to the gratification of their senses of pleasure and the stomach, who are given to thieving, and who always indulge in harsh words, even if they expiate their offences by performing the proper rites.

data.v: न वै देवा हीनसत्त्वेन तोष्याः; सर्वाशिना दुष्कृतकर्मणा वा । सत्यव्रता ये तु नराः कृतज्ञा; धर्मे रतास्तैः सह संभजन्ते ॥
data.md: The god are never gratified with one of mean soul, with one who observes no restraint in the matter of food, and with one who is of sinful deeds. On the other hand, the gods associate with those men who observe the vow of truth, who are grateful, and who are engaged in the practice of virtue.

data.v: अव्याहृतं व्याहृताच्छ्रेय आहुः; सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् । धर्मं वदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं; प्रियं वदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम् ॥
data.md: Silence is better than speech. To speak the truth is better than silence. To speak, again, truth what is connected with virtue is better than to speak the truth. To speak what, besides being true and righteous is agrecable, is better than to speak truth connected with virtue.

data.v: केनायमावृतो लोकः केन वा न प्रकाशते । केन त्यजति मित्राणि केन स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥
data.md: The Saddhyas said, By what is this world covered? Why does one fail to shine? For what cause do people renounce their friends? Why do people fail to go to heaven.

data.v: अज्ञानेनावृतो लोको मात्सर्यान्न प्रकाशते । लोभात्त्यजति मित्राणि सङ्गात्स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥
data.md: The Saddhyas said, By what is this world covered? Why does one fail to shine? For what cause do people renounce their friends? Why do people fail to go to heaven.

data.v: कः स्विदेको रमते ब्राह्मणानां; कः स्विदेको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते । कः स्विदेको बलवान्दुर्बलोऽपि; कः स्विदेषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥
data.md: Who alone among the Brahmanas is always happy? Who alone amongst them can practise the vow of silence though living in the midst of many? Who alone amongst them, though weak, is still considered as strong? And who alone amongst them does not quarrel.

data.v: प्राज्ञ एको रमते ब्राह्मणानां; प्राज्ञ एको बहुभिर्जोषमास्ते । प्राज्ञ एको बलवान्दुर्बलोऽपि; प्राज्ञ एषां कलहं नान्ववैति ॥
data.md: Who alone among the Brahmanas is always happy? Who alone amongst them can practise the vow of silence though living in the midst of many? Who alone amongst them, though weak, is still considered as strong? And who alone amongst them does not quarrel.

data.v: किं ब्राह्मणानां देवत्वं किं च साधुत्वमुच्यते । असाधुत्वं च किं तेषां किमेषां मानुषं मतम् ॥
data.md: The Saddhyas said Wherein lies the divinity of the Brahmanas? In what their purity? In what their impurity? And in what their status of humanity?

data.v: स्वाध्याय एषां देवत्वं व्रतं साधुत्वमुच्यते । असाधुत्वं परीवादो मृत्युर्मानुषमुच्यते ॥
data.md: The Swan said The divinity of the Brahmanas consists in the study of the Vedas. Their purity is in their status of humanity?

data.v: संवाद इत्ययं श्रेष्ठः साध्यानां परिकीर्तितः । क्षेत्रं वै कर्मणां योनिः सद्भावः सत्यमुच्यते ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Thus have I recited to you the excellent discourse between the Saddhyas (and the Swan). The body is the origin of acts, and existence or individual Soul is truth.

data.v: सांख्ये योगे च मे तात विशेषं वक्तुमर्हसि । तव सर्वज्ञ सर्वं हि विदितं कुरुसत्तम ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said You should explain to me, O sire, what the difference is between the Sankhya and the Yoga systems of philosophy. O foremost one of Kuru's race, you know everything is known, O you who are conversant with all duties.

data.v: सांख्याः सांख्यं प्रशंसन्ति योगा योगं द्विजातयः । वदन्ति कारणैः श्रैष्ठ्यं स्वपक्षोद्भावनाय वै ॥
data.md: Bhishma said The followers of Sankhya praise the Sankhya system and the Yogins praise the Yoga system. For fixing the superiority of their respective systems, each calls his own system to be better.

data.v: अनीश्वरः कथं मुच्येदित्येवं शत्रुकर्शन । वदन्ति कारणैः श्रैष्ठ्यं योगाः सम्यङ्मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: Wise men devoted to Yoga point out proper and very good reasons, O crusher of enemies, for showing that one who does not believe in the existence of God cannot acquire Liberation.

data.v: वदन्ति कारणं चेदं सांख्याः सम्यग्द्विजातयः । विज्ञायेह गतीः सर्वा विरक्तो विषयेषु यः ॥
data.md: Those twice-born ones, again, who are believers in the Sankhya doctrines forward good reasons for showing that a person by acquiring true knowledge of all objects, becomes dissociated from all earthly objects, and, after death, it is plain, becomes liberated and that it cannot be otherwise. Men of great wisdom have thus expounded the Sankhya philosophy of Liberation.

data.v: ऊर्ध्वं स देहात्सुव्यक्तं विमुच्येदिति नान्यथा । एतदाहुर्महाप्राज्ञाः सांख्यं वै मोक्षदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: Those twice-born ones, again, who are believers in the Sankhya doctrines forward good reasons for showing that a person by acquiring true knowledge of all objects, becomes dissociated from all earthly objects, and, after death, it is plain, becomes liberated and that it cannot be otherwise. Men of great wisdom have thus expounded the Sankhya philosophy of Liberation.

data.v: स्वपक्षे कारणं ग्राह्यं समर्थं वचनं हितम् । शिष्टानां हि मतं ग्राह्यं त्वद्विधैः शिष्टसंमतैः ॥
data.md: When reasons are thus equally placed on both sides, those are assigned on that side which one is otherwise inclined to follow as one's own, should be accepted. Indeed, those words that are said on that side should be considered as wholesome. Good men may be found on both sides. Persons like you may adot either opinion.

data.v: प्रत्यक्षहेतवो योगाः सांख्याः शास्त्रविनिश्चयाः । उभे चैते मते तत्त्वे मम तात युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: The evidences of Yoga are addressed to the direct perception of the senses; those of Sankhya are based on the scriptures. Both I systems of philosophy are approved by me, O Yudhishthira.

data.v: उभे चैते मते ज्ञाने नृपते शिष्टसंमते । अनुष्ठिते यथाशास्त्रं नयेतां परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: agree with noth those systems of science, O king, so do the good and wise. If practised duly according to the instructions laid down, both would, O king, make a person acquire the highest end. In both systems purity is equally recommended as also mercy towards all creatures, O sinless one. In both, again, the observance of vows has been equally sanctioned. Only the scriptures which point out their paths are different.

data.v: तुल्यं शौचं तयोर्युक्तं दया भूतेषु चानघ । व्रतानां धारणं तुल्यं दर्शनं न समं तयोः ॥
data.md: agree with noth those systems of science, O king, so do the good and wise. If practised duly according to the instructions laid down, both would, O king, make a person acquire the highest end. In both systems purity is equally recommended as also mercy towards all creatures, O sinless one. In both, again, the observance of vows has been equally sanctioned. Only the scriptures which point out their paths are different.

data.v: यदि तुल्यं व्रतं शौचं दया चात्र पितामह । तुल्यं न दर्शनं कस्मात्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said If the vows, the purity, the mercy, and the fruits thereof recommended in both systems be the same, tell me, O grandfather, why then are not their scriptures the same?

data.v: रागं मोहं तथा स्नेहं कामं क्रोधं च केवलम् । योगाच्छित्त्वादितो दोषान्पञ्चैतान्प्राप्नुवन्ति तत् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said By renouncing through the help of Yoga, these five faults, viz., attachment carelessness, affection, lust and anger one acquires Liberation.

data.v: यथा चानिमिषाः स्थूला जालं छित्त्वा पुनर्जलम् । प्राप्नुवन्ति तथा योगास्तत्पदं वीतकल्मषाः ॥
data.md: As large fishes, breaking through the net pass into their own element, similarly, Yogins, become purged of all sins and acquire the happiness of Liberation.

data.v: तथैव वागुरां छित्त्वा बलवन्तो यथा मृगाः । प्राप्नुयुर्विमलं मार्गं विमुक्ताः सर्वबन्धनैः ॥
data.md: As powerful animals breaking through the nets in which hunters catch them, enjoy the men happiness of freedom, so Yogins freed from all fetters, attain to the pure path that leads of Liberation.

data.v: लोभजानि तथा राजन्बन्धनानि बलान्विताः । छित्त्वा योगाः परं मार्गं गच्छन्ति विमलाः शिवम् ॥
data.md: Truly, O king, breaking through the fetter born of cupidity, Yogins, gifted with strength acquire the sinless and auspicious and high path of Liberation.

data.v: अबलाश्च मृगा राजन्वागुरासु तथापरे । विनश्यन्ति न संदेहस्तद्वद्योगबलादृते ॥
data.md: Feeble animals, O king, entangled in nets, are, forsooth, destroyed. Such is the case with persons shorn of Yoga power.

data.v: बलहीनाश्च कौन्तेय यथा जालगता झषाः । अन्तं गच्छन्ति राजेन्द्र तथा योगाः सुदुर्बलाः ॥
data.md: As weak fishes, O son of Kunti, fallen into the net, become entangled in it, so, O king, shorn of Yoga power meet with destruction.

data.v: यथा च शकुनाः सूक्ष्माः प्राप्य जालमरिंदम । तत्र सक्ता विपद्यन्ते मुच्यन्ते च बलान्विताः ॥
data.md: As birds, O chastiser of enemies, when entangled in the fine nets of fowlers, meet with their destruction, but if they are strong effect their escape, similarly, it is the case with Yogins, O chastiser of enemies, fettered by the bonds of action, they that are weak meet with destruction, while they who are strong break through them.

data.v: कर्मजैर्बन्धनैर्बद्धास्तद्वद्योगाः परंतप । अबला वै विनश्यन्ति मुच्यन्ते च बलान्विताः ॥
data.md: As birds, O chastiser of enemies, when entangled in the fine nets of fowlers, meet with their destruction, but if they are strong effect their escape, similarly, it is the case with Yogins, O chastiser of enemies, fettered by the bonds of action, they that are weak meet with destruction, while they who are strong break through them.

data.v: अल्पकश्च यथा राजन्वह्निः शाम्यति दुर्बलः । आक्रान्त इन्धनैः स्थूलैस्तद्वद्योगोऽबलः प्रभो ॥

data.md: The same fire, however, O king, when it becomes strong, would burn with the help of the wind the entire Earth.

data.md: Similarly, the Yogin when grown in strength, burning with energy, and endued with power is capable of scorching the entire Universe like the Sun that rises at the time of the universal dissolution.

data.md: As a man, fixing his mind on a vessel full of some liquid carefully ascends a flight of steps, so the Yogin, fixed and absorbed in his soul, purifies it and marks it as effulgent as the Sun.

data.md: As a boat, O son of Kunti, who is tossed on the bosom of the sea is very soon taken by a careful boatman to the other shore, so the man of knowledge by fixing his soul in concentration, acquires Liberation, which is so difficult to acquire, after renouncing his body, O king.

data.md: Vision is attached to form; the sense of scent to smells; the ear to sound; the tongue to juices; and the skin to touch. The Wind has for its refuge Ether. Stupefaction has Darkness for its refuge. Cupidity has the objects of the senses for its refuge.

data.md: Vision is attached to form; the sense of scent to smells; the ear to sound; the tongue to juices; and the skin to touch. The Wind has for its refuge Ether. Stupefaction has Darkness for its refuge. Cupidity has the objects of the senses for its refuge.

data.v: विष्णुं क्रान्ते बले शक्रं कोष्ठे सक्तं तथानलम् । अप्सु देवीं तथा सक्तामपस्तेजसि चाश्रिताः ॥
data.md: Vishnu is attached to (the organs of) motion. Indra is attached to (the organs of) strength. The god of fire is attached to the stomach. Earth is attached to the Waters. The Waters have fire for their refuge.

data.v: तेजो वायौ तु संसक्तं वायुं नभसि चाश्रितम् । नभो महति संयुक्तं महद्बुद्धौ च संश्रितम् ॥
data.md: Heat attaches itself to the Wind; and the Wind has Ether for its refuge; and Space has the principle of greatness for its refuge; and the principle of greatness has Understanding for its basis.

data.v: बुद्धिं तमसि संसक्तां तमो रजसि चाश्रितम् । रजः सत्त्वे तथा सक्तं सत्त्वं सक्तं तथात्मनि ॥
data.md: The Understanding has its refuge in Darkness; Darkness has Ignorance for its refuge; Rajas is founded upon the quality of goodness and quality of Goodness is attached to the Soul.

data.v: सक्तमात्मानमीशे च देवे नारायणे तथा । देवं मोक्षे च संसक्तं मोक्षं सक्तं तु न क्वचित् ॥
data.md: The Soul has the glorious and powerful goodness Narayana for its refuge. That glorious god has Liberation for his refuge. Liberation is independent of all refuge.

वैतरण्यां च यद्दुःखं पतितानां यमक्षये । योनीषु च विचित्रासु संसारानशुभांस्तथा ॥
जठरे चाशुभे वासं शोणितोदकभाजने । श्लेष्ममूत्रपुरीषे च तीव्रगन्धसमन्विते ॥

विज्ञायाहितमात्मानं योगांश्च विविधान्नृप । तामसानां च जन्तूनां रमणीयावृतात्मनाम् ॥
सात्त्विकानां च जन्तूनां कुत्सितं भरतर्षभ । गर्हितं महतामर्थे सांख्यानां विदितात्मनाम् ॥
उपप्लवांस्तथा घोराञ्शशिनस्तेजसस्तथा । ताराणां पतनं दृष्ट्वा नक्षत्राणां च पर्ययम् ॥

बहुमानमलब्धेषु लब्धे मध्यस्थतां पुनः । विषयाणां च दौरात्म्यं विज्ञाय नृपते पुनः ॥
गतासूनां च कौन्तेय देहान्दृष्ट्वा तथाशुभान् । वासं कुलेषु जन्तूनां दुःखं विज्ञाय भारत ॥

data.md: Yudhishthira said O you of immeasurable energy, what are those faults which you see in one's body? You should explain this doubt to me fully and truly.

data.md: Bhishma said Listen, O killer of enemies, the Sankhyas or followers of Kapila, who are conversant with all paths and gifted with wisdom, say that there are in all five faults, O powerful one, in the human, body.

data.v: कामक्रोधौ भयं निद्रा पञ्चमः श्वास उच्यते । एते दोषाः शरीरेषु दृश्यन्ते सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥
data.md: They are Desire, Anger, Fear, Sleep and Breath. These faults are seen in the bodies of all embodied creatures. They who are gifted with wisdom cut the root of anger with the help of Forgiveness. Desire is cut off by renouncing all purposes.

data.v: छिन्दन्ति क्षमया क्रोधं कामं संकल्पवर्जनात् । सत्त्वसंशीलनान्निद्रामप्रमादाद्भयं तथा । छिन्दन्ति पञ्चमं श्वासं लघ्वाहारतया नृप ॥
data.md: By cultivation of the quality of Goodness (Sattva) sleep is conquered and Fear in conquered by cultivating carefulness. Breath is conquered by restriction of diet, О king.

data.md: The Sun-god then bears, with his rays, those pious men who prastise the Sankhya doctrines. Like the fibres of the lotus-stalk carrying water to the flower into which they all converge, the Sun-God, drinking all things from the universe, conveys them to those good and wise men.

data.md: Darkness then carries them to the highest end of Goodness. Goodness then bears them,O you of pure soul, to the Supreme and powerful Narayana.

data.v: परमात्मानमासाद्य तद्भूतायतनामलाः । अमृतत्वाय कल्पन्ते न निवर्तन्ति चाभिभो । परमा सा गतिः पार्थ निर्द्वंद्वानां महात्मनाम् ॥
data.md: The powerful and pure-souled Narayana at last through himself, carries them to the Supreme Soul, those pure persons, who have become the body of Brahman, attain to immortality, and they have never afterwards to come back from that position, O King! That is the highest end, O son of Pritha, which is acquired by those great men who have got over the influence of all pairs of opposites.

data.v: स्थानमुत्तममासाद्य भगवन्तं स्थिरव्रताः । आजन्ममरणं वा ते स्मरन्त्युत न वानघ ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said O pure one, have those persons of firm Vows, after they have acquired that excellent position which is fraught with power and happiness, and recollection of their lives including birth and death?

If, again, consciousness disappear from the liberated state and one who has become liberated only resembles a person sunk in dreamless slumber, then nothing can be more improper than to say that there is really no consciousness in Liberation.

If, again, consciousness disappear from the liberated state and one who has become liberated only resembles a person sunk in dreamless slumber, then nothing can be more improper than to say that there is really no consciousness in Liberation.

data.v: यथान्यायं त्वया तात प्रश्नः पृष्टः सुसंकटः । बुद्धानामपि संमोहः प्रश्नेऽस्मिन्भरतर्षभ । अत्रापि तत्त्वं परमं शृणु सम्यङ्मयेरितम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said “However difficult it may be to answer it, the question which you have asked, O son, is proper. Verily, the question is of such a nature that even the highly learned men become stupefied in answering it, O chief of Bharata's racc.

data.v: बुद्धिश्च परमा यत्र कापिलानां महात्मनाम् । इन्द्रियाण्यपि बुध्यन्ते स्वदेहं देहिनो नृप । कारणान्यात्मनस्तानि सूक्ष्मः पश्यति तैस्तु सः ॥
data.md: The senses of knowledge, O king, placed in the bodies of embodied creatures, are engaged in their respective functions of perception. They form the instruments of the Soul, for it through them that subtile Being perceives.

data.v: आत्मना विप्रहीणानि काष्ठकुड्यसमानि तु । विनश्यन्ति न संदेहः फेना इव महार्णवे ॥
data.md: Disassociated from the Soul, the senses are like pieces of wood, and are, forsooth, destroyed like the forth that is seen on the bosom of the ocean.

data.v: इन्द्रियैः सह सुप्तस्य देहिनः शत्रुतापन । सूक्ष्मश्चरति सर्वत्र नभसीव समीरणः ॥
data.md: When the embodied creature, O scorcher of enemies, goes into sleep together with his senses, the subtile Soul then roves among all objects like the wind through ether.

data.v: स पश्यति यथान्यायं स्पर्शान्स्पृशति चाभिभो । बुध्यमानो यथापूर्वमखिलेनेह भारत ॥
data.md: The Subtile Soul, during sleep continues to see and touch all objects of touch, O king, and get other perceptions, as well as when it is awake.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणीह सर्वाणि स्वे स्वे स्थाने यथाविधि । अनीशत्वात्प्रलीयन्ते सर्पा हतविषा इव ॥
data.md: On account of their inability to act without their director, the senses, during slumber, all become extinguished in their respective places like snakes shorn of poison.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणां तु सर्वेषां स्वस्थानेष्वेव सर्वशः । आक्रम्य गतयः सूक्ष्माश्चरत्यात्मा न संशयः ॥
data.md: At such times, the subtile Soul, repairing into the respective places of all the senses, forsooth, performs all their functions,

data.v: सत्त्वस्य च गुणान्कृत्स्नान्रजसश्च गुणान्पुनः । गुणांश्च तमसः सर्वान्गुणान्बुद्धेश्च भारत ॥
गुणांश्च मनसस्तद्वन्नभसश्च गुणांस्तथा । गुणान्वायोश्च धर्मात्मंस्तेजसश्च गुणान्पुनः ॥
अपां गुणांस्तथा पार्थ पार्थिवांश्च गुणानपि । सर्वात्मना गुणैर्व्याप्य क्षेत्रज्ञः स युधिष्ठिर ॥
आत्मा च याति क्षेत्रज्ञं कर्मणी च शुभाशुभे । शिष्या इव महात्मानमिन्द्रियाणि च तं विभो ॥
प्रकृतिं चाप्यतिक्रम्य गच्छत्यात्मानमव्ययम् । परं नारायणात्मानं निर्द्वंद्वं प्रकृतेः परम् ॥
data.md: When the individual Soul, transcends Prakriti, it acquires Brahma that is changeless, that is highest, that is Narayana that is beyond all pairs of opposites, and that is above Nature.

data.v: विमुक्तः पुण्यपापेभ्यः प्रविष्टस्तमनामयम् । परमात्मानमगुणं न निवर्तति भारत ॥
data.md: Freed from both merit and demerit, the individual Soul, entering the Supreme Soul which is shorn of all attributes, and which is the home of all auspiciousness, does not return thence, O Bharata.

data.v: शिष्टं त्वत्र मनस्तात इन्द्रियाणि च भारत । आगच्छन्ति यथाकालं गुरोः संदेशकारिणः ॥
data.md: These remains, O son, only the mind with the senses, O Bharata. These have to return once more at the appointed time for satisfying the command of their great Master.

data.v: शक्यं चाल्पेन कालेन शान्तिं प्राप्तुं गुणार्थिना । एवं युक्तेन कौन्तेय युक्तज्ञानेन मोक्षिणा ॥
data.md: Soon after, O son of Kunti, cast off the Yati striving after Liberation, gifted as he is with knowledge and desirous as he is of quality, succeeds in attaining to that peace of Liberation which one enjoys without the body.

data.v: सांख्या राजन्महाप्राज्ञा गच्छन्ति परमां गतिम् । ज्ञानेनानेन कौन्तेय तुल्यं ज्ञानं न विद्यते ॥
data.md: The Sankhyas, O king, are gifted with great wisdom. They acquire the highest end by means of this kind of knowledge. There is no knowledge that is equal to this.

data.v: अत्र ते संशयो मा भूज्ज्ञानं सांख्यं परं मतम् । अक्षरं ध्रुवमव्यक्तं पूर्वं ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥
data.md: Do not give way to any sort of doubt. The Knowledge which is described in the system of the Sankhyas is considered all the highest. That knowledge is immutable and is eternal. It is eternal Brahma.

data.v: अनादिमध्यनिधनं निर्द्वंद्वं कर्तृ शाश्वतम् । कूटस्थं चैव नित्यं च यद्वदन्ति शमात्मकाः ॥
data.md: It has no beginning, middle, and end. It is above all pairs of opposites. It is the cause of the creation of the universe. It stands fully. It is without decrease of any kind. It is uniform, and everlasting. Thus are its praises recited by the wise.

data.v: यतः सर्वाः प्रवर्तन्ते सर्गप्रलयविक्रियाः । यच्च शंसन्ति शास्त्रेषु वदन्ति परमर्षयः ॥
data.md: From it originate creation and destruction and all metamorphoses. The great Rishis speak of it and praise it in the scriptures.

data.v: सर्वे विप्राश्च देवाश्च तथागमविदो जनाः । ब्रह्मण्यं परमं देवमनन्तं परतोऽच्युतम् ॥
data.md: All learned Brahmanas and all the gods and all pious men consider it as originating from Brahma. Supreme, Divine, Infinite, Immutable, and Undeteriorating.

data.v: प्रार्थयन्तश्च तं विप्रा वदन्ति गुणबुद्धयः । सम्यग्युक्तास्तथा योगाः सांख्याश्चामितदर्शनाः ॥
data.md: All Brahmanas, again, who are attached to objects of the senses worship and applaud it by ascribing to it attributes that belong to illusion. The same is the opinion of Yogins well observant of penances and meditation and of Sankhyas of great insight.

data.v: अमूर्तेस्तस्य कौन्तेय सांख्यं मूर्तिरिति श्रुतिः । अभिज्ञानानि तस्याहुर्मतं हि भरतर्षभ ॥
data.md: The Shrutis say, O son of Kunti, that the Sankhya system of philosophy is the form of that Formless One. The cognition have, O chief of Bharata's race, been said to be the knowledge of Brahma.

data.v: द्विविधानीह भूतानि पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपते । जङ्गमागमसंज्ञानि जङ्गमं तु विशिष्यते ॥
data.md: There are two kinds of creatures on Earth, O king, viz., mobile and immobile. Of these, those that are mobile are superior.

data.v: ज्ञानं महद्यद्धि महत्सु राज;न्वेदेषु सांख्येषु तथैव योगे । यच्चापि दृष्टं विविधं पुराणं; सांख्यागतं तन्निखिलं नरेन्द्र ॥
data.md: That high knowledge, O king, which is in persons conversant with Brahma, and that which is in the Vedas, and that which is seen in other scriptures, and that in Yoga, and that which may be seen in the various Puranas, are all, O monarch, to be found in Sankhya philosophy.

data.v: यच्चेतिहासेषु महत्सु दृष्टं; यच्चार्थशास्त्रे नृप शिष्टजुष्टे । ज्ञानं च लोके यदिहास्ति किंचि;त्सांख्यागतं तच्च महन्महात्मन् ॥
data.md: Whatever knowledge is seen to exist in great histories, whatever knowledge is, O king, in the sciences about the acquisition of riches as approved by the wise, whatever other knowledge exists in this world,-all these,-originate, O great king, from the high knowledge that is among the Sankhyas.

data.v: शमश्च दृष्टः परमं बलं च; ज्ञानं च सूक्ष्मं च यथावदुक्तम् । तपांसि सूक्ष्माणि सुखानि चैव; सांख्ये यथावद्विहितानि राजन् ॥
data.md: Tranquillity of soul, high power, all subtile knowledge of which the scriptures speak, penances of subtile force, and all sorts of happiness, O king, have all been duly ordained in the Sankhya system,

data.v: विपर्यये तस्य हि पार्थ देवा;न्गच्छन्ति सांख्याः सततं सुखेन । तांश्चानुसंचार्य ततः कृतार्थाः; पतन्ति विप्रेषु यतेषु भूयः ॥
data.md: Failing to acquire, O son of Pritha, that complete knowledge which is recommended by their system, the Sankhyas attain to the dignity of gods and pass many years in happiness. Ruling over the celestials as they will, they fall, upon the expiration of the fixed period, among learned Brahmanas and Yatis.

data.v: हित्वा च देहं प्रविशन्ति मोक्षं; दिवौकसो द्यामिव पार्थ सांख्याः । ततोऽधिकं तेऽभिरता महार्हे; सांख्ये द्विजाः पार्थिव शिष्टजुष्टे ॥
data.md: Renouncing this body, those twice-born ones that follow the Sankhya system enter into the superior state of Brahma like the gods entering into the sky by devoting themselves wholly to that worshipful system which is theirs and which is adored by all wise men.

data.v: तेषां न तिर्यग्गमनं हि दृष्टं; नावाग्गतिः पापकृतां निवासः । न चाबुधानामपि ते द्विजातयो; ये ज्ञानमेतन्नृपतेऽनुरक्ताः ॥
data.md: Those twice-born ones who are given to the acquisition of that knowledge which is recommended in the Sankhya system, even if they fail to acquire eminence, are never seen to fall among intermediate creatures, or to sink into the state of sinful men.

data.v: सांख्यं विशालं परमं पुराणं; महार्णवं विमलमुदारकान्तम् । कृत्स्नं च सांख्यं नृपते महात्मा; नारायणो धारयतेऽप्रमेयम् ॥
data.md: That great person who is fully conversant with the vast, high, ancient, oncean-like, and immeasurable Sankhya system who is pure and liberal and agreeable, becomes, O king, equal to Narayana.

data.v: एतन्मयोक्तं नरदेव तत्त्वं; नारायणो विश्वमिदं पुराणम् । स सर्गकाले च करोति सर्गं; संहारकाले च तदत्ति भूयः ॥
data.md: I have now told you, O god among men, the truth about the Sankhya system. It is the embodiment of Narayana, of the universe as it exists from antiquity. When the time of Creation comes, He causes the Creation to come into being, and when the time comes for destruction. He swallows up everything. Having withdrawn everything into his own body he goes to slumber,-that inner Soul of the universe.

data.v: किं तदक्षरमित्युक्तं यस्मान्नावर्तते पुनः । किं च तत्क्षरमित्युक्तं यस्मादावर्तते पुनः ॥
data.md: What is that which is called Undecaying and by acquiring which no one has to return? What, again, is that which is called Decaying, and by acquiring which one has to return once more?

data.v: अक्षरक्षरयोर्व्यक्तिमिच्छाम्यरिनिषूदन । उपलब्धुं महाबाहो तत्त्वेन कुरुनन्दन ॥
data.md: O destroyer of enemies, I ask you the distinction that exists, O you of mighty arms, between the Decaying and the Undecaying ones for understanding them both truly, O delighter of the Kurus.

data.v: त्वं हि ज्ञाननिधिर्विप्रैरुच्यसे वेदपारगैः । ऋषिभिश्च महाभागैर्यतिभिश्च महात्मभिः ॥
data.md: Brahmans conversant with the Vedas, speak of you as on Ocean of knowledge. Highly blessed Rishis and Yatis of great souls do the Salme.

data.v: शेषमल्पं दिनानां ते दक्षिणायनभास्करे । आवृत्ते भगवत्यर्के गन्तासि परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: You have very few days to live. When the Sun turns from his southern solstice for entering into the northern, you will attain to your high end.

data.v: त्वयि प्रतिगते श्रेयः कुतः श्रोष्यामहे वयम् । कुरुवंशप्रदीपस्त्वं ज्ञानद्रव्येण दीप्यसे ॥
data.md: When you will leave us, from whom shall we hear of all that is wholesome for us? You are the lamp of Kuru's race. Indeed, you are always shining with the light of knowledge.

data.v: तदेतच्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि त्वत्तः कुरुकुलोद्वह । न तृप्यामीह राजेन्द्र शृण्वन्नमृतमीदृशम् ॥
data.md: O perpetuator of Kuru's race, I wish, therefore, to hear all this from you. Listening to your discourses which are always sweet like nectar, my curiosity, without being satiated, is always increasing.

data.v: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्येऽहमितिहासं पुरातनम् । वसिष्ठस्य च संवादं करालजनकस्य च ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it I shall recite to you an old narrative, O Yudhishthira, of the discourse between the Sadhyas and a Swan.

data.v: वसिष्ठं श्रेष्ठमासीनमृषीणां भास्करद्युतिम् । पप्रच्छ जनको राजा ज्ञानं नैःश्रेयसं परम् ॥
data.md: Once on a time when that foremost of Rishis, viz., Vashishtha, effulgent like the Sun, was seated at his ease, king Janaka asked him about that highest knowledge which is for our supreme behoof.

data.v: परमध्यात्मकुशलमध्यात्मगतिनिश्चयम् । मैत्रावरुणिमासीनमभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः ॥
स्वक्षरं प्रश्रितं वाक्यं मधुरं चाप्यनुल्बणम् । पप्रच्छर्षिवरं राजा करालजनकः पुरा ॥
भगवञ्श्रोतुमिच्छामि परं ब्रह्म सनातनम् । यस्मान्न पुनरावृत्तिमाप्नुवन्ति मनीषिणः ॥
यच्च तत्क्षरमित्युक्तं यत्रेदं क्षरते जगत् । यच्चाक्षरमिति प्रोक्तं शिवं क्षेम्यमनामयम् ॥
data.md: I wish also to know that which is called Destructible and That into which this universe goes when destroyed. Indeed, what is That which is said to be indestructible. Auspicious, wholesome and free from all sorts of evil.

data.v: श्रूयतां पृथिवीपाल क्षरतीदं यथा जगत् । यन्न क्षरति पूर्वेण यावत्कालेन चाप्यथ ॥
data.md: Hear, O king, as to how this universe is destroyed, and of That which was never destroyed and which will never be destroyed at any time.

data.v: युगं द्वादशसाहस्रं कल्पं विद्धि चतुर्गुणम् । दशकल्पशतावृत्तं तदहर्ब्राह्ममुच्यते । रात्रिश्चैतावती राजन्यस्यान्ते प्रतिबुध्यते ॥
data.md: Twelve thousand years make a cycle. Four such cycles, taken a thousand times, make a Kalpa which measures one day of Brahman.

data.v: सृजत्यनन्तकर्माणं महान्तं भूतमग्रजम् । मूर्तिमन्तममूर्तात्मा विश्वं शंभुः स्वयंभुवः । अणिमा लघिमा प्राप्तिरीशानं ज्योतिरव्ययम् ॥
data.md: Brahman's night also, O king, is of the same measure. When Brahman himself is destroyed, Shambhu of formless soul and to whom the Yoga attributes of lightness, heaviness, etc., naturally stick, awakes, and once more creates that First of all creatures, possessed of huge proportions, of infinite deeds, endued with form, and at one with the universe. That Shambhu is otherwise called Ishana. He is pure Effulgence, and is above all decay, having his hands and feet stretching on all sides with eyes and head and mouth cverywhere, and with ears also in every place. That Being exists, possessing the entire universe.

data.v: सर्वतःपाणिपादान्तं सर्वतोक्षिशिरोमुखम् । सर्वतःश्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
data.md: His hands and feet extend over every part his eyes and head and face are everywhere, his reach every places, and he exists possessing all things.

data.v: हिरण्यगर्भो भगवानेष बुद्धिरिति स्मृतः । महानिति च योगेषु विरिञ्च इति चाप्युत ॥
data.md: The eldest-born Being is called Hiranyagarbha. This holy one has been called the Understanding. In the Yoga scriptures, He is called the Great, and Virinchi, and the Unborn.

data.v: सांख्ये च पठ्यते शास्त्रे नामभिर्बहुधात्मकः । विचित्ररूपो विश्वात्मा एकाक्षर इति स्मृतः ॥
data.md: In the Sankhya system, He is described by diverse names, and considered as having Infinity for his Soul. Of various forms and constituting the soul of the universe, He is considered as One and Indestructible.

data.v: वृतं नैकात्मकं येन कृत्स्नं त्रैलोक्यमात्मना । तथैव बहुरूपत्वाद्विश्वरूप इति स्मृतः ॥
data.md: The three worlds of numberless ingredients have been created by Him without help from any source and have been overwhelmed by him. On account of His manifold forins, He is said to be of universal form.

data.v: एष वै विक्रियापन्नः सृजत्यात्मानमात्मना । अहंकारं महातेजाः प्रजापतिमहंकृतम् ॥
data.md: Undergoing changes He creates Himself. Gifted with great energy, He first creates Consciousness and that Great Being called Prajapati endued with Consciousness.

data.v: अव्यक्ताद्व्यक्तमुत्पन्नं विद्यासर्गं वदन्ति तम् । महान्तं चाप्यहंकारमविद्यासर्गमेव च ॥
data.md: The Manifest is created from the Unmanifest. This is called by the learned the Creation of Knowledge. The creation of (Virat) and Consciousness, by Hiranyagarbha, is the Creation of Ignorance.

data.v: अविधिश्च विधिश्चैव समुत्पन्नौ तथैकतः । विद्याविद्येति विख्याते श्रुतिशास्त्रार्थचिन्तकैः ॥
data.md: Allotment of attributes and the destruction thereof, called respectively by the names of Ignorance and Knowledge by persons learned in the Shrutis, then arose, referring to this, that, or the other of the three.

data.v: भूतसर्गमहंकारात्तृतीयं विद्धि पार्थिव । अहंकारेषु भूतेषु चतुर्थं विद्धि वैकृतम् ॥
data.md: Know, O king, that the creation of the elements from Consciousness is the third. In all the kinds of Consciousness is the fourth creation which originates from modification of the third.

data.v: वायुर्ज्योतिरथाकाशमापोऽथ पृथिवी तथा । शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धस्तथैव च ॥
data.md: This fourth creation consists of Wind and Light and Ether and Water and Earth, with their properties of sound, touch, form, taste, and scent. arose

data.v: एवं युगपदुत्पन्नं दशवर्गमसंशयम् । पञ्चमं विद्धि राजेन्द्र भौतिकं सर्गमर्थवत् ॥
data.md: This aggregate of ten arose, forsooth, at the same time. The fifth creation, O king, is that which has originated, from combinations of the principal elements.

data.v: श्रोत्रं त्वक्चक्षुषी जिह्वा घ्राणमेव च पञ्चमम् । वाक्च हस्तौ च पादौ च पायुर्मेढ्रं तथैव च ॥
data.md: This comprises the ear, the skin, the eyes, the tongue, and the nose forming the fifth, and speech, and the two hands, and the two legs, and the lower canal, and the organs of generation.

data.v: बुद्धीन्द्रियाणि चैतानि तथा कर्मेन्द्रियाणि च । संभूतानीह युगपन्मनसा सह पार्थिव ॥
data.md: The first five of those form the organs of knowledge, and the last five the organs of action. All these, with mind, simultaneously, O king.

data.v: एषा तत्त्वचतुर्विंशा सर्वाकृतिषु वर्तते । यां ज्ञात्वा नाभिशोचन्ति ब्राह्मणास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: These form the twenty-four topics that exist in the forms of all living creatures. By understanding these properly. these properly. Brahmanas endued with insight into the truth have never to give way to sorrow.

data.v: एतद्देहं समाख्यातं त्रैलोक्ये सर्वदेहिषु । वेदितव्यं नरश्रेष्ठ सदेवनरदानवे ॥
सयक्षभूतगन्धर्वे सकिंनरमहोरगे । सचारणपिशाचे वै सदेवर्षिनिशाचरे ॥
सदंशकीटमशके सपूतिकृमिमूषके । शुनि श्वपाके वैणेये सचण्डाले सपुल्कसे ॥
हस्त्यश्वखरशार्दूले सवृक्षे गवि चैव ह । यच्च मूर्तिमयं किंचित्सर्वत्रैतन्निदर्शनम् ॥
जले भुवि तथाकाशे नान्यत्रेति विनिश्चयः । स्थानं देहवतामस्ति इत्येवमनुशुश्रुम ॥
कृत्स्नमेतावतस्तात क्षरते व्यक्तसंज्ञकम् । अहन्यहनि भूतात्मा ततः क्षर इति स्मृतः ॥
data.md: All these, O sire, included within the class called Manifest, are seen to be destroyed day after day. Hence, all creatures begotten by union of these twenty-four are said to be destructible.

data.v: एतदक्षरमित्युक्तं क्षरतीदं यथा जगत् । जगन्मोहात्मकं प्राहुरव्यक्तं व्यक्तसंज्ञकम् ॥
data.md: This then is the Indestructible. And since the universe, which is made up of Manifest and Unmanifest, is destroyed, therefore, it is said to be Destructible.

data.v: महांश्चैवाग्रजो नित्यमेतत्क्षरनिदर्शनम् । कथितं ते महाराज यस्मान्नावर्तते पुनः ॥
data.md: The Very Being called Mahan who is the first born is always spoken of as an instance of the Destructible. I have now told you, O king, all that you had asked me.

data.v: पञ्चविंशतिमो विष्णुर्निस्तत्त्वस्तत्त्वसंज्ञकः । तत्त्वसंश्रयणादेतत्तत्त्वमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: Above the twenty-four topics already referred to is the twenty-fifth called Vishnu. That Vishnu, on account of the absence of all qualities, is not a topic though as that which permeates all the topics, he has been called so by the wise.

data.v: यदमूर्त्यसृजद्व्यक्तं तत्तन्मूर्त्यधितिष्ठति । चतुर्विंशतिमो व्यक्तो ह्यमूर्तः पञ्चविंशकः ॥
data.md: Since that which is destructible has caused all this that is Manifest, therefore, all this is gifted with form. The twenty-fourth, which is Nature, is said to lord over all this. The twentyfifth, which is Vishnu, is formless and, therefore, cannot be said to lord over the universe.

data.v: स एव हृदि सर्वासु मूर्तिष्वातिष्ठतेऽऽत्मवान् । चेतयंश्चेतनो नित्यः सर्वमूर्तिरमूर्तिमान् ॥
data.md: It is that Unmanifest, which, when endued with body lives in the hearts of all creatures having body. As regards eternal Consciousness, although he is shorn of attributes and without form, yet he assumes all forins.

data.v: सर्गप्रलयधर्मिण्या असर्गप्रलयात्मकः । गोचरे वर्तते नित्यं निर्गुणो गुणसंज्ञकः ॥
data.md: Uniting with Nature which has has the attributes of birth and death, he also assumes the attributes of birth and death. And on account of such union he becomes an object of perception and though in reality shorn of all attributes yet he coines to be invested therewith.

data.v: एवमेष महानात्मा सर्गप्रलयकोविदः । विकुर्वाणः प्रकृतिमानभिमन्यत्यबुद्धिमान् ॥
data.md: It is in this way that the Soul, becoming united with Nature and invested with Ignorance, undergoes changes and becomes conscious of Self.

data.v: तमःसत्त्वरजोयुक्तस्तासु तास्विह योनिषु । लीयतेऽप्रतिबुद्धत्वादबुद्धजनसेवनात् ॥
data.md: Uniting with the qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance, he becomes at one with various creatures belonging to various orders of Being, on account of his forgetfulness and his waiting upon Ignorance.

data.v: सहवासो निवासात्मा नान्योऽहमिति मन्यते । योऽहं सोऽहमिति ह्युक्त्वा गुणाननु निवर्तते ॥
data.md: On account of his birth and death originating from the fact of living in union with Nature, he thinks himself to be no other than what he apparently is, Knowing himself as this or that, he follows the qualities of Goodness, Darkness and Ignorance.

data.v: तमसा तामसान्भावान्विविधान्प्रतिपद्यते । रजसा राजसांश्चैव सात्त्विकान्सत्त्वसंश्रयात् ॥
data.md: Under the influence of Ignorance, he comes by various kinds of conditions which are affected by Ignorance. Under the influences of Darkness and Goodness he attains likewise to conditions which are affected by Darkness and Goodness.

data.v: शुक्ललोहितकृष्णानि रूपाण्येतानि त्रीणि तु । सर्वाण्येतानि रूपाणि जानीहि प्राकृतानि वै ॥
data.md: There are three colours in all viz., White, Red, and Dark. All those colours belong to Nature.

data.v: तामसा निरयं यान्ति राजसा मानुषांस्तथा । सात्त्विका देवलोकाय गच्छन्ति सुखभागिनः ॥
