data.v: परमेष्ठी त्वहंकारोऽसृजद्भूतानि पञ्चधा । पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम् ॥
data.md: The powerful Consciousness created the five elements. These are Earth, Wind, Ether, Water, and Light as the fifth.

data.v: एतस्यापि निशामाहुस्तृतीयमिह कुर्वतः । पञ्च कल्पसहस्राणि तावदेवाहरुच्यते ॥
data.md: This Consciousness from whom originates the third creation, has five thousand Kalpas for his night, and his day is of equal duration.

data.v: शब्दः स्पर्शश्च रूपं च रसो गन्धश्च पञ्चमः । एते विशेषा राजेन्द्र महाभूतेषु पञ्चसु । यैराविष्टानि भूतानि अहन्यहनि पार्थिव ॥
data.md: Sound, Touch, Form. Taste, and Scent,-these five are called Vishesha. They inhere into the five great elements.

data.v: अन्योन्यं स्पृहयन्त्येते अन्योन्यस्य हिते रताः । अन्योन्यमभिमन्यन्ते अन्योन्यस्पर्धिनस्तथा ॥
ते वध्यमाना अन्योन्यं गुणैर्हारिभिरव्ययाः । इहैव परिवर्तन्ते तिर्यग्योनिप्रवेशिनः ॥
त्रीणि कल्पसहस्राणि एतेषामहरुच्यते । रात्रिरेतावती चैव मनसश्च नराधिप ॥
मनश्चरति राजेन्द्र चरितं सर्वमिन्द्रियैः । न चेन्द्रियाणि पश्यन्ति मन एवात्र पश्यति ॥
data.md: Three thousands of Kalpas form their day. Their night also is the same. The Mind roves over all things, O king, guided by the Senses. The Senses do not perceive anything. It is the Mind that perceives through them.

data.v: चक्षुः पश्यति रूपाणि मनसा तु न चक्षुषा । मनसि व्याकुले चक्षुः पश्यन्नपि न पश्यति । तथेन्द्रियाणि सर्वाणि पश्यन्तीत्यभिचक्षते ॥
data.md: The Eye sees forms when helped by the Mind is distracted, the Eye cannot see fully even the object before it.

data.v: मनस्युपरते राजन्निन्द्रियोपरमो भवेत् । न चेन्द्रियव्युपरमे मनस्युपरमो भवेत् । एवं मनःप्रधानानि इन्द्रियाणि विभावयेत् ॥
data.md: When the activity of the Mind, is stopped, the activity of the Senses is also stopped. One should thus consider the Senses to be under the control of the Mind.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणां हि सर्वेषामीश्वरं मन उच्यते । एतद्विशन्ति भूतानि सर्वाणीह महायशाः ॥
data.md: Indeed, the Mind is said to be the Lord of all the Senses. O you of great fame, these are all the twenty elements in the Universe.

data.v: तत्त्वानां सर्गसंख्या च कालसंख्या तथैव च । मया प्रोक्तानुपूर्व्येण संहारमपि मे शृणु ॥
data.md: I have, one after another, told you the order of the creation, with their total number, of the various principles, as also the extent of the duration of each. Hear as I tell you of their destruction.

data.v: यथा संहरते जन्तून्ससर्ज च पुनः पुनः । अनादिनिधनो ब्रह्मा नित्यश्चाक्षर एव च ॥
data.md: Listen to me how Brahman, who is eternal and undeteriorating, and who is without beginning and without end, repeatedly creates and destroys all created objects.

data.v: अहःक्षयमथो बुद्ध्वा निशि स्वप्नमनास्तथा । चोदयामास भगवानव्यक्तोऽहंकृतं नरम् ॥
data.md: When his day expires and night comes, he seeks sleep. At such a time the unmanifest and holy one moves the Being called Maharudra, who is conscious of his great powers.

data.v: ततः शतसहस्रांशुरव्यक्तेनाभिचोदितः । कृत्वा द्वादशधात्मानमादित्यो ज्वलदग्निवत् ॥
data.md: Urged by the unmanifest, that Being, assuming the form of the Sun of hundreds of thousands of rays, divides himself into a dozen parts each resembling a burning fire.

data.v: चतुर्विधं प्रजाजालं निर्दहत्याशु तेजसा । जराय्वण्डस्वेदजातमुद्भिज्जं च नराधिप ॥
data.md: He then consumes with his energy, O king, without any loss of time, the four sorts of created beings, viz., viviparous, oviparious, filth-born, and vegetable.

data.v: एतदुन्मेषमात्रेण विनष्टं स्थाणुजङ्गमम् । कूर्मपृष्ठसमा भूमिर्भवत्यथ समन्ततः ॥
data.md: Within, the twinkling of the eye all mobile and immobile creatures being thus destroyed, the Earth becomes on all sides, bare as a tortoise shell.

data.v: जगद्दग्ध्वामितबलः केवलं जगतीं ततः । अम्भसा बलिना क्षिप्रमापूर्यत समन्ततः ॥
data.md: Having burnt everything on the face of the Earth, Rudra of incomparable might, then quickly fills the bare Earth with Water, possessed of great force.

data.v: ततः कालाग्निमासाद्य तदम्भो याति संक्षयम् । विनष्टेऽम्भसि राजेन्द्र जाज्वलीत्यनलो महान् ॥
data.md: He then creates the cycle-fire which dries up that Water. The Water disappearing, the great element of Fire continues to blaze dreadfully.

data.v: तमप्रमेयोऽतिबलं ज्वलमानं विभावसुम् । ऊष्माणं सर्वभूतानां सप्तार्चिषमथाञ्जसा ॥
data.md: Then comes the powerful Wind of iinmeasurable force, in his eight forms, who devours speedily that blazing fire of transcendent force, possessed of seven flames, and al one with the heat that exists in every crcature. Having devoured that fire, the Wind passes in every direction, upwards, downwards and transversely.

data.v: भक्षयामास बलवान्वायुरष्टात्मको बली । विचरन्नमितप्राणस्तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधस्तथा ॥
data.md: Then comes the powerful Wind of iinmeasurable force, in his eight forms, who devours speedily that blazing fire of transcendent force, possessed of seven flames, and al one with the heat that exists in every crcature. Having devoured that fire, the Wind passes in every direction, upwards, downwards and transversely.

data.v: तमप्रतिबलं भीममाकाशं ग्रसतेऽऽत्मना । आकाशमप्यतिनदन्मनो ग्रसति चारिकम् ॥
data.md: Then Space of inmeasurable existent devours that Wind of transcendent power. Then mind cheerfully devours that immeasurable Space.

data.v: मनो ग्रसति सर्वात्मा सोऽहंकारः प्रजापतिः । अहंकारं महानात्मा भूतभव्यभविष्यवित् ॥
data.md: Then that Lord of all creatures, viz., Consciousness, who is the Soul of everything, devours the Mind. Consciousness in his turn, is devoured by the Great Soul who is conversant with the Past, the Present, and the Future.

data.v: तमप्यनुपमात्मानं विश्वं शंभुः प्रजापतिः । अणिमा लघिमा प्राप्तिरीशानो ज्योतिरव्ययः ॥
data.md: The incomparable Universe is then devoured by Shambhu, that Lord of all things in whom exist the lordly powers of Anima, Laghima, Prapti, etc., and who is considered as Supreme and pure Effulgence that is Iminutable.

data.v: सर्वतःपाणिपादान्तः सर्वतोक्षिशिरोमुखः । सर्वतःश्रुतिमाँल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति ॥
data.md: His hands and feet extend over every part his eyes and head and face are everywhere, his reach every places, and he exists possessing all things.

data.v: हृदयं सर्वभूतानां पर्वणोऽङ्गुष्ठमात्रकः । अनुग्रसत्यनन्तं हि महात्मा विश्वमीश्वरः ॥
data.md: He is the heart of all creatures. He measures a digit of the thumb. That Infinite and Supreme Soul that Lord of all, thus devours the Universe. cars

data.v: ततः समभवत्सर्वमक्षयाव्ययमव्रणम् । भूतभव्यमनुष्याणां स्रष्टारमनघं तथा ॥
data.md: After this, what remains is the Undeteriorating and the Immutable One who is without shortcoming of any sort, who is the Creator of the Past, the Present, and the Future; and who is perfectly faultless.

data.v: एषोऽप्ययस्ते राजेन्द्र यथावत्परिभाषितः । अध्यात्ममधिभूतं च अधिदैवं च श्रूयताम् ॥
data.md: I have thus, O king, duly told you of Destruction. I shall now describe to you the subject of Adhyatma (Spiritual), Adhibhuta (Eternal) and Adhidaivata (Accidental).

data.v: पादावध्यात्ममित्याहुर्ब्राह्मणास्तत्त्वदर्शिनः । गन्तव्यमधिभूतं च विष्णुस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: Brahmanas well read in the subjects of enquiry speak of the two feet as Spiritual, the act of walking as Elemental and Vishnu as Accidental.

data.v: पायुरध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथातत्त्वार्थदर्शिनः । विसर्गमधिभूतं च मित्रस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: Brahmanas well read in the subjects of enquiry speak of the two feet as Spiritual, the act of walking as Elemental and Vishnu as Accidental.

data.v: उपस्थोऽध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथायोगनिदर्शनम् । अधिभूतं तथानन्दो दैवतं च प्रजापतिः ॥
data.md: The organ of generation is called Spiritual. Its agreeable function is called Elemental and Prajapati is its Accidental.

data.v: हस्तावध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथासांख्यनिदर्शनम् । कर्तव्यमधिभूतं तु इन्द्रस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: Brahmanas well read in the subjects of enquiry speak of the two feet as Spiritual, the act of walking as Elemental and Vishnu as Accidental.

data.v: वागध्यात्ममिति प्राहुर्यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनम् । वक्तव्यमधिभूतं तु वह्निस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: The lower duct is Spiritual; its function of throwing out the excreta is Elemental, and Mitra (Surya) is the Accidental.

data.v: चक्षुरध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनम् । रूपमत्राधिभूतं तु सूर्यस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: The lower duct is Spiritual; its function of throwing out the excreta is Elemental, and Mitra (Surya) is the Accidental.

data.v: श्रोत्रमध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनम् । शब्दस्तत्राधिभूतं तु दिशस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: The lower duct is Spiritual; its function of throwing out the excreta is Elemental, and Mitra (Surya) is the Accidental.

data.v: जिह्वामध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथातत्त्वनिदर्शनम् । रस एवाधिभूतं तु आपस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: Brahmanas well read in the subjects of enquiry speak of the two feet as Spiritual, the act of walking as Elemental and Vishnu as Accidental.

data.v: घ्राणमध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनम् । गन्ध एवाधिभूतं तु पृथिवी चाधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: The organs of speech are spiritual; the words uttered by them are Elemental; and Agni is their Accidental.

data.v: त्वगध्यात्ममिति प्राहुस्तत्त्वबुद्धिविशारदाः । स्पर्श एवाधिभूतं तु पवनश्चाधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: The skin is Spiritual; touch is its Elemental; and Wind is its Accidental.

data.v: मनोऽध्यात्ममिति प्राहुर्यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनम् । मन्तव्यमधिभूतं तु चन्द्रमाश्चाधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: The hands are Spiritual; their function as represented by acts is Elemental; and Indra is the Accident of those limbs.

data.v: अहंकारिकमध्यात्ममाहुस्तत्त्वनिदर्शनम् । अभिमानोऽधिभूतं तु भवस्तत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: The lower duct is Spiritual; its function of throwing out the excreta is Elemental, and Mitra (Surya) is the Accidental.

data.v: बुद्धिरध्यात्ममित्याहुर्यथावेदनिदर्शनम् । बोद्धव्यमधिभूतं तु क्षेत्रज्ञोऽत्राधिदैवतम् ॥
data.md: The lower duct is Spiritual; its function of throwing out the excreta is Elemental, and Mitra (Surya) is the Accidental.

data.v: एषा ते व्यक्ततो राजन्विभूतिरनुवर्णिता । आदौ मध्ये तथा चान्ते यथातत्त्वेन तत्त्ववित् ॥
data.md: I have thus truly expounded to you, O king, with its details taken individually. The power of the supreme in the beginning, the middle, and the end, O you, who are fully conversant with the nature of the original principles.

data.v: प्रकृतिर्गुणान्विकुरुते स्वच्छन्देनात्मकाम्यया । क्रीडार्थं तु महाराज शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥
data.md: Nature, cheerfully and of her own accord, as if for sport, O king produces, by undergoing changes herself, thousands and thousands of combinations of her original qualities.

data.v: यथा दीपसहस्राणि दीपान्मर्त्याः प्रकुर्वते । प्रकृतिस्तथा विकुरुते पुरुषस्य गुणान्बहून् ॥
data.md: As men can light thousands of lamps from but a single lamp, similarly Nature, by change, multiplies into thousands of existent objects the (three) qualities of Purusha.

data.v: सत्त्वमानन्द उद्रेकः प्रीतिः प्राकाश्यमेव च । सुखं शुद्धित्वमारोग्यं संतोषः श्रद्दधानता ॥
अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः क्षमा धृतिरहिंसता । समता सत्यमानृण्यं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥
शौचमार्जवमाचारमलौल्यं हृद्यसंभ्रमः । इष्टानिष्टवियोगानां कृतानामविकत्थनम् ॥
दानेन चानुग्रहणमस्पृहार्थे परार्थता । सर्वभूतदया चैव सत्त्वस्यैते गुणाः स्मृताः ॥
रजोगुणानां संघातो रूपमैश्वर्यविग्रहे । अत्याशित्वमकारुण्यं सुखदुःखोपसेवनम् ॥
परापवादेषु रतिर्विवादानां च सेवनम् । अहंकारस्त्वसत्कारश्चिन्ता वैरोपसेवनम् ॥
परितापोऽपहरणं ह्रीनाशोऽनार्जवं तथा । भेदः परुषता चैव कामक्रोधौ मदस्तथा । दर्पो द्वेषोऽतिवादश्च एते प्रोक्ता रजोगुणाः ॥
तामसानां तु संघातं प्रवक्ष्याम्युपधार्यताम् । मोहोऽप्रकाशस्तामिस्रमन्धतामिस्रसंज्ञितम् ॥
मरणं चान्धतामिस्रं तामिस्रं क्रोध उच्यते । तमसो लक्षणानीह भक्षाणामभिरोचनम् ॥
भोजनानामपर्याप्तिस्तथा पेयेष्वतृप्तता । गन्धवासो विहारेषु शयनेष्वासनेषु च ॥
दिवास्वप्ने विवादे च प्रमादेषु च वै रतिः । नृत्यवादित्रगीतानामज्ञानाच्छ्रद्दधानता । द्वेषो धर्मविशेषाणामेते वै तामसा गुणाः ॥
एते प्रधानस्य गुणास्त्रयः पुरुषसत्तम । कृत्स्नस्य चैव जगतस्तिष्ठन्त्यनपगाः सदा ॥
data.md: These three, O foremost of men, are the qualities of Nature. These belong to all things of the universe.

data.v: शतधा सहस्रधा चैव तथा शतसहस्रधा । कोटिशश्च करोत्येष प्रत्यगात्मानमात्मना ॥
data.md: The uninanifest Purusha endued with the six Yoga qualities transforms himself by himself into hundreds and thousands and millions and millions of forms.

data.v: सात्त्विकस्योत्तमं स्थानं राजसस्येह मध्यमम् । तामसस्याधमं स्थानं प्राहुरध्यात्मचिन्तकाः ॥
data.md: Those that are conversant with the spiritual science say that to the quality of Sattva is assigned a high, to Rajas a middling, and to Tamas, a low place in the universe.

data.v: केवलेनेह पुण्येन गतिमूर्ध्वामवाप्नुयात् । पुण्यपापेन मानुष्यमधर्मेणाप्यधोगतिम् ॥
data.md: By the help of unmixed virtue one acquires a high end. Through virtue mixed with sin one acquires the status of humanity. While through unmixed sin one is visited by a vile end.

data.v: द्वंद्वमेषां त्रयाणां तु संनिपातं च तत्त्वतः । सत्त्वस्य रजसश्चैव तमसश्च शृणुष्व मे ॥
data.md: Listen now to me, king, as I speak to you of the intermixture of the three qualities of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas.

data.v: सत्त्वस्य तु रजो दृष्टं रजसश्च तमस्तथा । तमसश्च तथा सत्त्वं सत्त्वस्याव्यक्तमेव च ॥
data.md: Sometimes Rajas is seen mixed with Sattva Tamas also exists with Rajas. With Tamas may also be seen Sattva. Also Sattva and Rajas and Tamas may be seen existing together and in cqual parts. They then form the Nature.

data.v: अव्यक्तसत्त्वसंयुक्तो देवलोकमवाप्नुयात् । रजःसत्त्वसमायुक्तो मनुष्येषूपपद्यते ॥
रजस्तमोभ्यां संयुक्तस्तिर्यग्योनिषु जायते । रजस्तामससत्त्वैश्च युक्तो मानुष्यमाप्नुयात् ॥
data.md: When the Purusha becomes endued with only Sattva, he aquires the region of the gods. Endued with both Sattva and Rajas, he is born as a man. Endued with Rajas and Tamas, he is born the intermediate order of Being. Endued with all three, viz., Sattva and Rajas and Tamas, he becomes a man.

data.v: पुण्यपापवियुक्तानां स्थानमाहुर्मनीषिणाम् । शाश्वतं चाव्ययं चैव अक्षरं चाभयं च यत् ॥
data.md: Those great persons who are above both virtue and sin, attain, it is said, to that place which is eternal, immutable, undecaying, and immortal.

data.v: ज्ञानिनां संभवं श्रेष्ठं स्थानमव्रणमच्युतम् । अतीन्द्रियमबीजं च जन्ममृत्युतमोनुदम् ॥
data.md: Men of knowledge go by very superior births and their place is faultless and undecaying, transcending the perception of the senses, free from ignorance above birth and death, and full of light that removes all sorts of darkness,

data.v: अव्यक्तस्थं परं यत्तत्पृष्टस्तेऽहं नराधिप । स एष प्रकृतिष्ठो हि तस्थुरित्यभिधीयते ॥
data.md: You had asked me about the nature of the supreme living in the Unmanifest, Purusha. I shall tell you. He is said to live in His own nature without partaking of the nature of Prakriti.

data.v: अचेतनश्चैष मतः प्रकृतिस्थश्च पार्थिव । एतेनाधिष्ठितश्चैव सृजते संहरत्यपि ॥
data.md: Nature, O king, is inanimate and unintelligent. When presided over by Purusha (Soul) then only can she create and destroy.

data.v: अनादिनिधनावेतावुभावेव महामुने । अमूर्तिमन्तावचलावप्रकम्प्यौ च निर्व्रणौ ॥
data.md: Both Nature and Soul, O you of great intelligence, are without beginning and without end. Both of them are without end. Both of them are without form. Both of them are undeteriorating.

data.v: अग्राह्यावृषिशार्दूल कथमेको ह्यचेतनः । चेतनावांस्तथा चैकः क्षेत्रज्ञ इति भाषितः ॥
data.md: Both of them, again, cannot be comprehended. How then, O foremost of Rishis, can it be said that one of them is inanimate and unintelligent? How, is the other said to be animate and intelligent? And why is the latter called Kshetrajna (Soul).

data.v: त्वं हि विप्रेन्द्र कार्त्स्न्येन मोक्षधर्ममुपाससे । साकल्यं मोक्षधर्मस्य श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः ॥
data.md: You, O foremost of Brahmanas, are a master of the entire religion of Liberation. I wish to hear fully of the religion of Liberation.

data.v: अस्तित्वं केवलत्वं च विनाभावं तथैव च । तथैवोत्क्रमणस्थानं देहिनोऽपि वियुज्यतः ॥
कालेन यद्धि प्राप्नोति स्थानं तद्ब्रूहि मे द्विज । सांख्यज्ञानं च तत्त्वेन पृथग्योगं तथैव च ॥
अरिष्टानि च तत्त्वेन वक्तुमर्हसि सत्तम । विदितं सर्वमेतत्ते पाणावामलकं यथा ॥
data.md: Tell me, also, of the Knowledge expounded in the Sankhya system, and of the Yoga system separately. You also speak of the predicaments of death, O best of men. All these subjects are well known to you even as an embolic myrobalan in your hand. Tell me, also, of the Knowledge expounded in the Sankhya system, and of the Yoga system separately. You also speak of the predicaments of death, O best of men. All these subjects are well known to you even as an embolic myrobalan in your hand.

data.v: न शक्यो निर्गुणस्तात गुणीकर्तुं विशां पते । गुणवांश्चाप्यगुणवान्यथातत्त्वं निबोध मे ॥
data.md: That which is without qualities, O son, can never be explained by assigning qualities to it. Listen, however, to me as I explain to you what is endued with qualities and what is devoid of them.

data.v: गुणैर्हि गुणवानेव निर्गुणश्चागुणस्तथा । प्राहुरेवं महात्मानो मुनयस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: Great Munis conversant with the truth about principles say that when Soul seizes qualities like a crystal catching the reflection of a red flower, he is said to be possessed of qualities; but when freed from qualities like the crystal freed from reflection, he is seen in his real nature, which is as above all qualities.

data.v: गुणस्वभावस्त्वव्यक्तो गुणानेवाभिवर्तते । उपयुङ्क्ते च तानेव स चैवाज्ञः स्वभावतः ॥
data.md: Unmanifest Nature is by her nature endued with qualities. She cannot transcends them. Shorn of intelligence by nature she becomes attached to qualities.

data.v: अव्यक्तस्तु न जानीते पुरुषो ज्ञः स्वभावतः । न मत्तः परमस्तीति नित्यमेवाभिमन्यते ॥
data.md: Unmanifest Nature cannot know anything, while Purusha, by his nature, is endued with knowledge.—There is nothing higher than myself, the Soul is always conscious of it.

data.v: अनेन कारणेनैतदव्यक्तं स्यादचेतनम् । नित्यत्वादक्षरत्वाच्च क्षराणां तत्त्वतोऽन्यथा ॥
data.md: Therefore the unmanifest Nature, although by nature inanimate and unintelligent, still becomes animate and intelligent on account of her union with the Soul who is Eternal and Indestructible instead of remaining in her own nature owing to her destructibility.

data.v: यदाज्ञानेन कुर्वीत गुणसर्गं पुनः पुनः । यदात्मानं न जानीते तदाव्यक्तमिहोच्यते ॥
data.md: When Soul, through ignorance, repeatedly becomes associated with qualities, he fails to understand his own real nature and therefore he fails to acquire Liberation.

data.v: कर्तृत्वाच्चापि तत्त्वानां तत्त्वधर्मी तथोच्यते । कर्तृत्वाच्चैव योनीनां योनिधर्मा तथोच्यते ॥
data.md: On account of the Soul's Supremacy over the principles that originate from Nature he is said to partake of the nature of those principles. On account also of his agency in the matter of creation, he is said to possess the quality of creation. On account of his agency in the matter of Yoga, he is said to possess the quality of Yoga. For his Supremacy over those particular principles know by the name of Nature, he is said to possess the character of Nature.

data.v: कर्तृत्वात्प्रकृतीनां तु तथा प्रकृतिधर्मिता । कर्तृत्वाच्चापि बीजानां बीजधर्मी तथोच्यते ॥
गुणानां प्रसवत्वाच्च तथा प्रसवधर्मवान् । कर्तृत्वात्प्रलयानां च तथा प्रलयधर्मिता ॥
बीजत्वात्प्रकृतित्वाच्च प्रलयत्वात्तथैव च । उपेक्षकत्वादन्यत्वादभिमानाच्च केवलम् ॥
मन्यन्ते यतयः शुद्धा अध्यात्मविगतज्वराः । अनित्यं नित्यमव्यक्तमेवमेतद्धि शुश्रुम ॥
data.md: On account, again, of his being the witness of everything, and on account, also of there being nothing else than he, as also for his consciousness of oneness with Nature, Yatis endued with ascetic success, conversant with the spiritual science, and freed from fever of every sort, consider him as existing by himself without a second, immutable, unmanifest, unstable, and manifest.

data.v: अव्यक्तैकत्वमित्याहुर्नानात्वं पुरुषस्तथा । सर्वभूतदयावन्तः केवलं ज्ञानमास्थिताः ॥
data.md: This is what we have heard. Those Sankhyas, however, that depend upon Knowledge only and the practice of mercy for all creatures, say that it is Nature which is Ore but souls are many.

data.v: अन्यः स पुरुषोऽव्यक्तस्त्वध्रुवो ध्रुवसंज्ञकः । यथा मुञ्ज इषीकायास्तथैवैतद्धि जायते ॥
data.md: As a matter of fact, Soul is different from Nature which though unstable, still appears as stable. As a blade of reed is different from its outer cover, so is Soul different from Nature.

data.v: अन्यं च मशकं विद्यादन्यच्चोदुम्बरं तथा । न चोदुम्बरसंयोगैर्मशकस्तत्र लिप्यते ॥
data.md: Indeed, the worm that lies within the Udumvara should be known as different from the Udumvara, Though existing with the Udumvara, the worm is not to be considered as forming a part of the Udumvara.

data.v: अन्य एव तथा मत्स्यस्तथान्यदुदकं स्मृतम् । न चोदकस्य स्पर्शेन मत्स्यो लिप्यति सर्वशः ॥
data.md: The fish is separate from the water in which it lives, and the water is separate from the fish that lives in it. Though the fish and water exist together, yet it is never drenched by water.

data.v: अन्यो ह्यग्निरुखाप्यन्या नित्यमेवमवैहि भोः । न चोपलिप्यते सोऽग्निरुखासंस्पर्शनेन वै ॥
data.md: The fire that lies in an earthen saucepan is separate from the earthen saucepan, and the saucepan is separate from the fire it contains. although the fire exists in and with the saucepan, yet it is not to be considered as constituting any part of it.

data.v: पुष्करं त्वन्यदेवात्र तथान्यदुदकं स्मृतम् । न चोदकस्य स्पर्शेन लिप्यते तत्र पुष्करम् ॥
data.md: The fish is separate from the water in which it lives, and the water is separate from the fish that lives in it. Though the fish and water exist together, yet it is never drenched by water.

data.v: एतेषां सह संवासं विवासं चैव नित्यशः । यथा तथैनं पश्यन्ति न नित्यं प्राकृता जनाः ॥
data.md: The eternal existence of those objects in and with those mentioned, is never correctly understood by ordinary mortals.

data.v: ये त्वन्यथैव पश्यन्ति न सम्यक्तेषु दर्शनम् । ते व्यक्तं निरयं घोरं प्रविशन्ति पुनः पुनः ॥
data.md: They who see this universe as many are said to see incorrectly. These men are blind to Brahma. O chastiser of enemies, such persons have again and again to return to the world and assume bodies.

data.v: सांख्यदर्शनमेतत्ते परिसंख्यातमुत्तमम् । एवं हि परिसंख्याय सांख्याः केवलतां गताः ॥
data.md: I have thus told you the philosophy of the Sankhyas, that excellent science by which all things have been correctly determined. Ascertaining the nature of Soul and Nature in this way, the Sankhyas acquire Liberation.

data.v: ये त्वन्ये तत्त्वकुशलास्तेषामेतन्निदर्शनम् । अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि योगानामपि दर्शनम् ॥
data.md: I have also told of the systems of those others who are conversant with the great principles of the universe. I shall now describe to you the science of the Yogins,

data.v: सांख्यज्ञानं मया प्रोक्तं योगज्ञानं निबोध मे । यथाश्रुतं यथादृष्टं तत्त्वेन नृपसत्तम ॥
data.md: Yajnavalkya said, I have already spoken to you of the science of the Sankhyas. Hear now as I truly describe the science of the Yogins as heard and seen my me, O best of kings. are

data.v: नास्ति सांख्यसमं ज्ञानं नास्ति योगसमं बलम् । तावुभावेकचर्यौ तु उभावनिधनौ स्मृतौ ॥
data.md: There is no Knowledge like that of the Sankhyas. There is no power like that of Yoga. These two prescribe the same practices, and both are considered as capable of leading to Liberation.

data.v: पृथक्पृथक्तु पश्यन्ति येऽल्पबुद्धिरता नराः । वयं तु राजन्पश्याम एकमेव तु निश्चयात् ॥
data.md: Those men who not blest with intelligence consider the Sankhya and the Yoga systems to be different from each other. We, however, O king, regard them as one and the same, according to the conclusion to which we have arrived.

data.v: यदेव योगाः पश्यन्ति तत्सांख्यैरपि दृश्यते । एकं सांख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स तत्त्ववित् ॥
data.md: That which the Yogins behold is exactly what the Sankhyas strive after to attain. He who sees the Sankhya and the Yoga Systems to be one and the same is said to be gifted with intelligence.

data.v: रुद्रप्रधानानपरान्विद्धि योगान्परंतप । तेनैव चाथ देहेन विचरन्ति दिशो दश ॥
data.md: Know, O king, that the vital airs and the senses are the chief instruments for practising Yoga. By only regulating those vital airs and the senses, Yogins go everywhere at their will.

data.v: यावद्धि प्रलयस्तात सूक्ष्मेणाष्टगुणेन वै । योगेन लोकान्विचरन्सुखं संन्यस्य चानघ ॥
data.md: When the gross body is destroyed, Yogins, gifted with subtile bodies possessed of the eight Yoga powers wander over the universe, enjoying all sorts of happiness, O sinless one.

data.v: वेदेषु चाष्टगुणितं योगमाहुर्मनीषिणः । सूक्ष्ममष्टगुणं प्राहुर्नेतरं नृपसत्तम ॥
data.md: The wise have, in the scriptures, spoken of Yoga as giving eight sorts of power. They have spoken of Yoga as gifted with eight limbs.

data.v: द्विगुणं योगकृत्यं तु योगानां प्राहुरुत्तमम् । सगुणं निर्गुणं चैव यथाशास्त्रनिदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: Indeed, O king, they have not spoken of any other sort of Yoga. It has been said that the practices of Yogins, excellent as those are of two sorts. Those two sorts, according to the characteristics described in the scriptures, are practices endued with attributes and those freed from attributes.

data.v: धारणा चैव मनसः प्राणायामश्च पार्थिव । प्राणायामो हि सगुणो निर्गुणं धारणं मनः ॥
data.md: One is the concentration of the mind, and the other is called Pranayama (suppression of vital airs). Pranayama is said to be real; while concentration of mind is unsubstantial to it.

data.v: यत्र दृश्येत मुञ्चन्वै प्राणान्मैथिलसत्तम । वाताधिक्यं भवत्येव तस्माद्धि न समाचरेत् ॥
data.md: The, again, Regulation of the Vital air is Yoga with qualities. In Yoga without qualities, the mind, freed from its functions, should be fixed. Only the regulation of the vital air which is said to be endued with qualities should, in the first instance, be practised, for, O king of Mithila, if the vital air be exhaled without mentally thinking upon a definite image, the wind in the neophyte's system will increase to his great injury.

data.v: निशायाः प्रथमे यामे चोदना द्वादश स्मृताः । मध्ये सुप्त्वा परे यामे द्वादशैव तु चोदनाः ॥
data.md: In the first period of the night, twelve ways of suppressing the vital air are recommended. After sleep, in the last period of the night, other twelve ways of doing the same have been laid down.

data.v: तदेवमुपशान्तेन दान्तेनैकान्तशीलिना । आत्मारामेण बुद्धेन योक्तव्योऽऽत्मा न संशयः ॥
data.md: Forsooth, one endued with tranquillity, of controlled senses, living in retirement, rejoicing in one's in one's own self, and fully conversant with the meaning of the scriptures, should fix his Soul.

data.v: पञ्चानामिन्द्रियाणां तु दोषानाक्षिप्य पञ्चधा । शब्दं स्पर्शं तथा रूपं रसं गन्धं तथैव च ॥
data.md: Removing the five faults of the five sense, viz., (withdrawing them from their objects of) sound, form, touch, taste, and scent, and removing those conditions called Pratibha and Apavanga, O king, of the Mithilas, all the senses should be fixed upon the mind.

data.v: प्रतिभामपवर्गं च प्रतिसंहृत्य मैथिल । इन्द्रियग्राममखिलं मनस्यभिनिवेश्य ह ॥
data.md: Removing the five faults of the five sense, viz., (withdrawing them from their objects of) sound, form, touch, taste, and scent, and removing those conditions called Pratibha and Apavanga, O king, of the Mithilas, all the senses should be fixed upon the mind.

data.v: मनस्तथैवाहंकारे प्रतिष्ठाप्य नराधिप । अहंकारं तथा बुद्धौ बुद्धिं च प्रकृतावपि ॥
data.md: The mind should then be fixed on Consciousness, O king; Consciousness should next be fixed on Intelligence, and Buddhi should then be fixed on Nature.

data.v: एवं हि परिसंख्याय ततो ध्यायेत केवलम् । विरजस्कमलं नित्यमनन्तं शुद्धमव्रणम् ॥
data.md: Thus merging these one after another, Yogins meditate on the Supreme Soul which is One, which is freed from Darkness, which is Immutable and Infinite and Pure and without defect, and without blemish, who is Eternal Soul, who is unchangeable, who is Indivisible, who is without decay and death, who is everlasting who is above decrease, and which is Immutable Brahma.

data.v: तस्थुषं पुरुषं सत्त्वमभेद्यमजरामरम् । शाश्वतं चाव्ययं चैव ईशानं ब्रह्म चाव्ययम् ॥
data.md: Thus merging these one after another, Yogins meditate on the Supreme Soul which is One, which is freed from Darkness, which is Immutable and Infinite and Pure and without defect, and without blemish, who is Eternal Soul, who is unchangeable, who is Indivisible, who is without decay and death, who is everlasting who is above decrease, and which is Immutable Brahma.

data.v: युक्तस्य तु महाराज लक्षणान्युपधारयेत् । लक्षणं तु प्रसादस्य यथा तृप्तः सुखं स्वपेत् ॥
data.md: Listen, now, O king, to the marks of one that is Yoga. All the marks of cheerful contentment that are his who is sleeping in contentment are seen in the person, that is in Samadhi.

data.v: निवाते तु यथा दीपो ज्वलेत्स्नेहसमन्वितः । निश्चलोर्ध्वशिखस्तद्वद्युक्तमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: The person in contemplation, the wise hold looks like the fixed and upward flame of a lamp that is full of oil and that burns in a spot where there is no air.

data.v: पाषाण इव मेघोत्थैर्यथा बिन्दुभिराहतः । नालं चालयितुं शक्यस्तथा युक्तस्य लक्षणम् ॥
data.md: He is like a rock which is incapable of being moved in the last by even a heavy downpour from the clouds.

data.v: शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैर्विविधैर्गीतवादितैः । क्रियमाणैर्न कम्पेत युक्तस्यैतन्निदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: He is incapable of being moved by the sound of couchs and drums, or by songs, or the sound of hundreds of musical instruments beat or blown together. Even this is the characteristic of one in contemplation.

data.v: तैलपात्रं यथा पूर्णं कराभ्यां गृह्य पूरुषः । सोपानमारुहेद्भीतस्तर्ज्यमानोऽसिपाणिभिः ॥
संयतात्मा भयात्तेषां न पात्राद्बिन्दुमुत्सृजेत् । तथैवोत्तरमाणस्य एकाग्रमनसस्तथा ॥
स्थिरत्वादिन्द्रियाणां तु निश्चलत्वात्तथैव च । एवं युक्तस्य तु मुनेर्लक्षणान्युपधारयेत् ॥
स युक्तः पश्यति ब्रह्म यत्तत्परममव्ययम् । महतस्तमसो मध्ये स्थितं ज्वलनसंनिभम् ॥
data.md: While in contemplation, the Yogin sees Brahma which is Supreme and Immutable, and which is situated like a burning Effulgence in the midst of thick Darkness.

data.v: एतेन केवलं याति त्यक्त्वा देहमसाक्षिकम् । कालेन महता राजञ्श्रुतिरेषा सनातनी ॥
data.md: It is by this means that he acquires, after many years, Liberation after renouncing this inanimate body. Even this is what the eternal Shruti says.

data.v: एतद्धि योगं योगानां किमन्यद्योगलक्षणम् । विज्ञाय तद्धि मन्यन्ते कृतकृत्या मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: This is called the Yoga of the Yogins. What else is it? Knowing it, they who are gifted with wisdoin consider themselves as crowned with Success.

data.v: तथैवोत्क्रममाणं तु शृणुष्वावहितो नृप । पद्भ्यामुत्क्रममाणस्य वैष्णवं स्थानमुच्यते ॥
data.md: Yajnavalkya said Listen now to me, with attention, O king, as to what the places are to which those who die have to go. If the Individual soul escapes through the feet, it is said that the man goes to the region of Vishnu.

data.v: जङ्घाभ्यां तु वसून्देवानाप्नुयादिति नः श्रुतम् । जानुभ्यां च महाभागान्देवान्साध्यानवाप्नुयात् ॥
data.md: If through the calves, it has been heard by us that the man goes to the regions of the Vasus. If through the knees, he acquires the companionship of those gods who are called Sadhyas.

data.v: पायुनोत्क्रममाणस्तु मैत्रं स्थानमवाप्नुयात् । पृथिवीं जघनेनाथ ऊरुभ्यां तु प्रजापतिम् ॥
data.md: If through the lower duct, the man acquires the regions of Mitra. If through the posteriors, the man returns of the Earth, and if through the things to the region of Patriarch.

data.v: पार्श्वाभ्यां मरुतो देवान्नासाभ्यामिन्दुमेव च । बाहुभ्यामिन्द्रमित्याहुरुरसा रुद्रमेव च ॥
data.md: If through the flanks, the man acquires the regions of the Maruts, and if through the nostrils, to the region of the Moon. If through the arms, the man goes to the region of Indra, and if through the chest, to that of Rudra.

data.v: ग्रीवायास्तमृषिश्रेष्ठं नरमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् । विश्वेदेवान्मुखेनाथ दिशः श्रोत्रेण चाप्नुयात् ॥
data.md: If through the neck, the man goes to the excellent region of that foremost of ascetics known as Nara. If through the mouth, the man acquires the region of the Vishvedevas, and if through the ears, to the region of the gods presiding over the several points of the horizon.

data.v: घ्राणेन गन्धवहनं नेत्राभ्यां सूर्यमेव च । भ्रूभ्यां चैवाश्विनौ देवौ ललाटेन पितॄनथ ॥
data.md: If through the nose, the man acquires the region of the Wind-god; and if through the eyes, to the region of Agni. If through this brows, the man goes to the region of the Ashvins; and if through the forehead, to that of the departed manes.

data.v: ब्रह्माणमाप्नोति विभुं मूर्ध्ना देवाग्रजं तथा । एतान्युत्क्रमणस्थानान्युक्तानि मिथिलेश्वर ॥
data.md: If through the crown of the head, the man goes to the region of the powerful Brahman, that foremost of the gods. I have thus told you, O king of Mithila, the several places to which men go according to the manner in which their individual souls escape from their bodies.

data.v: अरिष्टानि तु वक्ष्यामि विहितानि मनीषिभिः । संवत्सरवियोगस्य संभवेयुः शरीरिणः ॥
data.md: I shall now tell you the presaging marks, as laid down by the wise, of those who have but one year to live.

data.v: योऽरुन्धतीं न पश्येत दृष्टपूर्वां कदाचन । तथैव ध्रुवमित्याहुः पूर्णेन्दुं दीपमेव च । खण्डाभासं दक्षिणतस्तेऽपि संवत्सरायुषः ॥
data.md: One who, having previously seen the fixed star called Arandhati, cannot see it, or that other star called Dhruva, or one that sees the full Moon or the flame of a burning lamp to be broken towards the south, has but one year to live.

data.v: परचक्षुषि चात्मानं ये न पश्यन्ति पार्थिव । आत्मच्छायाकृतीभूतं तेऽपि संवत्सरायुषः ॥
data.md: Those men, O king, who can no longer behold their own images reflected in the eyes of others, have but one year to live.

data.v: अतिद्युतिरतिप्रज्ञा अप्रज्ञा चाद्युतिस्तथा । प्रकृतेर्विक्रियापत्तिः षण्मासान्मृत्युलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: One who being gifted with lustre loses it, or being endued with wisdom loses it,-indeed, one whose inward and outward nature is thus metamorphosed,-has but six months more to live.

data.v: दैवतान्यवजानाति ब्राह्मणैश्च विरुध्यते । कृष्णश्यावच्छविच्छायः षण्मासान्मृत्युलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: He who disregards the gods, or falls out with the Brahmanas, or one who being naturally of a dark colour become pale of hue, has but six months more to live.

data.v: शीर्णनाभि यथा चक्रं छिद्रं सोमं प्रपश्यति । तथैव च सहस्रांशुं सप्तरात्रेण मृत्युभाक् ॥
data.md: One who sees the lunar disc full of holes like spider's web, or one who sees the solar disc to have similar holes, has but one week more to live.

data.v: शवगन्धमुपाघ्राति सुरभिं प्राप्य यो नरः । देवतायतनस्थस्तु षड्रात्रेण स मृत्युभाक् ॥
data.md: One who, when smelling sweet scents in places of Worship, perceives them to be as offensive as the smell of dead bodies, has but one week more to live.

data.v: कर्णनासावनमनं दन्तदृष्टिविरागिता । संज्ञालोपो निरूष्मत्वं सद्योमृत्युनिदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: The depression of the nose or of the cars, the discolour of the teeth or of the eyes, the loss of all consciousness, and the loss also of all animal magnetism, are symptoms indicating death that very day.

data.v: अकस्माच्च स्रवेद्यस्य वाममक्षि नराधिप । मूर्धतश्चोत्पतेद्धूमः सद्योमृत्युनिदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: If, without any ostensible cause tears suddenly flow from one's left eye, and if vapours be seen to issue from his head, it is a sure mark that the man will die before that day is over.

data.v: एतावन्ति त्वरिष्टानि विदित्वा मानवोऽऽत्मवान् । निशि चाहनि चात्मानं योजयेत्परमात्मनि ॥
data.md: on Knowing all these presaging symptoms, the man of purified soul should day and night unite his soul with the Supreme Soul.

data.v: प्रतीक्षमाणस्तत्कालं यत्कालं प्रति तद्भवेत् । अथास्य नेष्टं मरणं स्थातुमिच्छेदिमां क्रियाम् ॥
data.md: Thus should he go on till the day comes for his death. If, however, instead of wishing to die he wishes to live in this world, he renounces all enjoyments,-0 king, and lives in abstinence. He thus conquers death by uniting his Soul with the Supreme Soul.

data.v: सर्वगन्धान्रसांश्चैव धारयेत समाहितः । तथा हि मृत्युं जयति तत्परेणान्तरात्मना ॥
ससांख्यधारणं चैव विदित्वा मनुजर्षभ । जयेच्च मृत्युं योगेन तत्परेणान्तरात्मना ॥
data.md: Indeed, the man who is gifted with knowledge of the Soul, O king, follows the practises recommended by the Sankhyas and conquers death by uniting his Soul with Supreme Soul.

data.v: गच्छेत्प्राप्याक्षयं कृत्स्नमजन्म शिवमव्ययम् । शाश्वतं स्थानमचलं दुष्प्रापमकृतात्मभिः ॥
data.md: At last, he acquires what is entirely indestructible, which is without birth, which is auspicious, and immutable, and eternal, and stable, and which is incapable of being acquired by men of impure souls.

data.v: अव्यक्तस्थं परं यत्तत्पृष्टस्तेऽहं नराधिप । परं गुह्यमिमं प्रश्नं शृणुष्वावहितो नृप ॥
data.md: Yajnavalkya said You have asked me, O king, of that Supreme Brahma which lives in the Unmanifest. Your question relates to a deep mystery. Listen to me with rapt attention, O king.

data.v: यथार्षेणेह विधिना चरतावमतेन ह । मयादित्यादवाप्तानि यजूंषि मिथिलाधिप ॥
data.md: Having behaved humbly according to the ordinances laid down by the Rishis I obtained the Yajushes, O king, from the Sun-god.

data.v: महता तपसा देवस्तपिष्ठः सेवितो मया । प्रीतेन चाहं विभुना सूर्येणोक्तस्तदानघ ॥
वरं वृणीष्व विप्रर्षे यदिष्टं ते सुदुर्लभम् । तत्ते दास्यामि प्रीतात्मा मत्प्रसादो हि दुर्लभः ॥
data.md: With the hardest penances i formerly adored the heat-giving god. O sinless one, pleased with me, the powerful Sun, addressed me, saying, O regenerate Rishi, pray for the boon you covet, however difficult it may be of acquisition. I shall, with cheerful mind, grant it to you. It is very difficult to make me grant grace.

data.v: ततः प्रणम्य शिरसा मयोक्तस्तपतां वरः । यजूंषि नोपयुक्तानि क्षिप्रमिच्छामि वेदितुम् ॥
data.md: Bowing to him with my head, I addressed that foremost of heat-giving luminaries thus, I have no knowledge of the Yajushes. I wish to know them forthwith.

data.v: ततो मां भगवानाह वितरिष्यामि ते द्विज । सरस्वतीह वाग्भूता शरीरं ते प्रवेक्ष्यति ॥
data.md: The holy one, thus solicited, told ine,-I shall grant you the Yajushes. Made up of the essence of speech, the goddess of learning Sarasvati will enter into your person.

data.v: ततो मामाह भगवानास्यं स्वं विवृतं कुरु । विवृतं च ततो मेऽऽस्यं प्रविष्टा च सरस्वती ॥
data.md: The god then ordered me to open my mouth. I did as I was cominanded. The goddess Sarasvati then entered into my body, O sinless one.

data.v: ततो विदह्यमानोऽहं प्रविष्टोऽम्भस्तदानघ । अविज्ञानादमर्षाच्च भास्करस्य महात्मनः ॥
data.md: At this, I began to burn. Unable to suffer the pain I plunged into river. Not understanding what the great Sun had done for a me for my well-being, I became even angry with him.

data.v: ततो विदह्यमानं मामुवाच भगवान्रविः । मुहूर्तं सह्यतां दाहस्ततः शीतीभविष्यसि ॥
data.md: While I was burning with the energy of the goddess, the holy Sun told me.-Do you suffer this burning sensation for only a little time. That will soon come to an end and you will be cool.

data.v: शीतीभूतं च मां दृष्ट्वा भगवानाह भास्करः । प्रतिष्ठास्यति ते वेदः सोत्तरः सखिलो द्विज ॥
data.md: Indeed, I became cool. Beholding me restored to ease, the Maker of light said to me,-The whole Vedas, with its appendix, together with the Upanishads, will appear in you by inward light, О twice-born one.

data.v: कृत्स्नं शतपथं चैव प्रणेष्यसि द्विजर्षभ । तस्यान्ते चापुनर्भावे बुद्धिस्तव भविष्यति ॥
data.md: You will also edit the entire Satapathas, O foremost of twice-born ones. After that, your understanding will turn to the path of Liberation.

data.v: प्राप्स्यसे च यदिष्टं तत्सांख्ययोगेप्सितं पदम् । एतावदुक्त्वा भगवानस्तमेवाभ्यवर्तत ॥
data.md: You will also acquire that end which is desirable and which is coveted by both Sankhyas and Yogins. Having said so, the divine Sun proceeded to the setting hills.

data.v: ततोऽनुव्याहृतं श्रुत्वा गते देवे विभावसौ । गृहमागत्य संहृष्टोऽचिन्तयं वै सरस्वतीम् ॥
data.md: Hearing his last words, and after he had departed from where I was, I came home in joy and then remembered the goddess Sarasvati.

data.v: ततः प्रवृत्तातिशुभा स्वरव्यञ्जनभूषिता । ओंकारमादितः कृत्वा मम देवी सरस्वती ॥
data.md: Thought of by me, the auspicious Sarasvati appeared immediately before my eyes, adorned with all the vowels and the consonants and having placed the syllable OM in the van.

data.v: ततोऽहमर्घ्यं विधिवत्सरस्वत्यै न्यवेदयम् । तपतां च वरिष्ठाय निषण्णस्तत्परायणः ॥
data.md: was I then, according to the ordinance, offered to the goddess the usual Arghya, and dedicated another to the Sun, that foremost of all heatgiving gods. Doing this duty I took my seat, devoted to both those gods.

data.v: ततः शतपथं कृत्स्नं सरहस्यं ससंग्रहम् । चक्रे सपरिशेषं च हर्षेण परमेण ह ॥
data.md: Thereupon the entire Satapatha Brahmanas, with all their mysteries and with all their abstracts as also their appendices, appeared of themselves before my minds-eye, at which I became filled with great joy.

data.v: कृत्वा चाध्ययनं तेषां शिष्याणां शतमुत्तमम् । विप्रियार्थं सशिष्यस्य मातुलस्य महात्मनः ॥
data.md: I then taught them to a hundred competent disciples and thereby did what disagreeable to my great maternal uncle (Vaishampayana) with the disciples round him.

data.v: ततः सशिष्येण मया सूर्येणेव गभस्तिभिः । व्याप्तो यज्ञो महाराज पितुस्तव महात्मनः ॥
data.md: Then, shining in the midst of my disciples like the Sun himself with his rays, I took the management of the Sacrifice, of your noble father, O king.

data.v: मिषतो देवलस्यापि ततोऽर्धं हृतवानहम् । स्ववेददक्षिणायाथ विमर्दे मातुलेन ह ॥
data.md: In that Sacrifice, a quarrel arose between me and my maternal uncle as to who should be allowed to take the sacrificial fee that was paid for the recitation of the Vedas. In the very presence of Deval, I took half of that fee.

data.v: सुमन्तुनाथ पैलेन तथा जैमिनिना च वै । पित्रा ते मुनिभिश्चैव ततोऽहमनुमानितः ॥
data.md: Your father and Sumanta and Paila and Jaimini and other ascetics all agreed to that arrangement.

data.v: दश पञ्च च प्राप्तानि यजूंष्यर्कान्मयानघ । तथैव लोमहर्षाच्च पुराणमवधारितम् ॥
data.md: I had thus got from the Sun the five times ten Yajushes, O king. I then studied the Puranas with Romaharshan.

data.v: बीजमेतत्पुरस्कृत्य देवीं चैव सरस्वतीम् । सूर्यस्य चानुभावेन प्रवृत्तोऽहं नराधिप ॥
data.md: Keeping before me those Mantras and the goddess Sarasvati, I then, O king, helped by the inspiration of the Sun, set myself to compile the excellent Satapatha Brahmanas, and succeeded in performing the task never before undertaken by any one else. That path which I has wished to take, has been taken by me and I have also taught it to my disciples.

data.v: कर्तुं शतपथं वेदमपूर्वं कारितं च मे । यथाभिलषितं मार्गं तथा तच्चोपपादितम् ॥
शिष्याणामखिलं कृत्स्नमनुज्ञातं ससंग्रहम् । सर्वे च शिष्याः शुचयो गताः परमहर्षिताः ॥
data.md: Indeed I gave to my disciples the whole of those Vedas with their abstracts. Pure in mind and body, all those disciples have, on account of my instructions, become filled with joy.

data.v: शाखाः पञ्चदशेमास्तु विद्या भास्करदर्शिताः । प्रतिष्ठाप्य यथाकामं वेद्यं तदनुचिन्तयम् ॥
data.md: Having established this knowledge consisting of fifty branches which I had acquired from the Sun, I now meditate on the great object of that knowledge (viz., Brahma).

data.v: किमत्र ब्रह्मण्यमृतं किं च वेद्यमनुत्तमम् । चिन्तये तत्र चागत्य गन्धर्वो मामपृच्छत ॥
विश्वावसुस्ततो राजन्वेदान्तज्ञानकोविदः । चतुर्विंशतिकान्प्रश्नान्पृष्ट्वा वेदस्य पार्थिव । पञ्चविंशतिमं प्रश्नं पप्रच्छान्वीक्षिकीं तथा ॥
विश्वाविश्वं तथाश्वाश्वं मित्रं वरुणमेव च । ज्ञानं ज्ञेयं तथाज्ञो ज्ञः कस्तपा अतपास्तथा । सूर्यादः सूर्य इति च विद्याविद्ये तथैव च ॥
वेद्यावेद्यं तथा राजन्नचलं चलमेव च । अपूर्वमक्षयं क्षय्यमेतत्प्रश्नमनुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: What is Knowledge? What is the object of knowledge? What is Unintelligent? What is Intelligent? Who is Ka? Who is endued with the principle of change? Who is not endued with the same What is he that devours the Sun and what is the Sun? What is Vidya and what is Avidya? What is Vedya and Avedya? What is Immobile and Mobile? What is without beginning, what is indestructible, and what is Destructible? These were the transcendental questions put to me by that foremost of Gandharvas.

data.v: अथोक्तश्च मया राजन्राजा गन्धर्वसत्तमः । पृष्टवाननुपूर्वेण प्रश्नमुत्तममर्थवत् ॥
data.md: After king Vishvavasu, that foremost of Gandharvas, had asked me these questions one after another, I answered them duly.

data.v: मुहूर्तं मृष्यतां तावद्यावदेनं विचिन्तये । बाढमित्येव कृत्वा स तूष्णीं गन्धर्व आस्थितः ॥
data.md: At first, however, I told him,-Wait for a short time, till I reflect on your questions!—the Gandharva agreed to it, and sat in silence.

data.v: ततोऽन्वचिन्तयमहं भूयो देवीं सरस्वतीम् । मनसा स च मे प्रश्नो दध्नो घृतमिवोद्धृतम् ॥
data.md: I then thought once again of the goddess Sarasvati in my mind. The replies then to those questions naturally originated in my mind like butter from curds.

data.v: तत्रोपनिषदं चैव परिशेषं च पार्थिव । मथ्नामि मनसा तात दृष्ट्वा चान्वीक्षिकीं पराम् ॥
data.md: Keeping in view the high science of inferential ratioscination, I churned with my mind, O Monarch, the Upanishads and the supplementary works relating to the Vedas.

data.v: चतुर्थी राजशार्दूल विद्यैषा सांपरायिकी । उदीरिता मया तुभ्यं पञ्चविंशेऽधि धिष्ठिता ॥
data.md: I then expounded to him the fourth science that deals with Liberation, O foremost of kings, and on which I have already discoursed to thee, and which is based upon the twenty-fifth, viz., Individual Soul.

data.v: अथोक्तस्तु मया राजन्राजा विश्वावसुस्तदा । श्रूयतां यद्भवानस्मान्प्रश्नं संपृष्टवानिह ॥
data.md: Having said all this, O king, to king Vishvavasu, I then addressed him, saying, Listen now to the answers that I give to your several questions.

data.v: विश्वाविश्वेति यदिदं गन्धर्वेन्द्रानुपृच्छसि । विश्वाव्यक्तं परं विद्याद्भूतभव्यभयंकरम् ॥
data.md: I now dealt with the question which, O Gandharva, you ask, viz.,-what is Universe and what is Not-universe?—The Universe is Unmanifest and original Nature endued with the principles of birth and death which are terrible.

data.v: त्रिगुणं गुणकर्तृत्वादविश्वो निष्कलस्तथा । अश्वस्तथैव मिथुनमेवमेवानुदृश्यते ॥
अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिं प्राहुः पुरुषेति च निर्गुणम् । तथैव मित्रं पुरुषं वरुणं प्रकृतिं तथा ॥
data.md: It is, besides, possessed of the three qualities on account of its producing principles all of which are fraught with those attributes. That which is Not-universe is Purusha shorn of all attributes. By Ashva and Ashva are meant the female and the male. Similarly, Mitra is Soul, the Varuna is Nature.

data.v: ज्ञानं तु प्रकृतिं प्राहुर्ज्ञेयं निष्कलमेव च । अज्ञश्च ज्ञश्च पुरुषस्तस्मान्निष्कल उच्यते ॥
data.md: Knowledge, again, is said to be Nature, while the object to be know is called Soul. The Ignorant and the Knowing or Intelligent and both Soul without attributes.

data.v: कस्तपा अतपाः प्रोक्तः कोऽसौ पुरुष उच्यते । तपाः प्रकृतिरित्याहुरतपा निष्कलः स्मृतः ॥
data.md: You have asked what is Kah, who is endued with change, and who is unendued therewith. I answer, Kah is Soul. That which is endued with change is Nature. He who is not endued therewith is Soul.

data.v: तथैवावेद्यमव्यक्तं वेद्यः पुरुष उच्यते । चलाचलमिति प्रोक्तं त्वया तदपि मे शृणु ॥
data.md: Likewise is called the unknowable is Nature; and that which is called Knowable is Soul.

data.v: चलां तु प्रकृतिं प्राहुः कारणं क्षेपसर्गयोः । अक्षेपसर्गयोःकर्ता निश्चलः पुरुषः स्मृतः ॥
data.md: You have asked me about the Mobile and the Immobile. Hear my answer That which is mobile is Nature, which, undergoing changes, forms the cause of Creation and Destruction, The Immobile is Soul, for without himself undergoing changes he assists at Creation and Destruction.

data.v: अजावुभावप्रजौ च अक्षयौ चाप्युभावपि । अजौ नित्यावुभौ प्राहुरध्यात्मगतिनिश्चयाः ॥
data.md: What is Knowable is Nature; while what is Unknowable is Soul. Both Nature and Soul are said to be unintelligent, stable, indestructible, unborn and eternal, according to the decision of the philosophers who know the spiritual science.

data.v: अक्षयत्वात्प्रजनने अजमत्राहुरव्ययम् । अक्षयं पुरुषं प्राहुः क्षयो ह्यस्य न विद्यते ॥
data.md: On account of the indestructibility of Nature in the matter of Creation, Prakriti, which is unborn, is considered as not subject to decay destruction. Soul, again, is indestructible and unchangeable.

data.v: गुणक्षयत्वात्प्रकृतिः कर्तृत्वादक्षयं बुधाः । एषा तेऽऽन्वीक्षिकी विद्या चतुर्थी सांपरायिकी ॥
data.md: The qualities of Nature are destructible, but not Nature herself. The learned, therefore, call Nature indestructible. By undergoing changes Nature works as the cause of Creation. The results appear and disappear, but not original Nature. Hence also is Nature called indestructible. Thus have I told you the conclusions of the fourth Science based on the principles of inference and having Liberation for its end.

data.v: विद्योपेतं धनं कृत्वा कर्मणा नित्यकर्मणि । एकान्तदर्शना वेदाः सर्वे विश्वावसो स्मृताः ॥
data.md: Having acquired by the science of inference and by serving preceptors, the Richs, the Samans, and the Yajushes, all the or obligatory rites should be observed and all the Vedas read with reverence, O Vishvavasu,

data.v: जायन्ते च म्रियन्ते च यस्मिन्नेते यतश्च्युताः । वेदार्थं ये न जानन्ति वेद्यं गन्धर्वसत्तम ॥
data.md: O foremost of Gandharvas, they who study the Vedas with all their branches from which all things originate and into which all things merge when destruction sets in, and which is the one object whose knowledge the Vedas seek to preach,-indeed, they who have no acquaintance with what the Vedas seek to establish,-study the Vedas uselessly and carry their burthen of such study in vain.

data.v: साङ्गोपाङ्गानपि यदि पञ्च वेदानधीयते । वेदवेद्यं न जानीते वेदभारवहो हि सः ॥
यो घृतार्थी खरीक्षीरं मथेद्गन्धर्वसत्तम । विष्ठां तत्रानुपश्येत न मण्डं नापि वा घृतम् ॥
data.md: If a person seeking butter churns the milk of the she-ass, without finding what he seeks he simply finds a substance of foul smell like ordure.

data.v: तथा वेद्यमवेद्यं च वेदविद्यो न विन्दति । स केवलं मूढमतिर्ज्ञानभारवहः स्मृतः ॥
data.md: Similarly if one, having read the Vedas, fails to know what is Nature and what is Soul, one only proves his own foolishness of understanding and carries a useless load.

data.v: द्रष्टव्यौ नित्यमेवैतौ तत्परेणान्तरात्मना । यथास्य जन्मनिधने न भवेतां पुनः पुनः ॥
data.md: One should, with devoted attention, think on both Nature and Soul, so that he may avoid repeated birth and death.

data.v: अजस्रं जन्मनिधनं चिन्तयित्वा त्रयीमिमाम् । परित्यज्य क्षयमिह अक्षयं धर्ममास्थितः ॥
data.md: Thinking upon the incident of one's repeated births and deaths and avoiding the religion of acts which merely yield destructible results, one should follow the eternal religion of Yoga.

data.v: यदा तु पश्यतेऽत्यन्तमहन्यहनि काश्यप । तदा स केवलीभूतः षड्विंशमनुपश्यति ॥
data.md: O Kashyapa, if one continuously reflects on the nature of the Individual Soul and its connection with the Supreme Soul, he then succeeds in divesting him of all attributes and in seeing the Supreme Soul.

data.v: अन्यश्च शश्वदव्यक्तस्तथान्यः पञ्चविंशकः । तस्य द्वावनुपश्येत तमेकमिति साधवः ॥
data.md: The Eternal and Unmanifest Supreme Soul is considered by men of foolish understandings as distinct from the Individual Soul. They are really wise who see both these as truly one and the same.

data.v: तेनैतन्नाभिजानन्ति पञ्चविंशकमच्युतम् । जन्ममृत्युभयाद्योगाः सांख्याश्च परमैषिणः ॥
data.md: Frightened at repeated births and deaths, the Sankhyas and Yogins consider the Individual Soul and the Supreme Soul to be one and the same.

data.v: पञ्चविंशं यदेतत्ते प्रोक्तं ब्राह्मणसत्तम । तथा तन्न तथा वेति तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति ॥
data.md: Vishvavasu then said You have, O foremost of Brahmanas, said that Individual Soul is indestructible and truly undistinguished from the Supreme Soul. This, however, is difficult to understand. You should once more explain this subject to me.

data.v: जैगीषव्यस्यासितस्य देवलस्य च मे श्रुतम् । पराशरस्य विप्रर्षेर्वार्षगण्यस्य धीमतः ॥
भिक्षोः पञ्चशिखस्याथ कपिलस्य शुकस्य च । गौतमस्यार्ष्टिषेणस्य गर्गस्य च महात्मनः ॥
नारदस्यासुरेश्चैव पुलस्त्यस्य च धीमतः । सनत्कुमारस्य ततः शुक्रस्य च महात्मनः ॥
कश्यपस्य पितुश्चैव पूर्वमेव मया श्रुतम् । तदनन्तरं च रुद्रस्य विश्वरूपस्य धीमतः ॥
दैवतेभ्यः पितृभ्यश्च दैत्येभ्यश्च ततस्ततः । प्राप्तमेतन्मया कृत्स्नं वेद्यं नित्यं वदन्त्युत ॥
तस्मात्तद्वै भवद्बुद्ध्या श्रोतुमिच्छामि ब्राह्मण । भवान्प्रबर्हः शास्त्राणां प्रगल्भश्चातिबुद्धिमान् ॥
data.md: I wish, however, to hear what you say on those subjects with the help of your intelligence. You are the foremost of all persons, and a learned learned lecturer on the scriptures, and gifted with great intelligence.

data.v: न तवाविदितं किंचिद्भवाञ्श्रुतिनिधिः स्मृतः । कथ्यते देवलोके च पितृलोके च ब्राह्मण ॥
data.md: There is nothing which you do not know. You are an ocean of the Shrutis, as described, O Brahmana, in the world of both the gods and the departed manes.

data.v: ब्रह्मलोकगताश्चैव कथयन्ति महर्षयः । पतिश्च तपतां शश्वदादित्यस्तव भाषते ॥
data.md: The great Rishi living in the region of lords and who is said to be eternal lord of all luminaries, is your preceptor.

data.v: सांख्यज्ञानं त्वया ब्रह्मन्नवाप्तं कृत्स्नमेव च । तथैव योगज्ञानं च याज्ञवल्क्य विशेषतः ॥
data.md: O Yajnavalkya, you have acquired the entire science, O Brahmana, of the Sankhyas, as also the scriptures of the Yogins in particular.

data.v: निःसंदिग्धं प्रबुद्धस्त्वं बुध्यमानश्चराचरम् । श्रोतुमिच्छामि तज्ज्ञानं घृतं मण्डमयं यथा ॥
data.md: Forsooth, you are enlightened, fully conversant with the mobile and immobile universe. I wish to hear you describe that knowledge, which is compared to clarified butter having solid grains.

data.v: कृत्स्नधारिणमेव त्वां मन्ये गन्धर्वसत्तम । जिज्ञाससि च मां राजंस्तन्निबोध यथाश्रुतम् ॥
data.md: Yajnavalkya said You are, O foremost of Gandharvas, capable of comprehending every knowledge. As, however, you ask me, do you hear me then explain to you according as I myself have obtained it from my preceptor.

data.v: अबुध्यमानां प्रकृतिं बुध्यते पञ्चविंशकः । न तु बुध्यति गन्धर्व प्रकृतिः पञ्चविंशकम् ॥
data.md: Nature, which is unintelligent, is apprehended by Individual Soul, however, cannot be apprehended by Nature, 0 Gandharva.

data.v: अनेनाप्रतिबोधेन प्रधानं प्रवदन्ति तम् । सांख्ययोगाश्च तत्त्वज्ञा यथाश्रुतिनिदर्शनात् ॥
data.md: In consequence of Individual Soul being reflected in Nature, the latter is called Pradhana by Sankhyas and Yogins conversant with the original principles as laid down in the Shrutis.

data.v: पश्यंस्तथैवापश्यंश्च पश्यत्यन्यस्तथानघ । षड्विंशः पञ्चविंशं च चतुर्विंशं च पश्यति । न तु पश्यति पश्यंस्तु यश्चैनमनुपश्यति ॥
data.md: O sinless one, the other, seeing, sees the Nature and the Soul; not seeing, it sees the Supreme Soul.

data.v: पञ्चविंशोऽभिमन्येत नान्योऽस्ति परमो मम । न चतुर्विंशकोऽग्राह्यो मनुजैर्ज्ञानदर्शिभिः ॥
मत्स्येवोदकमन्वेति प्रवर्तति प्रवर्तनात् । यथैव बुध्यते मत्स्यस्तथैषोऽप्यनुबुध्यते । सस्नेहः सहवासाच्च साभिमानश्च नित्यशः ॥
स निमज्जति कालस्य यदैकत्वं न बुध्यते । उन्मज्जति हि कालस्य ममत्वेनाभिसंवृतः ॥
data.md: As the fish, though living in the water, is to be considered as separate from it, similarly is the Soul to be apprehended, i.e., though the Soul exists in a state of contact with the Nature, it is, however, in its real nature, separate form, and independent of Nature, When overwhelmed with the consciousness of Self, and when unable to understand its identity with the Supreme Soul, on account of the illusion that covers it, of its co-existence with Nature, and of its own manner of thinking, the Individual Soul always sinks down, but when freed from such consciousness it goes upwards.

data.v: यदा तु मन्यतेऽन्योऽहमन्य एष इति द्विजः । तदा स केवलीभूतः षड्विंशमनुपश्यति ॥
data.md: O Kashyapa, if one continuously reflects on the nature of the Individual Soul and its connection with the Supreme Soul, he then succeeds in divesting him of all attributes and in seeing the Supreme Soul.

data.v: अन्यश्च राजन्नवरस्तथान्यः पञ्चविंशकः । तत्स्थत्वादनुपश्यन्ति एक एवेति साधवः ॥
data.md: The Eternal and Unmanifest Supreme Soul is considered by men of foolish understandings as distinct from the Individual Soul. They are really wise who see both these as truly one and the same.

data.v: तेनैतन्नाभिनन्दन्ति पञ्चविंशकमच्युतम् । जन्ममृत्युभयाद्भीता योगाः सांख्याश्च काश्यप । षड्विंशमनुपश्यन्ति शुचयस्तत्परायणाः ॥
data.md: Frightened at repeated births and deaths, the Sankhyas and Yogins consider the Individual Soul and the Supreme Soul to be one and the same.

data.v: यदा स केवलीभूतः षड्विंशमनुपश्यति । तदा स सर्वविद्विद्वान्न पुनर्जन्म विन्दति ॥
एवमप्रतिबुद्धश्च बुध्यमानश्च तेऽनघ । बुद्धश्चोक्तो यथातत्त्वं मया श्रुतिनिदर्शनात् ॥
पश्यापश्यं योऽनुपश्येत्क्षेमं तत्त्वं च काश्यप । केवलाकेवलं चाद्यं पञ्चविंशात्परं च यत् ॥
तथ्यं शुभं चैतदुक्तं त्वया भोः; सम्यक्क्षेम्यं देवताद्यं यथावत् । स्वस्त्यक्षयं भवतश्चास्तु नित्यं; बुद्ध्या सदा बुद्धियुक्तं नमस्ते ॥
data.md: Vishvavasu said 0 powerful one, you have duly and adequately expounded what is the origin of all the gods and which produces Liberation. You have said what is true and excellent. May you enjoy inexhaustible blessings, and may your mind be ever united with intelligence.

data.v: एवमुक्त्वा संप्रयातो दिवं स; विभ्राजन्वै श्रीमता दर्शनेन । तुष्टश्च तुष्ट्या परयाभिनन्द्य; प्रदक्षिणं मम कृत्वा महात्मा ॥
data.md: Yajnavalkya said Having said those words, the king of Gandharvas proceeded towards heaven, shining in resplendence of beauty. Before leaving me, the great one duly honoured me by going round my body, and I found him, highly pleased.

data.v: ब्रह्मादीनां खेचराणां क्षितौ च; ये चाधस्तात्संवसन्ते नरेन्द्र । तत्रैव तद्दर्शनं दर्शयन्वै; सम्यक्क्षेम्यं ये पथं संश्रिता वै ॥
data.md: He inculcated the science he had learnt from me to those celestials that live in the regions of Brahman and other gods, unto those who live on Earth, to also the dwellers of the nether regions, and to them who had adopted the path of Liberation, O king.

data.v: सांख्याः सर्वे सांख्यधर्मे रताश्च; तद्वद्योगा योगधर्मे रताश्च । ये चाप्यन्ये मोक्षकामा मनुष्या;स्तेषामेतद्दर्शनं ज्ञानदृष्टम् ॥
data.md: The Sankhyas are devoted to the practices of their system. The Yogins are devoted to the practices of their system. There are others who are desirous of acquiring Liberation. To these latter this science yields palpable fruits.

data.v: ज्ञानान्मोक्षो जायते पूरुषाणां; नास्त्यज्ञानादेवमाहुर्नरेन्द्र । तस्माज्ज्ञानं तत्त्वतोऽन्वेषितव्यं; येनात्मानं मोक्षयेज्जन्ममृत्योः ॥
data.md: O foremost of kings, Liberation originates from Knowledge. Without Knowledge it can never be acquired. The wise have said it, O king. Hence, one should try his best for acquiring true Knowledge in all its particulars, by which one may succeed in freeing oneself from birth and death.

data.v: प्राप्य ज्ञानं ब्राह्मणात्क्षत्रियाद्वा; वैश्याच्छूद्रादपि नीचादभीक्ष्णम् । श्रद्धातव्यं श्रद्दधानेन नित्यं; न श्रद्धिनं जन्ममृत्यू विशेताम् ॥
data.md: Acquiring knowledge from a Brahmana or a Kashtriya or Vaishya or even a Shudra who is of low birth, one having faith should always show respect for such knowledge. Birth and death cannot attack one who has faith. arose

data.v: सर्वे वर्णा ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मजाश्च; सर्वे नित्यं व्याहरन्ते च ब्रह्म । तत्त्वं शास्त्रं ब्रह्मबुद्ध्या ब्रवीमि; सर्वं विश्वं ब्रह्म चैतत्समस्तम् ॥
data.md: All orders of men are Brahmanas. All originate from Brahman. All All men utter Brahma. Helped by an understanding that is derived from and directed to Brahma, I preach this science treating of Nature and Soul. Indeed this whole universe is Brahma.

data.v: ब्रह्मास्यतो ब्राह्मणाः संप्रसूता; बाहुभ्यां वै क्षत्रियाः संप्रसूताः । नाभ्यां वैश्याः पादतश्चापि शूद्राः; सर्वे वर्णा नान्यथा वेदितव्याः ॥
data.md: From the mouth of Brahman originated the Brahmanas; from his arms, the Kshatriyas; from his navel, the Vaishyas, and from his feet, the Shudras. All the orders should be considered as differing from one another.

data.v: अज्ञानतः कर्मयोनिं भजन्ते; तां तां राजंस्ते यथा यान्त्यभावम् । तथा वर्णा ज्ञानहीनाः पतन्ते; घोरादज्ञानात्प्राकृतं योनिजालम् ॥
data.md: Actuated by Ignorance, all men meet with death and go, O king, by birth which is the cause of acts. Shorn of Knowledge, all orders of men, dragged by terrible Ignorance, fall into varied orders of being on account of the principles that originate from Nature.

data.v: तस्माज्ज्ञानं सर्वतो मार्गितव्यं; सर्वत्रस्थं चैतदुक्तं मया ते । तस्थौ ब्रह्मा तस्थिवांश्चापरो य;स्तस्मै नित्यं मोक्षमाहुर्द्विजेन्द्राः ॥
data.md: Therefore, all should, by every means, try to acquire Knowledge. I have told you that every person is entitled to took for its acquisition. One who is endued with Knowledge, as Brahmana. Others, are possessed of knowledge. Hence, this science of a Liberation is always open to them all. The Wise, O king, have said this.

data.v: यत्ते पृष्टं तन्मया चोपदिष्टं; याथातथ्यं तद्विशोको भवस्व । राजन्गच्छस्वैतदर्थस्य पारं; सम्यक्प्रोक्तं स्वस्ति तेऽस्त्वत्र नित्यम् ॥
data.md: The questions you had put to me, have all been answered by me according to the truth. Do you, therefore, renounce all grief. Go you to the other end of this enquiry. Your questions were good. Blessings on your head for ever.

data.v: स एवमनुशास्तस्तु याज्ञवल्क्येन धीमता । प्रीतिमानभवद्राजा मिथिलाधिपतिस्तदा ॥
data.md: Thus instructed by the intelligent Yajanavalkya, the king of Mithila become filled with joy.

data.v: गते मुनिवरे तस्मिन्कृते चापि प्रदक्षिणे । दैवरातिर्नरपतिरासीनस्तत्र मोक्षवित् ॥
data.md: The king honoured that foremost of ascetics by going round his body. Dismissed by the king, he left his court. King Daivarati, having acquired the knowledge of the religion of Liberation, took his seat, and touching a million kine and a quantity of gold, of gems and jewels, gave them away to a number of Brahmanas.

data.v: गोकोटिं स्पर्शयामास हिरण्यस्य तथैव च । रत्नाञ्जलिमथैकं च ब्राह्मणेभ्यो ददौ तदा ॥
data.md: The king honoured that foremost of ascetics by going round his body. Dismissed by the king, he left his court. King Daivarati, having acquired the knowledge of the religion of Liberation, took his seat, and touching a million kine and a quantity of gold, of gems and jewels, gave them away to a number of Brahmanas.

data.v: विदेहराज्यं च तथा प्रतिष्ठाप्य सुतस्य वै । यतिधर्ममुपासंश्चाप्यवसन्मिथिलाधिपः ॥
data.md: Installing his son in the sovereignty of the Videhas, the old king began to lead the life of a Yati.

data.v: सांख्यज्ञानमधीयानो योगशास्त्रं च कृत्स्नशः । धर्माधर्मौ च राजेन्द्र प्राकृतं परिगर्हयन् ॥
data.md: Taking no notice of all ordinary duties, the king began to study the science of the Sankhyas and the Yogins in full.

data.v: अनन्तमिति कृत्वा स नित्यं केवलमेव च । धर्माधर्मौ पुण्यपापे सत्यासत्ये तथैव च ॥
जन्ममृत्यू च राजेन्द्र प्राकृतं तदचिन्तयत् । ब्रह्माव्यक्तस्य कर्मेदमिति नित्यं नराधिप ॥
data.md: Considering himself to the Infinite, he began to reflect on only the Eternal and Independent One. He renounced all ordinary duties, Virtue and Vice, Truth and Falsehood, Birth and Death, and all other things relating to the principles produced by Nature.

data.v: पश्यन्ति योगाः सांख्याश्च स्वशास्त्रकृतलक्षणाः । इष्टानिष्टवियुक्तं हि तस्थौ ब्रह्म परात्परम् । नित्यं तमाहुर्विद्वांसः शुचिस्तस्माच्छुचिर्भव ॥
data.md: Both Sankhyas and Yogins, according to the teachings of their sciences, consider this universe as the outcome of the action of the Manifest and the Unmanifest.

data.v: दीयते यच्च लभते दत्तं यच्चानुमन्यते । ददाति च नरश्रेष्ठ प्रतिगृह्णाति यच्च ह । ददात्यव्यक्तमेवैतत्प्रतिगृह्णाति तच्च वै ॥
आत्मा ह्येवात्मनो ह्येकः कोऽन्यस्त्वत्तोऽधिको भवेत् । एवं मन्यस्व सततमन्यथा मा विचिन्तय ॥
data.md: The giver, the receiver of the gift, the gift itself, and that what is ordered to be given away, are all to be deemed as the unmanifest Soul. The Soul is the Soul's possession. Who, therefore, can be a stranger to one? Do you think always in this way. Never think otherwise.

data.v: यस्याव्यक्तं न विदितं सगुणं निर्गुणं पुनः । तेन तीर्थानि यज्ञाश्च सेवितव्याविपश्चिता ॥
data.md: He who does not know what is Nature possessed of qualities and what is Soul transcending qualities, only he, not possessed as he is of knowledge, repairs to sacred waters and cerebrates sacrifices.

data.v: न स्वाध्यायैस्तपोभिर्वा यज्ञैर्वा कुरुनन्दन । लभतेऽव्यक्तसंस्थानं ज्ञात्वाव्यक्तं महीपते ॥
data.md: Not by study of the Vedas, not by penances, not by sacrifices, O son of Kuru, can one acquire the status of Brahma. Only when one succeeds in apprehending the Supreme or Unmanifest, he is respected.

data.v: तथैव महतः स्थानमाहंकारिकमेव च । अहंकारात्परं चापि स्थानानि समवाप्नुयात् ॥
data.md: They who wait upon Mahat acquires the regions of Mahat. They who wait upon Consciousness, go to the spot that belongs to Consciousness. They who wait upon what is higher, acquire higher places.

data.v: ये त्वव्यक्तात्परं नित्यं जानते शास्त्रतत्पराः । जन्ममृत्युवियुक्तं च वियुक्तं सदसच्च यत् ॥
data.md: Those persons learned in the scriptures, who succeed in apprehending eternal Brahma which is higher than Unmenifest nature, can acquire that which is above birth and death, which is free from qualities, and which is both existent and non-existent.

data.v: एतन्मयाप्तं जनकात्पुरस्ता;त्तेनापि चाप्तं नृप याज्ञवल्क्यात् । ज्ञानं विशिष्टं न तथा हि यज्ञा; ज्ञानेन दुर्गं तरते न यज्ञैः ॥
data.md: I got all this knowledge from Janaka. The latter had got it from Yajnavalkya. Knowledge is very superior. Sacrifices cannot compare with it. With the help of Knowledge one succeeds in crossing the world's ocean which is beset with difficulties and dangers. One can never cross that by means of sacrifices.

data.v: दुर्गं जन्म निधनं चापि राज;न्न भूतिकं ज्ञानविदो वदन्ति । यज्ञैस्तपोभिर्नियमैर्व्रतैश्च; दिवं समासाद्य पतन्ति भूमौ ॥
data.md: Birth and death, and other obstacles, O king, men of knowledge say, one cannot get over by ordinary exertion. Men acquire heaven through sacrifices, penances, observances. But they have again to drop down therefrom on the Earth. vows, and

data.v: तस्मादुपासस्व परं महच्छुचि; शिवं विमोक्षं विमलं पवित्रम् । क्षेत्रज्ञवित्पार्थिव ज्ञानयज्ञ;मुपास्य वै तत्त्वमृषिर्भविष्यसि ॥
data.md: Do you, therefore, worship with reverence that which is Supreme, most pure, blessed, stainless, and sacred, and which is above all states. By apprehending Soul, O king, and by celebrating the Sacrifice which consists in the acquisition of Knowledge, you will really be wise.

data.v: उपनिषदमुपाकरोत्तदा वै; जनकनृपस्य पुरा हि याज्ञवल्क्यः । यदुपगणितशाश्वताव्ययं त;च्छुभममृतत्वमशोकमृच्छतीति ॥
data.md: In former time, Yajnavalkya did that good to king Janaka which comes from a study of the Upanishads. The Eternal and Immutable Supreme was the subject which the great Rishi had described to the king of Mithila. It enabled him to attain to that Brahma which is auspicious and immortal, and which is above all sorts of sorrows.

data.v: ऐश्वर्यं वा महत्प्राप्य धनं वा भरतर्षभ । दीर्घमायुरवाप्याथ कथं मृत्युमतिक्रमेत् ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Having acquired great power and great riches, and having obtained a long period of life, how many one succeed in shunning death?

data.v: तपसा वा सुमहता कर्मणा वा श्रुतेन वा । रसायनप्रयोगैर्वा कैर्नोपैति जरान्तकौ ॥
data.md: By which of these means viz., penances, or the performance of the various acts, or by knowledge of the Shrutis, or the application of medicines, can one succeed in avoiding decrepitude and death.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । भिक्षोः पञ्चशिखस्येह संवादं जनकस्य च ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old narrative of Panchashikha who was a Bhikshu in his practices and Janaka.

data.v: वैदेहो जनको राजा महर्षिं वेदवित्तमम् । पर्यपृच्छत्पञ्चशिखं छिन्नधर्मार्थसंशयम् ॥
data.md: Once on a time, Janaka, the king of Videhas, questioned the great Rishi Panchashikha, who was the foremost of all persons conversant with the Vedas and who had all his doubts removed about the object and meaning of all duties.

data.v: केन वृत्तेन भगवन्नतिक्रामेज्जरान्तकौ । तपसा वाथ बुद्ध्या वा कर्मणा वा श्रुतेन वा ॥
data.md: The King said By what conduct, O holy one, may one get over Decrepitude and Death? Is it by penances, or by the understanding, or by religious practices, or by study and knowledge of the scriptures.

data.v: एवमुक्तः स वैदेहं प्रत्युवाच परोक्षवित् । निवृत्तिर्नैतयोरस्ति नानिवृत्तिः कथंचन ॥
data.md: Thus addressed by the king of the Videhas the learned Panchashikha, conversant with all invisible things, answered saying, Nothing can prevent two (viz., decrepitude and death); nor is it true that these cannot be prevented under any circumstances.

data.v: न ह्यहानि निवर्तन्ते न मासा न पुनः क्षपाः । सोऽयं प्रपद्यतेऽध्वानं चिराय ध्रुवमध्रुवः ॥
data.md: Neither days, nor nights, nor months, cease to go on. Only that man who, though transitory, follows the eternal path succeeds in avoiding birth and death.

data.v: सर्वभूतसमुच्छेदः स्रोतसेवोह्यते सदा । उह्यमानं निमज्जन्तमप्लवे कालसागरे । जरामृत्युमहाग्राहे न कश्चिदभिपद्यते ॥
data.md: Destruction overtakes all creatures. All creatures seem to be ceaselessly borne along the endless current of time. Those that are borne along the endless current of time which is without a vessel and which in infested by those two powerful alligators, viz., decrepitude and death, sink down without anybody coming to their help.

data.v: नैवास्य भविता कश्चिन्नासौ भवति कस्यचित् । पथि संगतमेवेदं दारैरन्यैश्च बन्धुभिः । नायमत्यन्तसंवासो लब्धपूर्वो हि केनचित् ॥
data.md: One meets with wives and other friends only on his road. One had never before enjoyed this sort of companionship with any one for any length of time.

data.v: क्षिप्यन्ते तेन तेनैव निष्टनन्तः पुनः पुनः । कालेन जाता जाता हि वायुनेवाभ्रसंचयाः ॥
data.md: Creatures, as they are carried along the current to time, become again and again are drawn towards one another like clouds moved by the wind meeting one another with loud noise.

data.v: जरामृत्यू हि भूतानां खादितारौ वृकाविव । बलिनां दुर्बलानां च ह्रस्वानां महतामपि ॥
data.md: Like wolves, descrepitude and death are devourers of all creatures. Indeed, they devour the strong and the weak, the short and the tall.

data.v: एवंभूतेषु भूतेषु नित्यभूताध्रुवेषु च । कथं हृष्येत जातेषु मृतेषु च कथं ज्वरेत् ॥
data.md: Among creatures, therefore, which are all so fickle only the Soul exists eternally. Why should he, then, rejoice when creatures are born and why should he grieve when the die.

data.v: कुतोऽहमागतः कोऽस्मि क्व गमिष्यामि कस्य वा । कस्मिन्स्थितः क्व भविता कस्मात्किमनुशोचसि ॥
data.md: Whence have I come? Who am I? Where shall I go? Whose am I? Before what do I rest? What shall I be? Why then do you grieve for what?

data.v: द्रष्टा स्वर्गस्य न ह्यस्ति तथैव नरकस्य च । आगमांस्त्वनतिक्रम्य दद्याच्चैव यजेत च ॥
data.md: Who else than you will see heaven or hell? Hence, without throwing aside the scriptures, one should make gifts and celebrate sacrifices.

data.v: अपरित्यज्य गार्हस्थ्यं कुरुराजर्षिसत्तम । कः प्राप्तो विनयं बुद्ध्या मोक्षतत्त्वं वदस्व मे ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said. Without giving up the domestic mode of life, O royal sage of Kuru's race, who ever acquired Liberation which is the annihilation of the Understanding? Do tell me this.

data.v: संन्यस्यते यथात्मायं संन्यस्तात्मा यथा च यः । परं मोक्षस्य यच्चापि तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: How may the gross and the subtile form be renounced? Do you also, O grandfather, tell me what the supreme excellence of Liberation is.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । जनकस्य च संवादं सुलभायाश्च भारत ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Janaka and Sulabha, O Bharata!

data.v: संन्यासफलिकः कश्चिद्बभूव नृपतिः पुरा । मैथिलो जनको नाम धर्मध्वज इति श्रुतः ॥
data.md: Formerly there was a king of Mithila, of the name of Dharmadhyaja, of Janaka's race. He was given to the religion of Renunciation,

data.v: स वेदे मोक्षशास्त्रे च स्वे च शास्त्रे कृतागमः । इन्द्रियाणि समाधाय शशास वसुधामिमाम् ॥
data.md: He was well conversant with the Veda, with the scriptures on Liberation, and with the scriptures dealing with royal duties. Governing his senses, he ruled this Earth.

data.v: तस्य वेदविदः प्राज्ञाः श्रुत्वा तां साधुवृत्तताम् । लोकेषु स्पृहयन्त्यन्ये पुरुषाः पुरुषेश्वर ॥
data.md: Hearing of his good conduct in the world, many wise men, well-conversant with wisdom, O foremost of men, wished to imitate him.

data.v: अथ धर्मयुगे तस्मिन्योगधर्ममनुष्ठिता । महीमनुचचारैका सुलभा नाम भिक्षुकी ॥
data.md: In the saine golden age, a woman by name sulabha, belonging to the mendicant order, practised the duties of Yoga and travelled over the entire Earth.

data.v: तया जगदिदं सर्वमटन्त्या मिथिलेश्वरः । तत्र तत्र श्रुतो मोक्षे कथ्यमानस्त्रिदण्डिभिः ॥
data.md: In course of her wanderings over the Earth, Sulabha heard from many ascetics of different places that the king of Mithila was given to the religion of Liberation.

data.v: सा सुसूक्ष्मां कथां श्रुत्वा तथ्यं नेति ससंशया । दर्शने जातसंकल्पा जनकस्य बभूव ह ॥
data.md: Hearing this report about king Janaka and desirous of learning whether it was true or not, Sulabha became desirous of seeing Janaka.

data.v: ततः सा विप्रहायाथ पूर्वरूपं हि योगतः । अबिभ्रदनवद्याङ्गी रूपमन्यदनुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Abandoning, by her Yoga powers, her former body and features, Sulabha assumed the most perfect features and peerless beauty.

data.v: चक्षुर्निमेषमात्रेण लघ्वस्त्रगतिगामिनी । विदेहानां पुरीं सुभ्रूर्जगाम कमलेक्षणा ॥
data.md: In the twinkling of an eye and with the speed of the quickest arrow the fair browed lady having eyes like lotus-petals went to the capital of the Videhas.

data.v: सा प्राप्य मिथिलां रम्यां समृद्धजनसंकुलाम् । भैक्षचर्यापदेशेन ददर्श मिथिलेश्वरम् ॥
data.md: Arrived at the metropolis of Mithila having a large population, she adopted the guise of a mendicant and appeared before the king.

data.v: राजा तस्याः परं दृष्ट्वा सौकुमार्यं वपुस्तथा । केयं कस्य कुतो वेति बभूवागतविस्मयः ॥
data.md: The king, beholding her delicate form, became filed with wonder and enquired who she was, whose she was, and whence she came.

data.v: ततोऽस्याः स्वागतं कृत्वा व्यादिश्य च वरासनम् । पूजितां पादशौचेन वरान्नेनाप्यतर्पयत् ॥
data.md: Welcoming her, he assigned her an excellent seat, honoured her by offering water to wash her feet, and pleased her with excellent refreshments.

data.v: अथ भुक्तवती प्रीता राजानं मन्त्रिभिर्वृतम् । सर्वभाष्यविदां मध्ये चोदयामास भिक्षुकी ॥
data.md: Refreshed duly and pleased with the rites of hospitality offered to her, Sulabha, the female mendicant, urged the king, who was encircled by his ministers and seated in the midst of learned scholars, (to speak out his fidelity to the religion of Liberation).

data.v: सुलभा त्वस्य धर्मेषु मुक्तो नेति ससंशया । सत्त्वं सत्त्वेन योगज्ञा प्रविवेश महीपते ॥
data.md: Doubting whether Janaka has succeeded in acquiring Liberation by following the religion of Renunciation, Sulabha, gifted with Yogapower, entered the understanding of the king by her own understanding.

data.v: नेत्राभ्यां नेत्रयोरस्य रश्मीन्संयोज्य रश्मिभिः । सा स्म संचोदयिष्यन्तं योगबन्धैर्बबन्ध ह ॥
data.md: Controlling, by means of the rays of light that came out from her own eyes, the rays issuing from the eyes of the king, the lady, desirous of ascertaining the truth, bound up king Janaka with Yoga fetters,

data.v: जनकोऽप्युत्स्मयन्राजा भावमस्या विशेषयन् । प्रतिजग्राह भावेन भावमस्या नृपोत्तमः ॥
data.md: Own Priding himself upon his invincibleness and defeating the intentions of Sulabha, that best of kings seized her resolution with his own resolution.

data.v: तदेकस्मिन्नधिष्ठाने संवादः श्रूयतामयम् । छत्रादिषु विमुक्तस्य मुक्तायाश्च त्रिदण्डके ॥
data.md: The king, in his subtile form, had no royal umbrella and sceptre. The lady Sulabha, in hers, was without the threefold stick. Both staying then in the same form, thus conversed with each other. Listen to that conversation as it took place between the king and Sulabha.

data.v: भगवत्याः क्व चर्येयं कृता क्व च गमिष्यसि । कस्य च त्वं कुतो वेति पप्रच्छैनां महीपतिः ॥
data.md: Janaka said O holy lady, to what course of conduct are you given? Whose are you? Whence have you come? After finishing your business here, where will you go?

data.v: श्रुते वयसि जातौ च सद्भावो नाधिगम्यते । एष्वर्थेषूत्तरं तस्मात्प्रवेद्यं सत्समागमे ॥
data.md: No one can, without questioning, determine another's proficiency in the scriptures, or age, or order of birth. You should, therefore, answer these questions of mine, when you have come to me.

data.v: छत्रादिषु विशेषेषु मुक्तं मां विद्धि सर्वशः । स त्वां संमन्तुमिच्छामि मानार्हासि मता हि मे ॥
data.md: Know that I am truly shorn of all vanity about my royal umbrella and sceptre. I wish to know you thoroughly. You are deserving, I think, of my respect.

data.v: यस्माच्चैतन्मया प्राप्तं ज्ञानं वैशेषिकं पुरा । यस्य नान्यः प्रवक्तास्ति मोक्षे तमपि मे शृणु ॥
data.md: Do you hear me as I describe to you Liberation, for there is none else who describe to you that subject. Hear me also as I tell you who that person is from whom in days of yore I acquired this distinguishing knowledge.

data.v: पाराशर्यसगोत्रस्य वृद्धस्य सुमहात्मनः । भिक्षोः पञ्चशिखस्याहं शिष्यः परमसंमतः ॥
data.md: I am the beloved disciple of the great and venerable Panchashikha, belonging to the mendicant order, or Parasara's family.

data.v: सांख्यज्ञाने तथा योगे महीपालविधौ तथा । त्रिविधे मोक्षधर्मेऽस्मिन्गताध्वा छिन्नसंशयः ॥
data.md: My doubts have been removed and I am fully conversant with the Sankhya and the Yoga systems, and the ordinances about sacrifices and other rites, which form the three well known paths of Liberation.

data.v: स यथाशास्त्रदृष्टेन मार्गेणेह परिव्रजन् । वार्षिकांश्चतुरो मासान्पुरा मयि सुखोषितः ॥
data.md: Wandering over the Earth and following path that is pointed out by the scriptures, the learned Panchashika formerly lived happily in my abode for four months during the rains.

data.v: तेनाहं सांख्यमुख्येन सुदृष्टार्थेन तत्त्वतः । श्रावितस्त्रिविधं मोक्षं न च राज्याद्विचालितः ॥
data.md: That foremost of Sankhyas described to me, according to the truth, and in an intelligible manner suited to my understanding, the several kinds of means for acquiring Liberation. He did not, however, order me to give up my kingdom.

data.v: सोऽहं तामखिलां वृत्तिं त्रिविधां मोक्षसंहिताम् । मुक्तरागश्चराम्येकः पदे परमके स्थितः ॥
data.md: Freed from attachments, and fixing my Soul on Supreme Brahma, and unaffected by companionship, I live, practising in all its minute details that threefold conduct which is laid down in treatises on Liberation.

data.v: वैराग्यं पुनरेतस्य मोक्षस्य परमो विधिः । ज्ञानादेव च वैराग्यं जायते येन मुच्यते ॥
data.md: Renunciation in the highest prescribed for Liberation. Renunciation, by which one becomes freed, emanate from Knowledge.

data.v: ज्ञानेन कुरुते यत्नं यत्नेन प्राप्यते महत् । महद्द्वंद्वप्रमोक्षाय सा सिद्धिर्या वयोतिगा ॥
data.md: From Knowledge originates the endeavour after Yoga, and through that exertion one acquires knowledge of Self. Through means knowledge of Self one gets over joy and grief. That enables one to transcend death and acquire great success.

data.v: सेयं परमिका बुद्धिः प्राप्ता निर्द्वंद्वता मया । इहैव गतमोहेन चरता मुक्तसङ्गिना ॥
data.md: That high intelligence has been acquired by me, and accordingly I have not over all pairs of opposites. Even in this life I have been freed from stupefaction and have got over all attachments.

data.v: यथा क्षेत्रं मृदूभूतमद्भिराप्लावितं तथा । जनयत्यङ्कुरं कर्म नृणां तद्वत्पुनर्भवम् ॥
data.md: As a soil, saturated with water and softened thereby, causes the seed to sprout forth, similarly, the acts of men cause rebirth.

data.v: यथा चोत्तापितं बीजं कपाले यत्र तत्र वा । प्राप्याप्यङ्कुरहेतुत्वमबीजत्वान्न जायते ॥
data.md: As a seed, fried on a pan or otherwise, becomes unfit to sprout forth although the power for sprouting lies there, similarly my understanding having been freed from the productive principle formed by desire, by the instructions of the holy Panchashikha of the mendicant order, it no longer gives its fruit in the form of attachment to the objects of the senses.

data.v: तद्वद्भगवता तेन शिखाप्रोक्तेन भिक्षुणा । ज्ञानं कृतमबीजं मे विषयेषु न जायते ॥
