data.md: As a seed, fried on a pan or otherwise, becomes unfit to sprout forth although the power for sprouting lies there, similarly my understanding having been freed from the productive principle formed by desire, by the instructions of the holy Panchashikha of the mendicant order, it no longer gives its fruit in the form of attachment to the objects of the senses.

data.v: नाभिषज्जति कस्मिंश्चिन्नानर्थे न परिग्रहे । नाभिरज्यति चैतेषु व्यर्थत्वाद्रागदोषयोः ॥
data.md: I never experience love for my wife or hate for my enemies. Indeed, I keep aloof from both, making the fruitlessness of attachment and anger.

data.v: यश्च मे दक्षिणं बाहुं चन्दनेन समुक्षयेत् । सव्यं वास्या च यस्तक्षेत्समावेतावुभौ मम ॥
data.md: I regard both person impartially, viz., him who smears my right hand with sandal-paste and him who wounds my left.

data.v: सुखी सोऽहमवाप्तार्थः समलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनः । मुक्तसङ्गः स्थितो राज्ये विशिष्टोऽन्यैस्त्रिदण्डिभिः ॥
data.md: Having attained my object, I am happy, and consider in the same light a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and a lump of gold. I am shorn of all attachments, though am engaged in ruling a kingdom. On account of all this I am better known over all bearers of triple sticks.

data.v: मोक्षे हि त्रिविधा निष्ठा दृष्टा पूर्वैर्महर्षिभिः । ज्ञानं लोकोत्तरं यच्च सर्वत्यागश्च कर्मणाम् ॥
data.md: Some foremost of men who are conversant with the Liberation say that Liberation has a triple path. Some consider Knowledge having all things of the world for its object as the means of Liberation. Some hold that the total renunciation of acts is the means thereof.

data.v: ज्ञाननिष्ठां वदन्त्येके मोक्षशास्त्रविदो जनाः । कर्मनिष्ठां तथैवान्ये यतयः सूक्ष्मदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: Another class of persons conversant with the scriptures Liberation say that Knowledge is the only means. Others, viz., Yatis, gifted with subtile vision; hold that acts form the means.

data.v: प्रहायोभयमप्येतज्ज्ञानं कर्म च केवलम् । तृतीयेयं समाख्याता निष्ठा तेन महात्मना ॥
data.md: The great Panchashikha, discarding both the opinion about knowledge and acts, considered the third as the only means or path of Liberation.

data.v: यमे च नियमे चैव द्वेषे कामे परिग्रहे । माने दम्भे तथा स्नेहे सदृशास्ते कुटुम्बिभिः ॥
data.md: If house-holders be endued with selfrestraint, and control over the senses, they become the equals of Sannyasins. If, on the other hand, Sannyasins be endued with desire and aversion and wives and honour and pride and affection, they become like householders.

data.v: त्रिदण्डादिषु यद्यस्ति मोक्षो ज्ञानेन केनचित् । छत्रादिषु कथं न स्यात्तुल्यहेतौ परिग्रहे ॥
data.md: If one can acquire Liberation by means of knowledge, then may Liberation exist in triple sticks. Why then may Liberation not exist in the umbrella and the sceptre as well, especially when the reason in taking up the triple stick and the scepture is the same.

data.v: येन येन हि यस्यार्थः कारणेनेह कस्यचित् । तत्तदालम्बते द्रव्यं सर्वः स्वे स्वे परिग्रहे ॥
data.md: One becomes attached to all those things and acts which are necessary for him for the sake of his own self for particular reasons.

data.v: दोषदर्शी तु गार्हस्थ्ये यो व्रजत्याश्रमान्तरम् । उत्सृजन्परिगृह्णंश्च सोऽपि सङ्गान्न मुच्यते ॥
data.md: If a person, seeing the faults of the domestic mode of life, renounce it for adopting another mode, he cannot, for such rejection and adoption, he considered as one who is at once freed from all attachments.

data.v: आधिपत्ये तथा तुल्ये निग्रहानुग्रहात्मनि । राजर्षिभिक्षुकाचार्या मुच्यन्ते केन हेतुना ॥
data.md: Sovereignty is fraught with the rewarding and the punishing of others. The life of a mendicant is equally fraught with the same. When, therefore, mendicants are like kings in this respect, why would mendicants only acquire Liberation, and not kings?

data.v: अथ सत्याधिपत्येऽपि ज्ञानेनैवेह केवलम् । मुच्यन्ते किं न मुच्यन्ते पदे परमके स्थिताः ॥
data.md: Not withstanding the possession of sovereignty, therefore, one becomes purged of all sins by means of knowledge alone, living in Supreme Brahma.

data.v: काषायधारणं मौण्ड्यं त्रिविष्टब्धः कमण्डलुः । लिङ्गान्यत्यर्थमेतानि न मोक्षायेति मे मतिः ॥
data.md: The putting on of brown cloths shaving of the head, bearing of the triple stick, and the water-pitcher, these are the external signs of one's mode of life. These are useless in helping one to acquire Liberation.

data.v: यदि सत्यपि लिङ्गेऽस्मिञ्ज्ञानमेवात्र कारणम् । निर्मोक्षायेह दुःखस्य लिङ्गमात्रं निरर्थकम् ॥
data.md: When, despite the adoption of these emblems of a particular mode of life, Knowledge along becomes the cause of one's Liberation from sorrow, it would appear that the adoption of mere emblems is absolutely useless.

data.v: अथ वा दुःखशैथिल्यं वीक्ष्य लिङ्गे कृता मतिः । किं तदेवार्थसामान्यं छत्रादिषु न लक्ष्यते ॥
data.md: Or, if, seeing the mitigation of sorrow in it, you have adopted these emblems of Sanyasa, why then should not the mitigation of sorrow be seen in the umbrella and the sceptre which I use.

data.v: आकिंचन्ये न मोक्षोऽस्ति कैंचन्ये नास्ति बन्धनम् । कैंचन्ये चेतरे चैव जन्तुर्ज्ञानेन मुच्यते ॥
data.md: Liberation does not exist in poverty; nor is bondage to be seen in riches. One acquires Liberation through Knowledge only, whether one is poor or rich.

data.v: तस्माद्धर्मार्थकामेषु तथा राज्यपरिग्रहे । बन्धनायतनेष्वेषु विद्ध्यबन्धे पदे स्थितम् ॥
data.md: For these reasons, know that I am living in a state of freedom, though outwardly engaged in the enjoyment of religion, wealth, and pleasure, in the form of kingdom and wives, which form a field of bondage.

data.v: राज्यैश्वर्यमयः पाशः स्नेहायतनबन्धनः । मोक्षाश्मनिशितेनेह छिन्नस्त्यागासिना मया ॥
data.md: I have cut off the fetters formed by kingdom and riches, and the bondage of attachments, which the sword of Renunciation whetted on the the stone of the of the scriptures describing Liberation.

data.v: सोऽहमेवंगतो मुक्तो जातास्थस्त्वयि भिक्षुकि । अयथार्थो हि ते वर्णो वक्ष्यामि शृणु तन्मम ॥
data.md: As regard myself then, I tell you that I have become freed in this way. O mendicant lady, I entertain an affection for you. But that should not prevent me from telling you that your conduct does not tally with the practices of the mode of life, which you have adopted.

data.v: सौकुमार्यं तथा रूपं वपुरग्र्यं तथा वयः । तवैतानि समस्तानि नियमश्चेति संशयः ॥
data.md: Under formation of the body is highly delicate. You have beauty. You have an exceedingly shapely form. You are young. You have all these, and you have also subjugation of the senses. I doubt it verily. ine as

data.v: यच्चाप्यननुरूपं ते लिङ्गस्यास्य विचेष्टितम् । मुक्तोऽयं स्यान्न वेत्यस्माद्धर्षितो मत्परिग्रहः ॥
data.md: You have stopped up my body for ascertaining as to whether I am really liberated or not. This åct of yours does not tally with that mode of life whose emblems you carry.

data.v: न च कामसमायुक्ते मुक्तेऽप्यस्ति त्रिदण्डकम् । न रक्ष्यते त्वया चेदं न मुक्तस्यास्ति गोपना ॥
data.md: The triple stick is unfit for a Yogin who has desire. As regards yourself, you do not adhere to your stick. As regards those who are freed, they should protect themselves from fall.

data.v: मत्पक्षसंश्रयाच्चायं शृणु यस्ते व्यतिक्रमः । आश्रयन्त्याः स्वभावेन मम पूर्वपरिग्रहम् ॥
data.md: Listen now to to what your transgression has been on account of your contact with me and your having entered into my gross body with the help of your understanding.

data.v: प्रवेशस्ते कृतः केन मम राष्ट्रे पुरे तथा । कस्य वा संनिसर्गात्त्वं प्रविष्टा हृदयं मम ॥
data.md: Why have you entered into my kingdom or my palace? At whose sign have you entered heart.

data.v: वर्णप्रवरमुख्यासि ब्राह्मणी क्षत्रियो ह्यहम् । नावयोरेकयोगोऽस्ति मा कृथा वर्णसंकरम् ॥
data.md: You belong to the foremost of all the orders, being, as you are, a Brahmana woman. As regards myself whoever, I am a Kshatriya. There is no union for us two. Do not help to cause an intermixture of races.

data.v: वर्तसे मोक्षधर्मेषु गार्हस्थ्ये त्वहमाश्रमे । अयं चापि सुकष्टस्ते द्वितीयोऽऽश्रमसंकरः ॥
data.md: You follow the duties that lead to Liberation. I am a householder. This act of yours, therefore, is another evil you have committed, for it produces an unnatural union of two opposite modes of life.

data.v: सगोत्रां वासगोत्रां वा न वेद त्वां न वेत्थ माम् । सगोत्रमाविशन्त्यास्ते तृतीयो गोत्रसंकरः ॥
data.md: into my I do not know whether you belong to my own family or do not belong to it. As regards yourself also, you do not know who I am. If you are of my own Gotra, you have by entering into my body, produced another evil,-viz., or unnatural union.

data.v: अथ जीवति ते भर्ता प्रोषितोऽप्यथ वा क्वचित् । अगम्या परभार्येति चतुर्थो धर्मसंकरः ॥
data.md: If, again, your husband be alive and living in an distant place, your union with me has produced the fourth evil of sinfulness, for you are not one whom I may lawfully marry.

data.v: सा त्वमेतान्यकार्याणि कार्यापेक्षा व्यवस्यसि । अविज्ञानेन वा युक्ता मिथ्याज्ञानेन वा पुनः ॥
data.md: Do you commit all these sinful deeds, actuated by the motive of performing a particular object? Do you do these from ignorance or from perverted intelligence.

data.v: अथ वापि स्वतन्त्रासि स्वदोषेणेह केनचित् । यदि किंचिच्छ्रुतं तेऽस्ति सर्वं कृतमनर्थकम् ॥
data.md: If, again, on account of your evil nature you have thus become thoroughly independent or unrestrained in your conduct, I tell you that if you have any knowledge of the scriptures, you will understand that everything you have done has been productive of evil.

data.v: इदमन्यत्तृतीयं ते भावस्पर्शविघातकम् । दुष्टाया लक्ष्यते लिङ्गं प्रवक्तव्यं प्रकाशितम् ॥
data.md: A third fault touches you on account of these acts of yours, a fault that is destructive of peace of mind. By trying to show your superiority, the indication of a wicked woman is seen in you.

data.v: न मय्येवाभिसंधिस्ते जयैषिण्या जये कृतः । येयं मत्परिषत्कृत्स्ना जेतुमिच्छसि तामपि ॥
data.md: Desirous of asserting your victory as you are, it is not myself alone whom you wish to defeat, for it is plain that you wish to win a victory over even the whole of my court.

data.v: तथा ह्येवं पुनश्च त्वं दृष्टिं स्वां प्रतिमुञ्चसि । मत्पक्षप्रतिघाताय स्वपक्षोद्भावनाय च ॥
data.md: By loO king thus towards all these meritorious Brahmanas, it is clear that you wish to humiliate them all the glorify yourself.

data.v: सा स्वेनामर्षजेन त्वमृद्धिमोहेन मोहिता । भूयः सृजसि योगास्त्रं विषामृतमिवैकधा ॥
data.md: Stupefied by your pride of Yoga power that has been born of your jealousy, you have caused a union of your understanding with mine and thereby have really mingled together nectar with poision.

data.v: इच्छतोर्हि द्वयोर्लाभः स्त्रीपुंसोरमृतोपमः । अलाभश्चाप्यरक्तस्य सोऽत्र दोषो विषोपमः ॥
data.md: The union, again, of man and woman, when each seek the other, is sweet as nectar. That association, however, of man and woman when the latter, herself coveting, cannot get an individual of the opposite sex that does not seek her, is, instead of being a merit, only a fault that is as noxious as poison.

data.v: मा स्प्राक्षीः साधु जानीष्व स्वशास्त्रमनुपालय । कृतेयं हि विजिज्ञासा मुक्तो नेति त्वया मम । एतत्सर्वं प्रतिच्छन्नं मयि नार्हसि गूहितुम् ॥
data.md: Do not continue to touch me. Know that I am righteous. Do you act according to your own scriptures. Your enquiry, viz., whether I am or I am not liberated, has been finished.

data.v: सा यदि त्वं स्वकार्येण यद्यन्यस्य महीपतेः । तत्त्वं सत्रप्रतिच्छन्ना मयि नार्हसि गूहितुम् ॥
data.md: You should not conceal from me all your secret motives. You should not who thus disguise yourself, conceal from me what your object is, that is, whether this call of yours has been prompted by the desire of accomplishing some object of your own or whether you have come for accomplishing the object of some other king.

data.v: न राजानं मृषा गच्छेन्न द्विजातिं कथंचन । न स्त्रियं स्त्रीगुणोपेतां हन्युर्ह्येते मृषागताः ॥
data.md: One should never appear deceitfully before a king; nor before a Brahmana; nor before his wife when that wife is possessed of every wifely virtue. Those who appear in deceitful guise before these three very soon meet with destruction.

data.v: राज्ञां हि बलमैश्वर्यं ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदां बलम् । रूपयौवनसौभाग्यं स्त्रीणां बलमनुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: The power of kings consists in their sovereignty. The power of Brahmanas wellversed in the Vedas is in the Vedas. Women hold a high power on account of their beauty and youth and blessedness.

data.v: अत एतैर्बलैरेते बलिनः स्वार्थमिच्छता । आर्जवेनाभिगन्तव्या विनाशाय ह्यनार्जवम् ॥
data.md: These are powerful in the possession of these powers. He, therefore, who seeks to accomplish his own object should always approach these three with sincerity and openmindedness, Insincerity and deceit cannot yield success.

data.v: सा त्वं जातिं श्रुतं वृत्तं भावं प्रकृतिमात्मनः । कृत्यमागमने चैव वक्तुमर्हसि तत्त्वतः ॥
data.md: You should, therefore, inform me of the order to which you belong by birth, of your learning and conduct and disposition and nature, as also of the object with which you have come here.

data.v: इत्येतैरसुखैर्वाक्यैरयुक्तैरसमञ्जसैः । प्रत्यादिष्टा नरेन्द्रेण सुलभा न व्यकम्पत ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Though chastised by the king in these unpleasant, improper, and ill-applied words, the lady Sulabha was not at all abashed.

data.v: उक्तवाक्ये तु नृपतौ सुलभा चारुदर्शना । ततश्चारुतरं वाक्यं प्रचक्रामाथ भाषितुम् ॥
data.md: After the king had said these words, the beautiful Sulabha then gave vent to the following words in reply which were more handsome than her person.

data.v: नवभिर्नवभिश्चैव दोषैर्वाग्बुद्धिदूषणैः । अपेतमुपपन्नार्थमष्टादशगुणान्वितम् ॥
data.md: O king, speech should always be free from the nine verbal faults and the nine faults of judgement. It should also, while setting forth the meaning with clearness, be possessed of the eighteen well-known merits.

data.v: सौक्ष्म्यं संख्याक्रमौ चोभौ निर्णयः सप्रयोजनः । पञ्चैतान्यर्थजातानि वाक्यमित्युच्यते नृप ॥
data.md: Ambiguity, determination of the faults and merits of premises and conclusions, weighing the respective strength or weakness of those faults and merits, establishment of the conclusion, and the element of persuasiveness or otherwise that belongs to the conclusion thus arrived at,-these five characteristics belonging to the sense-form the authoritativeness of what is said.

data.v: एषामेकैकशोऽर्थानां सौक्ष्म्यादीनां सुलक्षणम् । शृणु संसार्यमाणानां पदार्थैः पदवाक्यतः ॥
data.md: Listen now to the characteristics of these requirements beginning with ambiguity, one after another, as I explain them according to the combinations.

data.v: ज्ञानं ज्ञेयेषु भिन्नेषु यथाभेदेन वर्तते । तत्रातिशयिनी बुद्धिस्तत्सौक्ष्म्यमिति वर्तते ॥
data.md: When knowledge rests on difference from one another, and when the understanding rests upon many points one after another, the combination of words is said to be sullied by ambiguity.

data.v: दोषाणां च गुणानां च प्रमाणं प्रविभागशः । कंचिदर्थमभिप्रेत्य सा संख्येत्युपधार्यताम् ॥
data.md: By ascertainment called Sankhya, is meant the determination, by elimination, of faults or merits, adopting tentative meanings.

data.v: इदं पूर्वमिदं पश्चाद्वक्तव्यं यद्विवक्षितम् । क्रमयोगं तमप्याहुर्वाक्यं वाक्यविदो जनाः ॥
data.md: Krama, or weighing the relative strength or weakness of the faults or merits, consists in settling the propriety of the priority or subsequence of the words used in sentence. This is the meaning of the word Krama as held by person who can explain sentences or texts.

data.v: धर्मार्थकाममोक्षेषु प्रतिज्ञाय विशेषतः । इदं तदिति वाक्यान्ते प्रोच्यते स विनिर्णयः ॥
data.md: Conclusion is the final determination after this examination of what has been said on the subject of religion, pleasure, profit, and Liberation, in respect of what it particularly is that has been said in the text.

data.v: इच्छाद्वेषभवैर्दुःखैः प्रकर्षो यत्र जायते । तत्र या नृपते वृत्तिस्तत्प्रयोजनमिष्यते ॥
data.md: The sorrow begotten by wish or hatred multiplies itself greatly. The conduct, O king, that one follows in such a matter is called Prayojanam.

data.v: तान्येतानि यथोक्तानि सौक्ष्म्यादीनि जनाधिप । एकार्थसमवेतानि वाक्यं मम निशामय ॥
data.md: Take it for granted, O king, at my word, that these marks of Ambiguity and the others, vhen occurring together, make a complete and intelligible sentence.

data.v: उपेतार्थमभिन्नार्थं नापवृत्तं न चाधिकम् । नाश्लक्ष्णं न च संदिग्धं वक्ष्यामि परमं तव ॥
न गुर्वक्षरसंबद्धं पराङ्मुखमुखं न च । नानृतं न त्रिवर्गेण विरुद्धं नाप्यसंस्कृतम् ॥
न न्यूनं कष्टशब्दं वा व्युत्क्रमाभिहितं न च । न शेषं नानुकल्पेन निष्कारणमहेतुकम् ॥
कामात्क्रोधाद्भयाल्लोभाद्दैन्यादानार्यकात्तथा । ह्रीतोऽनुक्रोशतो मानान्न वक्ष्यामि कथंचन ॥
data.md: I shall not tell you anything, actuated by desire or anger or fear or cupidity or abjectness or deceipt or shame or mercy or pride.

data.v: वक्ता श्रोता च वाक्यं च यदा त्वविकलं नृप । सममेति विवक्षायां तदा सोऽर्थः प्रकाशते ॥
data.md: When the speaker, the hearer, and the words said, perfectly agree with one another in course of a speech, then does the sense or meaning come out very clearly.

data.v: वक्तव्ये तु यदा वक्ता श्रोतारमवमन्यते । स्वार्थमाह परार्थं वा तदा वाक्यं न रोहति ॥
data.md: When about what is to be said, the speaker does not care for the understanding of the hearer by uttering words whose meaning is understood by himself, then, however good those words may be, they cannot be comprehended by the hearer.

data.v: अथ यः स्वार्थमुत्सृज्य परार्थं प्राह मानवः । विशङ्का जायते तस्मिन्वाक्यं तदपि दोषवत् ॥
data.md: That speaker, again, who, without caring for his own meaning, uses words that are of excellent sound and sense, creates only erroneous impressions in the mind of the hearer. Such words in such matters are certainly faulty.

data.v: यस्तु वक्ता द्वयोरर्थमविरुद्धं प्रभाषते । श्रोतुश्चैवात्मनश्चैव स वक्ता नेतरो नृप ॥
data.md: That speaker, however, who uses words that are, while expressing his own meaning, intelligible to the hearer as well, is a true speaker. No other man deserves the name.

data.v: तदर्थवदिदं वाक्यमुपेतं वाक्यसंपदा । अविक्षिप्तमना राजन्नेकाग्रः श्रोतुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: You should, therefore, O king, hear with rapt attention these words of mine, fraught with meaning and endued with wealth of sound.

data.v: कासि कस्य कुतो वेति त्वयाहमभिचोदिता । तत्रोत्तरमिदं वाक्यं राजन्नेकमनाः शृणु ॥
data.md: You have asked me who I am, whose I am, whence I am coming, etc. Listen now to me, O king, with full mind, as I answer these questions of yours.

data.v: यथा जतु च काष्ठं च पांसवश्चोदबिन्दुभिः । सुश्लिष्टानि तथा राजन्प्राणिनामिह संभवः ॥
data.md: As lac and wood, as grains of dust and drops of water, exist mixed up when brought together, so are the existence of all creatures.

data.v: शब्दः स्पर्शो रसो रूपं गन्धः पञ्चेन्द्रियाणि च । पृथगात्मा दशात्मानः संश्लिष्टा जतुकाष्ठवत् ॥
data.md: Sound, touch, taste, form, and scent, these, and the senses, though different in their essences, exist yet in a state of unison like lac and wood.

data.v: न चैषां चोदना काचिदस्तीत्येष विनिश्चयः । एकैकस्येह विज्ञानं नास्त्यात्मनि तथा परे ॥
data.md: It is again well known that nobody asks any of these, saying, who are you? Each of them also has no knowledge either of itself or of the others.

data.v: न वेद चक्षुश्चक्षुष्ट्वं श्रोत्रं नात्मनि वर्तते । तथैव व्यभिचारेण न वर्तन्ते परस्परम् । संश्लिष्टा नाभिजायन्ते यथाप इह पांसवः ॥
data.md: The eye cannot see itself. The ear cannot hear itself. The eye, again, cannot satisfy the functions of any of the other senses, or can any of the senses satisfy the functions of any sense except its own.

data.v: बाह्यानन्यानपेक्षन्ते गुणांस्तानपि मे शृणु । रूपं चक्षुः प्रकाशश्च दर्शने हेतवस्त्रयः । यथैवात्र तथान्येषु ज्ञानज्ञेयेषु हेतवः ॥
data.md: The eye, form, and light, form the three requisites of the action called Seeing. The same holds good about the action of the other senses and the ideas which is their result.

data.v: ज्ञानज्ञेयान्तरे तस्मिन्मनो नामापरो गुणः । विचारयति येनायं निश्चये साध्वसाधुनी ॥
data.md: Then, again, between the functions of the senses and the ideas which are their result, the mind is an entity quite separate from the senses and is considered to have an action of its own. With its aid one distinguishes what is existent from what is non-existent for arriving at certainty.

data.v: द्वादशस्त्वपरस्तत्र बुद्धिर्नाम गुणः स्मृतः । येन संशयपूर्वेषु बोद्धव्येषु व्यवस्यति ॥
data.md: With the five senses of knowledge and five senses of action, the mind makes a total of eleven. The twelfth is the Understanding. When doubt originates about what is to be known, the Understanding comes forward and sets at rest all doubts,

data.v: अथ द्वादशके तस्मिन्सत्त्वं नामापरो गुणः । महासत्त्वोऽल्पसत्त्वो वा जन्तुर्येनानुमीयते ॥
data.md: After the twelfth, Sattva is another principle numbering the thirteenth. With its aid creatures are distinguished as possess more of it or less of it in their constitutions,

data.v: क्षेत्रज्ञ इति चाप्यन्यो गुणस्तत्र चतुर्दशः । ममायमिति येनायं मन्यते न च मन्यते ॥
data.md: After this, Consciousness (of self is an other principle.) It helps one to apprehend self as distinguished from what is not self.

data.v: अथ पञ्चदशो राजन्गुणस्तत्रापरः स्मृतः । पृथक्कलासमूहस्य सामग्र्यं तदिहोच्यते ॥
data.md: Desire is the fifteenth principle, O king, the whole universe. The sixteenth principle is Avidya or nescience. To it are attached the seventeenth and the eighteenth principles called Nature and Manifestation.

data.v: गुणस्त्वेवापरस्तत्र संघात इति षोडशः । आकृतिर्व्यक्तिरित्येतौ गुणौ यस्मिन्समाश्रितौ ॥
data.md: Desire is the fifteenth principle, O king, the whole universe. The sixteenth principle is Avidya or nescience. To it are attached the seventeenth and the eighteenth principles called Nature and Manifestation.

data.v: सुखदुःखे जरामृत्यू लाभालाभौ प्रियाप्रिये । इति चैकोनविंशोऽयं द्वंद्वयोग इति स्मृतः ॥
data.md: Happiness and sorrow, decrepitude and death, gain and loss, the agreeable and the disagreeable,-these form the nineteenth principle and are called pairs of opposites.

data.v: ऊर्ध्वमेकोनविंशत्याः कालो नामापरो गुणः । इतीमं विद्धि विंशत्या भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययम् ॥
data.md: Beyond the nineteenth principle is another, viz., Time, called the twentieth. Know that the births and deaths of all creatures are owing to the action of this twentieth principle.

data.v: विंशकश्चैष संघातो महाभूतानि पञ्च च । सदसद्भावयोगौ च गुणावन्यौ प्रकाशकौ ॥
इत्येवं विंशतिश्चैव गुणाः सप्त च ये स्मृताः । विधिः शुक्रं बलं चेति त्रय एते गुणाः परे ॥
एकविंशश्च दश च कलाः संख्यानतः स्मृताः । समग्रा यत्र वर्तन्ते तच्छरीरमिति स्मृतम् ॥
अव्यक्तं प्रकृतिं त्वासां कलानां कश्चिदिच्छति । व्यक्तं चासां तथैवान्यः स्थूलदर्शी प्रपश्यति ॥
data.md: Whether the Unmanifest or the Manifest be their cause, or whether the two be considered as their cause, or, fourthly, whether the four together be the cause, they that are conversant with spiritual science behold Nature as the cause of all creatures.

data.v: अव्यक्तं यदि वा व्यक्तं द्वयीमथ चतुष्टयीम् । प्रकृतिं सर्वभूतानां पश्यन्त्यध्यात्मचिन्तकाः ॥
data.md: Whether the Unmanifest or the Manifest be their cause, or whether the two be considered as their cause, or, fourthly, whether the four together be the cause, they that are conversant with spiritual science behold Nature as the cause of all creatures.

data.v: सेयं प्रकृतिरव्यक्ता कलाभिर्व्यक्ततां गता । अहं च त्वं च राजेन्द्र ये चाप्यन्ये शरीरिणः ॥
data.md: That Nature which is Unmanifest, becomes manifest in the form of these principles. Myself, yourself, O king, and all others that are gifted with body, are the result of that Nature.

data.v: बिन्दुन्यासादयोऽवस्थाः शुक्रशोणितसंभवाः । यासामेव निपातेन कललं नाम जायते ॥
data.md: Embryonic conditions are due to the mixture of the vital seed and blood. On account of insemination the result which first appears is called by the name of 'Kalala.

data.v: कललादर्बुदोत्पत्तिः पेशी चाप्यर्बुदोद्भवा । पेश्यास्त्वङ्गाभिनिर्वृत्तिर्नखरोमाणि चाङ्गतः ॥
data.md: From 'Kalala' originates bubble. From 'Budbuda' originates what is called 'Peshi.' From 'Peshi' that stage originates in which the various limbs are seen. From this last stage appear nails and hair.

data.v: संपूर्णे नवमे मासे जन्तोर्जातस्य मैथिल । जायते नामरूपत्वं स्त्री पुमान्वेति लिङ्गतः ॥
data.md: When the ninth months is gone, O king of Mithila, the creature takes its birth so that, its sex being known, it is called a boy or girl.

data.v: जातमात्रं तु तद्रूपं दृष्ट्वा ताम्रनखाङ्गुलि । कौमाररूपमापन्नं रूपतो नोपलभ्यते ॥
data.md: When the creature comes out of the womb, the form it presents is such that its nails and fingers seem to be of the colour of burnished copper. The next stage is called infancy, when the forin that was seen at the time of birth becomes metamorphosed.

data.v: कौमाराद्यौवनं चापि स्थाविर्यं चापि यौवनात् । अनेन क्रमयोगेन पूर्वं पूर्वं न लभ्यते ॥
data.md: From infancy youth is reached, and from youth, old age. As the creature advances from one stage into another, the from shown in the previous stage becomes changed.

data.v: कलानां पृथगर्थानां प्रतिभेदः क्षणे क्षणे । वर्तते सर्वभूतेषु सौक्ष्म्यात्तु न विभाव्यते ॥
data.md: The constituent elements of the body, which serve various functions in the general economy, undergo change every moment in every creature. Those changes, however, are so minute that they cannot be marked.

data.v: न चैषामप्ययो राजँल्लक्ष्यते प्रभवो न च । अवस्थायामवस्थायां दीपस्येवार्चिषो गतिः ॥
data.md: The birth of particles, and their death, in each successive stage, cannot be marked, O king, even as one cannot mark the changes in the flame of a burning lamp.

data.v: तस्याप्येवंप्रभावस्य सदश्वस्येव धावतः । अजस्रं सर्वलोकस्य कः कुतो वा न वा कुतः ॥
data.md: When such is the state of the bodies of all creatures,-i.e., when what is called the body is changing continually like the rapid motion of a house of good mettle,-who then has come whence or not whence, or whose is it or whose is it not, or whence does it not arise? What connection does there exist between creatures and their own bodies?

data.v: कस्येदं कस्य वा नेदं कुतो वेदं न वा कुतः । संबन्धः कोऽस्ति भूतानां स्वैरप्यवयवैरिह ॥
data.md: When such is the state of the bodies of all creatures,-i.e., when what is called the body is changing continually like the rapid motion of a house of good mettle,-who then has come whence or not whence, or whose is it or whose is it not, or whence does it not arise? What connection does there exist between creatures and their own bodies?

data.v: यथादित्यान्मणेश्चैव वीरुद्भ्यश्चैव पावकः । भवत्येवं समुदयात्कलानामपि जन्तवः ॥
data.md: As fire is generated from the contact of flint with iron, or from two sticks of wood when rubbed against each other, so are creatures created from combination of the (thirty) principles already named.

data.v: आत्मन्येवात्मनात्मानं यथा त्वमनुपश्यसि । एवमेवात्मनात्मानमन्यस्मिन्किं न पश्यसि । यद्यात्मनि परस्मिंश्च समतामध्यवस्यसि ॥
data.md: Indeed, as you yourself see your own body in your body and as you yourself see your soul in your own soul, why is it that you do not see your own body and your own soul in the bodies and souls of others.

data.v: अथ मां कासि कस्येति किमर्थमनुपृच्छसि । इदं मे स्यादिदं नेति द्वंद्वैर्मुक्तस्य मैथिल । कासि कस्य कुतो वेति वचने किं प्रयोजनम् ॥
data.md: If it is true that you have, O King, been freed from the knowledge of duality which says-this is mine and this other is not mine, then what use is there with such questions as Who are you, whose are you, and whence do you come?

data.v: रिपौ मित्रेऽथ मध्यस्थे विजये संधिविग्रहे । कृतवान्यो महीपाल किं तस्मिन्मुक्तलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: What marks of Liberation can be said to take place in that king who acts as others act towards enemies and allies and neutrals and in victory and trace and war?

data.v: त्रिवर्गे सप्तधा व्यक्तं यो न वेदेह कर्मसु । सङ्गवान्यस्त्रिवर्गे च किं तस्मिन्मुक्तलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: What inarks of Liberation are in him who do not know the true nature of the three-fold objects of life as shown in seven ways in all acts and who, on that account, is attached to that three-fold objects?

data.v: प्रिये चैवाप्रिये चैव दुर्बले बलवत्यपि । यस्य नास्ति समं चक्षुः किं तस्मिन्मुक्तलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: What marks of Liberation exist in him who cannot look impartially on the agreeable, on the weak, and the strong? Unworthy as you are of it, your pretence to Liberation should be suppressed by your counsellors.

data.v: तदमुक्तस्य ते मोक्षे योऽभिमानो भवेन्नृप । सुहृद्भिः स निवार्यस्ते विचित्तस्येव भेषजैः ॥
data.md: This your attempt to acquire Liberation is like the use of medicine by a patient who indulges in all sorts of forbidden food and practices.

data.v: तानि तान्यनुसंदृश्य सङ्गस्थानान्यरिंदम । आत्मनात्मनि संपश्येत्किं तस्मिन्मुक्तलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: O chastiser of enemies, thinking of wives and other sources of attachment, one should see these in his own soul. What else can be considered as the indication of Liberation.

data.v: इमान्यन्यानि सूक्ष्माणि मोक्षमाश्रित्य कानिचित् । चतुरङ्गप्रवृत्तानि सङ्गस्थानानि मे शृणु ॥
data.md: Listen now to me as I speak fully of these and certain other minute sources of attachment belonging to the four-well-known acts to which you are still fettered though you profess yourself to have adopted the religion of Liberation.

data.v: य इमां पृथिवीं कृत्स्नामेकच्छत्रां प्रशास्ति ह । एकमेव स वै राजा पुरमध्यावसत्युत ॥
data.md: That man who has to rule the entire world must, indeed, be a single king without a second. He is obliged to live in only a single palace.

data.v: तत्पुरे चैकमेवास्य गृहं यदधितिष्ठति । गृहे शयनमप्येकं निशायां यत्र लीयते ॥
data.md: In that palace he has again only one sleeping 'room. In that room he has, again, only one bed on which at night he is to lie down.

data.v: शय्यार्धं तस्य चाप्यत्र स्त्रीपूर्वमधितिष्ठति । तदनेन प्रसङ्गेन फलेनैवेह युज्यते ॥
data.md: Half that bed again he is obliged to give to his Queen. This may serve as an example of how little the king's share is of all he is said to possess.

data.v: एवमेवोपभोगेषु भोजनाच्छादनेषु च । गुणेषु परिमेयेषु निग्रहानुग्रहौ प्रति ॥
data.md: This is the case with his objects of enjoyment, with the food he eats, and with the dresses he puts on. He is thus attached to a very limited share of all things. He is, again, attached to the duties of rewarding and punishing.

data.v: परतन्त्रः सदा राजा स्वल्पे सोऽपि प्रसज्जते । संधिविग्रहयोगे च कुतो राज्ञः स्वतन्त्रता ॥
data.md: The king always depends on others. He enjoys a very small share of all he is supposed to possess, and to that small share he is compelled to be attached. In the matter also of peace and war, the king is not independent?

data.v: स्त्रीषु क्रीडाविहारेषु नित्यमस्यास्वतन्त्रता । मन्त्रे चामात्यसमितौ कुत एव स्वतन्त्रता ॥
data.md: In the matter of women, of sports and other sports of enjoyment, the king's inclinations are greatly limited. In the matter of taking advice and in the assembly of his councellors what independence can the king be said to have.

data.v: यदा त्वाज्ञापयत्यन्यांस्तदास्योक्ता स्वतन्त्रता । अवशः कार्यते तत्र तस्मिंस्तस्मिन्गुणे स्थितः ॥
data.md: When, indeed, he passes orders on other men, he is said to be perfectly independent. But the moment after, in the several matters of his orders, his independence is limited by the very men whom he has ordered.

data.v: स्वप्तुकामो न लभते स्वप्तुं कार्यार्थिभिर्जनैः । शयने चाप्यनुज्ञातः सुप्त उत्थाप्यतेऽवशः ॥
data.md: If the king wishes to sleep, he cannot satisfy his desire, resisted by those who have something to do with him. He must sleep when allowed, and while sleeping he is compelled to wake up for attending to those who have urgent business with him.

data.v: स्नाह्यालभ पिब प्राश जुहुध्यग्नीन्यजेति च । वदस्व शृणु चापीति विवशः कार्यते परैः ॥
data.md: Bathe, touch, drink, eat, pour libations on the fire, celebrate sacrifices, speak, hear,these are the words which kings have to hear from others and hearing them have to serve those that utter them.

data.v: अभिगम्याभिगम्यैनं याचन्ते सततं नराः । न चाप्युत्सहते दातुं वित्तरक्षी महाजनात् ॥
data.md: Men come in numbers to the king and pray to him for gifts. Being, however, the protector of the general treasury, he cannot make gifts even to the most worthy.

data.v: दाने कोशक्षयो ह्यस्य वैरं चाप्यप्रयच्छतः । क्षणेनास्योपवर्तन्ते दोषा वैराग्यकारकाः ॥
data.md: If he makes gifts, the treasury becomes exhausted. If he does not, disappointed solicitors regard him inimically. He becomes vexed and as the outcome of this, misanthropy possesses his mind.

data.v: प्राज्ञाञ्शूरांस्तथैवाढ्यानेकस्थानेऽपि शङ्कते । भयमप्यभये राज्ञो यैश्च नित्यमुपास्यते ॥
data.md: If many wise and heroic and rich men live together, the king's mind begins to be filled with distrust. Even when there is no cause of fear, the king fears those who always wait upon and adore him.

data.v: यदा चैते प्रदुष्यन्ति राजन्ये कीर्तिता मया । तदैवास्य भयं तेभ्यो जायते पश्य यादृशम् ॥
data.md: Those I have mentioned, O king, also find fault with him. See, how the king's fears may originate from even them.

data.v: सर्वः स्वे स्वे गृहे राजा सर्वः स्वे स्वे गृहे गृही । निग्रहानुग्रहौ कुर्वंस्तुल्यो जनक राजभिः ॥
data.md: Then again all men are kings in their own houses. All men, again, in their own houses are householders. Like kings, O Janaka, all men in their own houses punish and reward.

data.v: पुत्रा दारास्तथैवात्मा कोशो मित्राणि संचयः । परैः साधारणा ह्येते तैस्तैरेवास्य हेतुभिः ॥
data.md: Like kings others also have sons and wives and their own selves and treasuries and friends and stores. In these respects the king does not differ from other men.

data.v: हतो देशः पुरं दग्धं प्रधानः कुञ्जरो मृतः । लोकसाधारणेष्वेषु मिथ्याज्ञानेन तप्यते ॥
data.md: The country is ruined, the city is burnt by fire,-the foremost of elephants is dead, at all this the king grieves like others, little thinking that these impressions are all owing to ignorance and mistake.

data.v: अमुक्तो मानसैर्दुःखैरिच्छाद्वेषप्रियोद्भवैः । शिरोरोगादिभी रोगैस्तथैव विनिपातिभिः ॥
data.md: The king is seldom freed from mental sorrows caused by desire and aversion and fear. He is generally afflicted also by headaches and various other diseases.

data.v: द्वंद्वैस्तैस्तैरुपहतः सर्वतः परिशङ्कितः । बहुप्रत्यर्थिकं राज्यमुपास्ते गणयन्निशाः ॥
data.md: The king is afflicted by all pairs of opposites. He is alarmed at everything. Indeed, beset with enemies and obstacles as kingdom is, the king, while he enjoys it, passes sleepless nights.

data.v: तदल्पसुखमत्यर्थं बहुदुःखमसारवत् । को राज्यमभिपद्येत प्राप्य चोपशमं लभेत् ॥
ममेदमिति यच्चेदं पुरं राष्ट्रं च मन्यसे । बलं कोशममात्यांश्च कस्यैतानि न वा नृप ॥
मित्रामात्यं पुरं राष्ट्रं दण्डः कोशो महीपतिः । सप्ताङ्गश्चक्रसंघातो राज्यमित्युच्यते नृप ॥
सप्ताङ्गस्यास्य राज्यस्य त्रिदण्डस्येव तिष्ठतः । अन्योन्यगुणयुक्तस्य कः केन गुणतोऽधिकः ॥
data.md: You think also this army, this treasury, and these counsellors as yours. Whose, however, in sooth are they, and whose are they not? Allies, ministers, capital, provinces, punishment, treasury, and the king,—these seven which form the limbs of a kingdom exist, depending upon one another, like three sticks standing with one another's help. The merits of each are shown by the merits of the others. Which of them can be said to be superior to the rest?

data.v: तेषु तेषु हि कालेषु तत्तदङ्गं विशिष्यते । येन यत्सिध्यते कार्यं तत्प्राधान्याय कल्पते ॥
data.md: Some particular ones are regarded as superior to the rest when some important purpose is served through their agency. Superiority, for the time being, is said to belong to that one whose efficacy is thus seen.

data.v: सप्ताङ्गश्चापि संघातस्त्रयश्चान्ये नृपोत्तम । संभूय दशवर्गोऽयं भुङ्क्ते राज्यं हि राजवत् ॥
data.md: The seven limbs already mentioned, O best of kings, and the three others, forming ten, supporting one another, are said to enjoy the kingdom like the king himself.

data.v: यश्च राजा महोत्साहः क्षत्रधर्मरतो भवेत् । स तुष्येद्दशभागेन ततस्त्वन्यो दशावरैः ॥
data.md: That king who is gifted with great energy and who is firmly attached to Kshatriya duties, should be satisfied with only a tenth part of the produce of the subject's field.Other kings are seen to be satisfied with less than a tenth part of such produce.

data.v: नास्त्यसाधारणो राजा नास्ति राज्यमराजकम् । राज्येऽसति कुतो धर्मो धर्मेऽसति कुतः परम् ॥
data.md: There is no one who possessed the kingly office without some one else possessing it in the world, and there is no kingdom without a king. If there be no kingdom, there can be no virtue and if there be no virtue, whence can Liberation arise.

data.v: योऽप्यत्र परमो धर्मः पवित्रं राजराज्ययोः । पृथिवी दक्षिणा यस्य सोऽश्वमेधो न विद्यते ॥
data.md: Merit of the most sacred and the highest order is associated with kings and kingdoms. By ruling a kingdom well, a king acquires the merit of a Horse-sacrifice with the whole Earth given away as sacrificial gift.

data.v: साहमेतानि कर्माणि राज्यदुःखानि मैथिल । समर्था शतशो वक्तुमथ वापि सहस्रशः ॥
data.md: O king of Mithila, I can mention hundreds and thousands of faults like these that belong to kings and kingdoms.

data.v: स्वदेहे नाभिषङ्गो मे कुतः परपरिग्रहे । न मामेवंविधां मुक्तामीदृशं वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Then, again, when I have no real connection with even my body, how then can I be said to have any connection with the bodies of others? You cannot charge me with having tried to engender an inter-mixture of castes.

data.v: ननु नाम त्वया मोक्षः कृत्स्नः पञ्चशिखाच्छ्रुतः । सोपायः सोपनिषदः सोपासङ्गः सनिश्चयः ॥
data.md: Have you heard the religion of Liberation in all its bearings from the lips of Panchashikha, together with its means, it methods, its practises, and its conclusion?

data.v: तस्य ते मुक्तसङ्गस्य पाशानाक्रम्य तिष्ठतः । छत्रादिषु विशेषेषु कथं सङ्गः पुनर्नृप ॥
data.md: If you have prevailed over all your bonds and freed yourself from all attachments, may I ask you, O king, why you preserve your connections still with this umbrella and those other appendages of royalty.

data.v: श्रुतं ते न श्रुतं मन्ये मिथ्या वापि श्रुतं श्रुतम् । अथ वा श्रुतसंकाशं श्रुतमन्यच्छ्रुतं त्वया ॥
data.md: I think that you have not listened to the scriptures, or, you have listened to them without any advantage, or, perhaps, you have listened to some other books loO king like the scriptures.

data.v: अथापीमासु संज्ञासु लौकिकीषु प्रतिष्ठसि । अभिषङ्गावरोधाभ्यां बद्धस्त्वं प्राकृतो यथा ॥
data.md: It appears that you are endued with only worldly knowledge, and that like an ordinary man of the world, you are bound by the fetters of touch and wives and mansions and the like.

data.v: सत्त्वेनानुप्रवेशो हि योऽयं त्वयि कृतो मया । किं तवापकृतं तत्र यदि मुक्तोऽसि सर्वतः ॥
data.md: If be true that you have been freed from all fetters, what harm then have I done you by entering your body with only my Intellect?

data.v: नियमो ह्येष धर्मेषु यतीनां शून्यवासिता । शून्यमावासयन्त्या च मया किं कस्य दूषितम् ॥
data.md: The practice with Yatis is to live in uninhabited or deserted adodes. What harm them have I done to whom by entering your understanding which is indeed shorn of true knowledge?

data.v: न पाणिभ्यां न बाहुभ्यां पादोरुभ्यां न चानघ । न गात्रावयवैरन्यैः स्पृशामि त्वा नराधिप ॥
data.md: I have not touched you, O king, with my hands, or arms, or feet, or thighs, O sinless One, or with any other part of the body.

data.v: कुले महति जातेन ह्रीमता दीर्घदर्शिना । नैतत्सदसि वक्तव्यं सद्वासद्वा मिथः कृतम् ॥
data.md: You are born in a great family. You have modesty. You have foresight. Whether the act has been good or bad, my entrance into your person has been a private one, concerning us two only. Was it not unfair for you to proclaim that private act before all your ministers.

data.v: ब्राह्मणा गुरवश्चेमे तथामात्या गुरूत्तमाः । त्वं चाथ गुरुरप्येषामेवमन्योन्यगौरवम् ॥
data.md: All these Brahmanas deserve respect. They are foremost of preceptors. You also are worthy of their respect, being their king. Doing them respect, you are entitled to receive reverence from them.

data.v: तदेवमनुसंदृश्य वाच्यावाच्यं परीक्षता । स्त्रीपुंसोः समवायोऽयं त्वया वाच्यो न संसदि ॥
data.md: Thinking on all this, it was not proper for you to proclaim before these foremost of men the fact of this union between two persons of opposite sexes, if indeed, you are really acquainted with the rules of propriety about speech.

data.v: यथा पुष्करपर्णस्थं जलं तत्पर्णसंस्थितम् । तिष्ठत्यस्पृशती तद्वत्त्वयि वत्स्यामि मैथिल ॥
data.md: O king of Mithila, I am living in you without touching you at all even like a drop of water on a lotus leaf that rests on it without drenching it in the least.

data.v: यदि वाप्यस्पृशन्त्या मे स्पर्शं जानासि कंचन । ज्ञानं कृतमबीजं ते कथं तेनेह भिक्षुणा ॥
data.md: If, despite this, you still feel my touch, how can it be believed that through the instructions of the mendicant Panchashika, your knowledge has become disassociated from the sensual objects.

data.v: स गार्हस्थ्याच्च्युतश्च त्वं मोक्षं नावाप्य दुर्विदम् । उभयोरन्तराले च वर्तसे मोक्षवातिकः ॥
data.md: You have, it is evident, deviated from the domestic mode of life, but you have not yet acquired Liberation that is so difficult to acquire. You live between the two, pretending that you have reach the goal of Liberation.

data.v: न हि मुक्तस्य मुक्तेन ज्ञस्यैकत्वपृथक्त्वयोः । भावाभावसमायोगे जायते वर्णसंकरः ॥
data.md: The contact of one that is liberated with another that has been so, or of Soul with Nature, cannot lead to an intermingling which you fear.

data.v: वर्णाश्रमपृथक्त्वे च दृष्टार्थस्यापृथक्त्विनः । नान्यदन्यदिति ज्ञात्वा नान्यदन्यत्प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: Only those who consider the Soul to be at one with the body, and who think the several orders and modes of life to be really different from one another, commit the inistake of supposing an intermingling to be possible. My body is different from yours. But my soul is not different from your soul. When I am able to realise this, I have not the least doubt that my understanding is really not living in yours, though I have entered into you by Yoga.

data.v: पाणौ कुण्डं तथा कुण्डे पयः पयसि मक्षिकाः । आश्रिताश्रययोगेन पृथक्त्वेनाश्रया वयम् ॥
data.md: A pot is carried in the hand. In the pot there is milk. On the milk is a fly. Though the hand and pot, the pot and milk, and the milk and the fly, cxist together, yet they are all different from each other.

data.v: न तु कुण्डे पयोभावः पयश्चापि न मक्षिकाः । स्वयमेवाश्रयन्त्येते भावा न तु पराश्रयम् ॥
data.md: The pot does not assume the nature of the milk. Nor does the milk partake the nature of the fly. The condition of each is in dependent of itself, and can never be changed by the condition of that other with which it may for the time being exist.

data.v: पृथक्त्वादाश्रमाणां च वर्णान्यत्वे तथैव च । परस्परपृथक्त्वाच्च कथं ते वर्णसंकरः ॥
data.md: Simnilarly, colour and practices, though they may exist together with and in a person that is liberated, do not really belong to him. How then can an intermingly of orders be possible on account of this union of myself with you.

data.v: नास्मि वर्णोत्तमा जात्या न वैश्या नावरा तथा । तव राजन्सवर्णास्मि शुद्धयोनिरविप्लुता ॥
data.md: Then, again, I am not superior to you in colour. Nor am I a Vaishya, nor a Shudra, I am, O king, of the same caste with you, born of a pure family.

data.v: प्रधानो नाम राजर्षिर्व्यक्तं ते श्रोत्रमागतः । कुले तस्य समुत्पन्नां सुलभां नाम विद्धि माम् ॥
data.md: There was a royal sage named Pradhana. It is clear that you have heard of him. I am born in his family, and my name is Sulabha.

data.v: द्रोणश्च शतशृङ्गश्च वक्रद्वारश्च पर्वतः । मम सत्रेषु पूर्वेषां चिता मघवता सह ॥
data.md: In the sacrifices performed by my ancestors, the foremost of the gods, viz., Indra, used come, accompanied by Drona, Shatashringa, and Chakradvara.

data.v: साहं तस्मिन्कुले जाता भर्तर्यसति मद्विधे । विनीता मोक्षधर्मेषु चराम्येका मुनिव्रतम् ॥
data.md: Born in such a family, it was found that no fitting husband could be found for me. Instructed then in the religion of Liberation, I wander over the Earth alone, practising asceticism. to

data.v: नास्मि सत्रप्रतिच्छन्ना न परस्वाभिमानिनी । न धर्मसंकरकरी स्वधर्मेऽस्मि धृतव्रता ॥
data.md: I am not a hypocrite with regard to the life of Renunciation I follow; I am not a thief that appropriates others properties. I am not a confuser of the practices of the different castes. I am firm in the practices of the mode of life I follow.

data.v: नास्थिरा स्वप्रतिज्ञायां नासमीक्ष्यप्रवादिनी । नासमीक्ष्यागता चाहं त्वत्सकाशं जनाधिप ॥
data.md: I am firm and steady in my vows. I never utter any word without thinking of its fitness. I did not come to you, without having thought properly, O king!

data.v: मोक्षे ते भावितां बुद्धिं श्रुत्वाहं कुशलैषिणी । तव मोक्षस्य चाप्यस्य जिज्ञासार्थमिहागता ॥
data.md: Having heard that your understanding has been purified by the religion of Liberation, I came here from desire of some good. Indeed, it was for enquiring of you about Liberation that I had come.

data.v: न वर्गस्था ब्रवीम्येतत्स्वपक्षपरपक्षयोः । मुक्तो न मुच्यते यश्च शान्तो यश्च न शाम्यति ॥
data.md: I do not say so for glorifying myself and humiliating my opponents. But I say it, out of sincerity only. What I say is that he who is liberated never vaunts that intellectual superiority which one shows by logical discussions for the sake of victory. He, on the other hand, is really liberated who devotes himself to Brahima, that sole seat of peace.

data.v: यथा शून्ये पुरागारे भिक्षुरेकां निशां वसेत् । तथा हि त्वच्छरीरेऽस्मिन्निमां वत्स्यामि शर्वरीम् ॥
data.md: As a person of the mendicant order lives for only one night in an emphy house, similarly, I shall live for this one night in your body.

data.v: साहमासनदानेन वागातिथ्येन चार्चिता । सुप्ता सुशरणा प्रीता श्वो गमिष्यामि मैथिल ॥
data.md: You have honoured me with both words and other offers that are due from a host to a guest. Having slept this one night in your body, O king of Mithila, which is as it were my own chamber now, tomorrow I shall go.

data.v: इत्येतानि स वाक्यानि हेतुमन्त्यर्थवन्ति च । श्रुत्वा नाधिजगौ राजा किंचिदन्यदतः परम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Hearing these words fraught with excellent sense and with reason, king Janaka could not replay thereto.

data.v: कथं निर्वेदमापन्नः शुको वैयासकिः पुरा । एतदिच्छामि कौरव्य श्रोतुं कौतूहलं हि मे ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said How was Shuka the son of Vyasa, in days of yore, won over to Renunciation? I wish to hear you recite the story. My curiosity about it is irrepressible.

data.v: प्राकृतेन सुवृत्तेन चरन्तमकुतोभयम् । अध्याप्य कृत्स्नं स्वाध्यायमन्वशाद्वै पिता सुतम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Seeing his son Shuka living fearlessly as ordinary men do in practices that are regarded innocent by them, Vyasa taught him the entire Vedas and then discoursed to him one day in following manner.

data.v: धर्मं पुत्र निषेवस्व सुतीक्ष्णौ हि हिमातपौ । क्षुत्पिपासे च वायुं च जय नित्यं जितेन्द्रियः ॥
data.md: Vyasa said O son, becoming the master of your senses, do you conquer extreme cold and extreme heat, hunger and thirst, and the wind also, and having controlled them, do you practise virtue.

data.v: सत्यमार्जवमक्रोधमनसूयां दमं तपः । अहिंसां चानृशंस्यं च विधिवत्परिपालय ॥
data.md: Do you duly observe truth and sincerity, and freedom from anger and malice, and selfcontrol and penances, and the duties of benevolence and mercy.

data.v: सत्ये तिष्ठ रतो धर्मे हित्वा सर्वमनार्जवम् । देवतातिथिशेषेण यात्रां प्राणस्य संश्रय ॥
data.md: Rest you on truth, firmly devoted to virtue, renouncing all sorts of insincerity and deceit. Do you support your life on the remnants of food after feeding gods and guests.

data.v: फेनपात्रोपमे देहे जीवे शकुनिवत्स्थिते । अनित्ये प्रियसंवासे कथं स्वपिषि पुत्रक ॥
data.md: Your body is as fickle as the froth on the surface of water. The Individual Soul is sitting unattached in it as a bird on a tree. The companionship of all agreeable objects is transitory. Why then, O son, do you sleep in such forgetfulness?

data.v: अप्रमत्तेषु जाग्रत्सु नित्ययुक्तेषु शत्रुषु । अन्तरं लिप्समानेषु बालस्त्वं नावबुध्यसे ॥
data.md: Your enemies are careful and awake and ever-ready (to assail you) and always watchful of their opportunity. Why are you so foolish as not to know this?

data.v: गण्यमानेषु वर्षेषु क्षीयमाणे तथायुषि । जीविते शिष्यमाणे च किमुत्थाय न धावसि ॥
data.md: As the days are going one after another, and period of your life is being decreased. Indeed, when your life is being continually shortened, why do you not run to preceptors?

data.v: ऐहलौकिकमीहन्ते मांसशोणितवर्धनम् । पारलौकिककार्येषु प्रसुप्ता भृशनास्तिकाः ॥
data.md: Only they who have no faith, set their hearts on worldly things that have the only effect of increasing flesh and blood. They do not care for the next world.

data.v: धर्माय येऽभ्यसूयन्ति बुद्धिमोहान्विता नराः । अपथा गच्छतां तेषामनुयातापि पीड्यते ॥
data.md: Those men who are stupefied by erroneous understandings show a hatred for virtue. The man who follows those misguided persons that have taken to devious and wrong paths is afflicted equally with them.

data.v: ये तु तुष्टाः सुनियताः सत्यागमपरायणाः । धर्म्यं पन्थानमारूढास्तानुपास्स्व च पृच्छ च ॥
data.md: They, however, who are contented, devoted to the scriptures, gifted with high souls, and possessed of great might, follow the path of virtue. Do you wait upon them with respect and seek instruction from them.

data.v: उपधार्य मतं तेषां वृद्धानां धर्मदर्शिनाम् । नियच्छ परया बुद्ध्या चित्तमुत्पथगामि वै ॥
data.md: Do you act according to the instructions received from those wise men whose eyes are set upon virtue. With understanding purified by such instructions and made superior, do you then control your heart which is ever ready to deviate from the right course.

data.v: अद्यकालिकया बुद्ध्या दूरे श्व इति निर्भयाः । सर्वभक्षा न पश्यन्ति कर्मभूमिं विचेतसः ॥
data.md: They who always think about the present, who fearlessly consider the tomorrow as something quite remote,-they who do not observe any restrictions about food-are really senseless wights who fail to understand that this world is only a field of probation.

data.v: धर्मनिःश्रेणिमास्थाय किंचित्किंचित्समारुह । कोशकारवदात्मानं वेष्टयन्नावबुध्यसे ॥
data.md: Going to the flight of steps formed by Virtue. Do you ascend those steps one after another. At present you are like a worm which weaves its cocoon round itself and thereby closes up all means of escape.

data.v: नास्तिकं भिन्नमर्यादं कूलपातमिवास्थिरम् । वामतः कुरु विस्रब्धो नरं वेणुमिवोद्धतम् ॥
data.md: Do you shun unhesitatingly, the atheist who transgresses all restraints, who is situated like a house by the side of a dreadful and encroaching current, and who seems to stand like a bamboo with its head erect in pride.

data.v: कामं क्रोधं च मृत्युं च पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां नदीम् । नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संतर ॥
data.md: Do you with the raft of Yoga cross the ocean of the world those whose five senses constitute its waters, having Desires and Anger and Death for its fierce monsters, and birth for its votex.

data.v: मृत्युनाभ्याहते लोके जरया परिपीडिते । अमोघासु पतन्तीषु धर्मयानेन संतर ॥
data.md: Do you cross, with the raft of Virtue, the world that is affected by Death and afflicted by Decrepitude, and upon which the thunder-bolts formed by days and nights and falling incessantly.

data.v: तिष्ठन्तं च शयानं च मृत्युरन्वेषते यदा । निर्वृतिं लभसे कस्मादकस्मान्मृत्युनाशितः ॥
data.md: When Death is seeking you at every moment, it is certain that Death may get you for his victim at any time. Whence will you get your rescue.

data.v: संचिन्वानकमेवैनं कामानामवितृप्तकम् । वृकीवोरणमासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति ॥
data.md: Like the she-wolf snatching away a lamb, Death snatches away one who is still engaged in acquiring wealth and still unsatisfied in the enjoyment of pleasures.

data.v: क्रमशः संचितशिखो धर्मबुद्धिमयो महान् । अन्धकारे प्रवेष्टव्ये दीपो यत्नेन धार्यताम् ॥
data.md: When you are destined to enter into the dark, do you hold up the blazing lamp or righteous understanding and whose flame has been sufficiently kept.

data.v: संपतन्देहजालानि कदाचिदिह मानुषे । ब्राह्मण्यं लभते जन्तुस्तत्पुत्र परिपालय ॥
data.md: Getting by various forms one after another in the world of men, a creature acquires the status of Brahmanhood with great difficulty. You have acquired that status. Do you then, O son, try to maintain it.

data.v: ब्राह्मणस्य हि देहोऽयं न कामार्थाय जायते । इह क्लेशाय तपसे प्रेत्य त्वनुपमं सुखम् ॥
data.md: A Brahmana has not been born for the gratification of senses. On the other hand, his body, for being subjected to mortification and penances in this world so that he may enjoy peerless happiness in the next world.

data.v: ब्राह्मण्यं बहुभिरवाप्यते तपोभि;स्तल्लब्ध्वा न परिपणेन हेडितव्यम् । स्वाध्याये तपसि दमे च नित्ययुक्तः; क्षेमार्थी कुशलपरः सदा यतस्व ॥
data.md: The status of Brahmanhood is acquired by long-continued and austere penances. Having gained that status one should never waste his time in the gratification of his senses. Always engaged in penances and self-control and desirous of what is for your well being, do you live and act, devoted to peace and tranquillity.

data.v: अव्यक्तप्रकृतिरयं कलाशरीरः; सूक्ष्मात्मा क्षणत्रुटिशो निमेषरोमा । ऋत्वास्यः समबलशुक्लकृष्णनेत्रो; मासाङ्गो द्रवति वयोहयो नराणाम् ॥
data.md: The life, of every man, is like a horse. The nature of that horse unmanifest. The elements from its body. Its nature is highly subtile. Kshanas, and Trutis, and Nimeshas are the hair on its body. The twilight's form its shoulderjoints. The lighted and the dark fortnights form its two equally powerful eyes. Months are its other limbs. That horse is running incessantly.

data.v: तं दृष्ट्वा प्रसृतमजस्रमुग्रवेगं; गच्छन्तं सततमिहाव्यपेक्षमाणम् । चक्षुस्ते यदि न परप्रणेतृनेयं; धर्मे ते भवतु मनः परं निशम्य ॥
data.md: If your eyes be not blind, seeing then that horse continually moving forward in its invisible course, do you set your heart on virtue, after hearing what your preceptors have 10 say about the next world.

data.v: येऽमी तु प्रचलितधर्मकामवृत्ताः; क्रोशन्तः सततमनिष्टसंप्रयोगाः । क्लिश्यन्ते परिगतवेदनाशरीरा; बह्वीभिः सुभृशमधर्मवासनाभिः ॥
data.md: They who deviate from virtue and who act carelessly, who always show malice towards others and take to evil ways, are obliged to take bodies in the regions of Yama and suffer various afflictions on account of their various sinful deeds.

data.v: राजा धर्मपरः सदा शुभगोप्ता; समीक्ष्य सुकृतिनां दधाति लोकान् । बहुविधमपि चरतः प्रदिशति; सुखमनुपगतं निरवद्यम् ॥
data.md: That king who is given to virtue and who protects and punishes the good and the wicked with discrimination, acquires the regions of the men of righteous deeds. By doing various good acts, he acquires such happiness as is faultless and as is incapable of being attained to by going through even thousands of births.

data.v: श्वानो भीषणायोमुखानि वयांसि; वडगृध्रकुलपक्षिणां च संघाः । नरां कदने रुधिरपा गुरुवचन;नुदमुपरतं विशसन्ति ॥
data.md: Dreadful dogs, crows or iron beaks, flocks of ravens and vultures and other birds, and blood-sucking worms, attacks the man who disobeys the commands of his parents and preceptors when he goes to hell after death.

data.v: मर्यादा नियताः स्वयंभुवा य इहेमाः; प्रभिनत्ति दशगुणा मनोनुगत्वात् । निवसति भृशमसुखं पितृविषय;विपिनमवगाह्य स पापः ॥
data.md: That sinful wretch who, on account of his carelessness, transgresses the ten boundaries that have been fixed by the Self-create himself, is obliged to pass his time in great inisery in the wild deserts situated in the dominions of Death.

data.v: यो लुब्धः सुभृशं प्रियानृतश्च मनुष्यः; सततनिकृतिवञ्चनारतिः स्यात् । उपनिधिभिरसुखकृत्स परमनिरयगो; भृशमसुखमनुभवति दुष्कृतकर्मा ॥
data.md: That man who is sullied with cupidity, who is fond of falsehood, who always takes pleasure in deception and cheating, and who does injuries to others by practising hypocrisy and deception, has to go to deep hell and suffer great misery and afflictions for his acts of iniquity.

data.v: उष्णां वैतरणीं महानदी;मवगाढोऽसिपत्रवनभिन्नगात्रः । परशुवनशयो निपतितो; वसति च महानिरये भृशार्तः ॥
data.md: Such a man is compelled to bathe in the broad river called Vaitarani whose waters are scalding, to enter into a forest of trees whose leaves are as sharp as swords, and then to lie down on a bed of axes. He has thus to pass his days in dreadful hell in great misery.

data.v: महापदानि कत्थसे न चाप्यवेक्षसे परम् । चिरस्य मृत्युकारिकामनागतां न बुध्यसे ॥
data.md: You see only the regions of Brahman and other gods, but you cannot see what is the highest. Alas, you are ever blind also to what brings Death on its train.

data.v: प्रयास्यतां किमास्यते समुत्थितं महद्भयम् । अतिप्रमाथि दारुणं सुखस्य संविधीयताम् ॥
data.md: Follow the path of Liberation. Why do you delay? A frightful terror, destructive of your happiness, is before you: Do you take prompt mcasures for acquiring Liberation.

data.v: पुरा मृतः प्रणीयसे यमस्य मृत्युशासनात् । तदन्तिकाय दारुणैः प्रयत्नमार्जवे कुरु ॥
data.md: Soon after death you are sure to be taken before Yama at his behest. For acquiring happiness in the next world, try to acquire virtue by the practice of difficult and austere vows.

data.v: पुरा समूलबान्धवं प्रभुर्हरत्यदुःखवित् । तवेह जीवितं यमो न चास्ति तस्य वारकः ॥
data.md: The powerful Yama does not care for the sufferings of others, very soon takes the lives of all persons, that is, of yourself and your friends. there is none capable of resisting him.

data.v: पुरा विवाति मारुतो यमस्य यः पुरःसरः । पुरैक एव नीयसे कुरुष्व सांपरायिकम् ॥
data.md: Very soon the wind of Yama will blow before you. Very soon will you be taken alone to that fearful presence. Do you then achieve what will be for your behoof there.

data.v: पुरा सहिक्क एव ते प्रवाति मारुतोऽन्तकः । पुरा च विभ्रमन्ति ते दिशो महाभयागमे ॥
data.md: Where now is that Death-wind which will blow before you very soon? Very soon will the points of the horizon, when that time arrives, begin to whirl before your eyes.

data.v: स्मृतिश्च संनिरुध्यते पुरा तवेह पुत्रक । समाकुलस्य गच्छतः समाधिमुत्तमं कुरु ॥
data.md: O son, soon will your Vedas disappear from you as you go helplessly into that dread presence. Do you, therefore, think of Yoga abstraction which is endued with great excellence.

data.v: कृताकृते शुभाशुभे प्रमादकर्मविप्लुते । स्मरन्पुरा न तप्यसे निधत्स्व केवलं निधिम् ॥
data.md: Do you try to attain that one only treasure so that you may not have to grieve at the recollection of your pristine deeds good and bad all of which are marked by mistake.

data.v: पुरा जरा कलेवरं विजर्जरीकरोति ते । बलाङ्गरूपहारिणी निधत्स्व केवलं निधिम् ॥
data.md: Decrepitude very soon weakens your body and robs you of your strength and limbs and beauty. Do you, therefore, seek that one only treasure.

data.v: पुरा शरीरमन्तको भिनत्ति रोगसायकैः । प्रसह्य जीवितक्षये तपो महत्समाचर ॥
data.md: Very soon the Destroyer, having Disease as his charioteer, will with a strong hand, for taking your life, pierce and break your body. Do you, therefore, practise austere penances.

data.v: पुरा वृका भयंकरा मनुष्यदेहगोचराः । अभिद्रवन्ति सर्वतो यतस्व पुण्यशीलने ॥
data.md: Very soon will those terrible wolves that live within your body, attack from all sides. Do you try, therefore, to achieve acts acts of righteousness.

data.v: पुरान्धकारमेककोऽनुपश्यसि त्वरस्व वै । पुरा हिरण्मयान्नगान्निरीक्षसेऽद्रिमूर्धनि ॥
data.md: Very soon will you, all alone, see a thick darkness, and very soon will you see golden trees on the top of the hill. Do you, therefore, hurry to achieve acts of righteousness.

data.v: पुरा कुसंगतानि ते सुहृन्मुखाश्च शत्रवः । विचालयन्ति दर्शनाद्घटस्व पुत्र यत्परम् ॥
data.md: Very soon will those evil companions and enemies of yours, (viz., the senses), dressed as friends swerve you from correct vision. Do you, then, O son, try to achieve that which is of the highest good.

data.v: धनस्य यस्य राजतो भयं न चास्ति चौरतः । मृतं च यन्न मुञ्चति समर्जयस्व तद्धनम् ॥
data.md: Do you acquire that wealth which has no fear from either kings or thieves, and which one has not to renounce even at Death.

data.v: न तत्र संविभज्यते स्वकर्मभिः परस्परम् । यदेव यस्य यौतकं तदेव तत्र सोऽश्नुते ॥
data.md: Acquired by one's own deeds, that wealth has never to be distributed among partners. Each enjoys that wealth which each has acquired for himself.

data.v: परत्र येन जीव्यते तदेव पुत्र दीयताम् । धनं यदक्षयं ध्रुवं समर्जयस्व तत्स्वयम् ॥
data.md: O son, give that to others by which they may be able to live in the next world. Do you also try to acquire that wealth which is indestructible and durable.

data.v: न यावदेव पच्यते महाजनस्य यावकम् । अपक्व एव यावके पुरा प्रणीयसे त्वर ॥
data.md: Do not think that you should first enjoy all sorts of pleasures and then try to acquire Liberation, for before; you are satiated with enjoyment you may meet with Death. Do you, in view of this, hasten to do acts of goodness.

data.v: न मातृपितृबान्धवा न संस्तुतः प्रियो जनः । अनुव्रजन्ति संकटे व्रजन्तमेकपातिनम् ॥
data.md: Neither mother, nor son, nor relatives, nor dear friends even when begged with honours, accompany the man that dies. One alone has to go to the regions of Yama.

data.v: यदेव कर्म केवलं स्वयं कृतं शुभाशुभम् । तदेव तस्य यौतकं भवत्यमुत्र गच्छतः ॥
data.md: Only those deeds, good and bad, that one did before death follow the man who goes to the other world.

data.v: हिरण्यरत्नसंचयाः शुभाशुभेन संचिताः । न तस्य देहसंक्षये भवन्ति कार्यसाधकाः ॥
data.md: The gold and gems that one has acquired by good and bad means do not do any good to man after death.

data.v: परत्रगामिकस्य ते कृताकृतस्य कर्मणः । न साक्षिरात्मना समो नृणामिहास्ति कश्चन ॥
data.md: There is no witness, of men who have gone to the next world, better than the soul, of all acts done and undone in life.

data.v: मनुष्यदेहशून्यकं भवत्यमुत्र गच्छतः । प्रपश्य बुद्धिचक्षुषा प्रदृश्यते हि सर्वतः ॥
data.md: The Yogins when they enter the sky of their hearts, see by Yoga intelligence that the destruction of body sets in when Individual Soul enters into the witness-Chaitanya.

data.v: इहाग्निसूर्यवायवः शरीरमाश्रितास्त्रयः । त एव तस्य साक्षिणो भवन्ति धर्मदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: Even here, the god of Fire, the Sun, and the Wind,-these three live in the body. These, seeing as they do all the practices of one's life, become his witnesses.

data.v: यथानिशेषु सर्वतःस्पृशत्सु सर्वदारिषु । प्रकाशगूढवृत्तिषु स्वधर्ममेव पालय ॥
data.md: Days and Nights,—the former marked by the virtue of showing all things and the latter marked by the virtue of conccaling all things.-are running continually and touching all things. Do you, therefore, satisfy the duties of your own order.

data.v: अनेकपारिपन्थिके विरूपरौद्ररक्षिते । स्वमेव कर्म रक्ष्यतां स्वकर्म तत्र गच्छति ॥
data.md: The road in the other world is full of many foes and of many repulsive and terrible insects and worms. Do you take care of your own acts, for only acts will accompany you along that road.

data.v: न तत्र संविभज्यते स्वकर्मणा परस्परम् । यथाकृतं स्वकर्मजं तदेव भुज्यते फलम् ॥
data.md: Acquired by one's own deeds, that wealth has never to be distributed among partners. Each enjoys that wealth which each has acquired for himself.

data.v: यथाप्सरोगणाः फलं सुखं महर्षिभिः सह । तथाप्नुवन्ति कर्मतो विमानकामगामिनः ॥
data.md: As Apsaras and great Rishis acquires fruits of great happiness, similarly men of righteous deeds, acquire in the other world cars of transcendent brightness that go everywhere at the will of the riders.

data.v: यथेह यत्कृतं शुभं विपाप्मभिः कृतात्मभिः । तदाप्नुवन्ति मानवास्तथा विशुद्धयोनयः ॥
data.md: Men of pure deeds and purified souls and pure birth acquire in the next world fruits commensurate with their own righteous deeds in this life.

data.v: प्रजापतेः सलोकतां बृहस्पतेः शतक्रतोः । व्रजन्ति ते परां गतिं गृहस्थधर्मसेतुभिः ॥
data.md: By walking along the high road formed by the duties of domesticity, men acquire happy ends by acquiring the region of Prajapati or Brihaspati or of him of a hundred sacrifices.

data.v: सहस्रशोऽप्यनेकशः प्रवक्तुमुत्सहामहे । अबुद्धिमोहनं पुनः प्रभुर्विना न यावकम् ॥
data.md: I can give you thousands and thousands of instructions. Know, however, that the powerful cleanser keeps all foolish persons in the Dark.

data.v: गता द्विरष्टवर्षता ध्रुवोऽसि पञ्चविंशकः । कुरुष्व धर्मसंचयं वयो हि तेऽतिवर्तते ॥
data.md: You have passed twenty-four years. You are now full twenty-five years of age. Your years are passing away. Begin now to husband virtue.

data.v: पुरा करोति सोऽन्तकः प्रमादगोमुखं दमम् । यथागृहीतमुत्थितं त्वरस्व धर्मपालने ॥
data.md: The Destroyer that lives within error and carelessness will very soon deprive your senses of their respective powers. Do you, before that takes place, hasten to discharge your duties, relying on your body alone.

data.v: यदा त्वमेव पृष्ठतस्त्वमग्रतो गमिष्यसि । तथा गतिं गमिष्यतः किमात्मना परेण वा ॥
data.md: When it is your duty to go along that road in which your self only shall be in front and yourself only in the rear, what need then have you with either your body or your wife and children?

data.v: यदेकपातिनां सतां भवत्यमुत्र गच्छताम् । भयेषु सांपरायिकं निधत्स्व तं महानिधिम् ॥
data.md: When men have to go alone and without companions to the region of Yama, it is clear that in view of such a situation of terror, you should try to acquire that one only treasure.

data.v: सकूलमूलबान्धवं प्रभुर्हरत्यसङ्गवान् । न सन्ति यस्य वारकाः कुरुष्व धर्मसंनिधिम् ॥
data.md: The powerful Yama, not caring for the sufferings of others, snatches away the friends and relatives of one's race by the very roots. There is no one who can resist him. Do you, therefore, seek to acquire virtue.

data.v: इदं निदर्शनं मया तवेह पुत्र संमतम् । स्वदर्शनानुमानतः प्रवर्णितं कुरुष्व तत् ॥
data.md: I impart to you these lessons, O son, that are all at one with the scriptures I follow. Do you, therefore, seek to acquire virtue.

data.v: दधाति यः स्वकर्मणा धनानि यस्य कस्यचित् । अबुद्धिमोहजैर्गुणैः शतैक एव युज्यते ॥
data.md: He who maintains his body by performing the duties laid down for his own order, and who makes gifts for acquiring whatever fruits may attach to such acts, becomes freed from the consequences begotten by ignorance and errror.

data.v: श्रुतं समर्थमस्तु ते प्रकुर्वतः शुभाः क्रियाः । तदेव तत्र दर्शनं कृतज्ञमर्थसंहितम् ॥
data.md: The knowledge which a man of pious deeds acquires from Vedic sayings leads to omniscience. That omniscience is at on with the science of the highest object of human acquisition. Instructions, given to the grateful, become beneficial.

data.v: निबन्धनी रज्जुरेषा या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः । छित्त्वैनां सुकृतो यान्ति नैनां छिन्दन्ति दुष्कृतः ॥
data.md: The desire that one feels for living in the midst of human dwellings is like a binding fetter. They that are of good deeds succeed in snapping that fetter and freeing themselves. Only men of wicked deeds do not succeed in breaking them.

data.v: किं ते धनेन किं बन्धुभिस्ते; किं ते पुत्रैः पुत्रक यो मरिष्यसि । आत्मानमन्विच्छ गुहां प्रविष्टं; पितामहास्ते क्व गताश्च सर्वे ॥
data.md: What use have you of riches, O son, or of relatives, or of children, since you have to die? Do you engage in seeking for your soul which is hidden in a cave. Where have all your grandfathers gone?

data.v: श्वःकार्यमद्य कुर्वीत पूर्वाह्णे चापराह्णिकम् । को हि तद्वेद कस्याद्य मृत्युसेना निवेक्ष्यते ॥
data.md: Do that today which you would keep for tomorrow. Do that in the forenoon which you would keep for the afternoon. Death does not wait for any one, to seen whether one has or has not done his task.

data.v: अनुगम्य श्मशानान्तं निवर्तन्तीह बान्धवाः । अग्नौ प्रक्षिप्य पुरुषं ज्ञातयः सुहृदस्तथा ॥
नास्तिकान्निरनुक्रोशान्नरान्पापमतौ स्थितान् । वामतः कुरु विश्रब्धं परं प्रेप्सुरतन्द्रितः ॥
data.md: Following the body after one's death, one's relatives and kinsmen and friends return placing it on the funeral pyre. Do you unhesitatingly shun those who are men sceptics, who are destitute of mercy, and who are given to wicked ways, and do you try to seek, without listlessness or apathy, that which is for your greatest good.

data.v: एवमभ्याहते लोके कालेनोपनिपीडिते । सुमहद्धैर्यमालम्ब्य धर्मं सर्वात्मना कुरु ॥
data.md: When, therefore, the world is thus assailed by Death, do you, with your whole heart, achieve virtue, helped all the while by unswerving patience.

data.v: अथेमं दर्शनोपायं सम्यग्यो वेत्ति मानवः । सम्यक्स धर्मं कृत्वेह परत्र सुखमेधते ॥
data.md: That man who is well conversant with the means of acquiring Liberation and who duly satisfies the duties of his order, certainly acquires great happiness in the next world.

data.v: न देहभेदे मरणं विजानतां; न च प्रणाशः स्वनुपालिते पथि । धर्मं हि यो वर्धयते स पण्डितो; य एव धर्माच्च्यवते स मुह्यति ॥
data.md: There is no destruction for you who do not recognise death in the attainment of a different body and who do not deviate from the path of the pious. He who increases the stock of virtue is truly wise. He, on the other hand, who deviates from virtue is said to be fool.

data.v: प्रयुक्तयोः कर्मपथि स्वकर्मणोः; फलं प्रयोक्ता लभते यथाविधि । निहीनकर्मा निरयं प्रपद्यते; त्रिविष्टपं गच्छति धर्मपारगः ॥
data.md: One who is engaged to the accomplishment of good deeds, attains to heaven and other rewards as the fruits of those acts; but he who is addicted to wicked deeds has to sink in hell.

data.v: सोपानभूतं स्वर्गस्य मानुष्यं प्राप्य दुर्लभम् । तथात्मानं समादध्याद्भ्रश्येत न पुनर्यथा ॥
data.md: Having acquired the status of humanity, so difficult of getting, that is the stepping stone to heaven, one should fix his soul on Brahma so that he may not fall away once more.

data.v: यस्य नोत्क्रामति मतिः स्वर्गमार्गानुसारिणी । तमाहुः पुण्यकर्माणमशोच्यं मित्रबान्धवैः ॥
data.md: That man whose understanding, directed to the path of heaven, does not deviate therefrom, is considered by the wise as truly a man of virtue and when he dies his friends should indulge in grief.

data.v: यस्य नोपहता बुद्धिर्निश्चयेष्ववलम्बते । स्वर्गे कृतावकाशस्य तस्य नास्ति महद्भयम् ॥
data.md: That man whose understanding is not firm and which is directed to Brahma and who has attained to heaven, becomes freed from a great fear.

data.v: तपोवनेषु ये जातास्तत्रैव निधनं गताः । तेषामल्पतरो धर्मः कामभोगमजानताम् ॥
data.md: That who are born in asylums of ascetics and who die there, do not acquire much mnerit by abstaining all their life from enjoyments and the indulgence of desire.

data.v: यस्तु भोगान्परित्यज्य शरीरेण तपश्चरेत् । न तेन किंचिन्न प्राप्तं तन्मे बहुमतं फलम् ॥
data.md: He, however, who though possessed of objects of enjoyment renounces them and practices penances, succeeds in acquiring everything. The fruits of the penances of such a inan are, I think, much greater.

data.v: मातापितृसहस्राणि पुत्रदारशतानि च । अनागतान्यतीतानि कस्य ते कस्य वा वयम् ॥
data.md: Ever one had and will have in this world mothers and fathers and sons and wives, by hundreds and thousands. Who, however, were they and whose are we?

data.v: न तेषां भवता कार्यं न कार्यं तव तैरपि । स्वकृतैस्तानि यातानि भवांश्चैव गमिष्यति ॥
data.md: They have nothing to do with you. You have nothing to do with them. All creatures take birth according to their pristine deeds. You also shall have to go hence determined by your own deeds.

data.v: इह लोके हि धनिनः परोऽपि स्वजनायते । स्वजनस्तु दरिद्राणां जीवतामेव नश्यति ॥
data.md: It is seen in this world that the friends and followers of persons in affluence behaved towards them with devotion. The friends and followers, however, of the poor fall away during even the life-time of the poor.

data.v: संचिनोत्यशुभं कर्म कलत्रापेक्षया नरः । ततः क्लेशमवाप्नोति परत्रेह तथैव च ॥
data.md: Man commits numerous evil deeds for the sake of his wife. From those evil deeds he suffers much distress both in this world and in the next.

data.v: पश्य त्वं छिद्रभूतं हि जीवलोकं स्वकर्मणा । तत्कुरुष्व तथा पुत्र कृत्स्नं यत्समुदाहृतम् ॥
data.md: The wise man sees the world of life devastated by the deed performed by every living being. Do you, therefore, O son, act according to all the instructions I have delivered to you.

data.v: तदेतत्संप्रदृश्यैव कर्मभूमिं प्रविश्य ताम् । शुभान्याचरितव्यानि परलोकमभीप्सता ॥
data.md: Seeing this world to be only a field of action, the man endued with true vision, should, from desire of happiness in the next world, do acts that are good.

data.v: मासर्तुसंज्ञापरिवर्तकेन; सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन । स्वकर्मनिष्ठाफलसाक्षिकेण; भूतानि कालः पचति प्रसह्य ॥
data.md: Exerting his irresistible power, Time cooks all creatures, with the help of his ladle formed by months and seasons, the sun for his fire, and days and nights for his fuel, they being the witnesses of the fruits of every act done by every creature.

data.v: धनेन किं यन्न ददाति नाश्नुते; बलेन किं येन रिपून्न बाधते । श्रुतेन किं येन न धर्ममाचरे;त्किमात्मना यो न जितेन्द्रियो वशी ॥
data.md: For what object is that wealth which is not given away and which is not enjoyed? For what purpose is that strength which is not used in resisting or subjugating one's enemies? For what purpose is that knowledge of the scriptures which does not move one to deeds of virtue? And for what purpose is that soul which does not control the senses and abstain from evil deeds?

data.v: इदं द्वैपायनवचो हितमुक्तं निशम्य तु । शुको गतः परित्यज्य पितरं मोक्षदेशिकम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said-Having heard these wholesome words spoken by the Island-born (Vyasa), "Shuka, leaving his father, proceeded to seek a preceptor who could teach him the religion of Liberation.

data.v: कथं व्यासस्य धर्मात्मा शुको जज्ञे महातपाः । सिद्धिं च परमां प्राप्तस्तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Tell me, O grandfather, how the great Shuka of austere penances took birth as the son of Vyasa, and how did he succeed in acquiring the highest success?

data.v: कस्यां चोत्पादयामास शुकं व्यासस्तपोधनः । न ह्यस्य जननीं विद्म जन्म चाग्र्यं महात्मनः ॥
data.md: Upon what woman did Vyasa, having asceticism for his wealth, beget that son of his? We do not know who was Shuka's mother, nor do we know anything of the birth of that great ascetic.

data.v: कथं च बालस्य सतः सूक्ष्मज्ञाने गता मतिः । यथा नान्यस्य लोकेऽस्मिन्द्वितीयस्येह कस्यचित् ॥
data.md: How was it that, when he was a mere boy, his mind became bent to the knowledge of the subtile? Indeed, in this world no second person can be seen in whom such marks could be seen at so early an age.

data.v: एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं विस्तरेण महाद्युते । न हि मे तृप्तिरस्तीह शृण्वतोऽमृतमुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: I wish to hear all this in full, you of great intelligence. I am never satiated with hearing your excellent and nectar-like words.

data.v: माहात्म्यमात्मयोगं च विज्ञानं च शुकस्य ह । यथावदानुपूर्व्येण तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Tell me, grandfather, in their due order, of the greatness, and the knowledge of Shuka and of his union with the (Supreme) Soul!

data.v: न हायनैर्न पलितैर्न वित्तेन न बन्धुभिः । ऋषयश्चक्रिरे धर्मं योऽनूचानः स नो महान् ॥
data.md: The Rishis did not make merit depend upon years of decrepitude or riches or friends. They said that he amongst them was great who studied the Vedas.

data.v: तपोमूलमिदं सर्वं यन्मां पृच्छसि पाण्डव । तदिन्द्रियाणि संयम्य तपो भवति नान्यथा ॥
data.md: All this that you have asked has penances for its root. That penance, again, O son of Pandu, originates from the subjugation of the senses.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणां प्रसङ्गेन दोषमृच्छत्यसंशयम् । संनियम्य तु तान्येव सिद्धिं प्राप्नोति मानवः ॥
data.md: Forsooth, one incurs fault by letting loose his senses. It is only by controlling them that one succeeds in acquiring success.

data.v: अश्वमेधसहस्रस्य वाजपेयशतस्य च । योगस्य कलया तात न तुल्यं विद्यते फलम् ॥
data.md: The merit of a thousand Horse-sacrifices or a hundred Vajapeyas is not equal to even a sixteenth part of the merit of Yoga.

data.v: अत्र ते वर्तयिष्यामि जन्मयोगफलं यथा । शुकस्याग्र्यां गतिं चैव दुर्विदामकृतात्मभिः ॥
data.md: I shall, now, recite to you the circumstances of Shuka's birth, the fruits he acquired of his penances, and the foremost end he achieved. These are the topics which persons of uncleansed souls cannot understand.

data.v: मेरुशृङ्गे किल पुरा कर्णिकारवनायुते । विजहार महादेवो भीमैर्भूतगणैर्वृतः ॥
data.md: Once on a time on the summit of Meru adorned with Karnikara flowers, Mahadeva sported, in company of his followers, the terrible spirits.

data.v: शैलराजसुता चैव देवी तत्राभवत्पुरा । तत्र दिव्यं तपस्तेपे कृष्णद्वैपायनः प्रभुः ॥
data.md: The daughter of the king of mountains, viz., the goddess Parvati, was also there. There near that summit, the Island-born (Vyasa) practised extraordinary austerities.

data.v: योगेनात्मानमाविश्य योगधर्मपरायणः । धारयन्स तपस्तेपे पुत्रार्थं कुरुसत्तम ॥
data.md: O best of the Kuru, given to the practices of Yoga, the great ascetic, withdrawing himself by Yoga into his own soul, and engaged in concentration, practised many austerities for the sake of a son.

data.v: अग्नेर्भूमेरपां वायोरन्तरिक्षस्य चाभिभो । वीर्येण संमितः पुत्रो मम भूयादिति स्म ह ॥
data.md: The prayer he offered to the great God was,-~O powerful one, let me have a son that will have the might of Fire and Earth and Weather and Wind and Ether.

data.v: संकल्पेनाथ सोऽनेन दुष्प्रापेणाकृतात्मभिः । वरयामास देवेशमास्थितस्तप उत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Engaged in the austerest of penances the Island-born Rishi begged of that great God, who cannot be approached by persons of impure souls, by his Yoga.

data.v: अतिष्ठन्मारुताहारः शतं किल समाः प्रभुः । आराधयन्महादेवं बहुरूपमुमापतिम् ॥
data.md: The powerful Vyasa remained there for a hundred years, living on air alone, engaged in worshipping many formed Mahadeva, the lord ofUma.

data.v: तत्र ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव सर्वे देवर्षयस्तथा । लोकपालाश्च लोकेशं साध्याश्च वसुभिः सह ॥
आदित्याश्चैव रुद्राश्च दिवाकरनिशाकरौ । मरुतो मारुतश्चैव सागराः सरितस्तथा ॥
अश्विनौ देवगन्धर्वास्तथा नारदपर्वतौ । विश्वावसुश्च गन्धर्वः सिद्धाश्चाप्सरसां गणाः ॥
तत्र रुद्रो महादेवः कर्णिकारमयीं शुभाम् । धारयाणः स्रजं भाति ज्योत्स्नामिव निशाकरः ॥
data.md: There Mahadeva, called also Rudra, sat, adorned with an excellent garland of Karnikara flowers, and effulgent like the Moon with his rays.

data.v: तस्मिन्दिव्ये वने रम्ये देवदेवर्षिसंकुले । आस्थितः परमं योगमृषिः पुत्रार्थमुद्यतः ॥
data.md: In those delightful and celestial forests populous with gods and heavenly Rishis, the great Rishi remained, engaged in high Yogacontemplation, for getting a son.

data.v: न चास्य हीयते वर्णो न ग्लानिरुपजायते । त्रयाणामपि लोकानां तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥
data.md: His strength suffered no decrease, nor did he feel any pain. There at the three worlds were much surprised.

data.v: जटाश्च तेजसा तस्य वैश्वानरशिखोपमाः । प्रज्वलन्त्यः स्म दृश्यन्ते युक्तस्यामिततेजसः ॥
data.md: While the Rishi, gifted with immeasurable energy, sat in Yoga, his mattered locks, on account of his energy, were seen to blaze like flames of fire.

data.v: मार्कण्डेयो हि भगवानेतदाख्यातवान्मम । स देवचरितानीह कथयामास मे सदा ॥
data.md: I heard to this from the illustrious Markandeya. He used always to recite to me the acts of the gods.

data.v: ता एताद्यापि कृष्णस्य तपसा तेन दीपिताः । अग्निवर्णा जटास्तात प्रकाशन्ते महात्मनः ॥
data.md: It is for this that the matted locks of the great Vyasa, thus enblazed by his energy on that occasion, seem to this day to be gifted with the hue of fire.

data.v: एवंविधेन तपसा तस्य भक्त्या च भारत । महेश्वरः प्रसन्नात्मा चकार मनसा मतिम् ॥
data.md: Pleased with such penances and such devotion, O Bharata, of the Rishi, the great God resolved to grant him his wish.

data.v: उवाच चैनं भगवांस्त्र्यम्बकः प्रहसन्निव । एवंविधस्ते तनयो द्वैपायन भविष्यति ॥
data.md: Smiling with pleasure, the three-eyed god addressed him and said,-O Island-born one, you will have a son after your heart.

data.v: यथा ह्यग्निर्यथा वायुर्यथा भूमिर्यथा जलम् । यथा च खं तथा शुद्धो भविष्यति सुतो महान् ॥
data.md: Endued with greatness, he shall be as pure as Fire, as Wind, as Earth, as Water, and as Space.

data.v: तद्भावभावी तद्बुद्धिस्तदात्मा तदपाश्रयः । तेजसावृत्य लोकांस्त्रीन्यशः प्राप्स्यति केवलम् ॥
data.md: He will be conscious of his being Brahma's self ; his understanding and soul shall be devoted to Brahma, and he shall completely depend upon Brahma so as to be at one with.

data.v: स लब्ध्वा परमं देवाद्वरं सत्यवतीसुतः । अरणीं त्वथ संगृह्य ममन्थाग्निचिकीर्षया ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Having got this high boon from the great God, the son of Satyavati, was one day engaged in rubbing his sticks for making a fire.
