data.v: अथ रूपं परं राजन्बिभ्रतीं स्वेन तेजसा । घृताचीं नामाप्सरसमपश्यद्भगवानृषिः ॥
data.md: While thus engaged, the illustrious Rishi, O king, saw the . Apsara Ghritachi, who, on account of her energy, was then possessed of great beauty.

data.v: ऋषिरप्सरसं दृष्ट्वा सहसा काममोहितः । अभवद्भगवान्व्यासो वने तस्मिन्युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Seeing the Apasara in those woods, the illustrious Rishi Vyasa, O Yudhisthira, became suddenly possessed by desire.

data.v: सा च कृत्वा तदा व्यासं कामसंविग्नमानसम् । शुकी भूत्वा महाराज घृताची समुपागमत् ॥
data.md: The Apsara, seeing the Rishi's heart smitten with desire, changed herself into a she-parrot and came to that spot.

data.v: स तामप्सरसं दृष्ट्वा रूपेणान्येन संवृताम् । शरीरजेनानुगतः सर्वगात्रातिगेन ह ॥
data.md: Although he saw the Apsara disguised in another form, the desire that had arisen in the Rishi's heart spread itself over every part of his body.

data.v: स तु धैर्येण महता निगृह्णन्हृच्छयं मुनिः । न शशाक नियन्तुं तद्व्यासः प्रविसृतं मनः । भावित्वाच्चैव भावस्य घृताच्या वपुषा हृतः ॥
data.md: Inviting all his patience, the ascetic tried to suppress that desire. With all his efforts, however, Vyasa could not control his agitated mind. On account of the inevitability of what was to take place the Rishi's heart was drawn by Ghritachi's beauty.

data.v: यत्नान्नियच्छतस्तस्य मुनेरग्निचिकीर्षया । अरण्यामेव सहसा तस्य शुक्रमवापतत् ॥
data.md: He tried his best for making a fire for suppressing his emotion, but despite all his efforts his vital seed came out in the wood.

data.v: सोऽविशङ्केन मनसा तथैव द्विजसत्तमः । अरणीं ममन्थ ब्रह्मर्षिस्तस्यां जज्ञे शुको नृप ॥
data.md: That best of twice-born ones, however O king, continued to rub his stick without feeling any scruples for what had taken place. From the seed that feil, was born a son to him called Shuka.

data.v: शुक्रे निर्मथ्यमाने तु शुको जज्ञे महातपाः । परमर्षिर्महायोगी अरणीगर्भसंभवः ॥
data.md: On account of this incident about his birth, he came to be called by the name of Shuka. : Indeed, it was thus that great ascetic, that foremost of Rishis and highest of Yogins, was born from the two sticks.

data.v: यथाध्वरे समिद्धोऽग्निर्भाति हव्यमुपात्तवान् । तथारूपः शुको जज्ञे प्रज्वलन्निव तेजसा ॥
data.md: As in a sacrifice a blazing fire spreads its effulgence all around when libations of clarified butter are poured upon it, similarly did Shuka take his birth, blazing with effulgence on account of his own energy.

data.v: बिभ्रत्पितुश्च कौरव्य रूपवर्णमनुत्तमम् । बभौ तदा भावितात्मा विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन् ॥
data.md: Assuming the excellent form and hue of his father, Shuka, O son of Kuru, of purified Soul, shone like a smokeless fire.

data.v: तं गङ्गा सरितां श्रेष्ठा मेरुपृष्ठे जनेश्वर । स्वरूपिणी तदाभ्येत्य स्नापयामास वारिणा ॥
data.md: O king, coming to the breast of Meru, in her own embodied form, the foremost of rivers, viz., Ganga, bathed Shuka with her waters.

data.v: अन्तरिक्षाच्च कौरव्य दण्डः कृष्णाजिनं च ह । पपात भुवि राजेन्द्र शुकस्यार्थे महात्मनः ॥
data.md: There fell from the sky, O son of Kuru, an ascetic's stick and a dark deer skin for the use, O king, of the great Shuka.

data.v: जेगीयन्ते स्म गन्धर्वा ननृतुश्चाप्सरोगणाः । देवदुन्दुभयश्चैव प्रावाद्यन्त महास्वनाः ॥
data.md: The Gandharvas sang repeatedly and the various clans of Apsaras danced; and celestial kettle drums of loud sound began to bcat.

data.v: विश्वावसुश्च गन्धर्वस्तथा तुम्बुरुनारदौ । हाहाहूहू च गन्धर्वौ तुष्टुवुः शुकसंभवम् ॥
data.md: The Gandharvas Vishvavasu, and Tumvuru, and Narada, and those other Gandharvas called by the name of Haha, and Huhu, eulogised the birth of Shuka.

data.v: तत्र शक्रपुरोगाश्च लोकपालाः समागताः । देवा देवर्षयश्चैव तथा ब्रह्मर्षयोऽपि च ॥
data.md: There the regents of the world headed by Indra, as also the gods and the celestial and the regenerate Rishis.

data.v: दिव्यानि सर्वपुष्पाणि प्रववर्षात्र मारुतः । जङ्गमं स्थावरं चैव प्रहृष्टमभवज्जगत् ॥
data.md: The Wind-god poured there showers of celestial flowers. The entire universe, mobile and immobile, became filled with joy.

data.v: तं महात्मा स्वयं प्रीत्या देव्या सह महाद्युतिः । जातमात्रं मुनेः पुत्रं विधिनोपानयत्तदा ॥
data.md: The great and the highly effulgent Mahadeva, accompanied by the Goddess, and moved by affection, came there and soon after the birth of the Muni's son invested him with the sacred thread.

data.v: तस्य देवेश्वरः शक्रो दिव्यमद्भुतदर्शनम् । ददौ कमण्डलुं प्रीत्या देववासांसि चाभिभो ॥
data.md: Shakra, the king of the gods, gave him, from affection, a celestial pitcher of excellent form, and some celestial dresses.

data.v: हंसाश्च शतपत्राश्च सारसाश्च सहस्रशः । प्रदक्षिणमवर्तन्त शुकाश्चाषाश्च भारत ॥
data.md: Thousands of Swans and Shatapatras and cranes, and many parrots and Chasas, O Bharata, wheeled over his head.

data.v: आरणेयस्तथा दिव्यं प्राप्य जन्म महाद्युतिः । तत्रैवोवास मेधावी व्रतचारी समाहितः ॥
data.md: Highly effulgent and intelligent Shuka, having obtained his birth from the two sticks, continued to live there, practising many vows and fasts.

data.v: उत्पन्नमात्रं तं वेदाः सरहस्याः ससंग्रहाः । उपतस्थुर्महाराज यथास्य पितरं तथा ॥
data.md: As soon as Shuka was born, the Vedas, with all their mysteries and all their abstracts, came for living in him, O king, even as they live in his father.

data.v: बृहस्पतिं तु वव्रे स वेदवेदाङ्गभाष्यवित् । उपाध्यायं महाराज धर्ममेवानुचिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: For all that, Shuka, selected Brihaspati, who was a master of all the Vedas together with their branches and commentaries, for his preceptor, remembering universal practice.

data.v: सोऽधीत्य वेदानखिलान्सरहस्यान्ससंग्रहान् । इतिहासं च कार्त्स्न्येन राजशास्त्राणि चाभिभो ॥
गुरवे दक्षिणां दत्त्वा समावृत्तो महामुनिः । उग्रं तपः समारेभे ब्रह्मचारी समाहितः ॥
देवतानामृषीणां च बाल्येऽपि स महातपाः । संमन्त्रणीयो मान्यश्च ज्ञानेन तपसा तथा ॥
data.md: Even in his childhood, he became an object of reverence with the gods and Rishis for his knowledge and penances.

data.v: न त्वस्य रमते बुद्धिराश्रमेषु नराधिप । त्रिषु गार्हस्थ्यमूलेषु मोक्षधर्मानुदर्शिनः ॥
data.md: The mind of the great ascetic, O king, found pleasure in the three modes of life, keeping in view, as he did, the Religion of Liberation.

data.v: स मोक्षमनुचिन्त्यैव शुकः पितरमभ्यगात् । प्राहाभिवाद्य च गुरुं श्रेयोर्थी विनयान्वितः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said “Thinking of Liberation, Shuka approached his father, and possessed as he was of humility and desirous of acquiring his highest good, he saluted his great preceptor and said,-You are well-versed in the Religion of Liberation. Do you, O illustrious one, describe it to me, so that I may enjoy supreme tranquillity of mind, O powerful one.

data.v: मोक्षधर्मेषु कुशलो भगवान्प्रब्रवीतु मे । यथा मे मनसः शान्तिः परमा संभवेत्प्रभो ॥
श्रुत्वा पुत्रस्य वचनं परमर्षिरुवाच तम् । अधीष्व पुत्र मोक्षं वै धर्मांश्च विविधानपि ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of his son, the great Rishi said to him,-Do you study, O son, the Religion' of Liberation and all the various duties of life.

data.v: पितुर्नियोगाज्जग्राह शुको ब्रह्मविदां वरः । योगशास्त्रं च निखिलं कापिलं चैव भारत ॥
data.md: At the command of his father, Shuka, that foremost of all righteous men, mastered all the books on Yoga, O Bharata, as also the Science of Kapila.

data.v: स तं ब्राह्म्या श्रिया युक्तं ब्रह्मतुल्यपराक्रमम् । मेने पुत्रं यदा व्यासो मोक्षविद्याविशारदम् ॥
data.md: When Vyasa saw his son to be endued with the resplendence of the Vedas, and the energy of Brahman, and fully conversant with the Religion of Liberation, he addressed him, saying,-Go you to Janaka the king of Mithila. The king of Mithila will tell you everything for your Liberation.

data.v: उवाच गच्छेति तदा जनकं मिथिलेश्वरम् । स ते वक्ष्यति मोक्षार्थं निखिलेन विशेषतः ॥
पितुर्नियोगादगमन्मैथिलं जनकं नृपम् । प्रष्टुं धर्मस्य निष्ठां वै मोक्षस्य च परायणम् ॥
data.md: Bearing the command of his father, O king, Shuka, proceeded to Mithila for enquiring of its king about the truth of duties and the Refuge of Liberation.

data.v: उक्तश्च मानुषेण त्वं पथा गच्छेत्यविस्मितः । न प्रभावेण गन्तव्यमन्तरिक्षचरेण वै ॥
data.md: Before he started, his father further told him,-Do you go there be that path which ordinary human beings follow. Do not have recourses to your Yoga-power for proceeding through the skies. At this Shuka was not at all surprised.

data.v: आर्जवेणैव गन्तव्यं न सुखान्वेषिणा पथा । नान्वेष्टव्या विशेषास्तु विशेषा हि प्रसङ्गिनः ॥
data.md: He was further told that he should proceed there with simplicity and not from desire of pleasure.-Along your way do not seek for friends and wives, since friends and wives are causes of attachment to the world.

data.v: अहंकारो न कर्तव्यो याज्ये तस्मिन्नराधिपे । स्थातव्यं च वशे तस्य स ते छेत्स्यति संशयम् ॥
data.md: Although the king of Mithila is one in whose sacrifices we officiate, still you should not indulge in any feeling of superiority while living with him. You should live under his direction and in obedience to him. He will remove your doubts.

data.v: स धर्मकुशलो राजा मोक्षशास्त्रविशारदः । याज्यो मम स यद्ब्रूयात्तत्कार्यमविशङ्कया ॥
data.md: That king is well versed in all duties and well acquainted with the Scriptures on Liberation. He is one for whom I officiate in sacrifices. You should, unhesitatingly, do what he orders.

data.v: एवमुक्तः स धर्मात्मा जगाम मिथिलां मुनिः । पद्भ्यां शक्तोऽन्तरिक्षेण क्रान्तुं भूमिं ससागराम् ॥
data.md: Thus instructed, the pious Shuka proceeded to Mithila on foot although he was able to go through the skies over the whole Earth with her seas.

data.v: स गिरींश्चाप्यतिक्रम्य नदीस्तीर्त्वा सरांसि च । बहुव्यालमृगाकीर्णा विविधाश्चाटवीस्तथा ॥
मेरोर्हरेश्च द्वे वर्षे वर्षं हैमवतं तथा । क्रमेणैव व्यतिक्रम्य भारतं वर्षमासदत् ॥
data.md: Crossing many hills and mountains, many rivers, many waters and lakes, and many woods and forests full of beasts of prey and other animals, crossing the two insular continents of Meru and Hari successively and next the continent of Himavat, he came at last to the continent known by the name of Bharata.

data.v: स देशान्विविधान्पश्यंश्चीनहूणनिषेवितान् । आर्यावर्तमिमं देशमाजगाम महामुनिः ॥
data.md: Having seen many countries inhabited by Chins and Huns, the great ascetic at last reached Aryavarta.

data.v: पितुर्वचनमाज्ञाय तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन् । अध्वानं सोऽतिचक्राम खेऽचरः खे चरन्निव ॥
data.md: In obedience to the commands of his father and bearing them constantly in his mind, he gradually passed along his way on the Earth like a bird passing through the air.

data.v: पत्तनानि च रम्याणि स्फीतानि नगराणि च । रत्नानि च विचित्राणि शुकः पश्यन्न पश्यति ॥
data.md: Passing through many charming towns and populous cities, he saw various kinds of wealth without waiting to observe them.

data.v: उद्यानानि च रम्याणि तथैवायतनानि च । पुण्यानि चैव तीर्थानि सोऽतिक्रम्य तथाध्वनः ॥
data.md: On his way he passed through many charming gardens and planes and many sacred waters.

data.v: सोऽचिरेणैव कालेन विदेहानाससाद ह । रक्षितान्धर्मराजेन जनकेन महात्मना ॥
data.md: Before much time had passed he reached the country of the Videhas that was protected by the virtuous and great Janaka.

data.v: तत्र ग्रामान्बहून्पश्यन्बह्वन्नरसभोजनान् । पल्लीघोषान्समृद्धांश्च बहुगोकुलसंकुलान् ॥
data.md: There he saw many populous villages, and many kinds of food and drink and viands and houses of cowherds swelling with men and inany herbs of cattle.

data.v: स्फीतांश्च शालियवसैर्हंससारससेवितान् । पद्मिनीभिश्च शतशः श्रीमतीभिरलंकृतान् ॥
data.md: He saw many fields abounding with paddy and barley and other grain, and many lakes and waters inhabited by swans and cranes and adorned with beautiful lotuses.

data.v: स विदेहानतिक्रम्य समृद्धजनसेवितान् । मिथिलोपवनं रम्यमाससाद महर्द्धिमत् ॥
data.md: Passing through the Videha country full of rich people, he arrived at the delightful gardens of Mithila rich with many sorts to trees.

data.v: हस्त्यश्वरथसंकीर्णं नरनारीसमाकुलम् । पश्यन्नपश्यन्निव तत्समतिक्रामदच्युतः ॥
data.md: Abounding with elephants and horses and cars, and peopled by men and women, he passed through them without caring to see the things that were presented to his eye.

data.v: मनसा तं वहन्भारं तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन् । आत्मारामः प्रसन्नात्मा मिथिलामाससाद ह ॥
data.md: Bearing that caution in his mind and continually thinking of it, Shuka of cheerful soul and taking delight in internal survey only, reached Mithila at last.

data.v: तस्या द्वारं समासाद्य द्वारपालैर्निवारितः । स्थितो ध्यानपरो मुक्तो विदितः प्रविवेश ह ॥
स राजमार्गमासाद्य समृद्धजनसंकुलम् । पार्थिवक्षयमासाद्य निःशङ्कः प्रविवेश ह ॥
तत्रापि द्वारपालास्तमुग्रवाचो न्यषेधयन् । तथैव च शुकस्तत्र निर्मन्युः समतिष्ठत ॥
न चातपाध्वसंतप्तः क्षुत्पिपासाश्रमान्वितः । प्रताम्यति ग्लायति वा नापैति च तथातपात् ॥
data.md: Thereat, Shuka, without any anger, stopped and waited. Neither the sun nor the long distance he had walked had tried him in the least. Neither hunger, nor thirst, nor the exertion he had made, had weakened him. The heat of the Sun had not scorched or pained or distressed him in any way.

data.v: तेषां तु द्वारपालानामेकः शोकसमन्वितः । मध्यंगतमिवादित्यं दृष्ट्वा शुकमवस्थितम् ॥
data.md: Among those porters there was one who felt mercy for him, seeing him staying there like the midday Sun in his effulgence.

data.v: पूजयित्वा यथान्यायमभिवाद्य कृताञ्जलिः । प्रावेशयत्ततः कक्ष्यां द्वितीयां राजवेश्मनः ॥
data.md: Adoring him in due form and saluting him properly, with joined hands he conducted him to the first chamber of the palace.

data.v: तत्रासीनः शुकस्तात मोक्षमेवानुचिन्तयन् । छायायामातपे चैव समदर्शी महाद्युतिः ॥
data.md: Seated there, Shuka, O son, began to think of Liberation only. Gifted with equality he considered impartially a shaded spot and one exposed to the Sun's rays.

data.v: तं मुहूर्तादिवागम्य राज्ञो मन्त्री कृताञ्जलिः । प्रावेशयत्ततः कक्ष्यां तृतीयां राजवेश्मनः ॥
data.md: Adoring him in due form and saluting him properly, with joined hands he conducted him to the first chamber of the palace.

data.v: तत्रान्तःपुरसंबद्धं महच्चैत्ररथोपमम् । सुविभक्तजलाक्रीडं रम्यं पुष्पितपादपम् ॥
data.md: That chamber led to a spacious garden which formed a part of the inner apartments of the palace. It looked like a second Chaitraratha. Beautiful pools of water were here and there at regular intervals. Delightful trees, all of which were in their flowering season, were in that garden.

data.v: तद्दर्शयित्वा स शुकं मन्त्री काननमुत्तमम् । अर्हमासनमादिश्य निश्चक्राम ततः पुनः ॥
data.md: Bevies of damsels, of celestial beauty, were in attendance. The minister led Suka from the second chamber to that charming spot. commanding those ladies to give the ascetic a seat, the minister left him there.

data.v: तं चारुवेषाः सुश्रोण्यस्तरुण्यः प्रियदर्शनाः । सूक्ष्मरक्ताम्बरधरास्तप्तकाञ्चनभूषणाः ॥
data.md: Those well-dressed well-dressed damels were of beautiful features, possessed to excellent hips, young in years, clad in red dresses of fine texture, and decked with many ornaments of burnished gold.

data.v: संलापोल्लापकुशला नृत्तगीतविशारदाः । स्मितपूर्वाभिभाषिण्यो रूपेणाप्सरसां समाः ॥
data.md: They well-skilled in sweet conversation and maddening revelry, and consummate mistresses of the arts of dancing and singing. Always opening their lips with smiles, they were like the very Apsaras in beauty.

data.v: कामोपचारकुशला भावज्ञाः सर्वकोविदाः । परं पञ्चाशतो नार्यो वारमुख्याः समाद्रवन् ॥
data.md: Well-skilled in all the acts of dalliance, capable of reading the thoughts of men upon whom they wait, endued with every accomplishment, fifty damsels, of a very high order and of east virtue, surrounded the ascetic.

data.v: पाद्यादीनि प्रतिग्राह्य पूजया परयार्च्य च । देशकालोपपन्नेन साध्वन्नेनाप्यतर्पयन् ॥
data.md: Presenting him with water for washing his feet, and adoring him respectfully with the were offer of usual articles, they pleased him with excellent viands agreeable to the season.

data.v: तस्य भुक्तवतस्तात तदन्तःपुरकाननम् । सुरम्यं दर्शयामासुरेकैकश्येन भारत ॥
data.md: After he had eaten, those damsels then, one after another, singly conducted him through the grounds, showing him every objection of interest, O Bharata.

data.v: क्रीडन्त्यश्च हसन्त्यश्च गायन्त्यश्चैव ताः शुकम् । उदारसत्त्वं सत्त्वज्ञाः सर्वाः पर्यचरंस्तदा ॥
data.md: Sporting and laughing and singing, those ladies conversant with the thoughts of all men, entertained that ascetic of noble soul.

data.v: आरणेयस्तु शुद्धात्मा त्रिसंदेहस्त्रिकर्मकृत् । वश्येन्द्रियो जितक्रोधो न हृष्यति न कुप्यति ॥
data.md: The pure-souled ascetic born in the firesticks, performing all his duties unhesitatingly, having all his senses under complete control, and a thorough master of his anger, was neither pleased nor angered at all this.

data.v: तस्मै शय्यासनं दिव्यं वरार्हं रत्नभूषितम् । स्पर्ध्यास्तरणसंस्तीर्णं ददुस्ताः परमस्त्रियः ॥
पादशौचं तु कृत्वैव शुकः संध्यामुपास्य च । निषसादासने पुण्ये तमेवार्थं विचिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: Then those foremost of beautiful women offered him an excellent seat. Washing his feet and other limbs, Shuka said his evening prayers, sat on that excellent seat, and began to think of the object for which he had come there.

data.v: पूर्वरात्रे तु तत्रासौ भूत्वा ध्यानपरायणः । मध्यरात्रे यथान्यायं निद्रामाहारयत्प्रभुः ॥
data.md: In the first part of the night, he gave himself of Yoga. The powerful ascetic, passed the middle part of the night in sleep.

data.v: ततो मुहूर्तादुत्थाय कृत्वा शौचमनन्तरम् । स्त्रीभिः परिवृतो धीमान्ध्यानमेवान्वपद्यत ॥
data.md: Very soon waking up from his sleep, he performed the necessary rites of cleansing his body, and though surrounded by those beautiful ladies, he once again devoted himself to Yoga.

data.v: अनेन विधिना कार्ष्णिस्तदहःशेषमच्युतः । तां च रात्रिं नृपकुले वर्तयामास भारत ॥
data.md: It was in this way, O Bharata, that the son of the Island-born Krishna passed the latter part of that day and the whole of that night in the mansion of king Janaka.

data.v: ततः स राजा जनको मन्त्रिभिः सह भारत । पुरः पुरोहितं कृत्वा सर्वाण्यन्तःपुराणि च ॥
data.md: Bhishma said The next morning, king Janaka, O Bharata, accompanied by his minister and the whole household, came to Shuka, preceded by his priest.

data.v: आसनं च पुरस्कृत्य रत्नानि विविधानि च । शिरसा चार्घ्यमादाय गुरुपुत्रं समभ्यगात् ॥
data.md: Bringing with him rich seats and various sorts of jewels and gems, and bearing the ingredients of the Arghya on his own head, the king approached the son of his reverend preceptor.

data.v: स तदासनमादाय बहुरत्नविभूषितम् । स्पर्ध्यास्तरणसंस्तीर्णं सर्वतोभद्रमृद्धिमत् ॥
data.md: The king, taking with his own hands, from the hands of his priest, that seat adorned with many gems, covered with an excellent sheet, beautiful in all its parts and dearly costly, presented it with great respect to his preceptor's son Shuka.

data.v: पुरोधसा संगृहीतं हस्तेनालभ्य पार्थिवः । प्रददौ गुरुपुत्राय शुकाय परमार्चितम् ॥
data.md: The king, taking with his own hands, from the hands of his priest, that seat adorned with many gems, covered with an excellent sheet, beautiful in all its parts and dearly costly, presented it with great respect to his preceptor's son Shuka.

data.v: तत्रोपविष्टं तं कार्ष्णिं शास्त्रतः प्रत्यपूजयत् । पाद्यं निवेद्य प्रथममर्घ्यं गां च न्यवेदयत् । स च तां मन्त्रवत्पूजां प्रत्यगृह्णाद्यथाविधि ॥
data.md: After the son of Krishna had taken his seat on it, the king adored him according to prescribed rites. At first offering him water to wash his feet, he then presented him the Arghya and kine.

data.v: प्रतिगृह्य च तां पूजां जनकाद्द्विजसत्तमः । गां चैव समनुज्ञाय राजानमनुमान्य च ॥
पर्यपृच्छन्महातेजा राज्ञः कुशलमव्ययम् । अनामयं च राजेन्द्र शुकः सानुचरस्य ह ॥
अनुज्ञातः स तेनाथ निषसाद सहानुगः । उदारसत्त्वाभिजनो भूमौ राजा कृताञ्जलिः ॥
कुशलं चाव्ययं चैव पृष्ट्वा वैयासकिं नृपः । किमागमनमित्येव पर्यपृच्छत पार्थिवः ॥
data.md: Having a high soul and possessed of high birth, the king with joined hands, sat down on the bare ground and enquired after the wellbeing and unabated prosperity of Vyasa's son. The king then asked his guest the object of his visit.

data.v: पित्राहमुक्तो भद्रं ते मोक्षधर्मार्थकोविदः । विदेहराजो याज्यो मे जनको नाम विश्रुतः ॥
data.md: Shuka said Blessed be you, my father told me that his client, the king of the Videhas, known all over the world by the name of Janaka, is well-versed in the Religion of Liberation.

data.v: तत्र गच्छस्व वै तूर्णं यदि ते हृदि संशयः । प्रवृत्तौ वा निवृत्तौ वा स ते छेत्स्यति संशयम् ॥
data.md: He ordered me to come to him forthwith, if I had any doubts to be solved in the Religion of either Action or Renunciation. He gave me to understand that the king of Mithila would remove all my doubts.

data.v: सोऽहं पितुर्नियोगात्त्वामुपप्रष्टुमिहागतः । तन्मे धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ यथावद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: I have, therefore, come come here at the command of my father, for the purpose of receiving instruction from you. You should, O foremost of all righteous persons, instruct me!

data.v: किं कार्यं ब्राह्मणेनेह मोक्षार्थश्च किमात्मकः । कथं च मोक्षः कर्तव्यो ज्ञानेन तपसापि वा ॥
data.md: What are the duties of a Brahmana, and what is the essence of those duties that have Liberation for their object. How, also, is Liberation to be acquired. Is it to be acquired by the help of Knowledge or by that Penances?

data.v: यत्कार्यं ब्राह्मणेनेह जन्मप्रभृति तच्छृणु । कृतोपनयनस्तात भवेद्वेदपरायणः ॥
data.md: Janaka said Hear what the Duties are of a Brahmana from the time of his birth. After his investiture, O son, with the sacred thread, he should give his attention to the study of the Vedas.

data.v: तपसा गुरुवृत्त्या च ब्रह्मचर्येण चाभिभो । देवतानां पितॄणां चाप्यनृणश्चानसूयकः ॥
data.md: By practising penances and dutifully serving his preceptor, and observing the duties of Brahmacharya, O powerful one, he should satisfy the debt be owes to the gods, and the Pitris, and renounce all malice.

data.v: वेदानधीत्य नियतो दक्षिणामपवर्ज्य च । अभ्यनुज्ञामथ प्राप्य समावर्तेत वै द्विजः ॥
data.md: Having read the Vedas with close attention, and controlled his senses, and having given his preceptor the tuition-fee, he should, with the order of his preceptor, return home.

data.v: समावृत्तस्तु गार्हस्थ्ये सदारो नियतो वसेत् । अनसूयुर्यथान्यायमाहिताग्निस्तथैव च ॥
data.md: Coming back home, he should follow the domestic mode of life and marry a wife, confine himself to her, and live freeing himself from every sort of malice, and having established his domestic fire.

data.v: उत्पाद्य पुत्रपौत्रं तु वन्याश्रमपदे वसेत् । तानेवाग्नीन्यथाशास्त्रमर्चयन्नतिथिप्रियः ॥
data.md: Living as a householder, he should procreate sons and grandsons. After that, he should retire to the forest, and continue to adore the same fires and entertain guests with cordial hospitality.

data.v: स वनेऽग्नीन्यथान्यायमात्मन्यारोप्य धर्मवित् । निर्द्वंद्वो वीतरागात्मा ब्रह्माश्रमपदे वसेत् ॥
data.md: Living virtuously in the forest, he should, at last, establish his fire in his soul, and freed from all pairs of opposites, and renouncing all attachments, he should pass his days in the anchorite-mode of life, which is otherwise called the mode of Brahma.

data.v: उत्पन्ने ज्ञानविज्ञाने प्रत्यक्षे हृदि शाश्वते । किमवश्यं निवस्तव्यमाश्रमेषु वनेषु च ॥
data.md: Shuka said If one acquires an understanding cleansed by study of the scriptures and true conceptions of all things, and if the heart succeeds in freeing itself permanently from the effects of all pairs of opposites, is it still necessary for such a person to follow one after another, the three modes of life called Brahmacharya, Garahastya, and Vanaprastha.

data.v: एतद्भवन्तं पृच्छामि तद्भवान्वक्तुमर्हति । यथावेदार्थतत्त्वेन ब्रूहि मे त्वं जनाधिप ॥
data.md: This is what I ask you. You should me. Indeed, O king, do tell me this according to the true meaning of the Vedas.

data.v: न विना ज्ञानविज्ञानं मोक्षस्याधिगमो भवेत् । न विना गुरुसंबन्धं ज्ञानस्याधिगमः स्मृतः ॥
data.md: Janaka said It is impossible to aquire Liberation without the help of an understanding purified by the study of the scriptures and without that true conception of all things which is known by the name of Vijnana, again, without that cleansed understanding, one cannot get a Preceptor.

data.v: आचार्यः प्लाविता तस्य ज्ञानं प्लव इहोच्यते । विज्ञाय कृतकृत्यस्तु तीर्णस्तदुभयं त्यजेत् ॥
data.md: The Preceptor is the helmsman, and Knowledge is the Boat. After having got that Boat, one becomes successful. Indeed, having crossed the Ocean, one may renounce both.

data.v: अनुच्छेदाय लोकानामनुच्छेदाय कर्मणाम् । पूर्वैराचरितो धर्मश्चातुराश्रम्यसंकथः ॥
data.md: For preventing the destruction of all the worlds, and for preventing the destruction of deeds, the duties belonging to the four modes of life were practised by the wise of old.

data.v: अनेन क्रमयोगेन बहुजातिषु कर्मणा । कृत्वा शुभाशुभं कर्म मोक्षो नामेह लभ्यते ॥
data.md: By renouncing acts, good and bad, according to this order of acts, one succeeds, in course of many births, in acquiring Liberation.

data.v: भावितैः कारणैश्चायं बहुसंसारयोनिषु । आसादयति शुद्धात्मा मोक्षं वै प्रथमाश्रमे ॥
data.md: That man who, through penances, practised in many births, succeeds in acquiring purified mind and understanding, and soul, certainly becomes able to acquire Liberation in even the very first mode.

data.v: तमासाद्य तु मुक्तस्य दृष्टार्थस्य विपश्चितः । त्रिष्वाश्रमेषु को न्वर्थो भवेत्परमभीप्सतः ॥
data.md: When, having acquired cleansed understanding, Liberation becomes his, and on account thereof be becomes possessed of knowledge of all visible things, what desirable object is there to attain by following the three other modes of life? a

data.v: राजसांस्तामसांश्चैव नित्यं दोषान्विवर्जयेत् । सात्त्विकं मार्गमास्थाय पश्येदात्मानमात्मना ॥
data.md: One should always renounce faults produced by the qualities of Rajas and Tamas. Following the path of Sattva, one should see Self by Self.

data.v: सर्वभूतेषु चात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । संपश्यन्नोपलिप्येत जले वारिचरो यथा ॥
data.md: Seeing one's Self in all creatures and all creatures in one's self, one should live like acquatic animals living in water without being drenched by it.

data.v: पक्षीव प्लवनादूर्ध्वममुत्रानन्त्यमश्नुते । विहाय देहं निर्मुक्तो निर्द्वंद्वः प्रशमं गतः ॥
data.md: He who succeeds in getting over all pairs of opposites and resisting their influence, succeeds in renouncing all attachments, and acquires infinite happiness in the next world, going there like a bird soaring into the sky from below.

data.v: अत्र गाथाः पुरा गीताः शृणु राज्ञा ययातिना । धार्यन्ते या द्विजैस्तात मोक्षशास्त्रविशारदैः ॥
data.md: Regarding it, there is a saying sung of old by king Yayati, and remembered, O sire, by all persons conversant with the Scriptures dealing with Liberation.

data.v: ज्योतिरात्मनि नान्यत्र रतं तत्रैव चैव तत् । स्वयं च शक्यं तद्द्रष्टुं सुसमाहितचेतसा ॥
data.md: The effulgent ray exists in one's Soul and not any where else. It exists equally in all creatures. One can see it himself if his heart be given to Yoga.

data.v: न बिभेति परो यस्मान्न बिभेति पराच्च यः । यश्च नेच्छति न द्वेष्टि ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
data.md: When a person lives in such a way that another is not filled with fear on seeing him, and when a person is not himself filled with fear on seeing others, when a person ceases to cherish desire and malice, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

data.v: यदा भावं न कुरुते सर्वभूतेषु पापकम् । कर्मणा मनसा वाचा ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
data.md: When a person ceases to cherish a sinful attitude towards all creatures in thought, word, and deed, he is then said to attain to Brahima.

data.v: संयोज्य तपसात्मानमीर्ष्यामुत्सृज्य मोहिनीम् । त्यक्त्वा कामं च लोभं च ततो ब्रह्मत्वमश्नुते ॥
data.md: By controlling the mind and the soul, by renouncing malice that stupefies the mind, and by throwing off desire and stupefaction, one is said to attain to Brahma.

data.v: यदा श्रव्ये च दृश्ये च सर्वभूतेषु चाप्ययम् । समो भवति निर्द्वंद्वो ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
data.md: When a person assumes an equality of attitude about all objects of hearing and vision, as also about all living creatures, and gets over all pairs of opposites, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

data.v: यदा स्तुतिं च निन्दां च समत्वेनैव पश्यति । काञ्चनं चायसं चैव सुखदुःखे तथैव च ॥
data.md: When a person regards impartially praise and dispraise, gold and iron, happiness and misery, heat and cold, good and evil, the agreeable and the disagreeable, life and death, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

data.v: शीतमुष्णं तथैवार्थमनर्थं प्रियमप्रियम् । जीवितं मरणं चैव ब्रह्म संपद्यते तदा ॥
data.md: When a person regards impartially praise and dispraise, gold and iron, happiness and misery, heat and cold, good and evil, the agreeable and the disagreeable, life and death, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

data.v: प्रसार्येह यथाङ्गानि कूर्मः संहरते पुनः । तथेन्द्रियाणि मनसा संयन्तव्यानि भिक्षुणा ॥
data.md: One following the duties of the mendicant order should restrain his senses and the mind like a tortoise withdrawing its outstretched limbs.

data.v: तमःपरिगतं वेश्म यथा दीपेन दृश्यते । तथा बुद्धिप्रदीपेन शक्य आत्मा निरीक्षितुम् ॥
data.md: As a house covered with darkness, is capable of being seen with the help of a lighted lamp, similarly can the soul be seen with the help of the lamp of the understanding.

data.v: एतत्सर्वं प्रपश्यामि त्वयि बुद्धिमतां वर । यच्चान्यदपि वेत्तव्यं तत्त्वतो वेद तद्भवान् ॥
data.md: O foremost of intelligent persons, I see that all this knowledge that I am imparting to you, lives in you. Whatever else should be known by one desirous of learning the Religion of Liberation, is already known to you.

data.v: ब्रह्मर्षे विदितश्चासि विषयान्तमुपागतः । गुरोस्तव प्रसादेन तव चैवोपशिक्षया ॥
data.md: O regenerate Rishi, I am convinced that through the mercy of your preceptor and through the instructions you have received, you have already transcended all objects of the senses.

data.v: तस्यैव च प्रसादेन प्रादुर्भूतं महामुने । ज्ञानं दिव्यं ममापीदं तेनासि विदितो मम ॥
data.md: O great ascetic, through the grace of your father, I have acquired omniscience, and hence I have succeeded in knowing you.

data.v: अधिकं तव विज्ञानमधिका च गतिस्तव । अधिकं च तवैश्वर्यं तच्च त्वं नावबुध्यसे ॥
data.md: Your knowledge is much greater than what you think it to be. Your perceptions also that result from intuition, are much greater than what you think them to be. Your power also is much greater than you are conscious of.

data.v: बाल्याद्वा संशयाद्वापि भयाद्वाप्यविमोक्षजात् । उत्पन्ने चापि विज्ञाने नाधिगच्छति तां गतिम् ॥
data.md: Whether in consequence of your tender age, or of the doubts you have not been able to remove, or of the fear that is due to be unattainment of Liberation, you are conscious of that Knowledge due to Intuition, although it has originated in your mind.

data.v: व्यवसायेन शुद्धेन मद्विधैश्छिन्नसंशयः । विमुच्य हृदयग्रन्थीनासादयति तां गतिम् ॥
data.md: After one's doubts have been removed by persons like us, one succeeds in opening the knots of one's heart, and, then, by a righteous endeavour, acquires, and becomes conscious of, that Knowledge. not one

data.v: भवांश्चोत्पन्नविज्ञानः स्थिरबुद्धिरलोलुपः । व्यवसायादृते ब्रह्मन्नासादयति तत्परम् ॥
data.md: As regards yourself, you are one that has already acquired knowledge. Your intelligence is steady and tranquil. You are free from covetousness. For all that, O Brahmana, one never succeed, without endeavour in attaining to Brahma, which is the highest object of acquisition.

data.v: नास्ति ते सुखदुःखेषु विशेषो नास्ति लोलुपा । नौत्सुक्यं नृत्तगीतेषु न राग उपजायते ॥
data.md: You see no difference between happiness and misery. You are not covetous. You have no desire for dancing and song. You have no attachments.

data.v: न बन्धुषु निबन्धस्ते न भयेष्वस्ति ते भयम् । पश्यामि त्वां महाभाग तुल्यलोष्टाश्मकाञ्चनम् ॥
data.md: You have no attachment to friends. You have no fear in things which fill with fear. O blessed one, I see that you consider equally a lump of gold and a clod of Earth.

data.v: अहं च त्वानुपश्यामि ये चाप्यन्ये मनीषिणः । आस्थितं परमं मार्गमक्षयं तमनामयम् ॥
data.md: Myself and other persons endued with wisdom, see you established in the highest and indestructible path of peace.

data.v: यत्फलं ब्राह्मणस्येह मोक्षार्थश्च यदात्मकः । तस्मिन्वै वर्तसे विप्र किमन्यत्परिपृच्छसि ॥
data.md: O Brahmana, you discharge the duties of Brahmana and enjoy the fruit which should be his, and which is at one with the essence of the object represented by Liberation. What else have you to enquire of me?

data.v: एतच्छ्रुत्वा तु वचनं कृतात्मा कृतनिश्चयः । आत्मनात्मानमास्थाय दृष्ट्वा चात्मानमात्मना ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Having heard these words of king Janaka, Shuka of purified soul and settled conclusions began to stay in his Soul by his Soul, having of course seen Self by Self.

data.v: कृतकार्यः सुखी शान्तस्तूष्णीं प्रायादुदङ्मुखः । शैशिरं गिरिमुद्दिश्य सधर्मा मातरिश्वनः ॥
data.md: His object being fulfilled he became happy and tranquil, and without further questioning Janaka, he proceeded northwards to the mountains of Himavat with the speed of the wind and like the wind.

data.v: एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु देवर्षिर्नारदस्तदा । हिमवन्तमियाद्द्रष्टुं सिद्धचारणसेवितम् ॥
तमप्सरोगणाकीर्णं गीतस्वननिनादितम् । किंनराणां समूहैश्च भृङ्गराजैस्तथैव च ॥
मद्गुभिः खञ्जरीटैश्च विचित्रैर्जीवजीवकैः । चित्रवर्णैर्मयूरैश्च केकाशतविराजितैः । राजहंससमूहैश्च हृष्टैः परभृतैस्तथा ॥
पक्षिराजो गरुत्मांश्च यं नित्यमधिगच्छति । चत्वारो लोकपालाश्च देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा । यत्र नित्यं समायान्ति लोकस्य हितकाम्यया ॥
data.md: The four Regents of the world, the gods, and various classes of Rishis, used always to come there from desire of doing good to the world.

data.v: विष्णुना यत्र पुत्रार्थे तपस्तप्तं महात्मना । यत्रैव च कुमारेण बाल्ये क्षिप्ता दिवौकसः ॥
data.md: It was there that the great Vishnu had practised the severest penances for the object of getting a son.

data.v: शक्तिर्न्यस्ता क्षितितले त्रैलोक्यमवमन्य वै । यत्रोवाच जगत्स्कन्दः क्षिपन्वाक्यमिदं तदा ॥
योऽन्योऽस्ति मत्तोऽभ्यधिको विप्रा यस्याधिकं प्रियाः । यो ब्रह्मण्यो द्वितीयोऽस्ति त्रिषु लोकेषु वीर्यवान् ॥
सोऽभ्युद्धरत्विमां शक्तिमथ वा कम्पयत्विति । तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथिता लोकाः क इमामुद्धरेदिति ॥
अथ देवगणं सर्वं संभ्रान्तेन्द्रियमानसम् । अपश्यद्भगवान्विष्णुः क्षिप्तं सासुरराक्षसम् । किं न्वत्र सुकृतं कार्यं भवेदिति विचिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: Vishnu saw all the gods and Asuras and Rakshasas to be greatly troubled in mind. He thought of what should be done under the circumstances. Without being able to bear that challenge regarding the hurling of the dart, he directed his eyes towards Skanda, the son of the Fire-god.

data.v: स नामृष्यत तं क्षेपमवैक्षत च पावकिम् । स प्रहस्य विशुद्धात्मा शक्तिं प्रज्वलितां तदा । कम्पयामास सव्येन पाणिना पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
data.md: The pure Vishnu caught hold of the burning dart with his left hand, and began to shake it.

data.v: शक्त्यां तु कम्पमानायां विष्णुना बलिना तदा । मेदिनी कम्पिता सर्वा सशैलवनकानना ॥
data.md: When the dart was being thus shaken by the highly powerful Vishnu, the whole Earth with her mountains, forests, and seas, shook with the dart.

data.v: शक्तेनापि समुद्धर्तुं कम्पिता सा न तूद्धृता । रक्षता स्कन्दराजस्य धर्षणां प्रभविष्णुना ॥
data.md: Although Vishnu was fully capable to raise the dart, still he contented himself with only shaking it. In this, the powerful lord only kept the honour of Skanda intact.

data.v: तां कम्पयित्वा भगवान्प्रह्रादमिदमब्रवीत् । पश्य वीर्यं कुमारस्य नैतदन्यः करिष्यति ॥
data.md: Having shaken it himself, the divine Vishnu, addressing Prahlada, said,-see the might of Kumara! None else in the universe can raise this dart.

data.v: सोऽमृष्यमाणस्तद्वाक्यं समुद्धरणनिश्चितः । जग्राह तां तस्य शक्तिं न चैनामप्यकम्पयत् ॥
data.md: Unable to bear this, Prahlada determined to raise the dart. He caught it, but was unable to shake it at all.

data.v: नादं महान्तं मुक्त्वा स मूर्छितो गिरिमूर्धनि । विह्वलः प्रापतद्भूमौ हिरण्यकशिपोः सुतः ॥
data.md: Uttering a loud cry, he dropped down on the hill-top in a swoon. Indeed, the son of Hiranyakashipu dropped down on the Earth.

data.v: यत्रोत्तरां दिशं गत्वा शैलराजस्य पार्श्वतः । तपोऽतप्यत दुर्धर्षस्तात नित्यं वृषध्वजः ॥
data.md: Going towards the northern side of those grand mountains, Mahadeva, having the bull for his emblem, had practised the austerest penances.

data.v: पावकेन परिक्षिप्तो दीप्यता तस्य चाश्रमः । आदित्यबन्धनं नाम दुर्धर्षमकृतात्मभिः ॥
data.md: The asylum where Mahadeva had practised those austerities is encompassed on all sides with a burning fire. Unapproachable by person of impure souls, that mountain is known by the name of Aditya.

data.v: न तत्र शक्यते गन्तुं यक्षराक्षसदानवैः । दशयोजनविस्तारमग्निज्वालासमावृतम् ॥
data.md: There is a fiery girdle all around it, of ten Yojanas in width and it is incapable of being approached by Yakshas and Rakshasas and Danavas.

data.v: भगवान्पावकस्तत्र स्वयं तिष्ठति वीर्यवान् । सर्वविघ्नान्प्रशमयन्महादेवस्य धीमतः ॥
data.md: The illustrious God of Fire, endued with mighty energy, lives there in embodied form engaged in removing all obstacles from the side of Mahadeva of great wisdom who remained there for thousand celestial years, standing on one foot.

data.v: दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं हि पादेनैकेन तिष्ठतः । देवान्संतापयंस्तत्र महादेवो धृतव्रतः ॥
ऐन्द्रीं तु दिशमास्थाय शैलराजस्य धीमतः । विविक्ते पर्वततटे पाराशर्यो महातपाः । वेदानध्यापयामास व्यासः शिष्यान्महातपाः ॥
data.md: At the foot of those mountains, in a retired spot, Parashara's son of great ascetic merit, viz., Vyasa, taught the Vedas to his disciples.

data.v: सुमन्तुं च महाभागं वैशंपायनमेव च । जैमिनिं च महाप्राज्ञं पैलं चापि तपस्विनम् ॥
data.md: Those disciples were the highly blessed Sumanta, Vaishampayana, Jaimini of great wisdom, and Paila of great ascetic merit.

data.v: एभिः शिष्यैः परिवृतो व्यास आस्ते महातपाः । तत्राश्रमपदं पुण्यं ददर्श पितुरुत्तमम् । आरणेयो विशुद्धात्मा नभसीव दिवाकरः ॥
data.md: Shuka went to that charming asylum where his father, the great ascetic Vyasa, was living surrounded by his disciples.

data.v: अथ व्यासः परिक्षिप्तं ज्वलन्तमिव पावकम् । ददर्श सुतमायान्तं दिवाकरसमप्रभम् ॥
data.md: Seated in his asylum, Vyasa saw his son approach like a burning fire of scattered flames, or resembling the Sun himself in effulgence.

data.v: असज्जमानं वृक्षेषु शैलेषु विषमेषु च । योगयुक्तं महात्मानं यथा बाणं गुणच्युतम् ॥
data.md: As Shuka approached, he did not seem to touch the trees or the rocks of the mountain. Perfectly dissociated from all objects of the senses, and engaged in Yoga, the great ascetic came, resembling in speed an arrow shot off a bow.

data.v: सोऽभिगम्य पितुः पादावगृह्णादरणीसुतः । यथोपजोषं तैश्चापि समागच्छन्महामुनिः ॥
data.md: Born on the fire-sticks, Shuka approaching his father, touched his feet. With due formalities he then accosted the disciples of his father.

data.v: ततो निवेदयामास पित्रे सर्वमशेषतः । शुको जनकराजेन संवादं प्रीतमानसः ॥
data.md: With great cheerfulness he then described in full to his father all the particulars of his conversation with king Janaka.

data.v: एवमध्यापयञ्शिष्यान्व्यासः पुत्रं च वीर्यवान् । उवास हिमवत्पृष्ठे पाराशर्यो महामुनिः ॥
data.md: After the arrival of his powerful son, Vyasa, the son of Parashara, continued to live there on the Himavat, engaged in teaching his disciples, and his son.

data.v: ततः कदाचिच्छिष्यास्तं परिवार्यावतस्थिरे । वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नाः शान्तात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः ॥
data.md: One day as he was seated his disciples, all well-read in the Vedas, having their senses under control, and gifted with tranquil souls, sat themselves around him.

data.v: वेदेषु निष्ठां संप्राप्य साङ्गेष्वतितपस्विनः । अथोचुस्ते तदा व्यासं शिष्याः प्राञ्जलयो गुरुम् ॥
data.md: All of them had perfectly mastered the Vedas with their branches. All of them were observant of penances. With joined hands they addressed their preceptor in the following words.

data.v: महता श्रेयसा युक्ता यशसा च स्म वर्धिताः । एकं त्विदानीमिच्छामो गुरुणानुग्रहं कृतम् ॥
data.md: We have, through your favour, been ended with great energy. Our fame, also has spread. There is one favour that we pray you to grant us.

data.v: इति तेषां वचः श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मर्षिस्तानुवाच ह । उच्यतामिति तद्वत्सा यद्वः कार्यं प्रियं मया ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of theirs, the twiceborm Rishi answered them, saying,-You sons, tell me what that boon is which you want me to grant you.

data.v: एतद्वाक्यं गुरोः श्रुत्वा शिष्यास्ते हृष्टमानसाः । पुनः प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा प्रणम्य शिरसा गुरुम् ॥
data.md: Hearing this answer of their preceptor, the disciples became filled with joy. Bending their heads once more low to their preceptor, and joining their hands, all of them simultaneously, said, O king, these excellent words: If our preceptor has been gratified with us, then, O best of sages, we are sure to be successful.

data.v: ऊचुस्ते सहिता राजन्निदं वचनमुत्तमम् । यदि प्रीत उपाध्यायो धन्याः स्मो मुनिसत्तम ॥
data.md: Hearing this answer of their preceptor, the disciples became filled with joy. Bending their heads once more low to their preceptor, and joining their hands, all of them simultaneously, said, O king, these excellent words: If our preceptor has been gratified with us, then, O best of sages, we are sure to be successful.

data.v: काङ्क्षामस्तु वयं सर्वे वरं दत्तं महर्षिणा । षष्ठः शिष्यो न ते ख्यातिं गच्छेदत्र प्रसीद नः ॥
data.md: We all solicit you, O great Rishi, to grant us a boon. Do you show us favour. Let no sixth disciple succeed in acquiring fame.

data.v: चत्वारस्ते वयं शिष्या गुरुपुत्रश्च पञ्चमः । इह वेदाः प्रतिष्ठेरन्नेष नः काङ्क्षितो वरः ॥
data.md: We are four. Our preceptor's son forms the fifth. Let the Vedas shine in only us five! This is the boon that we pray for.

data.v: शिष्याणां वचनं श्रुत्वा व्यासो वेदार्थतत्त्ववित् । पराशरात्मजो धीमान्परलोकार्थचिन्तकः । उवाच शिष्यान्धर्मात्मा धर्म्यं नैःश्रेयसं वचः ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of his disciples, Vyasa, the son of Parashara, endued with great intelligence, well conversant with the meanings of the Vedas, endued with a pious soul, and always engaged in thinking of objects that grant benefits on a person in the next world, said to his disciples these righteous words, fraught with great benefit:-The Vedas should always be given to him, who is a Brahmana, or to him who is desirous of listening to Vedic instructions, by him who eagerly wishes to acquire a residence in the region of Brahman.

data.v: ब्राह्मणाय सदा देयं ब्रह्म शुश्रूषवे भवेत् । ब्रह्मलोके निवासं यो ध्रुवं समभिकाङ्क्षति ॥
भवन्तो बहुलाः सन्तु वेदो विस्तार्यतामयम् । नाशिष्ये संप्रदातव्यो नाव्रते नाकृतात्मनि ॥
एते शिष्यगुणाः सर्वे विज्ञातव्या यथार्थतः । नापरीक्षितचारित्रे विद्या देया कथंचन ॥
यथा हि कनकं शुद्धं तापच्छेदनिघर्षणैः । परीक्षेत तथा शिष्यानीक्षेत्कुलगुणादिभिः ॥
न नियोज्याश्च वः शिष्या अनियोगे महाभये । यथामति यथापाठं तथा विद्या फलिष्यति ॥
सर्वस्तरतु दुर्गाणि सर्वो भद्राणि पश्यतु । श्रावयेच्चतुरो वर्णान्कृत्वा ब्राह्मणमग्रतः ॥
data.md: Let all disciples master all difficulties, and let all of them be crowned with success. You are competent to expound the scriptures to persons of all the castes. Only ye should, while delivering instructions address a Brahmana, first of all.

data.v: वेदस्याध्ययनं हीदं तच्च कार्यं महत्स्मृतम् । स्तुत्यर्थमिह देवानां वेदाः सृष्टाः स्वयंभुवा ॥
data.md: These are the rules about the study of the Vedas. This again is considered as a high task. The Vedas were created by the Self-create for the purpose of praising the gods therewith.

data.v: यो निर्वदेत संमोहाद्ब्राह्मणं वेदपारगम् । सोऽपध्यानाद्ब्राह्मणस्य पराभूयादसंशयम् ॥
data.md: That man who, through stupefaction of intellect, speaks ill of a Brahmana well-read in the Vedas, is certain to meet with humiliation on account of such evil-speaking.

data.v: यश्चाधर्मेण विब्रूयाद्यश्चाधर्मेण पृच्छति । तयोरन्यतरः प्रैति विद्वेषं वाधिगच्छति ॥
data.md: He who, disregarding all rules of virtue, seeks knowledge, and he who, disregarding the rules of virtue, communicates knowledge, both of them fall off and instead of that love which should exist instead of that love which should exist between preceptor and disciple, such questioning and such communication are sure to create distrust and suspicion.

data.v: एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं स्वाध्यायस्य विधिं प्रति । उपकुर्याच्च शिष्याणामेतच्च हृदि वो भवेत् ॥
data.md: I have now told you everything about the way in which the Vedas should be studied and taught. You should treat your disciples thus, remembering these instructions.”

data.v: एतच्छ्रुत्वा गुरोर्वाक्यं व्यासशिष्या महौजसः । अन्योन्यं हृष्टमनसः परिषस्वजिरे तदा ॥
data.md: "Hearing these words of their preceptor, Vyasa's disciples gifted with great energy, became filled with the joy and embraced one another.

data.v: उक्ताः स्मो यद्भगवता तदात्वायतिसंहितम् । तन्नो मनसि संरूढं करिष्यामस्तथा च तत् ॥
data.md: Addressing one another, these said,-We will remember and act according to what has been said by our illustrious preceptor in view of our future well-being.

data.v: अन्योन्यं च सभाज्यैवं सुप्रीतमनसः पुनः । विज्ञापयन्ति स्म गुरुं पुनर्वाक्यविशारदाः ॥
data.md: Having said this to one another with gladdened hearts, the disciples of Vyasa, who were consummate masters of words, once more addressed their preceptor and said,-If it pleases you, O powerful one we wish to get down from this mountain to the Earth, O great ascetic, for the object of sub-dividing the Vedas.

data.v: शैलादस्मान्महीं गन्तुं काङ्क्षितं नो महामुने । वेदाननेकधा कर्तुं यदि ते रुचितं विभो ॥
शिष्याणां वचनं श्रुत्वा पराशरसुतः प्रभुः । प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं धर्मार्थसहितं हितम् ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of his disciples, the powerful son of Parashara, replied them in these wholesome words which were fraught, besides, with virtue and profit.-You may go to the Earth or to the regions of the gods as ye like. You should always be careful, for the Vedas are such that they are always liable to be misunderstood.

data.v: क्षितिं वा देवलोकं वा गम्यतां यदि रोचते । अप्रमादश्च वः कार्यो ब्रह्म हि प्रचुरच्छलम् ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of his disciples, the powerful son of Parashara, replied them in these wholesome words which were fraught, besides, with virtue and profit.-You may go to the Earth or to the regions of the gods as ye like. You should always be careful, for the Vedas are such that they are always liable to be misunderstood.

data.v: तेऽनुज्ञातास्ततः सर्वे गुरुणा सत्यवादिना । जग्मुः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा व्यासं मूर्ध्नाभिवाद्य च ॥
data.md: Permitted by their preceptor of truthful speech, the disciples left him after going round him and bowing their heads to him.

data.v: अवतीर्य महीं तेऽथ चातुर्होत्रमकल्पयन् । संयाजयन्तो विप्रांश्च राजन्यांश्च विशस्तथा ॥
data.md: Descending upon the Earth they celebrated the Agnishtoma and other sacrifices; and they began to officiate at the sacrifices of Brahinanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas.

data.v: पूज्यमाना द्विजैर्नित्यं मोदमाना गृहे रताः । याजनाध्यापनरताः श्रीमन्तो लोकविश्रुताः ॥
data.md: Happily spending their days in the domestic mode of life, they were treated by the Brahmanas with great reverence. Possessed of great fame and prosperity, they were engaged in teaching and officiating in sacrifices.

data.v: अवतीर्णेषु शिष्येषु व्यासः पुत्रसहायवान् । तूष्णीं ध्यानपरो धीमानेकान्ते समुपाविशत् ॥
data.md: After his disciples had departed, Vyasa remained in his hermitage, with only his son in his company. Passing his days in anxious thoughtfulness, and great Rishi, endued with wisdom, kept silent, sitting in a retired corner of the asylum.

data.v: तं ददर्शाश्रमपदे नारदः सुमहातपाः । अथैनमब्रवीत्काले मधुराक्षरया गिरा ॥
data.md: At that time Narada of great ascetic merit came there for seeing Vyasa, and addressing him, said these words of sweet sound.

data.v: भो भो महर्षे वासिष्ठ ब्रह्मघोषो न वर्तते । एको ध्यानपरस्तूष्णीं किमास्से चिन्तयन्निव ॥
data.md: Narada said O twice-born Rishi of Vashistha's family, why are Vedic sounds silent now? Why are you sitting silent and alone, engaged in meditation like one engrossed in thought?

data.v: ब्रह्मघोषैर्विरहितः पर्वतोऽयं न शोभते । रजसा तमसा चैव सोमः सोपप्लवो यथा ॥
data.md: Alas, destitute of Vedic sound, this mountain has lost its beauty, as the Moon shorn of splendour when possessed by Rahu or covered with dust.

data.v: न भ्राजते यथापूर्वं निषादानामिवालयः । देवर्षिगणजुष्टोऽपि वेदध्वनिनिराकृतः ॥
data.md: Though inhabited by the celestial Rishis, yet shorn of Vedic sounds, the mountain no longer appears beautiful now but resembles a village of Nishadas.

data.v: ऋषयश्च हि देवाश्च गन्धर्वाश्च महौजसः । विमुक्ता ब्रह्मघोषेण न भ्राजन्ते यथा पुरा ॥
data.md: The Rishis, the gods, and the Gandharvas, too, no longer shine as before on account of being deprived of Vedic sound.

data.v: नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा कृष्णद्वैपायनोऽब्रवीत् । महर्षे यत्त्वया प्रोक्तं वेदवादविचक्षण ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of Narada the Islandborn Krishna answered, saying,-0 Great Rishi, O you who are conversant with the sayings of the Vedas, all that you have said is agreeable to me, and you should say it to me! You are omniscient. You have seen everything. Your curiosity knows all things.

data.v: एतन्मनोनुकूलं मे भवानर्हति भाषितुम् । सर्वज्ञः सर्वदर्शी च सर्वत्र च कुतूहली ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of Narada the Islandborn Krishna answered, saying,-0 Great Rishi, O you who are conversant with the sayings of the Vedas, all that you have said is agreeable to me, and you should say it to me! You are omniscient. You have seen everything. Your curiosity knows all things.

data.v: त्रिषु लोकेषु यद्वृत्तं सर्वं तव मते स्थितम् । तदाज्ञापय विप्रर्षे ब्रूहि किं करवाणि ते ॥
data.md: You know everything in the three words. Do you, then, Otwice-born Rishi, order me.0, tell me what I am to do.

data.v: यन्मया समनुष्ठेयं ब्रह्मर्षे तदुदाहर । वियुक्तस्येह शिष्यैर्मे नातिहृष्टमिदं मनः ॥
data.md: Tell me, O twice-born Rishi, what should now be done by me. Separated from my disciples, my mind has become very dispirited.

data.v: अनाम्नायमला वेदा ब्राह्मणस्याव्रतं मलम् । मलं पृथिव्या वाहीकाः स्त्रीणां कौतूहलं मलम् ॥
data.md: Narada said The fault of the Vedas is the suspension of their recitation. The fault of the Brahmanas is their non-observance of vows. The Vahika race is the stain of the Earth. Curiosity is the fault of women.

data.v: अधीयतां भवान्वेदान्सार्धं पुत्रेण धीमता । विधुन्वन्ब्रह्मघोषेण रक्षोभयकृतं तमः ॥
data.md: Do you with your intelligent son recite the Vedas, and do you with the echoes of Vedic sounds remove the fears of the Rakshasas.

data.v: नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा व्यासः परमधर्मवित् । तथेत्युवाच संहृष्टो वेदाभ्यासे दृढव्रतः ॥
data.md: Bhishma continued Hearing these words of Narada, Vyasa, the best of all persons knowing duties and firmly devoted to Vedic recitation, became filled with joy and answered Narada, saying,-So be it.

data.v: शुकेन सह पुत्रेण वेदाभ्यासमथाकरोत् । स्वरेणोच्चैः स शैक्षेण लोकानापूरयन्निव ॥
data.md: With his son Shuka, be began to recite the Vedas in a loud sweet voice, observing all the rules of ortheopy and, as it were, filling the three worlds with that sound.

data.v: तयोरभ्यसतोरेवं नानाधर्मप्रवादिनोः । वातोऽतिमात्रं प्रववौ समुद्रानिलवेजितः ॥
data.md: One day as father and son, who knew well the ordinances of duties, were engaged in reciting the Vedas, a violent wind arose as if moved by the gales that blow on the bosom of the ocean.

data.v: ततोऽनध्याय इति तं व्यासः पुत्रमवारयत् । शुको वारितमात्रस्तु कौतूहलसमन्वितः ॥
data.md: Understanding from this incident that the hour was not suited to sacred recitation, Vyasa immediately ordered his son to stop the recitation. Shuka, thus forbidden by his father, became filled with curiosity.

data.v: अपृच्छत्पितरं ब्रह्मन्कुतो वायुरभूदयम् । आख्यातुमर्हति भवान्वायोः सर्वं विचेष्टितम् ॥
data.md: He asked his father saying,-0 twice-born one, whence is this Wind? You should tell me everything about the conduct of the Wind.

data.v: शुकस्यैतद्वचः श्रुत्वा व्यासः परमविस्मितः । अनध्यायनिमित्तेऽस्मिन्निदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Hearing this question of Shuka, Vyasa became filled with wonder. He answered Shuka by telling him that that was an omen which showed that the recitation of the Vedas should be stopped.

data.v: दिव्यं ते चक्षुरुत्पन्नं स्वस्थं ते निर्मलं मनः । तमसा रजसा चापि त्यक्तः सत्त्वे व्यवस्थितः ॥
data.md: You have acquired spiritual vision. Your mind too has, of itself, became purged off all impurities. You have been freed from the qualities of Darkness and Ignorance. You live now in the quality of Goodness.

data.v: आदर्शे स्वामिव छायां पश्यस्यात्मानमात्मना । न्यस्यात्मनि स्वयं वेदान्बुद्ध्या समनुचिन्तय ॥
data.md: You see now your Soul with your Soul as one sees his own shadow in a mirror. Staying yourself on your own Soul, do you reflect on the Vedas.

data.v: देवयानचरो विष्णोः पितृयानश्च तामसः । द्वावेतौ प्रेत्य पन्थानौ दिवं चाधश्च गच्छतः ॥
data.md: The path of the Supreme Soul is called the path of the gods. The path that is made up of the quality of Ignorance is called the path of Pitris. These are the two paths in the world hereafter. By one, people go to heaven. By the other people go to hell.

data.v: पृथिव्यामन्तरिक्षे च यत्र संवान्ति वायवः । सप्तैते वायुमार्गा वै तान्निबोधानुपूर्वशः ॥
data.md: The winds blow, on the Earth's surface and in the sky. There are seven courses in which they blow. Listen to me as I describe them one after another.

data.v: तत्र देवगणाः साध्याः समभूवन्महाबलाः । तेषामप्यभवत्पुत्रः समानो नाम दुर्जयः ॥
data.md: The body has the senses. The senses are ruled over by the Sadhyas and many great beings of great strength. These gave birth to an invincible son named Samana.

data.v: उदानस्तस्य पुत्रोऽभूद्व्यानस्तस्याभवत्सुतः । अपानश्च ततो ज्ञेयः प्राणश्चापि ततः परम् ॥
data.md: From Samana originated a son calle Udana. From Udana originated Vyana. From Vyana arose Apana, and lastly from Apana originated the wind called Prana.

data.v: अनपत्योऽभवत्प्राणो दुर्धर्षः शत्रुतापनः । पृथक्कर्माणि तेषां तु प्रवक्ष्यामि यथातथम् ॥
data.md: That invincible scorcher of all enemies, vis., Prana, became barren. I shall now recite to you the different functions of those winds.

data.v: प्राणिनां सर्वतो वायुश्चेष्टा वर्तयते पृथक् । प्राणनाच्चैव भूतानां प्राण इत्यभिधीयते ॥
data.md: The wind is the root of the various functions of all living creatures, and because living creatures are enabled to live by it, therefore is the wind called Prana (or life).

data.v: प्रेरयत्यभ्रसंघातान्धूमजांश्चोष्मजांश्च यः । प्रथमः प्रथमे मार्गे प्रवहो नाम सोऽनिलः ॥
data.md: That wind which is the first in the above number and which is known by the name of Pravaha (Samana) drives, along the first course, masses of clouds born of smoke and heat. Passing through the sky, and coming into contact with the water in the clouds, that wind shows itself in effulgence among the darts of lightening.

data.v: अम्बरे स्नेहमभ्रेभ्यस्तडिद्भ्यश्चोत्तमद्युतिः । आवहो नाम संवाति द्वितीयः श्वसनो नदन् ॥
उदयं ज्योतिषां शश्वत्सोमादीनां करोति यः । अन्तर्देहेषु चोदानं यं वदन्ति महर्षयः ॥
data.md: The second wind, called Avaha blows with a loud noise. It is this wind that make Soma and the other luminaries rise and appear. Within the body that wind is called Udana by the wise.

data.v: यश्चतुर्भ्यः समुद्रेभ्यो वायुर्धारयते जलम् । उद्धृत्याददते चापो जीमूतेभ्योऽम्बरेऽनिलः ॥
data.md: That wind which drinks up water from the four oceans, and having sucked it up gives it to the clouds in the sky and which, having given it to the clouds, presents them to the gods of rain, is third in the number and known by the name of Udvaha.

data.v: योऽद्भिः संयोज्य जीमूतान्पर्जन्याय प्रयच्छति । उद्वहो नाम वर्षिष्ठस्त्रितीयः स सदागतिः ॥
data.md: That wind which drinks up water from the four oceans, and having sucked it up gives it to the clouds in the sky and which, having given it to the clouds, presents them to the gods of rain, is third in the number and known by the name of Udvaha.

data.v: समुह्यमाना बहुधा येन नीलाः पृथग्घनाः । वर्षमोक्षकृतारम्भास्ते भवन्ति घनाघनाः ॥
संहता येन चाविद्धा भवन्ति नदतां नदाः । रक्षणार्थाय संभूता मेघत्वमुपयान्ति च ॥
योऽसौ वहति देवानां विमानानि विहायसा । चतुर्थः संवहो नाम वायुः स गिरिमर्दनः ॥
येन वेगवता रुग्णा रूक्षेणारुजता रसान् । वायुना विहता मेघा न भवन्ति बलाहकाः ॥
दारुणोत्पातसंचारो नभसः स्तनयित्नुमान् । पञ्चमः स महावेगो विवहो नाम मारुतः ॥
data.md: That wind causes portends of many sorts and creates roaring sounds in the sky. It is known by the name of Vivaha. The fifth wind has great force and speed. It is dry and roots out and breaks down all trees. Existing with it, the clouds are called Valahaka.

data.v: यस्मिन्पारिप्लवे दिव्या वहन्त्यापो विहायसा । पुण्यं चाकाशगङ्गायास्तोयं विष्टभ्य तिष्ठति ॥
data.md: The sixth wind carries all celestial waters in the sky and prevents them from falling down. Keeping the sacred waters of the celestial Ganga, that wind blows preventing them from having a downward course.

data.v: दूरात्प्रतिहतो यस्मिन्नेकरश्मिर्दिवाकरः । योनिरंशुसहस्रस्य येन भाति वसुंधरा ॥
data.md: Obstructed by the wind from a distance, the Sun, which is really the root of a thousand rays, and which lights up the world, appears as a luminous body of but one ray.

data.v: यस्मादाप्यायते सोमो निधिर्दिव्योऽमृतस्य च । षष्ठः परिवहो नाम स वायुर्जवतां वरः ॥
data.md: Through the action of that wind, the Moon, after waning increases again till he shows his full disc. That wind is known, O foremost of ascetics, by the name of Parivaha.

data.v: सर्वप्राणभृतां प्राणान्योऽन्तकाले निरस्यति । यस्य वर्त्मानुवर्तेते मृत्युवैवस्वतावुभौ ॥
सम्यगन्वीक्षतां बुद्ध्या शान्तयाध्यात्मनित्यया । ध्यानाभ्यासाभिरामाणां योऽमृतत्वाय कल्पते ॥
यं समासाद्य वेगेन दिशामन्तं प्रपेदिरे । दक्षस्य दश पुत्राणां सहस्राणि प्रजापतेः ॥
येन सृष्टः पराभूतो यात्येव न निवर्तते । परावहो नाम परो वायुः स दुरतिक्रमः ॥
एवमेतेऽदितेः पुत्रा मारुताः परमाद्भुताः । अनारमन्तः संवान्ति सर्वगाः सर्वधारिणः ॥
data.md: Wonderful are these winds all of whom are the sons of Diti. Capable of going everywhere and upholding all things, they blow all around you without being attached to you at any time.

data.v: एतत्तु महदाश्चर्यं यदयं पर्वतोत्तमः । कम्पितः सहसा तेन वायुनाभिप्रवायता ॥
data.md: This, however, is greatly wonderful, viz., that this foremost of mountains should thus be suddenly shaken by that wind which has begun to below.

data.v: विष्णोर्निःश्वासवातोऽयं यदा वेगसमीरितः । सहसोदीर्यते तात जगत्प्रव्यथते तदा ॥
data.md: This wind is the breath of Vishnu's nostrils. When moved with speed, it begins to blow with great vehemence at which the whole universe becomes agitated.

data.v: तस्माद्ब्रह्मविदो ब्रह्म नाधीयन्तेऽतिवायति । वायोर्वायुभयं ह्युक्तं ब्रह्म तत्पीडितं भवेत् ॥
data.md: Hence, when the wind begins to blow with violence, persons knowing the Vedas do not recite the Vedas, The Vedas are a form of wind. If uttered with vehemence, the external wind becomes agitated.

data.v: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं पराशरसुतः प्रभुः । उक्त्वा पुत्रमधीष्वेति व्योमगङ्गामयात्तदा ॥
data.md: Having said these words, the powerful son of Parashara ordered his son to go on with his Vedic recitation. He then left that place for plugging into the waters of the celestial Ganga."

data.v: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे शून्ये नारदः समुपागमत् । शुकं स्वाध्यायनिरतं वेदार्थान्वक्तुमीप्सितान् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said "After Vyasa had left the spot, Narada, passing through the sky, came to Shuka engaged in studying the scriptures The celestial Rishi came for the object of asking Shuka the meaning of certain parts of the Vedas.

data.v: देवर्षिं तु शुको दृष्ट्वा नारदं समुपस्थितम् । अर्घ्यपूर्वेण विधिना वेदोक्तेनाभ्यपूजयत् ॥
data.md: Seeing the celestial Rishi Narada arrived at his asylum, Shuka adored him by offering him the Arghya according to the rites laid down in the Vedas.

data.v: नारदोऽथाब्रवीत्प्रीतो ब्रूहि ब्रह्मविदां वर । केन त्वां श्रेयसा तात योजयामीति हृष्टवत् ॥
data.md: Pleased with the honours conferred upon him, Narada addressed Shuka, saying.-Tell me, O foremost of pious men, how, O dear child, may I acccomplished what is for your highest good.

data.v: नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शुकः प्रोवाच भारत । अस्मिँल्लोके हितं यत्स्यात्तेन मां योक्तुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of Narada, Shuka said to him, O Bharata, these words:-You should instruct me about what may be beneficial to me!

data.v: तत्त्वं जिज्ञासतां पूर्वमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम् । सनत्कुमारो भगवानिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Narada said In days of yore the illustrious Sanatkumara had said these words to certain Rishis of purified souls who had gone to him for enquiring after the truth.

data.v: नास्ति विद्यासमं चक्षुर्नास्ति विद्यासमं तपः । नास्ति रागसमं दुःखं नास्ति त्यागसमं सुखम् ॥
data.md: There is no eye like that of knowledge. There is no penance like the practice of truth. There is no sorrow like attachment. There is no happiness like renunciation.

data.v: निवृत्तिः कर्मणः पापात्सततं पुण्यशीलता । सद्वृत्तिः समुदाचारः श्रेय एतदनुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Abstention from sinful deeds, steady practice of virtue, good conduct, the due observance of all religious duties,—these form the highest good.

data.v: मानुष्यमसुखं प्राप्य यः सज्जति स मुह्यति । नालं स दुःखमोक्षाय सङ्गो वै दुःखलक्षणम् ॥
data.md: Having acquired the status of humanity which is mixed with sorrow, he who becomes attached to it, becomes stupefied; such a man never succeeds in freeing himself from sorrow. Attachment is a mark of sorrow.

data.v: सक्तस्य बुद्धिश्चलति मोहजालविवर्धिनी । मोहजालावृतो दुःखमिह चामुत्र चाश्नुते ॥
data.md: The understanding of a person who is attached to earthly object becomes more and more entangled in the net of stupefaction. The man who becomes entangled in the net of stupefaction comes by sorrow both in this world and in the next.

data.v: सर्वोपायेन कामस्य क्रोधस्य च विनिग्रहः । कार्यः श्रेयोर्थिना तौ हि श्रेयोघातार्थमुद्यतौ ॥
data.md: One should, by every means in his power, control both desire and anger if one tries to acquire what is for his good. Those two originate for only destroying his good.

data.v: नित्यं क्रोधात्तपो रक्षेच्छ्रियं रक्षेत मत्सरात् । विद्यां मानावमानाभ्यामात्मानं तु प्रमादतः ॥
data.md: One should always protect his penances from anger, and his prosperity from pride. One should always protect his knowledge from honour and dishonour, and his soul from error.

data.v: आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः क्षमा च परमं बलम् । आत्मज्ञानं परं ज्ञानं न सत्याद्विद्यते परम् ॥
data.md: Mercy is the highest virtue. Forgiveness is the highest power. The knowledge of self is the highest knowledge. There is nothing higher than truth.

data.v: सत्यस्य वचनं श्रेयः सत्यादपि हितं भवेत् । यद्भूतहितमत्यन्तमेतत्सत्यं मतं मम ॥
data.md: It is always meet to speak the truth. It is better again to speak what is wholesome than to speak what is true. I hold that that is truth which is filled with the greatest benefit to all creatures.

data.v: सर्वारम्भफलत्यागी निराशीर्निष्परिग्रहः । येन सर्वं परित्यक्तं स विद्वान्स च पण्डितः ॥
data.md: That man is said to be truly learned and truly endued with wisdom who renounces every act, who never indulges in hope, who is perfectly dissociated from all worldly surroundings, and who has renounced everything that belongs to the world.

data.v: इन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियार्थेभ्यश्चरत्यात्मवशैरिह । असज्जमानः शान्तात्मा निर्विकारः समाहितः ॥
data.md: That person who, without being attached thereto, enjoys all objects of sense with the help of senses which are completely under his control, who is endued with a tranquil soul, who is never moved by joy or sorrow, who is engaged in Yoga-meditation, who lives with the gods presiding over his senses and dissociated also from them, and who, though gifted with a body, never considers himself as identifiable with it, becomes liberated and very soon acquires what is his highest good.

data.v: आत्मभूतैरतद्भूतः सह चैव विनैव च । स विमुक्तः परं श्रेयो नचिरेणाधिगच्छति ॥
अदर्शनमसंस्पर्शस्तथासंभाषणं सदा । यस्य भूतैः सह मुने स श्रेयो विन्दते परम् ॥
data.md: One who never sees others, never touches others, never talks with others, soon, O ascetic, acquires what is for his highest good.

data.v: न हिंस्यात्सर्वभूतानि मैत्रायणगतश्चरेत् । नेदं जन्म समासाद्य वैरं कुर्वीत केनचित् ॥
data.md: One should not injure any creature. On the other hand, one should treat with friendliness to all. Having acquired the status of humanity, one should never treat inimically to any one.

data.v: आकिंचन्यं सुसंतोषो निराशीष्ट्वमचापलम् । एतदाहुः परं श्रेय आत्मज्ञस्य जितात्मनः ॥
data.md: A perfect disregard for all (worldly) things, perfect contentment, abandonment of hope of every sort, and patience,-these form the highest good of one who has governed his senses and acquired a knowledge of self.

data.v: परिग्रहं परित्यज्य भव तात जितेन्द्रियः । अशोकं स्थानमातिष्ठ इह चामुत्र चाभयम् ॥
data.md: Renouncing all attachments, O child, do you master all your senses, and thereby acquire happiness both in this world and in the next.

data.v: निरामिषा न शोचन्ति त्यजेहामिषमात्मनः । परित्यज्यामिषं सौम्य दुःखतापाद्विमोक्ष्यसे ॥
data.md: They who are free from cupidity have never to suffer any sorrow. One should, therefore, renounce all cupidity from one's soul. By renouncing cupidity, O amiable and blessed one, you will be able to liberate yourself from sorrow and pain.

data.v: तपोनित्येन दान्तेन मुनिना संयतात्मना । अजितं जेतुकामेन भाव्यं सङ्गेष्वसङ्गिना ॥
data.md: One who wishes to conquer that which is unconquerable should live giving himself up to penances, to self-control, to taciturnity, to a subjugation of the soul. Such a person should live in the midst of attachments without being attached thereto.

data.v: गुणसङ्गेष्वनासक्त एकचर्यारतः सदा । ब्राह्मणो नचिरादेव सुखमायात्यनुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: That Brahmana who lives in the midst of attachments without being attached to them and who always lives in seclusion, very soon acquires the highest happiness.

data.v: द्वंद्वारामेषु भूतेषु य एको रमते मुनिः । विद्धि प्रज्ञानतृप्तं तं ज्ञानतृप्तो न शोचति ॥
data.md: That man who lives alone in happiness in the midst of creatures who are seen to find pleasure in leading lives of sexual union, should be known to be a person whose thirst has been satisfied by knowledge. It is well known that that man whose thirst has been satisfied by knowledge has never to grieve.

data.v: शुभैर्लभति देवत्वं व्यामिश्रैर्जन्म मानुषम् । अशुभैश्चाप्यधोजन्म कर्मभिर्लभतेऽवशः ॥
data.md: One acquires the status of the god my means of good deeds; the status of humanity by means of acts which are good and bad; while by acts which are purely wicked, one helplessly falls down among the lower animals.

data.v: तत्र मृत्युजरादुःखैः सततं समभिद्रुतः । संसारे पच्यते जन्तुस्तत्कथं नावबुध्यसे ॥
data.md: Always attacked by sorrow and decrepitude and death, a living creature is being cooked in this world. Do you not know it?

data.v: अहिते हितसंज्ञस्त्वमध्रुवे ध्रुवसंज्ञकः । अनर्थे चार्थसंज्ञस्त्वं किमर्थं नावबुध्यसे ॥
data.md: You generally consider that to be beneficial which is really injurious; that to be certain which is really uncertain; and that to be desirable and good which is undesirable and not good. Alas, why do you not form a correct apprehension of these?

data.v: संवेष्ट्यमानं बहुभिर्मोहतन्तुभिरात्मजैः । कोशकारवदात्मानं वेष्टयन्नावबुध्यसे ॥
data.md: Like a silkworm that covers itself in its own cocoon, you are continually covering yourself in a cocoon made of your own numberless deeds born of stupefaction and mistake. Alas, why do you not form a correct apprehension of your situation?

data.v: अलं परिग्रहेणेह दोषवान्हि परिग्रहः । कृमिर्हि कोशकारस्तु बध्यते स्वपरिग्रहात् ॥
data.md: No need of attaching yourself to earthly objects. Attachment to earthly objects produces evil. The silk-worm that forms a cocoon round itself is at last destroyed by its own deed.

data.v: पुत्रदारकुटुम्बेषु सक्ताः सीदन्ति जन्तवः । सरःपङ्कार्णवे मग्ना जीर्णा वनगजा इव ॥
data.md: Those persons who become attached to sons and wives and relatives meet with destruction in the end, as wild elephants sunk in the mire of a lake are by and by weakened till overtaken by Death,

data.v: महाजालसमाकृष्टान्स्थले मत्स्यानिवोद्धृतान् । स्नेहजालसमाकृष्टान्पश्य जन्तून्सुदुःखितान् ॥
data.md: See, all creatures that allow themselves to be dragged by the net of affection become subject to great grief as fishes on land, dragged thereto by means of large nets.

data.v: कुटुम्बं पुत्रदारं च शरीरं द्रव्यसंचयाः । पारक्यमध्रुवं सर्वं किं स्वं सुकृतदुष्कृतम् ॥
data.md: Relatives, sons, wives, the body itself, and all properties amassed with care, unsubstantial and of no use in the next world. Only acts, good and bad, that one does, follow him to the other world.

data.v: यदा सर्वं परित्यज्य गन्तव्यमवशेन ते । अनर्थे किं प्रसक्तस्त्वं स्वमर्थं नानुतिष्ठसि ॥
data.md: When it is certain that you shall have to go helplessly to the other world, leaving behind all these things, alas, why do you then allow yourself to be attached to such worthless unsubstantial things, without attending to what forms your real and durable wealth?

data.v: अविश्रान्तमनालम्बमपाथेयमदैशिकम् । तमःकान्तारमध्वानं कथमेको गमिष्यसि ॥
data.md: The path which you shall have to pass through is without resting places of any sort. There is no support along that way which one may catch for maintaining oneself. The country are through which it passes is unknown and undiscovered. It is, again, covered with thick darkness. Alas, how will you go along that way without being supplied with the necessary expenses?

data.v: न हि त्वा प्रस्थितं कश्चित्पृष्ठतोऽनुगमिष्यति । सुकृतं दुष्कृतं च त्वा यास्यन्तमनुयास्यति ॥
data.md: When you shall go along that road, nobody will follow you. Only your deeds, good and bad, will follow you when you shall leave his world for the next.

data.v: विद्या कर्म च शौर्यं च ज्ञानं च बहुविस्तरम् । अर्थार्थमनुसार्यन्ते सिद्धार्थस्तु विमुच्यते ॥
data.md: One seeks the real object by means of learning, acts, purity and great knowledge. When that foremost of objects is acquired, one becomes liberated.

data.v: निबन्धनी रज्जुरेषा या ग्रामे वसतो रतिः । छित्त्वैनां सुकृतो यान्ति नैनां छिन्दन्ति दुष्कृतः ॥
data.md: The desire that one feels for living in the midst of human dwellings is like a binding fetter. They that are of good deeds succeed in snapping that fetter and freeing themselves. Only men of wicked deeds do not succeed in breaking them.

data.v: रूपकूलां मनःस्रोतां स्पर्शद्वीपां रसावहाम् । गन्धपङ्कां शब्दजलां स्वर्गमार्गदुरावहाम् ॥
data.md: The river of life is dreadful. Personal beauty or form forms is banks. The mind is the speed of its current. Touch forms its island. Taste forms its waters. That particular part of it which leads towards heaven is beset with great difficulties. Body is the boat by which one must cross that river. Forgiveness is the oar by which it is to be moved. Truth is the ballast that keeps that boat steady. The practice of virtue is the rope that is to be put to the mast for dragging that boat along difficult waters. Charity or gift forms the wind that moves the sails of that boat. Bifted with swift speed, it is with that boat that one must cross the river of life.

data.v: क्षमारित्रां सत्यमयीं धर्मस्थैर्यवटाकराम् । त्यागवाताध्वगां शीघ्रां बुद्धिनावा नदीं तरेत् ॥
त्यज धर्ममधर्मं च उभे सत्यानृते त्यज । उभे सत्यानृते त्यक्त्वा येन त्यजसि तं त्यज ॥
data.md: Renounce both virtue and vice, and truth and falsehood. Having renounced truth and falsehood, do you cast off that by which these are to be shaken off.

data.v: त्यज धर्ममसंकल्पादधर्मं चाप्यहिंसया । उभे सत्यानृते बुद्ध्या बुद्धिं परमनिश्चयात् ॥
data.md: By casting off all purpose, do you renounce virtue; do you cast off sin also by renouncing all desire. With the help of the understanding, do you renounce truth and falsehood; and, at last, do you renounce the understanding itself by knowledge of the highest subject.

data.v: अस्थिस्थूणं स्नायुयुतं मांसशोणितलेपनम् । चर्मावनद्धं दुर्गन्धि पूर्णं मूत्रपुरीषयोः ॥
data.md: Do you renounce this body having bones for its pillars; sinews for its binding strings and cords; flesh and blood for its outer plaster; the skin for its outer case; full of urine and faeces and, therefore, sending forth a bad smell; exposed to the attacks of decrepitude and sorrow; forming the seat of disease and weakened by pain; predominated by the quality of Darkness; not permanent or durable, and which serves as the habitation of the indwelling creature.

data.v: जराशोकसमाविष्टं रोगायतनमातुरम् । रजस्वलमनित्यं च भूतावासं समुत्सृज ॥
इदं विश्वं जगत्सर्वमजगच्चापि यद्भवेत् । महाभूतात्मकं सर्वं महद्यत्परमाणु यत् ॥
data.md: This entire universe of matier, and that which is called Mahat or Buddhi, are formed of great elements. That which is called Mahat is due to the action of the Supreme.

data.v: इन्द्रियाणि च पञ्चैव तमः सत्त्वं रजस्तथा । इत्येष सप्तदशको राशिरव्यक्तसंज्ञकः ॥
data.md: The five senses, the three qualities of Tamas, Sattva, and Rajas,-these make up seventeen.

data.v: सर्वैरिहेन्द्रियार्थैश्च व्यक्ताव्यक्तैर्हि संहितः । पञ्चविंशक इत्येष व्यक्ताव्यक्तमयो गुणः ॥
data.md: These seventeen, which are known by the name of the Unmanifest, with all those that are called Manifest, viz., the five objects of the five senses, with Consciousness and the Understanding, constitute the well-known twenty-four.

data.v: एतैः सर्वैः समायुक्तः पुमानित्यभिधीयते । त्रिवर्गोऽत्र सुखं दुःखं जीवितं मरणं तथा ॥
data.md: When endued with those twenty-four possessions, one comes to be called by the name of Jiva or Individual Soul. He who knows the three-fold objects as also happiness and sorrow and life and death, truly and in all their details, is said to know growth and decay All objects of knowledge, should be known by and by.

data.v: य इदं वेद तत्त्वेन स वेद प्रभवाप्ययौ । पाराशर्येह बोद्धव्यं ज्ञानानां यच्च किंचन ॥
data.md: When endued with those twenty-four possessions, one comes to be called by the name of Jiva or Individual Soul. He who knows the three-fold objects as also happiness and sorrow and life and death, truly and in all their details, is said to know growth and decay All objects of knowledge, should be known by and by.

data.v: इन्द्रियैर्गृह्यते यद्यत्तत्तद्व्यक्तमिति स्थितिः । अव्यक्तमिति विज्ञेयं लिङ्गग्राह्यमतीन्द्रियम् ॥
data.md: All objects that are perceived by the senses are called Manifest. Whatever objects are above the senses and are apprehended by means only of their marks are said to be Unimanifest.

data.v: इन्द्रियैर्नियतैर्देही धाराभिरिव तर्प्यते । लोके विततमात्मानं लोकं चात्मनि पश्यति ॥
data.md: By controlling the senses, one acquires great gratification, like a thirsty and parched traveller at a sweet shower of rain. Having restrained the senses one sees one's soul spread out for embracing all objects, and all objects in one's soul.

data.v: परावरदृशः शक्तिर्ज्ञानवेलां न पश्यति । पश्यतः सर्वभूतानि सर्वावस्थासु सर्वदा ॥
data.md: Having its roots in knowledge, the power is never lost of the man who (thus) sees the Supreme in his soul,-of the man, who always sees all creatures in all conditions.

data.v: ब्रह्मभूतस्य संयोगो नाशुभेनोपपद्यते । ज्ञानेन विविधान्क्लेशानतिवृत्तस्य मोहजान् । लोके बुद्धिप्रकाशेन लोकमार्गो न रिष्यते ॥
data.md: He who, by the help of knowledge, gets over all sorts of pain begotten of mistake stupefaction, never catches any evil by coming into contact with all creatures.

data.v: अनादिनिधनं जन्तुमात्मनि स्थितमव्ययम् । अकर्तारममूर्तं च भगवानाह तीर्थवित् ॥
यो जन्तुः स्वकृतैस्तैस्तैः कर्मभिर्नित्यदुःखितः । स दुःखप्रतिघातार्थं हन्ति जन्तूननेकधा ॥
ततः कर्म समादत्ते पुनरन्यन्नवं बहु । तप्यतेऽथ पुनस्तेन भुक्त्वापथ्यमिवातुरः ॥
अजस्रमेव मोहार्तो दुःखेषु सुखसंज्ञितः । बध्यते मथ्यते चैव कर्मभिर्मन्थवत्सदा ॥
ततो निवृत्तो बन्धात्स्वात्कर्मणामुदयादिह । परिभ्रमति संसारं चक्रवद्बहुवेदनः ॥
स त्वं निवृत्तबन्धस्तु निवृत्तश्चापि कर्मतः । सर्ववित्सर्वजित्सिद्धो भव भावविवर्जितः ॥
संयमेन नवं बन्धं निवर्त्य तपसो बलात् । संप्राप्ता बहवः सिद्धिमप्यबाधां सुखोदयाम् ॥
data.md: Possessed of oinniscience and the master of all things, may you be successful, and do you become freed from all existent objects. Through subjugation of their senses and the power of their penances, many persons, having destroyed the fetters of action, acquired great success and uninterrupted happiness.

data.v: अशोकं शोकनाशार्थं शास्त्रं शान्तिकरं शिवम् । निशम्य लभते बुद्धिं तां लब्ध्वा सुखमेधते ॥
data.md: Narada said By listening to such sacred scriptures, as bring about tranquillity, as remove grief, and as yield happiness, one acquired (a pure) understanding, and, having acquired it; obtains to great happiness.

data.v: शोकस्थानसहस्राणि भयस्थानशतानि च । दिवसे दिवसे मूढमाविशन्ति न पण्डितम् ॥
data.md: A thousand causes of sorrow, a hundred causes of fear, from day to day, attack one who is shorn of understanding but not one who is endued with wisdom and learning.

data.v: तस्मादनिष्टनाशार्थमितिहासं निबोध मे । तिष्ठते चेद्वशे बुद्धिर्लभते शोकनाशनम् ॥
data.md: Do you, therefore, listen to some old narratives as I recount them to you, for the object of removing your sorrow, If one can subjugate his understanding, he is sure to acquire happiness.

data.v: अनिष्टसंप्रयोगाच्च विप्रयोगात्प्रियस्य च । मनुष्या मानसैर्दुःखैर्युज्यन्ते अल्पबुद्धयः ॥
data.md: By accession of what is undesirable and dissociation from what is agreeable, only men of little intelligence yield to mental sorrow.

data.v: द्रव्येषु समतीतेषु ये गुणास्तान्न चिन्तयेत् । ताननाद्रियमाणस्य स्नेहबन्धः प्रमुच्यते ॥
data.md: When things are passed, one should not grieve, thinking of their merits. He who thinks of such past things with affection can never liberate himself.

data.v: दोषदर्शी भवेत्तत्र यत्र रागः प्रवर्तते । अनिष्टवद्धितं पश्येत्तथा क्षिप्रं विरज्यते ॥
data.md: One should always try to find out the faults of those things to which one becomes attached, One should always consider such things to be fraught with much evil, By doing so, one should soon free him therefrom.

data.v: नार्थो न धर्मो न यशो योऽतीतमनुशोचति । अप्यभावेन युज्येत तच्चास्य न निवर्तते ॥
data.md: The man who grieves for what is past, cannot acquire either riches or religious merit or fame. What exists no longer cannot be acquired. When such things go away, they do not return.

data.v: गुणैर्भूतानि युज्यन्ते वियुज्यन्ते तथैव च । सर्वाणि नैतदेकस्य शोकस्थानं हि विद्यते ॥
data.md: Creatures sometimes acquire and sometimes lose earthly objects. No man in this world can be grieved by all the events that befall him.

data.v: मृतं वा यदि वा नष्टं योऽतीतमनुशोचति । दुःखेन लभते दुःखं द्वावनर्थौ प्रपद्यते ॥
data.md: Dead or lost, he who grieves for what is gone only gets sorrow for sorrow. Instead of one sorrow, he gets two.

data.v: नाश्रु कुर्वन्ति ये बुद्ध्या दृष्ट्वा लोकेषु संततिम् । सम्यक्प्रपश्यतः सर्वं नाश्रुकर्मोपपद्यते ॥
data.md: Those men who, seeing the course of life and death in the world with the help of their intelligence, do not shed tears, are said to see properly. Such persons have never to shed tears.

data.v: दुःखोपघाते शारीरे मानसे वाप्युपस्थिते । यस्मिन्न शक्यते कर्तुं यत्नस्तन्नानुचिन्तयेत् ॥
data.md: When any such calamity comes, which creates either their physical or mental grief, as is incapable of being prevented by even his best endeavours, one should cease to think on it with sorrow.

data.v: भैषज्यमेतद्दुःखस्य यदेतन्नानुचिन्तयेत् । चिन्त्यमानं हि न व्येति भूयश्चापि प्रवर्धते ॥
data.md: Not to think of it is the panacea for sorrow. By thinking of it, one can never remove it; on the other hand, by thinking upon sorrow, one only increases it.

data.v: प्रज्ञया मानसं दुःखं हन्याच्छारीरमौषधैः । एतद्विज्ञानसामर्थ्यं न बालैः समतामियात् ॥
data.md: Mental sorrow should be destroyed by wisdom; while physical sorrow should be removed by medicines. This is the power of knowledge. One should not, in such matters, act like men of little understandings.

data.v: अनित्यं यौवनं रूपं जीवितं द्रव्यसंचयः । आरोग्यं प्रियसंवासो गृध्येत्तत्र न पण्डितः ॥
data.md: Youth, beauty, life, hoarded riches, health, association with those that are loved, these all are fickle. One endued with wisdom should never covet them.

data.v: न जानपदिकं दुःखमेकः शोचितुमर्हति । अशोचन्प्रतिकुर्वीत यदि पश्येदुपक्रमम् ॥
data.md: One should not lament individually for a sorrowful incident that concerns an entire community. Instead of indulgence in grief when it comes, one should try to avert it and apply a remedy as soon as he finds the opportunity for doing it.

data.v: सुखाद्बहुतरं दुःखं जीविते नात्र संशयः । स्निग्धत्वं चेन्द्रियार्थेषु मोहान्मरणमप्रियम् ॥
