data.md: There is no doubt that in this life misery is much greater than that of happiness. There is no doubt in this that all men show attachment for objects of the senses and that death is considered as disagreeable.

data.v: परित्यजति यो दुःखं सुखं वाप्युभयं नरः । अभ्येति ब्रह्म सोऽत्यन्तं न तं शोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
data.md: That man who renounces both joy and sorrow, is said to attain to Brahma. When such a man dies, men of wisdom never indulge in any grief for him.

data.v: दुःखमर्था हि त्यज्यन्ते पालने न च ते सुखाः । दुःखेन चाधिगम्यन्ते नाशमेषां न चिन्तयेत् ॥
data.md: There is pain in spending wealth. There is pain in protecting it. There is pain in acquiring it. Hence, when one's wealth is lost, he should not grieve for it.

data.v: अन्यामन्यां धनावस्थां प्राप्य वैशेषिकीं नराः । अतृप्ता यान्ति विध्वंसं संतोषं यान्ति पण्डिताः ॥
data.md: Men of little understandings, in their efforts to acquire different grades of wealth, lose their contentment and at last die broken-hearted. Wise men, however, are always contented.

data.v: सर्वे क्षयान्ता निचयाः पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः । संयोगा विप्रयोगान्ता मरणान्तं हि जीवितम् ॥
data.md: All combinations are sure to end in dissolution. All things that are high are destined to fall down and become low. Union is sure to end in disunion, and life is certain to end in death.

data.v: अन्तो नास्ति पिपासायास्तुष्टिस्तु परमं सुखम् । तस्मात्संतोषमेवेह धनं पश्यन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
data.md: Thirst can never be satiated. Contentment is the greatest happiness. Hence, wise men regard contentment as the most valuable wealth.

data.v: निमेषमात्रमपि हि वयो गच्छन्न तिष्ठति । स्वशरीरेष्वनित्येषु नित्यं किमनुचिन्तयेत् ॥
data.md: One's lease of life is running continually. It stops not in its course for even a single moment. When one's body itself is not durable, what other thing is there which one should consider as durable?

data.v: भूतेष्वभावं संचिन्त्य ये बुद्ध्वा तमसः परम् । न शोचन्ति गताध्वानः पश्यन्तः परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: Those persons who, meditating on the nature of all creatures and, concluding that it is beyond the grasp of the mind, direct their attention to the highest path, and, starting, acquire a fair progress in it, have not to indulge in sorrow.

data.v: संचिन्वानकमेवैनं कामानामवितृप्तकम् । व्याघ्रः पशुमिवासाद्य मृत्युरादाय गच्छति ॥
data.md: Like the she-wolf snatching away a lamb, Death snatches away one who is still engaged in acquiring wealth and still unsatisfied in the enjoyment of pleasures.

data.v: अथाप्युपायं संपश्येद्दुःखस्य परिमोक्षणे । अशोचन्नारभेतैव युक्तश्चाव्यसनी भवेत् ॥
data.md: One should always try to liberate himself from sorrow. One should try to remove sorrow by beginning his work with cheerfulness, that is without indulging, in sorrow, having freed himself from a particular sorrow, one should act in such a way as to keep sorrow at a distance by abstaining from all shortcomings of conduct.

data.v: शब्दे स्पर्शे च रूपे च गन्धेषु च रसेषु च । नोपभोगात्परं किंचिद्धनिनो वाधनस्य वा ॥
data.md: The rich and the poor alike find nothing in sound and touch and form and scent and taste, after the immediate enjoyment thereof.

data.v: प्राक्संप्रयोगाद्भूतानां नास्ति दुःखमनामयम् । विप्रयोगात्तु सर्वस्य न शोचेत्प्रकृतिस्थितः ॥
data.md: Before union, creatures never suffer sorrow. Hence, one who has not deviated from his original nature, never grieves when that union comes to an end.

data.v: धृत्या शिश्नोदरं रक्षेत्पाणिपादं च चक्षुषा । चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च मनसा मनो वाचं च विद्यया ॥
data.md: One should control his sexual appetite and the stomach with the help of patience. One should protect his hands and feet with the help of the eye. One's eyes and ears and the other senses, should be protected by the mind. One's mind and speech should be governed with the help of wisdomn.

data.v: प्रणयं प्रतिसंहृत्य संस्तुतेष्वितरेषु च । विचरेदसमुन्नद्धः स सुखी स च पण्डितः ॥
data.md: Renouncing love and affection for persons that are known as well as for those that are unknown, one should act with humility. Such a person is said to be endued with wisdom, and such a one surely finds happiness.

data.v: अध्यात्मरतिरासीनो निरपेक्षो निरामिषः । आत्मनैव सहायेन यश्चरेत्स सुखी भवेत् ॥
data.md: That man who is pleased with his own Soul, who is given to Yoga, who depends upon nothing out of self, who is without cupidity, and who acts without the help of anything but his self, succeeds in acquiring happiness.

data.v: सुखदुःखविपर्यासो यदा समुपपद्यते । नैनं प्रज्ञा सुनीतं वा त्रायते नापि पौरुषम् ॥
data.md: Narada said When the changes of happiness and sorrow appear or disappear, they cannot be prevented by either wisdom or policy or exertion.

data.v: स्वभावाद्यत्नमातिष्ठेद्यत्नवान्नावसीदति । जरामरणरोगेभ्यः प्रियमात्मानमुद्धरेत् ॥
data.md: Without suffering himself to deviate from his true nature, one should try his best for protecting his own Self. He who makes such care and exertion, has never to to perish. Considering Self as something dear, one should always try to rescue himself from decrepitude death, and disease.

data.v: रुजन्ति हि शरीराणि रोगाः शारीरमानसाः । सायका इव तीक्ष्णाग्राः प्रयुक्ता दृढधन्विभिः ॥
data.md: Metal and physical ailments afflict the body, like keen-pointed arrows discharged from the bow by a strong bowman.

सोऽभिवाद्य महात्मानमृषिं द्वैपायनं मुनिम् । शुकः प्रदक्षिणीकृत्य कृष्णमापृष्टवान्मुनिः ॥
data.md: Obtaining Narada's permission, Shuka then went to where his father was. Arrived before him, the great Muni, viz., the great and Islandborn Krishna, Shuka circumambulated him and addressed him the usual enquiries.

data.v: श्रुत्वा ऋषिस्तद्वचनं शुकस्य; प्रीतो महात्मा पुनराह चैनम् । भो भोः पुत्र स्थीयतां तावदद्य; यावच्चक्षुः प्रीणयामि त्वदर्थम् ॥
data.md: Hearing of Shuka's intention, the great Rishi became highly pleased. Addressing him the great Rishi said,-0 son, O dear son, do you stay here to-day so that I may see you for some time for gratifying my eyes.

data.v: निरपेक्षः शुको भूत्वा निःस्नेहो मुक्तबन्धनः । मोक्षमेवानुसंचिन्त्य गमनाय मनो दधे । पितरं संपरित्यज्य जगाम द्विजसत्तमः ॥
data.md: Shuka, however, paid no heed to that request. Freed from affection and all doubt, he began to think only of Liberation, and set his heart on the journey.

data.v: गिरिपृष्ठं समारुह्य सुतो व्यासस्य भारत । समे देशे विविक्ते च निःशलाक उपाविशत् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said. Having got upon the summit of the mountain, O Bharata, the son of Vyasa sat down upon a level place free from blades of grass and secluded.

data.v: धारयामास चात्मानं यथाशास्त्रं महामुनिः । पादात्प्रभृति गात्रेषु क्रमेण क्रमयोगवित् ॥
data.md: According to the direction of the scriptures and to the ordinances laid down, that ascetic, who knew the successive processes of Yoga, held his soul first in one place and then in another, beginning from his feet and proceeding through all the limbs.

data.v: ततः स प्राङ्मुखो विद्वानादित्ये नचिरोदिते । पाणिपादं समाधाय विनीतवदुपाविशत् ॥
data.md: Then when the Sun, had not risen long, Shuka sat, with his face turned towards the East, and hands and feet drawn in an humble posture.

data.v: न तत्र पक्षिसंघातो न शब्दो नापि दर्शनम् । यत्र वैयासकिर्धीमान्योक्तुं समुपचक्रमे ॥
data.md: In that spot where the intelligent son of Vyasa sat prepared to practise Yoga, there were no flocks of birds, no sound, and no sight that was repulsive or fearful.

data.v: स ददर्श तदात्मानं सर्वसङ्गविनिःसृतम् । प्रजहास ततो हासं शुकः संप्रेक्ष्य भास्करम् ॥
data.md: He then saw his own Soul freed from all attachments. Seeing that highest of all things, he laughed in joy.

data.v: स पुनर्योगमास्थाय मोक्षमार्गोपलब्धये । महायोगीश्वरो भूत्वा सोऽत्यक्रामद्विहायसम् ॥
data.md: He once more set himself to Yoga for acquiring the path of Liberation. Becoming the great master of Yoga he got over the element of ether.

data.v: ततः प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा देवर्षिं नारदं तदा । निवेदयामास तदा स्वं योगं परमर्षये ॥
data.md: He then went round the celestial Rishi Naradas, and informed him of the fact of his having begun to practise the highest Yoga.

data.v: दृष्टो मार्गः प्रवृत्तोऽस्मि स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु तपोधन । त्वत्प्रसादाद्गमिष्यामि गतिमिष्टां महाद्युते ॥
data.md: I have succeeded in seeing the path (of Emancipation). I have addressed myself to it. Blessed be you, O you having penances for your wealth. I shall through your favour, O you of great splendour, acquire an end that is highly desirable.

data.v: नारदेनाभ्यनुज्ञातस्ततो द्वैपायनात्मजः । अभिवाद्य पुनर्योगमास्थायाकाशमाविशत् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Having received the order of Naradas, Shuka the son of the Island-born Vyasa saluted the celestial Rishi and once more set himself to Yoga and entered the element of ether.

data.v: कैलासपृष्ठादुत्पत्य स पपात दिवं तदा । अन्तरिक्षचरः श्रीमान्व्यासपुत्रः सुनिश्चितः ॥
data.md: Ascending then from the breast of the Kailasa mountain, he soared into the sky. Capable of passing through the sky, the blessed Shuka of fixed conclusion, then made himself at one with the element of Wind.

data.v: तमुद्यन्तं द्विजश्रेष्ठं वैनतेयसमद्युतिम् । ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि मनोमारुतरंहसम् ॥
data.md: As that foremost of twice-born ones, effulgent like Garuda, was passing through the skies with the speed of the wind or thought, all creatures directed their eyes towards him.

data.v: व्यवसायेन लोकांस्त्रीन्सर्वान्सोऽथ विचिन्तयन् । आस्थितो दिव्यमध्वानं पावकार्कसमप्रभः ॥
data.md: Gifted with the splendour of fire or the Sun, Shuka then considered the three worlds as one Brahma, and went along that lengthy path.

data.v: तमेकमनसं यान्तमव्यग्रमकुतोभयम् । ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि जङ्गमानीतराणि च ॥
data.md: Indeed, all creatures, mobile and immobile, cast their eyes upon him as he went with rapt attention, and a tranquil and fearless soul.

data.v: यथाशक्ति यथान्यायं पूजयां चक्रिरे तदा । पुष्पवर्षैश्च दिव्यैस्तमवचक्रुर्दिवौकसः ॥
data.md: All creatures, according to the ordinance and according to their power, adored him with respect. The celestials poured showers of celestial flowers upon him.

data.v: तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मिताः सर्वे गन्धर्वाप्सरसां गणाः । ऋषयश्चैव संसिद्धाः परं विस्मयमागताः ॥
data.md: Seeing hiin, all the tribes of Apsaras and Gandharvas became filled with wonder. The Rishis also, that were crowned with success, became equally surprised.

data.v: अन्तरिक्षचरः कोऽयं तपसा सिद्धिमागतः । अधःकायोर्ध्ववक्त्रश्च नेत्रैः समभिवाह्यते ॥
data.md: And they asked themselves,Who is this one who has acquired success by his penances? With looks withdrawn from his own body but turned upwards, he is delighting us all with his glances.

data.v: ततः परमधीरात्मा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः । भास्करं समुदीक्षन्स प्राङ्मुखो वाग्यतोऽगमत् । शब्देनाकाशमखिलं पूरयन्निव सर्वतः ॥
data.md: Of highly righteous soul and celebrated throughout the three worlds, Shuka went silently, his face turned towards the East and look directed towards the Sun. As he went, along he seemed to fill the entire sky with an all-pervading noise.

data.v: तमापतन्तं सहसा दृष्ट्वा सर्वाप्सरोगणाः । संभ्रान्तमनसो राजन्नासन्परमविस्मिताः । पञ्चचूडाप्रभृतयो भृशमुत्फुल्ललोचनाः ॥

data.v: दैवतं कतमं ह्येतदुत्तमां गतिमास्थितम् । सुनिश्चितमिहायाति विमुक्तमिव निःस्पृहम् ॥
data.md: Headed by Panchachuda and others, they looked at Shuka with eyes expanded by surprise. And they asked one one another, saying,-What god is this one who has acquired such a high end? Forsooth, he comes here, freed from all attachments and desire.

data.v: ततः समतिचक्राम मलयं नाम पर्वतम् । उर्वशी पूर्वचित्तिश्च यं नित्यमुपसेवते । ते स्म ब्रह्मर्षिपुत्रस्य विस्मयं ययतुः परम् ॥
data.md: Shuka then went to the Malaya mountains where Urvashi and Purvachitti used to always live.

data.v: अहो बुद्धिसमाधानं वेदाभ्यासरते द्विजे । अचिरेणैव कालेन नभश्चरति चन्द्रवत् । पितृशुश्रूषया सिद्धिं संप्राप्तोऽयमनुत्तमाम् ॥
data.md: Both of them, seeing the energy of the son of the great twice-born Rishi, became filled with wonder. And they said,-Wonderful is this concentration of attention of a twice-born youth who was accustomed to the recitation and study of the Vedas! Soon will he pass through the entire sky like the Moon. It was by dutiful service and humble ministrations towards his father that he gained this excellent understanding.

data.v: पितृभक्तो दृढतपाः पितुः सुदयितः सुतः । अनन्यमनसा तेन कथं पित्रा विवर्जितः ॥
data.md: He is firmly devoted his father, endued with austere penances, and is very much loved by his father. Alas, why has he been dismissed by his inattentive father to go along a way whence no one returns.

data.v: उर्वश्या वचनं श्रुत्वा शुकः परमधर्मवित् । उदैक्षत दिशः सर्वा वचने गतमानसः ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of Urvashi, and attending to their meaning, Shuk:a, that foremost of all persons conversant with duties, looked on all sides, and once more saw the entire sky, the whole Earth with her mountains and waters and forests, and also all the lakes and rivers.

data.v: सोऽन्तरिक्षं महीं चैव सशैलवनकाननाम् । आलोकयामास तदा सरांसि सरितस्तथा ॥
ततो द्वैपायनसुतं बहुमानपुरःसरम् । कृताञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वा निरीक्षन्ते स्म देवताः ॥
data.md: All the gods also, of both sexes, joining their hands, paid respect to the son of Island bonr Rishi and looked act him with wonder and reverence.

data.v: अब्रवीत्तास्तदा वाक्यं शुकः परमधर्मवित् । पिता यद्यनुगच्छेन्मां क्रोशमानः शुकेति वै ॥
data.md: Shuka, addressing all of them, that foremost of all pious men, said these words-If my father follow me and repeatedly call after me by my name, do all of you in a body return him an answer for me. Moved by the affection all of you have for me, do you satisfy this request of mine!

data.v: ततः प्रतिवचो देयं सर्वैरेव समाहितैः । एतन्मे स्नेहतः सर्वे वचनं कर्तुमर्हथ ॥
शुकस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा दिशः सवनकाननाः । समुद्राः सरितः शैलाः प्रत्यूचुस्तं समन्ततः ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of Shuka, all the points of the horizon, all the forests, all the seas, all the rivers, and all the mountains answered him from all sides, saying,.-We accept your command, O twice-born one! It shall be as you say! It is thus that we answer the words spoken by the Rishi.

data.v: यथाज्ञापयसे विप्र बाढमेवं भविष्यति । ऋषेर्व्याहरतो वाक्यं प्रतिवक्ष्यामहे वयम् ॥
इत्येवमुक्त्वा वचनं ब्रह्मर्षिः सुमहातपाः । प्रातिष्ठत शुकः सिद्धिं हित्वा लोकांश्चतुर्विधान् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said “Having spoken in this way, the twice-born Rishi of austere penances, viz., Shuka, lived on his success, renouncing the four sorts of faults.

data.v: तमो ह्यष्टविधं हित्वा जहौ पञ्चविधं रजः । ततः सत्त्वं जहौ धीमांस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥
data.md: Renouncing also the eight kinds of Tamas, he dismissed the five kinds of Rajas. Gifted with great intelligence, he the renounced the attribute of Sattva. All this seemed extremely wonderful.

data.v: ततस्तस्मिन्पदे नित्ये निर्गुणे लिङ्गवर्जिते । ब्रह्मणि प्रत्यतिष्ठत्स विधूमोऽग्निरिव ज्वलन् ॥
data.md: He then lived in that eternal station which is shorn of attributes, freed from every indication, that is, in Brahma, shining like a smokeless fire.

data.v: उल्कापाता दिशां दाहा भूमिकम्पास्तथैव च । प्रादुर्भूताः क्षणे तस्मिंस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥
data.md: Meteors began to shoot. The points of the horizon seemed to be ablaze. The Earth trembled. All these phenomena seemed extremely wonderful.

data.v: द्रुमाः शाखाश्च मुमुचुः शिखराणि च पर्वताः । निर्घातशब्दैश्च गिरिर्हिमवान्दीर्यतीव ह ॥
data.md: The trees began to throw off their branches and the mountains their summits. Loud peals were heard that seemed to rive the Himavat mountains.

data.v: न बभासे सहस्रांशुर्न जज्वाल च पावकः । ह्रदाश्च सरितश्चैव चुक्षुभुः सागरास्तथा ॥
data.md: The Sun seemed at that moment to be shorn of effulgence. Fire refused to burn forth. The lakes and rivers and seas were all moved.

data.v: ववर्ष वासवस्तोयं रसवच्च सुगन्धि च । ववौ समीरणश्चापि दिव्यगन्धवहः शुचिः ॥
data.md: Vasava poured showers of rain of excellent taste and smell. A pure breeze began to blow, carrying excellent taste and smell. A pure breeze began to blow, carrying excellent perfumes.

data.v: स शृङ्गेऽप्रतिमे दिव्ये हिमवन्मेरुसंभवे । संश्लिष्टे श्वेतपीते द्वे रुक्मरूप्यमये शुभे ॥
data.md: Shuka, as he went through the sky, saw two beautiful summits, one belonging to Himavat and another to Meru. These were side by side with each other. One of them was made of gold and was, therefore, yellow; the other was white, being made of silver.

data.v: शतयोजनविस्तारे तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च भारत । उदीचीं दिशमाश्रित्य रुचिरे संददर्श ह ॥
data.md: Each of them, O Bharata, was a hundred Yojanas in height and of the same breath. Indeed, as Shuka went towards the north, he beheld those two beautiful summits,

data.v: सोऽविशङ्केन मनसा तथैवाभ्यपतच्छुकः । ततः पर्वतशृङ्गे द्वे सहसैव द्विधाकृते । अदृश्येतां महाराज तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥
data.md: With a fearless heart he dashed against those two summits that were close to each other. Unable to bear the force, the summits were suddenly rent in two parts.

data.v: ततः पर्वतशृङ्गाभ्यां सहसैव विनिःसृतः । न च प्रतिजघानास्य स गतिं पर्वतोत्तमः ॥
data.md: The spectacle, O monarch, was extremely wonderful to look at. Shuka pierced through those summits, for they were unable to stop his onward course. At this a loud noise was made in heaven by the dwellers thereof.

data.v: ततो महानभूच्छब्दो दिवि सर्वदिवौकसाम् । गन्धर्वाणामृषीणां च ये च शैलनिवासिनः ॥
दृष्ट्वा शुकमतिक्रान्तं पर्वतं च द्विधाकृतम् । साधु साध्विति तत्रासीन्नादः सर्वत्र भारत ॥
data.md: The Gandharvas and the Rishis also and others who lived in that mountain sent up loud cheers at the sight of the mountain being rent in two and Shuka passing through it. Indeed, O Bharata, a loud noise was heard everywhere at that moment, saying,-Excellent, Excellent.

data.v: स पूज्यमानो देवैश्च गन्धर्वैरृषिभिस्तथा । यक्षराक्षससंघैश्च विद्याधरगणैस्तथा ॥
data.md: He was worshipped by the Gandharvas and the Rishis, by Yakhas and Rakshasas, and by all tribes of the Vidyadharas.

data.v: दिव्यैः पुष्पैः समाकीर्णमन्तरिक्षं समन्ततः । आसीत्किल महाराज शुकाभिपतने तदा ॥
data.md: The entire sky became covered with celestial flowers showered from heaven at that moment when Shuka thus cut through that impenetrable barrier, O king.

data.v: ततो मन्दाकिनीं रम्यामुपरिष्टादभिव्रजन् । शुको ददर्श धर्मात्मा पुष्पितद्रुमकाननाम् ॥
data.md: The pious Shuka then saw from a high region the extremely beautiful celestial river Mandakini, running below through a region adorned by many flowering groves and forests.

data.v: तस्यां क्रीडन्त्यभिरताः स्नान्ति चैवाप्सरोगणाः । शून्याकारं निराकाराः शुकं दृष्ट्वा विवाससः ॥
data.md: In these waters many beautiful Apsaras were playing. Seeing Shuka who was bodiless, those naked aerial beings felt no shame.

data.v: तं प्रक्रमन्तमाज्ञाय पिता स्नेहसमन्वितः । उत्तमां गतिमास्थाय पृष्ठतोऽनुससार ह ॥
data.md: Learning that Shuka had undertaken his great journey, his father Vyasa, filled with affection, followed him behind along the same aerial path.

data.v: शुकस्तु मारुतादूर्ध्वं गतिं कृत्वान्तरिक्षगाम् । दर्शयित्वा प्रभावं स्वं सर्वभूतोऽभवत्तदा ॥
data.md: Meanwhile Shuka, passing through thai region of the sky which is above the region of the wind, showed his Yoga-power and identified himself with Brahma.

data.v: महायोगगतिं त्वग्र्यां व्यासोत्थाय महातपाः । निमेषान्तरमात्रेण शुकाभिपतनं ययौ ॥
data.md: Following the subtile path of high Yoga, Vyasa of austere penances, reached within the twinkling of the eye that place whence Shuka first started.

data.v: स ददर्श द्विधा कृत्वा पर्वताग्रं शुकं गतम् । शशंसुरृषयस्तस्मै कर्म पुत्रस्य तत्तदा ॥
data.md: Proceeding along the same way, Vyasa saw the mountain summit rent in two parts and through which Shuka has passed. Meeting the Island-born ascetic, the Rishis began to describe to him the achievements of his own.

data.v: ततः शुकेति दीर्घेण शैक्षेणाक्रन्दितस्तदा । स्वयं पित्रा स्वरेणोच्चैस्त्रीँल्लोकाननुनाद्य वै ॥
data.md: Vyasa, however, began to lament, loudly naming his son and causing the three worlds to resound with the noise he made.

data.v: शुकः सर्वगतो भूत्वा सर्वात्मा सर्वतोमुखः । प्रत्यभाषत धर्मात्मा भोःशब्देनानुनादयन् ॥
data.md: Meanwhile, the pious Shuka, who had entered all things, had become the soul of all things, and had acquired omnipresence, answered his fathers by uttering the monosyllable BHO in the form of an echo.

data.v: तत एकाक्षरं नादं भो इत्येव समीरयन् । प्रत्याहरज्जगत्सर्वमुच्चैः स्थावरजङ्गमम् ॥
data.md: Thereat, the entire universe of mobile and immobile creatures, uttering the monosyllable BHO, echoed the answer of Shuka.

data.v: ततः प्रभृति चाद्यापि शब्दानुच्चारितान्पृथक् । गिरिगह्वरपृष्ठेषु व्याजहार शुकं प्रति ॥
data.md: Thereforward, when sounds are made in mountain-caves or on mountain-breasts, the latter, as if in answer to Shuka, still echo them.

data.v: अन्तर्हितः प्रभावं तु दर्शयित्वा शुकस्तदा । गुणान्संत्यज्य शब्दादीन्पदमध्यगमत्परम् ॥
data.md: Having renounced all the attributes of sound, etc., and showing his Yoga-power in the manner of his disappearance, Shuka in this way acquired the highest station.

data.v: महिमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा पुत्रस्यामिततेजसः । निषसाद गिरिप्रस्थे पुत्रमेवानुचिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: Seeing that glory and power of his son of immeasurable energy, Vyasa sat down on the breast of the mountain and began to think of his son sorrowfully.

data.v: ततो मन्दाकिनीतीरे क्रीडन्तोऽप्सरसां गणाः । आसाद्य तमृषिं सर्वाः संभ्रान्ता गतचेतसः ॥
data.md: Seeing the Rishi seated there, the Apsaras who were sporting on the banks of the celestial river Mandakini, became all moved with shame and dispirited.

data.v: जले निलिल्यिरे काश्चित्काश्चिद्गुल्मान्प्रपेदिरे । वसनान्याददुः काश्चिद्दृष्ट्वा तं मुनिसत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Some of them, to hide their nakedness, plunged into the river, and some entered the groves hard by, and some quickly took up their clothes, at seeing the Rishi.

data.v: तां मुक्ततां तु विज्ञाय मुनिः पुत्रस्य वै तदा । सक्ततामात्मनश्चैव प्रीतोऽभूद्व्रीडितश्च ह ॥
data.md: Seeing these movements, the Rishi understood that his son had been liberated from all attachments, but that he himself was not freed therefrom. At this he became filled with both joy and shame.

data.v: तं देवगन्धर्ववृतो महर्षिगणपूजितः । पिनाकहस्तो भगवानभ्यागच्छत शंकरः ॥
data.md: As Vyasa was seated there, the auspicious god Shiva, armed with trident, surrounded on all sides by many gods and Gandharvas and worshipped of all the great Rishis, came there.

data.v: तमुवाच महादेवः सान्त्वपूर्वमिदं वचः । पुत्रशोकाभिसंतप्तं कृष्णद्वैपायनं तदा ॥
data.md: Consoling the Island-born Rishi who was burning with grief on account of his son, Mahadeva said these words to him

data.v: अग्नेर्भूमेरपां वायोरन्तरिक्षस्य चैव ह । वीर्येण सदृशः पुत्रस्त्वया मत्तः पुरा वृतः ॥
data.md: The prayer he offered to the great God was,-~O powerful one, let me have a son that will have the might of Fire and Earth and Weather and Wind and Ether.

data.v: स तथालक्षणो जातस्तपसा तव संभृतः । मम चैव प्रभावेन ब्रह्मतेजोमयः शुचिः ॥
data.md: Procreated by your penances, the son that was born to you was of that very sort. Proceeding from my favour, he was pure and full of Brahma-energy.

data.v: स गतिं परमां प्राप्तो दुष्प्रापामजितेन्द्रियैः । दैवतैरपि विप्रर्षे तं त्वं किमनुशोचसि ॥
data.md: He has acquired the highest end-an end that is, which none can acquire who has not completely mastered his senses, nor by even any of the gods, why then, O twice-born Rishi, do you grieve for that son?

data.v: यावत्स्थास्यन्ति गिरयो यावत्स्थास्यन्ति सागराः । तावत्तवाक्षया कीर्तिः सपुत्रस्य भविष्यति ॥
data.md: As long as the hills will last, as long as the ocean will last, so long will the fame of your son continue.

data.v: छायां स्वपुत्रसदृशीं सर्वतोऽनपगां सदा । द्रक्ष्यसे त्वं च लोकेऽस्मिन्मत्प्रसादान्महामुने ॥
data.md: Through my favour, O great Rishi, you will see in this world a shadowy form resembling your son, moving by the side and never leaving you for a single moment!

data.v: सोऽनुनीतो भगवता स्वयं रुद्रेण भारत । छायां पश्यन्समावृत्तः स मुनिः परया मुदा ॥
data.md: Thus favoured by the illustrious Rudra himself, O Bharata, the Rishi saw a shadow of his son by his side. He came back from that place, filled with joy at this.

data.v: इति जन्म गतिश्चैव शुकस्य भरतर्षभ । विस्तरेण मयाख्यातं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि ॥
data.md: I have now told you, O chief of Bharata's race, everything regarding the birth and life of Shukra about which you had asked me.

data.v: एतदाचष्ट मे राजन्देवर्षिर्नारदः पुरा । व्यासश्चैव महायोगी संजल्पेषु पदे पदे ॥
data.md: The celestial Rishi Narada and the great Yogin Vyasa had again and again told all this to me in days of yore when the subject was suggested in course of conversation.

data.v: इतिहासमिमं पुण्यं मोक्षधर्मार्थसंहितम् । धारयेद्यः शमपरः स गच्छेत्परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: That person devoted to tranquillity who hears this sacred history directly connected with the subject of Liberation is sure to acquire the highest end.

data.v: गृहस्थो ब्रह्मचारी वा वानप्रस्थोऽथ भिक्षुकः । य इच्छेत्सिद्धिमास्थातुं देवतां कां यजेत सः ॥
data.md: If a man be a house-holder or Brahmacharin, a hermit or a mendicant, and if he wishes to acquire success, what god should he worship?

data.v: कुतो ह्यस्य ध्रुवः स्वर्गः कुतो निःश्रेयसं परम् । विधिना केन जुहुयाद्दैवं पित्र्यं तथैव च ॥
data.md: Whence can he surely acquire heaven and whence that which is of the highest benefit? According to what ordinances should he perform the Homa in honour of the gods and the departed manes?

data.v: मुक्तश्च कां गतिं गच्छेन्मोक्षश्चैव किमात्मकः । स्वर्गतश्चैव किं कुर्याद्येन न च्यवते दिवः ॥
data.md: What is the end to which one goes when he becomes Liberated? What is the essence of Liberation? What should one do, so that he, having attained to heaven, would not have to drop down thence?

data.v: देवतानां च को देवः पितॄणां च तथा पिता । तस्मात्परतरं यच्च तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Who is the God of the gods? And who is the Pitri of the Pitris? Who is He who is superior to him who is the God of the gods and the Pitri of the Pitris? Tell me all this, O Grandfather?"

data.v: गूढं मां प्रश्नवित्प्रश्नं पृच्छसे त्वमिहानघ । न ह्येष तर्कया शक्यो वक्तुं वर्षशतैरपि ॥
data.md: Bhishma said "O you who are well acquainted with the art of questioning, this question which you have put to me, O pure one, is one which is enveloped in deep mystery. One cannot answer it with the help of logic even if one were to try for a hundred years.

data.v: ऋते देवप्रसादाद्वा राजञ्ज्ञानागमेन वा । गहनं ह्येतदाख्यानं व्याख्यातव्यं तवारिहन् ॥
data.md: Without the favour of Narayana, O king, or an acquisition of high knowledge, this question of yours cannot be answered. Though this subject is filled with deep mystery, I shall yet, O destroyer of enemies, explain it to you?

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । नारदस्य च संवादमृषेर्नारायणस्य च ॥
data.md: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Narada and the Rishi Narayana.

data.v: नारायणो हि विश्वात्मा चतुर्मूर्तिः सनातनः । धर्मात्मजः संबभूव पितैवं मेऽभ्यभाषत ॥
data.md: I heard it from my father that in the golden age, O king, during the epoch of the Self-create Manu, the eternal Narayana, the Soul of the universe, was born as the son of Dharma in a quadrupie form, viz., as Nara, Narayana, Hari, and the Self-create Krishna.

data.v: कृते युगे महाराज पुरा स्वायंभुवेऽन्तरे । नरो नारायणश्चैव हरिः कृष्णस्तथैव च ॥
तेभ्यो नारायणनरौ तपस्तेपतुरव्ययौ । बदर्याश्रममासाद्य शकटे कनकामये ॥
data.md: Amongst them all, Narayana and Nara practised severest austerities by going to the Himalayan retreat known by the name of Vadari, and riding on their golden cars.

data.v: अष्टचक्रं हि तद्यानं भूतयुक्तं मनोरमम् । तत्राद्यौ लोकनाथौ तौ कृशौ धमनिसंततौ ॥
data.md: Each of those cars had eight wheels, and was made up of the five primal elements, and supremely beautiful. Those original regents of the world who had taken birth as the sons of Dharma, became extremely emaciated in body on account of the austerities they practised. Indeed, for those austerities and for their energy, the very gods were unable to look at them. Only that god to whom they were kind could see them.

data.v: तपसा तेजसा चैव दुर्निरीक्षौ सुरैरपि । यस्य प्रसादं कुर्वाते स देवौ द्रष्टुमर्हति ॥
data.md: Each of those cars had eight wheels, and was made up of the five primal elements, and supremely beautiful. Those original regents of the world who had taken birth as the sons of Dharma, became extremely emaciated in body on account of the austerities they practised. Indeed, for those austerities and for their energy, the very gods were unable to look at them. Only that god to whom they were kind could see them.

data.v: नूनं तयोरनुमते हृदि हृच्छयचोदितः । महामेरोर्गिरेः शृङ्गात्प्रच्युतो गन्धमादनम् ॥
data.md: Forsooth, with his heart given to them, and moved by a longing desire to see them, Narada dropped down on Gandhamadana from a summit of the high mountains of Meru and walked over all the world.

data.v: नारदः सुमहद्भूतं लोकान्सर्वानचीचरत् । तं देशमगमद्राजन्बदर्याश्रममाशुगः ॥
data.md: Endued with great speed, he at last went to that spot whereon was situate the retreat of Vadari. Moved by curiosity he entered that retreat at the hour of Nara's and Narayana's performing their daily rites.

data.v: तयोराह्निकवेलायां तस्य कौतूहलं त्वभूत् । इदं तदास्पदं कृत्स्नं यस्मिँल्लोकाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥
data.md: He said to himself,-This is truly the retreat of that Being in whom are placed all the worlds including the gods, the Asuras, the Gandharvas, the Kinnaras, and the great snakes.

data.v: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वाः सर्षिकिंनरलेलिहाः । एका मूर्तिरियं पूर्वं जाता भूयश्चतुर्विधा ॥
धर्मस्य कुलसंतानो महानेभिर्विवर्धितः । अहो ह्यनुगृहीतोऽद्य धर्म एभिः सुरैरिह । नरनारायणाभ्यां च कृष्णेन हरिणा तथा ॥
data.md: How wonderful it is that Dharma has thus been honoured by these four great gods, viz., Nara, Narayana, Krishna and Hari.

data.v: तत्र कृष्णो हरिश्चैव कस्मिंश्चित्कारणान्तरे । स्थितौ धर्मोत्तरौ ह्येतौ तथा तपसि धिष्ठितौ ॥
data.md: In this spot Krishna and Hari lived formerly. The other two, however, viz., Nara and Narayana, are now living here performing penances for the object of increasing their merit.

data.v: एतौ हि परमं धाम कानयोराह्निकक्रिया । पितरौ सर्वभूतानां दैवतं च यशस्विनौ । कां देवतां नु यजतः पितॄन्वा कान्महामती ॥
data.md: These two are the highest refuge of the universe. What can be the nature of the daily rites these two perform? They are the fathers of all creatures and the illustrious gods of all beings. Gifted with great intelligence, what is that god whom these two adore? Who are those Pitris whom these two Pitris of all beings worship.

data.v: इति संचिन्त्य मनसा भक्त्या नारायणस्य ह । सहसा प्रादुरभवत्समीपे देवयोस्तदा ॥
data.md: Thinking of this mentally, and filled with devotion towards Narayana, Narada suddenly appeared before those two gods.

data.v: कृते दैवे च पित्र्ये च ततस्ताभ्यां निरीक्षितः । पूजितश्चैव विधिना यथाप्रोक्तेन शास्त्रतः ॥
data.md: After those two gods had finished their adorations to their deities and the Rishis, they looked at the celestial Rishi arrived at their asylum. The latter was honoured with those eternal rites that are laid down in their scriptures.

data.v: तं दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यमपूर्वं विधिविस्तरम् । उपोपविष्टः सुप्रीतो नारदो भगवानृषिः ॥
data.md: Seeing that extraordinary conduct of the two original gods in themselves adoring other deities and Pitris, the illustrious Rishi Narada took his seat there, well pleased with the honours he had received.

data.v: नारायणं संनिरीक्ष्य प्रसन्नेनान्तरात्मना । नमस्कृत्वा महादेवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: With a cheerful soul he looked at Narayana, and bowing to Mahadeva he said these words.

data.v: वेदेषु सपुराणेषु साङ्गोपाङ्गेषु गीयसे । त्वमजः शाश्वतो धाता मतोऽमृतमनुत्तमम् । प्रतिष्ठितं भूतभव्यं त्वयि सर्वमिदं जगत् ॥
data.md: In the Vedas and the Puranas in the auxiliary and sub-auxiliary treaties, you are sung with respect! You are unborn and eternal! you are the Creator! You are the mother of the universe! You are the embodiment of Immortality and you are the foremost of all things. The Past and the Future, indeed, the entire universe has been placed on you.

data.v: चत्वारो ह्याश्रमा देव सर्वे गार्हस्थ्यमूलकाः । यजन्ते त्वामहरहर्नानामूर्तिसमास्थितम् ॥
data.md: The four modes of life,olord, of which the domestic is the first, continually sacrifice to you who are of diverse forms.

data.v: पिता माता च सर्वस्य जगतः शाश्वतो गुरुः । कं त्वद्य यजसे देवं पितरं कं न विद्महे ॥
data.md: You are the father and the mother and the eternal preceptor of the universe. We know not who is that god or that Pitri to whom you are sacrificing to-day.

data.v: अवाच्यमेतद्वक्तव्यमात्मगुह्यं सनातनम् । तव भक्तिमतो ब्रह्मन्वक्ष्यामि तु यथातथम् ॥
data.md: This topic is one regarding which nothing should be said. It is an ancient ministry. Your devotion to me is very great. Hence, O twiceborn one, I shall describe it to you according to the truth.

data.v: यत्तत्सूक्ष्ममविज्ञेयमव्यक्तमचलं ध्रुवम् । इन्द्रियैरिन्द्रियार्थैश्च सर्वभूतैश्च वर्जितम् ॥
data.md: That which is minute, which is inconceivable, unmanifest, immobile, durable dissociated from the senses and the objects of the senses, as well as the (five) elements,—that is called the in-dwelling Soul of all existent creatures. That is known by the name of Kshetrajna. Transcending the three qualities of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas, that is regarded as Purusha in the scriptures.

data.v: स ह्यन्तरात्मा भूतानां क्षेत्रज्ञश्चेति कथ्यते । त्रिगुणव्यतिरिक्तोऽसौ पुरुषश्चेति कल्पितः । तस्मादव्यक्तमुत्पन्नं त्रिगुणं द्विजसत्तम ॥
अव्यक्ता व्यक्तभावस्था या सा प्रकृतिरव्यया । तां योनिमावयोर्विद्धि योऽसौ सदसदात्मकः । आवाभ्यां पूज्यतेऽसौ हि दैवे पित्र्ये च कल्पिते ॥
data.md: Know that from her we two have originated. That all-pervading Soul, which is made of all existent and non-existent things, is worshipped by us. Even He is what we adore in all those rites that we perform in honour of the gods and the departed manes.

data.v: नास्ति तस्मात्परोऽन्यो हि पिता देवोऽथ वा द्विजः । आत्मा हि नौ स विज्ञेयस्ततस्तं पूजयावहे ॥
data.md: There is no higher god, or father than He, O twice-born one! He should be known as our Soul. It is Him that we adore.

data.v: तेनैषा प्रथिता ब्रह्मन्मर्यादा लोकभाविनी । दैवं पित्र्यं च कर्तव्यमिति तस्यानुशासनम् ॥
data.md: This course of duties followed by men has, O twice-born one, been laid down by Him. It is his ordinance that we should duly perform all the rites laid down regarding the gods and the departed manes.

data.v: ब्रह्मा स्थाणुर्मनुर्दक्षो भृगुर्धर्मस्तपो दमः । मरीचिरङ्गिरात्रिश्च पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः ॥
वसिष्ठः परमेष्ठी च विवस्वान्सोम एव च । कर्दमश्चापि यः प्रोक्तः क्रोधो विक्रीत एव च ॥
एकविंशतिरुत्पन्नास्ते प्रजापतयः स्मृताः । तस्य देवस्य मर्यादां पूजयन्ति सनातनीम् ॥
दैवं पित्र्यं च सततं तस्य विज्ञाय तत्त्वतः । आत्मप्राप्तानि च ततो जानन्ति द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
data.md: Observing all the rites, in full, that were laid down in honor of the gods and the departed manes, all those foremost of twice-born ones acquired all those objects which they sought.

data.v: स्वर्गस्था अपि ये केचित्तं नमस्यन्ति देहिनः । ते तत्प्रसादाद्गच्छन्ति तेनादिष्टफलां गतिम् ॥
data.md: The bodiless dwellers of heaven, itself bow to that Supreme God and through His favour they acquire those fruits and that end which he ordains for them.

data.v: ये हीनाः सप्तदशभिर्गुणैः कर्मभिरेव च । कलाः पञ्चदश त्यक्त्वा ते मुक्ता इति निश्चयः ॥
data.md: This is the injunction of the scriptures that those persons who are freed from these seventeen attributes, who have renounced all facts, and who are divested of the fifteen elements which form the gross body, are said to be Liberated.

data.v: मुक्तानां तु गतिर्ब्रह्मन्क्षेत्रज्ञ इति कल्पितः । स हि सर्वगतश्चैव निर्गुणश्चैव कथ्यते ॥
data.md: The ultimate end of the Liberated is called by the name of Kshetrajna. He is considered as both possessed of, and freed from, all the attributes.

data.v: दृश्यते ज्ञानयोगेन आवां च प्रसृतौ ततः । एवं ज्ञात्वा तमात्मानं पूजयावः सनातनम् ॥
data.md: He can be apprehended by knowledge alone. We two have originated from Him. Knowing him in that way, we worship that eternal soul of all things.

data.v: तं वेदाश्चाश्रमाश्चैव नानातनुसमास्थिताः । भक्त्या संपूजयन्त्याद्यं गतिं चैषां ददाति सः ॥
data.md: The Vedas and all the modes of life, though marked by diversities of opinion, all adore Him with devotion. It is he who, inclined to show favour, confers on them high ends fraught with happiness.

data.v: ये तु तद्भाविता लोके एकान्तित्वं समास्थिताः । एतदभ्यधिकं तेषां यत्ते तं प्रविशन्त्युत ॥
data.md: Those persons in this world who, filled with His spirit, become fully and conclusively devoted to him, acquire much higher end, for they succed in entering Him and becoming merged in his self.

data.v: इति गुह्यसमुद्देशस्तव नारद कीर्तितः । भक्त्या प्रेम्णा च विप्रर्षे अस्मद्भक्त्या च ते श्रुतः ॥
data.md: I have now, O Narada, described to you what is highly mysterious, moved by the live I bear for you four devotion to me. Indeed, on account of that devotion which you profess towards me, you have succeeded in listening to this my discourse.

data.v: स एवमुक्तो द्विपदां वरिष्ठो; नारायणेनोत्तमपूरुषेण । जगाद वाक्यं द्विपदां वरिष्ठं; नारायणं लोकहिताधिवासम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said "Addressed by Narayana, that foremost of beings, in these words, Narada, the foremost of men, then said these words to Narayana for the behoof of the world.

data.v: यदर्थमात्मप्रभवेह जन्म; तवोत्तमं धर्मगृहे चतुर्धा । तत्साध्यतां लोकहितार्थमद्य; गच्छामि द्रष्टुं प्रकृतिं तवाद्याम् ॥
data.md: Narada said Let that object be fulfilled for which you, O Self-born Being, have taken birth in four forms in the house of Dharma! I shall now go for seeing your original nature.

data.v: वेदाः स्वधीता मम लोकनाथ; तप्तं तपो नानृतमुक्तपूर्वम् । पूजां गुरूणां सततं करोमि; परस्य गुह्यं न च भिन्नपूर्वम् ॥
गुप्तानि चत्वारि यथागमं मे; शत्रौ च मित्रे च समोऽस्मि नित्यम् । तं चादिदेवं सततं प्रपन्न; एकान्तभावेन वृणोम्यजस्रम् । एभिर्विशेषैः परिशुद्धसत्त्वः; कस्मान्न पश्येयमनन्तमीशम् ॥
data.md: As laid down in the scriptures, I have always protected the four that should be protected. I always treat impartially friends and enemies. Wholly and surely given to Him, that first of gods, viz., the Supreme Soul, I incessantly worship Him.

data.v: तत्पारमेष्ठ्यस्य वचो निशम्य; नारायणः सात्वतधर्मगोप्ता । गच्छेति तं नारदमुक्तवान्स; संपूजयित्वात्मविधिक्रियाभिः ॥
ततो विसृष्टः परमेष्ठिपुत्रः; सोऽभ्यर्चयित्वा तमृषिं पुराणम् । खमुत्पपातोत्तमवेगयुक्त;स्ततोऽधिमेरौ सहसा निलिल्ये ॥
तत्रावतस्थे च मुनिर्मुहूर्त;मेकान्तमासाद्य गिरेः स शृङ्गे । आलोकयन्नुत्तरपश्चिमेन; ददर्श चात्यद्भुतरूपयुक्तम् ॥
क्षीरोदधेरुत्तरतो हि द्वीपः; श्वेतः स नाम्ना प्रथितो विशालः । मेरोः सहस्रैः स हि योजनानां; द्वात्रिंशतोर्ध्वं कविभिर्निरुक्तः ॥
अतीन्द्रियाश्चानशनाश्च तत्र; निष्पन्दहीनाः सुसुगन्धिनश्च । श्वेताः पुमांसो गतसर्वपापा;श्चक्षुर्मुषः पापकृतां नराणाम् ॥
वज्रास्थिकायाः सममानोन्माना; दिव्यान्वयरूपाः शुभसारोपेताः । छत्राकृतिशीर्षा मेघौघनिनादाः; सत्पुष्करचतुष्का राजीवशतपादाः ॥
षष्ट्या दन्तैर्युक्ताः शुक्लै;रष्टाभिर्दंष्ट्राभिर्ये । जिह्वाभिर्ये विष्वग्वक्त्रं; लेलिह्यन्ते सूर्यप्रख्यम् ॥
data.md: Their heads seem to be like umbrellas. Their voices are deep like that of the clouds. Each of them have four testes. The soles of their feet have hundreds of lines. They had sixty white teeth, and eight small ones. They had many tongues. With those tongues they seemed to lick the very Sun whose face is turned towards all sides.

data.v: भक्त्या देवं विश्वोत्पन्नं; यस्मात्सर्वे लोकाः सूताः । वेदा धर्मा मुनयः शान्ता; देवाः सर्वे तस्य विसर्गाः ॥
data.md: Indeed, they seemed to be capable of devouring that great god from whom has originated the entire universe, the Vedas, the duties, and the ascetics possessing the quality of tranquillity.

data.v: अतीन्द्रिया निराहारा अनिष्पन्दाः सुगन्धिनः । कथं ते पुरुषा जाताः का तेषां गतिरुत्तमा ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said are “O grand-father, you have said that those beings have no senses, that they do not eat anything for maintaining their lives; that their eyes are winkless, and that they always emit excellent perfumes. I ask, how were they born? What also is the superior end which they acquire?

data.v: ये विमुक्ता भवन्तीह नरा भरतसत्तम । तेषां लक्षणमेतद्धि यच्छ्वेतद्वीपवासिनाम् ॥
data.md: O chief of Bharata's race, the characteristics of those men that become liberated the same as those by which the inhabitants of the White Island are distinguished?

data.v: तस्मान्मे संशयं छिन्धि परं कौतूहलं हि मे । त्वं हि सर्वकथारामस्त्वां चैवोपाश्रिता वयम् ॥
data.md: Do you remove my doubts! The curiosity I feel is very great. You are the repository of all histories and narratives. As regards ourselves, we entirely depend on you for knowledge and instruction.

data.v: विस्तीर्णैषा कथा राजञ्श्रुता मे पितृसंनिधौ । सैषा तव हि वक्तव्या कथासारो हि स स्मृतः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said "This narrative, O king, which I have heard from my father, is extensive. I shall now recite it to you. Indeed, it is considered as the cream of all narratives.

data.v: राजोपरिचरो नाम बभूवाधिपतिर्भुवः । आखण्डलसखः ख्यातो भक्तो नारायणं हरिम् ॥
data.md: There was, in days of yore, a king on Earth, Uparichara, by name. He was known to be the friend, of Indra the king of gods. He was devoted to Narayana called also by the name of Hari.

data.v: धार्मिको नित्यभक्तश्च पितॄन्नित्यमतन्द्रितः । साम्राज्यं तेन संप्राप्तं नारायणवरात्पुरा ॥
data.md: He used to discharge all the duties laid down in the scriptures. Ever devoted to his father, was always ready for action. He acquired sovereignty of the world on account of a boon he had obtained from Narayana.

data.v: सात्वतं विधिमास्थाय प्राक्सूर्यमुखनिःसृतम् । पूजयामास देवेशं तच्छेषेण पितामहान् ॥
data.md: Following the Satvata ritual that had been declared in days of yore by the Sun himself, king Uparichara used to adore the God of gods, and after his worship was over, to adore the Grandfather of the universe.

data.v: पितृशेषेण विप्रांश्च संविभज्याश्रितांश्च सः । शेषान्नभुक्सत्यपरः सर्वभूतेष्वहिंसकः । सर्वभावेन भक्तः स देवदेवं जनार्दनम् ॥
data.md: After adoring the departed manes, he adored the Brahmanas. He then divided the offerings among those who depended on him. With the remnant after serving those, the king satisfied his own hunger. Given to truth, the king abstained from doing any injury to any creature.

data.v: तस्य नारायणे भक्तिं वहतोऽमित्रकर्शन । एकशय्यासनं शक्रो दत्तवान्देवराट्स्वयम् ॥
data.md: Seeing the devotion to Narayana of that destroyer of foes, the divine king of the gods himself shared with him his own seat and bed.

data.v: आत्मा राज्यं धनं चैव कलत्रं वाहनानि च । एतद्भगवते सर्वमिति तत्प्रेक्षितं सदा ॥
data.md: His kingdom and riches and wives and animals were all considered by him as obtained from Narayana. He, therefore, offered all his belongings to that great god.

data.v: काम्यनैमित्तिकाजस्रं यज्ञियाः परमक्रियाः । सर्वाः सात्वतमास्थाय विधिं चक्रे समाहितः ॥
data.md: Adopting the Satvata ritual, king Uparichara, with concentrated soul, used to perform all his sacrificial acts and observances, both optional and obligatory.

data.v: पञ्चरात्रविदो मुख्यास्तस्य गेहे महात्मनः । प्रायणं भगवत्प्रोक्तं भुञ्जते चाग्रभोजनम् ॥
data.md: Many foremost Brahmanas, well conversant with the Pancharatra ritual, used to eat before all others the food offered to the god Narayana in the palace of that illustrious king.

data.v: तस्य प्रशासतो राज्यं धर्मेणामित्रघातिनः । नानृता वाक्समभवन्मनो दुष्टं न चाभवत् । न च कायेन कृतवान्स पापं परमण्वपि ॥
data.md: As long as that destroyer of enemies continued to rule his kingdom piously, no falsehood ever escaped his lips and no evil thought ever entered his mind.

data.v: ये हि ते मुनयः ख्याताः सप्त चित्रशिखण्डिनः । तैरेकमतिभिर्भूत्वा यत्प्रोक्तं शास्त्रमुत्तमम् ॥
मरीचिरत्र्यङ्गिरसौ पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः । वसिष्ठश्च महातेजा एते चित्रशिखण्डिनः ॥
सप्त प्रकृतयो ह्येतास्तथा स्वायंभुवोऽष्टमः । एताभिर्धार्यते लोकस्ताभ्यः शास्त्रं विनिःसृतम् ॥
एकाग्रमनसो दान्ता मुनयः संयमे रताः । इदं श्रेय इदं ब्रह्म इदं हितमनुत्तमम् । लोकान्संचिन्त्य मनसा ततः शास्त्रं प्रचक्रिरे ॥
data.md: This is good, This is Brahma,—-This is highly beneficial,-reflecting thus in their minds, those Rishis created the worlds, and the science of morality and duty that governs those worlds.

data.v: तत्र धर्मार्थकामा हि मोक्षः पश्चाच्च कीर्तितः । मर्यादा विविधाश्चैव दिवि भूमौ च संस्थिताः ॥
data.md: In that work the authors discoursed on Religion and Profit and Pleasure, and subsequently on Liberation also. The various restrictions and limitations were also laid down in it for the Earth as also for Heaven.

data.v: आराध्य तपसा देवं हरिं नारायणं प्रभुम् । दिव्यं वर्षसहस्रं वै सर्वे ते ऋषिभिः सह ॥
data.md: They wrote that work after having adored with penances the powerful and illustrious Narayana called also Hari, for a thousand divine years, in company with many other Rishis.

data.v: नारायणानुशास्ता हि तदा देवी सरस्वती । विवेश तानृषीन्सर्वाँल्लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
data.md: Pleased with their penances and adoration, Narayana ordered the goddess of speech, viz., Sarasvati, to enter into the bodies of those Rishis. The goddess, for the behoof of the worlds, did what she ordered.

data.v: ततः प्रवर्तिता सम्यक्तपोविद्भिर्द्विजातिभिः । शब्दे चार्थे च हेतौ च एषा प्रथमसर्गजा ॥
data.md: On account of the entrance of the goddess of speech into their bodies, those Rishis, well conversant with penances, succeeded in composing that foremost of works in respect of words, senses and reason.

data.v: आदावेव हि तच्छास्त्रमोंकारस्वरभूषितम् । ऋषिभिर्भावितं तत्र यत्र कारुणिको ह्यसौ ॥
data.md: Having composed that work sanctified with the syllable OM, the Rishis first of all read it to Narayana, who heard them from kindness.

data.v: ततः प्रसन्नो भगवाननिर्दिष्टशरीरगः । ऋषीनुवाच तान्सर्वानदृश्यः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
data.md: The illustrious and bodiless Narayana became highly pleased with what he heard. That foremost of all Beings then addressed those Rishis in an incorporeal voice and said,-Excellent is this work that you have composed containing a hundred thousand verses. The duties and observances of all the worlds will originate from this your work.

data.v: कृतं शतसहस्रं हि श्लोकानामिदमुत्तमम् । लोकतन्त्रस्य कृत्स्नस्य यस्माद्धर्मः प्रवर्तते ॥
data.md: The illustrious and bodiless Narayana became highly pleased with what he heard. That foremost of all Beings then addressed those Rishis in an incorporeal voice and said,-Excellent is this work that you have composed containing a hundred thousand verses. The duties and observances of all the worlds will originate from this your work.

data.v: प्रवृत्तौ च निवृत्तौ च योनिरेतद्भविष्यति । ऋग्यजुःसामभिर्जुष्टमथर्वाङ्गिरसैस्तथा ॥
data.md: Perfectly following the four Vedas, viz., the Yajushes, the Richs, the Samans, and the Atharvans of Angiras, this work of yours will be an authority in all the worlds with regard to both Work and Renunciation.

data.v: तथा प्रमाणं हि मया कृतो ब्रह्मा प्रसादजः । रुद्रश्च क्रोधजो विप्रा यूयं प्रकृतयस्तथा ॥
data.md: According to the authority of the scriptures I have created Brahman from the attribute of Grace, Rudra from my anger, and yourselves, ye Brahmanas, as representing the elements.

data.v: सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ वायुर्भूमिरापोऽग्निरेव च । सर्वे च नक्षत्रगणा यच्च भूताभिशब्दितम् ॥
अधिकारेषु वर्तन्ते यथास्वं ब्रह्मवादिनः । सर्वे प्रमाणं हि यथा तथैतच्छास्त्रमुत्तमम् ॥
भविष्यति प्रमाणं वै एतन्मदनुशासनम् । अस्मात्प्रवक्ष्यते धर्मान्मनुः स्वायंभुवः स्वयम् ॥
उशना बृहस्पतिश्चैव यदोत्पन्नौ भविष्यतः । तदा प्रवक्ष्यतः शास्त्रं युष्मन्मतिभिरुद्धृतम् ॥
data.md: When Ushanas and Brihaspati will be born, they also will promulgate their respective work on morality and religion, guided by and quoting from this your work.

data.v: स्वायंभुवेषु धर्मेषु शास्त्रे चोशनसा कृते । बृहस्पतिमते चैव लोकेषु प्रविचारिते ॥
युष्मत्कृतमिदं शास्त्रं प्रजापालो वसुस्ततः । बृहस्पतिसकाशाद्वै प्राप्स्यते द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
data.md: After the publication of his work by the Self-born Manu and of that by Ushanas, and after the publication of the work also by Brihaspati, this science composed by you will be acquired by king Vasu. Indeed, you foremost of twice-born ones, that king will acquire this knowledge of this work from Brihaspati.

data.v: स हि मद्भावितो राजा मद्भक्तश्च भविष्यति । तेन शास्त्रेण लोकेषु क्रियाः सर्वाः करिष्यति ॥
data.md: Filled with all good thoughts, that king will become deeply devoted to me. Guided by this work, he will perform all his religious deeds and observance.

data.v: एतद्धि सर्वशास्त्राणां शास्त्रमुत्तमसंज्ञितम् । एतदर्थ्यं च धर्म्यं च यशस्यं चैतदुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: Verily, this work composed by you will be the foremost of all works on morality and religion. Excellent as it is, this work is full of instructions for acquiring both Riches and Religious merit, and is full of mysteries.

data.v: अस्य प्रवर्तनाच्चैव प्रजावन्तो भविष्यथ । स च राजा श्रिया युक्तो भविष्यति महान्वसुः ॥
data.md: For the publication of this treatise, you will be progenitors of an extensive family! King Uparichara also will become endued with greatness and prosperity.

data.v: संस्थिते तु नृपे तस्मिञ्शास्त्रमेतत्सनातनम् । अन्तर्धास्यति तत्सत्यमेतद्वः कथितं मया ॥
data.md: Upon the death, however, of that king, this eternal work will disappear from the world. I all this.

data.v: एतावदुक्त्वा वचनमदृश्यः पुरुषोत्तमः । विसृज्य तानृषीन्सर्वान्कामपि प्रस्थितो दिशम् ॥
data.md: Having said these words to all those Rishis, the invisible Narayana left them and went to some place that was not known to them.

data.v: ततस्ते लोकपितरः सर्वलोकार्थचिन्तकाः । प्रावर्तयन्त तच्छास्त्रं धर्मयोनिं सनातनम् ॥
data.md: Then those progenitors of the world, those Rishis who conferred their thoughts on the worldly ends, duly promulgated that work which is the eternal origin of all duties and observances.

data.v: उत्पन्नेऽऽङ्गिरसे चैव युगे प्रथमकल्पिते । साङ्गोपनिषदं शास्त्रं स्थापयित्वा बृहस्पतौ ॥
data.md: Subsequently, when Brihaspati was born in Angiras's family in the golden age, those seven Rishis charged him with the task of tell you promulgating their work which was consistent with the Upanishads and the several branches of the Vedas.

data.v: जग्मुर्यथेप्सितं देशं तपसे कृतनिश्चयाः । धारणात्सर्वलोकानां सर्वधर्मप्रवर्तकाः ॥
data.md: The themselves who were upholders of the universe and the first promulgators of duties and religious observances, then went to the place they chose, determined to practise penances."

data.v: ततोऽतीते महाकल्पे उत्पन्नेऽङ्गिरसः सुते । बभूवुर्निर्वृता देवा जाते देवपुरोहिते ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Then, upon the expiration of the great cycle, when the celestial priest Brihaspati was born in the family of Angiras, all the gods became very happy.

data.v: बृहद्ब्रह्म महच्चेति शब्दाः पर्यायवाचकाः । एभिः समन्वितो राजन्गुणैर्विद्वान्बृहस्पतिः ॥
data.md: The words Vrihat, Brahma, and Mahat all carry the same significance. The celestial priest, O king, came to be called Brihaspati because he was gifted with all these accomplishments.

data.v: तस्य शिष्यो बभूवाग्र्यो राजोपरिचरो वसुः । अधीतवांस्तदा शास्त्रं सम्यक्चित्रशिखण्डिजम् ॥
data.md: King Uparichara, otherwise called Vasu, became a disciple of Brihaspati and soon became the greatest of his disciples. Admitted as such, he began of study from his preceptor that science which was composed by the seven Rishis who were known by the name of Chitrashikhandins.

data.v: स राजा भावितः पूर्वं दैवेन विधिना वसुः । पालयामास पृथिवीं दिवमाखण्डलो यथा ॥
data.md: With soul purified by sacrifices and other religious rites, he governed the Earth like Indra ruling the Heaven.

data.v: तस्य यज्ञो महानासीदश्वमेधो महात्मनः । बृहस्पतिरुपाध्यायस्तत्र होता बभूव ह ॥
data.md: The illustrious king celebrated a great Horse-sacrifice in which his preceptor Brihaspati became the priest offering libation.

data.v: प्रजापतिसुताश्चात्र सदस्यास्त्वभवंस्त्रयः । एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितश्चैव महर्षयः ॥
धनुषाक्षोऽथ रैभ्यश्च अर्वावसुपरावसू । ऋषिर्मेधातिथिश्चैव ताण्ड्यश्चैव महानृषिः ॥
ऋषिः शक्तिर्महाभागस्तथा वेदशिराश्च यः । कपिलश्च ऋषिश्रेष्ठः शालिहोत्रपितामहः ॥
आद्यः कठस्तैत्तिरिश्च वैशंपायनपूर्वजः । कण्वोऽथ देवहोत्रश्च एते षोडश कीर्तिताः । संभृताः सर्वसंभारास्तस्मिन्राजन्महाक्रतौ ॥
न तत्र पशुघातोऽभूत्स राजैवं स्थितोऽभवत् । अहिंस्रः शुचिरक्षुद्रो निराशीः कर्मसंस्तुतः । आरण्यकपदोद्गीता भागास्तत्रोपकल्पिताः ॥
data.md: He was full of mercy. Of pure and liberal mind, he had renounced all desire, and was well-conversant with all rites. The necessary articles of that sacrifice were the productions of the forest.

data.v: प्रीतस्ततोऽस्य भगवान्देवदेवः पुरातनः । साक्षात्तं दर्शयामास सोऽदृश्योऽन्येन केनचित् ॥
data.md: The ancient God of gods (viz., Hari), became highly pleased with the king on account of that sacrifice. Incapable of being seen by any one else, the great God appeared before his worshipper.

data.v: स्वयं भागमुपाघ्राय पुरोडाशं गृहीतवान् । अदृश्येन हृतो भागो देवेन हरिमेधसा ॥
data.md: Accepting by taking its scent, the share offered to him he himself took up the Purodasha (clarified butter with cakes of powdered barley). The great God took up the offerings without being seen by any one.

data.v: बृहस्पतिस्ततः क्रुद्धः स्रुवमुद्यम्य वेगितः । आकाशं घ्नन्स्रुवः पातै रोषादश्रूण्यवर्तयत् ॥
data.md: At this, Brihaspati became angry. Taking up the ladle he hurled it violently at the sky, and began to shed tears in anger.

data.v: उवाच चोपरिचरं मया भागोऽयमुद्यतः । ग्राह्यः स्वयं हि देवेन मत्प्रत्यक्षं न संशयः ॥
data.md: Addressing king Uparichara he said,-Here, I place this as Narayana's share of the sacrificial offerings! Forsooth, he shall take it before my eyes.

data.v: उद्यता यज्ञभागा हि साक्षात्प्राप्ताः सुरैरिह । किमर्थमिह न प्राप्तो दर्शनं स हरिर्विभुः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said In the great sacrifice of Uparichara, all the gods appeared in their respective forms for partaking of the sacrificial offerings and were seen by all. Why is it that the powerful Hari only acted otherwise by invisibly taking his share?

data.v: ततः स तं समुद्धूतं भूमिपालो महान्वसुः । प्रसादयामास मुनिं सदस्यास्ते च सर्वशः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said When Brihaspati yielded to anger, the great king Vasu and all his Sadasyas sought to pacify the great Rishi.

data.v: ऊचुश्चैनमसंभ्रान्ता न रोषं कर्तुमर्हसि । नैष धर्मः कृतयुगे यस्त्वं रोषमचीकृथाः ॥
data.md: With cool heads, all of them said to Brihaspati,-You should not yield to anger. In this golden age, this anger to which you have yielded should not be the characteristic of any one.

data.v: अरोषणो ह्यसौ देवो यस्य भागोऽयमुद्यतः । न स शक्यस्त्वया द्रष्टुमस्माभिर्वा बृहस्पते । यस्य प्रसादं कुरुते स वै तं द्रष्टुमर्हति ॥
data.md: The great god for whom the share of the sacrificial offerings was designed by you, is himself free from anger! He is incapable of being seen either by ourselves or by you, O Brihaspati.

data.v: वयं हि ब्रह्मणः पुत्रा मानसाः परिकीर्तिताः । गता निःश्रेयसार्थं हि कदाचिद्दिशमुत्तराम् ॥
data.md: We are the sons of Brahman, begotten by his will. Once on a time we went to the north for the acquisition of our highest good.

data.v: तप्त्वा वर्षसहस्राणि चत्वारि तप उत्तमम् । एकपादस्थिताः सम्यक्काष्ठभूताः समाहिताः ॥
data.md: Having practised penances for thousands of years and acquired a great ascetic merit, we again stood on only one foot like fixed rods of wood.

data.v: मेरोरुत्तरभागे तु क्षीरोदस्यानुकूलतः । स देशो यत्र नस्तप्तं तपः परमदारुणम् । कथं पश्येमहि वयं देवं नारायणं त्विति ॥
data.md: The country where we practised these austerest of penances, lies to the north of the mountains of Meru and on the shores of the ocean of milk.

data.v: ततो व्रतस्यावभृथे वागुवाचाशरीरिणी । सुतप्तं वस्तपो विप्राः प्रसन्नेनान्तरात्मना ॥
यूयं जिज्ञासवो भक्ताः कथं द्रक्ष्यथ तं प्रभुम् । क्षीरोदधेरुत्तरतः श्वेतद्वीपो महाप्रभः ॥
तत्र नारायणपरा मानवाश्चन्द्रवर्चसः । एकान्तभावोपगतास्ते भक्ताः पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
ते सहस्रार्चिषं देवं प्रविशन्ति सनातनम् । अतीन्द्रिया निराहारा अनिष्पन्दाः सुगन्धिनः ॥
एकान्तिनस्ते पुरुषाः श्वेतद्वीपनिवासिनः । गच्छध्वं तत्र मुनयस्तत्रात्मा मे प्रकाशितः ॥
data.md: They are shorn of senses. They do not live on any sort of food. Their eyes are winkless. Their bodies always emit a sweet smell. Indeed, the inhabitants of White Island believe and adore only one God. Go there, ye ascetics, for there I have revealed myself.

data.v: अथ श्रुत्वा वयं सर्वे वाचं तामशरीरिणीम् । यथाख्यातेन मार्गेण तं देशं प्रतिपेदिरे ॥
data.md: All of us, hearing these invisible words, proceeded by the way said to the country described.

data.v: प्राप्य श्वेतं महाद्वीपं तच्चित्तास्तद्दिदृक्षवः । ततो नो दृष्टिविषयस्तदा प्रतिहतोऽभवत् ॥
data.md: Eagerly desirous of seeing Him and our hearts full of Him, we reached that large island called White Island. Arrived there, we could see nothing. Indeed our vision was blinded by the energy of the great god and accordingly we could not see Him.

data.v: न च पश्याम पुरुषं तत्तेजोहृतदर्शनाः । ततो नः प्रादुरभवद्विज्ञानं देवयोगजम् ॥
data.md: At this, the idea, due to the grace of the great God Himself, sprung in our minds that one who had not practised sufficient penances could not soon see Narayana.

data.v: न किलातप्ततपसा शक्यते द्रष्टुमञ्जसा । ततः पुनर्वर्षशतं तप्त्वा तात्कालिकं महत् ॥
data.md: Under the influence of this idea we once more began to practise some severe austerities, suited to the time and place, for a hundred years. Upon the termination of our vows, we saw a number of men of auspicious marks.

data.v: व्रतावसाने सुशुभान्नरान्ददृशिरे वयम् । श्वेतांश्चन्द्रप्रतीकाशान्सर्वलक्षणलक्षितान् ॥
नित्याञ्जलिकृतान्ब्रह्म जपतः प्रागुदङ्मुखान् । मानसो नाम स जपो जप्यते तैर्महात्मभिः । तेनैकाग्रमनस्त्वेन प्रीतो भवति वै हरिः ॥
data.md: The recitation performed by those great persons was a mental Yapa. On account of their hearts, having been entirely fixed upon Him, Hari became highly gratified with them.

data.v: या भवेन्मुनिशार्दूल भाः सूर्यस्य युगक्षये । एकैकस्य प्रभा तादृक्साभवन्मानवस्य ह ॥
data.md: The effulgence that came out of the persons of those men resembled, O foremost of ascetics, the splendours which the sun assumed when the time comes for the dissolution of the universe.

data.v: तेजोनिवासः स द्वीप इति वै मेनिरे वयम् । न तत्राभ्यधिकः कश्चित्सर्वे ते समतेजसः ॥
data.md: Indeed, we thought that that Island was the seat of all Energy. All the denizens were perfectly equal in energy. There was no superiority or inferiority there among them.

data.v: अथ सूर्यसहस्रस्य प्रभां युगपदुत्थिताम् । सहसा दृष्टवन्तः स्म पुनरेव बृहस्पते ॥
data.md: We then suddenly saw once more a light arise that seemed to be the concentrated effulgence of a thousand Sons, O Brihaspati.

data.v: सहिताश्चाभ्यधावन्त ततस्ते मानवा द्रुतम् । कृताञ्जलिपुटा हृष्टा नम इत्येव वादिनः ॥
data.md: The denizens in a body, ran towards that light, with hands joined in reverential attitude, full of joy, and uttering the one word Salutation.

data.v: ततोऽभिवदतां तेषामश्रौष्म विपुलं ध्वनिम् । बलिः किलोपह्रियते तस्य देवस्य तैर्नरैः ॥
data.md: We then heard a very loud noise uttered by all of them together. It appeared that those men were engaged in offering a sacrifice to the great God.

data.v: वयं तु तेजसा तस्य सहसा हृतचेतसः । न किंचिदपि पश्यामो हृतदृष्टिबलेन्द्रियाः ॥
data.md: As regards ourselves, we were suddenly deprived of our senses by his Energy. Shorn of vision and strength and all the senses, we could not behold or feel anything.

data.v: एकस्तु शब्दोऽविरतः श्रुतोऽस्माभिरुदीरितः । जितं ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष नमस्ते विश्वभावन ॥
data.md: We only heard a loud sound uttered by the collected denizens. It said,-Victory to you, O you have eyes like lotus petals! Salutation to you, O Creator of the universe.

data.v: नमस्तेऽस्तु हृषीकेश महापुरुषपूर्वज । इति शब्दः श्रुतोऽस्माभिः शिक्षाक्षरसमीरितः ॥
data.md: Salutation to you, O Hrishikesha, O foremost of Beings, O First-born! This was the sound we heard, uttered distinctly and in accordance with the rules of orthoepy.

data.v: एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वायुः सर्वगन्धवहः शुचिः । दिव्यान्युवाह पुष्पाणि कर्मण्याश्चौषधीस्तथा ॥
data.md: Meanwhile, a fragrant and pure breeze blew, carrying perfumes of celestial flowers, and of certain herbs and plants that were necessary on the occasion.

data.v: तैरिष्टः पञ्चकालज्ञैर्हरिरेकान्तिभिर्नरैः । नूनं तत्रागतो देवो यथा तैर्वागुदीरिता । वयं त्वेनं न पश्यामो मोहितास्तस्य मायया ॥
data.md: Forsooth, Hari appeared in that place whence the sound we heard originated. As regards ourselves, stupefied by His illusion, we could not behold Him.

data.v: मारुते संनिवृत्ते च बलौ च प्रतिपादिते । चिन्ताव्याकुलितात्मानो जाताः स्मोऽङ्गिरसां वर ॥
data.md: After the breeze has ceased and the sacrifice had been over, our hearts became stricken with anxiety, O foremost one of Angiras's race.

data.v: मानवानां सहस्रेषु तेषु वै शुद्धयोनिषु । अस्मान्न कश्चिन्मनसा चक्षुषा वाप्यपूजयत् ॥
data.md: As we stood among those thousands of men all of whom were of pure birth, no one honoured us with a glance or a nod.

data.v: तेऽपि स्वस्था मुनिगणा एकभावमनुव्रताः । नास्मासु दधिरे भावं ब्रह्मभावमनुष्ठिताः ॥
data.md: Those ascetics, all of whom were cheerful and filled with devotion and who were all are practising the Brahma-frame of mind, showed no feeling for us.

data.v: ततोऽस्मान्सुपरिश्रान्तांस्तपसा चापि कर्शितान् । उवाच खस्थं किमपि भूतं तत्राशरीरकम् ॥
data.md: We had been greatly tired. Our penances had einaciated us. At that time, a bodiless Being addressed us from the sky and said to us

data.v: दृष्टा वः पुरुषाः श्वेताः सर्वेन्द्रियविवर्जिताः । दृष्टो भवति देवेश एभिर्दृष्टैर्द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
data.md: These white men, who are divested of all external senses, competent to see (Narayana). Only those foremost of twice-born persons whom these white men honoured with their looks, can see the great God.

data.v: गच्छध्वं मुनयः सर्वे यथागतमितोऽचिरात् । न स शक्यो अभक्तेन द्रष्टुं देवः कथंचन ॥
data.md: Go hence, ye Munis, to the place from where you have come! That great Deity is incapable of being ever seen by one who has no devotion.

data.v: कामं कालेन महता एकान्तित्वं समागतैः । शक्यो द्रष्टुं स भगवान्प्रभामण्डलदुर्दृशः ॥
data.md: Incapable of being seen on account of his dazzling effulgence, that illustrious Deity can be seen only by those person who succeed, in course of long time, in devoting themselves wholly and solely to Him. O foremost of twiceborn ones, you have a great duty to perform.

data.v: महत्कार्यं तु कर्तव्यं युष्माभिर्द्विजसत्तमाः । इतः कृतयुगेऽतीते विपर्यासं गतेऽपि च ॥
वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे विप्राः प्राप्ते त्रेतायुगे ततः । सुराणां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थं सहाया वै भविष्यथ ॥
data.md: After the expiration of this the golden age, when the Treta age comes in course of the Vivasvat cycle, a great calamity will befall the world. You Munis, you shall then have to help the gods.

data.v: ततस्तदद्भुतं वाक्यं निशम्यैवं स्म सोमप । तस्य प्रसादात्प्राप्ताः स्मो देशमीप्सितमञ्जसा ॥
data.md: no Having heard this wonderful words that were sweet as nectar, we soon returned to the place we desired, through the favour of that great Deity.

data.v: एवं सुतपसा चैव हव्यकव्यैस्तथैव च । देवोऽस्माभिर्न दृष्टः स कथं त्वं द्रष्टुमर्हसि । नारायणो महद्भूतं विश्वसृग्घव्यकव्यभुक् ॥
data.md: When with the help of even such austere penances of offerings devoutly given in sacrifices, we could not see the great Deity, how, indeed, can you except to see Him so easily?

data.v: एवमेकतवाक्येन द्वितत्रितमतेन च । अनुनीतः सदस्यैश्च बृहस्पतिरुदारधीः । समानीय ततो यज्ञं दैवतं समपूजयत् ॥
data.md: Induced by these words spoken by Ekata and approved by his companions, viz., Dvita and Trita, and solicited also by the other Sadasyas, the great Brihaspati terminated that sacrifice after duly offering the accustomed adorations to the gods.

data.v: समाप्तयज्ञो राजापि प्रजाः पालितवान्वसुः । ब्रह्मशापाद्दिवो भ्रष्टः प्रविवेश महीं ततः ॥
data.md: Having completed his great sacrifice, king Uparichara, also, began to rule his subjects piously. At last, renouncing his body, he ascended to heaven. After sometime, through the curse of the Brahmanas, he dropped down from those happy regions and sank deep into the bowels of the Earth.

data.v: अन्तर्भूमिगतश्चैव सततं धर्मवत्सलः । नारायणपरो भूत्वा नारायणपदं जगौ ॥
तस्यैव च प्रसादेन पुनरेवोत्थितस्तु सः । महीतलाद्गतः स्थानं ब्रह्मणः समनन्तरम् । परां गतिमनुप्राप्त इति नैष्ठिकमञ्जसा ॥
data.md: Getting up from the bowels of the Earth, king Vasu, on account of the very highest end that he attained, proceeded to a spot which is even higher than the region of Brahman himself.”

data.v: यदा भक्तो भगवत आसीद्राजा महावसुः । किमर्थं स परिभ्रष्टो विवेश विवरं भुवः ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said When the great king Vasu was so wholly devoted to Narayana, why then did he drop down from heaven and why again had he to sink beneath the surface of Earth?

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । ऋषीणां चैव संवादं त्रिदशानां च भारत ॥
data.md: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Narada and the Rishi Narayana.

data.v: अजेन यष्टव्यमिति देवाः प्राहुर्द्विजोत्तमान् । स च छागो ह्यजो ज्ञेयो नान्यः पशुरिति स्थितिः ॥
data.md: Once on a time, addressing many foremost of Brahmanas the gods said to them that sacrifices should be performed by offering up Ajas as victims. The word Aja means the goat and no other animal.

data.v: बीजैर्यज्ञेषु यष्टव्यमिति वै वैदिकी श्रुतिः । अजसंज्ञानि बीजानि छागं न घ्नन्तुमर्हथ ॥
data.md: The Rishis said The Veda declares that in sacrifices the offerings should consist of seeds. Seeds are called Ajas. You should not kill goats.

data.v: नैष धर्मः सतां देवा यत्र वध्येत वै पशुः । इदं कृतयुगं श्रेष्ठं कथं वध्येत वै पशुः ॥
data.md: O gods, that cannot be the religion of good and pious people in which the destruction of animals is sanctioned. This, again, is the golden age. How can animals be killed in this epoch of righteousness?

data.v: तेषां संवदतामेवमृषीणां विबुधैः सह । मार्गागतो नृपश्रेष्ठस्तं देशं प्राप्तवान्वसुः । अन्तरिक्षचरः श्रीमान्समग्रबलवाहनः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said While this conversation was going on between the Rishis and the gods, that foremost of kings, viz., Vasu, was seen to come that way. Gifted with great prosperity, the king was coming through the sky, accompanied by his troops and vehicles and animals.

data.v: तं दृष्ट्वा सहसायान्तं वसुं ते त्वन्तरिक्षगम् । ऊचुर्द्विजातयो देवानेष छेत्स्यति संशयम् ॥
data.md: Seeing king Vasu coming there through the skies, the Brahmanas addressing the gods, said,-This one will dispell our doubts.

data.v: यज्वा दानपतिः श्रेष्ठः सर्वभूतहितप्रियः । कथं स्विदन्यथा ब्रूयाद्वाक्यमेष महान्वसुः ॥
data.md: He celebrates sacrifices. He is liberal in making gifts. He always seeks the well being of all creatures. How, indeed, will the great Vasu speak otherwise.

data.v: एवं ते संविदं कृत्वा विबुधा ऋषयस्तथा । अपृच्छन्सहसाभ्येत्य वसुं राजानमन्तिकात् ॥
data.md: Having thus spoken each other, the gods and the Rishis quickly approached king Vasu and asked him, saying,-0 king, with what should one celebrate sacrifices?

data.v: भो राजन्केन यष्टव्यमजेनाहोस्विदौषधैः । एतन्नः संशयं छिन्धि प्रमाणं नो भवान्मतः ॥
data.md: Should one sacrifice with the goat or with herbs and plants? Do you remove this doubt of ours! We select you as our judge in this matter.

data.v: स तान्कृताञ्जलिर्भूत्वा परिपप्रच्छ वै वसुः । कस्य वः को मतः पक्षो ब्रूत सत्यं समागताः ॥
data.md: Thus accosted by them, Vasu joined his hands in humility and said to them,-Tell me truly, ye foremost of Brahmanas, what opinion is held by you individually in this matter?

data.v: धान्यैर्यष्टव्यमित्येष पक्षोऽस्माकं नराधिप । देवानां तु पशुः पक्षो मतो राजन्वदस्व नः ॥
data.md: The Rishis said The opinion held by us, O king, is that sacrifices should be celebrated with grain! The gods, however, hold that sacrifices should be celebrated with animals. Do you judge between us and tell us which of these opinions is correct.

data.v: देवानां तु मतं ज्ञात्वा वसुना पक्षसंश्रयात् । छागेनाजेन यष्टव्यमेवमुक्तं वचस्तदा ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Learning the opinion of the gods, Vasu, moved by partiality for them, said that sacrifices should be celebrated with animals.

data.v: कुपितास्ते ततः सर्वे मुनयः सूर्यवर्चसः । ऊचुर्वसुं विमानस्थं देवपक्षार्थवादिनम् ॥
सुरपक्षो गृहीतस्ते यस्मात्तस्माद्दिवः पत । अद्य प्रभृति ते राजन्नाकाशे विहता गतिः । अस्मच्छापाभिघातेन महीं भित्त्वा प्रवेक्ष्यसि ॥
ततस्तस्मिन्मुहूर्तेऽथ राजोपरिचरस्तदा । अधो वै संबभूवाशु भूमेर्विवरगो नृपः । स्मृतिस्त्वेनं न प्रजहौ तदा नारायणाज्ञया ॥
data.md: After the Rishis had said these words, king Uparichara immediately dropped down, O king, and went down a hole in the Earth. At the command, however,. of Narayana, Vasu's memory did not leave him.

data.v: देवास्तु सहिताः सर्वे वसोः शापविमोक्षणम् । चिन्तयामासुरव्यग्राः सुकृतं हि नृपस्य तत् ॥
अनेनास्मत्कृते राज्ञा शापः प्राप्तो महात्मना । अस्य प्रतिप्रियं कार्यं सहितैर्नो दिवौकसः ॥
इति बुद्ध्या व्यवस्याशु गत्वा निश्चयमीश्वराः । ऊचुस्तं हृष्टमनसो राजोपरिचरं तदा ॥
ब्रह्मण्यदेवं त्वं भक्तः सुरासुरगुरुं हरिम् । कामं स तव तुष्टात्मा कुर्याच्छापविमोक्षणम् ॥
मानना तु द्विजातीनां कर्तव्या वै महात्मनाम् । अवश्यं तपसा तेषां फलितव्यं नृपोत्तम ॥
data.md: It is proper, however, that the great Brahmanas should be honoured. Verily, O best of kings, their penances should bear fruits.

data.v: यतस्त्वं सहसा भ्रष्ट आकाशान्मेदिनीतलम् । एकं त्वनुग्रहं तुभ्यं दद्मो वै नृपसत्तम ॥
data.md: Indeed, you have already fallen down from the sky on the Earth! We wish, however, O best of kings, to show you a favour. As long as you, O sinless one, will live in this hole, so long you will receive (due sustenance).

data.v: यावत्त्वं शापदोषेण कालमासिष्यसेऽनघ । भूमेर्विवरगो भूत्वा तावन्तं कालमाप्स्यसि । यज्ञेषु सुहुतां विप्रैर्वसोर्धारां महात्मभिः ॥
data.md: You will get those streaks of clarified butter which Brahmanas with concentrated minds pour in sacrifices along with sacred Mantras, and which are called by the name of Vasudhara! Indeed, weakness or distress shall hot affect you.

data.v: प्राप्स्यसेऽस्मदनुध्यानान्मा च त्वां ग्लानिरास्पृशेत् । न क्षुत्पिपासे राजेन्द्र भूमेश्छिद्रे भविष्यतः ॥
वसोर्धारानुपीतत्वात्तेजसाप्यायितेन च । स देवोऽस्मद्वरात्प्रीतो ब्रह्मलोकं हि नेष्यति ॥
data.md: While living, O king of kings, in the hole of the Earth, neither hunger nor thirst shall assail you for you will drink those streaks of clarified butter called Vasudhara. Your energy also shall continue unabated. By virtue of this our boon that we grant you, the God of gods, viz., Narayana, will be pleased with you, and He will take you hence to the region of Brahman.

data.v: एवं दत्त्वा वरं राज्ञे सर्वे तत्र दिवौकसः । गताः स्वभवनं देवा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः ॥
data.md: Having granted these boons to the king, the dwellers of heaven, as also all those Rishis having penances for wealth, returned each to his respective place.

data.v: चक्रे च सततं पूजां विष्वक्सेनाय भारत । जप्यं जगौ च सततं नारायणमुखोद्गतम् ॥
data.md: Then Vasu, O Bharata, began to worship the Creator of the universe and to recite silently those sacred Mantras that had come out of Narayana's mouth in days of yore.

data.v: तत्रापि पञ्चभिर्यज्ञैः पञ्चकालानरिंदम । अयजद्धरिं सुरपतिं भूमेर्विवरगोऽपि सन् ॥
data.md: Although living in a pit of the Earth, the king still adored Hari, the Lord of all the gods in the well-known five-sacrifices that are celebrating five times every day, O destroyer of enemies.

data.v: ततोऽस्य तुष्टो भगवान्भक्त्या नारायणो हरिः । अनन्यभक्तस्य सतस्तत्परस्य जितात्मनः ॥
data.md: On account of these adorations of his, Narayana, otherwise called Hari, became highly gratified with him who thus showed himself to be entirely devoted to Him. Who entirely depended upon Him as his sole refuge, and who had completely mastered his senses.

data.v: वरदो भगवान्विष्णुः समीपस्थं द्विजोत्तमम् । गरुत्मन्तं महावेगमाबभाषे स्मयन्निव ॥
data.md: The illustrious Vishnu, that giver of boons, then addressed the fleet Garuda, that foremost of birds, who waited upon Him as his servant, and said these desirable words.

data.v: द्विजोत्तम महाभाग गम्यतां वचनान्मम । सम्राड्राजा वसुर्नाम धर्मात्मा मां समाश्रितः ॥
data.md: O foremost of birds, O you who are highly blessed, listen to what I say. There is a great king named Vasu who is of righteous soul and rigid vows! Through the anger of the Brahmanas, he has dropped into a pit of the Earth.

data.v: ब्राह्मणानां प्रकोपेन प्रविष्टो वसुधातलम् । मानितास्ते तु विप्रेन्द्रास्त्वं तु गच्छ द्विजोत्तम ॥
data.md: The Brahmanas have been sufficiently honoured. Do you go to that king now.

data.v: भूमेर्विवरसंगुप्तं गरुडेह ममाज्ञया । अधश्चरं नृपश्रेष्ठं खेचरं कुरु माचिरम् ॥
data.md: At my behest, O Garuda, go to that foremost of kings, viz., Uparichara, who is now living in a hole of the Earth and incapable of any longer passing through the sky, and bring him up forthwith into the sky.

data.v: गरुत्मानथ विक्षिप्य पक्षौ मारुतवेगवान् । विवेश विवरं भूमेर्यत्रास्ते वाग्यतो वसुः ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of Vishnu, Garuda, spreading his wings and going with the speed of the wind, entered that pit in the Earth in which king Vasu was residing.

data.v: तत एनं समुत्क्षिप्य सहसा विनतासुतः । उत्पपात नभस्तूर्णं तत्र चैनममुञ्चत ॥
data.md: All on a sudden taking the king up, the son of Vinata soared into the sky and there released the king from his beaks.

data.v: तस्मिन्मुहूर्ते संजज्ञे राजोपरिचरः पुनः । सशरीरो गतश्चैव ब्रह्मलोकं नृपोत्तमः ॥
data.md: At that moment, king Uparichara once more acquired his divine form and re-entered the region of Brahman.

data.v: एवं तेनापि कौन्तेय वाग्दोषाद्देवताज्ञया । प्राप्ता गतिरयज्वार्हा द्विजशापान्महात्मना ॥
data.md: It was the way, O son of Kunti, that that great king first dropped down through the curse of the Brahmanas for a faulty speech, and once more got up to heaven at the behest of the great God (Vishnu).

data.v: केवलं पुरुषस्तेन सेवितो हरिरीश्वरः । ततः शीघ्रं जहौ शापं ब्रह्मलोकमवाप च ॥
data.md: Only the powerful Lord Hari, that foremost of all Beings, was devoutly adored by him. It was for this devout worship that the king succeeded very soon in freeing himself from the curse imprecated upon him by the Brahmanas and in regaining the blessed regions of Brahman.

data.v: एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं ते भूता मानवा यथा । नारदोऽपि यथा श्वेतं द्वीपं स गतवानृषिः । तत्ते सर्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमना नृप ॥
data.md: Bhishma said I have thus told you everything regarding the origin of the spiritual sons of Brahman. Listen to me with rapt attention, for I shall now describe to you how the celestial Rishi Narada had proceeded in days of yore to White Island."

data.v: प्राप्य श्वेतं महाद्वीपं नारदो भगवानृषिः । ददर्श तानेव नराञ्श्वेतांश्चन्द्रप्रभाञ्शुभान् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said "Arrived at the spacious kingdom called White Island, the illustrious Rishi saw those same white men effulgent like the sun.

data.v: पूजयामास शिरसा मनसा तैश्च पूजितः । दिदृक्षुर्जप्यपरमः सर्वकृच्छ्रधरः स्थितः ॥
data.md: Adored by them, the Rishi worshipped them in return by bending his head and respecting them in his mind. Desirous of seeing Narayana, he began to live there, attentively engaged in the silent recitation of Mantras sacred to him, and practising the most difficult VOWS.

data.v: भूत्वैकाग्रमना विप्र ऊर्ध्वबाहुर्महामुनिः । स्तोत्रं जगौ स विश्वाय निर्गुणाय महात्मने ॥
data.md: With rapt mind, the twice-born Rishi, with arms upraised, stood in Yoga, and then sang the following hymn to the Lord of the universe, Him, viz., who is at once the soul of attributes and divested of ali attributes.

पञ्चाग्ने [92] त्रिणाचिकेत [93] षडङ्गविधान [94] प्राग्ज्योतिष [95] ज्येष्ठसामग [96] सामिकव्रतधर [97] अथर्वशिरः [98] पञ्चमहाकल्प [99] फेनपाचार्य [100] । वालखिल्य [101] वैखानस [102] अभग्नयोग [103] अभग्नपरिसंख्यान [104] युगादे [105] युगमध्य [106] युगनिधन [107] आखण्डल [108] प्राचीनगर्भ [109] कौशिक [110] । पुरुष्टुत [111] पुरुहूत [112] विश्वरूप [113] अनन्तगते [114] अनन्तभोग [115] अनन्त [116=6] [129] वासुदेव [130] । सर्वच्छन्दक [131] हरिहय [132] हरिमेध [133] महायज्ञभागहर [134] वरप्रद [135=157] यमनियममहानियमकृच्छ्रातिकृच्छ्रमहाकृच्छ्रसर्वकृच्छ्रनियमधर [136] निवृत्तधर्मप्रवचनगते [137] प्रवृत्तवेदक्रिय [138] अज [139] सर्वगते [140] । सर्वदर्शिन् [141] अग्राह्य [142] अचल [143] महाविभूते [144] माहात्म्यशरीर [145] पवित्र [146] महापवित्र [147] हिरण्मय [148] बृहत् [149] अप्रतर्क्य [150] । अविज्ञेय [151] ब्रह्माग्र्य [152] प्रजासर्गकर [153] प्रजानिधनकर [154] महामायाधर [155] चित्रशिखण्डिन् [156] वरप्रद [157=135] पुरोडाशभागहर [158] गताध्वन् [159] छिन्नतृष्ण [160] । छिन्नसंशय [161] सर्वतोनिवृत्त [162] ब्राह्मणरूप [163] ब्राह्मणप्रिय [164] विश्वमूर्ते [165] महामूर्ते [166] बान्धव [167] भक्तवत्सल [168] ब्रह्मण्यदेव [169] भक्तोऽहं त्वां दिदृक्षुः [170] एकान्तदर्शनाय नमो नमः [171] ॥
एवं स्तुतः स भगवान्गुह्यैस्तथ्यैश्च नामभिः । तं मुनिं दर्शयामास नारदं विश्वरूपधृक् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Thus sung with names that were not known to others, the Divine Narayana having the universe for his form appeared before the ascetic Narada.

data.v: किंचिच्चन्द्रविशुद्धात्मा किंचिच्चन्द्राद्विशेषवान् । कृशानुवर्णः किंचिच्च किंचिद्धिष्ण्याकृतिः प्रभुः ॥
data.md: His form was some what purer than the moon and differed from the moon in some particulars. He somewhat resembled a burning fire in complexion. The powerful Lord was somewhat of the form of Vishti,

data.v: शुकपत्रवर्णः किंचिच्च किंचित्स्फटिकसप्रभः । नीलाञ्जनचयप्रख्यो जातरूपप्रभः क्वचित् ॥
data.md: He looked in some respects like the feathers of the parrot, and in some a collection of pure crystal. He resembled in some respects a hill of antimony and in some a mass of pure gold.

data.v: प्रवालाङ्कुरवर्णश्च श्वेतवर्णः क्वचिद्बभौ । क्वचित्सुवर्णवर्णाभो वैडूर्यसदृशः क्वचित् ॥
data.md: His complexion somewhat resembled the coral when first formed, and was somewhat white. That complexion resembled in some respects the colour of gold and in some that of the lapis lazulus.

data.v: नीलवैडूर्यसदृश इन्द्रनीलनिभः क्वचित् । मयूरग्रीववर्णाभो मुक्ताहारनिभः क्वचित् ॥
data.md: It resembled in some respects the colour of the blue lapis lazulus and in some that of sapphire. It resembled in some respects of colour of the peacock's neck, and in some that of a string of pearls.

data.v: एतान्वर्णान्बहुविधान्रूपे बिभ्रत्सनातनः । सहस्रनयनः श्रीमाञ्शतशीर्षः सहस्रपात् ॥
data.md: Bearing these various sorts of hues on his body the eternal Deity appeared before Narada. He had a thousand eyes and was endued with great beauty. He had a hundred heads and a hundred feet.

data.v: सहस्रोदरबाहुश्च अव्यक्त इति च क्वचित् । ओंकारमुद्गिरन्वक्त्रात्सावित्रीं च तदन्वयाम् ॥
data.md: He had a thousand stomachs and a thousand arms. He seemed to be still inconceivable to the mind. With one of his mouths he uttered the syllable OM and then the Gayatri following OM.

data.v: शेषेभ्यश्चैव वक्त्रेभ्यश्चतुर्वेदोद्गतं वसु । आरण्यकं जगौ देवो हरिर्नारायणो वशी ॥
data.md: With mind under complete mastery, the great God, called by the names of Hari and Narayana, by his other mouths, many in nụmber, uttered many Mantras from the four Vedas which are known by the name of Aranyaka.

data.v: वेदीं कमण्डलुं दर्भान्मणिरूपानथोपलान् । अजिनं दण्डकाष्ठं च ज्वलितं च हुताशनम् । धारयामास देवेशो हस्तैर्यज्ञपतिस्तदा ॥
data.md: The Lord of all the gods, the great God who is worshipped in sacrifices, held in his hands a sacrificial altar, a Kamandalu, a few white gems, a pair of shoes, a bundle of Kusha blades, a deer-skin, a tooth-stick, and a little burning fire.

data.v: तं प्रसन्नं प्रसन्नात्मा नारदो द्विजसत्तमः । वाग्यतः प्रयतो भूत्वा ववन्दे परमेश्वरम् । तमुवाच नतं मूर्ध्ना देवानामादिरव्ययः ॥
data.md: The first of all the gods, who is free from decay, said the following words to him whose head was still bent low in veneration.

data.v: एकतश्च द्वितश्चैव त्रितश्चैव महर्षयः । इमं देशमनुप्राप्ता मम दर्शनलालसाः ॥
data.md: The Holy One said The great Rishis, Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, came to this country from desire of seeing me.

data.v: न च मां ते ददृशिरे न च द्रक्ष्यति कश्चन । ऋते ह्येकान्तिकश्रेष्ठात्त्वं चैवैकान्तिको मतः ॥
data.md: Their wishes, however, were not fulfilled. Excepting those who are devoted to with wholly and solely, no else can see me. As regards you, you are verily the foremost of all persons devoted to me with all their souls.

data.v: ममैतास्तनवः श्रेष्ठा जाता धर्मगृहे द्विज । तास्त्वं भजस्व सततं साधयस्व यथागतम् ॥
data.md: These are my bodies, the best ones that I assume. These were born, O twice-born one, in the house of Dharma. Do you worship them always, and do you perform those rites that are laid down in the ordinances in connexion with that worship.

data.v: वृणीष्व च वरं विप्र मत्तस्त्वं यमिहेच्छसि । प्रसन्नोऽहं तवाद्येह विश्वमूर्तिरिहाव्ययः ॥
