data.md: O foremost of Brahmanas, making over the duties of a house-holder to my son, I wish to satisfy the highest duties of man. What, O twice-born one, should be my path?

data.v: अहमात्मानमात्मस्थमेक एवात्मनि स्थितः । कर्तुं काङ्क्षामि नेच्छामि बद्धः साधारणैर्गुणैः ॥
data.md: Relying upon the soul, I wish to acquire existence in the One Soul. Alas, fettered by the bonds of attachment, I have not the heart to actually perform that task.

data.v: यावदेवानतीतं मे वयः पुत्रफलाश्रितम् । तावदिच्छामि पाथेयमादातुं पारलौकिकम् ॥
data.md: And since the best portion of my life has passed away as house-holder, I wish to devote the remaining part of my life in acquiring the means of defraying the expenses of my journey in respect of the time to come.

data.v: अस्मिन्हि लोकसंताने परं पारमभीप्सतः । उत्पन्ना मे मतिरियं कुतो धर्ममयः प्लवः ॥
data.md: The desire has originated in my mind of crossing the ocean of the world. Alas, whence shall I get the vessel of religion?

data.v: समुह्यमानानि निशम्य लोके; निर्यात्यमानानि च सात्त्विकानि । दृष्ट्वा च धर्मध्वजकेतुमालां; प्रकीर्यमाणामुपरि प्रजानाम् ॥
न मे मनो रज्यति भोगकाले; दृष्ट्वा यतीन्प्रार्थयतः परत्र । तेनातिथे बुद्धिबलाश्रयेण; धर्मार्थतत्त्वे विनियुङ्क्ष्व मां त्वम् ॥
सोऽतिथिर्वचनं तस्य श्रुत्वा धर्माभिलाषिणः । प्रोवाच वचनं श्लक्ष्णं प्राज्ञो मधुरया गिरा ॥
data.md: Bhishma said, Gifted with great wisdom, the guest hearing this speech of his host which was consistent with virtue, said these sweet words in melodious voice.

data.v: अहमप्यत्र मुह्यामि ममाप्येष मनोरथः । न च संनिश्चयं यामि बहुद्वारे त्रिविष्टपे ॥
data.md: The Guest said I also am confounded about this subject. The same thought occupies my mind. I am unable to arrive at certainty of conclusion. Heaven has many doors.

data.v: केचिन्मोक्षं प्रशंसन्ति केचिद्यज्ञफलं द्विजाः । वानप्रस्थाश्रमं केचिद्गार्हस्थ्यं केचिदाश्रिताः ॥
data.md: There are some that speak highly of Liberation. Some twice-born persons praise the fruits acquired by the by the performance of sacrifices. Some there are who take refuge in the forest mode of life. Some, again, follow the domestic mode of life.

data.v: राजधर्माश्रयं केचित्केचिदात्मफलाश्रयम् । गुरुचर्याश्रयं केचित्केचिद्वाक्यं यमाश्रयम् ॥
data.md: Some depend upon the merits attainable by an observance of the royal duties. Some depend upon the fruits of that culture which consists in the control of the soul, Some think that the merits originating from a dutiful obedience to preceptors and seniors efficacious. Some follow control of speech. are

data.v: मातरं पितरं केचिच्छुश्रूषन्तो दिवं गताः । अहिंसया परे स्वर्गं सत्येन च तथा परे ॥
data.md: Some, by waiting dutifully upon their mothers and fathers, have gone to heaven. Some have ascended to heaven by practising the duty of mercy, and some by practising Truth.

data.v: आहवेऽभिमुखाः केचिन्निहताः स्विद्दिवं गताः । केचिदुञ्छव्रतैः सिद्धाः स्वर्गमार्गसमाश्रिताः ॥
data.md: Some rush to battle, and sacrificing their lives, have attained to heaven. Some again, acquiring success by practising the vow called Unccha, are following the path of heaven.

data.v: केचिदध्ययने युक्ता वेदव्रतपराः शुभाः । बुद्धिमन्तो गताः स्वर्गं तुष्टात्मानो जितेन्द्रियाः ॥
data.md: Some have given themselves up to the study of the Vedas. Endued with auspiciousness and wedded to such study, these men, gifted with intelligence, and tranquil souls, and having their senses under complete control, attain to heaven.

data.v: आर्जवेनापरे युक्ता निहतानार्जवैर्जनैः । ऋजवो नाकपृष्ठे वै शुद्धात्मानः प्रतिष्ठिताः ॥
data.md: Others, marked by simplicity and truth, have been killed by wicked men. Gifted with pure souls, such men to truth and simplicity, have become respected inhabitants of heaven.

data.v: एवं बहुविधैर्लोके धर्मद्वारैरनावृतैः । ममापि मतिराविग्ना मेघलेखेव वायुना ॥
data.md: In this world, it is seen, that men go to heaven through a thousand doors of duty, all standing wide open. My understanding has been troubled by your question, like a cloud before the wind.

data.v: उपदेशं तु ते विप्र करिष्येऽहं यथागमम् । गुरुणा मे यथाख्यातमर्थतस्तच्च मे शृणु ॥
data.md: The Guest said-For all that, O Brahmana, I shall try to instruct you duly. Listen to me as I recount to you what I have heard from my preceptor.

data.v: यत्र पूर्वाभिसर्गेण धर्मचक्रं प्रवर्तितम् । नैमिषे गोमतीतीरे तत्र नागाह्वयं पुरम् ॥
data.md: In that place whence in course of a former creation, the wheel of virtue was set in motion, in that forest which is known by the name of Naimisha, and which is situate on the banks of the Gomati, there is a city called Nagapura.

data.v: समग्रैस्त्रिदशैस्तत्र इष्टमासीद्द्विजर्षभ । यत्रेन्द्रातिक्रमं चक्रे मान्धाता राजसत्तमः ॥
data.md: There, in that region, all the gods, asscmbled a grand sacrifice. There the foremost of earthly kings, Mandhatri, defeated Indra, the king of the gods.

data.v: कृताधिवासो धर्मात्मा तत्र चक्षुःश्रवा महान् । पद्मनाभो महाभागः पद्म इत्येव विश्रुतः ॥
data.md: A powerful Naga, of righteous soul, lives in the city that stands in that region. That great Naga is known by the name of Padmanabha or Padma.

data.v: स वाचा कर्मणा चैव मनसा च द्विजर्षभ । प्रसादयति भूतानि त्रिविधे वर्त्मनि स्थितः ॥
data.md: Walking in the three-fold path (of acts, knowledge, and adoration), he pleases all creatures in thought, word, and deed.

data.v: साम्ना दानेन भेदेन दण्डेनेति चतुर्विधम् । विषमस्थं जनं स्वं च चक्षुर्ध्यानेन रक्षति ॥
data.md: Thinking upon all things with great care, he protects the virtuous and punishes the wicked by following the four-fold policy on conciliation, creating dissensions, making gifts or giving bribes, and using force.

data.v: तमभिक्रम्य विधिना प्रष्टुमर्हसि काङ्क्षितम् । स ते परमकं धर्मं नमिथ्या दर्शयिष्यति ॥
data.md: Going there, you should put to him the questions you wish. He will show you truly what the highest religion is.

data.v: स हि सर्वातिथिर्नागो बुद्धिशास्त्रविशारदः । गुणैरनवमैर्युक्तः समस्तैराभिकामिकैः ॥
data.md: That Naga is always fond of guests. Gifted with great intelligence, he is well conversant with the Scriptures. He possesses all desirable virtues the like of which are not to be seen in any other person.

data.v: प्रकृत्या नित्यसलिलो नित्यमध्ययने रतः । तपोदमाभ्यां संयुक्तो वृत्तेनानवरेण च ॥
data.md: By nature he does those duties which are performed with or in water. He is given to the study of the Vedas. He is endued with penances and self-control. He has great riches.

data.v: यज्वा दानरुचिः क्षान्तो वृत्ते च परमे स्थितः । सत्यवागनसूयुश्च शीलवानभिसंश्रितः ॥
data.md: He celebrates sacrifices, makes gifts, abstains from doing injury, and practises forgiveness. His conduct is in every way good. Truthful in speech and shorn of malice, his conduct is good and his senses are under proper control.

data.v: शेषान्नभोक्ता वचनानुकूलो; हितार्जवोत्कृष्टकृताकृतज्ञः । अवैरकृद्भूतहिते नियुक्तो; गङ्गाह्रदाम्भोऽभिजनोपपन्नः ॥
data.md: He eats after feeding all his guests and attendants. He is kind of speech. He has knowledge of what is good and what is simple and right and what is censurable. He takes an account of what he does and what he leaves undone. He never acts with hostility towards any one. He is always engaged in doing what is good to all creatures. He belongs to a family which is as pure and stainless as the water of a lake in the midst of the Ganges.

data.v: अतिभारोद्यतस्यैव भारापनयनं महत् । पराश्वासकरं वाक्यमिदं मे भवतः श्रुतम् ॥
data.md: I have heard these words of yours that are so consoling, with as much satisfaction as is experienced by a person heavily loaded when that load is taken off his head or shoulders.

data.v: अध्वक्लान्तस्य शयनं स्थानक्लान्तस्य चासनम् । तृषितस्य च पानीयं क्षुधार्तस्य च भोजनम् ॥
ईप्सितस्येव संप्राप्तिरन्नस्य समयेऽतिथेः । एषितस्यात्मनः काले वृद्धस्येव सुतो यथा ॥
मनसा चिन्तितस्येव प्रीतिस्निग्धस्य दर्शनम् । प्रह्रादयति मां वाक्यं भवता यदुदीरितम् ॥
दत्तचक्षुरिवाकाशे पश्यामि विमृशामि च । प्रज्ञानवचनाद्योऽयमुपदेशो हि मे कृतः । बाढमेवं करिष्यामि यथा मां भाषते भवान् ॥
data.md: Like a person with upturned look I have heard what has fallen from your lips and am thinking upon their meaning. With these wise words of yours, you have truly instructed me!

data.v: इहेमां रजनीं साधो निवसस्व मया सह । प्रभाते यास्यति भवान्पर्याश्वस्तः सुखोषितः । असौ हि भगवान्सूर्यो मन्दरश्मिरवाङ्मुखः ॥
data.md: Yes, I shall do what you have ordered me to do. You may go tomorrow carily in the morning, passing the night happily with me and removing your fatigue by such rest. See, the rays of the divine Sun have been partially dimmed and the god of day is going in his downward course!

data.v: ततस्तेन कृतातिथ्यः सोऽतिथिः शत्रुसूदन । उवास किल तां रात्रिं सह तेन द्विजेन वै ॥
data.md: Bhishma continued Hospitably treated by that Brahmana, the learned guest, O destroyer of enemies, passed that night in the company of his host.

data.v: तत्तच्च धर्मसंयुक्तं तयोः कथयतोस्तदा । व्यतीता सा निशा कृत्स्ना सुखेन दिवसोपमा ॥
data.md: Indeed, both of them passed the night happily, conversing cheerfully with each other on the subject of the duties of the fourth mode of life, viz., Sannyasa. So engrossing was their conversation that the night passed away as if it were day.

data.v: ततः प्रभातसमये सोऽतिथिस्तेन पूजितः । ब्राह्मणेन यथाशक्त्या स्वकार्यमभिकाङ्क्षता ॥
data.md: When morning came, the guest was adored with due rites by the Brahmana, who was bent upon doing what was considered by him to be beneficial for himself.

data.v: ततः स विप्रः कृतधर्मनिश्चयः; कृताभ्यनुज्ञः स्वजनेन धर्मवित् । यथोपदिष्टं भुजगेन्द्रसंश्रयं; जगाम काले सुकृतैकनिश्चयः ॥
data.md: Having dismissed his guest, the virtuous Brahmana, determined to achieve his purpose, took leave of his kinsmen and relatives, and started in due time for the abode of that foremost of Nagas, with heart firmly directed towards it.

data.v: स वनानि विचित्राणि तीर्थानि च सरांसि च । अभिगच्छन्क्रमेण स्म कंचिन्मुनिमुपस्थितः ॥
data.md: Proceeding by many charming forests and lakes and sacred waters, the Brahmana at last arrived at the asylum of a certain ascetic.

data.v: तं स तेन यथोद्दिष्टं नागं विप्रेण ब्राह्मणः । पर्यपृच्छद्यथान्यायं श्रुत्वैव च जगाम सः ॥
data.md: Going there, he enquired of him, in proper words, about the Naga of whom he had heard from his guest, and instructed by him he pursued his journey.

data.v: सोऽभिगम्य यथाख्यातं नागायतनमर्थवित् । प्रोक्तवानहमस्मीति भोःशब्दालंकृतं वचः ॥
data.md: With a clear idea of the object of his journey the Brahman then reached the house of the Naga. Entering it duly, he announced his arrival in proper words, saying,-Ho! who is there! I am a Brahmana come here as a guest!

data.v: ततस्तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा रूपिणी धर्मवत्सला । दर्शयामास तं विप्रं नागपत्नी पतिव्रता ॥
data.md: Hearing these words, the chaste wife of the Naga, endued with great beauty and devoted to the observance of all duties, showed herself.

data.v: सा तस्मै विधिवत्पूजां चक्रे धर्मपरायणा । स्वागतेनागतं कृत्वा किं करोमीति चाब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: Always attentive to the duties of hospitality, she adored the guest with due rites, and welcoming him, said,-What can I do for you?

data.v: विश्रान्तोऽभ्यर्चितश्चास्मि भवत्या श्लक्ष्णया गिरा । द्रष्टुमिच्छामि भवति तं देवं नागमुत्तमम् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said O lady, I am sufficiently honoured by you with the sweet words you have said unto me. The fatigue of the journey has also been removed. I wish, O blessed lady, to see your excellent husband.

data.v: एतद्धि परमं कार्यमेतन्मे फलमीप्सितम् । अनेनार्थेन चास्म्यद्य संप्राप्तः पन्नगालयम् ॥
data.md: This is my great object. This is the one object of my desire. It is for this reason that I have come to-day to the house of the Naga your husband.

data.v: आर्य सूर्यरथं वोढुं गतोऽसौ मासचारिकः । सप्ताष्टभिर्दिनैर्विप्र दर्शयिष्यत्यसंशयम् ॥
data.md: The Wife of the Naga said Reverend Sir, my husband has gone to drag the car of the Sun for a month. O learned Brahmana, he return in fifteen days, and will, forsooth, appear before you.

data.v: एतद्विदितमार्यस्य विवासकरणं मम । भर्तुर्भवतु किं चान्यत्क्रियतां तद्वदस्व मे ॥
data.md: I have thus told you the reason of my husband's absence from home. Be that as it may, what else is there that I can do for you? Tell me this.

data.v: अनेन निश्चयेनाहं साध्वि संप्राप्तवानिह । प्रतीक्षन्नागमं देवि वत्स्याम्यस्मिन्महावने ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said O chaste lady, I have come here with the object of seeing your husband. O reverend dame, I shall live in the adjacent forest, waiting for his return.

data.v: संप्राप्तस्यैव चाव्यग्रमावेद्योऽहमिहागतः । ममाभिगमनं प्राप्तो वाच्यश्च वचनं त्वया ॥
data.md: When your husband returns, do kindly tell him that I have arrived at this place actuated by the desire of seeing him. You should also inform me of his return when that event takes place.

data.v: अहमप्यत्र वत्स्यामि गोमत्याः पुलिने शुभे । कालं परिमिताहारो यथोक्तं परिपालयन् ॥
data.md: O blessed lady, I shall, till then, live on the banks of the Gomati, waiting for his return and living restricted diet.

data.v: ततः स विप्रस्तां नागीं समाधाय पुनः पुनः । तदेव पुलिनं नद्याः प्रययौ ब्राह्मणर्षभः ॥
data.md: Having said this repeatedly to the wife of the Naga, the foremost of Brahmanas went to the banks of the Gomati for living there till the time of Naga's return.

data.v: अथ तेन नरश्रेष्ठ ब्राह्मणेन तपस्विना । निराहारेण वसता दुःखितास्ते भुजंगमाः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said These Nagas of that city became greatly distressed when they saw that that Brahmana, devoted to the practice of penances, continued to live in the forest, entirely abstaining from food, in expectation of the arrival of the Naga king.

data.v: सर्वे संभूय सहितास्तस्य नागस्य बान्धवाः । भ्रातरस्तनया भार्या ययुस्तं ब्राह्मणं प्रति ॥
data.md: All the kinsmen and relatives of the great Naga, including his brothers and children and wife, assembling together, went to the spot where the Brahmana was living.

data.v: तेऽपश्यन्पुलिने तं वै विविक्ते नियतव्रतम् । समासीनं निराहारं द्विजं जप्यपरायणम् ॥
data.md: Arrived on the banks of the Gomati, they saw that twice-born one seated in a solitary place, abstaining from food of every sort, observant all the while of excellent vows, and engaged in silently reciting certain Mantras.

data.v: ते सर्वे समभिक्रम्य विप्रमभ्यर्च्य चासकृत् । ऊचुर्वाक्यमसंदिग्धमातिथेयस्य बान्धवाः ॥
data.md: Approaching the Brahmana and offering him due adorations, the kinsmen and relatives of the great Naga said to him these candid words.

data.v: षष्ठो हि दिवसस्तेऽद्य प्राप्तस्येह तपोधन । न चाभिलषसे किंचिदाहारं धर्मवत्सल ॥
data.md: O Brahmana having asceticism, for your riches, that is the sixth day of your arrival here, but you speak no word about your food, O twice-born one you are devoted to virtue.

data.v: अस्मानभिगतश्चासि वयं च त्वामुपस्थिताः । कार्यं चातिथ्यमस्माभिर्वयं सर्वे कुटुम्बिनः ॥
data.md: You have come to us. We too are here in attendance upon you. It is absolutely necessary that we should do the duties of hospitality by you. We are all relations of the Naga king with whom you have business.

data.v: मूलं फलं वा पर्णं वा पयो वा द्विजसत्तम । आहारहेतोरन्नं वा भोक्तुमर्हसि ब्राह्मण ॥
data.md: Roots or fruit, leaves, or water, or rice or meat, O best of Brahmanas, you should take for food.

data.v: त्यक्ताहारेण भवता वने निवसता सता । बालवृद्धमिदं सर्वं पीड्यते धर्मसंकटात् ॥
data.md: For your living in this forest under such circumstances of total abstention from food, the whole community of Nagas young and old is being aggrieved, since this your fast implies negligence on our part to discharge the duties of hospitality.

data.v: न हि नो भ्रूणहा कश्चिद्राजापथ्योऽनृतोऽपि वा । पूर्वाशी वा कुले ह्यस्मिन्देवतातिथिबन्धुषु ॥
data.md: We have none amongst us who has been guilty of Brahmanicide. None of us has been guilty of Brahmanicide. None of us has ever lost a son immediately after birth. No one has been born in our race who has eaten before serving the gods or guests or relatives arrived at his house.

data.v: उपदेशेन युष्माकमाहारोऽयं मया वृतः । द्विरूनं दशरात्रं वै नागस्यागमनं प्रति ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said On account of these solicitations of you all, I may be considered to have broken my fast. Eight days remain when the king of the Nagas will return.

data.v: यद्यष्टरात्रे निर्याते नागमिष्यति पन्नगः । तदाहारं करिष्यामि तन्निमित्तमिदं व्रतम् ॥
data.md: If, on the expire of the eighth night hence, the king of the Nagas do not come back, I shall then break this fast by eating. Indeed, this vow of abstaining from all food that I am observing is on account of my respect for the Naga king.

data.v: कर्तव्यो न च संतापो गम्यतां च यथागतम् । तन्निमित्तं व्रतं मह्यं नैतद्भेत्तुमिहार्हथ ॥
data.md: You should not grieve for what I am doing. Do you all return to whence you came. This my vow is on his account. You should not do anything on account of which this my vow may be broken.

data.v: तेन ते समनुज्ञाता ब्राह्मणेन भुजंगमाः । स्वमेव भवनं जग्मुरकृतार्था नरर्षभ ॥
data.md: The assembled Nagas, thus addressed by Brahmana, were sent away by him, whereupon, O forcmost of men, they returned to their respective quarters.

data.v: अथ काले बहुतिथे पूर्णे प्राप्तो भुजंगमः । दत्ताभ्यनुज्ञः स्वं वेश्म कृतकर्मा विवस्वतः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Upon the expire of full fifteen days, the Naga king (Padmanabha), having finished his task of dragging the car of the Sun and obtained the latter's permission, returned to his own house.

data.v: तं भार्या समभिक्रामत्पादशौचादिभिर्गुणैः । उपपन्नां च तां साध्वीं पन्नगः पर्यपृच्छत ॥
data.md: Seeing him return, his wife approached him quickly for washing his feet and dutifully satisfying other tasks of a similar nature. Having performed these tasks, she sat by his side. The Naga then, refreshed from fatigue, addressed his dutiful and chaste wife, saying, I hope, my dear wife, that during my absence you have not neglected to adore the gods and guests according to the instructions I gave you, and according to the ordinances laid down in the scriptures.

data.v: अपि त्वमसि कल्याणि देवतातिथिपूजने । पूर्वमुक्तेन विधिना युक्ता युक्तेन मत्समम् ॥
data.md: Seeing him return, his wife approached him quickly for washing his feet and dutifully satisfying other tasks of a similar nature. Having performed these tasks, she sat by his side. The Naga then, refreshed from fatigue, addressed his dutiful and chaste wife, saying, I hope, my dear wife, that during my absence you have not neglected to adore the gods and guests according to the instructions I gave you, and according to the ordinances laid down in the scriptures.

data.v: न खल्वस्यकृतार्थेन स्त्रीबुद्ध्या मार्दवीकृता । मद्वियोगेन सुश्रोणि वियुक्ता धर्मसेतुना ॥
data.md: I hope, without yielding to that impure understanding which is natural to persons of your sex, you have, during my absence from home, been firm in the observance of the duties of hospitality. I trust that you have not gone beyond the barriers of duty and virtue.

data.v: शिष्याणां गुरुशुश्रूषा विप्राणां वेदपारणम् । भृत्यानां स्वामिवचनं राज्ञां लोकानुपालनम् ॥
data.md: The duty of disciples is to wait respectfully upon their preceptor for doing his bidding; that of Brahmanas is to study the Vedas and bear them in memory; that of servants is to obey the commands of their masters; that of the king is to protect his people by supporting the good and punishing the wicked. It is said that the duties of a Kshatriya are the protection of all creatures from wrong and oppression.

data.v: सर्वभूतपरित्राणं क्षत्रधर्म इहोच्यते । वैश्यानां यज्ञसंवृत्तिरातिथेयसमन्विता ॥
विप्रक्षत्रियवैश्यानां शुश्रूषा शूद्रकर्म तत् । गृहस्थधर्मो नागेन्द्र सर्वभूतहितैषिता ॥
data.md: The duty of the Shudra is to serve with humility persons of the twice-born orders, viz., Brahmanas and Kshatriyas and Vaishyas. The religion of the house-holder, O king of the Nagas, consists in doing good to all creatures.

data.v: नियताहारता नित्यं व्रतचर्या यथाक्रमम् । धर्मो हि धर्मसंबन्धादिन्द्रियाणां विशेषणम् ॥
data.md: Frugality of fare and observance of vows in due order, form merit (for persons of all classes) on account of the connection that exists between the senses and the duties religion.

data.v: अहं कस्य कुतो वाहं कः को मे ह भवेदिति । प्रयोजनमतिर्नित्यमेवं मोक्षाश्रमी भवेत् ॥
data.md: Who am I? Whence have I come? What are others to me and what am I to others?—these are the thoughts to which the mind should ever be given by him who leads that course of life which leads to Liberation.

data.v: पतिव्रतात्वं भार्यायाः परमो धर्म उच्यते । तवोपदेशान्नागेन्द्र तच्च तत्त्वेन वेद्मि वै ॥
data.md: Chastity and obedience to the husband from the highest duty of wife. Through your instruction, O king of Nagas, I have learnt this well.

data.v: साहं धर्मं विजानन्ती धर्मनित्ये त्वयि स्थिते । सत्पथं कथमुत्सृज्य यास्यामि विषमे पथि ॥
data.md: I, therefore, that am well versed in my duty, and that have you for my husband,—you who are devoted to virtue,-O, why shall I, falling off from the path of duty, tread along the path of disobedience and sin?

data.v: देवतानां महाभाग धर्मचर्या न हीयते । अतिथीनां च सत्कारे नित्ययुक्तास्म्यतन्द्रिता ॥
data.md: During your absence from home, the adorations to the gods have not suffered in any respect. I have also, without the slightest negligence, performed the duties of hospitality towards persons arrived as guests in your house.

data.v: सप्ताष्टदिवसास्त्वद्य विप्रस्येहागतस्य वै । स च कार्यं न मे ख्याति दर्शनं तव काङ्क्षति ॥
data.md: Fifteen days ago a Brahmana has come here. He has not given out his object to me. He wishes to see you.

data.v: गोमत्यास्त्वेष पुलिने त्वद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकः । आसीनोऽऽवर्तयन्ब्रह्म ब्राह्मणः संशितव्रतः ॥
data.md: Living on the banks of the Gomati, he is anxiously expecting your return. Of rigid vows, that Brahmana is sitting there, engaged in the recitation of Brahma.

data.v: अहं त्वनेन नागेन्द्र सामपूर्वं समाहिता । प्रस्थाप्यो मत्सकाशं स संप्राप्तो भुजगोत्तमः ॥
data.md: O king of the Nagas, I have made a promise to him that I would send you to him as soon as you would return to your house.

data.v: एतच्छ्रुत्वा महाप्राज्ञ तत्र गन्तुं त्वमर्हसि । दातुमर्हसि वा तस्य दर्शनं दर्शनश्रवः ॥
data.md: Hearing these words of men, O best of Nagas, you should go there. O you who hear with your eyes, you should great to that twiceborn person the object that has brought him here.

data.v: अथ ब्राह्मणरूपेण कं तं समनुपश्यसि । मानुषं केवलं विप्रं देवं वाथ शुचिस्मिते ॥
data.md: The Naga said O you of sweet smiles, for whom have you taken that Brahmana? Is he really a human being or is he some god that has come here in the disguise of a Brahmana?

data.v: को हि मां मानुषः शक्तो द्रष्टुकामो यशस्विनि । संदर्शनरुचिर्वाक्यमाज्ञापूर्वं वदिष्यति ॥
data.md: O you of great fame, who is there ainong men who would be desirous of seeing are or that would be competent for the purpose? Can a human being, desiring to see me, leave such a command with you about sending me to him for paying him a visit at the place where he is living?

data.v: सुरासुरगणानां च देवर्षीणां च भामिनि । ननु नागा महावीर्याः सौरसेयास्तरस्विनः ॥
data.md: Amongst the gods and Asuras and celestial Rishis, O amiable lady, the Nagas are endued with great energy. Having great speed, they are endued again with excellent fragrance.

data.v: वन्दनीयाश्च वरदा वयमप्यनुयायिनः । मनुष्याणां विशेषेण धनाध्यक्षा इति श्रुतिः ॥
data.md: They derseve to be adored. They are capable of granting boons. Indeed, we too deserve to be followed by others. I tell you, O lady, that we cannot be seen by human beings.

data.v: आर्जवेनाभिजानामि नासौ देवोऽनिलाशन । एकं त्वस्य विजानामि भक्तिमानतिरोषणः ॥
data.md: Judging by his simplicity and candour I know that that Brahmana is not any god who lives on air. O you of great anger, I also know this, viz., that he respects you with all his heart.

data.v: स हि कार्यान्तराकाङ्क्षी जलेप्सुः स्तोकको यथा । वर्षं वर्षप्रियः पक्षी दर्शनं तव काङ्क्षति ॥
data.md: He seeks the accomplishment of some object that depends upon your help. As the bird called Chataka, which if fond of rain, waits in earnest expectation of a shower, so is that Brahmana waiting is expectation of a meeting with you.

data.v: न हि त्वा दैवतं किंचिद्विविग्नं प्रतिपालयेत् । तुल्ये ह्यभिजने जातो न कश्चित्पर्युपासते ॥
data.md: Let no calamity befall him on account of his inability to obtain a sight of you. No person born like you in a respectable family can be considered to remain respectable by neglecting a guest arrived at his house.

data.v: तद्रोषं सहजं त्यक्त्वा त्वमेनं द्रष्टुमर्हसि । आशाछेदेन तस्याद्य नात्मानं दग्धुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Renouncing that anger which is natural to you, you should go and see that Brahmana. You should not allows yourself to be consumed by disappointing that Brahmana.

data.v: आशया त्वभिपन्नानामकृत्वाश्रुप्रमार्जनम् । राजा वा राजपुत्रो वा भ्रूणहत्यैव युज्यते ॥
data.md: The king or the prince, by refusing to wipe the tears of persons who come to him from hopes of relief, commits the sin of foeticide. By abstaining from speech one acquire wisdom.

data.v: मौनाज्ज्ञानफलावाप्तिर्दानेन च यशो महत् । वाग्मित्वं सत्यवाक्येन परत्र च महीयते ॥
data.md: By practising gifts one acquires great fame. By observing truthfulness of speech, one acquire the fit of eloquence and comes to be respected in heaven.

data.v: भूमिप्रदानेन गतिं लभत्याश्रमसंमिताम् । नष्टस्यार्थस्य संप्राप्तिं कृत्वा फलमुपाश्नुते ॥
data.md: By giving away land one acquires that high end which is ordained for Rishis leading the sacred mode of life. By acquiring riches through fair means one succeeds in acquiring many desirable fruits.

data.v: अभिप्रेतामसंक्लिष्टां कृत्वाकामवतीं क्रियाम् । न याति निरयं कश्चिदिति धर्मविदो विदुः ॥
data.md: By doing in full what is good for oneself, one can avoid going to hell. This is what the righteous say.

data.v: अभिमानेन मानो मे जातिदोषेण वै महान् । रोषः संकल्पजः साध्वि दग्धो वाचाग्निना त्वया ॥
data.md: The Naga said I had no arrogance. On account, however, of my birth, my pride was considerable. Of anger which is born of desire, O blessed lady, I have none. It has all been consumed by the fire of your excellent instructions.

data.v: न च रोषादहं साध्वि पश्येयमधिकं तमः । यस्य वक्तव्यतां यान्ति विशेषेण भुजंगमाः ॥
data.md: I do not see, O blessed lady, any darkness that is thicker than anger. On account, however of the Nagas having excess of anger, they have become objects of reproach with all persons.

data.v: दोषस्य हि वशं गत्वा दशग्रीवः प्रतापवान् । तथा शक्रप्रतिस्पर्धी हतो रामेण संयुगे ॥
data.md: By yielding to the influence of anger, the ten-headed Ravan of great prowess, became the rival Shakra and was for that reason killed by Rama in battle.

data.v: अन्तःपुरगतं वत्सं श्रुत्वा रामेण निर्हृतम् । धर्षणाद्रोषसंविग्नाः कार्तवीर्यसुता हताः ॥
data.md: Hearing that the Rishi Rama of Bhrigu's race had entered the inner apartments of their palace for bringing away the calf of the Homa cow of his father, the sons of Karttavirya, yielding to anger, took such entry as an insult to their royal house, and as the result thereof, they met with destruction at the hands of Rama.

data.v: जामदग्न्येन रामेण सहस्रनयनोपमः । संयुगे निहतो रोषात्कार्तवीर्यो महाबलः ॥
data.md: Indeed, Karttavirya of great strength, resembling the thousand-eyed Indra himself, on account of his having yielded to anger, was killed in battle by Rama of Jamadagni's race.

data.v: तदेष तपसां शत्रुः श्रेयसश्च निपातनः । निगृहीतो मया रोषः श्रुत्वैव वचनं तव ॥
data.md: Verily, O amiable lady, at your words I have controlled my anger, that enemy of penances, that destroyer of all that is beneficial for himself.

data.v: आत्मानं च विशेषेण प्रशंसाम्यनपायिनि । यस्य मे त्वं विशालाक्षि भार्या सर्वगुणान्विता ॥
data.md: I praise my own self greatly since, O largeeyed one, I am fortunate enough to have you as my wife,-you who are possessed of every virtue and who have inexhaustible merits.

data.v: एष तत्रैव गच्छामि यत्र तिष्ठत्यसौ द्विजः । सर्वथा चोक्तवान्वाक्यं नाकृतार्थः प्रयास्यति ॥
data.md: I shall now proceed to that spot where the Brahmana is living. I shall certainly address that Brahmana in proper words, and he shall certainly go hence, his wishes being done.

data.v: स पन्नगपतिस्तत्र प्रययौ ब्राह्मणं प्रति । तमेव मनसा ध्यायन्कार्यवत्तां विचारयन् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Having said these words to his dear wife, the king of the Nagas proceeded to in exposition of an interview with him. As wondered as to that the business could be that had brought him to the Naga city.

data.v: तमभिक्रम्य नागेन्द्रो मतिमान्स नरेश्वर । प्रोवाच मधुरं वाक्यं प्रकृत्या धर्मवत्सलः ॥
data.md: Arrived before him, O king of men, that foremost of Nagas, devoted by his nature to virtue, addressed his guest in sweet words, saying,-0 Brahmana, do not give way to anger. I address you in peace! Do not be angry! For whom have you come here? What is your object?

data.v: भो भो क्षाम्याभिभाषे त्वां न रोषं कर्तुमर्हसि । इह त्वमभिसंप्राप्तः कस्यार्थे किं प्रयोजनम् ॥
data.md: Arrived before him, O king of men, that foremost of Nagas, devoted by his nature to virtue, addressed his guest in sweet words, saying,-0 Brahmana, do not give way to anger. I address you in peace! Do not be angry! For whom have you come here? What is your object?

data.v: आभिमुख्यादभिक्रम्य स्नेहात्पृच्छामि ते द्विज । विविक्ते गोमतीतीरे किं वा त्वं पर्युपाससे ॥
data.md: Coming to you, I ask you in love, O twiceborn one! Whom do you worship in this retired spot on the banks of the Gomati?

data.v: धर्मारण्यं हि मां विद्धि नागं द्रष्टुमिहागतम् । पद्मनाभं द्विजश्रेष्ठं तत्र मे कार्यमाहितम् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said Know that my name is Dharmaranya; and that I have come here for seeing the Naga Padamanabha, O foremost O all twice-born persons! With him I have some business!

data.v: तस्य चाहमसांनिध्यं श्रुतवानस्मि तं गतम् । स्वजनं तं प्रतीक्षामि पर्जन्यमिव कर्षकः ॥
data.md: I have heard that he is not at home and that, therefore, I am not now near his present habitation. Like a Chataka waiting in expectation of the clouds, I am waiting for him whom I consider as dear to me!

data.v: तस्य चाक्लेशकरणं स्वस्तिकारसमाहितम् । वर्तयाम्ययुतं ब्रह्म योगयुक्तो निरामयः ॥
data.md: For removing all evil from him and bringing about what is good to him, I am engaged in reciting the Vedas till he comes and am in Yoga and passing my time happily!

data.v: अहो कल्याणवृत्तस्त्वं साधु सज्जनवत्सलः । श्रवाढ्यस्त्वं महाभाग परं स्नेहेन पश्यसि ॥
data.md: The Naga said-Indeed, your conduct is highly good. Pious you are and devoted to the well being of all pious persons, O highly blessed Brahmana, every praise is due to you? You see the Naga with eyes of affection.

data.v: अहं स नागो विप्रर्षे यथा मां विन्दते भवान् । आज्ञापय यथा स्वैरं किं करोमि प्रियं तव ॥
data.md: I am that Naga, O learned Rishi, whom you seek! Do you order me, as you wish, in respect of what is agreeable to you and what I should do for you!

data.v: भवन्तं स्वजनादस्मि संप्राप्तं श्रुतवानिह । अतस्त्वां स्वयमेवाहं द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो द्विज ॥
data.md: Having heard from any wife that you are here, I have to come this spot, O twice-born one, for seeing you!

data.v: संप्राप्तश्च भवानद्य कृतार्थः प्रतियास्यति । विस्रब्धो मां द्विजश्रेष्ठ विषये योक्तुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: When you come here, you are certain to return hence with your object fulfilled. You should, O foremost of twice-born persons, cmploy me to any task with all confidence!

data.v: वयं हि भवता सर्वे गुणक्रीता विशेषतः । यस्त्वमात्महितं त्यक्त्वा मामेवेहानुरुध्यसे ॥
data.md: All of us have certainly been purchased by you with your merits, since you disregarding what is for your own good, has employed your time in seeking the well-being of ourselves!

data.v: आगतोऽहं महाभाग तव दर्शनलालसः । कंचिदर्थमनर्थज्ञः प्रष्टुकामो भुजंगम ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said O highly blessed Naga, I have come here, actuated by the desire of seeing you! I have come here, ignorant as I am with all things, for asking you about something, O snake!

data.v: अहमात्मानमात्मस्थो मार्गमाणोऽऽत्मनो हितम् । वासार्थिनं महाप्राज्ञ बलवन्तमुपास्मि ह ॥
data.md: Relying on the Soul, I wish to attain to the Supreme Soul which is the end of the Individual Soul. I am neither attached to, nor dissociated from, the world.

data.v: प्रकाशितस्त्वं स्वगुणैर्यशोगर्भगभस्तिभिः । शशाङ्ककरसंस्पर्शैर्हृद्यैरात्मप्रकाशितैः ॥
data.md: You shine with the effulgence of your own merits covered by fame,-with an effulgence that is as sweet as that of the moon.

data.v: तस्य मे प्रश्नमुत्पन्नं छिन्धि त्वमनिलाशन । पश्चात्कार्यं वदिष्यामि श्रोतुमर्हति मे भवान् ॥
data.md: O you who subsist on air only, do you first answer a question that I wish to put to you! Afterwards I shall inform you of the object with which I have come here.

data.v: विवस्वतो गच्छति पर्ययेण; वोढुं भवांस्तं रथमेकचक्रम् । आश्चर्यभूतं यदि तत्र किंचि;द्दृष्टं त्वया शंसितुमर्हसि त्वम् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said You go for dragging the one-wheeled car of Vivasvat according to your turn. You should describe to me anything wonderful that you may have seen in those regions through which you pass.

data.v: यस्य रश्मिसहस्रेषु शाखास्विव विहंगमाः । वसन्त्याश्रित्य मुनयः संसिद्धा दैवतैः सह ॥
data.md: Numberless Munis, crowned with ascetic success, together with all the gods, live in the rays of the Sun like birds perching on the branches of trees.

data.v: यतो वायुर्विनिःसृत्य सूर्यरश्म्याश्रितो महान् । विजृम्भत्यम्बरे विप्र किमाश्चर्यतरं ततः ॥
data.md: What, again, can be more wonderful than this that the powerful Wind, emanating from the Sun, takes refuge in his rays and thence yawns over universe?

data.v: शुक्रो नामासितः पादो यस्य वारिधरोऽम्बरे । तोयं सृजति वर्षासु किमाश्चर्यमतः परम् ॥
data.md: What can be more wonderful than this that the Sun has a black ray which, changes itself into clouds charged with rain and pours showers of rain when the season comes?

data.v: योऽष्टमासांस्तु शुचिना किरणेनोज्झितं पयः । पर्यादत्ते पुनः काले किमाश्चर्यमतः परम् ॥
data.md: What can be more wonderful than this that drinking up for eight months the rain he pours down he pours it down again in the rainy season.

data.v: यस्य तेजोविशेषेषु नित्यमात्मा प्रतिष्ठितः । यतो बीजं मही चेयं धार्यते सचराचरम् ॥
data.md: In certain rays of the Sun, the Soul of the universe said to live. From Him is the seed of all things, and it is He that supports the earth with all her mobile and immobile creatures.

data.v: यत्र देवो महाबाहुः शाश्वतः परमोऽक्षरः । अनादिनिधनो विप्र किमाश्चर्यमतः परम् ॥
data.md: What can be more wonderful, O Brahmana, than this, that the foremost of Purushas, eternal and mighty-armed, endued with great effulgence, eternal, and without beginning and without end, lives in the Sun?

data.v: आश्चर्याणामिवाश्चर्यमिदमेकं तु मे शृणु । विमले यन्मया दृष्टमम्बरे सूर्यसंश्रयात् ॥
data.md: Listen, however, to one thing I shall tell you now. It is the wonder of wonders. I have seen it in the clear sky, on account of my nearless to the Sun.

data.v: पुरा मध्याह्नसमये लोकांस्तपति भास्करे । प्रत्यादित्यप्रतीकाशः सर्वतः प्रत्यदृश्यत ॥
data.md: In former times, one day at the hour of noon, while the Sun was shining in all his glory and giving heat to everything we saw a Being coming towards the Sun, who seemed to shine with effulgence that was equal to that of the Sun himself.

data.v: स लोकांस्तेजसा सर्वान्स्वभासा निर्विभासयन् । आदित्याभिमुखोऽभ्येति गगनं पाटयन्निव ॥
data.md: Making all the worlds shine up with his glory and filling them with his energy, he came, as I have already told you towards the Sun, rending the sky, as it were, for passing through it.

data.v: हुताहुतिरिव ज्योतिर्व्याप्य तेजोमरीचिभिः । अनिर्देश्येन रूपेण द्वितीय इव भास्करः ॥
data.md: The rays that came out of his body seemed to resemble the blazing effulgence of libations of clarified butter poured into the sacrificial fire. On account of his energy and splendour he could not he looked at. His form seemed to be indescribable. Indeed, he appeared to us to be like a second Sun.

data.v: तस्याभिगमनप्राप्तौ हस्तो दत्तो विवस्वता । तेनापि दक्षिणो हस्तो दत्तः प्रत्यर्चनार्थिना ॥
data.md: As soon as he came near the Sun extended his two hands. For honouring the Sun in return, he also extended his right-hand.

data.v: ततो भित्त्वैव गगनं प्रविष्टो रविमण्डलम् । एकीभूतं च तत्तेजः क्षणेनादित्यतां गतम् ॥
data.md: The latter the then, piercing through the sky, entered into the Sun's disc. Mingling then with the Sun's energy, he seemed to be changed into the Sun's self.

data.v: तत्र नः संशयो जातस्तयोस्तेजःसमागमे । अनयोः को भवेत्सूर्यो रथस्थो योऽयमागतः ॥
data.md: When the two energies thus met together, we were so confounded that we could not any longer make out which was which. Indeed, we could not make out who was the Sun whom we bore on his car, and who was Being that we had seen coming through the sky.

data.v: ते वयं जातसंदेहाः पर्यपृच्छामहे रविम् । क एष दिवमाक्रम्य गतः सूर्य इवापरः ॥
data.md: Filled with confusion, we then addressed the Sun, saying,-O illustrious one, who is this Being who has mixed himself with you and has been charged into your second self.

data.v: नैष देवोऽनिलसखो नासुरो न च पन्नगः । उञ्छवृत्तिव्रते सिद्धो मुनिरेष दिवं गतः ॥
data.md: This Being is not the god of the fire, he is not an Asura. Nor is he a Naga. he is a Brahmana who has attained to heaven on account of his having been crowned with success in the observance of the vow called Unccha.

data.v: एष मूलफलाहारः शीर्णपर्णाशनस्तथा । अब्भक्षो वायुभक्षश्च आसीद्विप्रः समाहितः ॥
data.md: This person had lived upon fruit and roots and upon the fallen leaves of trees. He had sometimes lived upon water, and sometimes upon air alone, passing his devas with concentrated soul.

data.v: ऋचश्चानेन विप्रेण संहितान्तरभिष्टुताः । स्वर्गद्वारकृतोद्योगो येनासौ त्रिदिवं गतः ॥
data.md: The god Mahadeva had been propitiated by him with constant recitation of the Samhitas. he had tried to perform those deeds which lead to heaven. Through the merits of those acts he had now attained to heaven.

data.v: असन्नधीरनाकाङ्क्षी नित्यमुञ्छशिलाशनः । सर्वभूतहिते युक्त एष विप्रो भुजंगम ॥
data.md: Without riches and without desire of any king he had observed the vow called Unccha with regard to his food. This learned Brahmana, ye Nagas, had been devoted to the good of all creatures.

data.v: न हि देवा न गन्धर्वा नासुरा न च पन्नगाः । प्रभवन्तीह भूतानां प्राप्तानां परमां गतिम् ॥
data.md: Neither gods, nor Gandharvas, nor Asuras, nor Nagas, can be considered as superior to those creatures who attain to this excellent end of coming into the solar disc. Even such, 0 twice-born one, was the wonderful incident that I saw on that occasion.

data.v: एतदेवंविधं दृष्टमाश्चर्यं तत्र मे द्विज । संसिद्धो मानुषः कायो योऽसौ सिद्धगतिं गतः । सूर्येण सहितो ब्रह्मन्पृथिवीं परिवर्तते ॥
data.md: That Brahmana, who was crowned with success by the observance of the Unccha vow and who thus obtained an end that persons crowned with ascetic success gain. to this day, Otwice-born one, goes round the Earth, staying in the disc of the Sun. crowned with ascetic success gain. to this day, Otwice-born one, goes round the Earth, staying in the disc of the Sun.

data.v: आश्चर्यं नात्र संदेहः सुप्रीतोऽस्मि भुजंगम । अन्वर्थोपगतैर्वाक्यैः पन्थानं चास्मि दर्शितः ॥
data.md: Forsooth, this is highly wonderful, ONaga. I have been highly pleased by listening to you. By these words of yours that are fraught with subtile meaning, you have shown me the way I am to follow.

data.v: स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि साधो भुजगसत्तम । स्मरणीयोऽस्मि भवता संप्रेषणनियोजनैः ॥
data.md: Blessed be you, I wish to depart hence, O best of Nagas. You should remember me now and then and enquire after me sending your servants.

data.v: अनुक्त्वा मद्गतं कार्यं क्वेदानीं प्रस्थितो भवान् । उच्यतां द्विज यत्कार्यं यदर्थं त्वमिहागतः ॥
data.md: The Naga said The object that brought you here is still in your mind, for you have not as yet given it out to me. Where then will you go? Tell me, O twice-born one, what should be done by me, and what that object is which brought you here.

data.v: उक्तानुक्ते कृते कार्ये मामामन्त्र्य द्विजर्षभ । मया प्रत्यभ्यनुज्ञातस्ततो यास्यसि ब्राह्मण ॥
data.md: After the fulfilment of your business, whatever it is, expressed or unexpressed in speech, you may depart, O foremost of twiceborn persons, saluting me and dismissed by me cheerfully, O you of excellent vows.

data.v: न हि मां केवलं दृष्ट्वा त्यक्त्वा प्रणयवानिह । गन्तुमर्हसि विप्रर्षे वृक्षमूलगतो यथा ॥
data.md: You have conceived a friendship for me. O twice-born Rishi, you should not depart from this place after having only seen me, yourself sitting under the shade of this tree.

data.v: त्वयि चाहं द्विजश्रेष्ठ भवान्मयि न संशयः । लोकोऽयं भवतः सर्वः का चिन्ता मयि तेऽनघ ॥
data.md: You have become dear to me and I have become dear to you. All the persons in this city are yours. What objection then, O sinless one, you have to pass some time in my house.

data.v: एवमेतन्महाप्राज्ञ विज्ञातार्थ भुजंगम । नातिरिक्तास्त्वया देवाः सर्वथैव यथातथम् ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said It is even so, O you of great wisdom, O Naga, who have acquired a knowledge of the Soul. It is very true that the gods are not superior to you in any respect.

data.v: य एवाहं स एव त्वमेवमेतद्भुजंगम । अहं भवांश्च भूतानि सर्वे सर्वत्रगाः सदा ॥
data.md: He that is yourself is varily myself, as that is myself is truly yourself. Myself, yourself, and all other creatures, shall all have to enter into the Supreme Soul.

data.v: आसीत्तु मे भोगपते संशयः पुण्यसंचये । सोऽहमुञ्छव्रतं साधो चरिष्याम्यर्थदर्शनम् ॥
data.md: A doubt had entered my mind, O king of Nagas, in the matter of the best means for acquiring virtue or merit. That doubt has been removed by your discourse, for I have learnt the value of the Unccha vow.

data.v: एष मे निश्चयः साधो कृतः कारणवत्तरः । आमन्त्रयामि भद्रं ते कृतार्थोऽस्मि भुजंगम ॥
data.md: I shall hence follow that yow which is so very efficacious in producing beneficial consequences. That, O blessed one, has become my certain conclusion now, based on good reasons. I take your leave. Blessing to you. My object has been done, ONaga.

data.v: स चामन्त्र्योरगश्रेष्ठं ब्राह्मणः कृतनिश्चयः । दीक्षाकाङ्क्षी तदा राजंश्च्यवनं भार्गवं श्रितः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Having saluted that foremost of Nagas in this way, the Brahmana, firmly resolved to follow the Unccha mode of life, went O king, to Chyavana of Bhrigu's race, from desire of being formally instructed and initiated in that VOW.

data.v: स तेन कृतसंस्कारो धर्ममेवोपतस्थिवान् । तथैव च कथामेतां राजन्कथितवांस्तदा ॥
data.md: Chyavana performed the initiating rites of the Brahmana and formally initiated him into the Unccha mode of life. The son of Bhrigu,.0 king, recited this history to king Janaka in his palace. King Janaka, in his turn, described it to the celestial Rishi Narada of high soul.

data.v: भार्गवेणापि राजेन्द्र जनकस्य निवेशने । कथैषा कथिता पुण्या नारदाय महात्मने ॥
data.md: Chyavana performed the initiating rites of the Brahmana and formally initiated him into the Unccha mode of life. The son of Bhrigu,.0 king, recited this history to king Janaka in his palace. King Janaka, in his turn, described it to the celestial Rishi Narada of high soul.

data.v: नारदेनापि राजेन्द्र देवेन्द्रस्य निवेशने । कथिता भरतश्रेष्ठ पृष्टेनाक्लिष्टकर्मणा ॥
data.md: The celestial Rishi Narada too of pure acts going on one occasion to the house of Indra the king of the gods, gave to Indra this history upon being asked by him.

data.v: देवराजेन च पुरा कथैषा कथिता शुभा । समस्तेभ्यः प्रशस्तेभ्यो वसुभ्यो वसुधाधिप ॥
data.md: The king of the gods, having acquired it thus from Narada, recited this blessed history to an assembly of all the foremost Brahmanas, O king.

data.v: यदा च मम रामेण युद्धमासीत्सुदारुणम् । वसुभिश्च तदा राजन्कथेयं कथिता मम ॥
data.md: On the occasion, again, of my dreadful fight with Rama of Bhrigu's race the celestial Vasus, O king, had recited this history.

data.v: पृच्छमानाय तत्त्वेन मया तुभ्यं विशां पते । कथेयं कथिता पुण्या धर्म्या धर्मभृतां वर ॥
data.md: Asked by you, O foremost of pious men, I have recited this history that is excellent and sacred and endued with great merit.

data.v: तदेष परमो धर्मो यन्मां पृच्छसि भारत । असन्नधीरनाकाङ्क्षी धर्मार्थकरणे नृप ॥
data.md: You had asked me about that which forms the highest duty, O king. This history is my answer to your query. A brave men he was, O king. This history is my answer to your query. A brave man he was, O king, who followed the practice of the Unccha vow in this way, without desiring for any fruit.

data.v: स च किल कृतनिश्चयो द्विजाग्र्यो; भुजगपतिप्रतिदेशितार्थकृत्यः । यमनियमसमाहितो वनान्तं; परिगणितोञ्छशिलाशनः प्रविष्टः ॥
data.md: Firmly resolved, that Brahmana, instructed by the king of Nagas in this way about his duty, followed the practice of restraint and self control, an living upon such food as the allowed the Uccha vow, proceeded to another forest.

data.v: शमो बहुविधाकारः सूक्ष्म उक्तः पितामह । न च मे हृदये शान्तिरस्ति कृत्वेदमीदृशम् ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, peace of mind has been described to be subtile and of various forms. I have heard all your discourses, but have not still been able to acquire tranquillity of mind.

data.v: अस्मिन्नर्थे बहुविधा शान्तिरुक्ता त्वयानघ । स्वकृते का नु शान्तिः स्याच्छमाद्बहुविधादपि ॥
data.md: Various means of quieting the mind have been described by you, O sire, but how can peace of mind be acquired from only a knowledge of the different sorts of tranquillity, when I myself have been the means of bringing all this about?

data.v: शराचितशरीरं हि तीव्रव्रणमुदीक्ष्य च । शमं नोपलभे वीर दुष्कृतान्येव चिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: Seeing your body covered with arrows and bad sores, I cannot get, O hero, any peace of mind. thinking of the evils I have done.

data.v: रुधिरेणावसिक्ताङ्गं प्रस्रवन्तं यथाचलम् । त्वां दृष्ट्वा पुरुषव्याघ्र सीदे वर्षास्विवाम्बुजम् ॥
data.md: Seeing your body, O bravest of the brave, covered with blood, like a hill covered with water from its springs, I am perishing with grief as the lotus in the rainy season.

data.v: अतः कष्टतरं किं नु मत्कृते यत्पितामहः । इमामवस्थां गमितः प्रत्यमित्रै रणाजिरे । तथैवान्ये नृपतयः सहपुत्राः सबान्धवाः ॥
data.md: What can be more painful than this, that, for me, you, O grandfather have been reduced to this condition by my people fighting against their enemies on the battlefield.

data.v: वयं हि धार्तराष्ट्राश्च कालमन्युवशानुगाः । कृत्वेदं निन्दितं कर्म प्राप्स्यामः कां गतिं नृप ॥
data.md: Tell us, O prince, what will befall us and the sons of Dhritarashtra, who, impelled by fate and anger, have done this hateful act.

data.v: अहं तव ह्यन्तकरः सुहृद्वधकरस्तथा । न शान्तिमधिगच्छामि पश्यंस्त्वां दुःखितं क्षितौ ॥
data.md: But I, who am the cause of your death as well as of that of our friends, am denied all peace of mind by seeing you on the naked earth in this miserable plight.

data.v: परतन्त्रं कथं हेतुमात्मानमनुपश्यसि । कर्मण्यस्मिन्महाभाग सूक्ष्मं ह्येतदतीन्द्रियम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Why, O fortunate one, do you regard your soul, which is dependent, to be the cause of your deeds? Its inaction is subtle and imperceptible to the senses.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । संवादं मृत्युगौतम्योः काललुब्धकपन्नगैः ॥
data.md: Regarding it is cited the old discourse between Brahman, O king, and the Three-eyed Mahadeva.

data.v: गौतमी नाम कौन्तेय स्थविरा शमसंयुता । सर्पेण दष्टं स्वं पुत्रमपश्यद्गतचेतनम् ॥
data.md: There was, O son of Kunti, an old lady named Gautami, who was endued with great patience and peace of mind. One day she found her son dead on account of having been bitten by a serpent.

data.v: अथ तं स्नायुपाशेन बद्ध्वा सर्पममर्षितः । लुब्धकोऽर्जुनको नाम गौतम्याः समुपानयत् ॥
data.md: An angry fowler, named Arjunaka, bound the serpent with a string and brought it before Gautami.

data.v: तां चाब्रवीदयं ते स पुत्रहा पन्नगाधमः । ब्रूहि क्षिप्रं महाभागे वध्यतां केन हेतुना ॥
data.md: He then said to her. This wretched serpent has been the cause of your son's death. O blessed lady! Tell me quickly how this wretch is to be killed!

data.v: अग्नौ प्रक्षिप्यतामेष च्छिद्यतां खण्डशोऽपि वा । न ह्ययं बालहा पापश्चिरं जीवितुमर्हति ॥
data.md: Shall I throw it into the fire or shall I cut it into pieces? This infamous killer of a child should not live longer!

data.v: विसृजैनमबुद्धिस्त्वं न वध्योऽर्जुनक त्वया । को ह्यात्मानं गुरुं कुर्यात्प्राप्तव्ये सति चिन्तयन् ॥
data.md: Gautami replied Do you, O Arjunaka of little understanding, set free this serpent! It should not be killed by you. Who is so foolish as not to care for the inevitable destiny that awaits him and make himself heavy for sinking into sin?

data.v: प्लवन्ते धर्मलघवो लोकेऽम्भसि यथा प्लवाः । मज्जन्ति पापगुरवः शस्त्रं स्कन्नमिवोदके ॥
data.md: Those who have made themselves light by performing virtuous deeds, manage to cross the sea of the world as a ship crosses the ocean. But those who have loaded themselves with sin sink into the bottom, as an arrow thrown into the water.

data.v: न चामृत्युर्भविता वै हतेऽस्मि;न्को वात्ययः स्यादहतेऽस्मिञ्जनस्य । अस्योत्सर्गे प्राणयुक्तस्य जन्तो;र्मृत्योर्लोकं को नु गच्छेदनन्तम् ॥
data.md: By killing this serpent, this my boy will not revive, and by letting it live, no harm will be caused to you. Who would go to the endless regions of Death by killing this living creature?

data.v: जानाम्येवं नेह गुणागुणज्ञाः; सर्वे नियुक्ता गुरवो वै भवन्ति । स्वस्थस्यैते तूपदेशा भवन्ति; तस्मात्क्षुद्रं सर्पमेनं हनिष्ये ॥
data.md: The fowler said I know, O lady, who know the difference between, right and wrong that great persons are pained at the miseries of all creatures. But these words which you have uttered carry instruction for only a selfcontained person. Therefore, I must kill this serpent.

data.v: समीप्सन्तः कालयोगं त्यजन्ति; सद्यः शुचं त्वर्थविदस्त्यजन्ति । श्रेयः क्षयः शोचतां नित्यशो हि; तस्मात्त्याज्यं जहि शोकं हतेऽस्मिन् ॥
data.md: Those who value peace of mind, attribute everything to the course of Time as the cause, but practical men soon pacify their grief. People, through perpetual error, fear loss of beatitude. Therefore, O lady, remove your grief by having this serpent killed (by me).

data.v: न चैवार्तिर्विद्यतेऽस्मद्विधानां; धर्मारामः सततं सज्जनो हि । नित्यायस्तो बालजनो न चास्ति; धर्मो ह्येष प्रभवाम्यस्य नाहम् ॥
न ब्राह्मणानां कोपोऽस्ति कुतः कोपाच्च यातना । मार्दवात्क्षम्यतां साधो मुच्यतामेष पन्नगः ॥
data.md: Brahmanas do not cherish resentment, because resentment leads to pain. Do you, O Goodman, forgive and set free this serpent out of mercy.

data.v: हत्वा लाभः श्रेय एवाव्ययं स्या;त्सद्यो लाभो बलवद्भिः प्रशस्तः । कालाल्लाभो यस्तु सद्यो भवेत; हते श्रेयः कुत्सिते त्वीदृशे स्यात् ॥
data.md: The fowler replied Let us acquire great and inexhaustible merit in the next worlds by destroying (this creature), as a man gains great merit, and confers it on his victim as well, by sacrifice upon the altar! Merit is won by killing an enemy: by killing this despicable creature, you will acquire great and true merit in the next world.

data.v: कार्थप्राप्तिर्गृह्य शत्रुं निहत्य; का वा शान्तिः प्राप्य शत्रुं नमुक्त्वा । कस्मात्सौम्य भुजगे न क्षमेयं; मोक्षं वा किं कारणं नास्य कुर्याम् ॥
data.md: Gautami replied What good is there in torturing and destroying an enemy, and what good is acquired by not setting free an enemy in our power? Therefore. O you of kind face, why should we not forgive this serpent and try to acquire merit by setting it free.

data.v: अस्मादेकस्माद्बहवो रक्षितव्या; नैको बहुभ्यो गौतमि रक्षितव्यः । कृतागसं धर्मविदस्त्यजन्ति; सरीसृपं पापमिमं जहि त्वम् ॥
data.md: The fowler replied A great number (of creatures)should be safeguarded against this one, instead of this single creature being protected. Virtuous men quit the vicious: do you, therefore, destroy the wicked creature.

data.v: नास्मिन्हते पन्नगे पुत्रको मे; संप्राप्स्यते लुब्धक जीवितं वै । गुणं चान्यं नास्य वधे प्रपश्ये; तस्मात्सर्पं लुब्धक मुञ्च जीवम् ॥
data.md: Gautami replied By killing this serpent, my son, O fowler, will not regain his life, nor do I see that any other end will be attained by its death: therefore, do you, O fowler, set this living serpent free.

data.v: वृत्रं हत्वा देवराट्श्रेष्ठभाग्वै; यज्ञं हत्वा भागमवाप चैव । शूली देवो देववृत्तं कुरु त्वं; क्षिप्रं सर्पं जहि मा भूद्विशङ्का ॥
data.md: The fowler said By destroying Vritra, Indra got the best portion (of sacrificial offerings), and by destroying a sacrifice Mahadeva secured his share of sacrificial offerings: do you, therefore, kill this serpent forthwith without any misgivings whatsoever.

data.v: असकृत्प्रोच्यमानापि गौतमी भुजगं प्रति । लुब्धकेन महाभागा पापे नैवाकरोन्मतिम् ॥
ईषदुच्छ्वसमानस्तु कृच्छ्रात्संस्तभ्य पन्नगः । उत्ससर्ज गिरं मन्दां मानुषीं पाशपीडितः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Although repeatedly urged on by the fowler for the destruction of the serpent, the great Gautami did nor bend her mind to that sinful deed. Painfully fettered with the cord, sighing a little and keeping up its composure with great difficulty, the serpent then uttered these words slowly, in a human voice.

data.v: को न्वर्जुनक दोषोऽत्र विद्यते मम बालिश । अस्वतन्त्रं हि मां मृत्युर्विवशं यदचूचुदत् ॥
data.md: The serpent said O foolish Arjunaka, what is my fanlt? I have no will of my own, and am not independent! Death sent me on this work.

data.v: तस्यायं वचनाद्दष्टो न कोपेन न काम्यया । तस्य तत्किल्बिषं लुब्ध विद्यते यदि किल्बिषम् ॥
data.md: By his order have I bitten this child, and not out of any anger or option an my part. Therefore, if there be any sin in this, O fowler, the sin is his.

data.v: यद्यन्यवशगेनेदं कृतं ते पन्नगाशुभम् । कारणं वै त्वमप्यत्र तस्मात्त्वमपि किल्बिषी ॥
data.md: The fowler said If you have committed this evil, urged thereto by another, the sin is your also as you are an instrument in the act.

data.v: मृत्पात्रस्य क्रियायां हि दण्डचक्रादयो यथा । कारणत्वे प्रकल्प्यन्ते तथा त्वमपि पन्नग ॥
data.md: As in the making of an earthen pot the potter's wheel and rod and other things are all considered as causes, so are you, O serpent.

data.v: किल्बिषी चापि मे वध्यः किल्बिषी चासि पन्नग । आत्मानं कारणं ह्यत्र त्वमाख्यासि भुजंगम ॥
सर्व एते ह्यस्ववशा दण्डचक्रादयो यथा । तथाहमपि तस्मान्मे नैष हेतुर्मतस्तव ॥
अथ वा मतमेतत्ते तेऽप्यन्योन्यप्रयोजकाः । कार्यकारणसंदेहो भवत्यन्योन्यचोदनात् ॥
data.md: If you hold otherwise, then these are to be considered as causes working with one another. For thus working with one other, a doubt springs up about their relation as cause and effect.

data.v: एवं सति न दोषो मे नास्मि वध्यो न किल्बिषी । किल्बिषं समवाये स्यान्मन्यसे यदि किल्बिषम् ॥
data.md: Such being the case, it is no fault of mine, nor should I be killed on this account, nor am I guilty of any sin! Or, if you think that there is sin, the sin lies in the aggregate of causes.

data.v: कारणं यदि न स्याद्वै न कर्ता स्यास्त्वमप्युत । विनाशे कारणं त्वं च तस्माद्वध्योऽसि मे मतः ॥
data.md: The fowler said If you are neither the principal cause nor the agent in this matter: you are still the cause of the death. Therefore, I think you should be killed.

data.v: असत्यपि कृते कार्ये नेह पन्नग लिप्यते । तस्मान्नात्रैव हेतुः स्याद्वध्यः किं बहु भाषसे ॥
data.md: If, O serpent, you think that when an evil deed is done the doer is not implicated therein, then there can be no cause in this matter: but having done this, you should surely be killed. What more do you think?

data.v: कार्याभावे क्रिया न स्यात्सत्यसत्यपि कारणे । तस्मात्त्वमस्मिन्हेतौ मे वाच्यो हेतुर्विशेषतः ॥
data.md: The serpent said Whether any prime cause exists or not, no effect is done without an (intermediate) act. Therefore, causation being of no importance in either case, my act as the cause should be considered in full.

data.v: यद्यहं कारणत्वेन मतो लुब्धक तत्त्वतः । अन्यः प्रयोगे स्यादत्र किल्बिषी जन्तुनाशने ॥
वध्यस्त्वं मम दुर्बुद्धे बालघाती नृशंसकृत् । भाषसे किं बहु पुनर्वध्यः सन्पन्नगाधम ॥
data.md: The fowler said You don't deserve life, O foolish one, why do you then exchange so many words, O wretched serpent? You should be killed by me. You have done a heinous crime by killing this infant.

data.v: यथा हवींषि जुह्वाना मखे वै लुब्धकर्त्विजः । न फलं प्राप्नुवन्त्यत्र परलोके तथा ह्यहम् ॥
data.md: The serpent said O fowler, as the priests officiating at a sacrifice do not gain the merit of the act by offering oblations of clarified butter to the fire, so should I be considered in this matter.

data.v: तथा ब्रुवति तस्मिंस्तु पन्नगे मृत्युचोदिते । आजगाम ततो मृत्युः पन्नगं चाब्रवीदिदम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma continued The serpent directed by Death having said this, Death himself appeared there and addressing the serpent said:

data.v: कालेनाहं प्रणुदितः पन्नग त्वामचूचुदम् । विनाशहेतुर्नास्य त्वमहं वा प्राणिनः शिशोः ॥
data.md: Mrityu said Guided by Kala, I, O serpent, sent you on this mission, and neither are you nor am I the cause of this child's death.

data.v: यथा वायुर्जलधरान्विकर्षति ततस्ततः । तद्वज्जलदवत्सर्प कालस्याहं वशानुगः ॥
data.md: As the clouds are driven hither and thither by the wind I, am, O serpent, moved by Kala.

data.v: सात्त्विका राजसाश्चैव तामसा ये च केचन । भावाः कालात्मकाः सर्वे प्रवर्तन्ते हि जन्तुषु ॥
data.md: All influences of Sattwa, or Rajas, or Tamas, originate from Kala as they work in all creatures.

data.v: जङ्गमाः स्थावराश्चैव दिवि वा यदि वा भुवि । सर्वे कालात्मकाः सर्प कालात्मकमिदं जगत् ॥
data.md: All creatures, mobile and immobile, in heaven, or earth, are pervaded by the influence of Kala. The whole universe, O serpent, is permeated by this same influence of Kala.

data.v: प्रवृत्तयश्च या लोके तथैव च निवृत्तयः । तासां विकृतयो याश्च सर्वं कालात्मकं स्मृतम् ॥
data.md: All acts in this world and all abstentions, as also all their changes, are owing to be influenced by Kala.

data.v: आदित्यश्चन्द्रमा विष्णुरापो वायुः शतक्रतुः । अग्निः खं पृथिवी मित्र ओषध्यो वसवस्तथा ॥
data.md: The Sun, Soma, Vishnu, Water, Wind, the god of a hundred sacrifices, Fire, Sky, Earth, Mitra and Parjanaya, Aditi, and the Vasus, Rivers and Oceans, all existent and nonexistent objects, are created and destroyed by Kala.

data.v: सरितः सागराश्चैव भावाभावौ च पन्नग । सर्वे कालेन सृज्यन्ते ह्रियन्ते च तथा पुनः ॥
एवं ज्ञात्वा कथं मां त्वं सदोषं सर्प मन्यसे । अथ चैवंगते दोषो मयि त्वमपि दोषवान् ॥
data.md: Knowing this, why do you, O serpent, consider me blameable? If I am to be blamed for this, you are also blameable.

data.v: निर्दोषं दोषवन्तं वा न त्वा मृत्यो ब्रवीम्यहम् । त्वयाहं चोदित इति ब्रवीम्येतावदेव तु ॥
data.md: The serpent said I do not, O Mrityu, blame you, nor do I set you free from all blame. I only say that I am directed and influenced by you.

data.v: यदि काले तु दोषोऽस्ति यदि तत्रापि नेष्यते । दोषो नैव परीक्ष्यो मे न ह्यत्राधिकृता वयम् ॥
data.md: If Kala is to be blamed, or, it is not for me to find the fault. We have nor right to do so.

data.v: निर्मोक्षस्त्वस्य दोषस्य मया कार्यो यथा तथा । मृत्यो विदोषः स्यामेव यथा तन्मे प्रयोजनम् ॥
data.md: As it is my duty to absolve myself from this blame, so it is my duty to see that Mrityu is not blamed.

data.v: सर्पोऽथार्जुनकं प्राह श्रुतं ते मृत्युभाषितम् । नानागसं मां पाशेन संतापयितुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: Bhishma continued Then the serpent, addressing Arjunaka said, 'You have heard what Mrityu has said. Therefore, it is not proper for you to torment me, who am innocent, by fettering me with this rope

data.v: मृत्योः श्रुतं मे वचनं तव चैव भुजंगम । नैव तावद्विदोषत्वं भवति त्वयि पन्नग ॥
data.md: The fowler said I have heard, you, O serpent, as well as the words of Mrityu, but these, O serpent, do not set you free from all blame.

data.v: मृत्युस्त्वं चैव हेतुर्हि जन्तोरस्य विनाशने । उभयं कारणं मन्ये न कारणमकारणम् ॥
data.md: Mrityu and you are the causes of this child's death. I regard both of you to be the cause and I do not call that to be the cause which is not truly so.

data.v: धिङ्मृत्युं च दुरात्मानं क्रूरं दुःखकरं सताम् । त्वां चैवाहं वधिष्यामि पापं पापस्य कारणम् ॥
data.md: Accursed be the wicked and vengeful Death that causes misery to the good! I shall also kill you who are sinful and engaged in sinful deeds.

data.v: विवशौ कालवशगावावां तद्दिष्टकारिणौ । नावां दोषेण गन्तव्यौ यदि सम्यक्प्रपश्यसि ॥
data.md: Mrityu said We both are not free, but are dependent on Kala, and are ordained to do our appointed work. You will not blame us if you do consider this matter thoroughly.

data.v: युवामुभौ कालवशौ यदि वै मृत्युपन्नगौ । हर्षक्रोधौ कथं स्यातामेतदिच्छामि वेदितुम् ॥
data.md: The fowler said If you both, O serpent and Mrityu, depend on Kala. I am curious to know how pleasure and anger are caused.

data.v: याः काश्चिदिह चेष्टाः स्युः सर्वाः कालप्रचोदिताः । पूर्वमेवैतदुक्तं हि मया लुब्धक कालतः ॥
तस्मादुभौ कालवशावावां तद्दिष्टकारिणौ । नावां दोषेण गन्तव्यौ त्वया लुब्धक कर्हिचित् ॥
data.md: Mrityu said We both are not free, but are dependent on Kala, and are ordained to do our appointed work. You will not blame us if you do consider this matter thoroughly.

data.v: अथोपगम्य कालस्तु तस्मिन्धर्मार्थसंशये । अब्रवीत्पन्नगं मृत्युं लुब्धमर्जुनकं च तम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Then Kala arrived there where ethics were being discussed, and spoke thus to the serpent and Mrityu and the fowler Arjunaka assembled together.

data.v: नैवाहं नाप्ययं मृत्युर्नायं लुब्धक पन्नगः । किल्बिषी जन्तुमरणे न वयं हि प्रयोजकाः ॥
data.md: Kala said Neither Mrityu, nor this serpent, nor I, O fowler, am guilty of the death of any creature. We are merely the immediate causes of the event. O Arjunaka, the Karma of this child was the exciting cause of our action in this matter.

data.v: अकरोद्यदयं कर्म तन्नोऽर्जुनक चोदकम् । प्रणाशहेतुर्नान्योऽस्य वध्यतेऽयं स्वकर्मणा ॥
data.md: There was no other cause by which this child met its death. It was killed by the result of its own Karma.

data.v: यदनेन कृतं कर्म तेनायं निधनं गतः । विनाशहेतुः कर्मास्य सर्वे कर्मवशा वयम् ॥
data.md: It has met 'with death as the result of its pristine Karma. Its Karma has been the root of its destruction. We all are subject to our respective Karma.

data.v: कर्मदायादवाँल्लोकः कर्मसंबन्धलक्षणः । कर्माणि चोदयन्तीह यथान्योन्यं तथा वयम् ॥
data.md: Karma is a help to salvation as sons are and Karma also expresses virtue and vice in man. We impell one another even acts urge one another.

data.v: यथा मृत्पिण्डतः कर्ता कुरुते यद्यदिच्छति । एवमात्मकृतं कर्म मानवः प्रतिपद्यते ॥
data.md: As men make from a lump of clay whatever they wish to make, so do men come by various results out of Karma.

data.v: यथा छायातपौ नित्यं सुसंबद्धौ निरन्तरम् । तथा कर्म च कर्ता च संबद्धावात्मकर्मभिः ॥
data.md: As light and shadow are connected with each other, so are men related to Karma through their own deeds.

data.v: एवं नाहं न वै मृत्युर्न सर्पो न तथा भवान् । न चेयं ब्राह्मणी वृद्धा शिशुरेवात्र कारणम् ॥
data.md: Therefore, neither are you, nor am I, nor Mrityu, nor the serpent, nor this old Brahmana lady, is the cause of this child's death.

data.v: तस्मिंस्तथा ब्रुवाणे तु ब्राह्मणी गौतमी नृप । स्वकर्मप्रत्ययाँल्लोकान्मत्वार्जुनकमब्रवीत् ॥
data.md: He himself is the cause here. Upon Kala, O king, explaining the matter thus, Gautami, convinced in her mind that men suffer according to their actions, spoke thus to Arjunaka.

data.v: नैव कालो न भुजगो न मृत्युरिह कारणम् । स्वकर्मभिरयं बालः कालेन निधनं गतः ॥
data.md: Gautami said Neither Kala, nor Mrityu, nor the serpent, is the cause here. This child has met with death as the result of its own Karma,

data.v: मया च तत्कृतं कर्म येनायं मे मृतः सुतः । यातु कालस्तथा मृत्युर्मुञ्चार्जुनक पन्नगम् ॥
data.md: I too have so acted that my son has died. Let now Kala and Mrityu retire from there, and do you too, O Arjunaka, set this serpent free.

data.v: ततो यथागतं जग्मुर्मृत्युः कालोऽथ पन्नगः । अभूद्विरोषोऽर्जुनको विशोका चैव गौतमी ॥
data.md: Bhishma continued Then Kala and Mrityu and the serpent returned to their respective places, and Gautami became consoled in mind as also the fowler.

data.v: एतच्छ्रुत्वा शमं गच्छ मा भूश्चिन्तापरो नृप । स्वकर्मप्रत्ययाँल्लोकांस्त्रीन्विद्धि मनुजर्षभ ॥
data.md: Having heard all this, O king, do you forego all grief, and acquire peace of mind! Men attain to heaven or hell as the result of their own Karma.

data.v: न तु त्वया कृतं पार्थ नापि दुर्योधनेन वै । कालेन तत्कृतं विद्धि विहता येन पार्थिवाः ॥
data.md: This evil has neither been of your own creation, nor of Duryodhana's! That these king's of Earth have all been killed, is the work of Kala.

data.v: इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बभूव विगतज्वरः । युधिष्ठिरो महातेजाः पप्रच्छेदं च धर्मवित् ॥
data.md: Vaishampayana said Having heard all this, the powerful and pious Yudhishthira became consoled in mind, and again enquired as follows.

data.v: पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद । श्रुतं मे महदाख्यानमिदं मतिमतां वर ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O wisest of men, O you who are learned in all the scriptures, I have heard, this great story, O foremost of intelligent men!

data.v: भूयस्तु श्रोतुमिच्छामि धर्मार्थसहितं नृप । कथ्यमानं त्वया किंचित्तन्मे व्याख्यातुमर्हसि ॥
data.md: I am desirous of again listening to the recital of some history full of religious instruction, and you should satisfy me.

data.v: केन मृत्युर्गृहस्थेन धर्ममाश्रित्य निर्जितः । इत्येतत्सर्वमाचक्ष्व तत्त्वेन मम पार्थिव ॥
data.md: O king, tell me if any householder has ever succeeded in conquering Death by the practice of virtue! Do you recite this to me in full.

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । यथा मृत्युर्गृहस्थेन धर्ममाश्रित्य निर्जितः ॥
data.md: Regarding it is cited the old story of the conversation between Mrityu and Gautami with Kala and the Fowler and the serpent.

data.v: मनोः प्रजापते राजन्निक्ष्वाकुरभवत्सुतः । तस्य पुत्रशतं जज्ञे नृपतेः सूर्यवर्चसः ॥
data.md: The Prajapati Manu had a son, O king, named Ikshvaku. That king, illustrious as the Sun, begat a hundred sons.

data.v: दशमस्तस्य पुत्रस्तु दशाश्वो नाम भारत । माहिष्मत्यामभूद्राजा धर्मात्मा सत्यविक्रमः ॥
data.md: His tenth son, O Bharata, was named Dashashva, and this virtuous prince of infallible prowess became the king of Mahismati.

data.v: दशाश्वस्य सुतस्त्वासीद्राजा परमधार्मिकः । सत्ये तपसि दाने च यस्य नित्यं रतं मनः ॥
data.md: Dashashva's son, o king, was a pious prince whose mind was continually devoted to the practice of truth and charity and devotion.

data.v: मदिराश्व इति ख्यातः पृथिव्यां पृथिवीपतिः । धनुर्वेदे च वेदे च निरतो योऽभवत्सदा ॥
data.md: He was known by the name of Madirashva and ruled the Earth as her master. He was continually given to the study of the Vedas as also of the science of arms.

data.v: मदिराश्वस्य पुत्रस्तु द्युतिमान्नाम पार्थिवः । महाभागो महातेजा महासत्त्वो महाबलः ॥
data.md: Madirashva's son was the king named Dyutimat who was ended with great good fortune and power and strength and energy.

data.v: पुत्रो द्युतिमतस्त्वासीत्सुवीरो नाम पार्थिवः । धर्मात्मा कोशवांश्चापि देवराज इवापरः ॥
सुवीरस्य तु पुत्रोऽभूत्सर्वसंग्रामदुर्जयः । दुर्जयेत्यभिविख्यातः सर्वशास्त्रविशारदः ॥
दुर्जयस्येन्द्रवपुषः पुत्रोऽग्निसदृशद्युतिः । दुर्योधनो नाम महान्राजासीद्राजसत्तम ॥
तस्येन्द्रसमवीर्यस्य संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिनः । विषयश्च प्रभावश्च तुल्यमेवाभ्यवर्तत ॥
रत्नैर्धनैश्च पशुभिः सस्यैश्चापि पृथग्विधैः । नगरं विषयश्चास्य प्रतिपूर्णं तदाभवत् ॥
न तस्य विषये चाभूत्कृपणो नापि दुर्गतः । व्याधितो वा कृशो वापि तस्मिन्नाभून्नरः क्वचित् ॥
सुदक्षिणो मधुरवागनसूयुर्जितेन्द्रियः । धर्मात्मा चानृशंसश्च विक्रान्तोऽथाविकत्थनः ॥
data.md: This king was very intelligent, mild in speech, without envy, a master of his passions, of a righteous soul, full of mercy, gifted with prowess, and not given to boasting.

data.v: यज्वा वदान्यो मेधावी ब्रह्मण्यः सत्यसंगरः । न चावमन्ता दाता च वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ॥
data.md: He celebrated sacrifices, and was selfcontrolled and intelligent, devoted to Brahmanas and Truth. He never humiliated others, and was charitable, and wellread in the Vedas and the Vedanta.

data.v: तं नर्मदा देवनदी पुण्या शीतजला शिवा । चकमे पुरुषश्रेष्ठं स्वेन भावेन भारत ॥
data.md: Auspicious and sacred and of cool waters, the celestial stream Narmada, in her own nature, O Bharata, courted him.

data.v: तस्य जज्ञे तदा नद्यां कन्या राजीवलोचना । नाम्ना सुदर्शना राजन्रूपेण च सुदर्शना ॥
data.md: He begot upon that river, a lotus eyed daughter, named Sudarshana, who was, O king, gifted with great beauty.

data.v: तादृग्रूपा न नारीषु भूतपूर्वा युधिष्ठिर । दुर्योधनसुता यादृगभवद्वरवर्णिनी ॥
data.md: No woman, O Yudhishthira, had been born before, who was so very beautiful as that excellent lady the daughter of Duryodhana.

data.v: तामग्निश्चकमे साक्षाद्राजकन्यां सुदर्शनाम् । भूत्वा च ब्राह्मणः साक्षाद्वरयामास तं नृपम् ॥
data.md: The god Agni himself courted the beautiful princess Sudarshana, and assuming the shape of a Brahmana, O king, sought her hand from the king.

data.v: दरिद्रश्चासवर्णश्च ममायमिति पार्थिवः । न दित्सति सुतां तस्मै तां विप्राय सुदर्शनाम् ॥
data.md: The king was reluctant to give his daughter in marriage to the Brahmana who was poor and not of equal rank with himself.

data.v: ततोऽस्य वितते यज्ञे नष्टोऽभूद्धव्यवाहनः । ततो दुर्योधनो राजा वाक्यमाहर्त्विजस्तदा ॥
data.md: Thereupon Agni disappeared from his great sacrifice. The king, grieved at heart, then addressed the Brahmanas, saying,

data.v: दुष्कृतं मम किं नु स्याद्भवतां वा द्विजर्षभाः । येन नाशं जगामाग्निः कृतं कुपुरुषेष्विव ॥
data.md: What sin have, I you excellent Brahmanas, or you, have committed, that Agni should disappear from this sacrifice, as good done to wicked men vanishes from their estimation.

data.v: न ह्यल्पं दुष्कृतं नोऽस्ति येनाग्निर्नाशमागतः । भवतां वाथ वा मह्यं तत्त्वेनैतद्विमृश्यताम् ॥
data.md: Indeed, we have committed a great iniquity for which Agni has thus disappeared! Either you have committed the sin, or I. Do you fully enquire into the matter.

data.v: एतद्राज्ञो वचः श्रुत्वा विप्रास्ते भरतर्षभ । नियता वाग्यताश्चैव पावकं शरणं ययुः ॥
data.md: Then hearing the king's words, O foremost prince of Bharata's race, the Brahmanas, controlling speech, sought with concentrated faculties the help of the god of fire.

data.v: तान्दर्शयामास तदा भगवान्हव्यवाहनः । स्वं रूपं दीप्तिमत्कृत्वा शरदर्कसमद्युतिः ॥
data.md: The divine carrier of oblations, effugent as the autumnal Sun, appeared before them, covering his self in glorious refulgence.

data.v: ततो महात्मा तानाह दहनो ब्राह्मणर्षभान् । वरयाम्यात्मनोऽर्थाय दुर्योधनसुतामिति ॥
data.md: The great Agni then addressed those excellent Brahmanas, saying, I seek the daughter of Duryodhana for my own self.

data.v: ततस्ते काल्यमुत्थाय तस्मै राज्ञे न्यवेदयन् । ब्राह्मणा विस्मिताः सर्वे यदुक्तं चित्रभानुना ॥
data.md: At this, all those Brahmanas were struck with surprise and rising on the morrow, they told the king what had been said by the firegod.

data.v: ततः स राजा तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं ब्रह्मवादिनाम् । अवाप्य परमं हर्षं तथेति प्राह बुद्धिमान् ॥
data.md: Hearing the words of those Brahmavadins, the wise king was delighted at heart, and said, Be it so! The king sought a boon of Do you, O Agni, be pleased to remain always with us here!

data.v: प्रायाचत नृपः शुल्कं भगवन्तं विभावसुम् । नित्यं सांनिध्यमिह ते चित्रभानो भवेदिति । तमाह भगवानग्निरेवमस्त्विति पार्थिवम् ॥
data.md: Be it so! said the divine Agni to that king. For this reason Agni has always been present in the kingdom of Mahismati to this day, and was seen by Sahadeva in his conquering expedition to the south.

data.v: ततः सांनिध्यमध्यापि माहिष्मत्यां विभावसोः । दृष्टं हि सहदेवेन दिशो विजयता तदा ॥
ततस्तां समलंकृत्य कन्यामहतवाससम् । ददौ दुर्योधनो राजा पावकाय महात्मने ॥
प्रतिजग्राह चाग्निस्तां राजपुत्रीं सुदर्शनाम् । विधिना वेददृष्टेन वसोर्धारामिवाध्वरे ॥
तस्या रूपेण शीलेन कुलेन वपुषा श्रिया । अभवत्प्रीतिमानग्निर्गर्भं तस्यां समादधे ॥
तस्यां समभवत्पुत्रो नाम्नाग्नेयः सुदर्शनः । शिशुरेवाध्यगात्सर्वं स च ब्रह्म सनातनम् ॥
अथौघवान्नाम नृपो नृगस्यासीत्पितामहः । तस्याप्योघवती कन्या पुत्रश्चौघरथोऽभवत् ॥
data.md: There was also a king named Oghavat, who was the grandfather of Nriga. He had a daughter named Oghavati, and a son, too, of the name of Ogharatha born to him.

data.v: तामोघवान्ददौ तस्मै स्वयमोघवतीं सुताम् । सुदर्शनाय विदुषे भार्यार्थे देवरूपिणीम् ॥
data.md: King Oghavat gave his daughter Oghavati, beautiful as a goddess, 10 the learned Sudarshana, for wife.

data.v: स गृहस्थाश्रमरतस्तया सह सुदर्शनः । कुरुक्षेत्रेऽवसद्राजन्नोघवत्या समन्वितः ॥
data.md: Sudarshana, o king, leading the domestic mode of life with Oghavati, used to live in Kurukshetra with her.

data.v: गृहस्थश्चावजेष्यामि मृत्युमित्येव स प्रभो । प्रतिज्ञामकरोद्धीमान्दीप्ततेजा विशां पते ॥
data.md: This intelligent prince of fiery energy took the vow, O lord, of conquering Death by leading the life of a householder.

data.v: तामथौघवतीं राजन्स पावकसुतोऽब्रवीत् । अतिथेः प्रतिकूलं ते न कर्तव्यं कथंचन ॥
data.md: The son of Agni, O king, said to Oghavati Do you never act against the wishes of those who seek our hospitality.

data.v: येन येन च तुष्येत नित्यमेव त्वयातिथिः । अप्यात्मनः प्रदानेन न ते कार्या विचारणा ॥
data.md: You should ungrudgingly welcome the guests, even if you have to offer your own body.

data.v: एतद्व्रतं मम सदा हृदि संपरिवर्तते । गृहस्थानां हि सुश्रोणि नातिथेर्विद्यते परम् ॥
data.md: O beautiful one, I always remember this vow, since for householders, there is no higher virtue than hospitality to guests.

data.v: प्रमाणं यदि वामोरु वचस्ते मम शोभने । इदं वचनमव्यग्रा हृदि त्वं धारयेः सदा ॥
data.md: Do you always remember without ever doubting it, if my words be any authority with you.

data.v: निष्क्रान्ते मयि कल्याणि तथा संनिहितेऽनघे । नातिथिस्तेऽवमन्तव्यः प्रमाणं यद्यहं तव ॥
data.md: O sinless and blessed one, if you have any faith in me, do you never disregard a guest whether I be at your side or at a distance from you.

data.v: तमब्रवीदोघवती यता मूर्ध्नि कृताञ्जलिः । न मे त्वद्वचनात्किंचिदकर्तव्यं कथंचन ॥
data.md: Oghavati placing her clasped hands on her forehead, replied, saying, I shall leave nothing indone of what you order me.

data.md: Then, O king, desiring to overreach Sudarshana, Mrityu began to watch him for Ginding out his short comings.

data.md: Once on a time, when the son of Agni went out fetch fuel from the forest, a graceful Brahmana sought the hospitality of Oghavati with these words.

data.v: आतिथ्यं दत्तमिच्छामि त्वयाद्य वरवर्णिनि । प्रमाणं यदि धर्मस्ते गृहस्थाश्रमसंमतः ॥
data.md: O beautiful lady, if you have any faith in the virtue of hospitality as laid down for householders, then I would request you to extend the rites of hospitality to me today.

data.v: इत्युक्ता तेन विप्रेण राजपुत्री यशस्विनी । विधिना प्रतिजग्राह वेदोक्तेन विशां पते ॥
data.md: Thus addressed by that Brahmana, O king, the illustrious princess welcomed him according to the rites laid down in the Vedas.

data.v: आसनं चैव पाद्यं च तस्मै दत्त्वा द्विजातये । प्रोवाचौघवती विप्रं केनार्थः किं ददामि ते ॥
data.md: Having offered him a seat, and water to wash his feet, she enquired, saying, What is your business? What can I offer you?

data.v: तामब्रवीत्ततो विप्रो राजपुत्रीं सुदर्शनाम् । त्वया ममार्थः कल्याणि निर्विशङ्के तदाचर ॥
data.md: The Brahmana said to her, my business is with your body, O blessed one! Do you act accordingly without any hesitation whatever.

data.v: यदि प्रमाणं धर्मस्ते गृहस्थाश्रमसंमतः । प्रदानेनात्मनो राज्ञि कर्तुमर्हसि मे प्रियम् ॥
data.md: If the duties prescribed for householders be acceptable to you, do you, O princess, satisfy me by offering up your body to me.

data.v: तथा संछन्द्यमानोऽन्यैरीप्सितैर्नृपकन्यया । नान्यमात्मप्रदानात्स तस्या वव्रे वरं द्विजः ॥
data.md: Though tempted by the princess witi, offers of various other things, the Brahmana, however, did not seek the Brahmana, however, did not seek any thing else than the offer of her own person.

data.v: सा तु राजसुता स्मृत्वा भर्तुर्वचनमादितः । तथेति लज्जमाना सा तमुवाच द्विजर्षभम् ॥
data.md: Finding him determined, that lady, recollecting the directions given to her by her husband, but filled with shame, said to that excellent Brahmana Be it so.

data.v: ततो रहः स विप्रर्षिः सा चैवोपविवेश ह । संस्मृत्य भर्तुर्वचनं गृहस्थाश्रमकाङ्क्षिणः ॥
data.md: Recollecting the words of her husband who was desirous of acquiring the virtue of householders, she cheerfully approached the i twiceborn Rishi.

data.v: अथेध्मान्समुपादाय स पावकिरुपागमत् । मृत्युना रौद्रभावेन नित्यं बन्धुरिवान्वितः ॥
data.md: Meanwhile, the son of Agni, having collected fuel, returned to his home. Mrityu, with his dreadful and inexorable nature, was always by his side, as one attends upon his devoted friend.

data.v: ततस्त्वाश्रममागम्य स पावकसुतस्तदा । तामाजुहावौघवतीं क्वासि यातेति चासकृत् ॥
data.md: When the son of Pavaka returned to his own asylum, he called out for Oghavati by name, and repeatedly exclaimed Where are you gone?

data.v: तस्मै प्रतिवचः सा तु भर्त्रे न प्रददौ तदा । कराभ्यां तेन विप्रेण स्पृष्टा भर्तृव्रता सती ॥
data.md: But the chaste lady, devoted to her husband, being then in the arms of that Brahmana, gave no reply to her husband.

data.v: उच्छिष्टास्मीति मन्वाना लज्जिता भर्तुरेव च । तूष्णींभूताभवत्साध्वी न चोवाचाथ किंचन ॥
data.md: Indeed, considering herself sullied, that chaste woman became speechless, overcome with shame.

data.v: अथ तां पुनरेवेदं प्रोवाच स सुदर्शनः । क्व सा साध्वी क्व सा याता गरीयः किमतो मम ॥
data.md: Sudarshana, addressing her again, exclaimed Where can my chaste wife be? Where has she gone? Nothing can be so very important to me than this.

data.md: Why does not that simple and truthful lady, devoted to her husband, alas reply as she used to do before with sweet smiles.

data.v: उटजस्थस्तु तं विप्रः प्रत्युवाच सुदर्शनम् । अतिथिं विद्धि संप्राप्तं पावके ब्राह्मणं च माम् ॥

data.md: Armed with the iron club, death pursued the Rishi at that moment, desirous of bringing about the destruction of one who would, he thought, deviate from his promise.

data.v: सुदर्शनस्तु मनसा कर्मणा चक्षुषा गिरा । त्यक्तेर्ष्यस्त्यक्तमन्युश्च स्मयमानोऽब्रवीदिदम् ॥
data.md: Sudarshana was struck with wonder, but renouncing all, jealousy and anger by look, word, deed, or thought, said Do you enjoy yourself, O Brahmana! It is a great pleasure to me! A householder acquires the highest merit by honouring a guest.

data.md: Sudarshana was struck with wonder, but renouncing all, jealousy and anger by look, word, deed, or thought, said Do you enjoy yourself, O Brahmana! It is a great pleasure to me! A householder acquires the highest merit by honouring a guest.

data.v: अतिथिः पूजितो यस्य गृहस्थस्य तु गच्छति । नान्यस्तस्मात्परो धर्म इति प्राहुर्मनीषिणः ॥
data.md: The learned say that to the householders, there is no higher merit than what comes from a guest leaving his house after having been duly honoured by him.

data.v: प्राणा हि मम दाराश्च यच्चान्यद्विद्यते वसु । अतिथिभ्यो मया देयमिति मे व्रतमाहितम् ॥
data.md: My life, my wife and all my earthly belongings, are all dedicated to the use of my guests! This is the vow that I have taken.

data.v: निःसंदिग्धं मया वाक्यमेतत्ते समुदाहृतम् । तेनाहं विप्र सत्येन स्वयमात्मानमालभे ॥
data.md: As I have truly made this statement, by that truth, O Brahmana, I shall acquire the knowledge of Self.

data.v: पृथिवी वायुराकाशमापो ज्योतिश्च पञ्चमम् । बुद्धिरात्मा मनः कालो दिशश्चैव गुणा दश ॥
data.md: O foremost of the virtuous, the five elements, viz., fire, air, earth, water, and sky, and the mind, the intellect and the Soul, and time and space and the ten organs of sense, are all in the bodies of men and always witness the good and evil deeds of men.

data.v: नित्यमेते हि पश्यन्ति देहिनां देहसंश्रिताः । सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चापि कर्म धर्मभृतां वर ॥
data.md: O foremost of the virtuous, the five elements, viz., fire, air, earth, water, and sky, and the mind, the intellect and the Soul, and time and space and the ten organs of sense, are all in the bodies of men and always witness the good and evil deeds of men.

data.v: यथैषा नानृता वाणी मयाद्य समुदाहृता । तेन सत्येन मां देवाः पालयन्तु दहन्तु वा ॥
data.md: This truth I have spoken today, and let the gods bless me for it or destroy me if I have spoken an untruth.

data.md: At this, O Bharata, there arose from all sides, in repeated echoes, a voice, crying This is true, this is not false.

data.md: Then that Brahmana came out of the hovel, and like the wind rising and covering both Earth and sky, and making the three worlds echo with Vedic recitations, and calling that virtuous man by name, and congratulating him, said:
