data.md: Then that Brahmana came out of the hovel, and like the wind rising and covering both Earth and sky, and making the three worlds echo with Vedic recitations, and calling that virtuous man by name, and congratulating him, said:

data.v: धर्मोऽहमस्मि भद्रं ते जिज्ञासार्थं तवानघ । प्राप्तः सत्यं च ते ज्ञात्वा प्रीतिर्मे परमा त्वयि ॥
data.md: O sinless one, I am Dharma! All glory to you! I came here, O truthloving one, to try you, and I am well pleased with you by knowing you to be virtuous.

data.v: विजितश्च त्वया मृत्युर्योऽयं त्वामनुगच्छति । रन्ध्रान्वेषी तव सदा त्वया धृत्या वशीकृतः ॥
data.md: You have controlled and conquered Death who always has pursued you, seeking your shortcomings.

data.v: न चास्ति शक्तिस्त्रैलोक्ये कस्यचित्पुरुषोत्तम । पतिव्रतामिमां साध्वीं तवोद्वीक्षितुमप्युत ॥
data.md: O best of men, no one in the three worlds has the power to insult, even with looks, this chaste lady devoted to her husband, far less to touch her body.

data.v: रक्षिता त्वद्गुणैरेषा पतिव्रतगुणैस्तथा । अधृष्या यदियं ब्रूयात्तथा तन्नान्यथा भवेत् ॥
data.md: She has been saved from contamination by your virtue and by her own chastity. There can be nothing against what this proud lady will say.

data.v: एषा हि तपसा स्वेन संयुक्ता ब्रह्मवादिनी । पावनार्थं च लोकस्य सरिच्छ्रेष्ठा भविष्यति ॥
data.md: This Brahmavadin, gifted with austere penances, shall, for the salvation of the world, be changed into a powerful river.

data.v: अर्धेनौघवती नाम त्वामर्धेनानुयास्यति । शरीरेण महाभागा योगो ह्यस्या वशे स्थितः ॥
data.md: And you will acquire all the worlds in this your body, and because the science of Yoga is within her control, this highly blessed lady will follow you with only half her body, and with the other half will she be celebrated as the river Oghavati.

data.v: अनया सह लोकांश्च गन्तासि तपसार्जितान् । यत्र नावृत्तिमभ्येति शाश्वतांस्तान्सनातनान् ॥
data.md: And you will acquire with her all the worlds that are acquired by penances.

data.v: अनेन चैव देहेन लोकांस्त्वमभिपत्स्यसे । निर्जितश्च त्वया मृत्युरैश्वर्यं च तवोत्तमम् ॥
data.md: You will acquire even in this material body those eternal and everlasting worlds from which none return.

data.v: पञ्च भूतान्यतिक्रान्तः स्ववीर्याच्च मनोभवः । गृहस्थधर्मेणानेन कामक्रोधौ च ते जितौ ॥
data.md: You have conquered Death, "and acquired the highest happiness and by your own power (of mind), attaining to the speed of thought, you have transcended the five elements.

data.v: स्नेहो रागश्च तन्द्री च मोहो द्रोहश्च केवलः । तव शुश्रूषया राजन्राजपुत्र्या विनिर्जिताः ॥
data.md: By thus following the duties of a householder, you have conquered your passions, desires, and anger and this princess, O best of virtuous men, has by serving you, conquered affliction, desire, illusion, enmity and lassitude of mind.

data.v: शुक्लानां तु सहस्रेण वाजिनां रथमुत्तमम् । युक्तं प्रगृह्य भगवान्व्यवसायो जगाम तम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Then, riding in a fine chariot drawn by a thousand white steeds, the glorious Vasava approached that Brahmana.

data.v: मृत्युरात्मा च लोकाश्च जिता भूतानि पञ्च च । बुद्धिः कालो मनो व्योम कामक्रोधौ तथैव च ॥
data.md: Therefore, O best of men, do you remember that a to householder there is no greater god than the guest.

data.v: तस्माद्गृहाश्रमस्थस्य नान्यद्दैवतमस्ति वै । ऋतेऽतिथिं नरव्याघ्र मनसैतद्विचारय ॥
data.md: The learned say that the blessings of an honoured guest are more fruitful than the merit of a hundred sacrifices.

data.md: The learned say that the blessings of an honoured guest are more fruitful than the merit of a hundred sacrifices.

data.v: पात्रं त्वतिथिमासाद्य शीलाढ्यं यो न पूजयेत् । स दत्त्वा सुकृतं तस्य क्षपयेत ह्यनर्चितः ॥
data.md: Whenever a deserving guest seeks the hospitality of a householder and is not respected by him, he takes away all the virtues of the latter giving him his sins.

data.v: एतत्ते कथितं पुत्र मयाख्यानमनुत्तमम् । यथा हि विजितो मृत्युर्गृहस्थेन पुराभवत् ॥
data.md: I have now recited to you, my son, this excellent story as to how Death was conquered in days of yore by a householder.

data.v: धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यमिदमाख्यानमुत्तमम् । बुभूषताभिमन्तव्यं सर्वदुश्चरितापहम् ॥
data.md: The recital of this excellent story gives glory, fame, and longevity. The man who seeks worldly prosperity should consider it as powerful in removing all evil.

data.v: य इदं कथयेद्विद्वानहन्यहनि भारत । सुदर्शनस्य चरितं पुण्याँल्लोकानवाप्नुयात् ॥
data.md: And, O Bharata, the learned man who daily recites this story of the life of Sudarshana acquires blessed regions.

data.v: ब्राह्मण्यं यदि दुष्प्रापं त्रिभिर्वर्णैर्नराधिप । कथं प्राप्तं महाराज क्षत्रियेण महात्मना ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said If, O prince, it is so very difficult for the other three castes to acquire Brahmanahood, how then did the great Vishvasmitra, O king, though a Kshatriya, acquire the status of a Brahmana? I desire to know this, O sire! Therefore, do you truly describe this matter to me.

data.v: विश्वामित्रेण धर्मात्मन्ब्राह्मणत्वं नरर्षभ । श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वेन तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥

data.md: O Sire, by virtue of his austerities that powerful man destroyed in a moment the hundred sons of the great Vasishtha.

data.md: Having been sought to be killed as an animal in the great sacrifice of Amvarisha, Shunashepha of austere penances the son of Richika acquired his deliverance through Vishvamitra.

data.md: These and many others are his feats. O descendant of Kuru, my curiosity has been kindled in this respect, because they were performed by a Kshstriya.

data.md: Bhishma said Listen truly in full, O son of Pritha, how, in days of yore, Vishvamitra acquired the status of a Brahmana, as also of a Brahmana Rishi!

data.md: There was O foremost of Bharata's descendants, in the family of Bharata, a king named Ajamida, who celebrated many sacrifices and was the best of all virtuous men.

data.v: तस्य पुत्रो महानासीज्जह्नुर्नाम नरेश्वरः । दुहितृत्वमनुप्राप्ता गङ्गा यस्य महात्मनः ॥
data.md: His son was the great king named Jahnu. Ganga was the daughter of this great prince.

data.md: The far-fained and equally virtuous Sindhudvipa was the son of this prince. From Sindhudvipa sprang the great royal sage Valakashva.

data.md: His son was named Vallabha who was like a second Dharina incarnate. His son was Kushika who was illustrious like the thousandeyed Indra.

data.v: कुशिकस्यात्मजः श्रीमान्गाधिर्नाम जनेश्वरः । अपुत्रः स महाबाहुर्वनवासमुदावसत् ॥
data.md: Kushika's son was the illustrious king Gadhi who, being childless and wishing to have a son born to him, went to the forest.

data.v: कन्या जज्ञे सुता तस्य वने निवसतः सतः । नाम्ना सत्यवती नाम रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि ॥
data.md: While living there, a daughter was born to him. She was called Satyavati, and she was peerless in beauty on Earth.

data.v: तां वव्रे भार्गवः श्रीमांश्च्यवनस्यात्मजः प्रभुः । ऋचीक इति विख्यातो विपुले तपसि स्थितः ॥
data.md: The illustrious son of Chyavana, known by the name of Richika, of the family of Bhrigu, gifted with austere penance's, sought the hand of this lady.

data.v: स तां न प्रददौ तस्मै ऋचीकाय महात्मने । दरिद्र इति मत्वा वै गाधिः शत्रुनिबर्हणः ॥
data.md: Thinking him to be poor, Gadhi, the destroyer of his enemies, did not bestow her in marriage upon the great Richika.

data.v: प्रत्याख्याय पुनर्यान्तमब्रवीद्राजसत्तमः । शुल्कं प्रदीयतां मह्यं ततो वेत्स्यसि मे सुताम् ॥
data.md: But when the latter, thus dismissed, was going away, the excellent king, addressing him, said If you can give me a marriage dower you will have my daughter as your wife!

data.v: किं प्रयच्छामि राजेन्द्र तुभ्यं शुल्कमहं नृप । दुहितुर्ब्रूह्यसंसक्तो मात्राभूत्ते विचारणा ॥
data.md: Richika said What dower, O king, shall I offer you for the hand of your daughter? Tell me truly, without any hesitation whatsoever! Gadhi said, O Descendant of Bhrigu, give me a thousand horses quickcoursing as the wind, and possessing the colour of moonbeams, and each having one ear black.

data.v: एकतः श्यामकर्णानां हयानां चन्द्रवर्चसाम् । सहस्रं वातवेगानां भिक्षे त्वां देवसत्तम ॥

data.md: The god Varuna, the son of Aditi, said to that scion Bhrigu's race Be it so! Whenever you will seek, the horses shall come. As soon as Richika thought of them, there came from the waters of Ganga a thousand highborn horses, as effulgent as the moon.

data.md: The god Varuna, the son of Aditi, said to that scion Bhrigu's race Be it so! Whenever you will seek, the horses shall come. As soon as Richika thought of them, there came from the waters of Ganga a thousand highborn horses, as effulgent as the moon.

data.md: Not far from Kanyakuvja, the sacred bank of Ganga is still famous among men as Ashvatirtha on account of the appearance of those horses.

data.md: Then Richika, that best of ascetics, pleased in mind, gave those thousand excellent horses to Gadhi as the marriage gift.

data.v: ततः स विस्मितो राजा गाधिः शापभयेन च । ददौ तां समलंकृत्य कन्यां भृगुसुताय वै ॥
data.md: King Gadhi, stricken with wonder and fearing to be cursed, gave his daughter, adorned with jewels, to that son of Bhrigu.

data.md: That foremost of twiceborn Rishis accepted her hand in marriage according to due rites. The princes too was wellpleased at seeing herself the wife of that Brahmana.

data.md: Then, O king, returning speedily to her husband Richika, the princess described to him all that had been wished for by her mother.

data.v: गुणवन्तमपत्यं वै त्वं च सा जनयिष्यथः । जनन्यास्तव कल्याणि मा भूद्वै प्रणयोऽन्यथा ॥
data.md: By my favour, O blessed one, she will soon give birth to a son gifted with every virtue! May your request be fulfilled!

data.v: तव चैव गुणश्लाघी पुत्र उत्पत्स्यते शुभे । अस्मद्वंशकरः श्रीमांस्तव भ्राता च वंशकृत् ॥
data.md: Of you too shall be born a powerful and glorious son who, gifted with virtue, shall perpetuate my race. Truly do I say this to you.

data.v: ऋतुस्नाता च साश्वत्थं त्वं च वृक्षमुदुम्बरम् । परिष्वजेथाः कल्याणि तत इष्टमवाप्स्यथः ॥
data.md: When you two shall bathe in your season, she shall embrace a pepul tree, and you, O excellent lady, shall embrace a fig tree, and by so doing you shall have the fruition of your desires.

data.v: चरुद्वयमिदं चैव मन्त्रपूतं शुचिस्मिते । त्वं च सा चोपयुञ्जीथां ततः पुत्राववाप्स्यथः ॥
data.md: O sweetlysmiling lady, both she and you shall have to partake of these two sacrificial offerings (charu) consecrated with hymns, and then you shall get sons.

data.v: ततः सत्यवती हृष्टा मातरं प्रत्यभाषत । यदृचीकेन कथितं तच्चाचख्यौ चरुद्वयम् ॥
data.md: Thereat, Satyavati, pleased at heart, told her mother all that had been said by Richika as also of the two balls of charu.

data.v: तामुवाच ततो माता सुतां सत्यवतीं तदा । पुत्रि मूर्ध्ना प्रपन्नायाः कुरुष्व वचनं मम ॥
data.md: Then the mother, addressing her daughter Satyavati, said: O daughter, as I deserve greater respect from you than your husband, do you obey my words.

data.v: भर्त्रा य एष दत्तस्ते चरुर्मन्त्रपुरस्कृतः । एतं प्रयच्छ मह्यं त्वं मदीयं त्वं गृहाण च ॥
data.md: Do you give me the charu, duly consecrated with hymns, which your husband has given you, and yourself take, the one that has been intended for me.

data.v: व्यत्यासं वृक्षयोश्चापि करवाव शुचिस्मिते । यदि प्रमाणं वचनं मम मातुरनिन्दिते ॥
data.md: O sweetlysmiling one of pure character, if you have any reverence for my word, let us change the trees respectively intended for us.

data.v: व्यक्तं भगवता चात्र कृतमेवं भविष्यति । ततो मे त्वच्चरौ भावः पादपे च सुमध्यमे । कथं विशिष्टो भ्राता ते भवेदित्येव चिन्तय ॥
data.md: Therefore, O beautiful girl, my heart is bent upon your charu and tree, and you too should also try to secure an excellent brother for yourself.

data.v: तथा च कृतवत्यौ ते माता सत्यवती च सा । अथ गर्भावनुप्राप्ते उभे ते वै युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: The mother and the daughter Satyavati having acted thus, they both, O Yudhishthira, became big with child.

data.v: दृष्ट्वा गर्भमनुप्राप्तां भार्यां स च महानृषिः । उवाच तां सत्यवतीं दुर्मना भृगुसत्तमः ॥
data.md: Finding his wife quick with child, that great Rishi, the descendant of Bhrigu, became pleased at heart, and addressing her, said:

data.v: व्यत्यासेनोपयुक्तस्ते चरुर्व्यक्तं भविष्यति । व्यत्यासः पादपे चापि सुव्यक्तं ते कृतः शुभे ॥
data.md: O excellent lady, you have not done well in exchanging the charu as will soon be seen. It is also clear that you have changed the trees.

data.v: मया हि विश्वं यद्ब्रह्म त्वच्चरौ संनिवेशितम् । क्षत्रवीर्यं च सकलं चरौ तस्या निवेशितम् ॥
data.md: I had put the entire accuinulated energy of Brahma in your charu and Kshatriya energy in the charu of your mother.

data.v: त्रिलोकविख्यातगुणं त्वं विप्रं जनयिष्यसि । सा च क्षत्रं विशिष्टं वै तत एतत्कृतं मया ॥
data.md: I had so settled that you would give birth to a Brahmana whose virtues would be famous throughout the three worlds, and that she would give birth to an excellent Kshatriya.

data.v: व्यत्यासस्तु कृतो यस्मात्त्वया मात्रा तथैव च । तस्मात्सा ब्राह्मणश्रेष्ठं माता ते जनयिष्यति ॥

data.md: But now, O excellent lady, as you have changed the order (of the charu so), your mother give birth to an excellent Brahmana, and you too, O excellent lady, will give birth to a Kshatriya of dreadful deeds. You have not done well, O lady, by doing this out of affection for your mother.

data.v: सा श्रुत्वा शोकसंतप्ता पपात वरवर्णिनी । भूमौ सत्यवती राजंश्छिन्नेव रुचिरा लता ॥
data.md: Hearing this, O king, the excellent lady Satyavati, filled with sorrow, dropped upon the ground like a beautiful creeper cut in two parts.

data.v: प्रतिलभ्य च सा संज्ञां शिरसा प्रणिपत्य च । उवाच भार्या भर्तारं गाधेयी ब्राह्मणर्षभम् ॥

data.md: Regaining her senses and bowing to her lord with head (bent), the daughter of Gadhi said to her husband, that foremost one of Bhrigu's race'O twiceborn Rishi, O you who are foremost amongst those versed in Brahma, have mercy on me, your wife, who is thus appeasing you and so order that a Kshatriya son may not be born to me.

data.v: कामं ममोग्रकर्मा वै पौत्रो भवितुमर्हति । न तु मे स्यात्सुतो ब्रह्मन्नेष मे दीयतां वरः ॥
data.md: Let my grandson be such a one as will be farnous for his dreadful feats if it be your desire, but not my son, O Brahmana! Do you grant me this favour.

data.v: एवमस्त्विति होवाच स्वां भार्यां सुमहातपाः । ततः सा जनयामास जमदग्निं सुतं शुभम् ॥
data.md: Be it so, said that Rishi of austere penances to his wife and then, O king, she gave birth to a blessed son named Jamadagni.

data.v: विश्वामित्रं चाजनयद्गाधेर्भार्या यशस्विनी । ऋषेः प्रभावाद्राजेन्द्र ब्रह्मर्षिं ब्रह्मवादिनम् ॥
data.md: The famous wife of Gadhi too gave birth to the twiceborn Rishi Vishvamitra versed in the knowledge of Brahma, by favour of that Rishi.

data.v: ततो ब्राह्मणतां यातो विश्वामित्रो महातपाः । क्षत्रियः सोऽप्यथ तथा ब्रह्मवंशस्य कारकः ॥
data.md: The highly pious Vishvamitra, though a Kshatriya, gained the dignity of a Brahmana and became the founder of a race of Brahmanas.

data.v: तस्य पुत्रा महात्मानो ब्रह्मवंशविवर्धनाः । तपस्विनो ब्रह्मविदो गोत्रकर्तार एव च ॥
data.md: His sons became great progenitors of many race of Brahmanas who were given to austere penances, learned in the Vedas, and founders of many clans.

data.v: मधुच्छन्दश्च भगवान्देवरातश्च वीर्यवान् । अक्षीणश्च शकुन्तश्च बभ्रुः कालपथस्तथा ॥
याज्ञवल्क्यश्च विख्यातस्तथा स्थूणो महाव्रतः । उलूको यमदूतश्च तथर्षिः सैन्धवायनः ॥
कर्णजङ्घश्च भगवान्गालवश्च महानृषिः । ऋषिर्वज्रस्तथाख्यातः शालङ्कायन एव च ॥
लालाट्यो नारदश्चैव तथा कूर्चमुखः स्मृतः । वादुलिर्मुसलश्चैव रक्षोग्रीवस्तथैव च ॥
अङ्घ्रिको नैकभृच्चैव शिलायूपः सितः शुचिः । चक्रको मारुतन्तव्यो वातघ्नोऽथाश्वलायनः ॥
श्यामायनोऽथ गार्ग्यश्च जाबालिः सुश्रुतस्तथा । कारीषिरथ संश्रुत्यः परपौरवतन्तवः ॥
महानृषिश्च कपिलस्तथर्षिस्तारकायनः । तथैव चोपगहनस्तथर्षिश्चार्जुनायनः ॥
मार्गमित्रिर्हिरण्याक्षो जङ्घारिर्बभ्रुवाहनः । सूतिर्विभूतिः सूतश्च सुरङ्गश्च तथैव हि ॥
आराद्धिर्नामयश्चैव चाम्पेयोज्जयनौ तथा । नवतन्तुर्बकनखः शयोनरतिरेव च ॥
शयोरुहश्चारुमत्स्यः शिरीषी चाथ गार्दभिः । उज्जयोनिरदापेक्षी नारदी च महानृषिः । विश्वामित्रात्मजाः सर्वे मुनयो ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥
तन्नैष क्षत्रियो राजन्विश्वामित्रो महातपाः । ऋचीकेनाहितं ब्रह्म परमेतद्युधिष्ठिर ॥
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं तत्त्वेन भरतर्षभ । विश्वामित्रस्य वै जन्म सोमसूर्याग्नितेजसः ॥
यत्र यत्र च संदेहो भूयस्ते राजसत्तम । तत्र तत्र च मां ब्रूहि च्छेत्तास्मि तव संशयान् ॥
data.md: 0 best of kings, if you have any doubt about any other subject, please let me know it, so that I may remove it.

data.v: आनृशंसस्य धर्मस्य गुणान्भक्तजनस्य च । श्रोतुमिच्छामि कार्त्स्न्येन तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said O you who know the truths of religion, I wish to hear of the merits of religion, I wish to hear of the merits of mercy, and of the marks of devout men! Do you, O sire, describe them to me.

data.v: विषये काशिराजस्य ग्रामान्निष्क्रम्य लुब्धकः । सविषं काण्डमादाय मृगयामास वै मृगम् ॥
data.md: In the dominion of the king of Kashi, a fowler, having poisoned arrows with him, went out of his village on hunting expedition in search of antelopes.

data.v: तत्र चामिषलुब्धेन लुब्धकेन महावने । अविदूरे मृगं दृष्ट्वा बाणः प्रतिसमाहितः ॥
data.md: Desirous of getting meat, when in a big forest in pursuit of the chase, he saw a drove of antelopes near at hand, and shot his arrow at one of them.

data.v: तेन दुर्वारितास्त्रेण निमित्तचपलेषुणा । महान्वनतरुर्विद्धो मृगं तत्र जिघांसता ॥
data.md: The arrow of that fowler of irresistible arms, shot for the destruction of the antelope, missing its aim, pierced a powerful foresttree.

data.v: स तीक्ष्णविषदिग्धेन शरेणातिबलात्कृतः । उत्सृज्य फलपत्राणि पादपः शोषमागतः ॥
data.md: The tree, pierced with that arrow covered with dreadful poison, withered away, shedding its leaves and fruits.

data.v: तस्मिन्वृक्षे तथाभूते कोटरेषु चिरोषितः । न जहाति शुको वासं तस्य भक्त्या वनस्पतेः ॥
data.md: The tree having thus withered, a parrot which had lived in a hollow of its trunk all his life, did not leave his nest out of affection for that lordly tree.

data.v: निष्प्रचारो निराहारो ग्लानः शिथिलवागपि । कृतज्ञः सह वृक्षेण धर्मात्मा स व्यशुष्यत ॥
data.md: Motionless starving, silent and sorrowful, that grateful and virtuous parrot also withered away with the tree.

data.v: तमुदारं महासत्त्वमतिमानुषचेष्टितम् । समदुःखसुखं ज्ञात्वा विस्मितः पाकशासनः ॥
data.md: The conqueror of Paka (Indra) was filled with wonder upon seeing that great and generous bird thus uninfluenced by misery or happiness and possessing extraordinary resolution.

data.v: ततश्चिन्तामुपगतः शक्रः कथमयं द्विजः । तिर्यग्योनावसंभाव्यमानृशंस्यं समास्थितः ॥
data.md: Then Shakra thought, How could this bird come to possess such humane and generous feelings which cannot be seen in one of the lower animal creation?

data.v: अथ वा नात्र चित्रं हीत्यभवद्वासवस्य तु । प्राणिनामिह सर्वेषां सर्वं सर्वत्र दृश्यते ॥
data.md: There is nothing wonderful in the matter, for all crcatures are seen to show kindly and generous feelings towards others.

data.v: ततो ब्राह्मणवेषेण मानुषं रूपमास्थितः । अवतीर्य महीं शक्रस्तं पक्षिणमुवाच ह ॥
data.md: Assuming then the shape of a Brahmana, Shakra went on the Earth and addressing the bird, said:

data.v: शुक भोः पक्षिणां श्रेष्ठ दाक्षेयी सुप्रजास्त्वया । पृच्छे त्वा शुष्कमेतं वै कस्मान्न त्यजसि द्रुमम् ॥
data.md: O Suka, O best of birds, the granddaughter of Daksha has become blessed (by having you as her offspring)! I ask you, why do you not leave this withered tree?

data.v: अथ पृष्टः शुकः प्राह मूर्ध्ना समभिवाद्य तम् । स्वागतं देवराजाय विज्ञातस्तपसा मया ॥
data.md: Thus accosted, the Shuka bowed to him and thus replied: Welcome to you, O king of the gods, I have recognised you by the merit of my austere penances.

data.v: ततो दशशताक्षेण साधु साध्विति भाषितम् । अहो विज्ञानमित्येवं तपसा पूजितस्ततः ॥
data.md: Well-done, well-done! said the thousandeyed god. Then the latter lauded him in his mind, saying 0, how wonderful is the knowledge which he possesses.

data.v: तमेवं शुभकर्माणं शुकं परमधार्मिकम् । विजानन्नपि तां प्राप्तिं पप्रच्छ बलसूदनः ॥
data.md: Although the destroyer of Vala knew that parrot to be of a greatly virtuous character and meritorious in action, he still enquired of him about the reason of his love for the tree.

data.v: निष्पत्रमफलं शुष्कमशरण्यं पतत्रिणाम् । किमर्थं सेवसे वृक्षं यदा महदिदं वनम् ॥
data.md: This tree is withered and it is without leaves and fruits, and is unfit to be the refuge of birds. Why do you then cling to it? This forest too is vast and in this wilderness there are numberless other good trees whose hollows are covered with leaves and which you can choose freely and to your heart's content.

data.v: अन्येऽपि बहवो वृक्षाः पत्रसंछन्नकोटराः । शुभाः पर्याप्तसंचारा विद्यन्तेऽस्मिन्महावने ॥
data.md: This tree is withered and it is without leaves and fruits, and is unfit to be the refuge of birds. Why do you then cling to it? This forest too is vast and in this wilderness there are numberless other good trees whose hollows are covered with leaves and which you can choose freely and to your heart's content.

data.v: गतायुषमसामर्थ्यं क्षीणसारं हतश्रियम् । विमृश्य प्रज्ञया धीर जहीमं ह्यस्थिरं द्रुमम् ॥
data.md: patient one, displaying proper discrimination in your wisdom, do you leave this old tree that is dead and useless and shorn of all its leaves and no longer capable of any good.

data.v: तदुपश्रुत्य धर्मात्मा शुकः शक्रेण भाषितम् । सुदीर्घमभिनिःश्वस्य दीनो वाक्यमुवाच ह ॥
data.md: Bhishma said Hearing these words of Shakra, the virtuous Shuka, heaved a deep sigh, and sorrowfully replied to him, saying O husband of Sachi, and chief of the gods, the ordinances of the gods should always be obeyed. Do you hear of the reason of the thing about which you have asked me.

data.v: अनतिक्रमणीयानि दैवतानि शचीपते । यत्राभवस्तत्र भवस्तन्निबोध सुराधिप ॥
अस्मिन्नहं द्रुमे जातः साधुभिश्च गुणैर्युतः । बालभावे च संगुप्तः शत्रुभिश्च न धर्षितः ॥
data.md: Here, within this tree, was I born and here in this tree have all the good traits of my character been developed, and here in this tree was I protected in my infancy from the attacks of my enemies.

data.v: किमनुक्रोशवैफल्यमुत्पादयसि मेऽनघ । आनृशंस्येऽनुरक्तस्य भक्तस्यानुगतस्य च ॥
data.md: O sinless one, why are you, in your kindness, interfering with the principle of my conduct in life? I am merciful and devoutly intent on virtue, and firm in conduct.

data.v: अनुक्रोशो हि साधूनां सुमहद्धर्मलक्षणम् । अनुक्रोशश्च साधूनां सदा प्रीतिं प्रयच्छति ॥
data.md: Kindliness of feeling is the highest test of virtue amongst the good, and this same merciful and humane feeling is the source of eternal happiness to the virtuous,

data.v: त्वमेव दैवतैः सर्वैः पृच्छ्यसे धर्मसंशयान् । अतस्त्वं देव देवानामाधिपत्ये प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
data.md: All the gods ask you to remove their doubts in religion, and for this reason, O lord, you have been elected their king.

data.v: नार्हसि त्वं सहस्राक्ष त्याजयित्वेह भक्तितः । समर्थमुपजीव्येमं त्यजेयं कथमद्य वै ॥
तस्य वाक्येन सौम्येन हर्षितः पाकशासनः । शुकं प्रोवाच धर्मज्ञमानृशंस्येन तोषितः ॥
data.md: You should not, O thousandeyed one, advise me now to leave this tree for good. When it was capable of good, it supported my life. How can I leave it now? Pleased with these wellmeant words of the parrot, the virtuous destroyer of Paka, thus said to him:I am pleased with your humane and merciful disposition.

data.v: वरं वृणीष्वेति तदा स च वव्रे वरं शुकः । आनृशंस्यपरो नित्यं तस्य वृक्षस्य संभवम् ॥
data.md: Do you ask a boon of me. At this, the merciful parrot craved this boon of him, saying Let this tree revive.

data.v: विदित्वा च दृढां शक्रस्तां शुके शीलसंपदम् । प्रीतः क्षिप्रमथो वृक्षममृतेनावसिक्तवान् ॥
data.md: Knowing the great attachment of the parrot to that tree and great high character, Indra, wellpleased, caused the tree to be quickly sprinkled over with nectar.

data.v: ततः फलानि पत्राणि शाखाश्चापि मनोरमाः । शुकस्य दृढभक्तित्वाच्छ्रीमत्त्वं चाप स द्रुमः ॥
data.md: Then that tree became revived and grand through the penanres of the parrot, and the latter, too, O great king, at the end of his life, acquired the companionship of Shakra by virtue of that act of mercy.

data.v: शुकश्च कर्मणा तेन आनृशंस्यकृतेन ह । आयुषोऽन्ते महाराज प्राप शक्रसलोकताम् ॥
data.md: Then that tree became revived and grand through the penanres of the parrot, and the latter, too, O great king, at the end of his life, acquired the companionship of Shakra by virtue of that act of mercy.

data.v: एवमेव मनुष्येन्द्र भक्तिमन्तं समाश्रितः । सर्वार्थसिद्धिं लभते शुकं प्राप्य यथा द्रुमः ॥
data.md: Thus, o king, by communion and companionship with the pious, people acquire all the objects of their desire even as the tree did through its companionship with the parrot."

data.v: पितामह महाप्राज्ञ सर्वशास्त्रविशारद । दैवे पुरुषकारे च किं स्विच्छ्रेष्ठतरं भवेत् ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Of Exertion and Destiny, tell me O learned sire who are versed in all the scriptures, which is the more potent?

data.v: अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् । वसिष्ठस्य च संवादं ब्रह्मणश्च युधिष्ठिर ॥
data.md: Bhishma said “Regarding it, this ancient legend, the story of Vasava and the great Shuka, is cited as an illustration.

data.v: दैवमानुषयोः किं स्वित्कर्मणोः श्रेष्ठमित्युत । पुरा वसिष्ठो भगवान्पितामहमपृच्छत ॥
data.md: In days of yore the worshipful Vasishta enquired of Brahman as to which among these two, viz., the Karma of a creature acquired in this life, or that acquired in pristine lives (and called Destiny), is the more powerful in shaping his life.

data.v: ततः पद्मोद्भवो राजन्देवदेवः पितामहः । उवाच मधुरं वाक्यमर्थवद्धेतुभूषितम् ॥
data.md: Then, O king, the great god Brahman, who had originated from the primeval lotus. answered him in these sweet and wellreasoned pregnant words.

data.v: नाबीजं जायते किंचिन्न बीजेन विना फलम् । बीजाद्बीजं प्रभवति बीजादेव फलं स्मृतम् ॥
data.md: Brahmana said Nothing springs into existence without seed. Without seed, fruits do not grow. From seeds originate other seeds. Hence are fruits known to be sprung from seeds.

data.v: यादृशं वपते बीजं क्षेत्रमासाद्य कर्षकः । सुकृते दुष्कृते वापि तादृशं लभते फलम् ॥
data.md: According to the good or bad seed that the husbandman sows in his field, he reaps good or bad fruits.

data.v: यथा बीजं विना क्षेत्रमुप्तं भवति निष्फलम् । तथा पुरुषकारेण विना दैवं न सिध्यति ॥
data.md: As, unsown with seed, the soil, through tilled, becomes fruitless, so, without personal Exertion, Destiny is of no use.

data.v: क्षेत्रं पुरुषकारस्तु दैवं बीजमुदाहृतम् । क्षेत्रबीजसमायोगात्ततः सस्यं समृध्यते ॥
data.md: One's own deeds are like the soil, and Destiny is compared to the seed. The harvest grows from the union of the soil and seed.

data.v: कर्मणः फलनिर्वृत्तिं स्वयमश्नाति कारकः । प्रत्यक्षं दृश्यते लोके कृतस्याप्यकृतस्य च ॥
data.md: It is seen every day in the world that the doer reaps the fruit of his good and evil acts; that happiness results from goods deeds, and pain is the outcome of evil ones; that acts, when done, always fructify; and that, if not done, no fruit arises.

data.v: शुभेन कर्मणा सौख्यं दुःखं पापेन कर्मणा । कृतं सर्वत्र लभते नाकृतं भुज्यते क्वचित् ॥
data.md: It is seen every day in the world that the doer reaps the fruit of his good and evil acts; that happiness results from goods deeds, and pain is the outcome of evil ones; that acts, when done, always fructify; and that, if not done, no fruit arises.

data.v: कृती सर्वत्र लभते प्रतिष्ठां भाग्यविक्षतः । अकृती लभते भ्रष्टः क्षते क्षारावसेचनम् ॥
data.md: A man of (good) act gains merits with good fortune, while and idler loses his estate, and reaps evil like the infusion of alkaline matter injected into a wound.

data.md: By reading all the Vedas, is immediately freed from misery, and by practising virtue in thought, one acquires the heavenly regions.

data.v: या दुस्त्यजा दुर्मतिभिर्या न जीर्यति जीर्यतः । योऽसौ प्राणान्तिको रोगस्तां तृष्णां त्यजतः सुखम् ॥
data.md: That man who shakes off the longing for happiness and material comforts-a thirst that is difficult of conquest by the foolish and which does not abate with the decline of physical vigour and which clings to him like a dreadful disease,-is able to secure happiness.

data.v: यथा धेनुसहस्रेषु वत्सो विन्दति मातरम् । एवं पूर्वकृतं कर्म कर्तारमनुगच्छति ॥
data.md: As the young calf is able to recognise its dam from among a thousand cows, so do the pristinc deeds of a man follow him.

data.v: अचोद्यमानानि यथा पुष्पाणि च फलानि च । स्वकालं नातिवर्तन्ते तथा कर्म पुराकृतम् ॥
data.md: As the flowers and fruits of a tree, unmoved by apparent influences, never miss their proper one season, so does Karma done in a pristine existence bring about its fruits in proper time.

data.v: जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः केशा दन्ता जीर्यन्ति जीर्यतः । चक्षुःश्रोत्रे च जीर्येते तृष्णैका तु न जीर्यते ॥
data.md: With age, man's hair grows grey; his teeth become loose; his eyes and ears too become dim in action; but the only thing that does not decline is his desire for enjoyments.

data.v: येन प्रीणाति पितरं तेन प्रीतः प्रजापतिः । प्रीणाति मातरं येन पृथिवी तेन पूजिता । येन प्रीणात्युपाध्यायं तेन स्याद्ब्रह्म पूजितम् ॥
data.md: Prajapati is pleased with those deeds which please one's father, and the Earth is pleased with those acts which please one's mother, and Brahma is pleased with those acts which please one's mother, and Brahma is adored with those acts that please one's preceptor. Virtue is honoured by him who honours these three. The acts of those who despise these three do not help them.

data.v: सर्वे तस्यादृता धर्मा यस्यैते त्रय आदृताः । अनादृतास्तु यस्यैते सर्वास्तस्याफलाः क्रियाः ॥
भीष्मस्य तद्वचः श्रुत्वा विस्मिताः कुरुपुंगवाः । आसन्प्रहृष्टमनसः प्रीतिमन्तोऽभवंस्तदा ॥
data.md: Vaishampayana said The princes of the line of Kuru became filled with surprise upon listening to this speech of Bhishma. All of them became pleased in mind and overpowered with joy.

data.v: यन्मन्त्रे भवति वृथा प्रयुज्यमाने; यत्सोमे भवति वृथाभिषूयमाणे । यच्चाग्नौ भवति वृथाभिहूयमाने; तत्सर्वं भवति वृथाभिधीयमाने ॥
data.md: As Mantras applied for gaining victory, or the performance of the Soma sacrifice made without proper gifts, or oblations poured on the fire without proper hymns, become fruitless and produce evil results, so sin and evil results originate from falsehood.

data.v: इत्येतदृषिणा प्रोक्तमुक्तवानस्मि यद्विभो । शुभाशुभफलप्राप्तौ किमतः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥
data.md: O prince, I have thus described to you this doctrine of the fruition of good and evil deeds, as recounted by the Rishis of old. What else do you wish to hear. O prince, I have thus described to you this doctrine of the fruition of good and evil deeds, as recounted by the Rishis of old. What else do you wish to hear.

data.v: के पूज्याः के नमस्कार्याः कान्नमस्यसि भारत । एतन्मे सर्वमाचक्ष्व येषां स्पृहयसे नृप ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said Who are deserving of adoration? Who are they to whom one may bow? Who are they, O Bharata, to whom you would lower your head? Who, again, are they whom you like? Tell me all this, O prince.

data.v: उत्तमापद्गतस्यापि यत्र ते वर्तते मनः । मनुष्यलोके सर्वस्मिन्यदमुत्रेह चाप्युत ॥
data.md: What is that upon which your mind turn when affliction overwhelms you. Do you describe to me what is beneficial here, that is, in this region of human beings, as also hereafter.

data.v: स्पृहयामि द्विजातीनां येषां ब्रह्म परं धनम् । येषां स्वप्रत्ययः स्वर्गस्तपःस्वाध्यायसाधनः ॥
data.md: Bhishma said I like those twiceborn persons whose highest wealth is Brahma, whose heaven is their knowledge of the soul, and whose penances are formed by their diligent study of the Vedas.

data.v: येषां वृद्धाश्च बालाश्च पितृपैतामहीं धुरम् । उद्वहन्ति न सीदन्ति तेषां वै स्पृहयाम्यहम् ॥
data.md: My heart longs for those in whose family persons young and old diligently bear the, ancestral burthens without languishing under them.

data.v: विद्यास्वभिविनीतानां दान्तानां मृदुभाषिणाम् । श्रुतवृत्तोपपन्नानां सदाक्षरविदां सताम् ॥
संसत्सु वदतां येषां हंसानामिव संघशः । मङ्गल्यरूपा रुचिरा दिव्यजीमूतनिःस्वनाः ॥
सम्यगुच्चारिता वाचः श्रूयन्ते हि युधिष्ठिर । शुश्रूषमाणे नृपतौ प्रेत्य चेह सुखावहाः ॥
ये चापि तेषां श्रोतारः सदा सदसि संमताः । विज्ञानगुणसंपन्नास्तेषां च स्पृहयाम्यहम् ॥
data.md: Indeed, my heart longs after them who endued with knowledge and all desirable attributes, and honoured by others, listen to such words when uttered in assemblies or the courts of kings.

data.v: सुसंस्कृतानि प्रयताः शुचीनि गुणवन्ति च । ददत्यन्नानि तृप्त्यर्थं ब्राह्मणेभ्यो युधिष्ठिर । ये चापि सततं राजंस्तेषां च स्पृहयाम्यहम् ॥
data.md: My heart, O king, always yearns after them who, for the satisfaction of Brahmanas, O Yudhishthira, give to them, with devotion, food that is well-cooked and clean and wholesome.

data.v: शक्यं ह्येवाहवे योद्धुं न दातुमनसूयितम् । शूरा वीराश्च शतशः सन्ति लोके युधिष्ठिर । तेषां संख्यायमानानां दानशूरो विशिष्यते ॥
data.md: In this world, O Yudhishthira, there are hundreds of brave men and heroes. While counting them, he who is a hero in gifts should be considered as superior.

data.v: धन्यः स्यां यद्यहं भूयः सौम्य ब्राह्मणकोऽपि वा । कुले जातो धर्मगतिस्तपोविद्यापरायणः ॥
data.md: O amiable one, if I had been even a vulgar Brahmana I would have considered myself as very great, not to speak of one born in a good family, gifted with righteousness of conduct, and given to penances and learning.

data.v: न मे त्वत्तः प्रियतरो लोकेऽस्मिन्पाण्डुनन्दन । त्वत्तश्च मे प्रियतरा ब्राह्मणा भरतर्षभ ॥
data.md: There is no one, O son of Pandu, in this world, who is dearer to me than you, O chief of Bharats's race, but Brahmans are dearer to me than you.

data.v: यथा मम प्रियतरास्त्वत्तो विप्राः कुरूद्वह । तेन सत्येन गच्छेयं लोकान्यत्र स शंतनुः ॥
data.md: And since, O best of the Kurus, the Brahmanas are very much dearer to me than you, it is by that truth that I expect to go to all those regions of happiness which have been gained by my father Shantanu.

data.v: न मे पिता प्रियतरो ब्राह्मणेभ्यस्तथाभवत् । न मे पितुः पिता वापि ये चान्येऽपि सुहृज्जनाः ॥
data.md: Neither my father, nor my grandfather, nor any one else connected with me by blood, is dearer to me than the Brahmanas.

data.v: न हि मे वृजिनं किंचिद्विद्यते ब्राह्मणेष्विह । अणु वा यदि वा स्थूलं विदितं साधुकर्मभिः ॥
data.md: I do not expect any fruit, small or great, from my adoration of the Brahmanas.

data.v: कर्मणा मनसा वापि वाचा वापि परंतप । यन्मे कृतं ब्राह्मणेषु तेनाद्य न तपाम्यहम् ॥
data.md: On account of what I have done to the Brahmanas in thought, word, and deed, I do not feel any pain now.

data.v: ब्रह्मण्य इति मामाहुस्तया वाचास्मि तोषितः । एतदेव पवित्रेभ्यः सर्वेभ्यः परमं स्मृतम् ॥
data.md: People used to call me as one devoted to the Brahmanas. This address always pleased me highly. To do good to the Brahmanas is the most sacred of all sacred duties.

data.v: पश्यामि लोकानमलाञ्छुचीन्ब्राह्मणयायिनः । तेषु मे तात गन्तव्यमह्नाय च चिराय च ॥
data.md: I see many regions of beatitude waiting for me who have respectfully followed the Brahmanas. Very soon shall I go to these regions for good, O son.

data.v: यथा पत्याश्रयो धर्मः स्त्रीणां लोके युधिष्ठिर । स देवः सा गतिर्नान्या क्षत्रियस्य तथा द्विजाः ॥
data.md: In this world, O Yudhishthira, the duties of women depend upon their husbands. To a woman, verily, the husband is the god and he is the highest end for which she should try. As the husband to wife, so are the Brahmanas to Kshatriyas.

data.v: क्षत्रियः शतवर्षी च दशवर्षी च ब्राह्मणः । पितापुत्रौ च विज्ञेयौ तयोर्हि ब्राह्मणः पिता ॥
data.md: If there be a Kshatriya hundred years old and a good Brahmana child of only ten years, the latter should be considered as a father and the former as a son, for among the two, the Brahmana is superior.

data.v: नारी तु पत्यभावे वै देवरं कुरुते पतिम् । पृथिवी ब्राह्मणालाभे क्षत्रियं कुरुते पतिम् ॥
data.md: A woman, in the absence of her husband, takes his younger brother for her lord; so the Earth, not having obtained Brahmana, made the Kshatriya her king.

data.v: पुत्रवच्च ततो रक्ष्या उपास्या गुरुवच्च ते । अग्निवच्चोपचर्या वै ब्राह्मणाः कुरुसत्तम ॥
data.md: The Brahmanas should be protected like sons and adored like fathers or preceptors. Indeed, O best of the Kurus, they served reverentially as people wait with respect upon their sacrificial or Homa fires.

data.v: ऋजून्सतः सत्यशीलान्सर्वभूतहिते रतान् । आशीविषानिव क्रुद्धान्द्विजानुपचरेत्सदा ॥
data.md: The Brahmanas are gifted with simplicity and righteousness. They are given to truth. They are always engaged in the behalf of all creatures. Yet when angry they are like snakes of dreadful venom. They should, for these reasons, be always waited upon and served with respect and humility.

data.v: तेजसस्तपसश्चैव नित्यं बिभ्येद्युधिष्ठिर । उभे चैते परित्याज्ये तेजश्चैव तपस्तथा ॥
data.md: One should, O Yudhishthira, always fear these two, viz., Energy and Penances. Both these should be shirked or kept at a distance.

data.v: व्यवसायस्तयोः शीघ्रमुभयोरेव विद्यते । हन्युः क्रुद्धा महाराज ब्राह्मणा ये तपस्विनः ॥
data.md: The effects of both are quick, There is this superiority, however, of Penances, viz., that Brahmanas gifted with Penances, O king, can, if angry, kill the object of their anger.

data.v: भूयः स्यादुभयं दत्तं ब्राह्मणाद्यदकोपनात् । कुर्यादुभयतःशेषं दत्तशेषं न शेषयेत् ॥
data.md: Even greatest Energy and Penances, become neutralised if applied against a Brahmana who has conquered anger. If the two that is, Energy and Penances-be set against each other, then both of them would be destroyed. Again when Energy, is set against Penances, it is sure to be destroyed without leaving a remnant. Penances applied against Energy cannot be destroyed completely.

data.v: दण्डपाणिर्यथा गोषु पालो नित्यं स्थिरो भवेत् । ब्राह्मणान्ब्रह्म च तथा क्षत्रियः परिपालयेत् ॥
data.md: As the herdsman, stick in hand, protects the herd, so should the Kshatriya always protect the Vedas and the Brahmanas.

data.v: पितेव पुत्रान्रक्षेथा ब्राह्मणान्ब्रह्मतेजसः । गृहे चैषामवेक्षेथाः कच्चिदस्तीह जीवनम् ॥
data.md: The Kshatriya should protect all pious Brahmanas as a father protects his sons. He should always look after the houses of the Brahmanas for finding out that the means of subsistence may not be wanting.

data.v: ब्राह्मणानां तु ये लोके प्रतिश्रुत्य पितामह । न प्रयच्छन्ति मोहात्ते के भवन्ति महामते ॥
data.md: Yudhishthira said O grandfather, O you of great splendour, what do those men become who, through stupefaction of intellect, do not make gifts to Brahmanas after having promised to make those gifts?

data.v: एतन्मे तत्त्वतो ब्रूहि धर्मं धर्मभृतां वर । प्रतिश्रुत्य दुरात्मानो न प्रयच्छन्ति ये नराः ॥
data.md: O foremost of all righteous persons, do tell me what the duties are in this matter. Indeed, what becomes the end of those wicked men who do not give after having promised to give.

data.v: यो न दद्यात्प्रतिश्रुत्य स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु । आशास्तस्य हताः सर्वाः क्लीबस्येव प्रजाफलम् ॥
data.md: Bhishma said The person who, after having promised, does not give, be it little or much, has the mortification to witness his hopes frustrated like the hopes of a eunuch about children.

data.v: यां रात्रिं जायते पापो यां च रात्रिं विनश्यति । एतस्मिन्नन्तरे यद्यत्सुकृतं तस्य भारत । यच्च तस्य हुतं किंचित्सर्वं तस्योपहन्यते ॥
data.md: Whatever good acts such a person does between the day of his birth and that of his death, O Bharata, whatever libations he pours on the sacrificial fire, whatever gifts he makes, o chief of Bharata's race, and whatever penances he performs, all becomes useless.

data.v: अत्रैतद्वचनं प्राहुर्धर्मशास्त्रविदो जनाः । निशम्य भरतश्रेष्ठ बुद्ध्या परमयुक्तया ॥
data.md: They who conversant with the scriptures hold this as their opinion, arriving at it, О chief of the Bharatas, with the help of a well-ordered understanding.
